verses.text: As though it were of any importance by what name it is called, when the thing itself is there—for a woman to have a child to whom she has not given birth, or a man a child whom he has not begotten.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:321
verses.text: And he may, without any opposition from me, refuse to call Joseph adopted, provided he grant that he may have been the son of a man of whose body he was not born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:322
verses.text: Yet the Apostle Paul 			 does continually use this very word "adoption," and that to express a great mystery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:323
verses.text: For though Scripture testifies that our Lord Jesus Christ is the only Son of God, it says, that the brethren and coheirs whom He hath vouchsafed to have, are made so by a kind of adoption through Divine grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:324
verses.text: "When," saith he, "the fulness of time was come, God sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:325
verses.text: And in another place: "We groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:326
verses.text: And again, when he was speaking of the Jews, "I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh; who are Israelites, to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the testaments, and the giving of the law; whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, Who is over all, God blessed for ever".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:327
verses.text: Where he shows, that the word "adoption," or at least the thing which it signifies, was of ancient use among the Jews, just as was the Testament and the giving of the Law, which he mentions together with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:328
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:329
verses.text: Added to this; there is another way peculiar to the Jews, in which a man might be the son of another of whom he was not born according to the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:330
verses.text: For kinsmen used to marry the wives of their next of kin, who died without children, to raise up seed to him that was deceased.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:331
verses.text: So then he who was thus born was both his son of whom he was born, and his in whose line of succession he was born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:332
verses.text: All this has been said, lest any one, thinking it impossible for two fathers to be mentioned properly for one man, should imagine that either of the Evangelists who have narrated the generations of the Lord are to be, by an impious calumny, charged so to say with a lie; especially when we may see that we are warned against this by their very words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:333
verses.text: For Matthew, 			 who is understood to make mention of that father of whom Joseph was born, enumerates the generations thus: "This one begat the other," so as to come to what he says at the end, "Jacob begat Joseph".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:334
verses.text: But Luke—because he cannot properly be said to be begotten who is made a child either by adoption, or who is born in the succession of the deceased, of her who was his wife—did not say, "Heli begat Joseph," or "Joseph whom Heli begat," but "Who was the son of Heli," whether 			 by adoption, or as being born of the next of kin in the succession of one deceased.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:335
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:336
verses.text: Enough has now been said to show that the question, why the generations are reckoned through Joseph and not through Mary, ought not to perplex us; for as she was a mother without carnal desire, so was he a father without any carnal intercourse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:337
verses.text: Let then the generations ascend and descend through him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:338
verses.text: And let us not exclude him from being a father, because he had none of this carnal desire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:339
verses.text: Let his greater purity only confirm rather his relationship of father, 			 lest the holy Mary herself reproach us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:340
verses.text: For she would not put her own name before her husband; but said, "Thy father and I have sought Thee sorrowing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:341
verses.text: Let not then these perverse murmurers do that which the chaste spouse of Joseph did not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:342
verses.text: Let us reckon then through Joseph, because as he is in chastity a husband, so is he in chastity a father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:343
verses.text: And let us put the man before the woman, according to the order of nature and the law of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:344
verses.text: For if we should cast him aside and leave her, he would say, and say with reason, "Why have you excluded me? Why do not the generations ascend and descend through me?" Shall we say to him, 			 "Because thou didst not beget Him by the operation of thy flesh?" Surely he will answer, "And is it by the operation of the flesh that the Virgin bare Him? What the Holy Spirit wrought, He wrought for both".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:345
verses.text: "Being a just man," saith the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:346
verses.text: The husband then was just and the woman just.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:347
verses.text: The Holy Spirit reposing in the justice of them both, gave to both a Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:348
verses.text: In that sex which is by nature fitted to give birth, He wrought that birth which was for the husband also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:349
verses.text: And therefore doth the Angel bid them both give the Child a name, and hereby is the authority of both parents established.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:350
verses.text: For when Zacharias was yet dumb, the mother gave a name to her newborn son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:351
verses.text: And when they who were present 			 "made signs to his father what he would have him called, he took a writing-table and wrote" the name which she had already pronounced.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:352
verses.text: So to Mary too the Angel saith, "Behold, thou shalt conceive a Son, and shalt call His name Jesus".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:353
verses.text: And to Joseph also he saith, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife; for That which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:354
verses.text: And she shall bring forth a Son, and thou shalt call His name Jesus, for He shall save His people from their sins".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:355
verses.text: Again it is said, "And she brought forth a Son to him," by which he is established to be a father, not in the flesh indeed, but in love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:356
verses.text: Let us then acknowledge him to be a father, as in truth he is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:357
verses.text: For most advisedly and most wisely do the Evangelists reckon through him, whether Matthew in descending from Abraham down to Christ, or Luke in ascending from Christ through Abraham up to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:358
verses.text: The one reckons in a descending, the other in an ascending order; but both through Joseph.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:359
verses.text: And why? Because he is the father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:360
verses.text: How the father? 			 Because he is the more undeniably a father in proportion as he is more chastely so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:361
verses.text: He was thought, it is true, to be the father of our Lord Jesus Christ in another way: that is, as other parents are according to a fleshly birth, and not through the fruitfulness of a wholly spiritual love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:362
verses.text: For Luke said, "Who was supposed to be the father of Jesus".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:363
verses.text: Why supposed? Because men's thoughts and suppositions were directed to what is usually the case with men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:364
verses.text: The Lord then was not of the seed of Joseph, though He was supposed to be; yet nevertheless the Son of the Virgin Mary, who is also the Son of God, was born to Joseph, the fruit of his piety and love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:365
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:366
verses.text: But why does St Matthew reckon in a descending, and Luke in an ascending order? I pray you give attentive ear to what the Lord may help me to say on this matter; with your minds now at ease, and disembarrassed from all the perplexity of these cavillings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:367
verses.text: Matthew descends through his generations, to signify our Lord Jesus Christ descending to bear our sins, that in the seed of Abraham all nations might be blessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:368
verses.text: Wherefore, he does not begin with Adam, for from 			 him is the whole race of mankind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:369
verses.text: Nor with Noe, because from his family again, after the flood, descended the whole human race.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:370
verses.text: Nor could the man Christ Jesus, as descended from Adam, from whom all men are descended, bear upon the fulfilment of prophecy; nor, again, as descended from Noe, from whom also all men are descended; but only as descended from Abraham, who at that time was chosen, that all nations should be blessed in his seed, when the earth was now full of nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:371
verses.text: But Luke reckons in an ascending order, and does not begin to enumerate the generations from the beginning of the account of our Lord's birth, but from that place, where he relates His Baptism by John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:372
verses.text: Now, as in the 			 incarnation of the Lord, the sins of the human race are taken upon Him to be borne, so in the consecration of His Baptism are they taken on Him to be expiated.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:373
verses.text: Accordingly, St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:374
verses.text: Matthew, as representing His descent to bear our sins, enumerates the generations in a descending order; but the other, as representing the expiation of sins, not His own, of course, but our sins, enumerates them in an ascending order.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:375
verses.text: Again, St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:376
verses.text: Matthew descends through Solomon, by whose mother David sinned; St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:377
verses.text: Luke 			 ascends through Nathan another son of the same David, through whom he was purged from his sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:378
verses.text: For we read, that Nathan was sent to him to reprove him, and that he might through repentance be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:379
verses.text: Both Evangelists meet together in David; the one in descending, the other in ascending; and from David to Abraham, or from Abraham to David, there is no difference in any one generation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:380
verses.text: And so Christ, both the Son of David and the Son of Abraham, comes up to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:381
verses.text: For to God must we be brought back, when renewed in Baptism, from the abolition of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:382
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:383
verses.text: Now, in the generations which Matthew enumerates, the predominant number is forty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:384
verses.text: For it is a custom of the Holy Scriptures, not to reckon what is over and above certain round numbers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:385
verses.text: For thus it is said to be four hundred years, after which the people of Israel went out of Egypt, whereas it is four hundred and thirty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:386
verses.text: And so here the one generation, which exceeds the fortieth, does not take away the predominance of that number.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:387
verses.text: Now this number signifies the life wherein we labour in this world, as long as we are absent from the Lord, during which the temporal dispensation of the preaching of the truth is necessary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:388
verses.text: For the number ten, by which the perfection of blessedness is signified, multiplied four times, because of the fourfold divisions of the seasons, and 			 the fourfold divisions of the world, will make the number forty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:389
verses.text: Wherefore Moses and Elias, and the Mediator Himself, our Lord Jesus Christ, fasted forty days, because in the time of this life, continence from the enticements of the body is necessary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:390
verses.text: Forty years also did the people wander in the wilderness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:391
verses.text: Forty days the waters of the flood lasted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:392
verses.text: Forty days after His resurrection did the Lord converse with the disciples, persuading them of the reality of His risen body, whereby He showed that in this life, "wherein we are absent from the Lord" (which the number forty, as has been already said, mystically figures), we have need to celebrate the memory of the Lord's Body, which we do in the Church, till He come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:393
verses.text: Forasmuch, then as our Lord descended to this life, and "the Word was made flesh, that He might be delivered for our sins, and rise again for our justification," Matthew followed the number forty; so that the one generation which there exceeds that number, either does not hinder its predominance—just as those thirty years do not hinder the perfect number of four hundred—or that it even has this further meaning, that the Lord Himself, by the addition of whom the forty-one is made up, so descended to this life to bear our sins, as yet, by a peculiar and especial excellency, whereby He is in such sense man, as to be also God, to be 			 found to be excepted from this life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:394
verses.text: For of Him only is that said, which never has been or shall be able to be said of any holy man, however perfected in wisdom and righteousness, "The Word was made Flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:395
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:396
verses.text: But Luke, who ascends up through the generations from the baptism of the Lord, makes up the number seventy-seven, beginning to ascend from our Lord Jesus Christ Himself through Joseph, and coming through Adam up to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:397
verses.text: And that is, because by this number is signified the abolition of all sins, which takes place in Baptism.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:398
verses.text: Not that the Lord Himself had any thing to be forgiven Him in baptism, but that by His humility He set forth its usefulness to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:399
verses.text: And 			 though that was only the baptism of John, yet there appeared in it to outward sense the Trinity of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and hereby was consecrated the Baptism of Christ Himself, whereby Christians were to be baptized.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:400
verses.text: The Father in the voice which came from heaven, the Son in the person of the Mediator Himself, the Holy Ghost in the dove.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:401
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:402
verses.text: Now, why the number seventy-seven should contain all sins which are remitted in Baptism, there occurs this probable reason, for that the number ten implies the perfection of all righteousness, and blessedness, when the creature denoted by seven cleaves to the Trinity of the Creator; whence also the Decalogue of the Law was consecrated in ten precepts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:403
verses.text: Now the "transgression" of the number ten is signified by the number eleven; and sin is known to be transgression, when a man, in seeking something "more," exceeds the rule of justice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:404
verses.text: And hence the Apostle calls avarice "the root of all evils".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:405
verses.text: And to the soul which goes a-whoring from God, it is said, in the Person of the same Lord, "Thou wast in hope, if thou didst depart from Me, that thou wouldest have something more".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:406
verses.text: Because the sinner then has in his transgression, that is, in his sin, regard to himself alone—in that he wishes to gratify himself by some private good of his own (whence they are blamed "who seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's;" and charity is commended, "which seeketh not her own"); therefore, this number eleven, by which transgression is signified, is multiplied, not ten times, but seven, and so makes up seventy-seven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:407
verses.text: For transgression looks not to the Trinity of the Creator, but to the creature, that is, to the man himself, which creature the number seven denotes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:408
verses.text: Three, because of the soul, in which there is a kind of image of the Trinity of the Creator (for it is in the soul that man has been made after the image of God); and four, because of the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:409
verses.text: For the four elements of which the body is made up are known by all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:410
verses.text: And if any one know them not, he may easily remember, that this body of the world, in which our bodies move along, has, so to say, four principal parts, which even Holy Scripture is constantly making mention of, East, and West, and North, and South.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:411
verses.text: And forasmuch as sins are committed either by the mind, as in the will only, or by the works of the body also, and so visibly; therefore the Prophet Amos continually introduces 			  God as threatening, and saying, "For three and four iniquities I will not turn away," that is," I will not dissemble My wrath".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:412
verses.text: Three, because of the nature of the soul; four, because of that of the body; of which two, man consists.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:413
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:414
verses.text: So, then, seven times eleven, that is, as has been explained, the transgression of righteousness, which has regard only to the sinner himself, make up the number seventy-seven, in which it is signified, that all sins which are remitted in Baptism are contained.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:415
verses.text: And hence it is that Luke ascends up through seventy-seven generations unto God, as showing that man is reconciled unto God by the abolition of all sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:416
verses.text: Hence the Lord Himself saith to Peter, 			 who asked Him how oft he ought to forgive a brother, "I say not unto thee seven times, but until seventy times and seven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:417
verses.text: Now, whatever else can be drawn out of these recesses and treasures of God's mysteries by those who are more diligent and more worthy than I, receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:418
verses.text: Yet have I spoken according to my poor ability, as the Lord hath aided and given me power, and as I best could, considering also the little time I had.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:419
verses.text: If any one of you be capable of anything further, let him knock at Him from whom I too receive what I am able to receive and speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 1:420
verses.text: But, above all things, remember this; not to 			 be disturbed by the Scriptures, which you do not yet understand, nor be puffed up by what you do understand; but what you do not understand, with submission wait for, and what you do understand, hold fast with charity.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:1
verses.text: Sermon II.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:2
verses.text: [LII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:4
verses.text: ]  Of the words of St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:5
verses.text: Matthew's Gospel, Chap.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:6
verses.text: iii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:7
verses.text: 13 , "Then Jesus cometh from Galilee to the Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:8
verses.text: Concerning the Trinity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:9
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:10
verses.text: The lesson of the Gospel hath set before me a subject whereof to speak to you, beloved, as though by the Lord's command, and by His command in very deed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:11
verses.text: For my heart hath waited for an order as it were from Him to speak, that I might understand thereby that it is His wish that I should speak on that which He hath also willed should be read to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:12
verses.text: Let your zeal and devotion then give ear, and before the Lord our God Himself aid ye my 			 labour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:13
verses.text: For we behold and see as it were in a divine spectacle exhibited to us, the notice of our God in Trinity, conveyed to us at the river Jordan.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:14
verses.text: For when Jesus came and was baptized by John, the Lord by His servant (and this He did for an example of humility; for He showeth that in this same humility is righteousness fulfilled, when as John said to Him, "I have need to be baptized of Thee, and comest Thou to me?" He answered, "Suffer it to be so now, that all righteousness may be fulfilled"), when He was baptized then, the heavens were opened, and the Holy Spirit came down upon Him in the form of a Dove: and then a Voice from on high followed, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:15
verses.text: Here then we have the Trinity in a certain sort distinguished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:16
verses.text: The Father in the Voice,—the Son in the Man,—the Holy Spirit in the Dove.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:17
verses.text: It was only needful just to mention this, for most obvious is it to see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:18
verses.text: For the notice of the Trinity is here conveyed to us plainly and without leaving room for doubt or hesitation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:19
verses.text: For the Lord Christ Himself coming in the form of a servant to John, is doubtlessly the Son: for it cannot be said that it was the Father, or the Holy 			 Spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:20
verses.text: "Jesus," it is said, "cometh;" that is, the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:21
verses.text: And who hath any doubt about the Dove? or who saith, "What is the Dove?" when the Gospel itself most plainly testifieth, "The Holy Spirit descended upon Him in the form of a dove".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:22
verses.text: And in like manner as to that voice there can be no doubt that it is the Father's, when He saith, "Thou art My Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:23
verses.text: Thus then we have the Trinity distinguished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:24
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:25
verses.text: And if we consider the places, I say with confidence (though in fear I say it), that the Trinity is in a manner separable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:26
verses.text: When Jesus came to the river, He came from one place to another; and the Dove descended from heaven to earth, from one place to another; and the very Voice of the Father sounded neither from the earth, nor from the water, but from heaven; these three are as it were separated in places, in offices, and in works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:27
verses.text: But one may say to me, "Show 			 the Trinity to be inseparable rather.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:28
verses.text: Remember that thou who art speaking art a Catholic, and to Catholics art thou speaking".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:29
verses.text: For thus doth our faith teach, that is, the true, the right Catholic faith, gathered not by the opinion of private judgment, but by the witness of the Scriptures, not subject to the fluctuations of heretical rashness, but grounded on Apostolic truth: this we know, this we believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:30
verses.text: This though we see it not with our eyes, nor as yet with the heart, so long as we are being purified by faith, yet by this faith we most lightly and most strenuously maintain—That the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are a Trinity inseparable; One God, not three Gods.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:31
verses.text: But yet so One God, as that the Son is not the Father, and the Father is not the Son, and the 			 Holy Spirit is neither the Father nor the Son, but the Spirit of the Father and of the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:32
verses.text: This ineffable Divinity, abiding ever in itself, making all things new, creating, creating anew, sending, recalling, judging, delivering, this Trinity, I say, we know to be at once ineffable and inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:33
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:34
verses.text: What am I then about? See: The Son came separately in the Man; The Holy Spirit descended separately from heaven in the form of a Dove; The Voice of the Father sounded separately out of heaven, "This is My Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:35
verses.text: Where then is this inseparable Trinity? God hath made you attentive by my words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:36
verses.text: Pray for me, and open, as it were, the folds of your hearts, and may He grant you wherewith your hearts so opened may be filled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:37
verses.text: Share my travail with me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:38
verses.text: For you see what I have undertaken; and not only what, but who I am that have undertaken it, and of what I wish to speak, and where and what my position is, even in that "body which is corruptible, and presseth down the soul, and the earthly habitation weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:39
verses.text: When therefore I abstract my mind from the multiplicity of things, and gather it up into the One God, the inseparable Trinity, that so I may see something which I may say of it, think ye that in this "body which presseth down the soul," I shall be able to say (in order that I may speak to you something worthy of the subject), "O Lord, I have lifted up my soul unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:40
verses.text: May He assist me, may He lift it up with me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:41
verses.text: For I am too infirm in respect of Him, and He in respect of me is too mighty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:42
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:43
verses.text: Now this is a question which is often proposed by the most earnest brethren, and often has place in the conversation of the lovers of God's word; for this much knocking is wont to be made unto God, while men say, "Doeth the Father anything which the Son doeth not? or doeth the Son anything which the Father doeth not?" Let us first speak of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:44
verses.text: And when He to Whom we say, "Be Thou my helper, leave me not," 			  shall have given good success to this essay of ours, then shall we understand how that the Holy Spirit also is in no way separated from the operation of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:45
verses.text: As concerning the Father and the Son, then, brethren, give ear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:46
verses.text: Doeth the Father anything without the Son? We answer, No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:47
verses.text: Do you doubt it? For what doeth He without Him "by Whom all things were made? All things," saith the Scripture, "were made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:48
verses.text: And to inculcate it fully upon the slow, and hard, and disputatious it added, And without Him was not anything made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:49
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:50
verses.text: What then, brethren? "All things were made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:51
verses.text: We understand then by this that the whole creation which was made by the Son, the Father made by His Word—God, by His Power and Wisdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:52
verses.text: Shall we then say, "All things" indeed when they were created, "were made by Him," but now the Father doeth not all things by Him? God forbid! Be such a thought as this far from the hearts of believers; be it driven away from the mind of the devout; from the 			 understanding of the godly! It cannot be that He created by Him, and doth not govern by Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:53
verses.text: God forbid that what existeth should be governed without Him, when by Him it was made, that it might have existence! But let us show by the testimony of the same Scripture that not only were all things created and made by Him as we have quoted from the Gospel, "All things were made by Him, and without Him was nothing made," but that the things which were made are also governed and ordered by Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:54
verses.text: You acknowledge Christ then to be the Power and Wisdom of God; acknowledge too what is said of Wisdom, "She reacheth from one end to another mightily, and sweetly doth she order all things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:55
verses.text: Let us not then doubt that by Him are all things ruled, by whom all things were made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:56
verses.text: So then the Father doeth nothing without the Son, nor the Son without the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:57
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:58
verses.text: But so a difficulty meets us, which we have undertaken to solve in the Name of the Lord, and by His will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:59
verses.text: If the Father doeth nothing without the Son, nor the Son without the Father, will it not follow, that we must say that the Father also was born of the Virgin Mary, the Father suffered under Pontius Pilate, the Father rose again and ascended into heaven? God forbid! We do not say this, because we do not believe it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:60
verses.text: "For I believed, therefore have I spoken: 			 we also believe, and therefore speak".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:61
verses.text: What is in the Creed? That the Son was born of a Virgin, not the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:62
verses.text: What is in the Creed? That the Son suffered under Pontius Pilate and was dead, not the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:63
verses.text: Have we forgotten, that some, misunderstanding this, are called "Patripassians," who say that the Father Himself was born of a woman, that the Father Himself suffered, that the Father is the same as the Son, that they are two names, not two things? And these hath the Church Catholic separated from the communion 			 of saints, that they might not deceive any, but dispute in separation from her.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:64
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:65
verses.text: Let us then recall the difficulty of the question to your minds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:66
verses.text: One may say to me, "You have said that the Father doeth nothing without the Son, nor the Son without the Father, and testimonies you have adduced out of the Scriptures, that the Father doeth nothing without the Son, for that 'all things were made by Him;' and again, that that which was made is not governed without the Son, for that He is the Wisdom of the Father, 'reaching from one end to another 			 mightily, and sweetly ordering all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:67
verses.text: ' And now you tell me, as if contradicting yourself, that the Son was born of a Virgin, and not the Father; the Son suffered, not the Father; the Son rose again, not the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:68
verses.text: See then, here I see the Son doing something which the Father doeth not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:69
verses.text: Do you therefore either confess that the Son doeth something without the Father, or else that the Father also was born and suffered, and died and rose again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:70
verses.text: Say one or the other of these, 			 choose one of the two".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:71
verses.text: No: I will choose neither, I will say neither the one nor the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:72
verses.text: I will neither say the Son doeth anything without the Father, for I should lie were I to say so; nor that the Father was born, suffered, and died, and rose again, for I should equally lie were I to say this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:73
verses.text: "How then, saith he, will you disentangle yourself from these straits?"  8.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:74
verses.text: The proposing of the question pleases you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:75
verses.text: May God grant His aid, that its solution may please you too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:76
verses.text: See, what I am asking Him, that He would free both me and you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:77
verses.text: For in one faith do we stand in the Name of Christ; and in one house do we live under one Lord, and in one body are we members under One Head, and by One Spirit are we quickened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:78
verses.text: That the Lord then may set both me who speak, and you who hear, free from the straits of this most perplexing question, I say as follows: The Son indeed and not the Father was born of the Virgin Mary; but this very birth of the Son, not of the Father, was the work both of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:79
verses.text: The Father indeed suffered not, but the Son, yet the suffering of the Son was the work of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:80
verses.text: The Father did not rise again, but the Son, yet the resurrection of 			 the Son was the work of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:81
verses.text: We seem then to be already quit of this question, but peradventure it is only by words of my own; let us see whether it is not as well by words divine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:82
verses.text: It is my place then to prove by testimonies of the sacred books, that the birth, and passion, and resurrection of the Son were in such sort the works of the Father and the Son, that whereas it is the birth, and passion, and resurrection of the Son only, yet these three things which belong to the 			 Son only, were wrought neither by the Father alone, nor by the Son alone, but by the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:83
verses.text: Let us prove each several point, you hear as judges; the case has been already laid open; now let the witnesses come forth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:84
verses.text: Let your judgment say to me, as is wont to be said to pleaders in a cause, "Establish what you promise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:85
verses.text: I will do so assuredly, with the Lord's assistance, and will cite the books of heavenly law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:86
verses.text: Ye have listened to me attentively while proposing the question, 			 listen now with still more attention while I prove my point.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:87
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:88
verses.text: I must first teach you concerning the birth of Christ, how it is the work of the Father and the Son, though what the Father and the Son did work pertains only to the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:89
verses.text: I will quote Paul; one competently versed in the divine law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:90
verses.text: That Paul, I say, will I quote, who prescribes the laws of peace, not of litigation, for lawyers at this day also have a Paul who prescribes the laws of the courts, not the Christian's laws.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:91
verses.text: Let the holy Apostle show us then how the birth of the Son was the work of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:92
verses.text: "But," saith he, "when the fulness of time was come, God sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the Law, to redeem them that were under the Law".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:93
verses.text: Thus have ye heard him, and because it is plain and express, have understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:94
verses.text: See, the Father made the Son to be born of a Virgin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:95
verses.text: For "when the fulness of time was come, God sent His Son;" the Father sent His Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:96
verses.text: How sent He Him? "made of a woman, made under the Law".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:97
verses.text: The Father then made Him of a woman under the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:98
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:99
verses.text: Doth this peradventure perplex you, that I said of a virgin, and Paul saith of a woman? Let not this perplex you; let us not stop here, for I am not speaking to persons without instruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:100
verses.text: The Scripture saith both, both "of a virgin," and "of a woman".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:101
verses.text: Where saith it, "of a virgin? Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:102
verses.text: And "of a woman," as you have just heard; here there is no contradiction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:103
verses.text: For the peculiarity of the Hebrew tongue gives the name of "women" not to such as have lost their virgin estate, but to females generally.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:104
verses.text: You have a plain passage in Genesis, when Eve herself was first made, "He made her a woman".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:105
verses.text: Scripture also in another place saith, that God ordered "the women" to be separated "which had not known man by lying with him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:106
verses.text: This then ought now to be well established, and should not detain us, that so we may be able to explain, by the Lord's assistance, what will deservedly detain us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:107
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:108
verses.text: We have then proved that the birth of the Son was the work of the Father; now let us prove that it was the work of the Son also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:109
verses.text: Now what is the birth of the Son of the Virgin Mary? Surely it is His assumption of the form of a servant in the Virgin's womb.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:110
verses.text: Is the birth of the Son ought else, but the taking of the form of a servant in the womb of the Virgin? Now hear how that this was the work of the Son also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:111
verses.text: "Who when He was in the form of God, thought it 			 not robbery to be equal with God, but emptied Himself, taking upon Him the form of a servant".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:112
verses.text: "When the fulness of time was come, God sent forth His Son, made of a woman," who was "made His Son of the seed of David according to the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:113
verses.text: In this then we see that the birth of the Son was the work of the Father; but in that the Son Himself "emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant," we see that the birth of the Son was the work also of the Son Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:114
verses.text: This then has been proved; so let us pass on from this point, and receive ye with attention that which comes next in order.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:115
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:116
verses.text: Let us prove that the Passion also of the Son was the work of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:117
verses.text: We may see that the Passion of the Son is the work of the Father, since it is written, "Who spared not His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all;" and that the Passion of the Son was His own work also, "Who loved me, and gave Himself for me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:118
verses.text: The Father delivered up the Son, and the Son delivered up Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:119
verses.text: This Passion was wrought out for one, but by both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:120
verses.text: As therefore the birth, so the Passion, of Christ, was not the work of the Son without the Father, nor of the Father without the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:121
verses.text: The Father delivered up the Son, and the Son delivered up Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:122
verses.text: What did Judas in it, but his own sin? Let us then pass on from this point also, and come we to the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:123
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:124
verses.text: Let us see the Son indeed, and not the Father, rising again, but both the Father and the Son working the resurrection of the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:125
verses.text: The resurrection of the Son is the work of the Father; for it is written, "Wherefore He exalted Him, and gave Him a name which is above every name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:126
verses.text: The Father therefore raised the Son to life again, in exalting, and awakening Him from the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:127
verses.text: And did the Son also raise Himself? Assuredly He did.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:128
verses.text: For He said of the temple, as the figure of His own body, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it again".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:129
verses.text: Lastly, as the laying down of life has reference to the Passion, so the taking it again has reference to the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:130
verses.text: Let us see then if the Son laid down His life indeed, and the Father restored His life to Him, and not He to Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:131
verses.text: For that the Father restored it is plain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:132
verses.text: For so saith the Psalm, "Raise Thou Me up, and I will requite them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:133
verses.text: But why do ye wait for a proof from me that the Son also restored life to Himself? Let Him speak Himself; "I have power to lay down My life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:134
verses.text: I have not yet said what I promised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:135
verses.text: I have said, "to lay it down;" and you are crying out already, for you are flying past me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:136
verses.text: For well-instructed as ye are in the school of your heavenly teacher, as attentively listening to, and in pious affection rehearsing, what is read, ye are not ignorant of what comes next.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:137
verses.text: "I have power," saith He,"to lay down My life, and I have power to take it again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:138
verses.text: No man taketh it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself, and take it again".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:139
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:140
verses.text: I have made good what I promised; I have established my propositions with, as I think, the strongest proofs and testimonies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:141
verses.text: Hold fast then what you have heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:142
verses.text: I will recapitulate it briefly, and entrust it to be stored up in your minds as a thing, to my thinking, of the greatest usefulness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:143
verses.text: The Father was not born of the Virgin; yet this birth of the Son from the Virgin was the work both of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:144
verses.text: The Father suffered not on the Cross; yet the 			 Passion of the Son was the work both of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:145
verses.text: The Father rose not again from the dead; yet the resurrection of the Son was the work both of the Father and the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:146
verses.text: You see then a distinction of Persons, and an inseparableness of operation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:147
verses.text: Let us not say therefore that the Father doeth any thing without the Son, or the Son any thing without the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:148
verses.text: But perhaps you have a difficulty as to the miracles which Jesus did, lest peradventure He did some which the Father did not! 			 Where then is that saying, "The Father who dwelleth in Me, He doeth the works?" All that I have now said was plain; it needed to be barely mentioned; there was no necessity for much labour to make it understood, but only that care should be taken, that it might be brought to your remembrance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:149
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:150
verses.text: I wish to say something further, and here ask sincerely both for your more earnest attention, and your devotion to Godward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:151
verses.text: For none but bodies are held or contained in places suited to the nature of bodies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:152
verses.text: The Divinity is beyond all such places: let no one seek for it as though it were in space.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:153
verses.text: It is everywhere invisible and inseparably present; not in one part greater, and another smaller; but whole everywhere, and nowhere divided.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:154
verses.text: Who can see? Who can comprehend this? Let us restrain ourselves: let us remember who we are; and of Whom we speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:155
verses.text: Let this and that, or whatever appertains to the nature of God, be with a pious faith embraced, with a holy respect entertained, and as far as is allowed us, as far as is possible for us, in an unspeakable sort understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:156
verses.text: Let words be hushed: let the tongue be silent, let the heart be aroused, let the heart be lifted up thither.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:157
verses.text: For it is not of such a nature as that it can ascend into the heart of man; but the heart of man must itself ascend to it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:158
verses.text: Let us consider the creatures ("for the invisible things of Him 			 from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made"), if haply in the things which God hath made, with which we have some familiarity of intercourse, we may find some resemblance, whereby we may prove that there are some three things which may be exhibited as three separably, yet whose operation is inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:159
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:160
verses.text: Come, brethren, give me your whole attention.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:161
verses.text: But first of all consider what it is that I promise; if haply I can find any resemblance in the creature, for the Creator is too high above us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:162
verses.text: And peradventure some one of us, whose mind the glare of truth hath, as it were, stricken with sparks of its brightness, can say those words, "I said in my ecstasy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:163
verses.text: —What saidst thou in thine ecstasy?—"I am cast away from the sight of Thine eyes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:164
verses.text: For it seems to me as if he who said this had lifted up his soul unto God, and had been carried beyond himself, while they said daily unto him, "Where is thy God?"—had reached by a kind of spiritual contact to that unchangeable Light, and through the weakness of his sight had been unable to endure it, and so had fallen back again into his own, as it were, sick and languid state, and had compared himself with that Light, and had felt that the eye of his mind could not yet be attempered to the light of God's wisdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:165
verses.text: And because he had done this in ecstasy, hurried away from his bodily senses, and taken up into God, when he was recalled in a manner from God to man, he said, "I said in my ecstasy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:166
verses.text: For I saw in ecstasy I know not what, which I could not long endure, and being restored to my mortal estate, and the manifold thoughts of mortal things from the body which presseth down the soul, I said, what? "I am cast away from the sight of Thine eyes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:167
verses.text: Thou art far above, and I am far below.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:168
verses.text: What then, brethren, shall we say of God? For if thou hast been able to comprehend what thou wouldest say, it is not God; if thou hast been able to comprehend it, thou hast comprehended something else instead of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:169
verses.text: If thou hast been able to comprehend Him as thou thinkest, by so 			 thinking thou hast deceived thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:170
verses.text: This then is not God, if thou hast comprehended it; but if it be God, thou hast not comprehended it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:171
verses.text: How therefore wouldest thou speak of that which thou canst not comprehend?  17.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:172
verses.text: Let us see then, if haply we cannot find something in the creature whereby we may prove that some three things are exhibited separately whose operation is yet inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:173
verses.text: But whither shall we go? To the heaven, to dispute of the sun and moon and stars? To the earth, to dispute of shrubs, and trees, and animals which fill the earth? Or of the heaven and the earth itself, which contain all the things that are in heaven and earth? How long, O man, wilt thou roam over the creation? Return unto thyself, see, consider, examine thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:174
verses.text: Thou art searching among the creatures for some three things 			 which are separately exhibited, whose operation is yet inseparable; if then thou art searching for this among the creatures, search for it first in thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:175
verses.text: For thou art not other than a creature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:176
verses.text: It is a resemblance thou art searching for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:177
verses.text: Wouldest thou search for it among the cattle? For of God it was thou wast speaking, when thou wast in search for this resemblance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:178
verses.text: Thou wast speaking of the Trinity of Majesty ineffable, and because thou didst fail in contemplating 			  the Divine Nature, and with becoming humility didst confess thine infirmity, thou didst come down to human nature; there then pursue thine enquiry.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:179
verses.text: Wilt thou make thy search among the cattle, in the sun, or the stars? What of these was made after the image and likeness of God? Thou mayest search in thine own self for something more familiar to thee, and more excellent than all these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:180
verses.text: For God made man after His own image and likeness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:181
verses.text: Search then in thine own self, if haply the 			 image of the Trinity bear not some vestige of the Trinity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:182
verses.text: And what is this image? It is an image very different from its model; yet different as it is, it is an image and a likeness notwithstanding, not indeed in the same way as the Son is the Image, being the Same Which the Father is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:183
verses.text: For an image is in one sort in a son, and in another in a mirror.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:184
verses.text: There is great difference between them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:185
verses.text: Thine image in thy son is thine own self, for the son is by nature what thou art.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:186
verses.text: In substance the same 			 as thou, in person other than thou.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:187
verses.text: Man then is not an image as the Only-begotten Son is, but made after a sort of image and likeness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:188
verses.text: Let him then search for something in himself, if so be he may find it, even for some three things which are exhibited separately, whose operation is yet inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:189
verses.text: I will search, and do ye search with me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:190
verses.text: I will not search in you, but do ye search in yourselves, and I in myself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:191
verses.text: Let us search in concert, and in concert discuss our common nature and substance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:192
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:193
verses.text: See, O man, and consider whether what I am saying be true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:194
verses.text: Hast thou a body and flesh? I have, you say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:195
verses.text: For how am I in this place that I now occupy, and how do I move from place to place? How do I hear the words of one who is speaking, but by the ears of my body? How do I see the mouth of him who is speaking, but by the eyes of my body? It is plain then that thou hast a body, no need is there to trouble one's self about so plain a matter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:196
verses.text: Consider then another 			 point, consider what it is that acts through this body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:197
verses.text: For thou hearest by means of the ear, but it is not the ear that hears.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:198
verses.text: There is something else within which hears by means of the ear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:199
verses.text: Thou seest by means of the eye—examine this eye.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:200
verses.text: What! hast thou acknowledged the house, and paid no regard to him that inhabiteth it? Doth the eye see by itself? Is it not another that sees by means of the eye? I will not say, that the eye of a dead man, from whose body it is plain 			 the inhabitant hath departed, sees not, but any man's eye who is only thinking of something else, sees not the form of the object that is before him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:201
verses.text: Look then into thine inner man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:202
verses.text: For there it is rather that the resemblance must be sought for of some three things which are exhibited separately, whose operation is yet inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:203
verses.text: What then is in thy mind? Peradventure if I search, I find many things there, but there is something very nigh at hand, which is understood more easily.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:204
verses.text: What then 			 is in thy soul? Call it to mind, reflect upon it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:205
verses.text: For I do not require that credit should be given me in what I am about to say; if thou find it not in thyself, admit it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:206
verses.text: Look inward then; but first let us see what had escaped me, whether man be not the image, not of the Son only, or of the Father only, but of the Father and the Son, and so consequently of course of the Holy Ghost also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:207
verses.text: The words in Genesis are, "Let Us make man after Our own image and likeness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:208
verses.text: So then the Father doth not act without the Son, nor the Son without the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:209
verses.text: "Let Us make man after Our own image and likeness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:210
verses.text: Let us make," not, "I will make," or "Make thou," or "Let him make," but, "Let Us make after," not "thine image," or "mine," but, "after Our image".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:211
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:212
verses.text: I am asking, I am speaking remember of a distant resemblance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:213
verses.text: So let no one say, See what he has compared to God! I have advertised you of this already, and by anticipation have both put you on your guard, and have guarded myself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:214
verses.text: The two are indeed very far removed from each other, as the lowest from the Highest, as the changeable from the Unchangeable, the created from the Creator, the human nature from the Divine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:215
verses.text: Lo! I apprise you of this at first, that no one may say ought against me, because there is so great a 			 difference in the things whereof I am about to speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:216
verses.text: Lest then while I am asking for your ears, ye should any of you be getting ready your teeth, remember I have undertaken merely to show, that there are some three things which are separately exhibited, whose operation is yet inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:217
verses.text: How like or how unlike these things are to the Almighty Trinity is no concern of mine at present; but in the very creatures of the lowest order, and subject to change, we do find three things which may be 			 separately exhibited, whose operation is yet inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:218
verses.text: O carnal imagination! obstinate, unbelieving conscience! Why as concerning that ineffable Majesty dost thou doubt as to that thing, which thou canst discover in thine own self? For I ask thee, O man, hast thou memory? If not, how hast thou retained what I have said? But perhaps thou hast forgotten already what I said but a little while ago.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:219
verses.text: Yet these very words, "I said"—these two syllables, thou couldest not retain except by 			 memory.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:220
verses.text: For how shouldest thou know they were two, if as the second sounded, thou hadst forgotten the first? But why do I dwell longer on this? Why am I so urgent? Why do I so press conviction? For thou hast memory; it is plain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:221
verses.text: I am searching then for something else.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:222
verses.text: Hast thou understanding? "I have," you will say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:223
verses.text: For hadst thou not memory, thou couldest not retain what I said; and hadst thou not understanding, thou couldest not comprehend what thou hast retained.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:224
verses.text: Thou hast then this as 			 well as the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:225
verses.text: Thou recallest thine understanding unto that which thou dost retain within, and so thou seest it, and by seeing art fashioned into that state as to be said to know.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:226
verses.text: But I am searching for a third thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:227
verses.text: Memory thou hast, whereby to retain what is said; and understanding thou hast, whereby to understand what is retained; but as touching these two, I ask again of thee, Hast thou not with thy will retained and understood? Undoubtedly, with my will, you will say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:228
verses.text: So then thou 			 hast will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:229
verses.text: These are the three things which I promised I would bring home to your ears and minds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:230
verses.text: These three things are in thee, which thou canst number, but canst not separate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:231
verses.text: These three then, memory, understanding, and will—these three, I say, consider how they are separately exhibited, yet is their operation inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:232
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:233
verses.text: The Lord will be my present help, and I see that He is present to help me; by your understanding what I say, I see that He is present to help me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:234
verses.text: For I perceive by these your voices how that you have understood me, and I surely trust that He will still assist us, that you may comprehend the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:235
verses.text: I promised to show you three things which are separately exhibited whose operation is yet inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:236
verses.text: See then; I did not know what was in thy mind, and thou showedest me 			 by saying, "Memory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:237
verses.text: This word, this sound, this expression came forth from thy mind to mine ears.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:238
verses.text: For before that, thou hadst the silent idea of this memory, but thou didst not express it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:239
verses.text: It was in thee, but it had not yet come to me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:240
verses.text: But in order that that which was in thee might be passed on to me, thou didst express the very word, that is, "Memory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:241
verses.text: I heard it, I heard these three syllables in the word, "Memory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:242
verses.text: It is a noun, a word of three syllables, it sounded, and came 			 to my ear, and impressed a certain idea on my mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:243
verses.text: The sound has passed away, but the word whereby the idea was conveyed, and the idea itself, remains.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:244
verses.text: But I ask, when thou didst pronounce this word, "Memory," thou seest certainly that it has reference to the memory only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:245
verses.text: For the other two things have their own proper names.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:246
verses.text: For one is called "the understanding," and the other, "the will," not the "memory," but that one alone is called "memory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:247
verses.text: Nevertheless, whereby didst thou 			 work in order to express this, in order to produce these three syllables? This word which has reference to the memory only, both memory was engaged in producing in thee, that thou mightest retain what thou saidst, and understanding, that thou mightest know what thou retainedst, and will, that thou mightest give expression to what thou knewest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:248
verses.text: Thanks be to the Lord our God! He hath helped us, both you and me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:249
verses.text: For I tell you the truth, beloved, that I undertook the examination and explanation of 			 this subject with exceeding fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:250
verses.text: For I was afraid lest haply I might gladden the spirit of the more enlarged in mind, and inflict on the slower capacities an afflictive weariness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:251
verses.text: But now I see both by the attention with which you have heard, and the quickness with which you have understood me, that you have not only caught what I have said, but that you have anticipated my words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:252
verses.text: Thanks be to the Lord!  21.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:253
verses.text: See then, henceforth I speak in all security of that which you have already understood; I am inculcating no unknown lesson, but am only conveying to you by recapitulation what you have already received.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:254
verses.text: Now, of these three things, one only has been yet named and expressed; "Memory" is the name of one only of those three, yet all the three concurred in producing the name of this single one of the three.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:255
verses.text: The single word "memory" could not be expressed, but by 			 the operation of the will, and the understanding, and the memory.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:256
verses.text: The single word "understanding" could not be expressed, but by the operation of the memory, the will, and the understanding; and the single word "will" could not be expressed, but by the operation of the memory and the understanding and the will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:257
verses.text: What I promised, then, I think has been explained, that which I have pronounced separately, I conceived inseparably.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:258
verses.text: The three together have produced each one of these, but yet 			 this one which the three have produced has reference not to the three, but to one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:259
verses.text: The three together have produced the word "memory," but this word has reference to none but the memory only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:260
verses.text: The three together have produced the word "understanding," but it has reference to none but the understanding only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:261
verses.text: The three together have produced the word "will," but it has reference to none but the will only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:262
verses.text: So the Trinity concurred in the formation of the Body of Christ, but it belongs 			 to none but Christ only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:263
verses.text: The Trinity concurred in the formation of the Dove from heaven; but it belongs to none but the Holy Spirit only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:264
verses.text: The Trinity formed the Voice from heaven, but this Voice belongs to none but the Father only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:265
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:266
verses.text: Let no one then say to me, no one with unfair cavils try to press upon my infirmity, saying, "Which then of these three, which you have shown to be in our mind or soul, which of them answers to the Father, that is, so to say, to the likeness of the Father, which of them to that of the Son, and which of them to that of the Holy Ghost?" I cannot say—I cannot explain this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:267
verses.text: Let us leave somewhat to meditation and to silence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:268
verses.text: Enter into thine own self; separate thyself from all tumult.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:269
verses.text: Look into thine inner self; see if thou have there some sweet retiring place of conscience, where there may be no noise, no disputation, no strife, or debatings; where there 			 will be not a thought of dissensions, and obstinate contention.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:270
verses.text: Be meek to hear the word, that so thou mayest understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:271
verses.text: Perhaps thou mayest soon have to say, "Thou wilt make me hear of joy and gladness, and my bones shall rejoice;" the bones, that is, which are humbled, not those that are lifted up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:272
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:273
verses.text: It is enough, then, that I have shown that there are some three things which are exhibited separately, whose operation is yet inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:274
verses.text: If thou hast discovered this in thine own self; if thou hast discovered it in man; if thou hast discovered it in a being that walketh on the earth, and beareth about a frail "body, which weigheth down the soul;" believe that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit may be exhibited separately, by certain visible symbols, by certain forms borrowed from the creatures, and still their operation be inseparable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:275
verses.text: This is enough.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:276
verses.text: I do not say that "memory" is the Father,—the "understanding" the Son,—and "will" the Spirit; I do not say this; let men understand it how they will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:277
verses.text: I do not 			 venture to say this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:278
verses.text: Let us reserve the greater truths for those who are capable of them: but, infirm as I am myself, I convey to the infirm only what is according to our powers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:279
verses.text: I do not say that these things are in any sort to be equalled with the Holy Trinity, to be squared after an analogy; that is, a kind of exact rule of comparison.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:280
verses.text: This I do not say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:281
verses.text: But what do I say? See.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:282
verses.text: I have discovered in thee three things, which are exhibited separately, whose operation is inseparable; and of 			 these three, every single name is produced by the three together; yet does not this name belong to the three, but to some one of the three.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:283
verses.text: Believe then in the Trinity, what thou canst not see, if in thyself thou hast heard, and seen, and retained it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:284
verses.text: For what is in thine own self thou canst know: but what is in Him who made thee, whatever it be, how canst thou know? And if thou shalt be ever able, thou art not able yet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:285
verses.text: And even when thou shalt be able, wilt thou be able so 			 to know God, as He knoweth Himself? Let then this suffice you, beloved: I have said all I could; I have made good my promise as ye required.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 2:286
verses.text: As to the rest which must be added, that your understanding may make advancement, this seek from the Lord.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:1
verses.text: Sermon III.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:2
verses.text: [LIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:4
verses.text: ]      On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:5
verses.text: Chap.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:6
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:7
verses.text: 3 and 8, "Blessed are the poor in spirit:" etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:8
verses.text: , but especially on that, "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:9
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:10
