verses.text: By the return of the commemoration of a holy virgin, who gave her testimony to Christ, and was found worthy of a testimony from Christ, who was put to death openly, and crowned invisibly, I am reminded to speak to you, beloved, on that exhortation which the Lord hath just now uttered out of the Gospel, assuring us that there are many sources of a blessed life, which there is not a man that does not wish for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:11
verses.text: There is not a man surely can be found, who does not wish to be blessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:12
verses.text: But oh! if as men desire the reward, so they would not decline the work that leads to it! Who would not run with all alacrity, were it told him, "Thou shalt be blessed"? Let him then also give a glad and ready ear when it is said, "Blessed, if thou shalt do thus".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:13
verses.text: Let not the contest be 			 declined, if the reward be loved; and let the mind be enkindled to an eager execution of the work, by the setting forth of the reward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:14
verses.text: What we desire, and wish for, and seek, will be hereafter; but what we are ordered to do for the sake of that which will be hereafter, must be now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:15
verses.text: Begin now, then, to recall to mind the divine sayings, and the precepts and rewards of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:16
verses.text: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:17
verses.text: The kingdom of heaven shall be thine hereafter; be poor in spirit now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:18
verses.text: Wouldest thou that the kingdom of heaven should be thine hereafter? Look well to thyself whose thou art now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:19
verses.text: Be poor in spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:20
verses.text: You ask me, perhaps, "What is to be poor in spirit?" No one who is puffed up is poor in spirit; therefore he that is lowly is poor in spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:21
verses.text: The kingdom of heaven is exalted; but "he who humbleth himself shall be exalted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:23
verses.text: Mark what follows: "Blessed," saith He, "are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:24
verses.text: Thou wishest to possess the earth now; take heed lest thou be possessed by it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:25
verses.text: If thou be meek, thou wilt possess it; if ungentle, thou wilt be possessed by it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:26
verses.text: And when thou hearest of the proposed reward, do not, in order that thou mayest possess the earth, unfold the lap of covetousness, whereby thou wouldest at present possess the earth, to the exclusion even of thy neighbour by whatever means; let no such imagination deceive thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:27
verses.text: Then wilt thou truly possess the earth, 			 when thou dost cleave to Him who made heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:28
verses.text: For this is to be meek, not to resist thy God, that in that thou doest well He may be well-pleasing to thee, not thou to thyself; and in that thou sufferest ill justly, He may not be unpleasing to thee, but thou to thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:29
verses.text: For no small matter is it that thou shalt be well-pleasing to Him, when thou art displeased with thyself; whereas if thou art well-pleased with thine own self, thou wilt be displeasing to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:31
verses.text: Attend to the third lesson, "Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:32
verses.text: The work consisteth in mourning, the reward in consolation; for they who mourn in a carnal sort, what consolations have they? Miserable consolations, objects rather of fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:33
verses.text: There the mourner is comforted by things which make him fear lest he have to mourn again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:34
verses.text: For instance, the death of a son causes the father sorrow, and the birth of a son joy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:35
verses.text: The one he has carried out to his burial, the other he has brought into the world; in the former is occasion of sadness, in the 			 latter of fear: and so in neither is there consolation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:36
verses.text: That therefore will be the true consolation, wherein shall be given that which may not be lost, so that they may rejoice for their after consolation, who mourn that they are in exile now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:37
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:38
verses.text: Let us come to the fourth work and its reward, "Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:39
verses.text: Dost thou desire to be filled? Whereby? If the flesh long for fulness, after digestion thou wilt suffer hunger again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:40
verses.text: So He saith, "Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:41
verses.text: If the remedy which is applied to a wound heal it, there is no more pain; but that which is applied against hunger, food that is, is so applied as to give relief only for a little while.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:42
verses.text: For when the fulness is past, hunger returns.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:43
verses.text: This remedy of fulness is applied day by day, yet the wound of weakness is not healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:44
verses.text: Let us therefore "hunger and thirst after righteousness, that we may be filled" with that righteousness after which we now hunger 			 and thirst.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:45
verses.text: For filled we shall be with that for which we hunger and thirst.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:46
verses.text: Let our inner man then hunger and thirst, for it hath its own proper meat and drink.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:47
verses.text: "I," saith He, "am the Bread which came down from heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:48
verses.text: Here is the bread of the hungry; long also for the drink of the thirsty, "For with Thee is the well of life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:49
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:50
verses.text: Mark what comes next: "Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:51
verses.text: Do this, and so shall it be done to thee; deal so with others, that God may so deal with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:52
verses.text: For thou art at once in abundance and in want—in abundance of temporal things, in want of things eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:53
verses.text: The man whom thou hearest is a beggar, and thou art thyself God's beggar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:54
verses.text: Petition is made to thee, and thou makest thy petition.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:55
verses.text: As thou hast dealt with thy petitioner, so shall God deal with His.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:56
verses.text: Thou art at once full and empty; fill the empty with thy fulness, that thy 			 emptiness may be filled with the fulness of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:57
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:58
verses.text: Mark what comes next: "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:59
verses.text: This is the end of our love; an end whereby we are perfected, and not consumed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:60
verses.text: For there is an end of food, and an end of a garment; of food when it is consumed by the eating; of a garment when it is perfected in the weaving.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:61
verses.text: Both the one and the other have an end; but the one is an end of consumption, the other of perfection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:62
verses.text: Whatsoever we now do, whatsoever we now do well, whatsoever we now strive for, or are in laudable sort eager for, or blamelessly desire, when we come 			 to the vision of God, we shall require no more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:63
verses.text: For what need he seek for, with whom God is present? or what shall suffice him, whom God sufficeth not? We wish to see God, we seek, we kindle with desire to see Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:64
verses.text: Who doth not? But mark what is said: "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:65
verses.text: Provide thyself then with that whereby thou mayest see Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:66
verses.text: For (to speak after the flesh) how with weak eyes desirest thou the rising of the sun? Let the eye be sound, and that light 			 will be a rejoicing, if it be not sound, it will be but a torment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:67
verses.text: For it is not permitted with a heart impure to see that which is seen only by the pure heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:68
verses.text: Thou wilt be repelled, driven back from it, and wilt not see it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:69
verses.text: For "blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:70
verses.text: How often already hath he enumerated the blessed, and the causes of their blessedness, and their works and recompenses, their merits and rewards! But nowhere hath it been said, "They shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:71
verses.text: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:72
verses.text: "Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:73
verses.text: "Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:74
verses.text: "Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness, they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:75
verses.text: "Blessed are the merciful, they shall obtain mercy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:76
verses.text: In none of these hath it been said, "They shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:77
verses.text: When we come to the "pure in heart," there is the vision of God promised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:78
verses.text: And not 			 without good cause; for there, in the heart, are the eyes, by which God is seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:79
verses.text: Speaking of these eyes, the Apostle Paul saith, "The eyes of your heart being enlightened".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:80
verses.text: At present then these eyes are enlightened, as is suitable to their infirmity, by faith; hereafter as shall be suited to their strength, they shall be enlightened by sight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:81
verses.text: "For as long as we are in the body we are absent from the Lord; For we walk by faith, not by sight".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:82
verses.text: Now as long as we are in this state of faith, what is said of us? "We see now through a glass darkly; but then face to face".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:84
verses.text: Let no thought be entertained here of a bodily face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:85
verses.text: For if enkindled by the desire of seeing God, thou hast made ready thy bodily face to see Him, thou wilt be looking also for such a face in God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:86
verses.text: But if now thy conceptions of God are at least so spiritual as not to imagine Him to be corporeal (of which subject I treated yesterday at considerable length, if yet it was not in vain), if I have succeeded in breaking down in your heart, as in God's temple, that image of human form; if the words in which the Apostle expresses his detestation of those, "who, professing themselves to be wise became fools, and changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like unto corruptible man," have entered deep into your minds, and taken possession of your inmost heart; if ye do now detest and abhor such impiety, if ye keep clean for the Creator His own temple, if ye would that He should come and make His abode with you, "Think of the Lord with a good heart, and in simplicity of heart seek for Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:87
verses.text: Mark well who it is to whom ye say, if so be ye do say it, and say it in sincerity, "My heart said to Thee, I will seek Thy face".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:88
verses.text: Let thine heart also say, and add, "Thy face, Lord, will I seek".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:89
verses.text: For so wilt thou seek it well, because thou seekest with thine heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:90
verses.text: Scripture speaks of the "face of God, the arm of God, the hands of God, the feet of God, the seat of God," and His footstool; but think not in all this of human members.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:91
verses.text: If thou wouldest be a temple of truth, break down the idol of falsehood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:92
verses.text: The hand of God is His power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:93
verses.text: The face of God is the knowledge of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:94
verses.text: The feet of God are His presence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:95
verses.text: The seat of God, if thou art so 			 minded, is thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:96
verses.text: But perhaps thou wilt venture to deny that Christ is God! "Not so," you say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:97
verses.text: Dost thou grant this too, that "Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God? "I grant it," you say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:98
verses.text: Hear then, "The soul of the righteous is the seat of wisdom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:99
verses.text: "Yes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:100
verses.text: For where hath God His seat, but where He dwelleth? And where doth He dwell, but in His temple? "For the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:101
verses.text: Take heed therefore how thou dost receive God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:102
verses.text: "God is a Spirit, and must be worshipped in spirit and in truth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:103
verses.text: Let the ark of testimony enter now into thy heart, if thou art so minded, and let Dagon fall.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:104
verses.text: Now therefore give ear at once, and learn to long for God; learn to make ready that whereby thou mayest see God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:105
verses.text: "Blessed," saith He, "are the pure in heart, for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:106
verses.text: Why dost thou make ready the eyes of the body? If He should be seen by them, that which should be so seen would be contained in space.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:107
verses.text: But He who is wholly everywhere is not contained in space.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:108
verses.text: Cleanse that whereby He may be seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:109
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:110
verses.text: Hear and understand, if haply through His help I shall be able to explain it; and may He help us to the understanding of all the above-named works and rewards, how suitable rewards are apportioned to their corresponding duties.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:111
verses.text: For where is there anything said of a reward which does not suit, and harmonize with its work? Because the lowly seem as it were aliens from a kingdom, He saith, "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:112
verses.text: Because meek men are easily despoiled of their land, He saith, "Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the land".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:113
verses.text: Now the rest are plain at once; they are understood of themselves, and require no one to treat of them at length; they need only one to mention them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:114
verses.text: "Blessed are they that mourn".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:115
verses.text: Now what mourner does not desire consolation? "They," saith He, "shall be comforted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:116
verses.text: "Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:117
verses.text: What hungry and thirsty man does not seek to be filled? "And they," saith He, "shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:118
verses.text: "Blessed are the 			 merciful".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:119
verses.text: What merciful man but wishes that a return should be rendered him by God of His own work, that it may be so done to him, as he doeth to the poor? "Blessed," saith He, "are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:120
verses.text: How in each case hath every duty its appropriate reward: and nothing is introduced in the reward which doth not suit the precept! For the precept is, that thou be "poor in spirit;" the reward, that thou shalt have the "kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:121
verses.text: The precept is, 			 that thou be "meek;" the reward, that thou shalt "possess the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:122
verses.text: The percept is, that thou "mourn;" the reward, that thou shalt be "comforted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:123
verses.text: The precept is, that thou "hunger and thirst after righteousness;" the reward, that thou shalt "be filled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:124
verses.text: The precept is, that thou be "merciful;" the reward, that thou shalt "obtain mercy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:125
verses.text: And so the precept is, that thou cleanse the heart; the reward, that thou shalt see God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:126
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:127
verses.text: But do not so conceive of these precepts and rewards, as to think when thou dost hear, "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God," that the poor in spirit, or the meek, or they that mourn, or they who hunger and thirst after righteousness, or the merciful, will not see Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:128
verses.text: Think not of those that are pure in heart, that they only will see Him, whilst the others will be excluded from the sight of Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:129
verses.text: For all these several characters are the 			 self-same persons.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:130
verses.text: They shall all see; but they shall not see in that they are poor in spirit, or meek, or in that they mourn, and hunger and thirst after righteousness, or are merciful, but in that they are pure in heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:131
verses.text: Just as if bodily works were duly assigned to the several members of the body, and one were to say for example, Blessed are they who have feet, for they shall walk; blessed are they that have hands, for they shall work; blessed are they that have a voice, for they shall cry 			 aloud; blessed are they who have a mouth and tongue, for they shall speak; blessed are they that have eyes, for they shall see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:132
verses.text: Even so our Lord arranging in their order the members as it were of the soul, hath taught what is proper to each.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:133
verses.text: Humility qualifies for the possession of the kingdom of heaven; meekness qualifies for possessing the earth; mourning for consolation; hunger and thirst after righteousness for being filled; mercy for the obtaining mercy; a pure heart for seeing God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:134
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:135
verses.text: If then we desire to see God, whereby shall our eye be purified? For who would not care for, and diligently seek the means of purifying that eye whereby he may see Him whom he longeth after with an entire affection? The Divine record has expressly mentioned this when it says, "purifying their hearts by faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:136
verses.text: The faith of God then purifies the heart, the pure heart sees God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:137
verses.text: But because this faith is sometimes so defined by men who deceive themselves, as though it were enough only to believe (for some promise themselves even the sight of God and the kingdom of heaven, who believe and live evilly); against these, the Apostle James, incensed and indignant as it were with a holy charity, saith in his Epistle, "Thou believest there is one God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:138
verses.text: Thou applaudest thyself for thy faith, for thou markest how that many ungodly men think there are gods many, and thou rejoicest in thyself because thou dost believe that there is but one God; "Thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:139
verses.text: Shall they also see God? They shall see Him who are pure in heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:140
verses.text: But who can say that unclean spirits are pure in heart? And yet they also "believe and tremble".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:141
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:142
verses.text: Our faith then must be different from the faith of devils.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:143
verses.text: For our faith purifies the heart; but their faith makes them guilty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:144
verses.text: For they do wickedly, and therefore say they to the Lord, "What have we to do with Thee?" When thou hearest the devils say this, thinkest thou that they do not acknowledge Him? "We know," they say, "who Thou art: Thou art the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:145
verses.text: This Peter says, and is commended; the devil says it, and is condemned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:146
verses.text: Whence cometh this, but that though the words be the same, the heart is different? Let us then make a distinction in our faith, and not be content to believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:147
verses.text: This is no such faith as purifieth the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:148
verses.text: "Purifying their hearts," it is said, "by faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:149
verses.text: But by what, and what kind of faith, save that which the Apostle Paul defines when he says, "Faith which worketh by love".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:150
verses.text: That faith distinguishes us from the faith of devils, and from the infamous and abandoned conduct of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:151
verses.text: "Faith," he says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:152
verses.text: What faith? "That which worketh by love," and which hopeth for what God doth promise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:153
verses.text: Nothing is more exact or perfect than this definition.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:154
verses.text: There are then in faith these three things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:155
verses.text: He in whom that faith is which worketh by love, must necessarily hope for that which God doth promise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:156
verses.text: Hope therefore is the associate of faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:157
verses.text: For hope is 			 necessary as long as we see not what we believe, lest perhaps through not seeing, and by despairing to see, we fail.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:158
verses.text: That we see not, doth make us sad; but that we hope we shall see, comforteth us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:159
verses.text: Hope then is here, and she is the associate of faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:160
verses.text: And then charity also, by which we long, and strive to attain, and glow with desire, and hunger and thirst.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:161
verses.text: This then is taken in also; and so there will be faith, hope, and charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:162
verses.text: For how shall there not be charity there, since charity is 			 nothing else but love? And this faith is itself defined as that "which worketh by love".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:163
verses.text: Take away faith, and all thou believest perisheth; take away charity, and all that thou dost perisheth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:164
verses.text: For it is the province of faith to believe, of charity to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:165
verses.text: For if thou believest without love, thou dost not apply thyself to good works; or if thou dost, it is as a servant, not as a son, through fear of punishment, not through love of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:166
verses.text: Therefore I say, that faith purifieth the 			 heart, which worketh by love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:167
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:168
verses.text: And what does this faith effect at present? What does it by so many testimonies of Scripture, by its manifold lessons, its various and plentiful exhortations, but make us "see now through a glass darkly, and hereafter face to face".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:169
verses.text: But return not now in thought again to this thy bodily face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:170
verses.text: Think only of the face of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:171
verses.text: Force, compel, press thine heart to think of things divine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:172
verses.text: Whatsoever occurs to thy mind that is like to a body, throw it off from 			 thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:173
verses.text: If thou canst not yet say, "It is this," yet at least say, "It is not this".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:174
verses.text: For when wilt thou be able to say, "This is God"? Not even then, when thou shall see Him; for what thou shalt then see is ineffable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:175
verses.text: Thus the Apostle says, that he "was caught up into the third heaven, and heard ineffable words".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:176
verses.text: If the words are ineffable, what is He whose words they are? Therefore as thou dost think of God, perchance there is presented to thee the idea of some human figure of marvellous and exceeding greatness, and thou hast set it before the eyesof thy mind as something very great, and grand, and of vast extension.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:177
verses.text: Still somewhere thou hast set bounds to it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:178
verses.text: If thou hast, it is not God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:179
verses.text: But if thou hast not set bounds to it, where can the face be? Thou art fancying to thyself some 			 huge body, and in order to distinguish the members in it, thou must needs set bounds to it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:180
verses.text: For in no other way but by setting bounds to this large body, canst thou distinguish the members.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:181
verses.text: But what art thou about, O foolish and carnal imagination! Thou hast made a large bulky body, and so much the larger, as thou hast thought the more to honour God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:182
verses.text: Another adds one cubit to it, and makes it greater than before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:183
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:184
verses.text: But "I have read," you will say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:185
verses.text: What hast thou read, who hast understood nothing? Yet tell me, what hast thou read? Let us not thrust back the babe in understanding with his play.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:186
verses.text: Tell me, what hast thou read? "Heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:187
verses.text: I hear thee; I have read it also: but it may be that thou thinkest thyself to have the advantage, in that thou hast both read and believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:188
verses.text: But I also believe what thou hast just said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:189
verses.text: Let us then believe it together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:190
verses.text: What do I say? Let us search it out together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:191
verses.text: Lo! hold fast what thou hast so read and believed; "Heaven is My throne (that is, "my seat," for "throne," in Greek, is "seat," in Latin), and the earth is My footstool".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:192
verses.text: But hast thou not read these words as well, "Who has meted out the heaven with the palm of His hand?" I conclude that thou hast read them; thou dost acknowledge them, and confess that thou believest them; for in that book we read both the one and the other, and believe both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:193
verses.text: But now think a while, and teach me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:194
verses.text: I make thee my teacher, and myself the little one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:195
verses.text: Teach me, I pray thee, "Who is He that sitteth on the palm of His hand?"  14.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:196
verses.text: See, thou hast drawn the figure and lineaments of the members of God from a human body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:197
verses.text: And perhaps it has occurred to thee to think, that it is according to the body that we were made after the Image of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:198
verses.text: I will admit this idea for a time to be considered, and canvassed, and examined, and by disputation to be thoroughly sifted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:199
verses.text: Now then, if it please thee, hear me; for I heard thee in what thou wast pleased to say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:200
verses.text: God sitteth in heaven, and meteth out the 			 heaven with His palm.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:201
verses.text: What! doth the same heaven become broad when it is God's seat, and narrow, when He meteth it out? Or is God when sitting, limited to the measure of His palm? If this be so, God did not make us after His likeness, for the palm of our hand is much narrower than that part of the body whereon we sit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:202
verses.text: But if He be as broad in His palm as in His sitting, He hath made our members quite unlike His.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:203
verses.text: There is no resemblance here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:204
verses.text: Let the Christian then blush to set up such an idol in his heart as this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:205
verses.text: Wherefore take heaven for all saints.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:206
verses.text: For the earth also is spoken of all who are in 			 the earth, "Let all the earth worship Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:207
verses.text: If we may properly say with regard to those who dwell on the earth, "Let all the earth worship Thee," we may with the same propriety say also as to those who dwell in heaven, "Let all the heaven bear Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:208
verses.text: For even the Saints who dwell on earth, though in their body they tread the earth, in heart dwell in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:209
verses.text: For it is not in vain that they are reminded to "lift up their hearts," and when they are so reminded, they answer, "that they lift them up:" nor in vain is it said, "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:210
verses.text: Set your affections on things above, not on things on the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:211
verses.text: In so far therefore as they have their conversation there, they do bear God, and they are heaven; because they are the seat of God; and when they declare the words of God, "The heavens declare the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:212
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:213
verses.text: Return then with me to the face of the heart, and make it ready.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:214
verses.text: That to which God speaketh is within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:215
verses.text: The ears, and eyes, and all the rest of the visible members, are either the dwelling place or the instrument of some thing within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:216
verses.text: It is the inner man where Christ doth dwell, now by faith, and hereafter He will dwell in it, by the presence of His Divinity, when we shall have known "what is the length, and breadth, and depth, and height; when we shall have known also the love of Christ that surpasseth knowledge, that we may be filled with all the fulness of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:217
verses.text: Now then if thou wouldest enter into the meaning of these words, summon all thy powers to comprehend the breadth, and length, and height, and depth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:218
verses.text: Wander not in the imagination of the thoughts through the spaces of the world, and the yet comprehensible extent of this so vast a body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:219
verses.text: Look for what I am speaking of in thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:220
verses.text: The "breadth" is in good works; the "length" is in long-suffering and perseverance in well-doing; the "height" is in the expectation of rewards above, for which height's sake thou art bidden "to lift up thy heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:221
verses.text: Do well, and persevere in well-doing, because of God's reward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:222
verses.text: Esteem earthly things as nothing, lest, when this earth shall be smitten with any scourge of that wise One, thou say that thou hast worshipped God in vain, hast done good works in vain, hast persevered in good works in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:223
verses.text: For by doing good works thou hadst as it were the "breadth," by persevering in them thou hadst as it were the "length;" but by seeking earthly things thou hast not had the "height".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:224
verses.text: Now observe the 			 "depth;" it is the grace of God in the secret dispensation of His will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:225
verses.text: "For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been His counsellor?" and, "Thy judgments are as a great depth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:226
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:227
verses.text: This conversation of well-doing, of perseverance in well-doing, of hoping for rewards above, of the secret dispensation of the grace of God, in wisdom not in foolishness, nor yet in finding fault, because one man is after this manner and another after that; for "there is no iniquity with God;" apply this, I say, if you think good, also to the Cross of thy Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:228
verses.text: For it was not without a meaning that He chose this kind of death, in whose power it was even either to die or not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:229
verses.text: Now if it was in His power to die or not, why was it not in His power also to die in this or the other manner! Not without a meaning then did He select the Cross, whereby to crucify thee to this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:230
verses.text: For the "breadth" is the transverse beam in the cross where the hands are fastened, to signify good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:231
verses.text: The "length" is in that part of the wood which reaches from this transverse beam 			 to the ground.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:232
verses.text: For there the body is crucified and in a manner stands, and this standing signifies perseverance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:233
verses.text: Now "the height" is in that part, which from the same transverse beam projects upward to the head, and hereby is signified the expectation of things above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:234
verses.text: And where is the "depth" but in that part which is fixed in the ground? For so is the dispensation of grace, hidden and in secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:235
verses.text: It is not seen itself, but from thence is projected all that is 			 seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:236
verses.text: After this, when thou shalt have comprehended all these things, not in the mere understanding but in action also ("for a good understanding have all they that do hereafter)," then if thou canst, stretch out thyself to attain to the knowledge of the "love of Christ which passeth knowledge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:237
verses.text: When thou hast attained to it, thou "wilt be filled with all the fulness of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:238
verses.text: Then will be fulfilled the "face to face".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:239
verses.text: Now thou wilt be filled with all the fulness of God, not as if God should be full of thee, but so that thou shalt be full of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:240
verses.text: Seek there, if thou canst, for any bodily face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:241
verses.text: Away with such trifles from the eye of the mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:242
verses.text: Let the child cast away his playthings, and learn to handle more serious matters.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:243
verses.text: And in many things we are but children; and when we were more so than we are, we were borne with by our betters.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:244
verses.text: "Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:245
verses.text: For by this is the heart purified; for that in it is that faith "which worketh by love".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 3:246
verses.text: Hence, "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:1
verses.text: Sermon IV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:2
verses.text: [LIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:4
verses.text: ]      On that which is written in the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:5
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:6
verses.text: 16, "Even so let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father Who is in Heaven:" and contrariwise, Chap.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:7
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:8
verses.text: , "Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men, to be seen of them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:9
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:10
verses.text: It is wont to perplex many persons, Dearly beloved, that our Lord Jesus Christ in His Evangelical Sermon, after He had first said, "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven;" said afterwards, "Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men to be seen of them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:11
verses.text: For so the mind of him who is weak in understanding is disturbed, is desirous to obey both precepts, and distracted by diverse, and contradictory commandments.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:12
verses.text: For a man can as little obey but one master, if he give contradictory orders, as he can serve two masters, which the Saviour Himself hath testified in the same Sermon to be impossible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:13
verses.text: What then must the mind that is in this hesitation do, when it thinks that it cannot, and yet is afraid not to obey? For if he set his good works in the light to be seen of men, that he may fulfil the command, "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven;" he will think himself involved in guilt because he has done contrary to 			 the other precept which says, "Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men to be seen of them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:14
verses.text: And again, if fearing and avoiding this, he conceal his good works, he will think that he is not obeying Him who commands, saying, "Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:16
verses.text: But he who is of a right understanding, fulfils both, and will obey in both the Universal Lord of all, who would not condemn the slothful servant, if he commanded those things which could by no means be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:17
verses.text: For give ear to "Paul, the servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an Apostle, separated unto the Gospel of God," both doing and teaching both duties.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:18
verses.text: See how his "light shineth before men, that they may see his good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:19
verses.text: We commend ourselves," saith he, "to every man's conscience in the sight of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:20
verses.text: And again, "For we provide things honest, not only in the sight of God, but also in the sight of men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:21
verses.text: And again, "Please all men in all things, even as I please all men in all things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:22
verses.text: See, on the other hand, how he takes heed, that he "do not his righteousness before men to be seen of them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:23
verses.text: Let every man," saith he, "prove his own work, and then shall he have glorying in himself, and not in another".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:24
verses.text: And again, "For our glorying is this, the testimony of our conscience".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:25
verses.text: And that, than which nothing is plainer, "If," saith he, "I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:26
verses.text: But lest any of those who are perplexed about the precepts of our Lord Himself as contradictory, should much more raise a question against His Apostle and say, How sayest thou, "Please all men in all things, even as I also please all men in all things:" and yet also sayest, "If I yet pleased men; I should not be the servant of Christ"? May the Lord Himself be with us, who spake also in His servant and Apostle, and open to us His will, and give us the means of obeying 			 it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:27
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:28
verses.text: The very words of the Gospel carry with them their own explanation; nor do they shut the mouths of those who hunger, seeing they feed the hearts of them that knock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:29
verses.text: The intention of a man's heart, its direction and its aim, is what is to be regarded.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:30
verses.text: For if he who wishes his good works to be seen of men, sets before men his own glory and advantage, and seeks for this in the sight of men, he does not fulfil either of those precepts which the Lord 			 has given as touching this matter; because He has at once looked to "doing his righteousness before men to be seen of them;" and his light has not so shined before men that they should see his good works, and glorify His Father which is in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:31
verses.text: It was himself he wished to be glorified, not God; he sought his own advantage, and loved not the Lord's will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:32
verses.text: Of such the Apostle says, "For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:33
verses.text: Accordingly, the sentence was not finished at the words, "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works;" but there was immediately subjoined why this was to be done; "that they may glorify your Father which is in heaven;" that when a man who does good works is seen of men, he may have only the intention of the good work in his own conscience, but may have no intention of being known, save for the praise of God, for their advantage-sake to whom 			 he is thus made known; for to them this advantage comes, that God who has given this power to man begins to be well-pleasing to them; and so they do not despair, but that the same power might be vouchsafed to themselves also if they would.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:34
verses.text: And so He did not conclude the other precept, "Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men," otherwise than in the words, "to be seen of them;" nor did He add in this case, "that they may glorify your Father which is in heaven," but 			 rather, "otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:35
verses.text: For by this He shows us, that they who are such, as He will not have His faithful ones to be, seek a reward in this very thing, that they are seen of men—that it is in this they place their good—in this that they delight the vanity of their heart—in this is their emptiness, and inflation, their swelling, and wasting away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:36
verses.text: For why was it not sufficient to say, "Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before 			 men," but that he added, "that ye may be seen of them," except because there are some who do their "righteousness before men;" not that they may be seen of them, but that the works themselves may be seen; and the Father which is in heaven, who hath vouchsafed to endow with these gifts the ungodly whom He had justified, may be glorified?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:37
verses.text: They who are such, neither do they account their righteousness as their own, but His, by the faith of whom they live (whence also the Apostle says, "That I may win Christ, and be found in Him, not having mine own righteousness which is of the law, but that which is of the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith;" and in another place, "That we may be the righteousness of God in Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:38
verses.text: Whence also he finds fault with the Jews in these words, "Being ignorant of God's righteousness, and wishing to establish their own righteousness, they have not submitted themselves to the righteousness of God").

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:39
verses.text: Whosoever then wish their good works to be so seen of men, that He may be glorified from whom they have received those things which are seen in them, and that thereby those very persons who see them, may through the dutifulness of faith be provoked to imitate the good, their light shines truly before men, because there beams forth from them the light of charity; theirs is no mere empty fume of pride; and in the very act they take precautions, that they do not their righteousness before men to be seen of them, in that they do not reckon that righteousness as their own, nor do they therefore do it that they may be seen; but that He may be made known, who is praised in them that are justified, that so 			 He may bring to pass in him that praises that which is praised in others, that is, that He may make him that praises to be himself the object of praise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:40
verses.text: Observe the Apostle too, how that when he had said, "Please all men in all things, as I also please all men in all things;" he did not stop there, as if he had placed in that, namely, the pleasing men, the end of his intention; for else he would have said falsely, "If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ;" but he subjoined immediately why it was that he pleased men; "Not seeking," saith he, "mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 4:41
verses.text: So he at once did not please men for his own profit, lest he should not be "the servant of Christ;" and he did please men for their salvation's sake, that he might be a faithful Minister of Christ; because for him his own conscience in the sight of God was enough, and from him there shined forth in the sight of men something which they might imitate.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:1
verses.text: Sermon V.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:2
verses.text: [LV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:4
verses.text: ]      On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:5
verses.text: v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:6
verses.text: 22, "Whosoever shall say to his brother, thou fool, shall be in danger of the hell of fire".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:8
verses.text: The section of the Holy Gospel which we just now heard when it was read, must have sorely alarmed us, if we have faith; but those who have not faith, it alarmed not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:9
verses.text: And because it does not alarm them, they are minded to continue in their false security, as knowing not how to divide and distinguish the proper times of security and fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:10
verses.text: Let him then who is leading now that life which has an end, fear, that in that life which is without end, he may have security.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:11
verses.text: Therefore were we alarmed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:12
verses.text: For who would not fear Him who speaketh the truth, and saith, "Whosoever shall say to his brother, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:13
verses.text: Yet "the tongue can no man tame".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:14
verses.text: Man tames the wild beast, yet he tames not his tongue; he tames the lion, yet he bridles not his own speech; he tames all else, yet he tames not himself; he tames what he was afraid of, and what he ought to be afraid of, in order that he may tame himself, that he does not fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:15
verses.text: But how is this? It is a true sentence, and came forth from an oracle of truth, "But the tongue can no man tame".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:17
verses.text: What shall we do then, my brethren? I see that I am speaking indeed to a large assembly, yet, seeing that we are one in Christ, let us take counsel as it were in secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:18
verses.text: No stranger heareth us, we are all one, because we are all united in one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:19
verses.text: What shall we do then? "Whosoever saith to his brother, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire: But the tongue can no man tame".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:20
verses.text: Shall all men go into hell fire? God forbid! "Lord, Thou art our refuge from generation to generation:" Thy wrath is just: Thou sendest no man into hell unjustly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:21
verses.text: "Whither shall I go from Thy Spirit?" and whither shall I flee from Thee, but to Thee? Let us then understand, Dearly beloved, that if no man can tame the tongue, we must have recourse to God, that He may tame it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:22
verses.text: For if thou shouldest wish to tame it, thou canst not, because thou art a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:23
verses.text: "The tongue can no man tame".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:24
verses.text: Observe a like instance to this in the case of those beasts which we do tame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:25
verses.text: The horse does not tame himself; the camel does not tame himself; the elephant does not tame himself; the viper 			 does not tame himself; the lion does not tame himself; and so also man does not tame himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:26
verses.text: But that the horse, and ox, and camel, and elephant, and lion, and viper, may be tamed, man is sought for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:27
verses.text: Therefore let God be sought to, that man may be tamed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:28
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:29
verses.text: Therefore, "O Lord, art Thou become our refuge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:30
verses.text: To Thee do we betake ourselves, and with Thy help it will be well with us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:31
verses.text: For ill is it with us by ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:32
verses.text: Because we have left Thee, Thou hast left us to ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:33
verses.text: Be we then found in Thee, for in ourselves were we lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:34
verses.text: "Lord, Thou art become our refuge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:35
verses.text: Why then, brethren, should we doubt that the Lord will make us gentle, if we give up ourselves to be tamed by him? Thou hast tamed the lion which 			 thou madest not; shall not He tame thee, who made thee? For from whence didst thou get the power to tame such savage beasts? Art thou their equal in bodily strength? By what power then hast thou been able to tame great beasts? The very beasts of burden, as they are called, are by their nature wild.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:36
verses.text: For in their untamed state they are unserviceable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:37
verses.text: But because custom has never known them except as in the hands and under the bridle and power of men, dost thou imagine that they could have been 			 born in this tame state? But now at all events mark the beasts which are unquestionably of savage kind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:38
verses.text: "The lion roareth, who doth not fear?" And yet wherein is it that thou dost find thyself to be stronger than he? Not in strength of body, but in the interior reason of the mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:39
verses.text: Thou art stronger than the lion, in that wherein thou wast made after the image of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:40
verses.text: What! Shall the image of God tame a wild beast; and shall not God tame His own image?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:41
verses.text: In Him is our hope; let us submit ourselves to Him, and entreat His mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:42
verses.text: In Him let us place our hope, and until we are tamed, and tamed thoroughly, that is, are perfected, let us bear our Tamer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:43
verses.text: For oftentimes does our Tamer bring forth His scourge too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:44
verses.text: For if thou dost bring forth the whip to tame thy beasts, shall not God do so to tame His beasts (which we are), who of His beasts will make us His sons? Thou tamest thine horse; and what wilt thou give thy 			 horse, when he shall have begun to carry thee gently, to bear thy discipline, to obey thy rule, to be thy faithful, useful beast? How dost thou repay him, who wilt not so much as bury him when he is dead, but cast him forth to be torn by the birds of prey? Whereas when thou art tamed, God reserveth for thee an inheritance, which is God Himself, and though dead for a little time, He will raise thee to life again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:45
verses.text: He will restore to thee thy body, even to the full number of thy hairs; and will set thee with the Angels for ever, where thou wilt need no more His taming hand, but only to be possessed 			 by His exceeding mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:46
verses.text: For God will then be "all in all;" neither will there be any unhappiness to exercise us, but happiness alone to feed us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:47
verses.text: Our God will be Himself our Shepherd; our God will be Himself our Cup; our God will be Himself our glory; our God will be Himself our wealth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:48
verses.text: What multiplicity of things soever thou seekest here, He alone will be Himself all these things to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:49
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:50
verses.text: Unto this hope is man tamed, and shall his Tamer then be deemed intolerable? Unto this hope is man tamed, and shall he murmur against his beneficent Tamer, if He chance to use the scourge? Ye have heard the exhortation of the Apostle, "If ye are without chastening, ye are bastards, and not sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? Furthermore," he says, "we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence; shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits, and live?" For what could thy father do for thee, that he corrected and chastised thee, brought out the scourge and beat thee? Could he make thee live for ever? What he could not do for himself, how should he do for thee? For some paltry sum of money which he had gathered together by usury and travail, did he discipline thee by the scourge, that the fruit of his labour when left to thee might not be squandered by thy evil living.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:51
verses.text: Yes, he beats his son, as fearing lest his labours should 			 be lost; forasmuch as he left to thee what he could neither retain here, nor carry away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:52
verses.text: For he did not leave thee anything here which could be his own; he went off, that so thou mightest come on.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:53
verses.text: But thy God, thy Redeemer, thy Tamer, thy Chastiser, thy Father, instructeth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:54
verses.text: To what end? That thou mayest receive an inheritance, when thou shalt not have to carry thy father to his grave, but shall have thy Father Himself for thine inheritance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:55
verses.text: Unto this hope art thou instructed, and dost thou 			 murmur? and if any sad chance befall thee, dost thou (it may be) blaspheme? Whither wilt thou go from His Spirit? But now He letteth thee alone, and doth not scourge thee; or He abandoneth thee in thy blaspheming; shalt thou not experience His judgment? Is it not better that He should scourge thee and receive thee, than that He should spare thee and abandon thee?  6.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:56
verses.text: Let us say then to the Lord our God, "Lord, Thou art become our refuge from generation to generation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:57
verses.text: In the first and second generations Thou art become our refuge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:58
verses.text: Thou wast our refuge, that we might be born, who before were not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:59
verses.text: Thou wast our refuge, that we might be born anew, who were evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:60
verses.text: Thou wast a refuge to feed those that forsake Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:61
verses.text: Thou art a refuge to raise up and direct Thy children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:62
verses.text: "Thou art become our refuge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:63
verses.text: We will not go back from 			 Thee, when Thou hast delivered us from all our evils, and filled us with Thine own good things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:64
verses.text: Thou givest good things now, Thou dealest softly with us, that we be not wearied in the way; Thou dost correct, and chastise, and smite, and direct us, that we may not wander from the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 5:65
verses.text: Whether therefore Thou dealest softly with us, that we be not wearied in the way, or chastisest us, that we wander not from the way, "Thou art become our refuge, O Lord".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:1
verses.text: Sermon VII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:2
verses.text: [LVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:4
verses.text: ]  Again, on Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:5
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:6
verses.text: on the Lord's Prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:7
verses.text: To the Competentes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:9
verses.text: The order established for your edification requires that ye learn first what to believe, and afterwards what to ask.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:10
verses.text: For so saith the Apostle, "Whosoever shall call upon the Name of the Lord, shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:11
verses.text: This testimony blessed Paul cited out of the Prophet; for by the Prophet were those times foretold, when all men should call upon God; "Whosoever shall call upon the Name of the Lord, shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:12
verses.text: And he added, "How then shall they call on Him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe in Him of whom they have not heard? Or how shall they hear without a preacher? Or how shall they preach except they be sent?" Therefore were preachers sent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:13
verses.text: They preached Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:14
verses.text: As they preached, the people heard, by hearing they believed, and by believing called upon Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:15
verses.text: Because then it was most rightly and most truly said, "How shall they call on Him in whom they have not believed?" therefore have ye first learned what to believe: and to-day have learnt to call on Him in whom ye have believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:17
verses.text: The Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, hath taught us a Prayer; and though He be the Lord Himself, as ye have heard and repeated in the Creed, the Only Son of God, yet He would not be alone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:18
verses.text: He is the Only Son, and yet would not be alone; He hath vouchsafed to have brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:19
verses.text: For to whom doth He say, "Say, Our Father, which art in heaven?" Whom did He wish us to call our Father, save His own Father? Did He grudge us this? Parents sometimes when they have gotten one, or two, or three children, fear to give birth to any more, lest they reduce the rest to beggary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:20
verses.text: But because the inheritance which He promiseth us is such as many may possess, and no one be straitened; therefore hath He called into His brotherhood the peoples of the nations; and the Only Son hath numberless brethren; who say, 			 "Our Father, which art in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:21
verses.text: So said they who have been before us; and so shall say those who will come after us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:22
verses.text: See how many brethren the Only Son hath in His grace, sharing His inheritance with those for whom He suffered death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:23
verses.text: We had a father and mother on earth, that we might be born to labours and to death: but we have found other parents, God our Father, and the Church our Mother, by whom we are born unto life eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:24
verses.text: Let us then consider, beloved, whose children we have begun 			 to be; and let us live so as becomes those who have such a Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:25
verses.text: See, how that our Creator hath condescended to be our Father!  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:26
verses.text: We have heard whom we ought to call upon, and with what hope of an eternal inheritance we have begun to have a Father in heaven; let us now hear what we must ask of Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:27
verses.text: Of such a Father what shall we ask? Do we not ask rain of Him, to-day, and yesterday, and the day before? This is no great thing to have asked of such a Father, and yet ye see with what sighings, and with what great desire we ask for rain, when death is feared, when that is feared which none can 			 escape.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:28
verses.text: For sooner or later every man must die, and we groan, and pray, and travail in pain, and cry to God, that we may die a little later.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:29
verses.text: How much more ought we to cry to Him, that we may come to that place where we shall never die!  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:30
verses.text: Therefore is it said, "Hallowed be Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:31
verses.text: This we also ask of Him that his Name may be hallowed in us; for Holy is it always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:32
verses.text: And how is His Name hallowed in us, except while it makes us holy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:33
verses.text: For once we were not holy, and we are made holy by His Name; but He is always Holy, and His Name always Holy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:34
verses.text: It is for ourselves, not for God, that we pray.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:35
verses.text: For we do not wish well to God, to whom no ill can ever happen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:36
verses.text: But we wish what is good for ourselves, that His 			 Holy Name may be hallowed, that that which is always Holy, may be hallowed in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:37
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:38
verses.text: "Thy kingdom come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:39
verses.text: Come it surely will, whether we ask or no.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:40
verses.text: Indeed, God hath an eternal kingdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:41
verses.text: For when did He not reign? When did He begin to reign? For His kingdom hath no beginning, neither shall it have any end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:42
verses.text: But that we may know that in this prayer also we pray for ourselves, and not for God (for we do not say, "Thy kingdom come," as though we were asking that God may reign); we shall be ourselves His kingdom, if believing in Him we make progress in this faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:43
verses.text: All the faithful, 			 redeemed by the Blood of His Only Son, will be His kingdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:44
verses.text: And this His kingdom will come, when the resurrection of the dead shall have taken place; for then He will come Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:45
verses.text: And when the dead are risen, He will divide them, as He Himself saith, "and He shall set some on the right hand, and some on the left".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:46
verses.text: To those who shall be on the right hand He will say, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:47
verses.text: This is what we wish and pray for when we say, "Thy kingdom come;" that it may come to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:48
verses.text: For if we shall be reprobates, that kingdom will come to others, but not to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:49
verses.text: But if we shall be of that number, who belong to the members of His Only-begotten Son, His kingdom will come to us, and will not tarry.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:50
verses.text: For are there as many ages yet remaining, as have already 			 passed away? The Apostle John hath said, "My little children, it is the last hour".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:51
verses.text: But it is a long hour proportioned to this long day; and see how many years this last hour lasteth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:52
verses.text: But nevertheless, be ye as those who watch, and so sleep, and rise again, and reign.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:53
verses.text: Let us watch now, let us sleep in death; at the end we shall rise again, and shall reign without end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:54
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:55
verses.text: "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:56
verses.text: The third thing we pray for is, that His will may be done as in heaven so in earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:57
verses.text: And in this too we wish well for ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:58
verses.text: For the will of God must necessarily be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:59
verses.text: It is the will of God that the good should reign, and the wicked be damned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:60
verses.text: Is it possible that this will should not be done? But what good do we wish for ourselves, when we say, "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth"? Give ear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:61
verses.text: For this petition may be understood in many ways, and many things 			 are to be in our thoughts in this petition, when we pray God, "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:62
verses.text: As Thy Angels offend Thee not, so may we also not offend Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:63
verses.text: Again, how is "Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth," understood? All the holy Patriarchs, all the Prophets, all the Apostles, all the spiritual are as it were God's heaven; and we in comparison of them are earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:64
verses.text: "Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth;" as in them, so in us also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:65
verses.text: Again, "Thy will 			 be done, as in heaven, so in earth;" the Church of God is heaven, His enemies are earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:66
verses.text: So we wish well for our enemies, that they too may believe and become Christians, and so the will of God be done, as in heaven, so also in earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:67
verses.text: Again, "Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:68
verses.text: Our spirit is heaven, and the flesh earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:69
verses.text: As our spirit is renewed by believing, so may our flesh be renewed by rising again; and "the will of God be done, as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:70
verses.text: Again, our mind 			 whereby we see truth, and delight in this truth, is heaven; as, "I delight in the law of God, after the inward man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:71
verses.text: What is the earth? "I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind?" When this strife shall have passed away, and a full concord brought about of the flesh and spirit, the will of God will be done as in heaven, so also in earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:72
verses.text: When we repeat this petition, let us think of all these things, and ask them all of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:73
