verses.text: Now all these things which we have mentioned, these three petitions, beloved, have respect to the life eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:74
verses.text: For if the Name of our God is sanctified in us, it will be for eternity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:75
verses.text: If His kingdom come, where we shall live 			 for ever, it will be for eternity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:76
verses.text: If His will be done as in heaven, so in earth, in all the ways which I have explained, it will be for eternity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:77
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:78
verses.text: There remain now the petitions for this life of our pilgrimage; therefore follows, "Give us this day our daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:79
verses.text: Give us eternal things, give us things temporal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:80
verses.text: Thou hast promised a kingdom, deny us not the means of subsistence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:81
verses.text: Thou wilt give everlasting glory with Thyself hereafter, give us in this earth temporal support.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:82
verses.text: Therefore is it "day by day," and "to-day," that is, in this present time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:83
verses.text: For when this life shall have passed away, shall we ask for daily bread then? For then it will not be called, "day by day," but "to-day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:84
verses.text: Now it is called, "day by day," 			 when one day passes away, and another day succeeds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:85
verses.text: Will it be called "day by day," when there will be one eternal day? This petition for daily bread is doubtless to be understood in two ways, both for the necessary supply of our bodily food, and for the necessities of our spiritual support.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:86
verses.text: There is a necessary supply of bodily food, for the preservation of our daily life, without which we cannot live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:87
verses.text: This is food and clothing, but the whole is understood in a part.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:88
verses.text: When we ask for bread, 			 we thereby understand all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:89
verses.text: There is a spiritual food also which the faithful know, which ye too will know, when ye shall receive it at the altar of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:90
verses.text: This also is "daily Bread," necessary only for this life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:91
verses.text: For shall we receive the Eucharist when we shall have come to Christ Himself, and begun to reign with Him for ever? So then the Eucharist is our daily bread; but let us in such wise receive it, that we be not refreshed in our bodies only, but in our souls.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:92
verses.text: For the virtue which is apprehended there, is unity, that 			 gathered together into His body, and made His members, we may be what we receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:93
verses.text: Then will it be indeed our daily bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:94
verses.text: Again, what I am handling before you now is "daily bread;" and the daily lessons which ye hear in church, are daily bread, and the hymns ye hear and repeat are daily bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:95
verses.text: For all these are necessary in our state of pilgrimage.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:96
verses.text: But when we shall have got to heaven, shall we hear the word, we who shall see the Word Himself, and hear the Word Himself, and eat and drink Him as the angels do now? Do the angels need books, and interpreters, and readers? Surely not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:97
verses.text: They read in seeing, for the Truth Itself they see, and are abundantly satisfied from that fountain, from which we obtain some few drops.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:98
verses.text: Therefore has it been said touching our daily bread, that this petition is necessary for us in this life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:99
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:100
verses.text: "Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:101
verses.text: Is this necessary except in this life? For in the other we shall have no debts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:102
verses.text: For what are debts, but sins? See, ye are on the point of being baptized, then all your sins will be blotted out, none whatever will remain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:103
verses.text: Whatever evil ye have ever done, in deed, or word, or desire, or thought, all will be blotted out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:104
verses.text: And yet if in the life which is after Baptism there were security from sin, we should not learn such a prayer as this, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:105
verses.text: Only let us by 			 all means do what comes next, "As we forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:106
verses.text: Do ye then who are about to enter in to receive a plenary and entire remission of your debts, do ye above all things see that ye have nothing in your hearts against any other, so as to come forth from Baptism secure, as it were free and discharged of all debts, and then begin to purpose to avenge yourselves on your enemies, who in time past have done you wrong.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:107
verses.text: Forgive, as ye are forgiven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:108
verses.text: God can do no one wrong, and yet He 			 forgiveth who oweth nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:109
verses.text: How then ought he to forgive, who is himself forgiven, when He forgiveth all, who oweth nothing that can be forgiven Him?  9.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:110
verses.text: "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:111
verses.text: Will this again be necessary in the life to come? "Lead us not into temptation," will not be said, except where there can be temptation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:112
verses.text: We read in the book of holy Job, "Is not the life of man upon earth a temptation?" What then do we pray for? Hear what.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:113
verses.text: The Apostle James saith, "Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:114
verses.text: He spoke of those evil temptations, whereby men are deceived, and brought under the yoke of the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:115
verses.text: This is the kind of temptation he spoke of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:116
verses.text: For there is another sort of temptation which is called a proving; of this kind of temptation it is written, "The Lord your God tempteth (proveth) you to know whether ye love Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:117
verses.text: What means "to know"? "To make you know," for He knoweth already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:118
verses.text: With that kind of temptation, whereby we are deceived and seduced, God tempteth no man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:119
verses.text: But undoubtedly in His deep and hidden judgment He abandons some.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:120
verses.text: And when He hath abandoned them, the tempter finds his opportunity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:121
verses.text: For he finds in him no resistance against his power, but forthwith presents himself to him as his possessor, if God abandon him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:122
verses.text: Therefore that He may not 			 abandon us, do we say, "Lead us not into temptation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:123
verses.text: "For every one is tempted," says the same Apostle James, "when he is drawn away of his own lust and enticed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:124
verses.text: Then lust, when it hath conceived, bringeth forth sin; and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:125
verses.text: What then has he hereby taught us? To fight against our lusts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:126
verses.text: For ye are about to put away your sins in Holy Baptism; but lusts will still remain, wherewith ye must fight after that ye are regenerate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:127
verses.text: For a conflict with your own selves still remains.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:128
verses.text: Let no enemy from without be feared: conquer thine own self, and the whole world is conquered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:129
verses.text: What can any tempter from without, whether the devil or the devil's minister, do against thee? Whosoever sets the hope of gain 			 before thee to seduce thee, let him only find no covetousness in thee; and what can he who would tempt thee by gain effect? Whereas if covetousness be found in thee, thou takest fire at the sight of gain, and art taken by the bait of this corrupt food.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:130
verses.text: But if he find no covetousness in thee, the trap remains spread in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:131
verses.text: Or should the tempter set before thee some woman of surpassing beauty; if chastity be within, iniquity from without is overcome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:132
verses.text: Therefore that he may not take thee with the bait of a strange woman's beauty, fight with thine own lust within; thou hast no sensible perception of thine enemy, but of thine own concupiscence thou hast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:133
verses.text: Thou dost not see the devil, but the object that engageth thee thou dost 			 see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:134
verses.text: Get the mastery then over that of which thou art sensible within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:135
verses.text: Fight valiantly, for He who hath regenerated thee is thy Judge; He hath arranged the lists, He is making ready the crown.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:136
verses.text: But because thou wilt without doubt be conquered, if thou have not Him to aid thee, if He abandon thee: therefore dost thou say in the prayer, "Lead us not into temptation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:137
verses.text: The Judge's wrath hath given over some to their own lusts; and the Apostle says, "God gave them over to the lusts of their 			 hearts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:138
verses.text: How did He give them up? Not by forcing, but by forsaking them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:139
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:140
verses.text: "Deliver us from evil," may belong to the same sentence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:141
verses.text: Therefore, that thou mayest understand it to be all one sentence, it runs thus, "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:142
verses.text: Therefore he added "but," to show that all this belongs to one sentence, "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:143
verses.text: How is this? I will propose them singly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:144
verses.text: "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:145
verses.text: By delivering us from evil, He 			 leadeth us not into temptation; by not leading us into temptation, He delivereth us from evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:146
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:147
verses.text: And truly it is a great temptation, dearly beloved, it is a great temptation in this life, when that in us is the subject of temptation, whereby we attain pardon, if in any of our temptations we have fallen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:148
verses.text: It is a frightful temptation, when that is taken from us, whereby we may be healed from the wounds of other temptations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:149
verses.text: I know that ye have not yet understood me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:150
verses.text: Give me your attention, that ye may understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:151
verses.text: Suppose avarice tempts a man, and he is conquered in any single temptation (for sometimes even a good wrestler and fighter may get roughly handled): avarice then has got the better of a man, good wrestler though he be, and he has done some avaricious act.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:152
verses.text: Or there has been a passing lust; it has not brought the man to fornication, nor reached unto adultery, for when this does take place, the man must at all events be kept back from the criminal act.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:153
verses.text: But he "hath seen a woman to lust after her;" he has let his thoughts dwell on her with more pleasure than was right; he has admitted the attack; excellent combatant though he be, he has been wounded, but he has not consented to it; he has beaten back the motion of his lust, has chastised it with the bitterness of grief, he has beaten it back; and has prevailed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:154
verses.text: Still in the very fact that he had slipped, has he ground for saying, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:155
verses.text: And so of all other temptations, it is a hard matter that in 			 them all there should not be occasion for saying, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:156
verses.text: What then is that frightful temptation which I have mentioned, that grievous, that tremendous temptation, which must be avoided with all our strength, with all our resolution; what is it? When we go about to avenge ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:157
verses.text: Anger is kindled, and the man burns to be avenged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:158
verses.text: O frightful temptation! Thou art losing that, whereby thou hadst to attain pardon for other faults.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:159
verses.text: If thou hadst committed any sin as to other 			 senses, and other lusts, hence mightest thou have had thy cure, in that thou mightest say, "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:160
verses.text: But whoso instigateth thee to take vengeance, will lose for thee the power thou hadst to say, "As we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:161
verses.text: When that power is lost, all sins will be retained; nothing at all is remitted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:162
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:163
verses.text: Our Lord and Master, and Saviour, knowing this dangerous temptation in this life, when He taught us six or seven petitions in this Prayer, took none of them for Himself to treat of, and to commend to us with greater earnestness, than this one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:164
verses.text: Have we not said, "Our Father, which art in heaven;" and the rest which follows? Why after the conclusion of the Prayer, did He not enlarge upon it to us, either as to what He had laid down in the 			 beginning, or concluded with at the end, or placed in the middle? For why said He not, if the Name of God be not hallowed in you, or if ye have no part in the kingdom of God, or if the will of God be not done in you, as in heaven, or if God guard you not, that ye enter not into temptation; why none of all these? but what saith He? "Verily I say unto you, that if ye forgive men their trespasses;" in reference to that petition, "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:165
verses.text: Having passed over all the other petitions which He taught us, this He taught us with an especial force.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:166
verses.text: There was no need of insisting so much upon those sins in which if a man offend, he may know the means whereby he may be cured: need of it there was, with regard to that sin in which if thou sin, there is no means whereby the rest can be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:167
verses.text: For this thou oughtest to be ever saying, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:168
verses.text: What debts? There is no lack of them; for we are but men; I have talked somewhat more than I ought, have said something I ought not, have laughed more than I ought, have eaten more than I ought, 			 have listened with pleasure to what I ought not, have drunk more than I ought, have seen with pleasure what I ought not, have thought with pleasure on what I ought not; "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:169
verses.text: This if thou hast lost, thou art lost thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:170
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:171
verses.text: Take heed, my brethren, my sons, sons of God, take heed, I beseech you, in that I am saying to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:172
verses.text: Fight to the uttermost of your powers with your own hearts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:173
verses.text: And if ye shall see your anger making a stand against you, pray to God against it, that God may make thee conqueror of thyself, that God may make thee conqueror, I say, not of thine enemy without, but of thine own soul within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:174
verses.text: For He will give thee His present help, and will do it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:175
verses.text: He would rather that we 			 ask this of Him, than rain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:176
verses.text: For ye see, beloved, how many petitions the Lord Christ hath taught us; and there is scarce found among them one which speaks of daily bread, that all our thoughts may be moulded after the life to come? For what can we fear that He will not give us, who hath promised and said, "Seek ye first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you; for your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things before ye ask Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:177
verses.text: Seek ye 			 first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:178
verses.text: For many have been tried even with hunger, and have been found gold, and have not been forsaken by God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:179
verses.text: They would have perished with hunger, if the daily inward bread were to leave their heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:180
verses.text: After this let us chiefly hunger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:181
verses.text: For, "Blessed are they who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:182
verses.text: But He can in mercy look upon our infirmity, and see us, as it is said, "Remember that we are dust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:183
verses.text: He who from the dust made and quickened man, for that His work of clay's sake, gave His Only Son to death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 6:184
verses.text: Who can explain, who can worthily so much as conceive, how much He loveth us?.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:1
verses.text: Sermon VIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:2
verses.text: [LVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:4
verses.text: ]  Again on the Lord's Prayer, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:5
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:6
verses.text: To the Competentes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:8
verses.text: You have just repeated the Creed, where in brief summary is contained the Faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:9
verses.text: I have already before now told you what the Apostle Paul says, "How shall they call on Him in whom they have not believed?" Because then you have both heard, and learnt, and repeated how you must believe in God; hear to-day how He must be called upon.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:10
verses.text: The Son Himself, as you heard when the Gospel was read, taught His disciples and His faithful ones this Prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:11
verses.text: Good hope have we of obtaining our cause, when such an Advocate hath dictated our suit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:12
verses.text: The Assessor of the Father, as you have confessed, who sitteth on the right hand of the Father; He is our Advocate who is to be our Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:13
verses.text: For from thence will He come to judge the quick and dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:14
verses.text: Learn then, this Prayer also which you will have to repeat in eight days time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:15
verses.text: But whosoever of you have not repeated the Creed well, have yet time enough, let them learn it; because on the Sabbath day in the hearing of all who shall be present, you will have to repeat it: on the last Sabbath day, when you will be here to be baptized.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:16
verses.text: But in eight days from to-day will you have to repeat this Prayer, which you have heard to-day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:17
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:18
verses.text: Of which the first clause is, "Our Father, which art in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:19
verses.text: We have found then a Father in heaven; let us take good heed how we live on earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:20
verses.text: For he who hath found such a Father, ought so to live that he may be worthy to come to his inheritance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:21
verses.text: But we say all in common, "Our Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:22
verses.text: How great a condescension! This the emperor says, and this says the beggar: this says the slave, and this his lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:23
verses.text: They say all together, "Our Father, which art in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:24
verses.text: Therefore do they understand that they are brethren, 			 seeing they have one Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:25
verses.text: Now let not the lord disdain to have his slave for a brother, seeing the Lord Christ has vouch-safed to have him for a brother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:26
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:27
verses.text: "Hallowed be Thy Name, Thy kingdom come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:28
verses.text: This hallowing of God's Name is that whereby we are made holy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:29
verses.text: For His Name is always Holy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:30
verses.text: We wish also for His kingdom to come; come it will, though we wish it not; but to wish and pray that His kingdom may come, is nothing else than to wish of Him, that He would make us worthy of His kingdom, lest haply, which God forbid, it should come, and not come to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:31
verses.text: For to many that will never come, which nevertheless must come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:32
verses.text: For to them will it come, to whom it shall be said, 			 "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:33
verses.text: But it will not come to them to whom it shall be said, "Depart from Me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:34
verses.text: Therefore when we say, "Thy kingdom come," we pray that it may come to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:35
verses.text: What is, "may come to us"? May find us good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:36
verses.text: This we pray for then, that He would make us good; for then to us will His kingdom come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:37
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:38
verses.text: We go on, "Thy will be done as in heaven so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:39
verses.text: The Angels serve Thee in heaven, may we serve Thee in earth! The Angels do not offend Thee in heaven, may we not offend Thee in earth! As they do Thy will, so may we do it also! And here what do we pray for, but that we may be good? For when we do God's will (for He without doubt doeth His own will), then is His will done in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:40
verses.text: And we may understand in another and a right sense these words, "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:41
verses.text: We receive the commandment of God, 			 and it is well-pleasing to us, well-pleasing to our mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:42
verses.text: "For we delight in the law of God after the inward man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:43
verses.text: Then is His will done in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:44
verses.text: For our spirit is compared to heaven, but to the earth our flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:45
verses.text: What then is "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth"? That as Thy command is well-pleasing to our mind, so may our flesh consent thereto; and so that strife be ended which is described by the Apostle, "for the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:46
verses.text: When the Spirit lusteth against the flesh, His will is even now done in heaven; when the flesh lusteth not against the Spirit, His will is now done in earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:47
verses.text: There will be harmony complete when He will; be then the contest now, that there may be victory hereafter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:48
verses.text: Thus again, "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth," may be well understood, by making "heaven" to be the Church, because it is the throne of God; and "earth" the unbelievers, to whom it is said, "Earth thou art, and unto earth shalt thou go".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:49
verses.text: When therefore we pray for our enemies, for the enemies of the Church, the enemies of the Christian name, we pray that His will may be done "as in heaven, so in earth," that is, as in Thy faithful ones, so in Thy blasphemers also, that they all may become "heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:50
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:51
verses.text: There follows next, "Give us this day our daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:52
verses.text: It may be understood simply that we pour forth this prayer for daily sustenance, that we may have abundance: or if not that, that we may have no want.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:53
verses.text: Now he said "daily," for as long as it is called "to-day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:54
verses.text: Daily we live, and daily rise, and are daily fed, and daily hunger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:55
verses.text: May He then give us daily bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:56
verses.text: Why did He not say "covering" too, for the support of our life is in meat and drink, our covering in raiment and lodging.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:57
verses.text: Man should desire nothing more than these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:58
verses.text: Forasmuch as the Apostle saith, "We brought nothing into this world, neither can we carry anything out: having food and covering, let us be therewith content".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:59
verses.text: Perish covetousness, and nature is rich.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:60
verses.text: Therefore if this prayer have reference to our daily sustenance, since this is a good understanding of the words, "Give us this day our daily bread;" let us not marvel, if under the name of bread other necessary things are also understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:61
verses.text: As when Joseph invited his brethren, "These men," saith he, "will eat bread with me to-day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:62
verses.text: Why, were they to eat bread only? No, but in the mention of bread only, all the rest was understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:63
verses.text: So when we pray for daily bread, we ask for whatever is necessary for us in earth for our bodies' sake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:64
verses.text: But what saith the Lord Jesus? "Seek ye first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:65
verses.text: Again, this is a very good sense of, "Give us this day our daily bread," thy Eucharist, our daily food.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:66
verses.text: For the faithful know what they receive, and good for them it is to receive that daily bread which is necessary for this time present.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:67
verses.text: They pray then for themselves, that they may become good, that they may persevere in goodness, and faith, and a holy life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:68
verses.text: This do they wish, this they pray for; for if they persevere not in this good life, they will be separated from 			 that Bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:69
verses.text: Therefore, "Give us this day our daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:70
verses.text: What is this? Let us live so,that we be not separated from Thy altar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:71
verses.text: Again, the Word of God which is laid open to us, and in a manner broken day by day, is "daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:72
verses.text: And as our bodies hunger after that other, so do our souls after this bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:73
verses.text: And so we both ask for this bread simply, and whatsoever is in this life needful both for our souls and bodies, is included in "daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:74
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:75
verses.text: "Forgive us our debts," we say, and we may well say so; for we say the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:76
verses.text: For who is he that lives here in the flesh, and hath no debts? What man is there that lives so, that this prayer is not necessary for him? He may puff himself up, justify himself he cannot.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:77
verses.text: It were well for him to imitate the Publican, and not swell as the Pharisee, "who went up into the temple," and boasted of his deserts, and covered up his wounds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:78
verses.text: Whereas he who said, "Lord, be merciful to me a sinner," knew wherefore he went up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:79
verses.text: This prayer the Lord Jesus, consider, my brethren, this prayer the Lord Jesus taught His disciples to offer, those great first Apostles of His, the leaders of our flock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:80
verses.text: If the leaders of the flock then pray for the remission of their sins, what ought the lambs to do, of whom it is said, "Bring young rams unto the Lord"? You knew then that you have repeated this in the Creed, because amongst the rest you have mentioned there "the remission of sins".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:81
verses.text: There is one remission of sins which is given once for all; another which is given day by day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:82
verses.text: There is one remission of sins which is given once for all in Holy Baptism; another which is given as long as we live here in the Lord's Prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:83
verses.text: Wherefore we say, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:84
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:85
verses.text: And God has brought us into a covenant, and agreement, and a firm bond with Him, in that we say, "as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:86
verses.text: He who would say it effectually, "Forgive us our debts," must say truly, "as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:87
verses.text: If this which is last he either say not, or say deceitfully, the other which is first he says in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:88
verses.text: We say to you then especially who are approaching to Holy Baptism, from your hearts forgive everything.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:89
verses.text: And ye faithful, who taking advantage of this occasion are listening to this prayer, and our exposition of it, do ye wholly and from your hearts forgive whatsoever ye have against any.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:90
verses.text: Forgive it there where God seeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:91
verses.text: For sometimes a man remitteth with the mouth, and in 			 the heart retaineth; he remitteth with the mouth for men's sake, and retaineth in the heart, as not fearing the eyes of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:92
verses.text: But do ye remit entirely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:93
verses.text: Whatever ye have retained up to these holy days, in these holy days at least remit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:94
verses.text: "The sun ought not to go down upon your wrath," yet many suns have passed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:95
verses.text: Let then your wrath at length pass away also, now that we are celebrating the days of the great Sun, of that Sun of which Scripture saith, "Unto you shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in His wings".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:96
verses.text: What is, "in His wings"? In His protection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:97
verses.text: Whence it is said in the Psalms, "Keep me under the shadow of Thy wings".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:98
verses.text: But as to others who in the day of judgment shall repent, but all too late, and who shall mourn, yet unavailingly, it hath been foretold by Wisdom what they shall then say as they repent and groan for anguish of spirit, "What hath pride profited us, or what good hath riches with our vaunting brought us? All these things are passed away like a shadow".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:99
verses.text: And, "Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness hath not shined unto us, and the Sun 			 of righteousness rose not upon us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:100
verses.text: That Sun riseth upon the righteous only; but this sun which we see, God "maketh," daily "to rise upon the good and evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:101
verses.text: The righteous attain to the seeing of that Sun; and that Sun dwelleth now in our hearts by faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:102
verses.text: If then thou art angry, let not this sun go down in thine heart upon thy wrath; "Let not the sun go down upon thy wrath;" lest haply thou be angry, and so the Sun of righteousness go down upon thee, and thou abide in darkness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:103
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:104
verses.text: Now do not think that anger is nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:105
verses.text: "Mine eye was disordered because of anger," saith the Prophet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:106
verses.text: Surely he whose eye is disordered cannot see the sun; and if he should try to see it, it were pain, and no pleasure to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:107
verses.text: And what is anger? The lust of vengeance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:108
verses.text: A man lusteth to be avenged, and Christ is not yet avenged, the holy martyrs are not yet avenged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:109
verses.text: Still doth the patience of God wait, that the enemies of Christ, the enemies of the martyrs, may be converted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:110
verses.text: And who are we, that we should seek for vengeance? If God should seek it at our hands, 			 where should we abide? He who hath never in any matter done us harm, doth not wish to avenge Himself of us; and do we seek to be avenged, who are almost daily offending God? Forgive therefore; from the heart forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:111
verses.text: If thou art angry, yet sin not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:112
verses.text: "Be ye angry, and sin not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:113
verses.text: Be ye angry as being but men, if so be ye are overcome by it; yet sin not, so as to retain anger in your heart (for if ye do retain it, ye retain it against yourselves), lest ye enter not into that Light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:114
verses.text: Therefore forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:115
verses.text: What then is anger? The lust of vengeance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:116
verses.text: And what is hatred? Inveterate anger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:117
verses.text: If anger become inveterate, it is then called hatred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:118
verses.text: And this he seems to acknowledge, who when he had said, "Mine eye is disordered because of anger;" added, "I have 			 become inveterate among all mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:119
verses.text: What was anger when it was new, became hatred when it was turned into long continuance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:120
verses.text: Anger is a "mote," hatred, a "beam".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:121
verses.text: We sometimes find fault with one who is angry, yet we retain hatred in our own hearts; and so Christ saith to us, "Thou seest the mote in thy brother's eye, and seest not the beam in thine own eye".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:122
verses.text: How grew the mote into a beam? Because it was not at once plucked out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:123
verses.text: Because thou didst suffer the sun to rise and go down so often upon thy wrath, and madest it inveterate, because thou contractedst evil suspicions, and wateredst the mote, and by watering hast nourished it, and by nourishing it, hast made it a beam.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:124
verses.text: Tremble then at least when it is said, "Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:125
verses.text: Thou hast not drawn the sword, nor inflicted any bodily wound, nor by any blow killed another; the thought only of hatred is in thy heart, and hereby art thou held to be a murderer, guilty art thou before the eyes of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:126
verses.text: The other man is alive, and yet thou hast killed him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:127
verses.text: As far as thou art concerned, thou hast killed the man whom thou hatest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:128
verses.text: Reform then, and amend thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:129
verses.text: If scorpions or adders were in your houses, how would ye toil to purify them, that ye might be able 			 to dwell in safety? Yet are ye angry, yea inveterate anger is in your hearts, and there grow so many hatreds, so many beams, so many scorpions, so many vipers, and will ye not then purify the house of God, your heart? Do then what is said, "As we also forgive our debtors;" and so say securely, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:130
verses.text: For without debts in this earth ye cannot live; but those great crimes which it is your blessing to have been forgiven in Baptism, and from which we ought to be ever free, 			 are of one sort, and of another are those daily sins, without which a man cannot live in this world, by reason of which this daily prayer with its covenant and agreement is necessary; that as we say with all cheerfulness, "Forgive us our debts;" so we may say with all truth, "As we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:131
verses.text: So much then have we said as touching past sins; what now for the future?  9.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:132
verses.text: "Lead us not into temptation:" forgive what we have done already, and grant that we may not commit any more sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:133
verses.text: For whosoever is overcome by temptation, committeth sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:134
verses.text: Thus the Apostle James saith, "Let no man say when he is tempted, he is tempted of God, for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth He any man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:135
verses.text: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:136
verses.text: Then lust, when it hath conceived, bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth 			 death".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:137
verses.text: Therefore that thou be not drawn away by thy lust; consent not to it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:138
verses.text: It hath no means of conceiving, but by thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:139
verses.text: Thou hast consented, hast as it were in thine heart admitted her embrace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:140
verses.text: Lust has risen up, deny thyself to her, follow her not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:141
verses.text: It is a lust unlawful, impure, and shameful, it will alienate thee from God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:142
verses.text: Give it not then the embrace of thy consent, lest thou have to bewail the birth; for if thou consent, that is, when thou hast embraced her, she conceives, "and when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:143
verses.text: Dost thou not yet fear? "Sin bringeth forth death;" at least, fear death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:144
verses.text: If thou fear not sin, yet fear that 			 whereunto it leads.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:145
verses.text: Sin is sweet; but death is bitter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:146
verses.text: This is the infelicity of men; that for which they sin, they leave here when they die, and the sin themselves they carry with them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:147
verses.text: Thou dost sin for money, it must be left here: or for a country seat; it must be left here: or for some woman's sake; she must be left here; and whatsoever it be for which thou dost sin, when thou shalt have closed thine eyes in death, thou must leave it here; yet the sin itself which thou committest, thou 			 carriest with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:148
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:149
verses.text: May sins then be forgiven; the past forgiven, and the future cease.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:150
verses.text: But without them here below thou canst not live; be they either lesser sins, or small, or trivial.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:151
verses.text: Yet let not even these small and trivial sins be despised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:152
verses.text: With little drops is the river filled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:153
verses.text: Let not even the lesser sins be despised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:154
verses.text: Through narrow chinks in the ship the water oozes in, the hold keeps filling, and if it be disregarded the ship is sunk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:155
verses.text: But the sailors are not idle; their hands are active,—active that the water may be drained off from day to day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:156
verses.text: So be thy hands active, that thou mayest pump from day to day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:157
verses.text: What is the meaning of "be thy hands active"? Let them give, do good works, so be thy hands engaged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:158
verses.text: "Break thy bread to the hungry, and bring the poor and houseless into thine house; if thou seest the naked, clothe him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:159
verses.text: Do all thou canst, do it with the means thou canst command, do it cheerfully, and so put up thy prayer with confidence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:160
verses.text: It will have two wings, a double alms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:161
verses.text: What is "a double alms"? "Forgive, and ye shall be forgiven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:162
verses.text: Give, and it shall be given unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:163
verses.text: The one alms is that which is done from the heart, when thou forgivest thy brother his sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:164
verses.text: The other alms is that which is done out of thy substance, when thou dealest bread to the poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:165
verses.text: Offer both, lest without either wing thy prayer remain motionless.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:166
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:167
verses.text: Therefore when we have said, "Lead us not into temptation," there follows, "But deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:168
verses.text: Now whoso wishes to be delivered from evil, bears witness that he is in evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:169
verses.text: And thus saith the Apostle, "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:170
verses.text: But who is there "that wisheth for life, and loveth to see good days"? Seeing that all men in this flesh have only evil days; who doth not wish it? Do thou what follows, "Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips that they speak no guile: depart from evil, and do good, seek peace, and ensue it;" and then thou hast got rid of evil days, and thy prayer, "deliver us from evil," is fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:171
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:172
verses.text: Therefore the three first petitions, "Hallowed be Thy Name, Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth," are for eternity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:173
verses.text: But the four following relate to this life, "Give us this day our daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:174
verses.text: Shall we ask day by day for daily bread, when we shall have come to that fulness of blessing? "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:175
verses.text: Shall we say this in that kingdom, when we shall have no debts? "Lead us not into temptation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:176
verses.text: Shall we be able to 			 say this then, when there will be no temptation? "Deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:177
verses.text: Shall we say this, when there shall be nothing from which to be delivered? Therefore these four are necessary, because of our daily life, but the three first in reference to the life eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:178
verses.text: But all things let us ask, with a view of attaining to that life, and let us pray here, that we be not separated from it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:179
verses.text: Every day must this prayer be said by you, when you are baptized.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:180
verses.text: For the Lord's Prayer is said daily in 			 the Church before the Altar of God, and the faithful hear it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:181
verses.text: We have no fear therefore as to your not learning it carefully, because even if any of you should be unable to get it perfectly, he will learn it by hearing it day by day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:182
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:183
verses.text: Therefore on the Saturday when by the grace of God you will keep the Vigil, you will have to repeat not the Prayer, but the Creed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:184
verses.text: For if you do not know the Creed now, you will not hear that every day in the Church, and among the people.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:185
verses.text: But when you have learnt it, that you may not forget it, say it every day when you rise; when you are preparing for sleep, rehearse your Creed, to the Lord rehearse it, remind yourselves of it, and be not weary of repeating it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:186
verses.text: For repetition is useful, lest 			 forgetfulness steal over you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:187
verses.text: Do not say, "I said it yesterday, I have said it today, I say it every day, I know it perfectly well".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:188
verses.text: Call thy faith to mind, look into thyself, let thy Creed be as it were a mirror to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:189
verses.text: Therein see thyself, whether thou dost believe all which thou professest to believe, and so rejoice day by day in thy faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:190
verses.text: Let it be thy wealth, let it be in a sort the daily clothing of thy soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:191
verses.text: Dost thou not always dress thyself when thou risest? So by the daily 			 repetition of thy Creed dress thy soul, lest haply forgetfulness make it bare, and thou remain naked, and that take place which the Apostle saith, (may it be far from thee!) "If so be that being unclothed, we shall not be found naked".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:192
verses.text: For we shall be clothed by our faith: and this faith is at once a garment and a breastplate; a garment against shame, a breastplate against adversity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:193
verses.text: But when we shall have arrived at that place where we shall reign, no need will there be to say the Creed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 7:194
verses.text: We shall see God; God Himself will be our vision; the vision of God will be the reward of our present faith.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:1
verses.text: Sermon IX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:2
verses.text: [LIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:4
verses.text: ]  Again, on the Lord's Prayer, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:5
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:6
verses.text: To the Competentes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:8
verses.text: You have rehearsed what you believe, hear now what you are to pray for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:9
verses.text: Forasmuch as you would not be able to call on Him, in whom you should not first have believed; as saith the Apostle, "How shall they call on Him, in whom they have not believed?" Therefore have you first learned the Creed, where is a brief and sublime rule of your faith; brief in the number of its words, sublime in the weight of its contents.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:10
verses.text: But the prayer which you receive to-day to be learned by heart, and to be repeated eight days hence, was dictated (as you heard when the Gospel was being read) by the Lord Himself to His disciples, and came from them unto us, since "their sound went into all the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:11
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:12
verses.text: Ye then who have found a Father in heaven, be loth to cleave to the things of earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:13
verses.text: For ye are about to say, "Our Father, which art in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:14
verses.text: You have begun to belong to a great family.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:15
verses.text: Under this Father the lord and the slave are brethren; under this Father the general and the common soldier are brethren; under this Father the rich man and the poor are brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:16
verses.text: All Christian believers have divers fathers in earth, some noble, some obscure; but they all call upon one Father which is in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:17
verses.text: If our Father be there, there is the inheritance prepared for us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:18
verses.text: But He is such a Father, that we can possess with Him 			 what He giveth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:19
verses.text: For He giveth an inheritance; but He doth not leave it to us by dying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:20
verses.text: For He doth not depart Himself, but He abideth ever, that we may come to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:21
verses.text: Seeing then we have heard of Whom we are to ask, let us know also what to ask for, lest haply we offend such a Father by asking amiss.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:23
verses.text: What then hath the Lord Jesus Christ taught us to ask of the Father which is in heaven? "Hallowed be Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:24
verses.text: What kind of blessing is this that we ask of God, that His Name may be hallowed? The Name of God is always Holy; why then do we pray that it may be hallowed, except that we may be hallowed by it? We pray then that that which is Holy always, may be hallowed in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:25
verses.text: The Name of God is hallowed in you when ye are baptized.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:26
verses.text: Why will ye offer this prayer after ye have been baptized, but that that which ye shall then receive may abide ever in you?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:27
verses.text: Another petition follows, "Thy kingdom come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:28
verses.text: God's kingdom will come, whether we ask it or not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:29
verses.text: Why then do we ask it, but that that which will come to all saints may also come to us; that God may count us also in the number of His saints, to whom His kingdom is to come?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:30
verses.text: We say in the third petition, "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:31
verses.text: What is this? That as the Angels serve Thee in heaven, so we may serve Thee in earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:32
verses.text: For His holy Angels obey Him; they do not offend Him; they do His commands through the love of Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:33
verses.text: This we pray for then, that we too may do the commands of God in love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:34
verses.text: Again, these words are understood in another way, "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:35
verses.text: Heaven in us is the soul, earth in us is the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:36
verses.text: What then is, "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth"? As we 			 hear Thy precepts, so may our flesh consent unto us; lest, whilst flesh and spirit strive together, we be not able to fulfil the commands of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:37
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:38
verses.text: "Give us this day our daily bread," comes next in the Prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:39
verses.text: Whether we ask here of the Father support necessary for the body, by "bread" signifying whatever is needful for us; or whether we understand that daily Bread, which ye are soon to receive from the Altar; well it is that we pray that He would give it us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:40
verses.text: For what is it we pray for, but that we may commit no evil, for which we should be separated from that holy Bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:41
verses.text: And the word of God which is preached daily is daily bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:42
verses.text: For because it is not bread for the body, it is not on that account not bread for the 			 soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:43
verses.text: But when this life shall have passed away, we shall neither seek that bread which hunger seeks; nor shall we have to receive the Sacrament of the Altar, because we shall be there with Christ, whose Body we do now receive; nor will those words which we are now speaking, need to be said to you, nor the sacred volume to be read, when we shall see Him who is Himself the Word of God, by whom all things were made, by whom the Angels are fed, by whom the Angels are enlightened, by whom the 			 Angels become wise; not requiring words of circuitous discourse; but drinking in the Only Word, filled with whom they burst forth and never fail in praise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:44
verses.text: For, "Blessed," saith the Psalm, "are they who dwell in Thy house; they will be always praising Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:45
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:46
verses.text: Therefore in this present life, do we ask what comes next, "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:47
verses.text: In Baptism, all debts, that is, all sins, are entirely forgiven us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:48
verses.text: But because no one can live without sin here below, and if without any great crime which entails separation from the Altar, yet altogether without sins can no one live on this earth, and we can only receive the one Baptism once for all; in this Prayer we hear how we may day by day be washed, that our sins may day by day be forgiven us; but only if we do what follows, "As we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:49
verses.text: Accordingly, my Brethren, I advise you, who are in the grace of God my sons, yet my Brethren under that heavenly Father; I advise you, whenever any one offends and sins against you, and comes, and confesses, and asks your pardon, that ye do pardon him, and forthwith from the heart forgive him; lest ye keep off from your own selves that pardon, which comes from God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:50
verses.text: For if ye forgive not, neither will He forgive you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:51
verses.text: Therefore it is in this life that we make this petition, for that it is in this 			 life that sins can be forgiven, where they can be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:52
verses.text: But in the life to come they are not forgiven, because they are not done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:53
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:54
verses.text: Next after this we pray, saying, "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:55
verses.text: This also, that we be not led into temptation, it is necessary for us to ask in this life, because in this life there are temptations; and that "we may be delivered from evil," because there is evil here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:56
verses.text: And thus of all these seven petitions, three have respect to the life eternal, and four to the present life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:57
verses.text: "Hallowed be Thy name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:58
verses.text: This will be for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:59
verses.text: "Thy kingdom come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:60
verses.text: This kingdom will be for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:61
verses.text: "Thy will be done as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:62
verses.text: This 			 will be for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:63
verses.text: "Give us this day our daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:64
verses.text: This will not be for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:65
verses.text: "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:66
verses.text: This will not be for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:67
verses.text: "Lead us not into temptation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:68
verses.text: This will not be for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:69
verses.text: "But deliver us from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 8:70
verses.text: This will not be for ever: but where there is temptation, and where there is evil, there is it necessary that we make this petition.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:1
verses.text: Sermon X.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:2
verses.text: [LX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:5
verses.text: vi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:6
verses.text: 19, "Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:7
verses.text: An exhortation to alms-deeds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:9
verses.text: Every man who is in any trouble, and his own resources fail him, looks out for some prudent person from whom he may take counsel, and so know what to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:10
verses.text: Let us suppose then the whole world to be as it were one single man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:11
verses.text: He seeks to escape evil, yet is slow in doing good; and as in this way tribulations thicken, and his own resources fail, whom can he find more prudent to receive counsel from than Christ? By all means, at least, let him 			 find a better, and do what he will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:12
verses.text: But if he cannot find a better, let him come to Him whom he may find everywhere: let him consult, and take advice from Him, keep the good commandment, escape the great evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:13
verses.text: For present temporal ills of which men are so sore afraid, under which they murmur exceedingly, and by their murmuring offend Him who is correcting them, so that they find not His saving Help; present ills I say without a doubt are but passing; either they pass through us, or we pass through them; either they pass away whilst we live, or they are left behind us when we die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:14
verses.text: Now that is not in the matter of tribulation great, which in duration is short.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:15
verses.text: Whosoever thou art that art thinking of to-morrow, thou dost not recall the remembrance of yesterday.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:16
verses.text: When the day after to-morrow comes, this to-morrow also will be yesterday.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:17
verses.text: But now if men are so disquieted with 			 anxiety to escape temporal tribulations which pass, or rather fly over, what thought ought they to take that they may escape those which abide and endure without end?  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:18
verses.text: A hard condition is the life of man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:19
verses.text: What else is it to be born, but to enter on a life of toil? Of our toil that is to be, the infant's very cry is witness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:20
verses.text: From this cup of sorrow no one may be excused.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:21
verses.text: The cup that Adam hath pledged, must be drunk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:22
verses.text: We were made, it is true, by the hands of Truth, but because of sin we were cast forth upon days of vanity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:23
verses.text: "We were made after the image of God," but we disfigured it by sinful transgression.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:24
verses.text: Therefore does the Psalm remind us how we were made, and to what a state we have come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:25
verses.text: For it says, "Though a man walk in the image of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:26
verses.text: See, what he was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:27
verses.text: Whither hath he come? Hearken to what follows, "Yet will he be disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:28
verses.text: He walks in the image of truth, and will be disquieted in the counsel of vanity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:29
verses.text: Finally, see his disquiet, see it, and as it were in a glass, be displeased with thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:30
verses.text: "Though," he says, "man walk in the image of God," and therefore be something great, "yet will he be disquieted in vain;" and as though we might ask, How I pray thee, how is man disquieted in vain? "He heapeth up treasure," saith he, "and knoweth not for whom he doth gather it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:31
verses.text: See then, 			 this man, that is the whole human race represented as one man, who is without resource in his own case, and hath lost counsel and wandered out of the way of a sound mind; "Heapeth up treasure, and knoweth not for whom he doth gather it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:32
verses.text: What is more mad, what more unhappy? But surely he is doing it for himself? Not so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:33
verses.text: Why not for himself? Because he must die, because the life of man is short, because the treasure lasts, but he who gathereth it, quickly passeth away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:34
verses.text: As pitying therefore 			 the man who "walketh in the image of God," who confesseth things that are true, yet followeth after vain things, he saith, "He will be disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:35
verses.text: I grieve for him; "he heapeth up treasure, and knoweth not for whom he doth gather it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:36
verses.text: Doth he gather it for himself? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:37
verses.text: Because the man dies whilst the treasure endures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:38
verses.text: For whom then? If thou hast any good counsel, give it to me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:39
verses.text: But counsel hast thou none to give me, and so thou hast none for thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:40
verses.text: Wherefore if we are 			 both without it, let us both seek it, let us both receive it, and both consider the matter together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:41
verses.text: He is disquieted, he heapeth up treasure, he thinks, and toils, and is kept awake by anxiety.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:42
verses.text: All day long art thou harassed by labour, all night agitated by fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:43
verses.text: That thy coffer may be filled with money, thy soul is in a fever of anxiety.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:44
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:45
verses.text: I see it, I am grieved for thee; thou art disquieted, and as He who cannot deceive, assures us, "Thou art disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:46
verses.text: For thou art heaping up treasures: supposing that all thy undertakings succeed, to say nothing of losses, of so great perils and deaths in the prosecution of every several kind of gain (I speak not of deaths of the body, but of evil thoughts, for that gold may come in, uprightness goeth out; that thou mayest be clothed outwardly, thou art made naked within), but to pass over these, and other such things in silence, to pass by all the things that are against thee, let us think only of the favourable circumstances.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:47
verses.text: See, thou art laying up treasures, gains flow into thee from every quarter, and thy money runs like fountains; everywhere where want presseth, there doth abundance flow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:48
verses.text: Hast thou not heard, "If riches increase, set not your heart upon 			 them?"  Lo, thou art getting, thou art disquieted, not fruitlessly indeed, still in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:49
verses.text: "How," thou wilt ask "am I disquieted in vain? I am filling my coffers, my walls will scarce hold what I get, how then am I disquieted in vain?" "Thou art heaping up treasure, and dost not know for whom thou gatherest it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:50
verses.text: Or if thou dost know, I pray thee tell me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:51
verses.text: I will listen to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:52
verses.text: For whom is it? If thou art not disquieted in vain, tell me for whom 			 thou art heaping up thy treasure? "For myself," thou sayest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:53
verses.text: Dost thou dare say so, who must so soon die? "For my children".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:54
verses.text: Dost thou dare say this of them who must so soon die? It is a great duty of natural affection (it will be said) for a father to lay up for his sons; rather it is a great vanity, one who must soon die is laying up for those who must soon die also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:55
verses.text: If it is for thyself, why dost thou gather, seeing thou leavest all when thou diest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:56
verses.text: This is the case also with thy children; they will succeed thee, but not to abide long.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:57
verses.text: I say nothing about what sort of children they may be, whether haply debauchery may not waste what covetousness hath amassed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:58
verses.text: So another by dissoluteness 			  squanders what thou by much toil hast gathered together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:59
verses.text: But I pass over this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:60
verses.text: It may be they will be good children, they will not be dissolute, they will keep what thou hast left, will increase what thou hast kept, and will not dissipate what thou hast heaped together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:61
verses.text: Then will thy children be equally vain with thyself, if they do so, if in this they imitate thee their father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:62
verses.text: I would say to them what I said just now to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:63
verses.text: I would say to thy son, to him for whom thou art 			 saving I would say, "Thou art heaping up treasure, and knowest not for whom thou dost gather it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:64
verses.text: For as thou knewest not, so neither doth he know.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:65
verses.text: If the vanity hath continued in him, hath the truth lost its power with respect to him?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:66
verses.text: I forbear to urge, that it may be even during thy life thou art but laying up for thieves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:67
verses.text: In one night may they come and find all ready the gathering of so many days and nights.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:68
verses.text: It may be thou art laying up for a robber, or a highwayman.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:69
verses.text: I will say no more on this, lest I call to mind and re-open the wound of past sufferings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:70
verses.text: How many things which an empty vanity hath heaped together, hath the cruelty of an enemy found ready to its hand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:71
verses.text: It is not my place to 			 wish for this: but it is the concern of all to fear it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:72
