verses.text: May God avert it! May His own scourges be sufficient.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:73
verses.text: May He to whom we pray, spare us! But if He ask thee for whom are we laying by, what shall we answer? How then, O man, whosoever thou art, that are heaping up treasure in vain, how wilt thou answer me, as I handle this matter with thee, and with thee seek counsel in a common cause? For thou didst speak and make answer, "I am laying up for myself, for my children, for my posterity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:74
verses.text: I have said already how many grounds of fear there are, even as to those children themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:75
verses.text: But I pass over the consideration, that thy children may so live as to be a curse to thee, and as thine enemy would wish them; grant that they live as the father himself would have them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:76
verses.text: Yet how many have fallen into those mischances, I have declared, and reminded you of already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:77
verses.text: Thou didst shudder at them, though thou didst not amend thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:78
verses.text: For what hast thou to answer but this, "Perhaps it may not be so"? Well, I said so too; perhaps I say thou art but laying up for the thief, or robber, or highwayman.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:79
verses.text: I did not say certainly, but perhaps.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:80
verses.text: Where 			 there is a perhaps, there is a perhaps-not; so then thou knowest not what will be, and therefore thou "art disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:81
verses.text: Thou seest now how truly spake the Truth, how vainly vanity is disquieted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:82
verses.text: Thou hast heard and at length learnt wisdom, because when thou sayest, "Perhaps it is for my children," but dost not dare to say, "I am sure that it is for my children," thou dost not in fact know for whom thou art gathering riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:83
verses.text: So then, as I see, and have said already, thou art 			 thyself without resource; thou findest nothing wherewith to answer me, nor can I to answer thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:84
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:85
verses.text: Let us both therefore seek and ask for counsel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:86
verses.text: We have opportunity of consulting not any wise man, but Wisdom Herself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:87
verses.text: Let us then both give ear to Jesus Christ, "to the Jews a stumbling stone, and to the Gentiles foolishness, but to them who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the Power of God and the Wisdom of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:88
verses.text: Why art thou preparing a strong defence for thy riches? Hear the Power of God, nothing is more strong than He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:89
verses.text: Why art thou preparing wise counsel to protect thy riches? Hear the Wisdom of God, nothing is more Wise than He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:90
verses.text: Peradventure when I say what I have to say, thou wilt be offended, and so thou wilt be a Jew, "because to the Jews is Christ an offence".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:91
verses.text: Or peradventure, when I have spoken, it will appear foolish to thee, and so wilt thou be a Gentile, "for to the Gentiles is Christ foolishness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:92
verses.text: Yet thou art a Christian, thou hast been called.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:93
verses.text: "But to them who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is 			 the Power of God and the Wisdom of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:94
verses.text: Be not sad then when I have said what I have to say; be not offended; mock not my folly, as you deem it, with an air of disdain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:95
verses.text: Let us give ear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:96
verses.text: For what I am about to say, Christ hath said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:97
verses.text: If thou despise the herald, yet fear the Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:98
verses.text: What shall I say then? The reader of the Gospel has but just now relieved me from this embarrassment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:99
verses.text: I will not read anything fresh, but will recall only to your recollection what has just been read.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:100
verses.text: Thou wast seeking counsel, as failing in thine own resources; see then what the Fountain of right counsel saith, the Fountain from whose streams is 			 no fear of poison, fill from It what thou mayest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:101
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:102
verses.text: "Lay not up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust doth destroy, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where no thief approacheth, nor moth corrupteth: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:103
verses.text: What more dost thou wait for? The thing is plain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:104
verses.text: The counsel is open, but evil desire lies hid; nay, not so, but what is worse, it too lies open.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:105
verses.text: For plunder does not cease its ravages; avarice does not cease to defraud; maliciousness does not cease to swear falsely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:106
verses.text: And all for what? that treasure may be heaped together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:107
verses.text: To be laid up where? In the earth, and rightly indeed, by earth for earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:108
verses.text: For to the man who sinned and who pledged us, as I have 			 said, our cup of toil, was it said, "Earth thou art, and to earth shalt thou return".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:109
verses.text: With good reason is the treasure in earth, because the heart is there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:110
verses.text: Where then is that, "we lift them up unto the Lord?" Sorrow for your case, ye who have understood me; and if ye sorrow truly, amend yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:111
verses.text: How long will ye be applauding and not doing? What ye have heard is true, nothing truer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:112
verses.text: Let that then which is true be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:113
verses.text: One God we praise, yet we change not, that we may not in this very praise be disquieted in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:114
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:115
verses.text: Therefore, "Lay not up for yourselves treasures on earth;" whether ye have found by experience how what is laid up in the earth is lost, or whether ye have not so experienced it, yet do ye too fear lest ye should do so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:116
verses.text: Let experience reform him whom words will not reform.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:117
verses.text: One cannot rise up now, one cannot go out, but all together with one voice are crying, "Woe to us, the world is falling".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:118
verses.text: If it be falling, why dost thou not remove? If an architect were to tell thee, that thy house would soon fall, wouldest thou not remove before thou didst indulge in thy vain lamentations? The Builder of the world telleth thee the world will soon fall, and wilt thou not believe it? Hear the voice of Him who foretelleth it, hear the counsel of Him who giveth thee warning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:119
verses.text: The voice of prediction is, "Heaven and earth shall pass away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:120
verses.text: The voice of warning is, "Lay not up for yourselves treasure on earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:121
verses.text: If then thou dost believe God in His prediction; if thou despise not His warning, let what He says be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:122
verses.text: He who has given thee such counsel doth not deceive thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:123
verses.text: Thou shalt not lose what thou hast given away, but shalt follow what thou hast only sent before thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:124
verses.text: Therefore my counsel is, "Give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:125
verses.text: Thou shalt not remain without treasure; but what thou hast on earth with anxiety, thou shalt possess in heaven free from care.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:126
verses.text: Transport thy goods then.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:127
verses.text: I am giving thee counsel for keeping, not for losing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:128
verses.text: "Thou shalt have," saith He, "treasure in heaven, and come, follow Me," that I may bring thee to thy treasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:129
verses.text: This is not a wasting, but a saving.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:130
verses.text: Why do men keep silence? Let them hear, and having at last by experience found what to fear, let them do that which 			 will give them no cause of fear, let them transport their goods to heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:131
verses.text: Thou puttest wheat in the low ground; and thy friend comes, who knows the nature of the corn and the land, and instructs thy unskilfulness, and says to thee, "What hast thou done?" Thou hast put the corn in the flat soil, in the lower land; the soil is moist; it will all rot, and thou wilt lose thy labour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:132
verses.text: Thou answerest, What then must I do? Remove it, he says, into the higher ground.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:133
verses.text: Dost thou then give ear to a friend who gives thee counsel about thy corn, and despisest thou God who gives thee counsel about 			 thine heart? Thou fearest to put thy corn in the low earth, and wilt thou lose thy heart in the earth? Behold the Lord thy God when He giveth thee counsel touching thine heart, saith, "Where thy treasure is, there will thy heart be also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:134
verses.text: Lift up, saith He, thine heart to heaven, that it rot not in the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:135
verses.text: It is His counsel, who wisheth to preserve thy heart, not to destroy it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:136
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:137
verses.text: If then this be so, what must be their repentance who have not done thereafter? How must they now reproach themselves! We might have had in heaven what we have now lost in earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:138
verses.text: The enemy has broken up our house; but could he break heaven open? He has killed the servant who was set to guard; but could he kill the Lord who would have kept them, "where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:139
verses.text: How many now are saying, "There we might have had, and hid our 			 treasures safe, where after a little while we might have followed them securely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:140
verses.text: Why have we not hearkened to our Lord? Why have we despised the admonitions of the Father, and so have experienced the invasion of the enemy?" If then this be good counsel, let us not be slow in taking heed to it; and if what we have must be transported, let us transfer it into that place, from whence we cannot lose it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:141
verses.text: What are the poor to whom we give, but our carriers, by whom we convey our goods from earth to heaven? Give then: thou art but giving to thy carrier, he carrieth what thou givest to heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:142
verses.text: How, sayest thou, does he carry it to heaven? For I see that he makes an end of it by eating.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:143
verses.text: No doubt, he carries it, not by keeping it, but by making it his food.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:144
verses.text: What? Hast thou forgotten, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom; for I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat:" and," Inasmuch as ye did it to one of the least 			 of Mine, ye did it to Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:145
verses.text: If thou hast not despised the beggar that standeth before thee, consider to Whom what thou gavest him hath come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:146
verses.text: "Inasmuch," saith he, "as ye did it to one of the least of Mine, ye did it to Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:147
verses.text: He hath received it, who gave thee wherewith to give.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:148
verses.text: He hath received it, who in the end will give His Own Self to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:149
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:150
verses.text: For this have I at divers times called to your remembrance, Beloved, and I confess to you it astonishes me much in the Scriptures of God, and I ought repeatedly to call your attention to it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:151
verses.text: I pray you to think of what our Lord Jesus Christ Himself saith, that at the end of the world, when He shall come to judgment, He will gather together all nations before Him, and will divide men into two parts; that He will place some at His right hand, and others on His 			 left; and will say to those on the right hand, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:152
verses.text: But to those on the left, "Depart ye into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:153
verses.text: Search out the reasons either for so great a reward, or so great a punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:154
verses.text: "Receive the kingdom," and "Go into everlasting fire".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:155
verses.text: Why shall the first receive the kingdom? "For I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:156
verses.text: Why 			 shall the other depart into everlasting fire? "For I was hungry, and ye gave Me no meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:157
verses.text: What meaneth this, I ask? I see touching those who are to receive the kingdom, that they gave as good and faithful Christians, not despising the words of the Lord, and with sure trust hoping for the promises they did accordingly; because had they not done so, this very barrenness would not surely have accorded with their good life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:158
verses.text: For it may be they were chaste, no cheats, nor drunkards, and kept 			 themselves from evil works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:159
verses.text: Yet if they had not added good works, they would have remained barren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:160
verses.text: For they would have kept, "Depart from evil," but they would not have kept, "and do good".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:161
verses.text: Notwithstanding, even to them He doth not say, "Come, receive the kingdom," for ye have lived in chastity; ye have defrauded no man, ye have not oppressed any poor man, ye have invaded no one's landmark, ye have deceived no one by oath.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:162
verses.text: He said not this, but, "Receive the kingdom, because I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:163
verses.text: How excellent is this above all, when the Lord made no mention of the rest, but named this only! And again to the others, "Depart ye into 			 everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:164
verses.text: How many things could He urge against the ungodly, were they to ask, "Why are we going into everlasting fire!" Why? Do ye ask, ye adulterers, menslayers, cheats, sacrilegious blasphemers, unbelievers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:165
verses.text: Yet none of these did He name, but, "Because I was hungry, and ye gave Me no meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:166
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:167
verses.text: I see that you are surprised as I am.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:168
verses.text: And indeed it is a marvellous thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:169
verses.text: But I gather as best I can the reason of this thing so strange, and I will not conceal it from you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:170
verses.text: It is written, "As water quencheth fire, so alms quencheth sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:171
verses.text: Again it is written, "Shut up alms in the heart of a poor man, and it shall make supplication for thee before the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:172
verses.text: Again it is written, "Hear, O king, my counsel, and redeem thy sins by alms".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:173
verses.text: And many other testimonies of the Divine oracles are there, whereby it is shown that alms avail much to the quenching and effacing of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:174
verses.text: Wherefore to those whom He is about to condemn, yea, rather to those whom He is about to crown, He will impute alms only, as though He would say, "It were a hard matter for me not to find occasion to condemn you, were I to examine and weigh you accurately and with much exactness to scrutinize your deeds; but, "Go into the kingdom, for 			 I was hungry, and ye gave Me meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:175
verses.text: Ye shall therefore go into the kingdom, not because ye have not sinned, but because ye have redeemed your sins by alms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:176
verses.text: And again to the others, "Go ye into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:177
verses.text: They too, guilty as they are, old in their sins, late in their fear for them, in what respect, when they turn their sins over in their mind, could they dare to say that they are undeservedly condemned, that this sentence is pronounced against 			 them undeservedly by so righteous a Judge? In considering their consciences, and all the wounds of their souls, in what respect could they dare to say, We are unjustly condemned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:178
verses.text: Of whom it was said before in Wisdom, "Their own iniquities shall convince them to their face".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:179
verses.text: Without doubt they will see that they are justly condemned for their sins and wickednesses; yet it will be as though He said to them, "It is not in consequence of this that ye think, but 'because I was hungry, and ye gave Me no meat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:180
verses.text: '" For if turning away from all these your deeds, and turning to Me, ye had redeemed all those crimes and sins by alms, those alms would now deliver you, and absolve you from the guilt of so great offences; for, 			 "Blessed are the merciful, for to them shall be shown mercy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:181
verses.text: But now go away into everlasting fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:182
verses.text: "He shall have judgment without mercy, who hath showed no mercy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:183
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:184
verses.text: O that I may have induced you, my brethren, to give away your earthly bread, and to knock for the heavenly! The Lord is that Bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:185
verses.text: He saith, "I am the Bread of life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:186
verses.text: But how shall He give to thee, who givest not to him that is in need? One is in need before thee, and thou art in need before Another, and since thou art in need before Another, and another is in need before thee, that other is in need before him who is in need himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:187
verses.text: For He before whom thou art in need, needeth nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:188
verses.text: Do then to others as thou wouldest have done to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:189
verses.text: For it is not in this case as with those friends who are wont to upbraid in a way one another with 			 their kindnesses; as, "I did this for thee," and the other answers, "and I this for thee," that He wishes us to do Him some good office, because He has first done such an office for us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:190
verses.text: He is in want of nothing, and therefore is He the very Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:191
verses.text: I said unto the Lord, "Thou art my God, for Thou needest not my goods".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:192
verses.text: Notwithstanding though He be the Lord, and the Very Lord, and needeth not our goods, yet that we might do something even for Him, hath He vouchsafed to be hungry in His poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:193
verses.text: "I was hungry," saith He, "and ye gave Me meat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:194
verses.text: Lord, when saw we Thee hungry? Forasmuch as ye did it to one of the least of Mine, ye did it to Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:195
verses.text: To be brief then, let men hear, and consider as they ought, how great a merit it is to have fed Christ when He hungereth, and how great a crime it is to have despised Christ when He hungereth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:196
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:197
verses.text: Repentance for sins changes men, it is true, for the better; but it does not appear as if even it would profit ought, if it should be barren of works of mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:198
verses.text: This the Truth testifieth by the mouth of John, who said to them that came to him, "O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance; And say not we have Abraham to our father; for I say unto you, that God is able of these 			 stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:199
verses.text: For now is the axe laid unto the root of the trees.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:200
verses.text: Every tree therefore that bringeth not forth good fruit shall be cut down, and cast into the fire".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:201
verses.text: Touching this fruit he said above, "Bring forth fruits worthy of repentance".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:202
verses.text: Whoso then bringeth not forth these fruits, hath no cause to think that he shall attain pardon for his sins by a barren repentance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:203
verses.text: Now what these fruits are, he showeth afterwards himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:204
verses.text: For after these his words the multitude asked him, saying, "What shall we do then?" That is, what are these fruits, which thou exhortest us with such alarming force to bring forth? "But he answering said unto them, he that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:205
verses.text: My brethren, what is more plain, what more certain, 			 or express than this? What other meaning then can that have which he said above, "Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, shall be cut down, and cast into the fire;" but that same which they on the left shall hear, "Go ye into everlasting fire, for I was hungry, and ye gave Me no meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:206
verses.text: So then it is but a small matter to depart from sins, if thou shalt neglect to cure what is past, as it is written, "Son, thou hast sinned, do so no more".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:207
verses.text: And that he might not think to be 			 secure by this only, he saith, "And for thy former sins pray that they may be forgiven thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 9:208
verses.text: But what will it profit thee to pray for forgiveness, if thou shalt not make thyself meet to be heard, by not bringing forth fruits meet for repentance, that thou shouldest be cut down as a barren tree, and be cast into the fire? If then ye will be heard when ye pray for pardon of your sins, "Forgive, and it shall be forgiven you; Give, and it shall be given you".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:1
verses.text: Sermon XI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:2
verses.text: [LXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:5
verses.text: vii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:6
verses.text: 7, "Ask, and it shall be given you;" etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:7
verses.text: An exhortation to alms-deeds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:9
verses.text: In the lesson of the Holy Gospel the Lord hath exhorted us to prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:10
verses.text: "Ask," saith He, "and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:11
verses.text: For every one that asketh receiveth, and he that seeketh findeth, and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:12
verses.text: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone? Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent? 			  Or if he ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion? If ye then," saith He, "though ye be evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask Him? Though ye be evil," He saith, "ye know how to give good gifts unto your children".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:13
verses.text: A marvellous thing, Brethren! we are evil: yet have we a good Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:14
verses.text: What is more evident? We have heard our proper name: "Though ye be evil, ye know how to give good gifts unto your children".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:15
verses.text: And now see what kind of Father He showeth them, whom he called evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:16
verses.text: "How much more shall your Father?" Father of whom? undoubtedly of the evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:17
verses.text: And what kind of 			 Father? "None is good but God only".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:18
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:19
verses.text: For this cause have we who are evil a good Father, that we may not always continue evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:20
verses.text: No evil man can make another man good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:21
verses.text: If no evil man can make another good, how can an evil man make himself good? He only can make of an evil man a good man, who is good eternally.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:22
verses.text: "Heal me, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:23
verses.text: Why then do those vain ones say to me in words vain as themselves, "Thou canst save thyself if thou wilt"? "Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:24
verses.text: We were created good by The Good; for "God made man upright," but by our own free will, we became evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:25
verses.text: We had power from being good to become evil, and we shall have power from being evil to become good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:26
verses.text: But it is He who is ever Good, who maketh the good out of the evil; for man by his own will had no power to heal himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:27
verses.text: Thou dost not look out for a physician to wound thyself; but when thou hast wounded thyself, thou lookest out for one to cure thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:28
verses.text: Good things then after the time present, temporal good things, such as are concerned 			 with the body and flesh, we do know how to give to our children, even though we are evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:29
verses.text: For even these are good things, who would doubt it? A fish, an egg, bread, fruit, wheat, the light we see, the air we breathe, all these are good; the very riches by which men are lifted up, and which make them loth to acknowledge other men to be their equals; by which, I say, men are lifted up rather in love of their dazzling clothing, than with any thought of their common nature, even these riches, I 			 repeat, are good; but all these goods which I have now mentioned may be possessed by good and bad alike; and though they be good themselves, yet cannot they make their owners good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:31
verses.text: A good then there is which maketh good, and a good there is whereby thou mayest do good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:32
verses.text: The Good which maketh good is God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:33
verses.text: For none can make man good, save He who is Good eternally.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:34
verses.text: Therefore that thou mayest be good, call upon God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:35
verses.text: But there is another good whereby thou mayest do good, and that is, whatever thou mayest possess.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:36
verses.text: There is gold, there is silver; they are good, not such as can make thee good, but whereby thou mayest do good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:37
verses.text: Thou hast gold and 			 silver, and thou desirest more gold and silver.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:38
verses.text: Thou both hast, and desirest to have; thou art at once full, and thirsty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:39
verses.text: This is a disease, not opulence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:40
verses.text: When men are in the dropsy, they are full of water, and yet are always thirsty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:41
verses.text: They are full of water, and yet they thirst for water.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:42
verses.text: How then canst thou take pleasure in opulence, who hast thereby this dropsical desire? Gold then thou hast, it is good; yet thou hast not whereby thou canst be made good, but whereby thou canst do good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:43
verses.text: Dost thou ask, What good can I do with gold? Hast thou not heard in the Psalm, "He hath dispersed abroad, he hath given to the poor, his righteousness remaineth for 			 ever".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:44
verses.text: This is good, this is the good whereby thou art made good; righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:45
verses.text: If thou have the good whereby thou art made good, do good with that good which cannot make thee good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:46
verses.text: Thou hast money, deal it out freely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:47
verses.text: By dealing it out freely, thou increasest righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:48
verses.text: "For he hath dispersed abroad, hath distributed, hath given to the poor; his righteousness remaineth for ever".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:49
verses.text: See what is diminished and what increased.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:50
verses.text: Thy money is diminished, thy righteousness 			 increased.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:51
verses.text: That is diminished which thou must soon have lost, that diminished which thou must soon have left behind thee; that increased which thou shalt possess for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:52
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:53
verses.text: It is then a secret of gainful dealing I am giving; learn so to trade.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:54
verses.text: For thou dost commend the merchant who selleth lead and getteth gold, and wilt thou not commend the merchant, who layeth out money, and getteth righteousness? But thou wilt say, I do not lay out my money, because I have not righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:55
verses.text: Let him who has righteousness lay his money out; I have not righteousness, so at least let me have my money.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:56
verses.text: Dost thou not then wish to lay out thy money, 			 because thou hast not righteousness? Yea, lay it out then rather that thou mayest have righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:57
verses.text: For from whence shalt thou have righteousness but from God, the Fountain of righteousness? Therefore, if thou wilt have righteousness, be God's beggar, who just now out of the Gospel urged thee to ask, and seek, and knock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:58
verses.text: He knew His beggar, and lo the Householder, the mighty rich One, rich, to wit, in riches spiritual and eternal, exhorteth thee and saith, "Ask, seek, knock; he that 			 asketh receiveth, he that seeketh findeth, to him that knocketh it shall be opened".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:59
verses.text: He exhorteth thee to ask, and will he refuse thee what thou askest?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:60
verses.text: Consider a similitude or comparison drawn from a contrary case (as of that unjust judge), which is an encouragement to us to prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:61
verses.text: "There was," saith the Lord, "in a city a certain judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:62
verses.text: A certain widow importuned him daily, and said, "Avenge me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:63
verses.text: He would not for a long time; but she ceased not to petition, and he did through her importunity what he would not of his own good will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:64
verses.text: For thus by a contrary case hath He recommended us to pray.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:66
verses.text: Again, He saith, "A certain man to whom some guest had come, went to his friend, and began to knock and say, A guest is come to me, lend me three loaves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:67
verses.text: He answered, "I am already in bed, and my servants with me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:68
verses.text: The other does not leave off, but stands and presses his case, and knocks and begs as one friend of another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:69
verses.text: And what saith He? "I say unto you that he riseth, and not because of his friendship," but "because of the other's importunity 			 he giveth him as many as he wanted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:70
verses.text: Not because of his friendship," though he is his friend, but "because of his importunity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:71
verses.text: What is the meaning of "because of his importunity?" Because he did not leave off knocking; because even when his request was refused, he did not turn away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:72
verses.text: He who was not willing to give, gave what was asked, because the other fainted not in asking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:73
verses.text: How much more then shall that Good One give who exhorteth us to ask, who is displeased if we ask not? But when at times He giveth somewhat slowly, it is that He is showing us the value of His good things; not that He refuses them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:74
verses.text: Things which have been long desired, are obtained with the greater pleasure, whereas those which are given quickly, are held cheap.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:75
verses.text: Ask then, seek, be instant.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:76
verses.text: By the very asking and seeking thou dost grow so as to contain the more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:77
verses.text: God is keeping in reserve for thee, what it is not His will to give thee quickly, that thou mayest learn for great things to long with great desire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:78
verses.text: Therefore "ought we always to pray, and not to faint".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:79
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:80
verses.text: If then God hath made us His beggars by admonishing, and exhorting, and commanding us to ask, and seek, and knock, let us for our part pay regard to those who ask from us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:81
verses.text: We ask, and from whom do we ask? Who are we that ask? What do we ask? From whom, or who are we, or what is it that we ask? We ask of the Good God; and we that ask are evil men; but we ask for righteousness, whereby we may be good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:82
verses.text: We ask then for that which we may have for ever, wherewith when 			 we shall be filled, we shall want no more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:83
verses.text: But in order that we may be filled, let us hunger and thirst; hungering and thirsting, let us ask, and seek, and knock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:84
verses.text: "For blessed are they who hunger and thirst after righteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:85
verses.text: Wherefore are they blessed? They do hunger and thirst, and are they blessed? Is want ever a blessing? They are not blessed in that they hunger and thirst, but in that they will be filled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:86
verses.text: There will there be blessedness, in the fulness, not in the hunger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:87
verses.text: But hunger must go before the fulness, that no loathing attach to the bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:88
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:89
verses.text: We have said then, from whom it is that we ask, and who we are that ask, and what we ask.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:90
verses.text: But we also are asked ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:91
verses.text: For we are God's mendicants; that He may acknowledge His mendicants, let us on our part acknowledge ours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:92
verses.text: But let us think in this case again, when anything is asked of us, who they are that ask, from whom they ask, and what they ask? Who then are they that ask? Men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:93
verses.text: From whom do they ask? From men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:94
verses.text: Who are they that ask? Mortals.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:95
verses.text: From whom? From 			 mortals.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:96
verses.text: Who are they that ask? Frail beings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:97
verses.text: From whom? From frail beings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:98
verses.text: Who are they that ask? Wretches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:99
verses.text: And from whom? From wretches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:100
verses.text: Excepting in the matter of wealth, they that ask are as they of whom they ask.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:101
verses.text: With what face canst thou ask before thy lord, who dost not acknowledge thine own equal? "I am not," he will say, "as he is," far be it from me to be such as he.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:102
verses.text: It is thus that one clad in silk, and puffed up with pride, speaks of one who is wrapped in rags.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:103
verses.text: But I ask you 			 when you both are stripped.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:104
verses.text: I ask you not as you are now when clothed, but as you were when you were first born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:105
verses.text: Both were naked, both weak, beginning a life of misery, and therefore beginning it with cries.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:106
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:107
verses.text: See then, recall, O rich man, to mind thy first beginnings; see whether thou broughtest anything into the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:108
verses.text: Now thou hast come indeed, and hast found so great abundance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:109
verses.text: But tell me, I pray thee, what didst thou bring hither? Tell me, or if thou art ashamed to say, hear the Apostle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:110
verses.text: "We brought nothing into this world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:111
verses.text: He saith, "We brought nothing into this world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:112
verses.text: But perhaps because thou broughtest in nothing, but yet hast found much here, thou wilt take away something hence? This too, peradventure through love of riches, thou art afraid to confess.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:113
verses.text: Hear this also, and let the Apostle who will not flatter, tell thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:114
verses.text: "We brought nothing into this world," to wit when we were born; "neither can we carry anything out," to wit when we shall depart out of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:115
verses.text: Thou broughtest 			 in nothing, and thou shalt carry nothing away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:116
verses.text: Why then dost thou puff up thyself against the poor man? When infants first are born, let only the parents, servants, dependants, and the crowds of obsequious attendants, get out of the way; and then let the wealthy children with their cries be recognised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:117
verses.text: Let the rich woman and the poor give birth together; let them take no notice of their children, let them go away for a little while; then let them return, and recognise them 			 if they can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:118
verses.text: See then, O rich man, "thou broughtest nothing into this world; neither canst thou carry anything out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:119
verses.text: What I have said of them at their birth, I may say of them in death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:120
verses.text: If it be not so, when by any chance old sepulchres are broken up, let the bones of the rich be recognised if they can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:121
verses.text: Therefore, thou rich man, give ear to the Apostle, "We brought nothing into this world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:122
verses.text: Acknowledge it, true it is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:123
verses.text: "Neither can we carry anything out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:124
verses.text: Acknowledge it, this is true 			 also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:125
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:126
verses.text: What follows then? "Having food and covering, let us be therewith content; for they who wish to be rich fall into temptation, and many and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:127
verses.text: For avarice is the root of all evil, which some following after, have erred from the faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:128
verses.text: Now consider what they have abandoned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:129
verses.text: Grieved thou art that they have abandoned this, but see now in what they have entangled themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:130
verses.text: Hear; "They have erred from the faith, and entangled themselves in many sorrows".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:131
verses.text: But who? "They who wish to be rich".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:132
verses.text: It is one thing to be rich, another to wish to become rich.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:133
verses.text: He is rich, who is born of rich parents, and he is rich not because he wished it, but because many left him their inheritances.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:134
verses.text: His 			  wealth I see, I make no question as to the pleasure he takes in it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:135
verses.text: In this Scripture it is covetousness that is condemned, not gold, or silver, or riches, but covetousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:136
verses.text: For they who do not wish to become rich, or do not care about it, who do not burn with covetous desires, nor are inflamed by the fires of avarice, but who yet are rich, let them hear the Apostle (it has been read to-day), "Charge them that are rich in this world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:137
verses.text: Charge them what? Charge them before all things, not to be proud in their conceits, for there is nothing which riches do so much generate as pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:138
verses.text: Each several fruit, each several grain of corn, each several tree, has its peculiar worm, and the worm of the apple is of one kind, and of the pear another, and of the bean another, and of the wheat another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:139
verses.text: The worm of riches is pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:140
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:141
verses.text: "Charge therefore the rich of this world that they be not proud in their conceits".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:142
verses.text: He hath shut out the abuse, let him teach now the proper use.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:143
verses.text: "That they be not proud in their conceits".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:144
verses.text: But whence cometh the defence against pride? From that which follows: "Nor trust in the uncertainty of riches".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:145
verses.text: They who trust not in the uncertainty of riches, are not proud in their conceits.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:146
verses.text: If they be not proud in their conceits, let them fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:147
verses.text: If they fear, they are not proud in their conceits.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:148
verses.text: How many are they who were rich yesterday, and are poor to-day? How many go to sleep rich, and 			 through robbers coming and taking all away, wake up poor? Therefore "charge them not to trust in the uncertainty of riches, but in the Living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy," things temporal, and things eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:149
verses.text: But things eternal more for enjoyment, the things temporal for use.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:150
verses.text: Things temporal as for travellers, things eternal as for inhabitants.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:151
verses.text: Things temporal, whereby we may do good; things eternal, whereby we may be made good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:152
verses.text: Therefore let the rich do this, "Let them 			 not be proud in their conceits, nor trust in the uncertainty of riches, but in the Living God, who giveth us all things richly to enjoy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:153
verses.text: Let them do this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:154
verses.text: But what can they do with what they have? Hear what.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:155
verses.text: "Let them be rich in good works, let them easily distribute".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:156
verses.text: For they have wherewithal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:157
verses.text: Why then do they not do it? Poverty is a hard estate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:158
verses.text: But they may give easily, for they have the means.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:159
verses.text: "Let them communicate," that is, let them acknowledge their fellow-mortals as their equals.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:160
verses.text: "Let them communicate, let them lay up for themselves a good foundation against the time to come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:161
verses.text: For, saith he, when I say, "Let them distribute easily, let them communicate," I have no wish to spoil, or strip them, or leave them empty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:162
verses.text: It is a painful lesson I teach; I show them a place to put their goods, "let them lay up in store for themselves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:163
verses.text: For I have no wish that they should remain in poverty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:164
verses.text: "Let them lay up for themselves in store".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:165
verses.text: I do not bid them lose their goods, but I show them whither to remove them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:166
verses.text: "Let them lay up in store for 			 themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may hold on the true life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:167
verses.text: The present then is a false life; let them lay hold on the true life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:168
verses.text: "For it is vanity of vanities, and all is vanity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:169
verses.text: What so great abundance hath man in all his labour, wherewith he laboureth under the sun?" Therefore the true life must be laid hold upon, our riches must be removed to the place of the true life, that we may find there what we give here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:170
verses.text: He maketh this exchange of our goods who also changeth ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:171
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:172
verses.text: Give then, my brethren, to the poor, "Having food and covering, let us be therewith content".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:173
verses.text: The rich man has nothing from his riches, but what the poor man begs of him, food and covering.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:174
verses.text: What more hast thou from all that thou possessest? Thou hast got food and necessary covering.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:175
verses.text: Necessary I say, not useless, not superfluous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:176
verses.text: What more dost thou get from thy riches? Tell me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:177
verses.text: Assuredly all thou hast more will be superfluous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:178
verses.text: Let thy superfluities then be the 			 poor man's necessaries.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:179
verses.text: But thou wilt say, I get costly banquets, I feed on costly meats.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:180
verses.text: But the poor man, what does he feed on? On cheap food; the poor man feeds on cheap, and I, says he, on costly meats.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:181
verses.text: Well, I ask you, when you both are filled, the costly enters into thee, but when it is once entered, what does it become? If we had but looking-glasses within us, should we not be put to shame for all the costly meat whereby thou hast been filled? The poor man hungers, 			 and so does the rich; the poor man seeks to be filled, so does the rich.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:182
verses.text: The poor man is filled with inexpensive, the rich with costly meats.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:183
verses.text: Both are filled alike, the object whither both wish to attain is one and the same, only the one reaches it by a short, the other by a circuitous way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:184
verses.text: But thou wilt say, I relish better my costly food.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:185
verses.text: True, and it is hard for thee to be satisfied, dainty as thou art.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:186
verses.text: Thou knowest not the relish of that which hunger seasons.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:187
verses.text: Not that I have said this to force the rich to feed on the meat and drink of the poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:188
verses.text: Let the rich use what their infirmity has accustomed them to; but let them be sorry, that they are not able to do otherwise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:189
verses.text: For it would be better for them if they could.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:190
verses.text: If then the poor man be not puffed up for his poverty, why shouldest thou for thine infirmity? Use then choice, and costly meats, because thou art so accustomed, because thou canst not do otherwise, because if thou dost 			 change thy custom, thou art made ill.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:191
verses.text: I grant thee this, make use of superfluities, but give to the poor necessaries; make use of costly meats, but give to the poor inexpensive food.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:192
verses.text: He is looking to receive from thee, and thou art looking to receive from God; he is looking to the hand which was made as he was, and thou art looking to the hand that made thee, and made not thee only, but the poor man with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:193
verses.text: He set you both one and the same journey, this present life: you have found 			 yourselves companions in it, you are walking one way: he is carrying nothing, thou art loaded excessively: he is carrying nothing with him, thou art carrying with thee more than thou dost need.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:194
verses.text: Thou art loaded: give him of that thou hast; so shalt thou at once feed him, and lessen thine own burden.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:195
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:196
verses.text: Give then to the poor; I beg, I advise, I charge, I command you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:197
verses.text: Give to the poor whatever ye will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:198
verses.text: For I will not conceal from you, Beloved, why it is that I have deemed it necessary to deliver this discourse to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:199
verses.text: As I am going to and from the Church, the poor importune me, and beg me to speak to you, that they may receive something of you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:200
verses.text: They have urged me to speak to you; and when they see that they receive nothing from you, they suppose that all my labour 			 among you is in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:201
verses.text: Something also they expect from me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:202
verses.text: I give them all I can; but have I the means sufficient to supply all their necessities? Forasmuch then as I have not means sufficient to supply all their necessity, I am at least their ambassador to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:203
verses.text: You have heard and applauded; God be thanked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:204
verses.text: You have received the seed, you have returned an answer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:205
verses.text: But these your commendations weigh me down rather, and expose me to danger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:206
verses.text: I bear them, and tremble whilst I bear them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 10:207
verses.text: Nevertheless, 			 my brethren, these your commendations are but the tree's leaves; it is the fruit I am in quest of.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:1
verses.text: Sermon XII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:2
verses.text: [LXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:5
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:6
verses.text: 8 , "I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:7
verses.text: , and of the words of the apostle, 1 Cor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:8
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:9
verses.text: 10 , "For if a man see thee who hast knowledge sitting at meat in an idol's temple," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:10
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:11
verses.text: We have heard, as the Gospel was being read, the praise of our faith as manifested in humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:12
verses.text: For when the Lord Jesus promised that He would go to the Centurion's house to heal His servant, He answered, "I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and he shall be healed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:13
verses.text: By calling himself unworthy, he showed himself worthy for Christ to come not into his house, but into his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:14
verses.text: Nor would he have said this with so great faith and humility, had he not borne Him in his heart, of whose coming into his house he was afraid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:15
verses.text: For it were no great happiness for the Lord Jesus to enter into his house, and yet not to be in his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:16
verses.text: For this Master of humility both by word and example, sat down even in the house of a certain proud Pharisee, by name 			 Simon; and though He sat down in his house, there was no place in this heart, "where the Son of Man could lay His Head".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:17
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:18
verses.text: For so, as we may understand from the words of the Lord Himself, did He call back from His discipleship a certain proud man, who of his own accord was desirous to go with Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:19
verses.text: "Lord, I will follow Thee whithersoever Thou goest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:20
verses.text: And the Lord seeing in his heart what was invisible, said, "Foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man hath not where to lay His Head".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:21
verses.text: That is, in thee, guile like the fox doth dwell, and pride as the birds of heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:22
verses.text: But the Son of Man simple as opposed to guile, lowly as opposed to pride, hath not where to lay His Head; and this very laying, not the raising up of the head, teaches humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:23
verses.text: Therefore doth He call back this one who was desirous to go, and another who refused He draweth onward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:24
verses.text: For in the same place He saith to a certain man, "Follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:25
verses.text: And he said, "I will 			 follow Thee, Lord, but let me first go and bury my father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:26
verses.text: His excuse was indeed a dutiful one: and therefore was he the more worthy to have his excuse removed, and his calling confirmed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:27
verses.text: What he wished to do was an act of dutifulness; but the Master taught him what he ought to prefer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:28
verses.text: For He wished him to be a preacher of the living word, to make others live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:29
verses.text: But there were others by whom that first necessary office might be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:30
verses.text: "Let the dead," He saith, "bury their dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:31
verses.text: When unbelievers bury a dead body, the dead 			 bury the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:32
verses.text: The body of the one hath lost its soul, the soul of the others hath lost God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:33
verses.text: For as the soul is the life of the body; so is God the life of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:34
verses.text: As the body expires when it loses the soul, so doth the soul expire when it loses God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:35
verses.text: The loss of God is the death of the soul: the loss of the soul the death of the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:36
verses.text: The death of the body is necessary; the death of the soul voluntary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:37
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:38
verses.text: The Lord then sat down in the house of a certain proud Pharisee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:39
verses.text: He was in his house, as I have said, and was not in his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:40
verses.text: But into this centurion's house He entered not, yet He possessed his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:41
verses.text: Zacchaeus again received the Lord both in house and heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:42
verses.text: Yet the centurion's faith is praised for its humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:43
verses.text: For he said, "I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof;" and the Lord said, "Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel;" according to the flesh, that is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:44
verses.text: For he too was an Israelite undoubtedly according to the spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:45
verses.text: The Lord had come to fleshly Israel, that is, to the Jews, there to seek first for the lost sheep, among this people, and of this people also He had assumed His Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:46
verses.text: "I have not found there so great faith," He saith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:47
verses.text: We can but measure the faith of men, as men can judge of it; but He who saw the inward parts, He whom no man can deceive, gave His testimony to this man's 			 heart, hearing words of lowliness, and pronouncing a sentence of healing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:48
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:49
verses.text: But whence did he get such confidence? "I also," saith he, "am a man set under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh: and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:50
verses.text: I am an authority to certain who are placed under me, being myself placed under a certain authority above me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:51
verses.text: If then I a man under authority have the power of commanding, what power must Thou have, whom all powers serve? Now this man was of the Gentiles, for he was a centurion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:52
verses.text: At that time the Jewish nation had soldiers of the Roman empire among them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:53
verses.text: There he was engaged in a military life, according to the extent of a centurion's authority, both under authority himself, 			 and having authority over others; as a subject obedient, ruling others who were under him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:54
verses.text: But the Lord (and mark this especially, Beloved, as need there is you should), though He was among the Jewish people only, even now announced beforehand that the Church should be in the whole world, for the establishment of which He would send Apostles; Himself not seen, yet believed on by the Gentiles: by the Jews seen, and put to death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:55
verses.text: For as the Lord did not in body enter into this man's house, and 			 still, though in body absent, yet present in majesty, healed his faith, and his house; so the same Lord also was in body among the Jewish people only: among the other nations He was neither born of a Virgin, nor suffered, nor walked, nor endured His human sufferings, nor wrought His divine miracles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:56
verses.text: None of all this took place in the rest of the nations, and yet was that fulfilled which was spoken of Him, "A people whom I have not known, hath served Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:57
verses.text: And how if it did not know Him? 			 "Hath obeyed Me by the hearing of the ear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:58
verses.text: The Jewish nation knew, and crucified Him; the whole world besides heard and believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:59
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:60
verses.text: This absence, so to say, of His body, and presence of His power among all nations, He signified also in the instance of that woman who had touched the edge of His garment, when He asketh, saying, "Who touched Me?" He asketh, as though He were absent; as though present, He healeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:61
verses.text: "The multitude," say the disciples, "press Thee, and sayest Thou, Who touched Me?" For as if He were so walking as not to be touched by anybody at all, He said, "Who touched Me?" And they answer, "The multitude press Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:62
verses.text: And the Lord would seem to say, I am asking for one who touched, not for one who pressed Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:63
verses.text: In this case also is His Body now, that is, His Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:64
verses.text: The faith of the few 			 "touches" it, the throng of the many "press" it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:65
verses.text: For ye have heard, as being her children, that Christ's Body is the Church, and if ye will, ye yourselves are so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:66
verses.text: This the Apostle says in many places, "For His body's sake, which is the Church;" and again, "But ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:67
verses.text: If then we are His body, what His body then suffered in the crowd, that doth His Church suffer now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:68
verses.text: It is pressed by many, touched by few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:69
verses.text: The flesh presses it, faith touches it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:70
verses.text: Lift up therefore your eyes, I beseech you, ye who have wherewithal to see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:71
verses.text: For ye have before you something to see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:72
verses.text: Lift up the eyes of faith, touch but the extreme border of His garment, it will be sufficient for saving health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:73
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:74
verses.text: See ye how that which ye have heard out of the Gospel was at that time to come is now present.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:75
verses.text: Therefore, said He, on occasion of the commendation of the Centurion's faith, as in the flesh an alien, but of the household in heart, "Therefore I say unto you, Many shall come from the east and west".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:76
verses.text: Not all, but "many;" yet they shall "come from the East and West;" the whole world is denoted by these two parts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:77
verses.text: "Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven; but the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:78
verses.text: "But the children of the kingdom," the Jews, namely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:79
verses.text: And how "the children of the kingdom"? Because they received the Law; to them the Prophets were 			 sent, with them was the temple and the Priesthood; they celebrated the figures of all the things to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:80
verses.text: Yet of what things they celebrated the figures, they acknowledged not the presence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:81
verses.text: And, "Therefore the children of the kingdom," He saith, shall go into outer darkness, there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:82
verses.text: And so we see the Jews reprobate, and Christians called from the East and West, to the heavenly banquet, to sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, where the bread 			 is righteousness, and the  cup wisdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:84
verses.text: Consider then, brethren, for of these are ye; ye are of this people, even then foretold, and now exhibited.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:85
verses.text: Yes, verily, ye are of those who have been called from the East and West, to sit down in the kingdom of heaven, not in the temple of idols.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:86
verses.text: Be ye then the Body of Christ, not the pressure of His Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:87
verses.text: Ye have the border of His garment to touch, that ye may be healed of the issue of blood, that is, of carnal pleasures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:88
verses.text: Ye have, I say, the border of the garment to touch.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:89
verses.text: Look upon the Apostles as the garment, by the texture of unity clinging closely to the sides of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:90
verses.text: Among 			 these Apostles was Paul, as it were the border, the least and last; as he saith himself, "I am the least of the Apostles".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:91
verses.text: In a garment the last and least thing is the border.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:92
verses.text: The border is in appearance contemptible, yet is it touched with saving efficacy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:93
verses.text: "Even to this hour we both hunger and thirst, and are naked and buffeted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:94
verses.text: What state so low, so contemptible as this! Touch then, if thou art suffering from a bloody flux.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:95
verses.text: There will go power out of Him whose garment it is, and it will heal thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:96
verses.text: The border was proposed to you just now to be touched, when out of the same Apostle there was read, "For if any one see him which hath knowledge sit at meat in an idol's temple, shall not the conscience of him who is weak, be emboldened to eat things offered to idols? And through thy knowledge shall thy 			 weak brother perish, for whom Christ died!" How think ye may men be deceived by idols, which they suppose are honoured by Christians? A man may say, "God knows my heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:97
verses.text: Yes, but thy brother did not know thy heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:98
verses.text: If thou art weak, beware of a still greater weakness; if thou art strong, have a care of thy brother's weakness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:99
verses.text: They who see what you do, are emboldened to do more, so as to desire not only to eat, but also to sacrifice there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:100
verses.text: And lo, "Through thy knowledge the weak brother perisheth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:101
verses.text: Hear then, 			 my brother; if thou didst disregard the weak, wouldest thou disregard a brother also? Awake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:102
