verses.text: What if so thou sin against Christ Himself? For attend to what thou canst not by any means disregard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:103
verses.text: "But," saith he, "when ye sin so against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:104
verses.text: Let them who disregard these words, go now, and sit at meat in the idol's temple; will they not be of those who press, and do not touch? And when they have been at meat in the idol's temple, let them come and fill the Church; not to receive saving health, but to make a pressure there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:105
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:106
verses.text: But thou wilt say, I am afraid lest I offend those above me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:107
verses.text: By all means be afraid of offending them, and so thou wilt not offend God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:108
verses.text: For thou who art afraid lest thou offend those above thee, see whether there be not One above him whom thou art afraid of offending.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:109
verses.text: By all means then be loth to offend those above thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:110
verses.text: This is an established rule with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:111
verses.text: But then is it not plain, that he must on no account be offended, who is above all others? Run over now the 			 list of those above thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:112
verses.text: First are thy father and mother, if they are educating thee aright; if they are bringing thee up for Christ; they are to be heard in all things, they must be obeyed in every command; let them enjoin nothing against one above themselves, and so let them be obeyed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:113
verses.text: And who, thou wilt say, is above him who begat me? He who created thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:114
verses.text: For man begets, but God creates.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:115
verses.text: How it is that man begets, he does not know; and what he shall beget, he does not know.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:116
verses.text: But He who saw 			 thee that He might make thee, before that he whom He made existed, is surely above thy father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:117
verses.text: Thy country again should be above thy very parents; so that whereinsoever thy parents enjoin aught against thy country, they are not to be listened to.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:118
verses.text: And whatsoever thy country enjoin against God, it is not to be listened to.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:119
verses.text: For if thou wilt be healed, if after the issue of blood, if after twelve years' continuance in that disease, if after having spent thine all upon 			 physicians, and not having received health, thou dost wish at length to be made whole; O woman, whom I am addressing as a figure of the Church, thy father enjoineth thee this, and thy people that.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:120
verses.text: But thy Lord saith to thee, "Forget thine own people, and thy father's house".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:121
verses.text: For what good? for what advantage? with what useful result? "Because the King hath desired thy beauty".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:122
verses.text: He hath desired what He made, since when deformed He loved thee, that He might make thee beautiful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:123
verses.text: For thee unbelieving, and deformed, He shed His Blood, and He made thee faithful and beauteous, He hath loved His own gifts in thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:124
verses.text: For what didst thou bring to thy spouse? What didst thou receive for dowry from thy former father, and former people? Was it not the 			 excesses  and the rags of sins? Thy rags He cast away, thy robe impure He tore asunder.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:125
verses.text: He pitied thee that He might adorn thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:126
verses.text: He adorned thee, that He might love thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:127
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:128
verses.text: What need of more, Brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:129
verses.text: Ye are Christians, and have heard, that "If ye sin against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:130
verses.text: Do not disregard it, if ye would not be wiped out of the book of life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:131
verses.text: How long shall I go about to speak in bright and pleasing terms to you, what my grief forceth me to speak in some sort, and will not suffer me to keep secret? Whosoever they are who are minded to disregard these things, and sin 			 against Christ, let them only consider what they are doing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:132
verses.text: We wish the rest of the Heathen to be gathered in; and ye are stones in their way: they have a wish to come; they stumble, and so return.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:133
verses.text: For they say in their hearts, Why should we leave the gods whom the very Christians worship as we do? God forbid, thou wilt say, that I should worship the gods of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:134
verses.text: I know, I understand, I believe thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:135
verses.text: But what account art thou making of the consciences of the weak which thou art 			 wounding? What account art thou making of their price, if thou disregard the purchase? Consider for how great a price was the purchase made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:136
verses.text: "Through thy knowledge," saith the Apostle, "shall the weak brother perish;" that knowledge which thou professest to have, in that thou knowest that an idol is nothing, and that in thy mind thou art thinking only of God, and so sittest down in the idol's temple.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:137
verses.text: In this knowledge the weak brother perisheth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:138
verses.text: And lest thou shouldest pay no regard 			 to the weak brother, he added, "for whom Christ died".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:139
verses.text: If thou wouldest disregard him, yet consider his Price, and weigh the whole world in the balance with the Blood of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:140
verses.text: And lest thou shouldest still think that thou art sinning against a weak brother, and so esteem it after that he had heard that he was "Peter," a trivial fault, and of small account, he saith, "Ye sin against Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:141
verses.text: For men are in the habit of saying, I sin against man; am I sinning against God?" Deny 			 then that Christ is God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:142
verses.text: Dost thou dare deny that Christ is God? Hast thou learned this other doctrine, when thou didst sit at meat in the idol's temple? The school of Christ doth not admit that doctrine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:143
verses.text: I ask; Where learnedst thou that Christ is not God? The Pagans are wont to say so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:144
verses.text: Seest thou what bad associations do? Seest thou, "that evil communications corrupt good manners?" There thou canst not speak of the Gospel, and thou dost hear others talking of idols.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:145
verses.text: There thou losest the truth that Christ is God; and what thou dost drink in there, thou vomitest out in the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:146
verses.text: It may be thou art bold enough to speak here; bold enough to mutter among the crowds; "Was not then Christ a man? Was He not crucified?" This hast thou learned of the Pagans.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:147
verses.text: Thou hast lost thy soul's health, thou hast not touched the border.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:148
verses.text: On this point then touch again 			 the border, and receive health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:149
verses.text: As I taught thee to touch it in this that is written, "Whoso seeth a brother sit at meat in the idol's temple;" touch it also concerning the Divinity of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:150
verses.text: The same border said of the Jews, "Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:151
verses.text: Behold, against Whom, even the Very God, thou dost sin, when thou sittest down with false gods.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:152
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:153
verses.text: It is no god, you will say; because it is the tutelary genius of Carthage.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:154
verses.text: As though if it were Mars or Mercury, it would be a god.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:155
verses.text: But consider in what light it is esteemed by them; not what it is in itself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:156
verses.text: For I know also as well as thou, that it is but a stone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:157
verses.text: If this "genius" be any ornament, let the citizens of Carthage live well; and they themselves will be this "genius" of Carthage.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:158
verses.text: But if the "genius" be a devil, ye have heard in that same 			 Scripture, "The things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God; and I would not that ye should have fellowship with devils".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:159
verses.text: We know well that it is no God; would that they knew it too! but because of those weak ones who do not know it, their conscience ought not to be wounded.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:160
verses.text: It is this that the Apostle warns us of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:161
verses.text: For that they regard that statue as something divine, and take it for a god, the altar is witness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:162
verses.text: What does the altar there, if it be not accounted a god? Let no one tell me; it is no deity, it is no God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:163
verses.text: I have said already, "Would that they only knew this, as 			 we all do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:164
verses.text: But how they regard it, for what they take it, and what they do about it, that altar is witness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:165
verses.text: It is convincing against the intentions of all who worship there, grant that it may not be convincing also against those who sit at meat with them!  11.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:166
verses.text: Yes, let not Christians press the Church, if the Pagans do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:167
verses.text: She is the Body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:168
verses.text: Were we not saying, that the Body of Christ was pressed, and not touched.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:169
verses.text: He endured those who pressed Him; and was looking out for those who "touched" Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:170
verses.text: And, Brethren, I would that if the Body of Christ be pressed by Pagans, by whom it is wont to be pressed; that at least Christians would not press the Body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:171
verses.text: Brethren, it is my business to speak to you, my 			 business it is to speak to Christians; "For what have I to do to judge them that are without?" the Apostle himself saith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:172
verses.text: Them we address in another way, as being weak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:173
verses.text: With them we must deal softly, that they may hear the truth; in you the corruption must be cut out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:174
verses.text: If ye ask whereby the Pagans are to be gained over, whereby they are to be illuminated, and called to salvation; forsake their solemnities, forsake their trifling shows; and then if they do not consent to our truth, let them blush at their own scantiness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:175
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:176
verses.text: If he who is over thee be a good man, he is thy nourisher; if a bad man, he is thy tempter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:177
verses.text: Receive the nourishment in the one case with gladness, and in the temptation show thyself approved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:178
verses.text: Be thou gold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:179
verses.text: Regard this world as the furnace of the goldsmith; in one narrow place are there things, gold, chaff, fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:180
verses.text: To the two former the fire is applied, the chaff is burned, and the gold purified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:181
verses.text: A man has yielded to threats, and been led away to the idol's 			 temple: Alas! I bewail the chaff; I see the ashes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:182
verses.text: Another has not yet yielded to threats nor terrors; has been brought before the judge, and stood firm in his confession, and has not bent down to the idol image: what does the flame with him? Does it not purify the gold? Stand, fast then, Brethren, in the Lord; greater in power, is He who hath called you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:183
verses.text: Be not afraid of the threats of the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:184
verses.text: Bear with your enemies; in them ye have those for whom ye may pray; let them by no means terrify 			 you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:185
verses.text: This is saving health, draw out in this feast here from this source; here drink that wherewith ye may be satisfied, and not in those other feasts, that only whereby ye may be maddened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:186
verses.text: Stand fast in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:187
verses.text: Ye are silver, ye shall be gold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:188
verses.text: This similitude is not our own, it is out of Holy Scripture.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:189
verses.text: Ye have read and heard, "As gold in the furnace hath He tried them, and received them as a burnt-offering".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:190
verses.text: See what ye shall be among the treasures of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:191
verses.text: Be ye rich as touching God, not as if to make Him rich, but as to become rich from Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:192
verses.text: Let Him replenish you; admit nought else into your heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:193
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:194
verses.text: Do we lift up ourselves unto pride, or tell you to be despisers against the powers ordained? Not so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:195
verses.text: Do ye again who are sick on this point, touch also that border of the garment? The Apostle himself saith, "Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers, for there is no power but of God, the powers that be are ordained of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:196
verses.text: He then who resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:197
verses.text: But what if it enjoin what thou oughtest not to do? In this case by all means disregard the power through fear of Power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:198
verses.text: Consider these several grades of human powers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:199
verses.text: If the magistrate enjoin anything, must it not be done? Yet if his order be in opposition to the Proconsul, thou dost not surely despise the power, but choosest to obey a greater power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:200
verses.text: Nor in this case ought the less to be angry, if the greater be preferred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:201
verses.text: Again, if the Proconsul himself enjoin anything, and the Emperor another thing, is there any doubt, that disregarding the former, we ought to obey the latter? So then if the Emperor enjoin one thing, and God another, what judge ye? Pay me 			 tribute, submit thyself to my allegiance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:202
verses.text: Right, but not in an idol's temple.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:203
verses.text: In an idol's temple He forbids it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:204
verses.text: Who forbids it? A greater Power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:205
verses.text: Pardon me then: thou threatenest a prison, He threateneth hell.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:206
verses.text: Here must thou at once take to thee thy "faith as a shield, whereby thou mayest be able to quench all the fiery darts of the enemy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:207
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:208
verses.text: But one of these powers is plotting, and contriving evil designs against thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:209
verses.text: Well: he is but sharpening the razor wherewith to shave the hair, but not to cut the head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:210
verses.text: Ye have but just now heard this that I have said in the Psalm, "Thou hast worked deceit like a sharp razor".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:211
verses.text: Why did He compare the deceit of a wicked man in power to a razor? Because it does not reach, save to our superfluous parts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:212
verses.text: As hairs on our body seem as it were superfluous, and are shaven off without any loss of the flesh; so whatsoever an angry man in power can take from thee, count only among thy superfluities.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:213
verses.text: He takes away thy poverty; can he take away thy wealth? Thy poverty is thy wealth in thy heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:214
verses.text: Thy superfluous things only hath he power to take away, these only 			 hath he power to injure, even though he had license given him so far as to hurt the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:215
verses.text: Yea even this life itself to those whose thoughts are of another life, this present life, I say, may be reckoned among the things superfluous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:216
verses.text: For so the Martyrs have despised it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:217
verses.text: They did not lose life, but they gained Life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:218
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:219
verses.text: Be sure, Brethren, that enemies have no power against the faithful, except so far as it profiteth them to be tempted and proved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:220
verses.text: Of this be sure, Brethren, let no one say ought against it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:221
verses.text: Cast all your care upon the Lord, throw yourselves wholly and entirely upon Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:222
verses.text: He will not withdraw Himself that ye should fall.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:223
verses.text: He who created us, hath given us security touching our very hairs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:224
verses.text: "Verily I say unto you, even the hairs of your head are all numbered".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:225
verses.text: Our hairs are numbered by God; how much more is our conduct known to Him to whom our hairs are thus known? See then, how that God doth not disregard our least things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:226
verses.text: For if He disregarded them, He would not create them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:227
verses.text: For He verily both created our hairs, and still taketh count of them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:228
verses.text: But thou wilt say, though they are preserved at present, perhaps they will perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:229
verses.text: On this point also hear His word, "Verily I say unto you, there shall not an hair of your head perish".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:230
verses.text: Why art thou afraid of man, O man, whose place is in the Bosom of God? Fall not out of His Bosom; whatsoever thou shall suffer there, will avail to thy salvation, not to thy destruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:231
verses.text: Martyrs have endured the tearing of their limbs, and shall Christians fear the injuries of Christian times? He who would do thee an injury now, can only do it in fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:232
verses.text: He does not say openly, come to the idol-feast; he does not say openly, come to my altars, and banquet there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:233
verses.text: And if he should 			 say so, and thou wast to refuse, let him make a complaint of it, let him bring it as an accusation and charge against thee: "He would not come to my altars, he would not come to my temple, where I worship".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:234
verses.text: Let him say this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:235
verses.text: He does not dare; but in his guile he contrives another attack.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:236
verses.text: Make ready thy hair; he is sharpening the razor; he is about to take off thy superfluous things, to shave what thou must soon leave behind thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:237
verses.text: Let him take off what shall endure, if he can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:238
verses.text: This powerful 			 enemy, what has he taken away? what great thing has he taken away? That which a thief or housebreaker could take: in his utmost rage, he can but take what a robber can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:239
verses.text: Even if he should have license given him to the slaying of the very body, what does he take away, but what the robber can take? I did him too much honour, when I said, "a robber".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:240
verses.text: For be the robber who and what he may, he is a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:241
verses.text: He takes from thee what a fever, or an adder, or a poisonous mushroom can take.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:242
verses.text: Here lies the 			 whole power of the rage of men, to do what a mushroom can! Men eat a poisonous mushroom, and they die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:243
verses.text: Lo! in what frail estate is the life of man; which sooner or later thou must abandon; do not struggle then in such wise for it, as that thou shouldest be abandoned thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:244
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:245
verses.text: Christ is our Life; think then of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:246
verses.text: He came to suffer, but also to be glorified; to be despised, but to be exalted also; to die; but also to rise again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:247
verses.text: If the labour alarm thee, see its reward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:248
verses.text: Why dost thou wish to arrive by softness at that to which nothing but hard labour can lead? Now thou art afraid, lest thou shouldest lose thy money; because thou earnest thy money with great labour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:249
verses.text: If thou didst not attain to thy money, which thou must some time or 			 other lose, at all events when thou diest, without labour, wouldest thou desire without labour to attain to the Life eternal? Let that be of higher value in thine eyes, to which after all thy labours thou shalt in such sort attain as never more to lose it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:250
verses.text: If this money, to which thou hast attained after all thy labours on such condition as that thou must some time lose it, be of high value with thee; how much more ought we to long after those things which are everlasting!  17.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:251
verses.text: Give no credit to their words, neither be afraid of them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:252
verses.text: They say that we are enemies of their idols.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:253
verses.text: May God so grant, and give all into our power, as He hath already given us that which we have broken down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:254
verses.text: For this I say, Beloved, that ye may not attempt to do it, when it is not lawfully in your power to do it; for it is the way of ill-regulated men, and the mad Circumcelliones, both to be violent when they have no power, and to be ever eager in their wishes to die without a cause.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:255
verses.text: Ye heard what we read to you, all of you who were present in the Mappalia.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:256
verses.text: "When the land shall have been given into your power" (he saith first, "into your power," and so enjoined what was to be done); "then," saith he, "ye shall destroy their altars, and break in pieces their groves, and hew down all their images".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:257
verses.text: When we shall have got the power, do this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:258
verses.text: When the power has not been given us, we do not do it; when it is given, we do not neglect it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:259
verses.text: Many Pagans have these abominations on their own estates; do we go and break them in pieces? No, for our first efforts are that the idols in their hearts should be broken down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:260
verses.text: When they too are made Christians themselves, they either invite us to so good a work, or anticipate us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:261
verses.text: At present we must pray for them, not be 			 angry with them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:262
verses.text: If very painful feelings excite us, it is rather against Christians, it is against our brethren, who will enter into the Church in such a mind, as to have their body there, and their heart anywhere else.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:263
verses.text: The whole ought to be within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:264
verses.text: If that which man seeth is within, why is that which God seeth without?  18.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:265
verses.text: Now ye may know, Dearly Beloved, that these unite their murmurings with Heretics and with Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:266
verses.text: Heretics, Jews, and Heathens have made a unity against Unity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:267
verses.text: Because it has happened, that in some places the Jews have received chastisement because of their wickednesses; they charge and suspect us, or pretend, that we are always seeking the like treatment for them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:268
verses.text: Again, because it has happened that the heretics in some places have suffered the penalty of the laws for the impiety and fury of their deeds of violence; they say immediately that we are seeking by every means some harm for their destruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:269
verses.text: Again, because it has been resolved that laws should be passed against the Heathen, yea for them rather, if they were only wise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:270
verses.text: (For as when silly boys are playing with the mud, and dirtying their hands, the strict master comes, shakes the mud out of their hands, and holds out their 			 book; so has it pleased God by the hands of princes His subjects to alarm their childish, foolish hearts, that they may throw away the dirt from their hands, and set about something useful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:271
verses.text: And what is this something useful with the hands, but, "Break thy bread to the hungry, and bring the houseless poor into thy house"? But nevertheless these children escape from their master's sight, and return stealthily to their mud, and when they are discovered they hide their hands that they may not be seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:272
verses.text: ) Because then it has so pleased God, they think that we are looking out for the idols everywhere, and that we break them down in all places where we have discovered them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:273
verses.text: How so? Are there not places before our very eyes in which they are? Or are we indeed ignorant where they are? And yet we do not 			 break them down, because God has not given them into our power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:274
verses.text: When does God give them into our power? When the masters of these things shall become Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:275
verses.text: The master of a certain place has just lately wished this to be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:276
verses.text: If he had not been minded to give the place itself to the Church, and only had given orders that there should be no idols on his property; I think that it ought to have been executed with the greatest devotion, that the soul of the absent Christian brother, who 			 wishes on his land to return thanks to God, and would not that there should be anything there to God's dishonour, might be assisted by his fellow-Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:277
verses.text: Added to this, that in this case he gave the place itself to the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:278
verses.text: And shall there be idols in the Church's estate? Brethren, see then what it is that displeases the Heathens.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:279
verses.text: It is but a little matter with them that we do not take them away from their estates, that we do not break them down: they would have them kept up even in 			 our own places.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:280
verses.text: We preach against idols, we take them away from the hearts of men; we are persecutors of idols; we openly profess it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 11:281
verses.text: Are we then to be the preservers of them? I do not touch them when I have not the power; I do not touch them when the lord of the property complains of it; but when he wishes it to be done, and gives thanks for it, I should incur guilt if I did it not.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:1
verses.text: Sermon XIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:2
verses.text: [LXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:5
verses.text: viii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:6
verses.text: 23, "And when he was entered into a boat," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:8
verses.text: By the Lord's blessing, I will address you upon the lesson of the Holy Gospel which has just been read, and take occasion thereby to exhort you, that against the tempest and waves of this world, faith sleep not in your hearts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:9
verses.text: "For the Lord Christ had not indeed death nor sleep in His power, and peradventure sleep overcame the Almighty One as He was sailing against His will?" If ye believe this, He is asleep in you; but if Christ be 			 awake in you, your faith is awake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:10
verses.text: The Apostle saith, "that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:11
verses.text: This sleep then of Christ is a sign of a high mystery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:12
verses.text: The sailors are the souls passing over the world in wood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:13
verses.text: That ship also was a figure of the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:14
verses.text: And all, individually indeed are temples of God, and his own heart is the vessel in which each sails; nor can he suffer shipwreck, if his thoughts are only good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:16
verses.text: Thou hast heard an insult, it is the wind; thou art angry, it is a wave.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:17
verses.text: When therefore the wind blows, and the wave swells, the ship is endangered, the heart is in jeopardy, the heart is tossed to and fro.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:18
verses.text: When thou hast heard an insult, thou longest to be avenged; and, lo, avenged thou hast been, and so rejoicing in another's harm thou hast suffered shipwreck.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:19
verses.text: And why is this? Because Christ is asleep in thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:20
verses.text: What does this mean, Christ is 			 asleep in thee? Thou hast forgotten Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:21
verses.text: Rouse Him up then, call Christ to mind, let Christ awake in thee, give heed to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:22
verses.text: What didst thou wish? To be avenged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:23
verses.text: Hast thou forgotten, that when He was being crucified, He said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do?" He who was asleep in thy heart did not wish to be avenged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:24
verses.text: Awake Him up then, call Him to remembrance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:25
verses.text: The remembrance of Him is His word; the remembrance of Him is His command.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:26
verses.text: And then wilt thou say if Christ, awake in thee, What manner of man am I, who wish to be avenged! Who am I, who deal out threatenings against another man? I may die perhaps before I am avenged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:27
verses.text: And when at my last breath, inflamed with rage, and thirsting for vengeance, I shall depart out of this body, 			 He will not receive me, who did not wish to be avenged; He will not receive me, who said, "Give, and it shall be given unto you; forgive, and it shall be forgiven you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:28
verses.text: Therefore will I refrain myself from my wrath, and return to the repose of my heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:29
verses.text: Christ hath commanded the sea, tranquillity is restored.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:31
verses.text: Now what I have said as to anger, hold fast as a rule in all your temptations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:32
verses.text: A temptation has sprung up; it is the wind; thou art disturbed; it is a wave.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:33
verses.text: Awake up Christ then, let Him speak with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:34
verses.text: "Who is this, since the winds and the sea obey Him?" Who is this, whom the sea obeyeth? "The sea is His, and He made it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:35
verses.text: "All things were made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:36
verses.text: Imitate the winds then, and the sea rather; obey the Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:37
verses.text: At Christ's command the sea giveth ear; and art thou deaf? The sea heareth, and the wind ceaseth: and dost thou still blow on? What! I say, I do, I devise; what is all this, but to be blowing on, and to be unwilling to stop in obedience to the word of Christ? Let not the wave master you in this troubled state of your heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:38
verses.text: Yet since we are but men, if the wind should drive us on, and stir up the affections of our 			 souls, let us not despair; let us awake Christ, that we may sail on a tranquil sea, and so come to our country.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 12:39
verses.text: "Let us turn to the Lord," etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:1
verses.text: Sermon XIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:2
verses.text: [LXIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:5
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:6
verses.text: 16, "Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:7
verses.text: Delivered on a Festival of Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:9
verses.text: When the Holy Gospel was read, Brethren, ye heard how our Lord Jesus Christ strengthened His Martyrs by His teaching, saying, "Behold, I send you forth as lambs in the midst of wolves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:10
verses.text: Now consider, my Brethren, what he does.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:11
verses.text: If but one wolf come among many sheep, be they ever so many thousands, they will all be put to confusion by one wolf in the midst of them: and though all may not be torn, yet all are frightened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:12
verses.text: What manner of design is this then, what manner of counsel, what manner of power, not to let in a wolf amongst the sheep, but to send the sheep against the wolves! "I send you," saith He, "as sheep in the midst of wolves;" not to the 			 neighbourhood of wolves, but "in the midst of wolves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:13
verses.text: There was then at that time a herd of wolves, and but few sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:14
verses.text: For when the many wolves killed the few sheep, the wolves were changed and became sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:16
verses.text: Let us hear then what advice He hath given, who hath promised the crown, but hath first appointed the combat; who is a spectator of the combatants, and assisteth them in their toil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:17
verses.text: What manner of conflict hath He prescribed? "Be ye," saith He, "wise as serpents, and simple as doves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:18
verses.text: Whoso understandeth, and holdeth to this, may die in assurance that he will not really die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:19
verses.text: For no one ought to die in this assurance, but he who knows that he shall in such sort die, as that death only shall die in him, and life be crowned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:21
verses.text: Wherefore, Beloved, I must explain to you, though I have often spoken already on this subject, what it is to be "simple as doves, and wise as serpents".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:22
verses.text: Now if the simplicity of doves be enjoined us, what hath the wisdom of the serpent to do in the simplicity of the dove? This in the dove I love, that she has no gall; this I fear in the serpent, that he has poison.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:23
verses.text: But now do not fear the serpent altogether; something he has for thee to hate, and something 			 for thee to imitate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:24
verses.text: For when the serpent is weighed down with age, and he feels the burden of his many years, he contracts and forces himself into a hole, and lays aside his old coat of skin, that he may spring forth into new life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:25
verses.text: Imitate him in this, thou Christian, who dost hear Christ saying, "Enter ye in at the strait gate".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:26
verses.text: And the Apostle Paul saith to thee, "Put ye off the old man with his deeds, and put ye on the new man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:27
verses.text: Thou hast then something to imitate in the serpent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:28
verses.text: Die not for the "old man," but for the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:29
verses.text: Whoso dies for any temporal good dies "for the old man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:30
verses.text: But when thou hast stripped thyself of all "that old man," thou hast imitated the wisdom of the serpent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:31
verses.text: Imitate him in this again; "keep thy head safe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:32
verses.text: And what does this mean, keep thy head safe? Keep Christ with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:33
verses.text: Have not some of you, it may be, observed, on occasions when 			 you have wished to kill an adder, how to save his head, he will expose his whole body to the strokes of his assailant? He would not that that part of him should be struck, where he knows that his life resides.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:34
verses.text: And our Life is Christ, for He hath said Himself, "I am the way, and the truth, and the life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:35
verses.text: Here the Apostle also; "The Head of the man is Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:36
verses.text: Whoso then keepeth Christ in him, keepeth his head for his protection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:37
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:38
verses.text: Now what need is there to commend to you in many words the simplicity of the dove? For the serpent's poison had need to be guarded against: there, there was a danger in imitation; there, there was something to be feared; but the dove may you imitate securely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:39
verses.text: Mark how the doves rejoice in society; everywhere do they fly and feed together; they do not love to be alone, they delight in communion, they preserve affection; their cooings are the plaintive cries 			  of love, with kissings they beget their young.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:40
verses.text: Yea even when doves, as we have often noticed, dispute about their holes, it is as it were but a peaceful strife.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:41
verses.text: Do they separate, because of their contentions? Nay, still do they fly and feed together, and their very strife is peaceful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:42
verses.text: See this strife of doves, in what the Apostle saith, "If any man obey not our word by this epistle, mark that man, and have no company with him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:43
verses.text: Behold the strife; but observe now how it is 			 the strife of doves, not of wolves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:44
verses.text: He subjoined immediately, "Yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:45
verses.text: The dove loves even when she is in strife; and the wolf even when he caresses, hates.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:46
verses.text: Therefore having the simplicity of doves, and the wisdom of serpents, celebrate the solemnities of the Martyrs in sobriety of mind, not in bodily excess, sing lauds to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:47
verses.text: For He who is the Martyrs' God, is our Lord God also, He it is who will crown us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 13:48
verses.text: If we shall have wrestled well, we shall be crowned by Him, who hath crowned already those whom we desire to imitate.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:1
verses.text: Sermon XV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:2
verses.text: [LXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:5
verses.text: x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:6
verses.text: 28, "Be not afraid of them that kill the body".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:7
verses.text: Delivered on a Festival of Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:9
verses.text: The Divine oracles which have just been read teach us in fearing not to fear, and in not fearing to fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:10
verses.text: Ye observed when the Holy Gospel was being read, that our Lord God before He died for us, would have us to be firm; and this by admonishing us "not" to fear, and withal to fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:11
verses.text: For he said, "Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:12
verses.text: See where He advised us not to fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:13
verses.text: See now where He advised us 			 to fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:14
verses.text: "But," saith he, "fear Him who hath power to destroy both body and soul in hell".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:15
verses.text: Let us fear therefore, that we may not fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:16
verses.text: Fear seems to be allied to cowardice: seems to be the character of the weak, not the strong.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:17
verses.text: But see what saith the Scripture, "The fear of the Lord is the hope of strength".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:18
verses.text: Let us then fear, that we may not fear; that is, let us fear prudently, that we may not fear vainly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:19
verses.text: The holy Martyrs on the occasion of whose solemnity this lesson was read out of the Gospel, in fearing, feared not; because in fearing God, they did not regard men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:21
verses.text: For what need a man fear from man? And what is that whereby one man should cause another fear, since both of them are men? One threatens and says, "I will kill thee;" and does not fear, lest after his threat he die before he have fulfilled it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:22
verses.text: "I will kill thee," he says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:23
verses.text: Who says it, and to whom? I hear two men, the one threatening, and the other alarmed: of whom the one is powerful, and the other weak, yet both are mortal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:24
verses.text: Why then does he so stretch out 			 himself, he, in honour, a somewhat more inflated power, in body, equal weakness? Let him securely threaten death who does not fear death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:25
verses.text: But if he fear that whereby he causes fear; let him think of himself, and compare himself with him whom he is threatening.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:26
verses.text: Let him see in him whom he threateneth a likeness of condition, and so together with him let him seek like pity from the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:27
verses.text: For he is but a man, and he threatens another man, a creature, another creature; only the one puffed up under 			 his Creator's eye, and the other fleeing for refuge to the same Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:28
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:29
verses.text: Let the stout Martyr then, as he stands a man before another man, say; "I do not fear, because I fear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:30
verses.text: Thou canst not do what thou art threatening, unless He will; but what He threateneth, none can hinder Him from doing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:31
verses.text: And then again, what dost thou threaten, and what canst thou do, if thou art permitted? Thy violence extends but to the flesh, the soul is safe from thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:32
verses.text: Thou canst not kill what thou dost not see: visible thyself, thou threatenest 			 that which is visible in me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:33
verses.text: But we have both an invisible Creator, whom we ought both to fear; who of that which was both visible and invisible created man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:34
verses.text: He made Him visible out of the earth, and with His Breath He breathed into Him an invisible Spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:35
verses.text: Therefore the invisible substance, that is, the soul, which has raised from the earth the earth as it lay, does not fear, when thou assaultest the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:36
verses.text: Thou canst strike the habitation, but canst thou strike him who dwells there? When the 			 chain is broken, he escapes who before was bound, and he will now be crowned in secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:37
verses.text: Why then dost thou threaten me, who canst do nothing to my soul? Through the desert of that to which thou canst do nothing, will that to which thy power extends rise again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:38
verses.text: For through the soul's desert, will the flesh also rise again; and will be restored to its inhabitant, now no more to fail, but to endure for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:39
verses.text: Behold (I am using the words of a Martyr), behold, I say, not even on account of my body 			 do I fear thy threats.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:40
verses.text: My body indeed is subject to thy power; but even the hairs of my head are numbered by my Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:41
verses.text: Why should I fear lest I lose my body, who cannot even lose a hair? How shall he not have a care of my body, to whom my meanest things are so well known? This body which may be wounded and slain will for a time be ashes, but it will be for ever immortal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:42
verses.text: But to whom shall this be? To whom shall the body be restored for life eternal, even though it have been slain, destroyed, 			 and scattered to the winds? to whom shall it be so restored? To him who has not been afraid to lay down his own life, since he does not fear, lest his body should be slain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:43
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:44
verses.text: For, Brethren, the soul is said to be immortal, and immortal it is according to a certain manner of its own: for it is a kind of life which is able to give life to the body by its presence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:45
verses.text: For by the soul doth the body live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:46
verses.text: This life cannot die, and therefore is the soul immortal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:47
verses.text: Why then said I according to a certain manner of its own? Hear why.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:48
verses.text: Because there is a true immortality, an immortality which is an entire unchangeableness; of which the Apostle 			 saith, speaking of God, "Who only hath immortality, dwelling in that light which no man may approach unto, whom no man hath seen, nor can see, to whom be honour and glory for ever and ever, Amen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:49
verses.text: If then God only hath immortality, the soul must needs be mortal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:50
verses.text: See then why it was that I said that the soul is immortal after a certain manner of its own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:51
verses.text: For in fact it may also die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:52
verses.text: Understand this, Beloved, and there will remain no difficulty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:53
verses.text: I venture to say then that the soul can die, can be slain also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:54
verses.text: Yet it is undoubtedly immortal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:55
verses.text: See, I venture to say, it is at once immortal, and it may be slain; and therefore I said that there is a kind of immortality, an 			 entire unchangeableness, that is, which God Only hath, of whom it is said, "Who Only hath immortality;" for if the soul cannot be slain, how did the Lord Himself say, when He would make us fear, "Fear Him who hath power to slay both body and soul in hell"?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:56
verses.text: Hitherto I have confirmed, not solved, the difficulty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:57
verses.text: I have proved that the soul can be slain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:58
verses.text: The Gospel cannot be gainsaid but by the ungodly soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:59
verses.text: Lo, something occurs to me here, and comes into my mind to speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:60
verses.text: Life cannot be gainsaid, but by a dead soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:61
verses.text: The Gospel is life, impiety and infidelity are the death of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:62
verses.text: See then, it can die, and yet it is immortal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:63
verses.text: How then is it immortal? Because there is always a sort of life which is never extinguished in 			 it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:64
verses.text: And how does it die? Not in ceasing to be life, but by losing its life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:65
verses.text: For the soul is both life to something else, and it has its own proper life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:66
verses.text: Consider the order of the creatures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:67
verses.text: The soul is the life of the body: God is the life of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:68
verses.text: As the life, that is the soul, is present with the body, that the body die not; so ought the life of the soul, that is God, to be with it that the soul die not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:69
verses.text: How does the body die? By the soul's leaving it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:70
verses.text: I say, by the soul's leaving it 			 the body dies; and it lies along a mere carcass, what was a little before a desirable, now a contemptible, object.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:71
verses.text: There are in it still its several members, the eyes, and ears; but these are but the windows of the house, its inhabitant is gone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:72
verses.text: They who bewail the dead, cry in vain at the windows of the house; there is none within to hear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:73
verses.text: How many things does the fond affection of the mourner give utterance to, how many enumerate and call to mind; and with what a madness of sorrow, so to say, 			 does he speak, as with one who was sensible of what was doing, when he is really speaking with one who is no longer there? He recounts his good qualities, and the tokens of his goodness towards himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:74
verses.text: It was thou that didst give me this; and did this and that for me; it was thou who didst thus and thus dearly love me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:75
verses.text: But if thou wouldest only consider and understand, and restrain the madness of thy grief, he who once loved thee, is gone; in vain does the house receive thy knockings, in which 			 thou canst not find a dweller.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:76
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:77
verses.text: Let us return to the subject I was speaking of a little while since.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:78
verses.text: The body is dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:79
verses.text: Why? Because its life, that is the soul, is gone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:80
verses.text: Again, the body is alive, and the man is impious, unbelieving, hard of belief, incorrigible; in this case whilst the body is alive, the soul by which the body lives is dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:81
verses.text: For the soul is so excellent a thing, that it has power even though dead to give life to the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:82
verses.text: So excellent a thing, I say, is the soul, so 			 excellent a creature, that even though dead itself, it has power to quicken the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:83
verses.text: For the soul of the impious, unbelieving, unregulated man is dead, and yet by it though dead the body lives.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:84
verses.text: And therefore is it in the body; it sets on the hands to work, and the feet to walk; it directs the eye to see, it disposes the ears to hear, it discriminates tastes, avoids pains, seeks after pleasures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:85
verses.text: All these are tokens of the life of the body; but they are from the presence of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:86
verses.text: If I were 			 to ask a body whether it were alive; it would answer me, You see me walking, you see me working, you hear me talking, you perceive that I have certain aims and aversions, and do you not understand that the body is alive? By these works then of the soul which is placed within, I understand that the body is alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:87
verses.text: I ask the soul also whether it is alive? It also has its proper works, by which it manifests its life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:88
verses.text: The feet walk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:89
verses.text: I understand by this that the body lives, but by the presence of 			 the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:90
verses.text: I ask now, does the soul live? These feet walk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:91
verses.text: (To speak only of this one movement.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:92
verses.text: ) I am questioning both body and soul, as touching their life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:93
verses.text: The feet walk, I understand that the body lives.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:94
verses.text: But whither do they walk? To adultery, it is said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:95
verses.text: Then is the soul dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:96
verses.text: For so hath unerring Scripture said, "The widow who liveth in pleasure is dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:97
verses.text: Now since the difference is great between "pleasure" and adultery, how can the soul which is said to be dead in pleasure, live in adultery? It is surely dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:98
verses.text: But it is dead even though it be not in this case.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:99
verses.text: I hear a man speaking; the body then lives.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:100
verses.text: For the tongue could not move itself in the mouth, and by its several motions give utterance to articulate sounds, were there not an inhabitant within; and a musician as it were to this instrument, to make use of his 			 tongue.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:101
verses.text: I understand it perfectly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:102
verses.text: Thus the body speaks; the body then lives.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:103
verses.text: But I ask, is the soul alive also? Lo, the body speaks, and so is alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:104
verses.text: But what does it speak? As I said concerning the feet; they walk, and so the body is alive, and I then asked, whither do they walk? that I might understand whether the soul was alive also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:105
verses.text: So also when I hear a man speak, I understand that the body is alive; I ask what does he speak, that I may know whether the soul is alive also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:106
verses.text: He speaks a 			 lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:107
verses.text: If so, then is the soul dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:108
verses.text: How do we prove this? Let us ask the truth itself, which saith, "The mouth that lieth, slayeth the soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:109
verses.text: I ask, why is the soul dead? I ask as I did just now, why is the body dead? Because the soul, its life, was gone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:110
verses.text: Why is the soul dead? Because God, its life, hath forsaken it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:111
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:112
verses.text: After this brief examination then, know and hold for certain that the body is dead without the soul, and that the soul is dead without God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:113
verses.text: Every man without God hath a dead soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:114
verses.text: Thou dost bewail the dead: bewail the sinner rather, bewail rather the ungodly man, bewail the unbeliever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:115
verses.text: It is written, "The mourning for the dead is seven days; for a fool and an ungodly man all the days of his life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:116
verses.text: What! are there no bowels of Christian compassion in thee; that thou mournest for a body from which the soul is gone, and mournest not for the soul, from which God is departed? Let the Martyr remembering this make answer to him that threatens him, "Why dost thou force me to deny Christ?" Wouldest thou then force me to deny the truth? And if I will not, what wilt thou do? Thou wilt assault my body, that my soul shall depart from it; but this same soul of mine has its body 			 only for the soul's sake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:117
verses.text: It is not so foolish or unwise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:118
verses.text: Thou wouldest wound my body; but wouldest thou, that through fear lest thou shouldest wound my body, and my soul should depart from it, I should wound mine own soul, and my God should depart from it? Fear not then, O Martyr, the sword of thy executioner; fear only thine own tongue, lest thou do execution upon thine own self, and slay, not thy body, but thy soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:119
verses.text: Fear for thy soul, lest it die in hell-fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:120
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:121
verses.text: Therefore said the Lord, "Who hath power to slay both body and soul in hell-fire".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:122
verses.text: How? when the ungodly shall be cast into hell-fire, will his body and his soul burn there? Everlasting punishment will be the death of the body; the absence of God will be the death of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:123
verses.text: Wouldest thou know what the death of the soul is? Understand the Prophet who saith, "Let the ungodly be taken away, that he may not see the glory of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:124
verses.text: Let the soul then fear its proper death, and not fear the death of its body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:125
verses.text: Because if it fear its own death, and so live in its God, by not offending and thrusting Him away from him, it will be found worthy to receive its body again at the end; not unto everlasting punishment, as the ungodly, but unto life eternal, as the righteous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 14:126
verses.text: By fearing this death, and loving that life, did the Martyrs, in hope of the promises of God, and in contempt of the threats of persecutors, attain themselves to be crowned with God, and have left to us the celebration of these solemnities.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:1
verses.text: Sermon XVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:2
verses.text: [LXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:5
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:6
verses.text: 2, "Now when John heard in the prison the works of the Christ, he sent by his disciples, and said unto him, art thou He that cometh, or look we for another?" etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:8
verses.text: The lesson of the Holy Gospel has set before us a question touching John the Baptist.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:9
verses.text: May the Lord assist me to resolve it to you, as He hath resolved it to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:10
verses.text: John was commended, as ye have heard, by the testimony of Christ, and in such terms commended, as that there had not risen a greater among those who were born of women.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:11
verses.text: But a greater than he had been born of a Virgin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:12
verses.text: How much greater? Let the herald himself declare, how great the 			 difference is between himself and his Judge, whose herald he is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:13
verses.text: For John went before Christ both in his birth and preaching; but it was in obedience that he went before Him; not in preferring himself before Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:14
verses.text: For so the whole train of attendants walks before the judge; yet they who walk before, are really after him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:15
verses.text: How signal a testimony then did John give to Christ? Even to saying that he "was not worthy to loose the latchet of His shoes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:16
verses.text: And what more? "Of His fulness," saith he, "have all we received".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:17
verses.text: He confessed that he was but a lamp lighted at His Light, and so he took refuge at His feet, lest venturing on high, he should be extinguished by the wind of pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:18
verses.text: So great indeed was he, that he was taken for Christ; and if he had not himself testified that he was not He, the mistake would have continued, and he would have been reputed to be the Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:19
verses.text: What striking humility! Honour was proffered him by the people, and he himself refused it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:20
verses.text: Men were at fault in his 			 greatness, and he humbled himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:21
verses.text: He had no wish to increase by the words of men, seeing he had comprehended the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:23
verses.text: This then did John say concerning Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:24
verses.text: And what said Christ of John? We have just now heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:25
verses.text: "He began to say to the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?" Surely not; for John was not "blown about by every wind of doctrine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:26
verses.text: "But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment?" No, for John was clothed in rough apparel; he had his raiment of camel's hair, not of down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:27
verses.text: "But what went ye out for to see? A Prophet? yea, and more than a Prophet".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:28
verses.text: Why "more than a Prophet"? The Prophets foretold that the Lord would come, whom they desired to see, and saw not; but to him was vouchsafed what they sought.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:29
verses.text: John saw the Lord; he saw Him, pointed his finger toward Him, and said, "Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sins of the world;" behold, here He is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:30
verses.text: Now had He come and was not acknowledged; and so a mistake was made also as to John himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:31
verses.text: Behold then here is He whom the Patriarchs desired to see, whom the Prophets foretold, whom the Law prefigured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:32
verses.text: "Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sins of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:33
verses.text: And he gave a goodly testimony to the Lord, and the Lord to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:34
verses.text: "Among them that are born of women," saith the Lord, "there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: 			 notwithstanding, he that is less in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he;" less in time, but greater in majesty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:35
verses.text: This He said, meaning Himself to be understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:36
verses.text: Now exceedingly great among men is John the Baptist, than whom among men Christ alone is greater.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:37
verses.text: It may also be thus stated and explained, "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding, he that is the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:38
verses.text: Not in the sense that I have before explained it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:39
verses.text: "Notwithstanding, he that is the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he;" the kingdom of heaven he meant where the Angels are; he then that is the least among the Angels, is greater than John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:40
verses.text: Thus He set 			 forth to us the excellence of that kingdom which we should long for; set before us a city, of which we should desire to be citizens.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:41
verses.text: What sort of citizens are there? how great are they! Whoso is the least there, is greater than John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:42
verses.text: Than what John? "Than whom there hath not risen a greater among them that are born of women".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:43
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:44
verses.text: Thus have we heard the true and good record both of John concerning Christ, and of Christ concerning John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:45
verses.text: What then is the meaning of this; that John sent his disciples to Him when He was shut up in prison, on the eve of being put to death, and said to them, "Go, say to Him, Art Thou He that should come, or do we look for another?" Is this then all that praise? That praise is it turned to doubting? What sayest thou, John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:46
verses.text: To Whom art thou speaking? What sayest thou? Thou speakest to thy Judge, thyself the herald.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:47
verses.text: Thou stretchedst out the finger, and pointedst Him out; thou saidst, "Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him who taketh away the sins of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:48
verses.text: Thou saidst, "Of His fulness have we all received".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:49
verses.text: Thou saidst, "I am not worthy to unloose the latchet of His shoes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:50
verses.text: And dost 			 thou now say, "Art Thou He that should come, or do we look for another?" Is not this the same Christ? And who art thou? Art thou not His forerunner? Art thou not he of whom it was foretold, "Behold, I send my messenger before Thy face, who shall prepare Thy way before thee?" How dost thou prepare the way, and thou art thyself straying from the way?
