So then the disciples of John came; and the Lord said to them, "Go, tell John, the blind see, the deaf hear, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the poor have the Gospel preached to them; and blessed is he whosoever shall not be offended in Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:51
verses.text: Do not suspect that John was offended in Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:52
verses.text: And yet his words do sound so; "Art Thou He that should come?" Ask my works; "The blind see, the deaf hear, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the dead are raised, the poor have the Gospel preached to them;" and dost thou ask whether I am He? My works, saith He, are My words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:53
verses.text: "Go, show him again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:54
verses.text: And as they departed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:55
verses.text: Lest haply any one should say, John was good at first, and the Spirit of God forsook him; 			 therefore after their departure, he spake these words; after their departure whom John had sent, Christ commended John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:56
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:57
verses.text: What is the meaning then of this obscure question? May that Sun shine upon us, from which that lamp derived its flame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:58
verses.text: And so the resolution of it is altogether plain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:59
verses.text: John had separate disciples of his own; not as in separation from Christ, but prepared as a witness to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:60
verses.text: For meet it was that such an one should give his testimony to Christ, who was himself also gathering disciples, and who might have been envious of Him, for that he could not see Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:61
verses.text: Therefore 			 because John's disciples highly esteemed their master, they heard from John his record concerning Christ, and marvelled; and as he was about to die, it was his wish that they should be confirmed by him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:62
verses.text: For no doubt they were saying among themselves; Such great things doth he say of Him, but none such of himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:63
verses.text: "Go then, ask Him;" not because I doubt, but that ye may be instructed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:64
verses.text: "Go, ask Him," hear from Himself what I am in the habit of telling you; ye have heard the herald, be 			 confirmed by the Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:65
verses.text: "Go, ask Him, Art Thou He that should come, or do we look for another?" They went accordingly and asked; not for John's sake, but for their own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:66
verses.text: And for their sakes did Christ say, "The blind see, the lame walk, the deaf hear, the lepers are cleansed, the dead are raised, the poor have the Gospel preached to them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:67
verses.text: Ye see Me, acknowledge Me then; ye see the works, acknowledge the Doer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:68
verses.text: "And blessed is he whosoever shall not be offended in Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:69
verses.text: But it is of 			 you I speak, not of John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:70
verses.text: For that we might know that He spake not this of John, as they departed, "He began to speak to the multitudes concerning John;" the True, the Truth Himself, proclaimed his true praises.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:71
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:72
verses.text: I think this question has been sufficiently explained.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:73
verses.text: Let it suffice then to have prolonged my address thus far.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:74
verses.text: Now keep the poor in mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:75
verses.text: Give, ye who have not given hitherto; believe me, ye will not lose it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:76
verses.text: Yes, truly, that only it seems ye lose, which ye do not carry to the circus.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:77
verses.text: Now must we render unto the poor the offerings of such of you as have offered anything, and the amount which we have is much less than your usual offerings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:78
verses.text: Shake off this sloth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 15:79
verses.text: I am become a beggar for beggars; what is that to me? I would be a beggar for beggars, that ye may be reckoned among the number of children.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:1
verses.text: Sermon XVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:2
verses.text: [LXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:5
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:6
verses.text: 25, "I thank thee, O Father, Lord of Heaven and Earth, that thou didst hide these things from the wise and understanding," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:8
verses.text: When the Holy Gospel was being read, we heard that the Lord Jesus exulted in Spirit, and said, "I confess to Thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, for that Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:9
verses.text: Thus much to begin with, we find before we pass on further, if we consider the words of the Lord with due attention, with diligence, and above all with piety, that we ought not invariably to understand when we read of "confession" in the Scriptures, the confession of a sinner.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:10
verses.text: Now especial need there was of saying this, and of reminding you, Beloved, of this, because as soon as this word was uttered by the reader's voice, there followed upon it the sound of the beating of your breasts, when ye had heard, I mean, what the Lord said, "I confess to Thee, O Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:11
verses.text: At the uttering of these words, "I confess," ye beat your breasts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:12
verses.text: Now what means this beating of the breast, but to show that which lies hid within the breast, and to 			 chastise by the visible beating the secret sin? And why did ye this, but because ye heard, "I confess to Thee, O Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:13
verses.text: Ye heard the words "I confess," but ye did not consider, who it is that confesses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:14
verses.text: But consider now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:15
verses.text: If Christ, from whom all sin is far removed, said, "I confess:" confession does not belong to the sinner only, but sometimes to him also that praiseth God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:16
verses.text: We confess then, whether in praising God, or accusing ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:17
verses.text: In either case it is a 			 godly confession, either when thou blamest thyself, who art not without sin, or when thou praisest Him who can have no sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:18
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:19
verses.text: But if we consider it well: thine own blame is His praise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:20
verses.text: For why is it that thou dost now confess in accusing thyself for thy sin? in accusing thyself why dost thou confess? but because thou art become alive from the dead? for the Scripture saith, "Confession perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:21
verses.text: If confession perisheth from the dead, he who confesseth must be alive; and if he confesseth sin he hath undoubtedly risen again from death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:22
verses.text: Now if he that confesseth sin hath risen again from the dead, who hath raised him? No dead man can raise himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:23
verses.text: He only was able to raise Himself, who though His Body was dead, was not dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:24
verses.text: For He raised up that which was dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:25
verses.text: He raised up Himself, who in Himself was alive, but in His Body that was to be raised was dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:26
verses.text: For not the 			 Father only, of whom it was said by the Apostle, "Wherefore God also hath exalted Him," raised the Son, but the Lord also raised Himself, that is, His Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:27
verses.text: Whence He said, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it again".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:28
verses.text: But the sinner is dead, especially he whom the load of sinful habit presseth down, who is buried as it were like Lazarus.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:29
verses.text: For he was not merely dead, he was buried also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:30
verses.text: Whosoever then is oppressed by the load of evil habit, of a wicked life, of earthly lusts, I mean, so that that in his case is true which is piteously described in a certain Psalm, "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God," he is such an one, of whom it is said, "Confession perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:31
verses.text: And who shall raise him up, but He who when the stone was removed, cried out, and said, "Lazarus, Come forth?" Now what is to "come forth," but to bring forth what was hidden? He then who confesseth "cometh forth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:32
verses.text: "Come forth" he could not were he not alive; he could not be alive, had he not been raised again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:33
verses.text: And therefore in confession the accusing of one's self, is the praise of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:34
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:35
verses.text: Now one may say, what profit then is the Church, if he that confesseth comes forth, at once raised to life again by the voice of the Lord? What profit to Him that confesseth, is the Church, to which the Lord said, "Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:36
verses.text: Consider this very case of Lazarus: he comes forth, but with his bands.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:37
verses.text: He was alive already through confession, but he did not yet walk free, entangled as he was in his bands.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:38
verses.text: What then doth the Church to which it was said, "Whatsoever ye shall loose, shall be loosed;" but what the Lord said forthwith to His disciples, "Loose him, and let him go"?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:39
verses.text: Whether then we accuse ourselves, or directly praise God, in both ways do we praise God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:40
verses.text: If with a pious intention we accuse ourselves, by so doing we praise God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:41
verses.text: When we praise God directly, we do as it were celebrate His Holiness, who is without sin: but when we accuse ourselves, we give Him glory, by whom we have risen again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:42
verses.text: This if thou shalt do, the enemy will find none occasion whereby to overreach thee before the judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:43
verses.text: For when thou shall be thine own accuser, and the Lord thy Deliverer, what shall he be but a mere calumniator? With good reason hath the Christian hereby provided protection for himself against his enemies, not those that may be seen, flesh and blood, to be pitied, rather than to be feared, but against those against whom the Apostle exhorts us to arm ourselves: "We wrestle not against flesh and blood;" that is, against men whom ye see raging against you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:44
verses.text: They are but vessels, which another uses, they are but instruments which another handles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:45
verses.text: "The devil," saith the Scripture, "entered into the heart of Judas, that he should betray the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:46
verses.text: One may say then, what have I done? Hear the Apostle, "Give not place to the devil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:47
verses.text: Thou hast given him place by an evil will: he entered, and possessed, and now uses thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:48
verses.text: He had not possessed thee, hadst thou not given him place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:49
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:50
verses.text: Therefore doth he warn and say, "We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:51
verses.text: Any one might suppose this meant against the kings of the earth, against the powers of this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:52
verses.text: How so? are they not flesh and blood? And once for all it is said, "not against flesh and blood".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:53
verses.text: Turn thy attention from all men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:54
verses.text: What enemies then remain? "Against principalities and powers of spiritual wickedness, the rulers of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:55
verses.text: It might seem as though he gave the devil and his angels more than they have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:56
verses.text: It is so, he has called them the "rulers of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:57
verses.text: But to prevent misunderstanding, he explains what this world is, of which they are the rulers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:58
verses.text: "The rulers of the world, of this darkness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:59
verses.text: What is, "of the world, of this darkness?" The world is full of those who love it, and of unbelievers, over whom he is ruler.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:60
verses.text: This the Apostle calls darkness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:61
verses.text: This darkness the devil and his 			 angels are the rulers of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:62
verses.text: This is not the natural, and unchangeable darkness: this darkness changes, and becomes light; it believes, and by believing is enlightened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:63
verses.text: When this takes place in it, it will hear the words, "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:64
verses.text: For when ye were darkness, ye were not in the Lord: again, when ye are light, ye are light not in yourselves, but in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:65
verses.text: "For what hast thou which thou hast not received?" Inasmuch then as they are invisible enemies, by invisible means must they be subdued.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:66
verses.text: A visible enemy indeed thou mayest overcome by blows; thy invisible enemy thou conquerest by belief.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:67
verses.text: A man is a visible enemy; to strike a blow is visible also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:68
verses.text: The devil is an invisible enemy; to believe is invisible also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:69
verses.text: Against invisible enemies then there is an invisible fight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:70
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:71
verses.text: From these enemies how can any man say that he is safe? For this I had begun to speak of, but I thought it necessary to treat of these enemies at some little length.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:72
verses.text: But now that we know our enemies, let us see to our defence against them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:73
verses.text: "In praising I will call upon the Lord, so shall I be safe from mine enemies".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:74
verses.text: Thou seest what thou hast to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:75
verses.text: "In praising call;" that is, "in praising the Lord, call".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:76
verses.text: For thou wilt not be safe from thine enemies, if thou praise thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:77
verses.text: "In praising call upon the Lord, and thou shalt be safe from thine enemies".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:78
verses.text: For what doth the Lord Himself say? "The sacrifice of praise shall glorify Me, and there is the way, in which I will show him My salvation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:79
verses.text: Where is the way? In the sacrifice of praise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:80
verses.text: Let not your foot then wander out of this way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:81
verses.text: Keep in the way; depart not from it; from the praise of the Lord depart not a foot, nay, not a nail's breadth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:82
verses.text: For if thou wilt deviate from this way, and praise thyself instead of the Lord, thou wilt not be safe from thine enemies; for it is said of them, "They have laid stumbling-blocks for me by the way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:83
verses.text: Therefore in whatever measure thou thinkest that thou hast good of thine own self, thou hast deviated from the praise of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:84
verses.text: Why dost thou marvel then, if thine enemy seduce thee, when thou art thine own seducer? Hear the Apostle, "For if a man think himself to be something when he is nothing, he seduceth himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:85
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:86
verses.text: Give heed then to the Lord confessing; "I confess to Thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:87
verses.text: I confess to Thee, that is, I praise Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:88
verses.text: I praise Thee, not I accuse myself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:89
verses.text: Now as far as the taking of very man is concerned, all is grace, singular and perfect grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:90
verses.text: What merit had that man who is Christ, if thou take away the grace, even that so pre-eminent grace, whereby it behoved that there should be One Christ, and that He whom we acknowledge should be He? Take away this grace, and what is Christ but a mere man? what but the same as thou art thyself? He took a Soul, He took a Body, He took a perfect Man; He uniteth him to Himself, the Lord maketh one Person with the servant.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:91
verses.text: What pre-eminent grace is this! Christ in heaven, Christ on earth; Christ at once 			 both in heaven and earth; not two Christs, but the same Christ, both in heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:92
verses.text: Christ with the Father, Christ in the Virgin's womb; Christ on the Cross, Christ succouring some souls in hell; and on the self-same day Christ in paradise with the robber who confessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:93
verses.text: And how did the robber attain to this blessedness, but because he held on that way, in which "He showeth His salvation"? That way, from which let not thy foot wander.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:94
verses.text: For in that he accused himself, he praised God, and made his own life blessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:95
verses.text: He looked in hope for this from the Lord, and said to Him, "Lord, remember me when Thou comest into Thy kingdom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:96
verses.text: For he considered his own wicked deeds, and thought it much, if mercy should be shown him even at the last.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:97
verses.text: But the Lord immediately after He had said, "Remember me"—when? "when Thou comest into Thy kingdom," saith, "Verily I say unto thee, Today shall thou be with Me in paradise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:98
verses.text: Mercy offered at once, what misery deferred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:99
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:100
verses.text: Hear then the Lord confessing; "I confess to Thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:101
verses.text: What do I confess? Wherein do I praise thee? For this confession, as I have said before, signifieth praise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:102
verses.text: "Because Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:103
verses.text: What is this, Brethren? Understand by that which is opposed to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:104
verses.text: "Thou hast hid these things," saith he, "from the wise and prudent;" and he did not say, thou hast revealed them to the foolish and imprudent, but "Thou hast hid these things" indeed 			 "from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:105
verses.text: To these wise and prudent, who are really objects of derision, to the arrogant who in false pretence are great, yet in truth are only swollen up, he opposed not the foolish, nor the imprudent, but babes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:106
verses.text: Who are babes? The humble.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:107
verses.text: Therefore "Thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:108
verses.text: Under the name of the wise and prudent, He hath Himself explained that the proud are understood, when 			 He said, "Thou hast revealed them unto babes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:109
verses.text: Therefore from those who are not babes Thou hast hidden them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:110
verses.text: What is from those who are not babes? From those who are not humble.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:111
verses.text: And who are they but the proud? O way of the Lord! Either there was none, or it lay hid, that it might be revealed to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:112
verses.text: Why did the Lord exult? "Because it was revealed unto babes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:113
verses.text: We must be little babes; for if we would wish to be great, "wise and prudent" as it were, it is not revealed unto us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:114
verses.text: Who are 			 these great ones? The wise and prudent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:115
verses.text: "Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:116
verses.text: Here then thou hast a remedy suggested from its opposite.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:117
verses.text: For if by "professing thyself wise, thou art become a fool; profess thyself a fool, and thou wilt be wise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:118
verses.text: But profess it in truth, profess it from the heart, for it is really so as thou professest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:119
verses.text: If thou profess it, do not profess it before men, and forbear to profess it before God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:120
verses.text: As to thyself, and all that is thine, thou art altogether dark.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:121
verses.text: For what else is it to be a fool, but to be dark in heart? He saith 			 of them at last, "Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:122
verses.text: Before they professed this, what do we find? "And their foolish heart was darkened".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:123
verses.text: Acknowledge then that thou art not to thyself a light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:124
verses.text: At best thou art but an eye, thou art not the light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:125
verses.text: And what good is even an open and a sound eye, if the light be wanting? Acknowledge therefore that of thine own self thou art no light to thyself; and cry out as it is written, "Thou, Lord, wilt light my candle: Thou wilt enlighten, O Lord, my darkness with Thy Light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:126
verses.text: For myself I was all darkness; but Thou art the Light that scattereth the darkness, and enlighteneth me; of myself I am no light to myself, yea I have no portion of light but in Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:127
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:128
verses.text: So John also, the friend of the Bridegroom, was thought to be the Christ, was thought to be the Light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:129
verses.text: "He was not that Light, but that he might bear witness of the Light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:130
verses.text: But what was the Light? It was the true Light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:131
verses.text: What is the true Light? "That which lighteneth every man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:132
verses.text: If that be the true Light which lighteneth every man, then it lightened John also, who professed and confessed rightly, "Of His fulness have all we received".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:133
verses.text: See if he said ought else, but "Thou, O Lord, shalt lighten my candle".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:134
verses.text: Finally, being now enlightened, He gave His testimony.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:135
verses.text: For the benefit of the blind the lamp gave witness to the Day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:136
verses.text: See how that He is a lamp; "Ye sent," He said, "unto John, and ye were willing for a season to rejoice in his light; he was a burning and a shining lamp".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:137
verses.text: He, the lamp, that is, a thing enlightened, was lighted that it might shine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:138
verses.text: That which can be lighted can be extinguished also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:139
verses.text: Now that it may not be extinguished, let it not expose itself to the wind of pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:140
verses.text: Therefore, "I confess to Thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent," from those who thought themselves to be light, and were darkness; and who because they were darkness, and thought themselves to be 			 light, could not even be enlightened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:141
verses.text: But they who were darkness, and confessed that they were darkness, were little babes, not great; were humble, not proud.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:142
verses.text: Rightly therefore did they say, "O Lord, Thou wilt lighten my candle".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:143
verses.text: They knew themselves, they praised the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:144
verses.text: They did not stray from the way of salvation; "They in praise called upon the Lord, and they were saved from their enemies".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:145
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 16:146
verses.text: Turning then to the Lord our God, the Father Almighty, in purity of heart, let us render unto Him, as our frailty best can, our highest and abundant thanks, with our whole mind praying His singular goodness, that in His good pleasure He would vouchsafe to hear our prayers, that by His Power He would drive out the enemy from our deeds and thoughts, would enlarge our faith, direct our minds, grant us spiritual thoughts, and bring us safe to His endless blessedness, 			 through His Son Jesus Christ, Amen.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:1
verses.text: Sermon XVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:2
verses.text: [LXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:4
verses.text: ]  Again on the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:5
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:6
verses.text: 25, "I thank thee, O Father, Lord of Heaven and Earth," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:8
verses.text: We have heard the Son of God saying, "I confess to Thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:9
verses.text: What doth he confess to Him? Wherein doth he praise Him? "Because Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:10
verses.text: Who are the "wise and prudent"? Who the "babes"? What hath He hid from the wise and prudent, and revealed unto babes? By the "wise and prudent," He signifieth those of whom St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:11
verses.text: Paul speaks; "Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world? Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?" Yet perhaps thou still askest who they are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:12
verses.text: They are they peradventure who in their much disputation concerning God, have spoken falsely of Him; who, puffed up by their own doctrines, could in no wise find out and know God, and who for the God whose substance is incomprehensible and invisible, have thought the air and sky to be God, or the sun to be God, or anything which holds high place among the creatures to be God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:13
verses.text: For observing the grandeur and beauty and powers of the creatures, they rested in them, and found not the Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:14
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:15
verses.text: These men does the Book of wisdom reprove, where it is said, "For if they were able to know so much as to aim at the world, how did they not sooner find out the Lord thereof?" They are accused as wasting their time and their busy disputes in investigating and measuring as it were the creature; they sought out the courses of the stars, the intervals of the planets, the movements of the heavenly bodies, so as to arrive by certain calculations to that degree of knowledge as to foretell the eclipses of the sun and moon; and that as they had foretold, so should the event be according to the day and hour, and to the portion of the bodies which should be eclipsed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:16
verses.text: Great industry, great activity of mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:17
verses.text: But in these things they sought after the Creator, who was not far off from them, and they found Him not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:18
verses.text: Whom if they could have found, they might have had within them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:19
verses.text: With the best reason then, and very 			 rightly were they accused, who could investigate the numbers of the stars, and their varied movements, and know and foretell the eclipses of the luminaries: rightly accused, I say, in that they found not Him by whom these had been created and ordained, because they neglected to seek Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:20
verses.text: But be not thou much disquieted, if thou art ignorant of the courses of the stars, and the proportions of the celestial and terrestrial bodies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:21
verses.text: Behold the fair beauty of the world, and praise its Creator's counsel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:22
verses.text: Behold what He has made, and love Him who made it: be this thy greatest care.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:23
verses.text: Love Him who made it; for He made thee also after His own image, that thou mightest love Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:24
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:25
verses.text: If then it is strange that those things of which Christ said, "Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent," were hidden from such wise men as these, who, occupied wholly about the creatures, chose to seek the Creator carelessly, and could not find Him; still more strange is it that there should even be found some "wise and prudent" men who were able to know Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:26
verses.text: "For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness, and 			 unrighteousness of men who hold the truth in unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:27
verses.text: Perhaps thou dost ask, what truth do they hold in unrighteousness? "Because that which may be known of God is manifest among them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:28
verses.text: How is it manifest? He goes on to say, "For God hath manifested it to them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:29
verses.text: Dost thou still enquire how He manifested it to them to whom He gave not the law? How? "For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:30
verses.text: There were then some such, not as Moses the servant of God, not as many Prophets who had an insight into and knowledge of these things, and were aided by the Spirit of God, which they drew in by faith, and drank with the throat of godliness, and poured forth again by the mouth of the interior man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:31
verses.text: Not such as these were they; but far unlike them, who by means of this visible creation were able to attain to the understanding of the Creator, and to say of these things which God hath made; Behold what things He hath made, He governeth and containeth also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:32
verses.text: He who hath made them, Himself filleth what He hath made with His own presence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:33
verses.text: Thus much they were enabled to say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:34
verses.text: For these Paul also made mention of in the Acts of the Apostles, where, when he had said of God, "For in Him we live and move and have our being" (forasmuch as he was speaking to the Athenians among whom those learned men had existed); he subjoined immediately; "As certain also of your own have said".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:35
verses.text: Now it was no trivial thing they said; "That in Him we live and move and have our being".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:36
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:37
verses.text: In what then were they unlike the others? why were they blamed? why rightly accused? Hear the words of the Apostle which I had begun to quote; "The wrath of God," saith he, "is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness" (even of those, namely, who had not received the law); "against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:38
verses.text: What truth? "Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:39
verses.text: By whose 			 manifestation of it? "For God hath manifested it to them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:40
verses.text: How? "For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even His Eternal Power and Godhead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:41
verses.text: Why did He manifest it? "That they might be without excuse".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:42
verses.text: Wherein then are they to be blamed? "Because that when they knew God, they glorified Him not as God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:43
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:44
verses.text: What mean these words, "Glorified Him not as God?" They did not give Him thanks.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:45
verses.text: Is this then to glorify God; to give God thanks? Yes, verily.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:46
verses.text: For what can be worse, if having been created after the image of God, and having come to know God, thou shalt not be thankful to Him? This surely, this is to glorify God, to give God thanks.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:47
verses.text: The faithful know where and when it is said, "Let us give thanks unto our Lord God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:48
verses.text: But who gives thanks to 			 God, save he who "lifts up his heart unto the Lord?" Therefore are they blameable and without excuse, "Because when they knew God, they glorified Him not as God, nor gave Him thanks.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:49
verses.text: But"—what? "But they became vain in their imaginations".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:50
verses.text: Whence did they become vain, but because they were proud? Thus smoke vanishes away by rising up aloft, and a flame burns the more brightly and strongly in proportion as it is kept low; "They became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:51
verses.text: So smoke, though it rise higher than the flame, is dark.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:52
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:53
verses.text: Finally, mark what follows, and see the point on which the whole matter depends.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:54
verses.text: "For professing themselves to be wise, they became fools".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:55
verses.text: For arrogating to themselves what God had given, God took away what He had given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:56
verses.text: Therefore from the proud He hid Himself, who conveyed the knowledge of Himself only to those who through the creature sought diligently after the Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:57
verses.text: Well then did our Lord say, "Thou hast hid these things from the wise and 			 prudent;" whether from those who in their manifold disputations, and most busy search, have reached to the full investigation of the creature, but knew nothing of the Creator, or from them who when they knew God, glorified Him not as God, nor gave Him thanks, and who could not see perfectly or healthfully because they were proud.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:58
verses.text: "Therefore Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:59
verses.text: What babes? To the lowly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:60
verses.text: Say on whom doth My Spirit rest? 			 "Upon him that is lowly and quiet, and who trembleth at My words".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:61
verses.text: At these words Peter trembled; Plato trembled not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:62
verses.text: Let the fisherman hold fast what that most famous philosopher has lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:63
verses.text: "Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:64
verses.text: Thou hast hid them from the proud, and revealed them to the humble.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:65
verses.text: What things are these? For when He said this, He did not intend the heaven and earth, or point them out as it were with His hand as He spake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:66
verses.text: For these who does not see? The good see them, the 			 bad see them; for He "maketh His sun to rise on the evil and the good".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 17:67
verses.text: What then are these things? "All things are delivered unto Me of My Father".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:1
verses.text: Sermon XIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:2
verses.text: [LXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:5
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:6
verses.text: 28, "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:8
verses.text: We heard in the Gospel that the Lord, rejoicing greatly in Spirit, said unto God the Father, "I confess to Thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:9
verses.text: Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in Thy sight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:10
verses.text: All things are delivered unto Me of My Father: and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, 			 and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:11
verses.text: I have labour in talking, you in hearing: let us then both give ear to Him who goes on to say, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:12
verses.text: For why do we labour all, except that we are mortal men, frail creatures and infirm, bearing about vessels of clay which crowd and straiten one another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:13
verses.text: But if these vessels of flesh are straitened, let the open expanse of charity be enlarged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:14
verses.text: What then does He mean by, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour," but that ye may labour no more? In a word, His promise is clear enough; forasmuch as He called those who were in labour, they might perchance enquire, for what profit they were called: "and," saith He, "I will refresh you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:16
verses.text: "Take My yoke upon you, and learn of Me;" not to raise the fabric of the world, not to create all things visible and invisible, not in the world so created to work miracles and raise the dead; but, "that I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:17
verses.text: Thou wishest to be great, begin from the least.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:18
verses.text: Thou art thinking to construct some mighty fabric in height; first think of the foundation of humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:19
verses.text: And how great soever a mass of building one may wish and design to place above it, the greater the building is to be, the deeper 			 does he dig his foundation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:20
verses.text: The building in the course of its erection, rises up on high, but he who digs its foundation, must first go down very low.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:21
verses.text: So then you see even a building is low before it is high, and the top is raised only after humiliation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:23
verses.text: What is the top in the erection of that building which we are constructing? Whither will the highest point of this building reach? I say at once, even to the Vision of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:24
verses.text: Ye see how high, how great a thing it is to see God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:25
verses.text: Whoso longeth after it, understands both what I say and what he hears.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:26
verses.text: The Vision of God is promised to us, of the very God, the Supreme God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:27
verses.text: For this is good, to see Him who seeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:28
verses.text: For they who worship false gods, see them 			 easily; but they see them "who have eyes and see not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:29
verses.text: But to us is promised the Vision of the Living and the Seeing God, that we may desire eagerly to see that God of whom Scripture saith, "He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? He that formed the eye, doth he not consider?" Doth He then not hear, who hath made for thee that whereby thou hearest? and doth not He see, who hath created that whereby thou seest? Well therefore in the foregoing words of this very Psalm doth He say, "Understand therefore ye unwise among the people, and ye fools at length be wise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:30
verses.text: For many men commit evil deeds whilst they think they are not seen by God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:31
verses.text: And it is difficult indeed for them to believe that He cannot see them; but they think that He will not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:32
verses.text: Few are found of such great impiety, that that should be fulfilled in them which is written, "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:33
verses.text: This is but the madness of a few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:34
verses.text: For as great piety belongs but to the few, no less also does great impiety.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:35
verses.text: But the multitude of men speak thus: What! is God thinking now upon this, that He should know what I am doing in my house, and does God care for what I may choose to do upon my bed? Who says this? "Understand, ye unwise among the people, and ye fools at length be wise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:36
verses.text: Because as being a man, it is a labour for thee to know all that takes place in thy house, and 			 for all the doings and words of thy servants to reach thee; thinkest thou that it is a like labour for God to observe thee, who did not labour to create thee? Doth not He fix His eye upon thee, who made thine eye? Thou wast not, and He created thee and gave thee being; and doth not He care for thee now that thou art, who "calleth those things which be not as though they were"? Do not then promise thyself this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:37
verses.text: Whether thou wilt or no, He seeth thee, and there is no place whither thou canst hide thyself from His eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:38
verses.text: "For if thou goest up into heaven, He is there; if thou goest down into hell, He is there also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:39
verses.text: Great is thy labour, whilst unwilling to depart from evil deeds: yet wishest not to be seen by God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:40
verses.text: Hard labour truly! Daily art thou wishing to do evil, and dost thou suspect that thou art not seen? Hear the Scripture which saith, "He that planted the ear, shall He not hear? He that formed the eye, doth not He consider?" Where canst thou hide thy evil deeds from the eyes of God? If thou wilt not depart from them, thy labour is great indeed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:41
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:42
verses.text: Hear Him then who saith, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:43
verses.text: Thou canst not end thy labour by flying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:44
verses.text: Dost thou choose to fly from Him, and not rather to Him? Find out then whither thou canst escape, and so fly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:45
verses.text: But if thou canst not fly from Him, for that He is everywhere present; fly (it is quite nigh) to God, who is present where thou art standing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:46
verses.text: Fly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:47
verses.text: Lo in thy flight thou hast passed the heavens, He is there; thou hast descended into hell, He is there; whatever deserts of the earth thou shalt choose, there is He, who hath said, "I fill heaven and earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:48
verses.text: If then He fills heaven and earth, and there is no place whither thou canst fly from Him; cease this thy labour, and fly to His presence, lest thou feel His coming.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:49
verses.text: Take courage from the hope that thou shalt by well-living see Him, by whom even in thy evil living thou art seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:50
verses.text: For in evil living thou canst be seen, thou canst not see; but by well-living thou art both seen and seest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:51
verses.text: For with how much more tender nearness will He who crowneth the worthy look on thee, who in His pity saw thee that He might call thee when unworthy? Nathanael said to the Lord whom as yet he did not know, "Whence knewest thou me?" The Lord said unto him, "When thou wast under the fig-tree I saw thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:52
verses.text: Christ saw thee in thine own shade; and will He not see thee in His Light? For what is, "When thou wast under the fig-tree I saw thee"? What does it mean? Call to mind the original sin of Adam, in whom we all die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:53
verses.text: When he first sinned, he made himself aprons of fig-leaves, signifying by these leaves the irritations of lust to which he had been reduced by sinning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:54
verses.text: Hence are we born; in this condition are we born; born in sinful flesh, which "the likeness of sinful flesh" alone can cure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:55
verses.text: Therefore "God sent His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:56
verses.text: He came of this flesh, but He came not as other men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:57
verses.text: For the Virgin conceived Him not by lust, but by faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:58
verses.text: He came into the Virgin, who was before the Virgin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:59
verses.text: He made choice of her whom He created, He created her whom He designed to choose.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:60
verses.text: He brought to the Virgin fruitfulness: He took not away her unimpaired purity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:61
verses.text: He then who came to thee without the irritation of the leaves of the fig-tree, "when thou wast under the fig-tree," saw thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:62
verses.text: Make ready then to see Him in 			 His height of glory, by whom in His pity thou wast seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:63
verses.text: But because the top is high, think of the foundation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:64
verses.text: What foundation? dost thou say? "Learn of Him, for He is meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:65
verses.text: Dig this foundation of lowliness deep in thee, and so wilt thou attain to the crowning top of charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 18:66
verses.text: "Turning to the Lord," etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:1
verses.text: Sermon XX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:2
verses.text: [LXX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:4
verses.text: ]  Again on the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:5
verses.text: xi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:6
verses.text: 28, "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:8
verses.text: It seems strange to some, Brethren, when they hear the Lord say, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:9
verses.text: Take my yoke upon you and learn of Me, for I am meek and lowly in heart, and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:10
verses.text: For My yoke is easy and My burden is light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:11
verses.text: And they consider that they who have fearlessly bowed their necks to this yoke, and have with much submission taken this burden upon their shoulders, are tossed about and exercised by so great difficulties in the world, that they seem not to be called from labour to rest, but from rest to labour rather; since the Apostle also saith, "All who will live godly in Christ Jesus, shall suffer persecution".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:12
verses.text: So one will say, "How is the yoke easy, and the burden light," when to bear this yoke and burden is nothing else, but to live godly in Christ? And how is it said, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you"? and not rather said, "Come ye who are at ease and idle, that ye may labour".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:13
verses.text: For so he found those men idle and at ease, whom he hired into the vineyard, that they might bear the heat of the day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:14
verses.text: And we hear the Apostle under that easy yoke and light burden say, "In all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses, in stripes," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:15
verses.text: , and in another place of the same Epistle, "Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:16
verses.text: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice have I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day have I been in the deep:" and the rest of the perils, which may be enumerated indeed, but endured they cannot be but by the help of the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:17
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:18
verses.text: All these grievous and heavy trials which he mentioned, did he very frequently and abundantly sustain; but in very deed the Holy Spirit was with him in the wasting of the outward man, to renew the inner man from day to day, and by the taste of spiritual rest in the affluence of the delights of God to soften down by the hope of future blessedness all present hardships, and to alleviate all heavy trials.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:19
verses.text: Lo, how sweet a yoke of Christ did he bear, and how light a 			 burden; so that he could say that all those hard and grievous sufferings at the recital of which as just above every hearer shudders, were a "light tribulation;" as he beheld with the inward eyes, the eyes of faith, at how great a price of things temporal must be purchased the life to come, the escape from the everlasting pains of the ungodly, the full enjoyment, free from all anxiety, of the eternal happiness of the righteous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:20
verses.text: Men suffer themselves to be cut and burnt, that the pains not 			 of eternity, but of some more lasting sore than usual, may be bought off at the priceof severer pain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:21
verses.text: For a languid and uncertain period of a very short repose, and that too at the end of life, the soldier is worn down by all the hard trials of war, restless it may be for more years in his labours, than he will have to enjoy his rest in ease.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:22
verses.text: To what storms and tempests, to what a fearful and tremendous raging of sky and sea, do the busy merchantmen expose themselves, that they may acquire 			 riches inconstant as the wind, and full of perils and tempests, greater even than those by which they were acquired! What heats, and colds, what perils, from horses, from ditches, from precipices, from rivers, from wild beasts, do huntsmen undergo, what pain of hunger and thirst, what straitened allowances of the cheapest and meanest meat and drink, that they may catch a beast! and sometimes after all, the flesh of the beast for which they endure all this is of no use for the table.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:23
verses.text: And 			 although a boar or a stag be caught, it is more sweet to the hunter's mind because it has been caught, than it is to the eater's palate because it is dressed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:24
verses.text: By what sharp corrections of almost daily stripes is the tender age of boys brought under! By what great pains even of watching and abstinence in the schools are they exercised, not to learn true wisdom, but for the sake of riches, and the honours of an empty show, that they may learn arithmetic, and other literature, and the deceits of eloquence!  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:25
verses.text: Now in all these instances, they who do not love these things feel them as great severities; whereas they who love them endure the same, it is true, but they do not seem to feel them severe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:26
verses.text: For love makes all, the hardest and most distressing things, altogether easy, and almost nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:27
verses.text: How much more surely then and easily will charity do with a view to true blessedness, that which mere desire does as it can, with a view to what is but misery? How easily is any 			 temporal adversity endured, if it be that eternal punishment may be avoided, and eternal rest procured! Not without good reason did that vessel of election say with exceeding joy, "The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:28
verses.text: See then how it is that that "yoke is easy, and that burden light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:29
verses.text: And if it be strait to the few who choose it, yet is it easy to all who love it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:30
verses.text: The Psalmist saith, "Because of the words of Thy lips I have kept hard ways".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:31
verses.text: But the things which are hard to those who labour, lose their roughness to those same men when they love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:32
verses.text: Wherefore it has been so arranged by the dispensation of the Divine goodness, that to "the inner man who is renewed from day to day," placed no longer under the Law but under Grace, and freed from the burdens of numberless observances which were indeed a heavy yoke, but meetly imposed on a stubborn neck, every grievous trouble which that prince who is cast forth could inflict from without on the outward man, should through the easiness of a simple faith, and a good hope, and a holy charity, become light through the joy within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:33
verses.text: For to a good will nothing is so easy, as this good will to itself, and this is 			 enough for God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:34
verses.text: How much soever therefore this world may rage, most truly did the angels exclaim when the Lord was born in the flesh, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will;" because "His yoke," who was then born, "is easy, and His burden light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 19:35
verses.text: And as the Apostle saith, "God is faithful, who will not suffer us to be tempted above that we are able to bear; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that we may be able to bear it".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:1
verses.text: Sermon XXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:2
verses.text: [LXXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:5
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:6
verses.text: 32, "Whosoever shall speak a word against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in that which is to come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:7
verses.text: Or, "on the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:9
verses.text: There has been a great question raised touching the late lesson of the Gospel, to the solution of which I am unequal by any power of mine own; but "our sufficiency is of God," to whatever degree we are capable of receiving His aid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:10
verses.text: First then consider the magnitude of the question; that when ye see the weight of it laid upon my shoulders, ye may pray in aid of my labours, and in the assistance which is vouchsafed to me, may find edification for your own souls.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:11
verses.text: When "one possessed with a devil was brought to the Lord, blind and dumb, and He had healed him so that he could speak and see, and all the people were amazed and said, Is not this the Son 			 of David? the Pharisees hearing it said, This fellow doth not cast out devils but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:12
verses.text: But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself shall be brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:13
verses.text: And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand?" In these words He wished it to be understood from their own confession, that, through their not believing in Him they had chosen to belong to the kingdom of the devil, which as being divided against itself could accordingly not stand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:14
verses.text: Let then the Pharisees make choice of which they will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:15
verses.text: If Satan cannot cast out Satan, they can find nothing to say against the Lord; but if he can, then let them much more look to themselves, and depart out of his kingdom, which as being divided 			 against itself cannot stand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:17
verses.text: But now that they may not think that it is the prince of the devils in whom the Lord Jesus Christ casteth out devils, let them attend to what follows; "And if I," He saith, "by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore shall they be your judges".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:18
verses.text: He spoke this undoubtedly of his disciples, the "children" of that people; who as being the disciples of the Lord Jesus Christ were well conscious that they had learnt no evil arts from their Good Master, that through the prince of the devils they should cast out devils.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:19
verses.text: "Therefore," He saith, "shall they be your judges".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:20
verses.text: They, He saith, the base and contemptible things of this world, in whom none of this artificial malice, but the holy simplicity of My power 			  is seen; they shall be My witnesses, they shall be your judges.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:21
verses.text: Then He subjoins, "But if I by the Spirit of God cast out devils, then the kingdom of God is come unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:22
verses.text: What is this? "If I by the Spirit of God cast out devils," He saith, and your children, to whom I have given no hurtful and deceitful doctrine but a simple faith, can in no other way cast them out; no doubt the kingdom of God is come unto you; whereby the kingdom of the devil is subverted, and ye also are subverted with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:23
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:24
verses.text: And after that He had said, "By whom do your children cast them out?" to show that in them it was His grace, not their own desert; He saith, "Or else how can one enter into a strong man's house and spoil his goods, except He first bind the strong man, and then He will spoil his house?" Your children, saith He, who either have already believed in Me, or who shall yet believe, and cast out devils, not through the prince of the devils, but through the simplicity of holiness, who assuredly either once were, or still are what ye are also, sinners and ungodly; and so in the house of the devil, and the vessels of the devil, how could they be rescued from him whom he held so firmly through the iniquity which reigned over them, unless he 			 were bound by the chains of My justice, that I might take away from him his vessels which once were vessels of wrath, and make them vessels of mercy? This it is which the blessed Apostle also says when he rebukes the proud, and those who boast as it were of their own deserts, "For who maketh thee to differ?" That is, who maketh thee to differ from the mass of perdition derived from Adam and from the vessels of wrath.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:25
verses.text: And that no man might say, "My own righteousness," he says, "What hast thou, that thou didst not receive?" And on this point he says of himself also, "We also once were by nature the children of wrath, even as others".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:26
verses.text: So then he himself was a vessel in the house of that strong one, strong in evil, when he was a persecutor of the Church, a "blasphemer, injurious, living in malice and envy," as he confesses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:27
verses.text: But He who bound the strong one, took away from him this vessel of perdition, and made it a vessel of election.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:28
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:29
verses.text: Afterwards, that the unbelievers and ungodly, the enemies of the Christian name, might not suppose by reason of the divers heresies and schisms of those who under the Christian name gather together flocks of lost sheep, that the kingdom of Christ also is divided against itself, He next adds, "He that is not with Me is against Me, and he that gathereth not with Me, scattereth abroad".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:30
verses.text: He does not say, he who is under the outward profession of My Name; or the form of My Sacrament; but "he who is not with Me is against Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:31
verses.text: Nor doth He say, he who gathereth not under the outward profession of My Name; but "he who gathereth not with Me, scattereth abroad".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:32
verses.text: Christ's kingdom then is not divided against itself; but men try to divide that which was bought with the price of the Blood of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:33
verses.text: "For the Lord knoweth them that are His.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:34
verses.text: And, let every one that nameth the Name of Christ depart from iniquity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:35
verses.text: For if he depart not from iniquity, he belongeth not to the kingdom of Christ, even though he name the Name of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:36
verses.text: To give then some illustrations for example's sake, the spirit of covetousness, and the spirit of luxuriousness, because the one heaps together, and the other lavishes, are divided against themselves; yet they belong both to the kingdom of the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:37
verses.text: Among idolaters the spirit of Juno and the spirit of Hercules, are divided against themselves; and both 			 belong to the kingdom of the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:38
verses.text: The heathen Christ's enemy, and the Jew Christ's enemy, are divided against themselves; and both belong to the kingdom of the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:39
verses.text: Arianus and Photinianus both are heretics, and both are divided against themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:40
verses.text: The Donatist and Maximianist both are heretics, and both divided against themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:41
verses.text: All men's vices and errors that are contrary to each other are divided against themselves, and all belong to the kingdom of the devil; therefore his kingdom shall not stand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:42
verses.text: But the righteous and the ungodly, the believer and the unbeliever, the Catholic and the heretic, are indeed divided against themselves, but they do not belong all to the kingdom of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:43
verses.text: "The Lord knoweth them that are His".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:44
verses.text: Let no one 			 flatter himself upon a mere name.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:45
verses.text: If he would that the Name of the Lord should profit him, let "him that calleth upon the Name of the Lord depart from iniquity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:46
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:47
verses.text: But these words of the Gospel, though they had some obscurity, which I think by the Lord's assistance I have explained, were yet not so difficult, as that which follows would seem to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:48
verses.text: "Wherefore I say unto you, all manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven unto men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:49
verses.text: And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him; but whosoever speaketh against the Holy 			 Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:50
verses.text: What then will become of those whom the Church desires to gain? When they have been reformed and come into the Church from whatsoever error, is the hope in the remission of all sins that is promised them a false hope? For who is not convicted of having spoken a word against the Holy Ghost, before he became a Christian or a Catholic? In the first place, are not they who are called Pagans, the worshippers of many and false gods, and the adorers of idols, forasmuch as they say 			 that the Lord Christ wrought miracles by magical arts, are not they like these who said that He cast out devils through the prince of the devils? And again, when day by day they blaspheme our sanctification, what else blaspheme they but the Holy Ghost? What? Do not the Jews—they who spoke concerning our Lord what gave occasion to this very discourse—do they not even to the present day speak a word against the Holy Ghost, by denying that He is now in Christians, just as the others denied Him 			 to be in Christ? For not even did they revile the Holy Ghost, by asserting either that He existed not, or that though He existed, yet that He was not God, but a creature; or that He had no power to cast out devils; they did not speak thus unworthily, or anything like it, of the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:51
verses.text: For the Sadducees indeed denied the Holy Ghost; but the Pharisees maintained His existence against their heresy, but they denied that He was in the Lord Jesus Christ, who they thought cast out devils through the prince of the devils, whereas He did cast them out through the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:52
verses.text: And hence, both Jews and whatsoever heretics there are who confess the Holy Ghost, but deny that He is in the Body of Christ, which is His One Only Church, none other than the One Catholic Church, are without doubt like the Pharisees who at that time although they confessed the existence of the Holy Ghost, 			 yet denied that He was in Christ, whose works in casting out devils they attributed to the prince of devils.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:53
verses.text: I say nothing of the fact that some heretics either boldly maintain that the Holy Ghost is not the Creator but a creature, as the Arians, and Eunomians, and Macedonians, or so entirely deny His existence, as to deny that God is Trinity, but assert that He is God the Father only, and that He is sometimes called the Son, and sometimes the Holy Ghost; as the Sabellians, whom some call 			 Patripassians, because they hold that the Father suffered; and forasmuch as they deny that He has any Son, without doubt they deny His Holy Spirit also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:54
verses.text: The Photinians again who say that the Father only is God, and the Son a mere man, deny altogether that there is any third Person of the Holy Ghost.
