verses.text: I have through the mercy and assistance of the Lord handled, as I best was able, this most difficult question, if indeed I have been able to do it in any measure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:328
verses.text: Nevertheless, whatever I have not been able to apprehend in the difficulties of it, let it not be imputed to the truth itself, which is a healthful exercise to the godly, even when it is hidden, but to my infirmity, who either could not see what others might have understood, or could not explain 			 what I did understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 20:329
verses.text: But for that which perhaps I have been able to discover by force of meditation, and to develop in words, to Him must the thanks be given, from whom I have sought, from whom I have asked, unto whom I have knocked, that I might have wherewithal to be nourished myself in meditation, and to minister to you in speaking.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:1
verses.text: Sermon XXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:2
verses.text: [LXXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:5
verses.text: xii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:6
verses.text: 33, "Either make the tree good, and its fruit good," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:8
verses.text: The Lord Jesus hath admonished us, that we be good trees, and that so we may be able to bear good fruits.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:9
verses.text: For He saith, "Either make the tree good, and his fruit good, or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt, for the tree is known by his fruit".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:10
verses.text: When He says, "Make the tree good, and his fruit good;" this of course is not an admonition, but a wholesome precept, to which obedience is necessary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:11
verses.text: But when He saith, "Make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt;" this is not a precept that thou shouldest do it; but an admonition, that thou shouldest beware of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:12
verses.text: For He spoke against those, who thought that although they were evil, they could speak good things or have good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:13
verses.text: This the Lord Jesus saith is 			 impossible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:14
verses.text: For the man himself must first be changed, in order that his works may be changed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:15
verses.text: For if a man abide in his evil state, he cannot have good works; if he abide in his good state, he cannot have evil works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:17
verses.text: But who was found good by the Lord, since "Christ died for the ungodly"? He found them all corrupt trees, but to those who "believed in His Name, He gave power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:18
verses.text: Whosoever then now is a good man, that is, a good tree, was found corrupt, and made good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:19
verses.text: And if when He came He had chosen to root up the corrupt trees, what tree would have remained which did not deserve to be rooted up? But He came first to impart mercy, that He might afterwards exercise judgment, to whom it is said, "I will sing unto Thee O Lord, of mercy and judgment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:20
verses.text: He gave then remission of sins to those who believed in Him, He would not even take account with them of past reckonings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:21
verses.text: He gave remission of sins, He made them good trees.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:22
verses.text: He delayed the ax, He gave security.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:23
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:24
verses.text: Of this ax does John speak, saying, "Now is the ax laid unto the root of the trees; every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit shall be hewn down, and cast into the fire".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:25
verses.text: With this ax does the Householder in the Gospel threaten, saying, "Behold these three years I come to this tree, and find no fruit on it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:26
verses.text: Now I must clear the ground; wherefore let it be cut down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:27
verses.text: And the husbandman intercedes, saying, "Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it and dung it; and if it bear fruit, well; and if not, then Thou shalt come and cut it down".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:28
verses.text: So the Lord hath visited mankind as it were three years, that is, at three several times.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:29
verses.text: The first time was before the Law; the second under the Law; the third is now, which is the time of grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:30
verses.text: For if He did not visit mankind before the Law, whence was Abel, and Enoch, and Noe, and Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, whose Lord He was pleased to be called? And He to whom all nations belonged, as though He were the God of three men only, said, "I am the God of Abraham, and 			 Isaac, and Jacob".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:31
verses.text: But if He did not visit under the Law, He would not have given the Law itself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:32
verses.text: After the Law, came the very Master of the house in person; He suffered, and died, and rose again; He gave the Holy Spirit, He made the Gospel to be preached throughout all the world, and yet a certain tree remained unfruitful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:33
verses.text: Still is there a certain portion of mankind, which doth not yet amend itself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:34
verses.text: The husbandman intercedes; the Apostle prays for the people; "I bow my knees," he saith, 			 "unto the Father for you, that being rooted and grounded in love, ye may be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; and to know the love of Christ which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:35
verses.text: By bowing the knees, he intercedes with the Master of the house for us, that we be not rooted up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:36
verses.text: Therefore since He must necessarily come, let us take care that He find us fruitful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:37
verses.text: The digging about the tree is the lowliness of the penitent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:38
verses.text: For every ditch is low.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:39
verses.text: The dunging it, is the filthy robe of repentance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:40
verses.text: For what is more filthy than dung; yet if well used, what more profitable?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:41
verses.text: Let each one then be a good tree; let him not suppose that he can bear good fruit, if he remain a corrupt tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:42
verses.text: There will be no good fruit, but from the good tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:43
verses.text: Change the heart, and the work will be changed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:44
verses.text: Root out desire, plant in charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:45
verses.text: "For as desire is the root of all evil," so is charity the root of all good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:46
verses.text: Why then do men fret and contend one with another, saying, "What is good?" O that thou knewest what good is! What thou dost wish to have is not very good; this is good which thou dost not wish to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:47
verses.text: For thou dost wish to have health of body; it is good indeed; yet thou canst not think that to be any great good, which the wicked have as well.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:48
verses.text: Thou dost wish to have gold and silver; I grant that these also are good things, but then only 			 if thou make a good use of them; and a good use of them thou wilt not make, if thou art evil thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:49
verses.text: And hence gold and silver are to the evil evil; to the good are good, not because gold and silver make them good; but because they find them good, they are turned to a good use.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:50
verses.text: Again, thou dost wish to have honour, it is good; but this too only if thou make a good use of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:51
verses.text: To how many has honour been the occasion of destruction! And again, to how many has honour been the instrument 			  of good works!  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:52
verses.text: Let us then, if we can, make a distinction as to these goods; for it is of good trees that we are speaking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:53
verses.text: And here there is nothing, which every one ought so much to think of, as to turn his eyes upon himself, to learn in himself, examine himself, inspect himself, search into himself, and find out himself; and kill what is displeasing; and long for and plant in that which is well-pleasing (to God).

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:54
verses.text: For when a man finds himself so empty of better goods, why is 			 he greedy of external goods? And what profit is there in a coffer full of goods, with an empty conscience? Thou wishest to have good things, and dost thou not then wish to be good thyself? Seest thou not that thou oughtest rather to blush for thy good things, if thy house is full of good things, and thou its owner art evil? For what is there, tell me, thou wouldest wish to have that is bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:55
verses.text: Not any one thing I am sure; neither wife; nor son; nor daughter; nor manservant; nor maidservant; nor 			 country seat; nor a coat; nay nor a shoe; and yet thou art willing to have a bad life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:56
verses.text: I pray thee prefer thy way of life to thy shoes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:57
verses.text: All things which encompass thy sight, as being of elegance and beauty, are highly prized by thee; and art thou so lightly esteemed by thyself, and so devoid of beauty? If the good things of which thine house is full, which thou hast longed to possess, and feared to lose, could make answer to thee, would they not cry out to thee, As thou wishest to have us good, so do we also wish to 			 have a good owner? And now in speechless accents do they address thy Lord against thee: "Lo! thou hast given him so many good things, and he himself is evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:58
verses.text: What profit is there to him in that he hath, when he hath not Him who hath given him all!"  6.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:59
verses.text: One then who has been admonished, and it may be moved to compunction by these words, may ask what is good? what is the nature of good? and whence it comes? Well is it that thou hast understood that it is thy duty to ask this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:60
verses.text: I will answer thy enquiries, and will say, "That is good which thou canst not lose against thy will".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:61
verses.text: For gold thou mayest lose even against thy will; and so thou canst a house; and honours, and even the health of the body; but the good 			 whereby thou art truly good, thou dost neither receive against thy will, nor against thy will dost lose it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:62
verses.text: I enquire then, "What is the nature of this good?" One of the Psalms teaches us an important matter, perchance it is even this that we are seeking for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:63
verses.text: For it says, "O ye sons of men, how long will ye be heavy in heart?" How long will that tree be in its three years fruitlessness? "O ye sons of men, how long will ye be heavy in heart?" What is "heavy in heart"? "Why do ye love vanity, and seek after leasing?" And then it goes on to say what we must really seek after; "Know ye that the Lord hath magnified His Holy One?" Now Christ hath come, now hath He been magnified, now hath He risen again, and ascended into heaven, now is His Name preached through the world: "How long will ye be heavy in heart?" Let the times past suffice; now that that Holy One hath been magnified, "How long will ye be heavy in heart?" After the three years, what remains but the ax? "How long will ye be heavy in heart? Why do ye love vanity, and seek after leasing?" Vain, useless, frivolous, 			  fleeting things are these still sought after, now that Christ the Holy One hath been so magnified? Truth now is crying aloud, and is vanity still sought after? "How long will ye be heavy in heart?"  7.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:64
verses.text: With good reason is this world severely scourged; for the world hath known now its Master's words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:65
verses.text: "And the servant," He saith, "that knew not his Master's will, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:66
verses.text: Why? That he may seek after his Master's will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:67
verses.text: The servant then who knew not His will, this was the world, before "He magnified His Holy One;" it was "the servant who knew not his Master's will," and therefore "shall be beaten with few stripes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:68
verses.text: But the servant who now knoweth his Master's will, that is now, since the Godhead "sanctified His Holy One," and "doeth not His will, shall be beaten with many stripes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:69
verses.text: What marvel then, if the world be now 			 much beaten? "It is the servant which knew his Master's will, and did commit things worthy of stripes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:70
verses.text: Let him then not refuse to be beaten with many stripes; since if in unrighteousness he will not hear his teacher, in righteousness must he feel his avenger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 21:71
verses.text: At least, let him not murmur against Him that chasteneth him, when he sees that he is worthy of stripes, that so he may attain mercy; through Christ our Lord, who liveth and reigneth, with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever, Amen.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:1
verses.text: Sermon XXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:2
verses.text: [LXXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:5
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:6
verses.text: 19, etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:7
verses.text: , where the Lord Jesus explaineth the parables of the sower.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:9
verses.text: Both yesterday and to-day ye have heard the parables of the sower, in the words of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:10
verses.text: Do ye who were present yesterday, recollect to-day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:11
verses.text: Yesterday we read of that sower, who when he scattered seed, "some fell by the way side," which the birds picked up; "some in stony places," which dried up from the heat; "some among thorns, which were choked," and could not bring forth fruit; and "other some into good ground, and it brought forth fruit, a hundred, sixty, thirty fold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:12
verses.text: But to-day the Lord hath again spoken another parable of the sower, "who sowed good seed in his field.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:13
verses.text: While men slept the enemy came, and sowed tares upon it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:14
verses.text: As long as it was only in the blade, it did not appear; but when the fruit of the good seed began to appear, "then appeared the tares also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:15
verses.text: The servants of the householder were offended, when they saw a quantity of tares among the good wheat, and wished to root them out, but they were not suffered to do so; but it was said to them, "Let both grow together until the harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:16
verses.text: Now the Lord Jesus Christ explained this parable also; and said that He was the sower of the good seed, and He showed how that the enemy who sowed the tares was the devil; the time of harvest, the end of the world; His field the whole world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:17
verses.text: And what saith He? "In the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, to burn them, but gather the wheat into My barn".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:18
verses.text: Why are ye so hasty, He says, ye servants full of zeal? Ye see tares among the 			 wheat, ye see evil Christians among the good; and ye wish to root up the evil ones; be quiet, it is not the time of harvest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:19
verses.text: That time will come, may it only find you wheat! Why do ye vex yourselves? Why bear impatiently the mixture of the evil with the good? In the field they may be with you, but they will not be so in the barn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:21
verses.text: Now ye know that those three places mentioned yesterday where the seed did not grow, "the way side," "the stony ground," and "the thorny places," are the same as these "tares".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:22
verses.text: They received only a different name under a different similitude.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:23
verses.text: For when similitudes are used, or the literal meaning of a term is not expressed, not the truth but a similitude of the truth is conveyed by them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:24
verses.text: I see that but few have understood my meaning; yet it is for 			 the benefit of all that I speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:25
verses.text: In things visible, a way side is a way side, stony ground is stony ground, thorny places are thorny places; they are simply what they are, because the names are used in their literal sense.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:26
verses.text: But in parables and similitudes one thing may be called by many names; therefore there is nothing inconsistent in my telling you that that "way side," that "stony ground," those "thorny places," are bad Christians, and that they too are the "tares".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:27
verses.text: Is not 			 Christ called "the Lamb"? Is not Christ "the Lion" too? Among wild beasts, and cattle, a lamb is simply a lamb, and a lion, a lion: but Christ is both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:28
verses.text: The first are respectively what they are in propriety of expression; the Latter both together in a figurative sense.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:29
verses.text: Nay much more; besides this it may happen that under a figure, things very different from one another may be called by one and the same name.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:30
verses.text: For what is so different as Christ and the devil? yet both Christ and the devil are called "a lion".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:31
verses.text: Christ is called "a lion:" "The Lion hath prevailed of the tribe of Judah;" and the devil is called a lion: "Know ye not that your adversary the Devil walketh about as a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour?" Both the one and the other then is a lion; the one a lion by reason of His strength; the other for his savageness; the one a lion for His "prevailing;" the other for his injuring.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:32
verses.text: The devil again is a serpent, "that old serpent;" are we commanded then to imitate the devil, when our Shepherd told us, "Be ye wise as serpents, and simple as doves"?  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:33
verses.text: Accordingly I yesterday addressed "the way side," I addressed the "stony ground," I addressed the "thorny places;" and I said, Be ye changed whilst ye may: turn up with the plough the hard ground, cast the stones out of the field, pluck up the thorns out of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:34
verses.text: Be loth to retain that hard heart, from which the word of God may quickly pass away and be lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:35
verses.text: Be loth to have that lightness of soil, where the root of charity can take no deep hold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:36
verses.text: Be loth to 			 choke the good seed which is sown in you by my labours, with the lusts and the cares of this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:37
verses.text: For it is the Lord who sows; and we are only His labourers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:38
verses.text: But be ye the "good ground".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:39
verses.text: I said yesterday, and I say again today to all, Let one bring forth "a hundred, another sixty, another thirty fold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:40
verses.text: In one the fruit is more, in another less; but all will have a place in the barn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:41
verses.text: Yesterday I said all this, to-day I am addressing the tares; but the sheep 			 themselves are the tares.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:42
verses.text: O evil Christians, O ye, who in filling only press the Church by your evil lives; amend yourselves before the harvest come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:43
verses.text: "Say not, I have sinned, and what hath befallen me?" God hath not lost His power; but He is requiring repentance from thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:44
verses.text: I say this to the evil, who yet are Christians; I say this to the tares.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:45
verses.text: For they are in the field; and it may so be, that they who to-day are tares, may to-morrow be wheat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:46
verses.text: And so I will address the wheat also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:47
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:48
verses.text: O ye Christians, whose lives are good, ye sigh and groan as being few among many, few among very many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:49
verses.text: The winter will pass away, the summer will come; lo! the harvest will soon be here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:50
verses.text: The angels will come who can make the separation, and who cannot make mistakes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:51
verses.text: We in this time present are like those servants of whom it was said, "Wilt Thou that we go and gather them up?" for we were wishing, if it might be so, that no evil ones should remain among the good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:52
verses.text: But it has been told us, "Let both grow together until the harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:53
verses.text: Why? For ye are such as may be deceived.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:54
verses.text: Hear finally; "Lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:55
verses.text: What good are ye doing? Will ye by your eagerness make a waste of My harvest? The reapers will come, and who the reapers are He hath explained, "And the reapers are the angels".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:56
verses.text: We are but men, the reapers are the angels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:57
verses.text: We too indeed, if we finish our course, shall be equal to the angels of God; but now when we chafe against the wicked, we are as yet but men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:58
verses.text: And we ought now to give ear to the words, "Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth, take heed lest he fall".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:59
verses.text: For do ye think, my Brethren, that these tares we read of do not get up into this seat? Think ye that they are all below, and none above up here? God grant we may not be so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:60
verses.text: "But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:61
verses.text: I tell you of a truth, my Beloved, even in these high seats there is both wheat, and tares, and among the laity there is wheat, and tares.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:62
verses.text: Let the good tolerate the bad; let the bad change themselves, and imitate the good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:63
verses.text: Let us all, if it may be so, attain to God; let us all through His mercy escape the evil of this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 22:64
verses.text: Let us seek after good days, for we are now in evil days; but in the evil days let us not blaspheme, that so we may be able to arrive at the good 			 days.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:1
verses.text: Sermon XXIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:2
verses.text: [LXXIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:5
verses.text: xiii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:6
verses.text: 52, "Therefore every scribe who hath been made a disciple to the kingdom of Heaven," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:8
verses.text: The lesson of the Gospel reminds me to seek out, and to explain to you, Beloved, as the Lord shall give me power, who is "that Scribe instructed in the kingdom of God, who is "like unto an householder bringing out of his treasure things new and old".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:9
verses.text: For here the lesson ended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:10
verses.text: "What are the new and old things of an instructed Scribe?" Now it is well known who they were, whom the ancients, after the custom of our Scriptures, called Scribes, those, namely, who professed the knowledge of the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:11
verses.text: For such were called Scribes among the Jewish people, not such as are so called now in the service of judges, or the custom of states.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:12
verses.text: For we must not enter school to no purpose, but we must know in what signification to take the words of Scripture; lest when anything is mentioned out of it, which is usually understood in another secular use of the term, the hearer mistake it, and by thinking of its customary meaning, understand not what he has heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:13
verses.text: The Scribes then were they who professed the knowledge of the Law, and to them belonged both the keeping and the studying, 			 as well as also the transcribing and the expounding, of the books of the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:14
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:15
verses.text: Such were they whom our Lord Jesus Christ rebukes, because they have the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and "would neither enter in themselves, nor suffer others to enter in;" in these words finding fault with the Pharisees and Scribes, the teachers of the law of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:16
verses.text: Of whom in another place He says, "Whatsoever they say, do, but do not ye after their works, for they say and do not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:17
verses.text: Why is it said to you, "For they say and do not?" but that there are some of whom what the Apostle says, is clearly exemplified, "Thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal? Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? Thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege? Thou that makest thy boast of the Law, through breaking the Law dishonourest thou God? For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through 			 you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:18
verses.text: It is surely plain that the Lord speaks of these, "For they say and do not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:19
verses.text: They then are Scribes, but not "instructed in the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:21
verses.text: Peradventure some of you may say, "And how can a bad man speak what is good, when it is written, in the words of the Lord Himself, 'A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth good things, and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth evil things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:22
verses.text: Ye hypocrites, how can ye being evil speak good things?'" In the one place He says, "How can ye being evil speak good things?" in the other He says, "What they say, do, but do ye not after their works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:23
verses.text: For they say, and do not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:24
verses.text: If "they say and do not," they are evil; if they are evil, they cannot "speak good things;" how then are we to do what we hear from them, when we cannot hear from them what is good? Now take heed, Holy and Beloved, how this question may be solved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:25
verses.text: Whatever an evil man brings forth from himself, is evil; whatever an evil man brings forth out of his own heart, is evil; for there is the evil treasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:26
verses.text: But whatever a good man brings forth out of his heart, is good; for there is the good treasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:27
verses.text: Whence then did those evil men bring forth good things? "Because they sat in Moses' seat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:28
verses.text: Had He not first said, "They sit in Moses' seat;" He would never have enjoined that evil men should be heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:29
verses.text: For what they brought forth out of the evil treasure of their own heart, was one thing; another what they gave utterance to out of the seat of Moses, the criers so to say of the judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:30
verses.text: What the crier says, will never be attributed to him if he speak in the presence of the judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:31
verses.text: What the crier says in his own house is one thing, what the crier says as hearing it 			 from the judge is another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:32
verses.text: For whether he will or no, the crier must proclaim the sentence of punishment even of his own friend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:33
verses.text: And so whether he will or no, must he proclaim the sentence of the acquittal even of his own enemy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:34
verses.text: Suppose him to speak from his heart; he acquits his friend, and punishes his enemy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:35
verses.text: Suppose him to speak from the judge's chair; he punishes his friend, and acquits his enemy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:36
verses.text: So with the Scribes; suppose them to speak out of their own heart; thou wilt hear, "Let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we shall die".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:37
verses.text: Suppose them to speak from Moses' seat; thou wilt hear, "Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shall not steal, Thou shall not bear false witness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:38
verses.text: Honour thy father and mother; thou shall love thy neighbour as thyself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:39
verses.text: Do then this which the official seat proclaims by the mouth of the Scribes; not that which their heart utters.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:40
verses.text: For so embracing both judgments of the Lord, thou wilt not be obedient in the one, and guilty of disobedience in the other; but wilt understand that both agree together, and wilt regard both that as true, "that a good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth good things, and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things;" and that other also, that those Scribes did 			 not speak good things out of the evil treasure of their heart, but that they were able to speak good things out of the treasure of Moses' seat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:41
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:42
verses.text: So then those words of the Lord will not disturb you, when He says, "Every tree is known by his own fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:43
verses.text: Do men gather grapes of thorns, and figs of thistles?" The Scribes and Pharisees of the Jews therefore were thorns and thistles, and notwithstanding, "what they say do, but do ye not after their works".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:44
verses.text: So then the grape is gathered from thorns, and the fig from thistles, as He has given thee to understand according to the method I have just laid down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:45
verses.text: For so sometimes in the vineyard's thorny hedge, the vines get entangled, and clusters of grapes hang from the brambles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:46
verses.text: Thou hadst no sooner heard the name of thorns, than 			 thou wert on the point of disregarding the grape.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:47
verses.text: But seek for the root of the thorns, and thou wilt see where to find it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:48
verses.text: Follow too the root of the hanging cluster, and thou wilt see where to find it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:49
verses.text: So understand that the one refers to the Pharisee's heart, the other to Moses' seat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:50
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:51
verses.text: But why were they such as they were? "Because," says St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:52
verses.text: Paul, "the vail is upon their heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:53
verses.text: And they do not see that the old things are passed away, and all things are become new".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:54
verses.text: Hence it is that they were such, and all others who even now are like them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:55
verses.text: Why are they old things? Because they have been a long while published.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:56
verses.text: Why new? Because they relate to the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:57
verses.text: How the vail then is taken away, the Apostle himself tells us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:58
verses.text: "But when thou shalt turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:59
verses.text: So then the Jew who does not turn to the Lord, does not carry on his mind's eye to the end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:60
verses.text: Just as at that time the children of Israel in this figure did not carry on the gaze of their eyes "to the end," that is, to the face of Moses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:61
verses.text: For the shining face of Moses contained a figure of the truth; the vail was interposed because the children of Israel could not yet behold the glory of his countenance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:62
verses.text: "Which figure is done away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:63
verses.text: For so said the Apostle; "which is done away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:64
verses.text: Why done away? Because when the emperor comes, the images of him are taken away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:65
verses.text: The image is looked upon, when the emperor is not present; but where he is, whose image it is, there the image is removed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:66
verses.text: There were then images borne before Him, before that our Emperor the Lord Jesus Christ came.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:67
verses.text: When the images were taken away, the glory of the Emperor's presence is seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:68
verses.text: Therefore, "When any one 			 turneth to the Lord, the vail is taken away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:69
verses.text: For the voice of Moses sounded through the vail, but the face of Moses was not seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:70
verses.text: And so now the voice of Christ sounds to the Jews by the voice of the old Scriptures: they hear their voice, but they see not the face of Him that speaketh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:71
verses.text: Would they then that the vail should be taken away? "Let them turn to the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:72
verses.text: For then the old things are not taken away, but laid up in a treasury, that the Scribe may henceforth be "instructed in 			 the kingdom of God, bringing forth out of his treasure" not "new things" only, nor "old things" only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:73
verses.text: For if he bring forth "new things" only or "old things" only; he is not "a scribe instructed in the kingdom of God, bringing forth out of his treasure things new and old".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:74
verses.text: If he say and do them not; he brings forth from the official seat, not from the treasure of his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:75
verses.text: And (we speak the truth, Holy Brethren) what things are brought out of the old, are illustrated by 			 the new.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 23:76
verses.text: Therefore do "we turn to the Lord, that the vail may be taken away".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:1
verses.text: Sermon XXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:2
verses.text: [LXXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:5
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:6
verses.text: 24, "But the boat was now in the midst of the sea, distressed by the waves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:8
verses.text: The lesson of the Gospel which we have just heard is a lesson of humility to us all, that we may see and know where we are, and whither we must tend and hasten.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:9
verses.text: For that ship which carries the disciples, which was tossed in the waves by a contrary wind, is not without its meaning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:10
verses.text: Nor without a meaning did the Lord after He had left the multitudes, go up into a mountain to pray alone; and then coming to His disciples found them in danger, walking on the sea, and getting up into the ship strengthened them, and appeased the waves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:11
verses.text: But what marvel if He can appease all things who created all? Nevertheless after He was come up into the ship, they who were being borne in her, came saying, "Of a truth Thou art the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:12
verses.text: But before this plain discovery of Himself they were troubled, saying, "It is a phantom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:13
verses.text: But He coming up into the ship took away the fluctuation of mind from their hearts, when they were now more endangered in their souls by doubting, than before in their bodies by the waves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:14
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:15
verses.text: Yet in all this that the Lord did, He instructs us as to the nature of our life here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:16
verses.text: In this world there is not a man who is not a stranger; though all do not desire to return to their own country.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:17
verses.text: Now by this very journey we are exposed to waves and tempests; but we must needs be at least in the ship.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:18
verses.text: For if there be perils in the ship, without the ship there is certain destruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:19
verses.text: For whatever strength of arm he may have who swims in the open sea, yet in time 			 he is carried away and sunk, mastered by the greatness of its waves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:20
verses.text: Need then there is that we be in the ship, that is, that we be carried in the wood, that we may be able to cross this sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:21
verses.text: Now this Wood in which our weakness is carried is the Cross of the Lord, by which we are signed, and delivered from the dangerous tempests of this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:22
verses.text: We are exposed to the violence of the waves; but He who helpeth us is God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:23
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:24
verses.text: For in that when the Lord had left the multitudes, "He went up alone into a mountain to pray;" that mountain signifies the height of heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:25
verses.text: For having left the multitudes, the Lord after His Resurrection ascended Alone into heaven, and "there," as the Apostle says, "He maketh intercession for us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:26
verses.text: There is some meaning then in His "leaving the multitudes, and going up into a mountain to pray Alone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:27
verses.text: For He Alone is as yet the First-begotten from the dead, after the resurrection of His Body, unto the right hand of the Father, the High Priest and Advocate of our prayers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:28
verses.text: The Head of the Church is above, that the rest of the members may follow at the end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:29
verses.text: If then "He maketh intercession for us," above the height of all creatures, as it were on the mountain top, 			 "He prayeth Alone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:31
verses.text: Meanwhile the ship which carries the disciples, that is, the Church, is tossed and shaken by the tempests of temptation; and the contrary wind, that is, the devil her adversary, rests not, and strives to hinder her from arriving at rest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:32
verses.text: But greater is "He who maketh intercession for us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:33
verses.text: For in this our tossing to and fro in which we toil, He giveth us confidence in coming to us, and strengthening us; only let us not in our trouble throw ourselves out of the ship, 			 and cast ourselves into the sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:34
verses.text: For though the ship be in trouble, still it is the ship.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:35
verses.text: She alone carrieth the disciples, and receiveth Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:36
verses.text: There is danger, it is true, in the sea; but without her there is instant perishing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:37
verses.text: Keep thyself therefore in the ship, and pray to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:38
verses.text: For when all counsels fail, when even the rudder is unserviceable, and the very spreading of the sails is rather dangerous than useful, when all human help and strength is gone, there remains only for the sailors 			 the earnest cry of entreaty, and pouring out of prayer to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:39
verses.text: He then who grants to sailors to reach the haven, shall He so forsake His own Church, as not to bring it on to rest?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:40
verses.text: Yet, Brethren, this exceeding trouble is not in this ship, save only in the absence of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:41
verses.text: What! can he who is in the Church, have his Lord absent from him? When has he his Lord absent from him? When he is overcome by any lust.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:42
verses.text: For as we find it said in a certain place in a figure, "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath: neither give place to the devil:" and this is understood not of this visible sun which holds as it were the zenith of glory among the rest of the visible creation, and which can be seen equally by us and by the beasts; but of that Light which none but the pure hearts of the faithful see; as it is written, "That was the true Light, which lighteneth every man that cometh into the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:43
verses.text: For this light of the visible sun "lighteneth" even the minutest and smallest animals.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:44
verses.text: Righteousness then and wisdom is that true light, which the mind ceases to see, when it is overcome by the disordering of anger as by a cloud; and then, as it were, the sun goes down upon a man's wrath.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:45
verses.text: So also in this ship, when Christ is absent, every one is shaken by his own storms, and iniquities, and evil desires.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:46
verses.text: For, for example, the law tells thee, "Thou shall not bear false 			 witness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:47
verses.text: If thou observe the truth of witness, thou hast light in the soul; but if overcome by the desire of filthy lucre, thou hast determined in thy mind to speak false witness, thou wilt at once begin through Christ's absence to be troubled by the tempest, thou wilt be tossed to and fro by the waves of thy covetousness, thou wilt be endangered by the violent storm of thy lusts, and as it were through Christ's absence be well nigh sunk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:48
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:49
verses.text: What cause of fear is there, lest the ship be diverted from her course, and take a backward direction; which happens when, abandoning the hope of heavenly rewards, desire turneth the helm, and a man is turned to those things which are seen and pass away! For whosoever is disturbed by the temptations of lusts, and nevertheless still looks into those things which are within, is not so utterly in a desperate state, if he beg pardon for his faults, and exert himself to 			 overcome and surmount the fury of the raging sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:50
verses.text: But he who is so turned aside from what he was, as to say in his heart, "God does not see me; for He does not think of me, nor care whether I sin;" he hath turned the helm, borne away by the storm, and driven back to the point he came from.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:51
verses.text: For there are many thoughts in the hearts of men; and when Christ is absent, the ship is tossed by the waves of this world, and by tempests manifold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:52
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:53
verses.text: Now the fourth watch of the night, is the end of the night; for each watch consists of three hours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:54
verses.text: It signifies then, that now in the end of the world the Lord is come to help, and is seen to walk upon the waters.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:55
verses.text: For though this ship be tossed about by the storms of temptations, yet she sees her Glorified God walking above all the swellings of the sea; that is, above all the principalities of this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:56
verses.text: For before it was said by an expression suited to the 			 time of His Passion,when according to the flesh He showed forth an example of humility, that the waves of the sea vainly raged against Him, to which He yielded voluntarily for our sakes, that that prophecy, "I am come into the depths of the sea, and the floods overflow Me," might be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:57
verses.text: For He did not repel the false witnesses, nor the savage shout of those that said, "Let Him be crucified".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:58
verses.text: He did not by His power repress the savage hearts and words of those furious men, but in patience endured them all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:59
verses.text: They did unto Him whatsoever they listed; because He "became obedient to death, even the death of the Cross".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:60
verses.text: But after that He was risen from the dead, that He might pray alone for His disciples placed in the Church as in a ship, and borne on in the faith of His Cross, as in wood, and in peril through this world's temptations as through the waves of the sea; His Name began to be honoured even in this world in which He was despised, accused, and slain; that He who in the dispensation of His suffering in the flesh, "had come into the depths of the sea, and the floods had 			 overwhelmed Him," might now through the glory of His Name tread upon the necks of the proud as on the foaming waters.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:61
verses.text: Just as we now see the Lord walking as it were upon the sea, under whose feet we behold the whole madness of this world subjected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:62
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:63
verses.text: But to the perils of tempests are added also the errors of heretics; and there are not wanting those who so try the minds of them that are in the ship, as to say that Christ was not born of a Virgin, nor had a real body, but seemed to the eyes what He was not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:64
verses.text: And these opinions of heretics have sprung up now, when the Name of Christ is already glorified throughout all nations; when Christ, that is, is as it were now walking on the sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:65
verses.text: The disciples in their trial said, "It is a phantom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:66
verses.text: But He giveth us strength against these pestilent opinions by His own voice, "Be of good cheer, it is I; be not afraid".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:67
verses.text: For men in vain fear have conceived these opinions concerning Christ, looking at his Honour and Majesty; and they think that He could not be so born, who hath deserved to be so Glorified, fearing Him as it were "walking on the sea".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:68
verses.text: For by this action the excellency of His honour is figured; and so they think that He was a phantom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:69
verses.text: But when he saith, "It is I;" what else doth He say but that there is nothing in Him which does not really exist? 			 Accordingly if He showeth His flesh, it is flesh; if bones, they are bones; if scars, they are scars.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:70
verses.text: For "there was not in Him yea and nay, but in Him was yea," as the Apostle says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:71
verses.text: Hence that expression, "Be of good cheer, it is I; be not afraid".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:72
verses.text: That is, do not so stand in awe of My Majesty, as to wish to take away the reality of My Being from Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:73
verses.text: Though I walk upon the sea, though I have under My feet the elation and the pride of this world, as the raging waves, yet have I appeared as very Man, yet does My Gospel proclaim the very truth concerning Me, that I was born of a Virgin, that I am the Word made flesh; that I said 			 truly, "Handle Me, and see, for a spirit hath not bones as ye see Me have," that they were true impresses of My wounds which the hands of the doubting Apostle handled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:74
verses.text: And therefore "It is I; be not afraid".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:75
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:76
verses.text: But this, that the disciples thought He was a phantom, does not represent these only, does not designate them only who deny that the Lord had human flesh, and who sometimes by their blind perverseness disturb even those who are in the ship; but those also who think that the Lord has in anything spoken falsely, and who do not believe that the things which He has threatened the ungodly will come to pass.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:77
verses.text: As though He were partly true, and partly false, appearing 			 like a phantom in His words, as though He were something which is "yea and nay".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:78
verses.text: But they who understand His voice aright, who saith, "It is I; be not afraid;" believe at once all the words of the Lord, so that as they hope for the rewards He promises, so do they fear the punishments He threatens.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:79
verses.text: For as that is true which He will say to those who are set on the right hand, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;" 			  so is that true, which they on the left hand will hear, "Depart ye into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his Angels".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:80
verses.text: For this very opinion, by which men think that Christ's threatenings against the unrighteous and the abandoned are not true, has arisen from this, that they see many nations and multitudes innumerable subject to His Name; so that hence Christ appears to them to be a phantom, because He walked upon the sea; that is, He seems to speak falsely in His threats of punishment, because, as it were, He cannot destroy such numberless people who are subject to His Name and honour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:81
verses.text: But 			 let them hear Him, saying, "It is I;" let them not therefore "be afraid," who believing Christ to be true in all things, not only seek after what He hath promised, but avoid also what He hath threatened; because though He walk upon the sea, that is, though all the nations of men in this world are subject unto Him; yet is He no phantom, and therefore He doth not speak falsely, when He saith, "Not every one that saith unto Me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:82
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:83
verses.text: What then does Peter's daring to come to Him on the waters also signify? For Peter generally stands for a figure of the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:84
verses.text: What else then do we think is meant by, "Lord, if it be Thou, bid me come unto Thee on the water;" but, Lord, if Thou art true, and in nothing speakest falsely, let Thy Church also be glorified in this world, because prophecy hath proclaimed this concerning Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:85
verses.text: Let her walk then on the waters, and so let her come to Thee, to whom it is said, "The rich among the people shall entreat Thy favour".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:86
verses.text: But since to the Lord the praise of men is no temptation, but men are ofttimes in the Church disordered by human praises and honours, and well nigh sunk by them; therefore did Peter tremble in the sea, terrified at the great violence of the storm.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:87
verses.text: For who does not fear those words, "They who call thee blessed cause thee to err, and disturb the ways of thy feet?" And because the soul hath much wrestling against the eager desire of human praise, good is it in such peril to betake one's self to prayer and earnest entreaty: lest haply he who is charmed with praise, be overwhelmed and sunk by blame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:88
verses.text: Let Peter cry out as he totters in the water, and say, "Lord, save me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:89
verses.text: For the Lord will reach forth His hand, and though He chide, saying, "O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?" wherefore didst thou not look straight 			 forward upon Him to whom thou wast making thy way, and glory only in the Lord? Nevertheless He will snatch him from the waves, and will not suffer Him to perish, who confesses his own infirmity, and begs His help.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:90
verses.text: But when they had received the Lord into the ship, and their faith was strengthened and all doubt removed, and the tempests of the sea assuaged, so that they were come to a firm and secure landing, they all worship Him, saying, "Of a truth Thou art the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 24:91
verses.text: For this is 			 that everlasting joy, where Truth made manifest, and the Word of God, and the Wisdom by which all things were made, and the exceeding height of His Mercy, are both known and loved.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:1
verses.text: Sermon XXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:2
verses.text: [LXXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:4
verses.text: ]  Again on Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:5
verses.text: xiv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:6
verses.text: 25: Of the Lord walking on the waves of the sea, and of Peter tottering.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:8
verses.text: The Gospel which has just been read touching the Lord Christ, who walked on the waters of the sea; and the Apostle Peter, who as he was walking, tottered through fear, and sinking in distrust, rose again by confession, gives us to understand that the sea is the present world, and the Apostle Peter the type of the One Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:9
verses.text: For Peter in the order of Apostles first, and in the love of Christ most forward, answers oftentimes alone for all the rest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:10
verses.text: Again, when the Lord Jesus Christ asked, whom men said that He was, and when the disciples gave the various opinions of men, and 			 the Lord asked again and said, "But whom say ye that I am?" Peter answered, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:11
verses.text: One for many gave the answer, Unity in many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:12
verses.text: Then said the Lord to Him, "Blessed art thou, Simon Barjonas: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but My Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:13
verses.text: Then He added, "and I say unto thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:14
verses.text: As if He had said, "Because thou hast said unto Me, 'Thou art the Christ the Son of the living God;' I also say unto thee, 'Thou art Peter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:15
verses.text: '" For before he was called Simon.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:16
verses.text: Now this name of Peter was given him by the Lord, and that in a figure, that he should signify the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:17
verses.text: For seeing that Christ is the rock (Petra), Peter is the Christian people.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:18
verses.text: For the rock (Petra) is the original name.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:19
verses.text: Therefore Peter is so called 			  from the rock; not the rock from Peter; as Christ is not called Christ from the Christian, but the Christian from Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:20
verses.text: "Therefore," he saith, "Thou art Peter; and upon this Rock" which thou hast confessed, upon this Rock which thou hast acknowledged, saying, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God, will I build My Church;" that is upon Myself, the Son of the living God, "will I build My Church".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:21
verses.text: I will build thee upon Myself, not Myself upon 			 thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:23
verses.text: For men who wished to be built upon men, said, "I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas," who is Peter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:24
verses.text: But others who did not wish to be built upon Peter, but upon the Rock, said, "But I am of Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:25
verses.text: And when the Apostle Paul ascertained that he was chosen, and Christ despised, he said, "Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?" And, as not in the name of Paul, so neither in the name of Peter; but in the name of Christ: that Peter might be built upon the Rock, not the Rock upon Peter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:26
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:27
verses.text: This same Peter therefore who had been by the Rock pronounced "blessed," bearing the figure of the Church, holding the chief place in the Apostleship, a very little while after that he had heard that he was "blessed," a very little while after that he had heard that he was "Peter," a very little while after that he had heard that he was to be "built upon the Rock," displeased the Lord when He had heard of His future Passion, for He had foretold His disciples that it was soon to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:28
verses.text: He feared lest he should by death, lose Him whom he had confessed as the fountain of life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:29
verses.text: He was troubled, and said, "Be it far 			 from Thee, Lord: this shall not be to Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:30
verses.text: Spare Thyself, O God, I am not willing that Thou shouldest die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:31
verses.text: Peter said to Christ, I am not willing that Thou shouldest die; but Christ far better said, I am willing to die for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:32
verses.text: And then He forthwith rebuked him, whom He had a little before commended; and calleth him Satan, whom he had pronounced "blessed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:33
verses.text: "Get thee behind Me, Satan," he saith, "thou art an offence unto Me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:34
verses.text: What would He have us do in our present state, who thus findeth fault because we are men? Would you know what He would have us do? Give ear to the Psalm; "I have said, Ye are gods, and ye are all the children of the Most High".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:35
verses.text: But by savouring the things of men; "ye shall die like men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:36
verses.text: The very same Peter a little while before blessed, afterwards Satan, in one moment, within a few words! Thou wonderest at the difference of the names, mark the difference of the reasons of them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:37
verses.text: Why wonderest thou that he who was a little before blessed, is afterwards Satan? Mark the reason wherefore he is blessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:38
verses.text: "Because flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but My Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:39
verses.text: Therefore blessed, because flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:40
verses.text: For if flesh and blood revealed this to thee, it were of thine own; but because flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but My Father which is in heaven, it is of Mine, not of thine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:41
verses.text: Why of Mine? "Because all things that the Father hath are Mine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:42
verses.text: So then thou hast heard the cause, why he is "blessed," and why he is "Peter".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:43
verses.text: But why was he that which we shudder at, and are loth to repeat, why, but because it was of thine own? "For thou savourest not the things which be of God, but those that be of men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:44
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:45
verses.text: Let us, looking at ourselves in this member of the Church, distinguish what is of God, and what of ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:46
verses.text: For then we shall not totter, then shall we be founded on the Rock, shall be fixed and firm against the winds, and storms, and streams, the temptations, I mean, of this present world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:47
verses.text: Yet see this Peter, who was then our figure; now he trusts, and now he totters; now he confesses the Undying, and now he fears lest He should die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:48
verses.text: Wherefore? 			 because the Church of Christ hath both strong and weak ones; and cannot be without either strong or weak; whence the Apostle Paul says, "Now we that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:49
verses.text: In that Peter said, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God," he represents the strong: but in that he totters, and would not that Christ should suffer, in fearing death for Him, and not acknowledging the Life, he represents the weak ones of the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:50
verses.text: In that one Apostle then, that is, Peter, in the order of Apostles first and chiefest, in whom the Church was figured, both sorts were to be represented, that is, both the strong and weak; because the Church doth 			 not exist without them both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:51
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:52
verses.text: And hence also is that which was just now read, "Lord, if it be Thou, bid me come unto Thee on the water".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:53
verses.text: For I cannot do this in myself, but in Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:54
verses.text: He acknowledged what he had of himself, and what of Him, by whose will he believed that he could do that, which no human weakness could do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:55
verses.text: Therefore, "if it be Thou, bid me;" because when thou biddest, it will be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:56
verses.text: What I cannot do by taking it upon myself, Thou canst do by bidding me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:57
verses.text: And the Lord said "Come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:58
verses.text: And without any doubting, at the word of Him who bade him, at the presence of Him who sustained, at the presence of Him who guided him, without any delay, Peter leaped down into the water, and began to walk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:59
verses.text: He was able to do what the Lord was doing, not in himself, but in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:60
verses.text: "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:61
verses.text: What no one can do in Paul, no one in Peter, no one in any other of the Apostles, this can he do in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:62
verses.text: Therefore well said Paul by a wholesome despising of himself, and commending of Him; "Was Paul crucified for you, or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?" So then, ye are not in me, but together with me; not under me, but under Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:63
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:64
verses.text: Therefore Peter walked on the water by the bidding of the Lord, knowing that he could not have this power of himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:65
verses.text: By faith he had strength to do what human weakness could not do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:66
verses.text: These are the strong ones of the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:67
verses.text: Mark this, hear, understand, and act accordingly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:68
verses.text: For we must not deal with the strong on any other principle than this, that so they should become weak; but thus we must deal with the weak, that they may become strong.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:69
verses.text: But the presuming on their own strength keeps many back from strength.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:70
verses.text: No one will have strength from God, but he who feels himself weak of himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:71
verses.text: "God setteth apart a spontaneous rain for His inheritance".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:72
verses.text: Why do you, who know what I was about to say, anticipate me? Let your quickness be moderated, that the slowness of the rest may follow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:73
verses.text: This I said, and I say it again; hear it, receive it, and act on this principle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:74
verses.text: No one is made strong by God, but he who feels himself weak of his own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:75
verses.text: And therefore a "spontaneous rain," as the Psalm says, "spontaneous;" not of our deserts, but "spontaneous".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:76
verses.text: "A spontaneous rain" therefore "God setteth apart for his 			 inheritance;" for "it was weak; but Thou hast perfected it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:77
verses.text: Because Thou "hast set apart for it a spontaneous rain," not looking to men's deserts, but to Thine own grace and mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:78
verses.text: This inheritance then was weakened, and acknowledged its own weakness in itself, that it might be strong in Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:79
verses.text: It would not be strengthened, if it were not weak, that by Thee it might be "perfected" in Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:80
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:81
verses.text: See Paul a small portion of this inheritance, see him in weakness, who said, "I am not meet to be called an Apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:82
verses.text: Why then art thou an Apostle? "By the grace of God I am what I am.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:83
verses.text: I am not meet, but by the grace of God I am what I am".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:84
verses.text: Paul was "weak," but Thou hast "perfected" him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:85
verses.text: But now because by "the grace of God he is what he is," look what follows; "And His grace in me was not in vain, but 			 I laboured more abundantly than they all".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:86
verses.text: Take heed lest thou lose by presumption what thou hast attained through weakness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:87
verses.text: This is well, very well; that "I am not meet to be called an Apostle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:88
verses.text: By His grace I am what I am, and His grace in me was not in vain:" all most excellent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:89
verses.text: But, "I laboured more abundantly than they all;" thou hast begun, it would seem, to ascribe to thyself what a little before thou hadst given to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:90
verses.text: Attend and follow on; "Yet not I, but the grace of God with me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:91
verses.text: Well! thou weak one; thou shalt be exalted in exceeding strength, seeing thou 			 art not unthankful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:92
verses.text: Thou art the very same Paul, little in thyself; and great in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:93
verses.text: Thou art he who didst thrice beseech the Lord, that "the thorn of the flesh, the messenger of Satan, by whom thou wast buffeted, might be taken away from thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:94
