verses.text: And what was said to thee? what didst thou hear when thou madest this petition? "My grace is sufficient for thee: for My strength is made perfect in weakness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:95
verses.text: For he was "weak," but Thou didst "perfect" him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:96
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:97
verses.text: So Peter also said, "Bid me come unto Thee on the water".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:98
verses.text: I who dare this am but a man, but it is no man whom I beseech.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:99
verses.text: Let the God-man bid, that man may be able to do what man cannot do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:100
verses.text: "Come," said He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:101
verses.text: And He went down, and began to walk on the water; and Peter was able, because the Rock had bidden him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:102
verses.text: Lo, what Peter was in the Lord; what was he in himself? "When he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried out, Lord, 			 I perish, save me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:103
verses.text: When he looked for strength from the Lord, he had strength from the Lord; as a man he tottered, but he returned to the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:104
verses.text: "If I said, my foot hath slipped" (they are the words of a Psalm, the notes of a holy song; and if we acknowledge them they are our words too; yea, if we will, they are ours also).

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:105
verses.text: "If I said my foot hath slipped".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:106
verses.text: How slipped, except because it was mine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:107
verses.text: And what follows? "Thy mercy, Lord, helped me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:108
verses.text: Not mine own strength, but Thy mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:109
verses.text: For will God forsake him as he totters, whom He heard when calling upon Him? Where then is that, "Who hath called upon God, and hath been forsaken by Him?" 			  where again is that, "Whosoever shall call on the Name of the Lord, shall be delivered".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:110
verses.text: Immediately reaching forth the help of His right hand, He lifted him up as he was sinking, and rebuked his distrust; "O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?" Once thou didst trust in Me, hast thou now doubted of Me?  9.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:111
verses.text: Well, brethren, my sermon must be ended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:112
verses.text: Consider the world to be the sea; the wind is boisterous, and there is a mighty tempest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:113
verses.text: Each man's peculiar lust is his tempest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:114
verses.text: Thou dost love God; thou walkest upon the sea, and under thy feet is the swelling of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:115
verses.text: Thou dost love the world, it will swallow thee up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:116
verses.text: It skilleth only how to devour its lovers, not to carry them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:117
verses.text: But when thy heart is tossed about by lust, in order that thou mayest get the better of thy 			 lust, call upon the Divinity of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:118
verses.text: Think ye that the wind is then contrary, when there is this life's adversity? For so when there are wars, when there is tumult, when there is famine, when there is pestilence, when even to every individual man his private calamity arriveth, then the wind is thought to be contrary, then it is thought that God must be called upon.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:119
verses.text: But when the world wears her smile of temporal happiness, it is as if there were no contrary wind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:120
verses.text: But do not ask upon this 			 matter the tranquil state of the times: ask only your own lust.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:121
verses.text: See if there be tranquillity within thee: see if there be no inner wind which overturns thee; see to this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:122
verses.text: There needs great virtue to struggle with happiness, lest this very happiness allure, corrupt, and overthrow thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:123
verses.text: There needs, I say, great virtue to struggle with happiness, and great happiness not to be overcome by happiness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:124
verses.text: Learn then to tread upon the world; remember to trust in Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:125
verses.text: And "if thy foot have 			 slipped;" if thou totter, if some things there are which thou canst not overcome, if thou begin to sink, say, "Lord, I perish, save me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:126
verses.text: Say, "I perish," that thou perish not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:127
verses.text: For He only can deliver thee from the death of the body, who died in the body for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 25:128
verses.text: Let us turn to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:1
verses.text: Sermon XXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:2
verses.text: [LXXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:5
verses.text: xv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:6
verses.text: 21,"Jesus went out thence, and withdrew into the parts of Tyre and Sidon.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:7
verses.text: And behold, a Canaanitish woman," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:9
verses.text: This woman of Canaan, who has just now been brought before us in the lesson of the Gospel, shows us an example of humility, and the way of godliness; shows us how to rise from humility unto exaltation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:10
verses.text: Now she was, as it appears, not of the people of Israel, of whom came the Patriarchs, and Prophets, and the parents of the Lord Jesus Christ according to the flesh; of whom the Virgin Mary herself was, who was the Mother of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:11
verses.text: This 			 woman then was not of this people; but of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:12
verses.text: For, as we have heard, the Lord "departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, and behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts," and with the greatest earnestness begged of Him the mercy to heal her daughter, "who was grievously vexed with a devil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:13
verses.text: Tyre and Sidon were not cities of the people of Israel, but of the Gentiles; though they bordered on that people.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:14
verses.text: So then, as being eager to obtain mercy she cried out, and boldly knocked; and He made as though He heard her not, not to the end that mercy might be refused her, but that her desire might be enkindled; and not only that her desire might be enkindled, but that, as I have said before, her humility might be set forth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:15
verses.text: Therefore did she cry, while the Lord was as though He heard her not, but was ordering in silence what He was about to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:16
verses.text: The disciples besought the Lord for her, and said, "Send her away; for she crieth after us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:17
verses.text: And He said, "I am not sent, but unto the lost sheep of 			 the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:18
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:19
verses.text: Here arises a question out of these words; "If He was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, how came we from among the Gentiles into Christ's fold? What is the meaning of the so deep economy of this mystery, that whereas the Lord knew the purpose of His coming—that He might have a Church in all nations, He said that 'He was not sent, but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel'?" We understand then by this that it behoved Him to manifest His Bodily presence, His Birth, the exhibition of His miracles, and the power of His Resurrection, among that people: that so it had been ordained, so set forth from the beginning, so predicted, and so fulfilled; that 			 Christ Jesus was to come to the nation of the Jews, to be seen and slain, and to gain from among them those whom He foreknew.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:20
verses.text: For that people was not wholly condemned, but sifted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:21
verses.text: There was among them a great quantity of chaff, but there was also the hidden worth of the grain; there was among them that which was to be burnt, there was among them also that wherewith the barn was to be filled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:22
verses.text: For whence came the Apostles? whence came Peter? whence the rest?  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:23
verses.text: Whence was Paul himself, who was first called Saul? That is, first proud, afterwards humble? For when he was Saul, his name was derived from Saul: now Saul was a proud king; and in his reign he persecuted the humble David.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:24
verses.text: So when he who was afterwards Paul, was Saul, he was proud, at that time a persecutor of the innocent, at that time a waster of the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:25
verses.text: For he had received letters from the chief priests (burning as he was with zeal for the synagogue, and persecuting the Christian name), that he might show up whatever Christians he should find, to be punished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:26
verses.text: While he is on his way, while he is breathing out slaughter, while he is thirsting for blood, he is thrown to the ground by the voice of Christ from heaven the persecutor, he is raised up the preacher.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:27
verses.text: In him was fulfilled that which is written in the Prophet, "I will wound and I will heal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:28
verses.text: For that only in man doth God wound, which lifteth itself up against God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:29
verses.text: He is no unkind physician who opens the swelling, who cuts, or cauterizes the corrupted part.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:30
verses.text: He gives pain, it is true; but he only gives pain, that he may bring the patient on to health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:31
verses.text: He gives pain; but if he did not, he would do no good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:32
verses.text: Christ then by one word laid Saul low, and raised up Paul; that is, He laid low the proud, and raised up the humble.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:33
verses.text: For what was the reason of his change of name, that whereas he was afore called Saul, he chose afterwards to be called Paul; but that he 			 acknowledged in himself that the name of Saul when he was a persecutor, had been a name of pride? He chose therefore a humble name; to be called Paul, that is, the least.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:34
verses.text: For Paul is, "the least".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:35
verses.text: Paul is nothing else but little.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:36
verses.text: And now glorying in this name, and giving us a lesson of humility, he says, "I am the least of the Apostles".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:37
verses.text: Whence then, whence was he, but of the people of the Jews? Of them were the other Apostles, of them was Paul, of them were they whom the same Paul mentions, as having seen the Lord after His resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:38
verses.text: For he says, "That He was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:39
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:40
verses.text: Of this people too, of the people of the Jews, were they, who when Peter was speaking, setting forth the Passion, and Resurrection, and Divinity of Christ (after that the Holy Ghost had been received, when all they on whom the Holy Ghost had come, spake with the tongues of all nations), being pricked in spirit as they heard him, sought counsel for their salvation, understanding as they did that they were guilty of the Blood of Christ; because they had crucified, 			 and slain Him, in whose name though slain by them they saw such great miracles wrought; and saw the presence of the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:41
verses.text: And so seeking counsel they received for answer; "Repent, and be baptized every one of you, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and your sins shall be forgiven you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:42
verses.text: Who should despair of the forgiveness of his sins, when the crime of killing Christ was forgiven to those who were guilty of it? They were converted from among this people of the Jews; were converted, and baptized.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:43
verses.text: They came to the Lord's table, and in faith drank that Blood, which in their fury they had shed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:44
verses.text: Now in what sort they were converted, how decidedly, and how perfectly, the Acts of the Apostles show.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:45
verses.text: "For they sold all that they possessed, and laid the prices of their things at the Apostles' feet; and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need; and no man said that ought was his own, but they had all things common".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:46
verses.text: And, "They were," as it is written, "of one heart and of one soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:47
verses.text: Lo here are the sheep of whom He said, "I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:48
verses.text: For to them He exhibited His Presence, for them in the midst of their violence against Him He prayed as He was being crucified, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:49
verses.text: The Physician understood how those frenzied men were in their madness putting the Physician to death, and in putting their Physician to death, though they knew it not, were preparing a medicine for themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:50
verses.text: For by the Lord so put to death are all we cured, by His Blood redeemed, by the Bread of His Body delivered from famine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:51
verses.text: This Presence then did Christ exhibit to the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:52
verses.text: And so He said, "I am not sent, but unto the lost sheep of the house of 			 Israel;" that to them He might exhibit the Presence of His body; not that He might disregard, and pass over the sheep which He had among the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:53
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:54
verses.text: For to the Gentiles He went not Himself, but sent His disciples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:55
verses.text: And in this was fulfilled what the Prophet said; "A people whom I have not known hath served Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:56
verses.text: See how deep, how clear, how express the prophecy is; "a people whom I have not known," that is, to whom I have not exhibited My Presence, "hath served Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:57
verses.text: How? It goes on to say, "By the hearing of the ear they have obeyed Me:" that is, they have believed, not by seeing, but by hearing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:58
verses.text: Therefore have the Gentiles the greater praise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:59
verses.text: For the others saw and slew Him; the Gentiles heard and believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:60
verses.text: Now it was to call and gather together the Gentiles, that that might be fulfilled which we have just now chanted, "Gather us from among the Gentiles, that we may confess to Thy Name, and glory in Thy praise," that the Apostle Paul was sent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:61
verses.text: He, the least, made great, not by himself, but by Him whom he once persecuted, was sent to the Gentiles, from a robber become a shepherd, from a wolf a sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:62
verses.text: He, the least Apostle, was sent to the Gentiles, and laboured much among the Gentiles, and through him the Gentiles believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:63
verses.text: His Epistles are the witnesses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:64
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:65
verses.text: Of this you have a very sacred figure in the Gospel also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:66
verses.text: A daughter of a ruler of the synagogue was really dead, and her father besought the Lord, that He would go to her; he had left her sick, and in extreme danger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:67
verses.text: The Lord set out to visit and heal the sick; in the mean time it was announced that she was dead, and it was told the father; "Thy daughter is dead, trouble not the Master".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:68
verses.text: But the Lord who knew that He could raise the dead, did not deprive the despairing father of hope, and said to him, "Fear not: only believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:69
verses.text: So he set out to the maiden; and in the way a certain woman, who had suffered from an issue of blood, and in her lengthened illness had spent to no purpose 			 all that she had upon physicians, pressed herself in, how she could, amongst the crowds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:70
verses.text: When she touched the border of His garment, she was made whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:71
verses.text: And the Lord said, "Who touched Me?" The disciples who knew not what had taken place, and saw that He was thronged by the multitudes, and that He was troubling Himself about one single woman who had touched Him gently, answered in astonishment, "The multitudes press Thee, and sayest Thou, Who touched Me? And He said, Somebody hath touched 			 Me? for the other press, she hath touched.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:72
verses.text: The many then rudely press the Body of Christ, few touch it healthfully.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:73
verses.text: "Somebody," saith He, "hath touched Me, for I perceive that virtue is gone out of Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:74
verses.text: And when the woman saw that she was not hid, she fell down at His feet," and confessed what had taken place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:75
verses.text: After this He set out again, and arrived whither He was going, and raised to life the young daughter of the ruler of the synagogue who was found to be dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:76
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:77
verses.text: This was a literal fact, and was fulfilled as it is related; but nevertheless these very things which were done by the Lord had some further signification, being (if we may so say) a sort of visible and significative words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:78
verses.text: And this is especially plain, in that place where He sought fruit on the tree out of season, and because He found none, dried up the tree by His curse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:79
verses.text: Unless this action be regarded as a figure, there is no good meaning in it; first to have sought fruit on that tree when it was not the season for fruit on any tree; and then even if it were now the time of fruit, what fault in the tree was it to have none? But because it signified, that He seeketh not for leaves only, but for fruit also, that is, not for the words only, but for the deeds of men, by drying up that tree whereon he found only leaves, he signified their 			 punishment who can speak good things, but will not do them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:80
verses.text: And so it is in this place also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:81
verses.text: For surely there is a mystery in it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:82
verses.text: He who foreknoweth all things saith, "Who touched Me?" The Creator maketh Himself like one who is ignorant; and He asketh, who not only knew this, but who even foreknew all other things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:83
verses.text: Doubtless there is something which Christ would speak to us in this significant mystery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:84
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:85
verses.text: That daughter of the ruler of the synagogue was a figure of the people of the Jews, for whose sake Christ had come, who said, "I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:86
verses.text: But the woman who suffered from the issue of blood, figured the Church from among the Gentiles, to which Christ was not sent in His bodily presence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:87
verses.text: He was going to the former, He was intent on her recovery; meanwhile the latter runs to meet Him, touches His border as 			 though He knew it not; that is, she is healed by Him who is in some sense absent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:88
verses.text: He saith, "Who touched Me?" as though He would say; I do not know this people; "A people whom I have not known hath served Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:89
verses.text: Some one hath touched Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:90
verses.text: For I perceive that virtue is gone out of Me;" that is, that My Gospel hath gone out and filled the whole world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:91
verses.text: Now it is the border that is touched, a small and outside part of the garment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:92
verses.text: Consider the Apostles as it were the garment of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:93
verses.text: Among them Paul was the border; that is, the last and least.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:94
verses.text: For he said of himself that he was both; "I am the least of the Apostles".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:95
verses.text: For he was called after them all, he believed after them all, he healed more than they all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:96
verses.text: The Lord was not sent but "unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:97
verses.text: But because a "people whom He had not known, was also to serve Him, and to obey Him in the hearing of the ear," He made mention of them too when He was among the others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:98
verses.text: For the same Lord said in a certain place, "Other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, that there may be one 			 fold and one shepherd".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:99
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:100
verses.text: Of these was this woman; therefore she was not refused, but only put off.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:101
verses.text: "I am not sent," saith He, "but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:102
verses.text: And she was instant in her cries: she persevered, she knocked, as if she had already heard, "Ask, and receive; seek, and thou shalt find; knock, and it shall be opened unto thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:103
verses.text: She kept on, she knocked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:104
verses.text: For so the Lord when He spake these words, "Ask, and ye shall receive; seek, and ye shall find; 			 knock, and it shall be opened unto you;" had also said before, "Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you;" that is, lest after despising your pearls, they should even ill use you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:105
verses.text: Cast not therefore before them what they despise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:106
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:107
verses.text: And how distinguish we (as might be answered) who are "swine," and who are "dogs"? This has been shown in the case of this woman.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:108
verses.text: For He only answered to her entreaties, "It is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it to dogs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:109
verses.text: Thou art a dog, thou art one of the Gentiles, thou worshippest idols.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:110
verses.text: But for dogs what is so proper as to lick stones? "It is not" therefore "meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it to dogs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:111
verses.text: Had she retired after these words, she had gone away as she had come, a dog; but by knocking she was made of a dog one of human kind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:112
verses.text: For she persevered in asking, and from that reproach as it were she manifested her humility, and obtained mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:113
verses.text: For she was not excited, nor incensed, because she was called a dog, as she asked the blessing, and prayed for mercy, but she said, "Truth, Lord;" "Thou hast called me a dog, and truly a dog I am, I acknowledge my name: it is the Truth that speaks: but I ought not on that account to be refused this blessing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:114
verses.text: Verily I am a dog; 'yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:115
verses.text: ' It is but a moderate and a small blessing I desire; I do not press to the table, I only seek for the crumbs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:116
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:117
verses.text: See, Brethren, how the value of humility is set before us! The Lord had called her a dog; and she did not say, "I am not," but she said, "I am".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:118
verses.text: And because she acknowledged herself to be a dog, immediately the Lord said, "Woman, great is thy faith; be it unto thee even as thou hast asked".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:119
verses.text: Thou hast acknowledged thyself to be a dog, I now acknowledge thee to be of human kind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:120
verses.text: "O woman, great is thy faith;" thou hast asked, and sought, and knocked; receive, find, be it opened unto thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:121
verses.text: See, Brethren, how in this woman who was a Canaanite, that is, who came from among the Gentiles, and was a type, that is a figure, of the Church, the grace of humility has been eminently set before us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:122
verses.text: For the Jewish nation, to the end that it might be deprived of the grace of 			 the Gospel, was puffed up with pride, because to them it had been vouchsafed to receive the Law, because out of this nation the Patriarchs had proceeded, the Prophets had sprung, Moses, the servant of God, had done the great miracles in Egypt which we have heard of in the Psalm, had led the people through the Red Sea, when the waters retired, and had received the Law, which he gave to this people.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:123
verses.text: This was that whereupon the Jewish nation was lifted up, and through this very pride it happened that they were not willing to humble themselves to Christ the author of humility, and the restrainer of proud swelling, to God the Physician, who, being God, for this cause became Man, that man might know himself to be but man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:124
verses.text: O mighty remedy! If this remedy 			 cure not pride, I know not what can cure it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:125
verses.text: He is God, and is made Man; He lays aside His Divinity, that is, in a manner sequestrates, hides, that is, what was His Own, and appears only in that He had taken to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:126
verses.text: Being God He is made man: and man will not acknowledge himself to be man, that is, will not acknowledge himself to be mortal, will not acknowledge himself to be frail, will not acknowledge himself to be a sinner, will not acknowledge himself to be sick, that so at least as sick he may seek the physician; but what is more perilous still, he fancies himself in sound health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:127
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:128
verses.text: So then for this reason that people did not come to Him, that is by reason of pride; and the natural branches are said to be broken off from the olive tree, that is from that people founded by the Patriarchs; in other words, the Jews are for their punishment justly barren through the spirit of pride; and the wild olive is grafted into that olive tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:129
verses.text: The wild olive tree is the people of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:130
verses.text: So says the Apostle, "that the wild olive tree is grafted into the good olive tree, but the natural branches are broken off".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:131
verses.text: Because of pride they were broken off: and the wild olive tree grafted in because of humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:132
verses.text: This humility did the woman show forth when she said, "Truth, Lord," "I am a dog, I desire only the crumbs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:133
verses.text: In this humility also did the Centurion please Him; who when he desired that his servant might be healed by the Lord, and the Lord said, "I will come and heal him," answered, "Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof, but speak the word only, 			 and my servant shall be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:134
verses.text: I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:135
verses.text: He did not receive Him into his house, but he had received Him already in his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:136
verses.text: The more humble, the more capacious, and the more full.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:137
verses.text: For the hills drive back the water, but the valleys are filled by it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:138
verses.text: And what then, what said the Lord to those who followed Him after that he had said, "I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof"? "Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel;" that is, in that people to whom I came, 			 "I have not found so great faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:139
verses.text: And whence great? Great from being the least, that is, great from humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:140
verses.text: "I have not found so great faith;" like a grain of mustard seed, which by how much smaller it is, by so much the more burning is it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:141
verses.text: Therefore did the Lord at once graft the wild olive into the good olive tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:142
verses.text: He did it then when He said, "Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:143
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:144
verses.text: Lastly, mark what follows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:145
verses.text: "Therefore,"—that is, because "I have not found so great faith in Israel," that is, so great humility with faith,—"Therefore I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:146
verses.text: "Shall sit," that is, "shall rest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:147
verses.text: For we must not form notions of carnal banquets there, or desire any such thing in that kingdom, as to change not vices for virtues, but only to make an exchange of vices.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:148
verses.text: For it is one thing to desire the kingdom of heaven for the sake of wisdom and life eternal; another, for the sake of earthly felicity, as though there we should have it in more abundant and greater measure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:149
verses.text: If thou think to be rich in that kingdom, thou dost not 			 cut off, but only changest desire; and yet rich thou wilt really be, and in none other place but there wilt thou be rich; for here thy want gathers together the abundance of things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:150
verses.text: Why have rich men much? Because they want much.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:151
verses.text: A greater want heaps together as it were greater means; there want itself shall die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:152
verses.text: Then thou shalt be truly rich, when thou shalt be in want of nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:153
verses.text: For now thou art not surely rich, and an Angel poor, who has not horses, and carriages, and servants.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:154
verses.text: Why? Because 			 he does not want any of these: because in proportion to his greater strength, is his want the less.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:155
verses.text: Therefore there there are riches, and the true riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:156
verses.text: Figure not to yourselves then banquets of this earth in that place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:157
verses.text: For the banquets of this world are daily medicines; they are necessary for a kind of sickness we have, wherewith we are born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:158
verses.text: This sickness every one is sensible of, when the hour for refreshment is passed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:159
verses.text: Wouldest thou see how great a sickness this is, that as an acute 			 fever would be fatal in seven days? Do not fancy thyself then to be in health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:160
verses.text: Immortality will be health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:161
verses.text: For this present is only one long sickness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:162
verses.text: Because thou dost support thy disease by daily medicines; thou fanciest thyself in health; take away the medicines, and then see what thou canst do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:163
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:164
verses.text: For from the moment we are born, we must needs be dying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:165
verses.text: This disease must needs bring us to death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:166
verses.text: This indeed physicians say when they examine their patients.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:167
verses.text: For instance, "This man has the dropsy, he is dying; this disease cannot be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:168
verses.text: This man has the leprosy: this disease too cannot be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:169
verses.text: He is in a consumption.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:170
verses.text: Who can cure this? He must needs die, he must perish".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:171
verses.text: See, the physician has now pronounced that he is in a consumption; that he cannot but die; and yet sometimes the dropsical patient does not die of his disease, and the leprous does not die of his, nor the consumptive patient of his; but now it is absolutely necessary that every one who is born should die of this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:172
verses.text: He dies of it, he cannot do otherwise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:173
verses.text: This the 			 physician and the unskilled both pronounce upon; and though he die somewhat more slowly, does he on that account not die? Where then is there true health, except where there is true immortality? But if it be true immortality, and no corruption, no wasting, what need will there be there of nourishment? Therefore, when you hear it said, "They shall sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob;" get not your body, but your soul in order.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:174
verses.text: There shall thou be filled; and this inner man has its proper food.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:175
verses.text: In relation to it is it said, "Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:176
verses.text: And so truly filled shall they be that they shall hunger no more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:177
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:178
verses.text: Therefore did the Lord graft in at once the wild olive tree, when He said, "Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven;" that is, they shall be grafted into the good olive tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:179
verses.text: For Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, are the roots of this olive tree; "but the children of the kingdom," that is, the unbelieving Jews, "shall go away into outer darkness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:180
verses.text: The "natural 			 branches shall be broken off," that the "wild olive tree may be grafted in".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:181
verses.text: Now why did the natural branches deserve to be cut off, except for pride? why the wild olive tree to be grafted in, except for humility? Whence also that woman said, "Truth, Lord, yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:182
verses.text: And thereupon she hears, "O woman, great is thy faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:183
verses.text: And so again that centurion, "I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:184
verses.text: "Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:185
verses.text: Let us then learn, or let us hold fast, humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:186
verses.text: If we have it not yet, let us learn it; if we have it, let us not lose it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 26:187
verses.text: If we have it not yet, let us have it, that we may be grafted in; if we have it already, let us hold it fast, that we may not be cut off.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:1
verses.text: Sermon XXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:2
verses.text: [LXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:5
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:6
verses.text: 1, "After six days Jesus taketh with Him Peter, and James, and John his brother," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:8
verses.text: We must now look into and treat of that vision which the Lord showed on the mount.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:9
verses.text: For it is this of which He had said, "Verily I say unto you, there be some standing here which shall not taste of death till they see the Son of Man in His Kingdom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:10
verses.text: Then began the passage which has just been read.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:11
verses.text: "When He had said this, after six days He took three disciples, Peter, and James, and John, and went up into a mountain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:12
verses.text: These three were those "some," of whom He had said, "There be some here which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of Man in His kingdom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:13
verses.text: There is no small difficulty here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:14
verses.text: For that mount was not the whole extent of His kingdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:15
verses.text: What is a mountain to Him who possesseth the heavens? Which we not only read He doth, but in some sort see it with the eyes of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:16
verses.text: He calleth that His kingdom, which in many places He calleth the "kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:17
verses.text: Now the kingdom of heaven is the kingdom of the saints.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:18
verses.text: "For the heavens declare the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:19
verses.text: And of these heavens it is immediately said in the Psalm, "There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:20
verses.text: Their sound is gone out through all the earth, and their words unto the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:21
verses.text: Whose words, but of the heavens? And of the Apostles, and all faithful preachers of the word of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:22
verses.text: These heavens therefore shall reign together with Him who made the heavens.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:23
verses.text: Now consider what was done, that this might be made manifest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:24
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:25
verses.text: The Lord Jesus Himself shone bright as the sun; His raiment became white as the snow; and Moses and Elias talked with Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:26
verses.text: Jesus Himself indeed shone as the sun, signifying that "He is the light which lighteth every man that cometh into the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:27
verses.text: What this sun is to the eyes of the flesh, that is He to the eyes of the heart; and what that is to the flesh of men, that is He to their hearts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:28
verses.text: Now His raiment is His Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:29
verses.text: For if the raiment be not held together by him who puts it on, it will fall off.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:30
verses.text: Of this raiment, Paul was as it were a sort of last border.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:31
verses.text: For he says himself, "I am the least of the Apostles".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:32
verses.text: And in another place, "I am the last of the Apostles".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:33
verses.text: Now in a garment the border is the last and least part.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:34
verses.text: Wherefore as that woman which suffered from an issue of blood, when she had touched the Lord's border was made whole, so the Church which came from out of the Gentiles, was made whole by the preaching of Paul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:35
verses.text: What wonder if the Church is signified by white raiment, when you hear the Prophet Isaiah saying, "Though your sins be as scarlet, I will make them white as snow"? Moses and Elias, that is, the Law and the Prophets, what avail they, except they converse with the Lord? Except they give witness to the Lord, who would read the Law or the Prophets? Mark how briefly the Apostle expresses this; "For by the Law is the knowledge of sin; but now the righteousness of God without the Law is manifested:" behold the sun; "being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets," behold the shining of the Sun.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:36
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:37
verses.text: Peter sees this, and as a man savouring the things of men says, "Lord, it is good for us to be here".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:38
verses.text: He had been wearied with the multitude, he had found now the mountain's solitude; there he had Christ the Bread of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:39
verses.text: What! should he depart thence again to travail and pains, possessed of a holy love to Godward, and thereby of a good conversation? He wished well for himself; and so he added, "If Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles; one for Thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:40
verses.text: To this the Lord made no answer; but notwithstanding Peter was 			 answered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:41
verses.text: "For while he yet spake, a bright cloud came, and overshadowed them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:42
verses.text: He desired three tabernacles; the heavenly answer showed him that we have One, which human judgment desired to divide.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:43
verses.text: Christ, the Word of God, the Word of God in the Law, the Word in the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:44
verses.text: Why, Peter, dost thou seek to divide them? It were more fitting for thee to join them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:45
verses.text: Thou seekest three; understand that they are but One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:46
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:47
verses.text: As the cloud then overshadowed them, and in a way made one tabernacle for them, "a voice also sounded out of the cloud, which said, This is My beloved Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:48
verses.text: Moses was there; Elias was there; yet it was not said, "These are My beloved sons".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:49
verses.text: For the Only Son is one thing; adopted sons another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:50
verses.text: He was singled out in whom the Law and the prophets glorified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:51
verses.text: "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear Him!" Because ye have heard Him in the Prophets, and ye have heard Him in the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:52
verses.text: And where have ye not heard Him? "When they heard this, they fell" to the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:53
verses.text: See then in the Church is exhibited to us the Kingdom of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:54
verses.text: Here is the Lord, here the Law and the Prophets; but the Lord as the Lord; the Law in Moses, Prophecy in Elias; only they as servants and as 			 ministers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:55
verses.text: They as vessels: He as the fountain: Moses and the Prophets spake, and wrote; but when they poured out, they were filled from Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:56
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:57
verses.text: But the Lord stretched out His hand, and raised them as they lay.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:58
verses.text: And then "they saw no man, save Jesus only".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:59
verses.text: What does this mean? When the Apostle was being read, you heard, "For now we see through a glass darkly, but then face to face".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:60
verses.text: And "tongues shall cease," when that which we now hope for and believe shall come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:61
verses.text: In then that they fell to the earth, they signified that we die, for it was said to the flesh, "Earth thou art, and unto earth shalt thou return".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:62
verses.text: But when the Lord raised them up, He signified the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:63
verses.text: After the resurrection, what is the Law to thee? what Prophecy? Therefore neither Moses nor Elias is seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:64
verses.text: He only remaineth to thee, "Who in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:65
verses.text: He remaineth to thee, "that God may be all in all".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:66
verses.text: Moses will be there; but now no more the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:67
verses.text: We shall see Elias there too; but now no more the Prophet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:68
verses.text: For the Law and the Prophets have only given witness to Christ, that it behoved Him to suffer, and to rise again from the dead the third day, and to enter into His glory.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:69
verses.text: And in this glory is fulfilled what He hath promised to them that love Him, "He that loveth Me shall be loved of My Father, and I will love him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:70
verses.text: And as if it were said, What wilt Thou give him, seeing Thou wilt love him? "And I will manifest Myself unto him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:71
verses.text: Great gift! great promise! God doth not reserve for thee as a reward anything of His own, but Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:72
verses.text: O thou covetous one; why doth not what Christ promiseth suffice thee? Thou dost seem to thyself to be rich; yet if thou have not God, what hast thou? Another is poor, yet if he hath God, what hath he not?  6.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:73
verses.text: Come down, Peter: thou wast desiring to rest on the mount; come down, "preach the word, be instant in season, out of season, reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:74
verses.text: Endure, labour hard, bear thy measure of torture; that thou mayest possess what is meant by the white raiment of the Lord, through the brightness and the beauty of an upright labouring in charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:75
verses.text: For when the Apostle was being read we heard in praise of charity, "She seeketh not her own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:76
verses.text: She seeketh not her own;" since she gives what she possesses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:77
verses.text: In another place there is more danger in the expression, if you do not understand it right.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:78
verses.text: For the Apostle, charging the faithful members of Christ after this rule of charity, says, "Let no man seek his own, but another's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:79
verses.text: For on hearing this, covetousness is ready with its deceits, that in a matter of business under pretence of seeking another's, it may defraud a man, and so, "seek not his own, but another's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:80
verses.text: But let covetousness restrain itself, let justice come forth; so let us hear and understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:81
verses.text: It is to charity that it is said, "Let no man seek his own, but another's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:82
verses.text: Now, O thou covetous one, if thou wilt still resist, and twist the precept rather to this point, that thou 			 shouldest covet what is another's; then lose what is thine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:83
verses.text: But as I know thee well, thou dost wish to have both thine own and another's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:84
verses.text: Thou wilt commit fraud that thou mayest have what is another's; submit then to robbery that thou mayest lose thine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:85
verses.text: Thou dost not wish to seek thine own, but then thou takest away what is another's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:86
verses.text: Now this if thou do, thou doest not well.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:87
verses.text: Hear and listen, thou covetous one: the Apostle explains to thee in another place more clearly this that 			 he said, "Let no man seek his own, but another's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:88
verses.text: He says of himself, "Not seeking mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:89
verses.text: This Peter understood not yet when he desired to live on the mount with Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:90
verses.text: He was reserving this for thee, Peter, after death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:91
verses.text: But now He saith Himself, "Come down, to labour in the earth; in the earth to serve, to be despised, and crucified in the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:92
verses.text: The Life came down, that He might be slain; the Bread came down, that He might hunger; the Way came down, that life might be wearied in the way; the Fountain came down, that He might thirst; and dost thou refuse to 			 labour? 'Seek not thine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 27:93
verses.text: ' Have charity, preach the truth; so shall thou come to eternity, where thou shalt find security".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:1
verses.text: Sermon XXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:2
verses.text: [LXXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:4
verses.text: ]  Again on the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:5
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:6
verses.text: , where Jesus showed Himself on the mount to His three disciples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:8
verses.text: We heard when the Holy Gospel was being read of the great vision on the mount, in which Jesus showed Himself to the three disciples, Peter, James, and John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:9
verses.text: "His face did shine as the sun:" this is a figure of the shining of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:10
verses.text: "His raiment was white as the snow:" this is a figure of the purity of the Church, to which it was said by the Prophet, "Though your sins be as scarlet, I will make them white as snow".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:11
verses.text: Elias and Moses were talking with Him; because the grace of the Gospel receives witness from the Law and the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:12
verses.text: The Law is represented in Moses, the Prophets in Elias; to speak briefly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:13
verses.text: For there are the mercies of God vouchsafed through a holy Martyr to be rehearsed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:14
verses.text: Let us give ear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:15
verses.text: Peter desired three tabernacles to be made, one for Moses, one for Elias, and one for Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:16
verses.text: The solitude of the mountain had charms for him; he had been wearied with the tumult of the 			 world's business.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:17
verses.text: But why sought he three tabernacles, but because he knew not as yet the unity of the Law, and of Prophecy, and of the Gospel? Lastly, he was corrected by the cloud, "While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:18
verses.text: Lo, the cloud hath made one tabernacle; wherefore didst thou seek for three? "And a voice came out of the cloud, This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased, hear ye Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:19
verses.text: Elias speaketh; but "hear Him;" "Moses speaketh; but "hear Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:20
verses.text: The Prophets speak, the Law speaketh; but "hear Him," who is the voice of the Law, and the tongue of the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:21
verses.text: He spake in them, and when He vouchsafed so to do, He appeared in His own person.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:22
verses.text: "Hear ye Him:" let us then hear Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:23
verses.text: When the Gospel spake, think it was the cloud: from thence hath the voice sounded out to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 28:24
verses.text: Let us hear Him; that is, let us do what He saith, let us hope for what 			 He hath promised.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:1
verses.text: Sermon XXX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:2
verses.text: [LXXX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:5
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:6
verses.text: 19, "Why could not we cast it out"? etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:7
verses.text: , and on prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:9
verses.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ reproved unbelief even in His own disciples, as we heard just now when the Gospel was being read.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:10
verses.text: For when they had said, "Why could not we cast him out?" He answered, "Because of your unbelief".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:11
verses.text: If the Apostles were unbelievers, who is a believer? What must the lambs do, if the rams totter? Yet the mercy of the Lord did not disdain them in their unbelief; but reproved, nourished, perfected, crowned them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:12
verses.text: For they themselves, as mindful of their own weakness, said to Him, as we read in a certain place in the Gospel, "Lord, increase our faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:13
verses.text: Lord," say they, "increase our faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:14
verses.text: The knowing that they had a deficiency, was the first advantage; a greater happiness still, to know who it was of whom they were asking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:15
verses.text: "Lord," say they, "increase our faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:16
verses.text: See, if they did not bring their hearts as it were to the fountain, and knocked that that might be opened to them, out of which they might fill them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:17
verses.text: For He would that men should knock at Him, not that He might repel those that knock, but that He 			 might exercise those who long.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:18
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:19
verses.text: For do you think, Brethren, that God doth not know what is needful for you? He knoweth and preventeth our desires, who knoweth our want.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:20
verses.text: And so when He taught His disciples to pray, and warned them not to use many words in prayer, He saith, "Use not many words; for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of before ye ask Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:21
verses.text: Now the Lord saith something different from this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:22
verses.text: What is this? Because He misliked that we should use many words in prayer, He said to us, "When ye pray, use not many words; for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of before ye ask Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:23
verses.text: If our "Father knoweth what things we have need of before we ask Him," why do we use even few words? What is the use of prayer at all, if "our Father knoweth" already "what things we have need of"? He saith to one, Do 			 not make thy prayer to Me at great length; for I know what is needful for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:24
verses.text: If so, Lord, why should I so much as pray at all? Thou wouldest not that I should use long prayers, yea rather Thou dost even bid me to use near none at all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:25
verses.text: And then what meaneth that precept in another place? For He who saith, "Use not many words in prayer," saith in another place, "Ask, and it shall be given you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:26
verses.text: And that thou mightest not think that this first precept to ask was given cursorily, He added, "Seek, and ye shall find".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:27
verses.text: And that thou mightest not think that this too was cursorily given, see what He added further, see with what He finished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:28
verses.text: "Knock, and it shall be opened unto you:" see what He added.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:29
verses.text: He would have thee ask that thou mayest receive, and seek that thou mayest find, and knock that thou mayest enter in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:30
verses.text: Seeing then that our Father knoweth already what 			 is needful for us, how and why do we ask? why seek? why knock? why weary ourselves in asking, and seeking, and knocking, to instruct Him who knoweth already? And in another place the words of the Lord are, "Men ought always to pray, and not to faint".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:31
verses.text: If men "ought always to pray," how doth He say, "Use not many words"? How can I always pray, if I so quickly make an end? Here Thou biddest me to finish quickly; there "always to pray and not to faint:" what doth this mean? Now that thou mayest understand this, "ask, seek, knock".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:32
verses.text: For for this cause is it closed, not to shut thee out, but to exercise thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:33
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, ought we to exhort to prayer, both ourselves and you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:34
verses.text: For other hope have we none 			 amid the manifold evils of this present world, than to knock in prayer, to believe and to maintain the belief firm in the heart, that thy Father only doth not give thee what He knoweth is not expedient for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:35
verses.text: For thou knowest what thou dost desire; He knoweth what is good for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:36
verses.text: Imagine thyself under a physician, and in weak health, as is the very truth; for all this life of ours is a weakness; and a long life is nothing else but a prolonged weakness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:37
verses.text: Imagine thyself then to be sick under 			 the physician's hand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:38
verses.text: Thou hast a desire to ask thy physician leave to drink a draught of fresh wine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:39
verses.text: Thou art not prohibited from asking, for it may chance to do thee no harm, or even good to receive it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:40
verses.text: Do not then hesitate to ask; ask, hesitate not; but if thou receive not, do not take it to heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:41
verses.text: Now if thou wouldest act thus in the hands of a man, the physician of the body, how much more in the hands of God, who is the Physician, the Creator, and Restorer, both of thy body and 			 soul?  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:42
verses.text: Wherefore, see how the Lord in this passage exhorted His disciples to prayer, when He said, "Ye could not cast out this devil because of your unbelief".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:43
verses.text: For then exhorting them to prayer He ended thus; "this kind is not cast out but by prayer and fasting".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:44
verses.text: If a man must pray, to cast out devils from another, how much more to cast out his own covetousness? how much more to cast out his own drunkenness? how much more to cast out his own luxuriousness? how much more to cast out his own uncleanness? How many things in a man are there, which if they are persevered in, allow of no admission into the kingdom of heaven! Consider, 			 Brethren, how a physician is entreated for the preservation of temporal health, how, if any one is desperately ill, is he ashamed or slow to throw himself at a man's feet? to bathe in tears the footsteps of any very able chief physician? And what if the physician say to him, "Thou canst not else be cured, except I bind thee, and use the fire and knife"? He will answer," Do what thou wilt, only cure me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:45
verses.text: With what eagerness does he long for the health of a few days, fleeting as a 			 vapour, that for it he is content to be bound, and submit to the fire, and knife, and to be watched, that he neither eat nor drink what, or when, he pleases! All this he will endure, that he may die a little later; and yet he will not endure ever so little, that he may never die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:46
verses.text: If God, who is the Heavenly Physician over us, saith to thee, "Wilt thou be cured?" what wouldest thou say but "Yes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:47
verses.text: Or it may be thou wouldest not say so, because thou fanciest thyself to be in health, that 			 is, because thou art more grievously sick.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:48
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:49
verses.text: For if we suppose two sick persons, one who implores the physician with tears, the other, who in his sickness with infatuation derides him; he will hold out hope to the one that weeps, and will deplore the case of the other that laughs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:50
verses.text: Why? but because the sounder in health he thinks himself, the more dangerous his sickness is! This was the case with the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:51
verses.text: Christ came to them that were sick; He found them all sick.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:52
verses.text: Let no one then flatter himself on his 			 healthful state, lest the physician give him up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:53
verses.text: He found all sick; it is the Apostle's judgment, "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:54
verses.text: Though He found them all sick, yet were there two sorts of sick folk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:55
verses.text: The one came to the Physician, clave to Christ, heard, honoured, followed Him, were converted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:56
verses.text: He received all without disdaining any, for to heal them, who healed of free favour, who cured by Almighty power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:57
verses.text: When then He received them, and joined them to Himself to be healed, they rejoiced.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:58
verses.text: But there was another sort of sick, who had already become infatuated through the sickness of iniquity, and did not 			 know themselves to be sick; they mocked Him, because He received the sick, and said to His disciples, "Lo, what manner of man is your Master, who eateth with publicans and sinners".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:59
verses.text: And He who knew what and who they were answered them, "They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:60
verses.text: And He showed them who the "whole" were, and who the "sick".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:61
verses.text: "I am not come," He saith, "to call the righteous, but sinners".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:62
verses.text: If sinners, He would say, do not come to Me, wherefore am I come? for whose sake am I come? If all are whole, wherefore hath so great a Physician come down from heaven? why hath He prepared for us a medicine not out of His stores, but of His own blood? That sort of sick then who had a milder sickness, who felt themselves to be sick, clave to the Physician, that they might be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:63
verses.text: But they whose sickness was more dangerous mocked the Physician, and abused the sick.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:64
verses.text: Whither did their frenzy proceed at last? To seize the Physician, bind, scourge, crown Him with thorns, hang Him upon a Tree, kill Him on the Cross! Why dost thou marvel? The sick slew the Physician; but the Physician by 			 being slain healed the frantic patient.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:66
verses.text: For first, not forgetting on the Cross His own character, and manifesting forth His patience to us, and giving us an example of love to our enemies; as He saw them raging round Him, who had known their disease, seeing He was the Physician, who had known the frenzy by which they had become infatuated, He said at once to the Father, "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:67
verses.text: Now suppose ye that those Jews were not malignant, cruel, bloody, turbulent, and enemies of the Son of God? Suppose ye that that cry, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do," was ineffectual and in vain? He saw them all, but He knew amongst them those that should one day be His.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:68
verses.text: In a word, He died, because it was so expedient, that by His Death He might kill death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:69
verses.text: God died, that an exchange might be effected by a kind of heavenly contract, that man might 			 not see death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:70
verses.text: For Christ is God, but He died not in that Nature in which He is God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:71
verses.text: For the same Person is God and man; for God and man is one Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:72
verses.text: The human nature was assumed, that we might be changed for the better; He did not degrade the Divine Nature down to the lower.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:73
verses.text: For He assumed that which He was not, He did not lose that which He was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:74
verses.text: Forasmuch then as He is both God and man, being pleased that we should live by that which was His, He died in that which was ours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:75
verses.text: For He had nothing Himself, whereby He could die; nor had we anything whereby we could live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:76
verses.text: For what was He who had nothing whereby He could die? "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:77
verses.text: If thou seek for anything in God whereby He may die, thou wilt not find it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:78
verses.text: But we all die, who are flesh; men bearing about sinful flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:79
verses.text: Seek out for that whereby sin may live; it hath it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:80
verses.text: So then neither could He have death in that which was His own, nor we life in that which was our own; but we have life from that which is His, He death from what is ours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:81
verses.text: What an exchange! What hath He given, and what received? Men who trade enter into commercial intercourse for 			 exchange of things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:82
verses.text: For ancient commerce was only an exchange of things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:83
verses.text: A man gave what he had, and received what he had not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:84
verses.text: For example, he had wheat, but had no barley; another had barley, but no wheat; the former gave the wheat which he had, and received the barley which he had not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:85
