verses.text: How simple it was that the larger quantity should make up for the cheaper sort! So then another man gives barley, to receive wheat; lastly, another gives lead, to receive silver, only he gives much lead against a little silver; another gives wool, to receive a ready-made garment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:86
verses.text: And who can enumerate all these exchanges? But no one gives life to receive death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:87
verses.text: Not in vain then was the voice of the Physician as He hung upon the tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:88
verses.text: For in order that He might die for us because 			 the Word could not die, "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:89
verses.text: He hung upon the Cross, but in the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:90
verses.text: There was the meanness, which the Jews despised; there the dearness, by which the Jews were delivered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:91
verses.text: For for them was it said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:92
verses.text: And that voice was not in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:93
verses.text: He died, was buried, rose again, having passed forty days with His disciples, He ascended into heaven, He sent the Holy Ghost on them, who waited for the promise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:94
verses.text: They were filled with the Holy Ghost, whom they had received, and began to speak with the tongues of all nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:95
verses.text: Then the Jews who were present, amazed that unlearned and ignorant men, whom they had known as brought up among them with one tongue, should in the Name of Christ speak in 			 all tongues, were in astonishment, and learnt from Peter's words whence this gift came.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:96
verses.text: He gave it, who hung upon the tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:97
verses.text: He gave it, who was derided as He hung upon the tree, that from His seat in heaven He might give the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:98
verses.text: They of whom He had said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do," heard, believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:99
verses.text: They believed, were baptized, and their conversion was effected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:100
verses.text: What conversion? In faith they drank the Blood of Christ, which in fury they had 			 shed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:101
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:102
verses.text: Therefore, to finish this discourse with that with which we began it, let us pray, and let us rely on God; let us live as He enjoineth; and when we totter in this life, let us call upon Him as the disciples called, saying, "Lord, increase our faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:103
verses.text: Peter both put his trust in Him, and tottered; but notwithstanding he was not disregarded and left to sink, but was lifted up and raised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:104
verses.text: For his trust whence was it? Not from anything of his own; but from what was the Lord's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:105
verses.text: How? "Lord, if it be Thou, bid me come unto Thee on the water".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:106
verses.text: For on the water was the Lord walking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:107
verses.text: "If it be Thou, bid me come unto Thee on the water".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:108
verses.text: For I know that if it be Thou, Thou biddest, and it is done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:109
verses.text: "And He saith, Come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:110
verses.text: He went down at His bidding, but in his own weakness he was afraid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:111
verses.text: Nevertheless when he was afraid, he cried out, "Lord, save me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:112
verses.text: Then the Lord took him by the hand, and said, "O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?" He first invited him, He delivered him, as he tottered, and stumbled; that it might be fulfilled which was said in the Psalm, "If I said my foot hath slipped, Thy mercy, O Lord, aided me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:113
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:114
verses.text: There are then two kinds of blessings, temporal and eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:115
verses.text: Temporal blessings are health, substance, honour, friends, a home, children, a wife, and the other things of this life in which we are sojourners.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:116
verses.text: Put we up then in the hostelry of this life as travellers passing on, and not as owners intending to remain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:117
verses.text: But eternal blessings are, first, eternal life itself, the incorruption and immortality of body and soul, the society of Angels, the heavenly city, 			 glory unfailing, Father and father-land, the former without death, the latter without a foe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:118
verses.text: These blessings let us desire with all eagerness, let us ask with all perseverance, not with length of words, but with the witness of groans.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:119
verses.text: Longing desire prayeth always, though the tongue be silent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:120
verses.text: If thou art ever longing, thou art ever praying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:121
verses.text: When sleepeth prayer? When desire groweth cold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:122
verses.text: So then let us beg for these eternal blessings with all eager desire, let us seek for those 			 good things with an entire earnestness, let us ask for those good things with all assurance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:123
verses.text: For those good things do profit him that hath them, they cannot harm him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:124
verses.text: But those other temporal good things sometimes profit, and sometimes harm.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:125
verses.text: Poverty hath profited many, and wealth hath harmed many; a private life hath profited many, and exalted honour hath harmed many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:126
verses.text: And again, money hath profiled some, honourable distinction hath profited some; profited them who use them well; but from those 			 who use them ill, the not withdrawing them hath harmed them more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:127
verses.text: And so, Brethren, let us ask for those temporal blessings too, but in moderation, being sure that if we do receive them, He giveth them, who knoweth what is expedient for us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:128
verses.text: Thou hast asked, and what thou hast asked, hath not been given thee? Trust thy Father, who would give it thee, were it expedient for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:129
verses.text: Lo! judge in this case by thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:130
verses.text: For such as thy son who knows not the ways of men is in regard to thee, such 			 in regard to the Lord art thou thyself, who knowest not the things of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:131
verses.text: Lo, thy son cries a whole day before thee, that thou wouldest give him a knife, or a sword; thou dost refuse to give it him, thou wilt not give it, thou disregardest his tears, lest thou shouldest have to bewail his death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:132
verses.text: Let him cry, and beat himself, or throw himself upon the ground, that thou mayest set him on horseback; thou wilt not do it, because he does not know how to govern the horse, he may throw and kill him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:133
verses.text: To whom thou refusest a part, thou art reserving the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:134
verses.text: But that he may grow up, and possess the whole in safety, thou givest him not that little thing which is full of peril to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:135
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:136
verses.text: And so, Brethren, we say, pray as much as ye are able.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:137
verses.text: Evils abound, and God hath willed that evils should abound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:138
verses.text: Would that evil men did not abound, and then evils would not abound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:139
verses.text: Bad times! troublesome times! this men are saying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:140
verses.text: Let our lives be good; and the times are good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:141
verses.text: We make our times; such as we are, such are the times.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:142
verses.text: But what can we do? We cannot, it may be, convert the mass of men to a good life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:143
verses.text: But let the few who do give ear live well; let 			 the few who live well endure the many who live ill.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:144
verses.text: They are the corn, they are in the floor; in the floor they can have the chaff with them, they will not have them in the barn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:145
verses.text: Let them endure what they would not, that they may come to what they would.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:146
verses.text: Wherefore are we sad, and blame we God? Evils abound in the world, in order that the world may not engage our love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:147
verses.text: Great men, faithful saints were they who have despised the world with all its attractions; we are not able to despise it even disfigured as it is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:148
verses.text: The world is evil, lo, it is evil, and yet it is loved as though it were good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:149
verses.text: But what is this evil world? For the heavens and the earth, and the waters, and the things that are therein, the fish, and birds, and trees, are not evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:150
verses.text: All these are good: but it is evil men who make this evil world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:151
verses.text: Yet as we cannot be without evil men, let us, as I have said, whilst we live pour out our groans before the Lord our God, and 			 endure the evils, that we may attain to the things that are good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:152
verses.text: Let us not find fault with the Master of the household; for He is loving to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:153
verses.text: He beareth us, and not we him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 29:154
verses.text: He knoweth how to govern what He made; do what He hath bidden, and hope for what He hath promised.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:1
verses.text: Sermon XXXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:2
verses.text: [LXXXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:5
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:6
verses.text: 7, where we are admonished to beware of the offences of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:8
verses.text: The divine lessons, which we have just heard as they were being read, warn us to gather in a stock of virtues, to fortify a Christian heart, against the offences which were predicted to come, and this from the mercy of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:9
verses.text: "For what is man," saith Scripture, "saving that Thou art mindful of him?" "Woe unto the world because of offences," saith the Lord; the Truth says so; He alarmeth and warneth us, He would not have us to be off our guard; for surely He would not make us desperate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:10
verses.text: Against this "woe," against this evil, that is, which is to be feared, and dreaded, and guarded against, Scripture counsels, and exhorts, and instructs us in that place, where it is said, "Great praise have they who love Thy law, and nothing is an offence to them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:11
verses.text: He hath shown us an enemy to be guarded against, but He hath not omitted to show us also a wall of defence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:12
verses.text: Thou wast thinking, as thou heardest, "Woe unto the world because of offences," whither thou mightest go beyond the world, that thou mightest not be exposed to offences.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:13
verses.text: Therefore to avoid offences, whither wilt thou go beyond the world, unless thou fly to Him who made the world? And how shall we be able to fly to Him who made the world, unless we give ear to His law 			 which is preached everywhere? And to give ear to it is but a small matter, unless we love it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:14
verses.text: For divine Scripture in making thee secure against offences doth not say, "Great peace have they who" hear "Thy law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:15
verses.text: For not the hearers of the law are just before God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:16
verses.text: But" because "the doers of the law shall be justified," and, "faith worketh by love:" it saith, "Great peace have they who love Thy law, and nothing is an offence to them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:17
verses.text: To this sentiment also agrees the passage which we have chanted in course; "But the meek shall inherit the earth, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:18
verses.text: Because, "great peace have they who love Thy law".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:19
verses.text: For these "meek" ones are they who "love the law of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:20
verses.text: For, "Blessed is the man whom Thou chastenest, O Lord, and teachest him out of Thy law, that Thou mayest give him rest from the days of adversity, until the pit be digged for the sinner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:21
verses.text: How diverse seem those words of Scripture, yet into one meaning do they so flow and meet together, that whatsoever out of that most rich fountain thou canst hear, so that thou acquiesce therein, and art in loving harmony with the truth, thou will be at once filled with peace; glowing with love, and fortified against offences.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:23
verses.text: It is our place then to see, or seek, or learn, how we must be "meek;" and we are guided by that which I have just brought forward out of the Scriptures, to find what we are in quest of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:24
verses.text: Be attentive then, Beloved, for a little while; it is a weighty matter that is in hand, that we may be meek; a necessary thing in the adversities of life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:25
verses.text: But it is not the adverse circumstances of this life which are called offences; but mark what "offences" are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:26
verses.text: A man, 			 for instance, under some hard necessity is weighed down by a press of trouble.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:27
verses.text: That he is weighed down with a press of trouble, is no offence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:28
verses.text: By such pressure were even Martyrs pressed, but not oppressed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:29
verses.text: Of an offence beware, but of a press of trouble not so much.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:30
verses.text: The last presseth thee, an offence oppresseth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:31
verses.text: What then is the difference between the two? In the press of trouble thou didst make ready to maintain patience, to hold fast constancy, not to abandon faith, not to consent to 			 sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:32
verses.text: This if thou maintain, or shall have maintained, the trouble that presseth thee shall not be thy fall; but that press of trouble shall avail to the same end as in the oil press, not to destroy the olive, but to extract the oil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:33
verses.text: In a word, if in this trouble that presseth thee thou ascribe praise unto God, how useful will the press be to thee, whereby such oil is pressed out! Under such a press the Apostles sat in chains, and in that press they sang a hymn to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:34
verses.text: What precious oil was this 			 that was pressed and forced out! Beneath a heavy press did Job sit on the dunghill, without resource, without help, without substance, without children; full, but of worms only, as far, that is, as concerned the outward man, but because he too was full of God within, he praised God, and that press was no "offence" to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:35
verses.text: Where then was the "offence"? When his wife came to him and said, "Speak a word against God, and die".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:36
verses.text: When all had been taken from him by the devil, an Eve was reserved for the exercised sufferer, not to console but to tempt her husband.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:37
verses.text: See then where the offence was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:38
verses.text: She exaggerated his miseries, and her miseries too with his, and began to persuade him to blaspheme.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:39
verses.text: But he who was "meek," because "God had taught him out of His law, and given him rest from the days of adversity;" had "great peace" in his heart as "loving the law of God, and nothing was an 			 offence to him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:40
verses.text: She was an offence, but not to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:41
verses.text: In a word, behold the meek man, behold one taught in the law of God, the eternal law of God I mean.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:42
verses.text: For that law on tables was not yet given to the Jews in the time of Job, but in the hearts of the godly there remained still the eternal law, from which that which was given to the people was copied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:43
verses.text: Because then by the law of God he had "rest given him from the days of adversity," and "had great peace as loving the law of God," 			 behold how "meek" he is, and what he answers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:44
verses.text: Learn hereby what I propose to enquire; who are the meek.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:45
verses.text: "Thou speakest," he says, "as one of the foolish women speaketh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:46
verses.text: If we have received good from the hand of the Lord, shall we not bear the evil?"  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:47
verses.text: We have heard by an example who the meek are: let us, if we can, define them in words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:48
verses.text: The meek are they, to whom in all their good deeds, in all the things they do well, nothing is pleasing but God; to whom in all the evils they suffer, God is not displeasing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:49
verses.text: Now, Brethren, attend to this rule, to this pattern; let us stretch ourselves out to it, let us seek for increase, that we may fill it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:50
verses.text: For what does it profit, that we plant, and water, except God shall 			 give the increase? "For neither is he that planteth anything, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:51
verses.text: Give ear, whosoever thou art, that wouldest be "meek," who wouldest have "rest from the days of adversity, who lovest the law of God," that there may be "no offence unto thee," and that thou mayest "have great peace," that thou mayest "possess the earth, and delight in the multitude of peace;" give ear, whosoever thou art that wouldest be "meek".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:52
verses.text: Whatsoever good thou doest, be not pleased with thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:53
verses.text: "For God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace 			 unto the humble".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:54
verses.text: So then whatever good thou doest, let nought but God be pleasing to thee; whatever evil thou sufferest, let not God be displeasing to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:55
verses.text: What needest thou more? Do this, and thou shalt live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:56
verses.text: The days of adversity shall not overwhelm thee; thou shall escape that which is said, "Woe unto the world because of offences".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:57
verses.text: For to what world is there woe because of offences, but to that of which it is said, "And the world knew Him not?" Not to that world of which it is said, "God was in Christ reconciling the world unto Himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:58
verses.text: There is an evil world, and there is a good world; the evil world, are all the evil men in this world; and the good world, all the good in this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:59
verses.text: As we observe frequently with a field.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:60
verses.text: This field is full: of what? Of wheat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:61
verses.text: Yet we say also, and say truly too, This field is full of chaff.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:62
verses.text: So with a tree, it is full of fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:63
verses.text: Another says, it is full of leaves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:64
verses.text: And both he who says it is full of fruit, says true; and he who says it is full of leaves, says true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:65
verses.text: Neither has 			 the full display of leaves taken away the room for the fruit, nor the full display of the fruit driven off the abundance of leaves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:66
verses.text: It is full of both; but the one the wind searcheth out, the other the husbandman gathereth in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:67
verses.text: So therefore when thou dost hear, "Woe unto the world because of offences," be not afraid; "love the law of God, nothing shall be an offence to thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:68
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:69
verses.text: But thy wife comes to thee advising thee to some evil thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:70
verses.text: Thou dost love her as a wife should be loved; she is one of thy members.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:71
verses.text: "But if thine eye offend thee, if thine hand offend thee, if thy foot offend thee," thou hast just heard the Gospel, "cut them off, and cast them from thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:72
verses.text: Whosoever he be that is dear to thee, whosoever he be that is held in high estimation by thee, let him be so long of high esteem with thee, so long thy beloved member, as he shall not begin to offend thee, that is, to advise thee to any evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:73
verses.text: Hear now how that this is the meaning of "offence".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:74
verses.text: I have brought forward the example of Job and his wife; but there the word "offence" did not occur.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:75
verses.text: Hear the Gospel: when the Lord prophesied of His Passion, Peter began to 			 persuade him not to suffer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:76
verses.text: "Get thee behind Me, Satan, thou art an offence to Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:77
verses.text: Here undoubtedly the Lord who hath given thee an example of life, hath taught thee both what an "offence" is, and how an offence is to be avoided.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:78
verses.text: Him to whom He had a little while before said, "Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona;" He had shown to be His member.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:79
verses.text: But when he begins to be an offence, He cuts off the member; only He restored the member, and put it into its place again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:80
verses.text: He then will be an "offence" to thee, who shall begin to persuade thee to any evil thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:81
verses.text: And here, Beloved, take heed; this takes place for the most part not through any evil will, but through a mistaken good will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:82
verses.text: Thy friend who loves thee, and is loved by thee again, thy father, thy brother, thy child, thy wife, sees 			 thee in an evil case, and would have thee do what is evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:83
verses.text: What do I mean by "sees thee in an evil case"? Sees thee in some press of trouble.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:84
verses.text: This pressure it may be thou art suffering for righteousness' sake; art suffering it because thou will not give false witness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:85
verses.text: I would speak merely by way of illustration.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:86
verses.text: Examples abound; for "woe to the world, because of offences".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:87
verses.text: See, for instance, some powerful person, to cover his rapine and plunder, asks of you the service of a false 			 witness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:88
verses.text: You refuse: refuse the false oath, lest thou shouldest deny Him that is true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:89
verses.text: That I may not dwell long on this, he is angry, he is powerful, he oppresses thee: a friend comes who would not have thee in this press of trouble, in this evil case; "I pray thee, do what is told thee; what great matter is it?" And then perhaps as Satan with the Lord, "It is written of Thee, He shall give His Angels charge concerning Thee, that Thou dash not Thy foot against a stone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:90
verses.text: Perhaps too this friend of thine, because he sees thou art a Christian, wishes to persuade thee out of the Law to do what he thinks you ought to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:91
verses.text: "Do what the other tells".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:92
verses.text: "What? Do what the other wishes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:93
verses.text: "But it is a lie, it is false".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:94
verses.text: "Well, have you not read, 'All men are liars'?" Now is he an "offence".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:95
verses.text: He is a friend, what will you do? He is an eye, he is a hand: "Cut it off, and cast it from thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:96
verses.text: What is, "cut it off, and cast it from thee"? Consent not to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:97
verses.text: For members in our body make up unity by consent, by consent they live, by consent are joined together one with the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:98
verses.text: Where there is dissent, there is disease, or a sore.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:99
verses.text: He is then one of thy members; thou wilt love him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:100
verses.text: But he is an offence to thee; 			 "Cut him off, and cast him from thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:101
verses.text: Consent not to him; drive him off from thine ears, it may be he will return amended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:102
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:103
verses.text: And how wilt thou do this that I say, "Cut him off, and cast him from thee," and so, it may be, amend him? answer me, how thou art going to do it? He wished to persuade thee out of the Law to tell a lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:104
verses.text: For he said, "speak".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:105
verses.text: And perhaps he did not dare to say, "speak a lie;" but thus, "speak what the other wishes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:106
verses.text: Thou sayest, "But it is a lie".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:107
verses.text: And he to excuse it, says, "All men are liars".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:108
verses.text: Then do thou, my brother, say against this, 			 "The mouth that lieth slayeth the soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:109
verses.text: Mark, it is no light thing thou hast heard, "The mouth that lieth slayeth the soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:110
verses.text: What can that powerful enemy, who oppresseth me, do to me, that thou pitiest me, and my condition, and wouldest not have me be in this evil case; whereas thou wouldest that I should be evil? What can that powerful man do to me, and what can he oppress? The flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:111
verses.text: He can oppress thy body, thou wilt say: I grant he may oppress it to destruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:112
verses.text: Still how much more mildly does he deal with me, than I should with myself were I to lie! He kills my flesh; I kill my soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:113
verses.text: He in his power and anger slays the body; "the mouth that lieth slayeth the soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:114
verses.text: He slays the body; and die it must, though it should not be slain; but the soul which iniquity slayeth not, the truth receiveth for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:115
verses.text: Preserve then what thou canst preserve; and let that perish which must perish sometime or other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:116
verses.text: Thou hast given an answer then, 			 but thou hast not solved the "All men are liars".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:117
verses.text: Make answer to him to this too, that he may not fancy that he has said anything to persuade to lying, in bringing a testimony out of the Law; so urging thee out of the Law against the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:118
verses.text: For it is written in the Law, "Thou shalt not bear false witness;" and it is written in the Law, "All men are liars".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:119
verses.text: Recur then to that which I just lately suggested, when I defined in words as best I could the "meek" man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:120
verses.text: He is "meek" to whom in all things that he does well, nothing but God is pleasing, and in all the evils which he suffers, God is not displeasing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:121
verses.text: Make answer then to him who says, Lie, for it is written, "All men are liars:" I will not lie, for it is written, "The mouth that lieth slayeth the soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:122
verses.text: I 			 will not lie, because it is written, "Thou shalt destroy them that speak lying".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:123
verses.text: I will not lie, because it is written, "Thou shalt not bear false witness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:124
verses.text: Though he whom I displease by the truth harass my body with oppressions, I will give ear to my Lord, "Fear not them which kill the body".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:125
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:126
verses.text: "How then are all men liars? What! Thou art not a man, I suppose?" Answer quickly and truly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:127
verses.text: "And O that I may not be a man, that so I may not be a liar".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:128
verses.text: For see; "God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that did understand, and seek after God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:129
verses.text: They are all gone out of the way, they are all together become unprofitable: there is none that doeth good, no not even one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:130
verses.text: Why? Because they wished to be sons of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:131
verses.text: But in order that he might deliver them from these iniquities, cure, heal, change, the sons of men; "he gave them power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:132
verses.text: What marvel then! Ye were men, if we were the sons of men; ye were all men, and were liars, for, "All men are liars".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:133
verses.text: The grace of God came to you, and "gave you power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:134
verses.text: Hear the voice of My Father saying, "I have said, Ye are gods; and ye are all the children of the Most High".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:135
verses.text: Since then they are men, and the sons of men, if they are not the children of the Most High, they are liars, for, "all men are liars".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:136
verses.text: If they are the sons of God, if they have been redeemed by the Saviour's grace, if purchased with His precious Blood, if born again of water and of the Spirit, if predestinated to the inheritance of heaven, then indeed are they children of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:137
verses.text: And so thereby are gods.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:138
verses.text: What then would a lie have to do with thee? For Adam was a mere man, 			 Christ, man and God; God, the Creator of all creation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:139
verses.text: Adam a mere man, the Man Christ, the Mediator with God, the Only Son of the Father, the God-man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:140
verses.text: Lo, thou, O man, art far from God, and God is far above man; between them the God-man placed Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:141
verses.text: Acknowledge Christ, and by Him as Man ascend up to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:142
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:143
verses.text: Being then now reformed, and, if my words have been so blessed, "meek," let us "hold fast our profession without wavering".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:144
verses.text: Let us love the law of God, that we may escape that which is written, "Woe unto the world because of offences".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:145
verses.text: Now I would say a few words about "offences," of which the world is full, and how it is that offences thicken, pressing troubles abound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:146
verses.text: The world is laid waste, the winepress is trodden.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:147
verses.text: Ah! Christians, heavenly shoot, ye strangers on the earth, who seek a city in heaven, who long to be associated with the holy Angels; understand that ye have come here on this condition only, that ye should soon depart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:148
verses.text: Ye are passing on through the world, endeavouring to reach Him who created it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:149
verses.text: Let not the lovers of the world, who wish to remain in the world, and yet, whether they will or no, are compelled to move 			 from it; let them not disturb you, let them not deceive nor seduce you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:150
verses.text: These pressing troubles are not offences.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:151
verses.text: Be ye righteous, and they will be only exercises.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:152
verses.text: Tribulation comes; it will be as ye choose it, either an exercise, or a condemnation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:153
verses.text: Such as it shall find you to be, will it be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:154
verses.text: Tribulation is a fire; does it find thee gold? it takes away the filth: does it find thee chaff? it turns it into ashes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:155
verses.text: The pressing troubles then which abound are not "offences".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:156
verses.text: But what are 			 "offences"? Those expressions, those words in which we are thus addressed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:157
verses.text: "See what Christian times bring about;" lo, these are the true offences.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:158
verses.text: For this is said to thee, to this end, that if thou love the world, thou mayest blaspheme Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:159
verses.text: And this he saith to thee who is thy friend, and counsellor; and so "thine eye".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:160
verses.text: This he saith to thee who ministereth to thee, and shareth thy labours, and so "thine hand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:161
verses.text: This he saith to thee it may be who supporteth thee, who 			 lifteth thee up from a low earthly state; and so "thy foot".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:162
verses.text: Cast them all aside, cut them off, throw them all away from thee; consent not unto them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:163
verses.text: Answer such men, as he who was advised to give false witness answered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:164
verses.text: So do thou answer too; say to the man who saith to thee, "See, it is in Christian times that there are such pressing troubles; that the whole world is laid waste;" answer him, "And this Christ foretold me, before it came to pass".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:165
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:166
verses.text: For wherefore art thou disturbed? Thine heart is disturbed by the pressing troubles of the world, as that ship was, in which Christ was asleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:167
verses.text: Lo! what is the cause, stout-hearted man, that thy heart is disturbed? That ship in which Christ is asleep, is the heart in which faith is asleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:168
verses.text: For what new thing, what new thing, I ask, is told thee, Christian? "In Christian times is the world laid waste, the world is failing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:169
verses.text: Did not thy Lord tell thee, the world shall be laid waste? Did not thy Lord tell thee, the world shall fail? Why when the promise was made, didst thou believe, and art disturbed now, when it is being completed? So then the tempest beats furiously against thine heart; beware of shipwreck, awake up 			 Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:170
verses.text: The Apostle says, "that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:171
verses.text: Christ dwelleth in thee by faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:172
verses.text: Present faith, is Christ present; waking faith, is Christ awake; slumbering faith, is Christ asleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:173
verses.text: Arise and stir thyself; say, "Lord, we perish".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:174
verses.text: See what the Heathen say to us; and what is worse, what evil Christians say! Awake up, O Lord, we perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:175
verses.text: Let thy faith awake, and Christ begins to speak to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:176
verses.text: "'Why art thou troubled?' I told thee beforehand of all these things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:177
verses.text: I foretold them, that when evils came, thou mightest hope for good things, that thou mightest not faint in the evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:178
verses.text: Wonderest thou that the world is failing? 			 Wonder that the world is grown old.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:179
verses.text: It is as a man who is born, and grows up, and waxes old.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:180
verses.text: There are many complaints in old age; the cough, the rheum, the weakness of the eyes, fretfulness, and weariness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:181
verses.text: So then as when a man is old; he is full of complaints; so is the world old; and is full of troubles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:182
verses.text: Is it a little thing that God hath done for thee, in that in the world's old age, He hath sent Christ unto thee, that He may renew thee then, when all is failing? Dost thou not know that 			 He notified this in the seed of Abraham? "The seed of Abraham," says the Apostle, "which is Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:183
verses.text: He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of One, And to thy seed, which is Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:184
verses.text: Therefore was there a son born to Abraham in his old age, because in the old age of this world was Christ to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:185
verses.text: He came when all things were growing old, and made them new.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:186
verses.text: As a made, created, perishing thing, the world was now declining to its fall.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:187
verses.text: It could not but be that it should abound in troubles; He came both to console thee in the midst of present troubles, and to promise thee everlasting rest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:188
verses.text: Choose not then to cleave to this aged world, and to be unwilling to 			 grow young in Christ, who telleth thee, "The world is perishing, the world is waxing old, the world is failing; is distressed by the heavy breathing of old age.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:189
verses.text: But do not fear, "Thy youth shall be renewed as the eagle's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:190
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:191
verses.text: See, they say, in Christian times it is that Rome perishes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:192
verses.text: Perhaps Rome is not perishing; perhaps she is only scourged, not utterly destroyed; perhaps she is chastened, not brought to nought.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:193
verses.text: It may be so; Rome will not perish, if the Romans do not perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:194
verses.text: And perish they will not if they praise God; perish they will if they blaspheme Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:195
verses.text: For what is Rome, but the Romans? For the question is not of her wood and stones, of her lofty insulated 			  palaces, and all her spacious walls.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:196
verses.text: All this was made only on this condition that it should fall some other day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:197
verses.text: When man built it, he laid stone on stone; and when man destroyed it, he removed stone from stone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:198
verses.text: Man made it, man destroyed it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:199
verses.text: Is any injury done to Rome, because it is said, "She is falling"? No, not to Rome, but to her builder perhaps.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:200
verses.text: Do we then its builder any injury, because we say, Rome is falling, which Romulus built? This 			 world itself will be burnt with fire, which God built.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:201
verses.text: But neither does what man has made fall to ruin, except when God wills it; nor what God has made, except when He wills.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:202
verses.text: For if the work of man fall not without God's will, how can God's work fall by the will of man? Yet God both made the world that was one day to fall for thee; and therefore made He thee as one who was one day to die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:203
verses.text: Man himself, the city's ornament, man himself, the city's inhabitant, ruler, governor, comes on 			 this condition that he may go, is born on this condition that he may die, entered into the world on this condition that he may pass away; "Heaven and earth shall pass away:" what wonder then if some time or other there should be an end of a single city? And yet peradventure the city's end is not come now; yet some time or other come it will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:204
verses.text: But why does Rome perish amid the sacrifices of Christians? Why was her mother Troy burnt amid the sacrifices of Heathens? The gods in whom the Romans have placed all their hope, yea the Roman gods in whom the Heathen Romans placed their hope, removed from the flames of Troy to found Rome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:205
verses.text: These very gods of 			 Rome were originally the gods of Troy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:206
verses.text: Troy was burnt, and aeneas took the fugitive gods; yea rather himself a fugitive he took away these senseless gods.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:207
verses.text: For they could be carried by the fugitive; but they could not flee away themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:208
verses.text: And coming with these gods into Italy, with these false gods, he founded Rome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:209
verses.text: It is too long to go through the whole story; yet would I briefly mention what their own writings contain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:210
verses.text: An author of theirs well known to all speaks thus; "As I have received 			 the account, the Trojans who under the guidance of aeneas were wandering about as fugitives without any settled abode, originally built and inhabited Rome".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:211
verses.text: So they had their gods with them, they builded Rome in Latium, and there they placed the gods to be worshipped, which before were worshipped in Troy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:212
verses.text: Juno is introduced by their poet, incensed against aeneas and the fugitive Trojans, saying,  "A race of wandering slaves abhorred by me,  With prosperous passage cuts the Tuscan sea,  To fruitful Italy their course they steer,  And for their vanquished gods, design new temples  there".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:213
verses.text: Now when these vanquished gods were carried into Italy, was it as a protecting deity, or as a presage of their future fall? "Love" therefore "the law of God, and nothing shall be an offence to you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:214
verses.text: We pray you, we beseech you, we exhort you; be meek, sympathize with the suffering, bear the weak; and on this occasion of the concourse of so many strangers, and needy, and suffering people, let your hospitality and your good works abound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 30:215
verses.text: Let but Christians do what Christ enjoineth, and so will the Heathen blaspheme only to their own hurt.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:1
verses.text: Sermon XXXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:2
verses.text: [LXXXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:5
verses.text: xviii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:6
verses.text: 15, "If thy brother sin against thee, go, shew him his fault between thee and him alone;" and of the words of Solomon, he that winketh with the eyes deceitfully, heapeth sorrow upon men; but he that reproveth openly, maketh peace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:8
verses.text: Our Lord warns us not to neglect one another's sins, not by searching out what to find fault with, but by looking out for what to amend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:9
verses.text: For He said that his eye is sharp to cast out a mote out of his brother's eye, who has not a beam in his own eye.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:10
verses.text: Now what this means, I will briefly convey to you, Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:11
verses.text: A mote in the eye is anger; a beam in the eye is hatred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:12
verses.text: When therefore one who has hatred finds fault with one who is angry, 			 he wishes to take a mote out of his brother's eye, but is hindered by the beam which he carries in his own eye.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:13
verses.text: A mote is the beginning of a beam.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:14
verses.text: For a beam in the course of its growth, is first a mote.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:15
verses.text: By watering the mote, you bring it to a beam; by nourishing anger with evil suspicions, you bring it on to hatred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:17
verses.text: Now there is a great difference between the sin of one who is angry, and the cruelty of one who holds another in hatred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:18
verses.text: For even with our children are we angry; but who is ever found to hate his children? Among the very cattle too, the cow in a sort of weariness will sometimes in anger drive away her sucking calf; but anon she embraces it with all the affection of a mother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:19
verses.text: She is in a way disgusted with it, when she butts at it; yet when she misses it, she will seek 			 after it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:20
verses.text: Nor do we discipline our children otherwise, than with a degree of anger and indignation; yet we should not discipline them at all, but in love to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:21
verses.text: So far then is every one who is angry from hating; that sometimes one would be rather convicted of hating, if he were not angry.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:22
verses.text: For suppose a child wishes to play in some river's stream, by whose force he would be like to perish; if you see this, and patiently suffer it, this would be hating; your patient suffering him, is his 			 death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:23
verses.text: How far better is it to be angry and correct him, than by not being angry to suffer him to perish! Above all things then is hatred to be avoided, and the beam to be cast out of the eye.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:24
verses.text: Great is the difference indeed between one's exceeding due limits in some words through anger, which he afterwards wipes off by repenting of it; and the keeping an insidious purpose shut up in the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:25
verses.text: Great, lastly, the difference between these words of Scripture; "Mine eye is 			 disordered because of anger".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:26
verses.text: Whereas of the other it is said, "Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:27
verses.text: Great is the difference between an eye disordered, and clean put out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:28
verses.text: A mote disorders, a beam puts clean out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:29
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:30
verses.text: In order then that we may be able well to do and to fulfil what we have been admonished of to-day, let us first persuade ourselves to this, above all things to have no hate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:31
verses.text: For when there is no beam in thine own eye, thou seest rightly whatever may be in thy brother's eye; and art uneasy, till thou cast out of thy brother's eye what thou seest to hurt it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:32
verses.text: The light that is in thee, doth not allow thee to neglect thy brother's light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:33
verses.text: Whereas if thou hate, 			 and wouldest correct him, how dost thou improve his light, when thou hast lost thine own light? For the same Scripture, where it is written, "Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer," hath expressly told us this also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:34
verses.text: "He that hateth his brother is in darkness even until now".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:35
verses.text: Hatred then is darkness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:36
verses.text: Now it cannot but be, that he who hateth another, should first injure himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:37
verses.text: For him he endeavours to hurt outwardly, he lays himself waste inwardly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:38
verses.text: Now in proportion as our soul is of more value than our body, so much the more ought we to provide for it, that it be not hurt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:39
verses.text: But he that hateth another, doth hurt his own soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:40
verses.text: And what would he do to him whom he hateth? What would he do? He takes away his money, can he take his faith away? he wounds 			 his good fame, can he wound his conscience? Whatever injury he does, is but external; now observe what his injury to himself is? For he who hateth another is an enemy to himself within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:41
verses.text: But because he is not sensible of what harm he is doing to himself, he is violent against another, and that the more dangerously, that he is not sensible of the evil he is doing to himself; because by this very violence he has lost the power of perception.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:42
verses.text: Thou art violent against thine enemy; by this violence 			 of thine he is spoiled, and thou art wicked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:43
verses.text: Great is the difference between the two.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:44
verses.text: He hath lost his money, thou thine innocence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:45
verses.text: Ask which hath suffered the heavier loss? He hath lost a thing that was sure to perish, and thou art become one who must now perish thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:46
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:47
verses.text: Therefore ought we to rebuke in love; not with any eager desire to injure, but with an earnest care to amend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:48
verses.text: If we be so minded, most excellently do we practise that which we have been recommended to-day; "If thy brother shall sin against thee, rebuke him between thee and him alone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:49
verses.text: Why dost thou rebuke him? Because thou art grieved, that he should have sinned against thee? God forbid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:50
verses.text: If from love of thyself thou do it, thou doest nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:51
verses.text: If from love to him thou do it, thou doest excellently.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:52
verses.text: In fact, observe in these words themselves, for the love of whom thou oughtest to do it, whether of thyself or him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:53
verses.text: "If he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:54
verses.text: Do it for his sake then, that thou mayest "gain" him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:55
verses.text: If by so doing thou "gain" 			 him, hadst thou not done it, he would have been lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:56
verses.text: How is it then that most men disregard these sins, and say, "What great thing have I done? I have only sinned against man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:57
verses.text: Disregard them not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:58
verses.text: Thou hast sinned against man; but wouldest thou know that in sinning against man thou art lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:59
verses.text: If he, against whom thou hast sinned, have "rebuked thee between thee and him alone," and thou hast listened to him, he hath "gained" thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:60
verses.text: What can "hath gained thee," mean; but that thou 			 hadst been lost, if he had not gained thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:61
verses.text: For if thou wouldest not have been lost, how hath he gained thee? Let no man then disregard it, when he sins against a brother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:62
verses.text: For the Apostle saith in a certain place, "But when ye sin so against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ;" for this reason, because we have been all made members of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:63
verses.text: How dost thou not sin against Christ, who sinnest against a member of Christ?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:64
verses.text: Let no one therefore say, "I have not sinned against God, but against a brother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:65
verses.text: I have sinned against a man, it is a trifling sin, or no sin at all".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:66
verses.text: It may be, thou sayest it is a trifling sin, because it is soon cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:67
verses.text: Thou hast sinned against a brother; give him satisfaction, and thou art made whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:68
verses.text: Thou didst a deadly thing quickly, but quickly too hast thou found a remedy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:69
verses.text: Who of us, my Brethren, can hope for the kingdom of heaven, when the Gospel 			 says, "Whosoever shall say to his brother, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire?" Exceeding terror! but behold in the same place the remedy: "If thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee, leave there thy gift before the altar".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:70
verses.text: God is not angry that thou deferrest to lay thy gift upon the Altar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:71
verses.text: It is thee that God seeketh more than thy gift.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:72
verses.text: For if thou come with a gift to thy God, bearing an evil mind against thy brother, He will answer thee, "Thou art lost, what hast thou brought Me? Thou bringest thy gift, and thou art thyself no proper gift for God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:73
verses.text: Christ seeketh him whom He hath redeemed with His Blood, more than what thou hast found in thy barn".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:74
verses.text: So then, "Leave 			 there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way, first be reconciled to thy brother, and so thou shalt come and offer thy gift".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:75
verses.text: Lo that "danger of hell fire," how quickly dissolved it is! When thou wast not yet reconciled, thou wast "in danger of hell fire;" once reconciled, thou offerest thy gift before the altar in all security.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:76
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:77
verses.text: But men are easy and ready enough to inflict injuries, and hard to seek for reconciliation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:78
verses.text: Ask pardon, says one, of him whom thou hast offended, of him whom thou hast injured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:79
verses.text: He answers, "I will not so humble myself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:80
verses.text: But now if thou despise thy brother, at least give ear to thy God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:81
verses.text: "He that humbleth himself shall be exalted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:82
verses.text: Wilt thou refuse to humble thyself, who hast already fallen? Great is the difference between one who humbleth himself, and one who lieth on the ground.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:83
verses.text: Already dost thou lie on the ground, and wilt thou then not humble thyself? Thou mightest well say, I will not descend; if thou hadst first been unwilling to fall.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:84
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:85
verses.text: This then ought one to do who hath done an injury.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:86
verses.text: And he who hath suffered one, what ought he to do? What we have heard to-day, "If thy brother shall sin against thee, rebuke him between thee and him alone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:87
verses.text: If thou shall neglect this, thou art worse than he.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:88
verses.text: He hath done an injury, and by doing an injury, hath stricken himself with a grievous wound; wilt thou disregard thy brother's wound? Wilt thou see him perishing, or already lost, and disregard his case? Thou art worse in keeping silence, than he in his reviling.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:89
verses.text: Therefore when any one sins against us, let us take great care, not for ourselves, for it is a glorious thing to forget injuries; only forget thine own injury, not 			 thy brother's wound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:90
verses.text: Therefore "rebuke him between thee and him alone," intent upon his amendment, but sparing his shame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:91
verses.text: For it may be that through shame-facedness he will begin to defend his sin, and so thou wilt make him whom thou desirest to amend, still worse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:92
verses.text: "Rebuke him" therefore "between him and thee alone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:93
verses.text: If he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother;" because he would have been lost, hadst thou not done it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:94
verses.text: But "if he will not hear thee," that is, if he will 			 defend his sin as if it were a just action, "take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established; and if he will not hear them, refer it to the Church; but if he will not hear the Church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:95
verses.text: Reckon him no more amongst the number of thy brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:96
verses.text: But yet neither is his salvation on that account to be neglected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:97
verses.text: For the very heathen, that is, the Gentiles and Pagans, we do not reckon among the number of brethren; but yet are we ever seeking their salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:98
verses.text: This then have we heard the Lord so advising, and with such great carefulness enjoining, that He even added this immediately, "Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven; 			 and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:99
verses.text: Thou hast begun to hold thy brother for a publican; "thou bindest him on earth;" but see that thou bind him justly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:100
verses.text: For unjust bonds justice doth burst asunder.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:101
verses.text: But when thou hast corrected, and been "reconciled to thy brother," thou hast "loosed him on earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:102
verses.text: And when "thou shalt have loosed him on earth, he shall be loosed in heaven also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:103
verses.text: Thus thou doest a great thing, not for thyself, but for him; for a great injury had he done, not to thee, but to 			 himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:104
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:105
verses.text: But since this is so, what is that which Solomon says, and which we heard first to-day out of another lesson, "He that winketh with the eyes deceitfully, heapeth sorrow upon men; but he that reproveth openly, maketh peace"? If then "he that reproveth openly, maketh peace;" how "rebuke him between him and thee alone"? We must fear, lest the divine precepts should be contrary to one another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:106
verses.text: But no: let us understand that there is the most perfect agreement in them, let us not follow the conceits of certain vain ones, who in their error think that the two Testaments in the Old and New Books are contrary to each other; that so we should think that there is any contradiction here, because one is in the book of Solomon, and the other in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:107
verses.text: For if any one unskilful in, and a reviler of the divine Scriptures, were to say, "See where the two Testaments contradict each other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:108
verses.text: The Lord saith, 'Rebuke him between him and thee alone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:109
verses.text: ' Solomon saith, 'He that reproveth openly maketh 			 peace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:110
verses.text: '" Doth not the Lord then know what He hath commanded? Solomon would have the sinners' hard forehead bruised: Christ spareth his shame who blushes for his sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:111
verses.text: For in the one place it is written, "He that reproveth openly maketh peace;" but in the other, "Rebuke him between him and thee alone;" not "openly," but apart and secretly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:112
verses.text: But wouldest thou know, whosoever thou art that thinkest such things, that the two Testaments are not opposed to each other, because the 			 first of these passages is found in the book of Solomon, and the other in the Gospel? Hear the Apostle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:113
verses.text: And surely the Apostle is a Minister of the New Testament.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:114
verses.text: Hear the Apostle Paul then, charging Timothy, and saying, "Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:115
verses.text: So then not the book of Solomon, but an Epistle of Paul the Apostle seems to be at issue with the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:116
verses.text: Let us then without any prejudice to his honour lay aside Solomon for a while; let us hear the Lord Christ and His servant Paul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:117
verses.text: What sayest Thou, O Lord? "If thy brother sin against thee, rebuke him between him and thee alone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:118
verses.text: What sayest thou, O Apostle? "Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:119
verses.text: What are we about? Are we listening to this controversy as judges? That be far from us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:120
verses.text: Yea, rather as those whose place is under the Judge, let us knock, that we may obtain, 			 that it be opened to us; let us fly beneath the wings of our Lord God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:121
verses.text: For He did not speak in contradiction to His Apostle, seeing that He Himself spoke "in" him also, as he says, "Would ye receive a proof of Christ, who speaketh in me?" Christ in the Gospel, Christ in the Apostle: Christ therefore spake both; one by His own Mouth, the other by the mouth of His herald.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:122
verses.text: For when the herald pronounces anything from the tribunal, it is not written in the records, "the herald said it;" but he is written as having said it, who commanded the herald what to say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:123
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:124
verses.text: Let us then so give ear to these two precepts, Brethren, as that we may understand them, and let us settle ourselves in peace between them both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:125
verses.text: Let us but be in agreement with our own heart, and Holy Scripture will in no part disagree with itself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:126
verses.text: It is entirely true, both precepts are true; but we must make a distinction, that sometimes the one, sometimes the other must be done; that sometimes a brother must be "reproved between him and thee alone," sometimes a 			 brother "must be reproved before all, that others also may fear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:127
verses.text: If we do sometimes the one, and sometimes the other, we shall hold fast the harmony of the Scriptures, and shall not err in fulfilling and obeying them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:128
verses.text: But a man will say to me, "When am I to do this one, and when the other? lest I 'reprove between me and him alone,' when I ought to 'reprove before all;' or 'reprove before all,' when I ought to reprove in secret".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:129
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:130
verses.text: You will soon see, Beloved, what we ought to do, and when; only I would we may not be slow to practise it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:131
verses.text: Attend and see: "If thy brother sin against thee, rebuke him between him and thee alone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:132
verses.text: Why? Because it is against thee that he hath sinned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:133
verses.text: What is that, "hath sinned against thee"? Thou knowest that he hath sinned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:134
verses.text: For because it was secret when he sinned against thee, seek for secresy, when thou dost correct his sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:135
verses.text: For if thou only know that 			 he hath sinned against thee, and thou wouldest "rebuke him before all," thou art not a reprover, but a betrayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:136
verses.text: Consider how that "just man" Joseph spared his wife with such exceeding kindness, in so great a crime as he had suspected her of, before he knew by whom she had conceived; because he perceived that she was with child, and he knew that he had not come in unto her.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:137
verses.text: There remained then an unavoidable suspicion of adultery, and yet because he only had perceived, he only knew it, what does the Gospel say of him? "Then Joseph being a just man, and not willing to make her a public example".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:138
verses.text: The husband's grief sought no revenge; he wished to profit, not to punish the sinner.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:139
verses.text: "And not willing to make her a public example, he was minded to put her away privily".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:140
verses.text: But while he thought on these things, "behold, the Angel of the Lord appeared unto him," in sleep; and told him how it was, that she had not defiled her husband's bed, but that she had conceived of the Holy Ghost the Lord of them both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:141
verses.text: Thy brother then hath sinned against thee; if thou alone know it, then hath he really sinned against thee alone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:142
verses.text: For if in the hearing of many he hath done thee an injury, he hath sinned against them also whom he hath made witnesses of his iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:143
verses.text: For I tell you, my dearly beloved Brethren, what you can yourselves recognise in 			 your own case.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:144
verses.text: When any one does my brother an injury in my hearing, God forbid that I should think that injury unconnected with myself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:145
verses.text: Certainly he has done it to me also; yea to me the rather, to whom he thought what he did was pleasing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:146
