verses.text: Therefore those sins are to be reproved before all, which are committed before all; they are to be reproved with more secresy, which are committed more secretly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:147
verses.text: Distinguish times, and Scripture is in harmony with itself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:148
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:149
verses.text: So let us act; and so must we act not only when the sin is committed against ourselves, but when the sin is so committed by any one as that it is unknown by the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:150
verses.text: In secret ought we to rebuke, in secret to reprove him; lest if we would reprove him publicly, we should betray the man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:151
verses.text: We wish to rebuke and reform him; but what if his enemy is looking out to hear something that he may punish? For example, a Bishop knows of some one who has killed 			 another, and no one else knows of him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:152
verses.text: I wish to reprove him publicly; but thou art seeking to prosecute him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:153
verses.text: Decidedly then I will neither betray him, nor neglect him; I will reprove him in secret; I will set the judgment of God before his eyes; I will alarm his bloodstained conscience; I will persuade him to repentance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:154
verses.text: With this charity ought we to be endued.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:155
verses.text: And hence men sometimes find fault with us, as if we do not reprove; or they think that we know what we do not know, or that we hush up what we know.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:156
verses.text: And it may be that what thou knowest, I know also 			 but I will not reprove in thy presence I because I wish to cure, not to act informer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:157
verses.text: There are men who commit adultery in their own houses, they sin in secret, sometimes they are discovered to us by their own wives, generally through jealousy, sometimes as seeking their husband's salvation; in such cases we do not betray them openly, but reprove them in secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:158
verses.text: Where the evil has happened, there let the evil die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:159
verses.text: Yet do we not neglect that wound; above all things showing the man who is in 			 such a sinful state, and bears such a wounded conscience, that that is a deadly wound which they who suffer from, sometimes by an unaccountable perverseness despise; and seek out testimonies in their favour, I know not whence, null certainly and void, saying, "God careth not for sins of the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:160
verses.text: Where is that then which we have heard to-day, "Whoremongers and adulterers God will judge"? Lo! whosoever thou art that labourest under such a disease attend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:161
verses.text: Hear what God saith; not what thine own mind, in indulgence to thine own sins, may say, or what thy friend, thine enemy rather and his own too, bound in the same bond of iniquity with thee may say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:162
verses.text: Hear then what the Apostle saith; "Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:163
verses.text: But whoremongers and adulterers God will judge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:164
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:165
verses.text: Come then, Brother, be reformed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:166
verses.text: Thou art afraid lest thine enemy should prosecute thee; and art thou not afraid lest God should judge thee? Where is thy faith? Fear whilst there is the time for fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:167
verses.text: Far off indeed is the day of judgment; but every man's last day cannot be far off; for life is short.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:168
verses.text: And since this shortness is ever uncertain, thou knowest not when thy last day may be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:169
verses.text: Reform thyself today, because of to-morrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:170
verses.text: Let the reproof in secret be 			 of service to thee now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:171
verses.text: For I am speaking openly, yet do I reprove in secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:172
verses.text: I knock at the ears of all; but I accost the consciences of some.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:173
verses.text: If I were to say, "Thou adulterer, reform thyself;" perhaps in the first place I might say what I had no knowledge of; perhaps suspect on a rash hearsay report.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:174
verses.text: I do not then say, "Thou adulterer, reform thyself;" but "whosoever thou art among this people who art an adulterer, reform thyself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:175
verses.text: So the reproof is public; the reformation secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:176
verses.text: This I know, that whoso feareth, will reform himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:177
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:178
verses.text: Let no one say in his heart, "God careth not for sins of the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:179
verses.text: "Know ye not," saith the Apostle, "that ye are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? If any man defile the temple of God, him will God destroy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:180
verses.text: "Let no man deceive himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:181
verses.text: But perhaps a man will say, "My soul is the temple of God, not my body," and will add this testimony also, "All flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:182
verses.text: Unhappy interpretation! conceit meet for punishment! The flesh is called grass, because it dies; but take thou heed that that which dies for a time, rise not again with guilt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:183
verses.text: Wouldest thou ascertain a plain judgment on this point also? "Know ye not," says the same Apostle, "that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God?" Do not then any longer disregard sins of the body; seeing that your "bodies are the temples of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:184
verses.text: If thou didst disregard a sin of the body, wilt thou disregard a sin which thou committest against a temple? Thy very body is a temple of the Spirit of God within thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:185
verses.text: Now take heed what thou doest with the temple of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:186
verses.text: If thou wert to choose to commit adultery in the Church within these walls, what wickedness could be 			 greater? But now thou art thyself the temple of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:187
verses.text: In thy going out, in thy coming in, as thou abidest in thy house, as thou risest up, in all thou art a temple.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:188
verses.text: Take heed then what thou doest, take heed that thou offend not the Indweller of the temple, lest He forsake thee, and thou fall into ruins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:189
verses.text: "Know ye not," he says, "that your bodies" (and this the Apostle spake touching fornication, that they might not think lightly of sins of the body) "are the temples of the Holy Ghost 			 which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?" For "ye have been bought with a great price".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:190
verses.text: If thou think so lightly of thine own body, have some consideration for thy price.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:191
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:192
verses.text: I know, and as I do every one knows, who has used a little more than ordinary consideration, that no man who has any fear of God omits to reform himself in obedience to His words, but he who thinks that he has longer time to live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:193
verses.text: This it is which kills so many, while they are saying, "To-morrow, To-morrow;" and suddenly the door is shut.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:194
verses.text: He remains outside with the raven's croak, because he had not the moaning of the dove.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:195
verses.text: "To-morrow, To-morrow;" is the raven's croak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:196
verses.text: Moan plaintively as the dove, and beat thy breast; but whilst thou art inflicting blows on thy breast, be the better for the beating; lest thou seem not to beat thy conscience, but rather with blows to harden it, and make an evil conscience more unyielding instead of better.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:197
verses.text: Moan with no fruitless moaning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:198
verses.text: For it may be thou art saying to thyself, "God hath promised me 			 forgiveness, whenever I reform myself I am secure; I read the divine Scripture, "In the day that the wicked man turneth away from his wickedness, and doeth that which is lawful and right, I will forget all his iniquities".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:199
verses.text: I am secure then, whenever I reform myself, God will give me pardon for my evil deeds".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:200
verses.text: What can I say to this? Shall I lift up my voice against God? Shall I say to God, Do not give him pardon? Shall I say, This is not written, God hath not promised this? If I should say ought of this, I should say falsely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:201
verses.text: Thou speakest well and truly; God hath promised pardon on thy amendment, I cannot deny it; but tell me, I pray thee; see, I consent, I grant, I acknowledge that God hath 			 promised thee pardon, but who hath promised thee a to-morrow? Where thou dost read to me that thou shalt receive pardon, if thou reform thyself; there read to me how long thou hast to live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:202
verses.text: Thou dost confess, "I cannot read it there".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:203
verses.text: Thou knowest not then how long thou hast to live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:204
verses.text: Reform thyself, and so be always ready.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:205
verses.text: Be not afraid of the last day, as a thief, who will break up thy house as thou sleepest; but awake and reform thyself to-day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:206
verses.text: Why dost thou put it off till to-morrow? If 			 thy life is to be a long one, let it be both long and good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:207
verses.text: No one puts off a good dinner, because it is to be a long one, and dost thou wish to have a long evil life? Surely if it is to be long, it will be all the better if it be good; if it is to be short, it is well that its good be as long as possible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:208
verses.text: But men neglect their life to such a degree, as that they are unwilling to have anything bad except it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:209
verses.text: You buy a farm, and you look out for a good one; you wish to marry a wife, you choose a good one; you wish for the birth of children, and you long for good ones; you bargain for shoes, and you do not wish for bad ones; and yet a bad life you do love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:210
verses.text: How hath thy life offended thee, that thou art willing to have it only bad; that amid all thy good things thou shouldest thyself alone be evil?  15.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:211
verses.text: So then, my Brethren, if I should wish to reprove any of you individually in secret, perhaps he would listen to me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:212
verses.text: I reprove many of you now in public; all praise me; may some give attentive heed to me! I have no love for him who praises me with his voice, and with his heart despises me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:213
verses.text: For when thou dost praise, and not reform thyself, thou art a witness against thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:214
verses.text: If thou art evil, and thou art pleased with what I say, be displeased with thyself; 			 because if thou art displeased with thyself as being evil, when thou dost reform, thou wilt be well pleased with thyself, which if I mistake not I said the day before yesterday.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:215
verses.text: In all my words I set a mirror before you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:216
verses.text: Nor are they my words, but I speak at the bidding of the Lord, by whose terrors I refrain from keeping silence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:217
verses.text: For who would not rather choose to keep silence, and not to give account for you? But now I have undertaken the burden, and I cannot, and I ought not to shake it off 			 my shoulders.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:218
verses.text: When the Epistle to the Hebrews was being read, my Brethren, ye heard, "Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves; for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief; for that is unprofitable for you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:219
verses.text: When do we it with joy? When we see man making progress in the words of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:220
verses.text: When does the labourer in the field work with joy? When he looks at the tree, and sees the fruit; when he looks at the crop, and sees the prospect of abundance of corn in the floor; when he sees that he has not laboured in vain, has not bowed his back, and bruised his hands, and endured the cold and heat in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:221
verses.text: This is what he says, "That they may do it with joy, and not with grief; for that is 			 unprofitable for you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:222
verses.text: Did he say, "unprofitable for them"? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:223
verses.text: He said, "unprofitable for you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:224
verses.text: For when those who are set over you are saddened at your evil deeds, it is profitable for them; their very sadness is profitable for them; but it is unprofitable for you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:225
verses.text: But we do not wish that anything should be profitable for us, which for you is unprofitable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 31:226
verses.text: Let us then, Brethren, do good together in the Lord's field; that at the reward we may rejoice together.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:1
verses.text: Sermon XXXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:2
verses.text: [LXXXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:5
verses.text: xvii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:6
verses.text: 21, "How oft shall my brother sin against me," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:8
verses.text: Yesterday the holy Gospel warned us not to neglect the sins of our brethren: "But if thy brother shall sin against thee, rebuke him between him and thee alone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:9
verses.text: If he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:10
verses.text: But if he shall refuse to hear thee, take with thee two or three more; that in the mouth of two or three witnesses, every word may be established.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:11
verses.text: And if he shall neglect to hear them too, tell it to the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:12
verses.text: But if he shall 			 neglect to hear the Church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:13
verses.text: To-day also the section which follows, and which we heard when it was read, relates to the same subject.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:14
verses.text: For when the Lord Jesus had said this to Peter, he went on to ask his Master, how often he should forgive a brother who had sinned against him; and he enquired whether seven times would be enough.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:15
verses.text: "The Lord answered him, Not only seven times, but seventy times seven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:16
verses.text: Then he added a parable very full of terror: That the "kingdom of heaven is like unto an householder, which took account with his servants; among whom he found one that owed ten thousand talents.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:17
verses.text: And when he commanded all that he had, and all his family, and himself to be sold, and the debt to be paid, he fell down at his lord's feet," and prayed for delay, and obtained entire remission.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:18
verses.text: For as we have heard, "His lord was moved with compassion, and forgave him all the debt".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:19
verses.text: Then that man free from his debt, but a bondslave of iniquity, after he had gone out from the presence of his lord, found in his turn a debtor of his own, who owed him, not ten thousand talents, the sum which had been remitted to him, but a hundred denarii; and "he began to drag him by the throat, and say, Pay me that thou owest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:20
verses.text: Then he besought his fellow-servant as he had done his lord; but he did not find his fellow-servant such a man as the other had found his lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:21
verses.text: He not only would not forgive him the debt; but he did not even grant him a delay.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:22
verses.text: He hurried him along with great violence to make him pay, he who had been but just now set free from his debt to his lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:23
verses.text: His fellow-servants were displeased; and "went and told their lord what was done;" and the lord summoned his servant to his presence, and said to him, "O thou wicked servant, when thou didst owe me so great a debt, in pity to thee I forgave thee all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:24
verses.text: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellow-servant, even as I had pity on thee?" And he commanded that all which he had forgiven him should be paid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:25
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:26
verses.text: It is then for our instruction that He put forth this parable, and by this warning He would save us from perishing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:27
verses.text: "So," said He, "shall My heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:28
verses.text: Lo, Brethren, the thing is plain, useful is the admonition, and a wholesome obedience is by all means due, that what hath been bidden may be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:29
verses.text: For every man is at once God's debtor, and hath also some brother a debtor to himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:30
verses.text: For who is there who is not God's debtor, but he in whom there can be found no sin? And who is there who hath not a brother his debtor, but he against whom no one hath sinned? Think you that any one among mankind can be found, who is not 			 himself bounden to his brother by some sin? So then every man is a debtor, yet having himself his own debtors too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:31
verses.text: The righteous God therefore appointeth a rule for thee toward thy debtor, which He also will observe with His.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:32
verses.text: For two works of mercy are there, which deliver us, which the Lord hath Himself briefly laid down in the Gospel: "Forgive, and ye shall be forgiven: give, and it shall be given unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:33
verses.text: "Forgive, and ye shall be forgiven," relates to pardoning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:34
verses.text: "Give, and it shall be given unto you," relates to doing kindnesses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:35
verses.text: As to what He saith of pardoning, thou both wishest thy sin to be pardoned thee, and thou hast another whom thou mayest pardon.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:36
verses.text: Again, as to the doing kindnesses; a beggar asks of thee, and thou art God's beggar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:37
verses.text: For we are all when we pray God's beggars; we stand, yea rather we fall prostrate before the door of the Great Householder, we 			 groan in supplication wishing to receive something; and this something is God Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:38
verses.text: What does the beggar ask of thee? Bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:39
verses.text: And what dost thou ask of God, but Christ, who saith, "I am the living Bread which came down from heaven"? Would you be forgiven? Forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:40
verses.text: "Forgive, and it shall be forgiven you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:41
verses.text: Would you receive? "Give, and it shall be given unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:42
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:43
verses.text: But now hear what in so plain a precept I may cause a difficulty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:44
verses.text: In this question of forgiveness when pardon is asked, and it is due from him who should grant it, it may be a difficulty to us as it was to Peter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:45
verses.text: "How often ought I to forgive? Is up to seven times sufficient?" "It is not sufficient," saith the Lord, "I say not unto thee, Until seven times; but, Until seventy times seven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:46
verses.text: Now reckon up how often thy brother hath sinned against thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:47
verses.text: If thou canst reach the seventy-eighth fault, so as to get beyond the seventy times seven, then set about revenge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:48
verses.text: Is this then what He really means, and is it really so, that if he shall sin "seventy times seven," thou shouldest forgive him; but if he shall sin seventy times and eight, it should then be lawful for thee not to forgive? Nay I am bold to say, that if he should even sin seventy-eight times, thou 			 must forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:49
verses.text: Yea, as I have said, if he shall sin seventy-eight times, forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:50
verses.text: And if he sin a hundred times, forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:51
verses.text: And why need I say, so and so often? In one word, as often as he shall sin, forgive him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:52
verses.text: Have I then taken upon me to overpass the measure of my Lord? He fixed the limit of forgiveness in the number seventy-seven; shall I presume to overleap this limit? It is not so, I have not presumed to go at all beyond.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:53
verses.text: I have heard the Lord Himself speaking in His Apostle where there is no measure or number fixed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:54
verses.text: For He says, "Forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any, as God in Christ hath forgiven you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:55
verses.text: Here you have the rule.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:56
verses.text: If Christ have forgiven thee thy sins "seventy times and seven" only, if He have pardoned up to this point, and refused to pardon beyond it; then do thou also fix this limit, and be loth to forgive beyond it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:57
verses.text: But if Christ hath found thousands of sins upon sins, and hath yet forgiven all; withdraw not then thy mercy, but ask the forgiveness of that large number.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:58
verses.text: For it was not without a meaning that the Lord said "seventy times 			 seven;" forasmuch as there is no trespass whatever which thou oughtest not to forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:59
verses.text: See this servant in the parable, who being a debtor was found to have a debtor, owed ten thousand talents.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:60
verses.text: And I suppose that ten thousand talents are at least ten thousand sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:61
verses.text: For I will not say how but one talent will include all sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:62
verses.text: But how much did the other servant owe him? He owed a hundred denarii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:63
verses.text: Now is not this more than "seventy and seven"? And yet the Lord was wroth, because he did not 			 forgive him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:64
verses.text: For not only is a hundred more than "seventy-seven;" but a hundred denarii, perhaps are a thousand" asses".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:65
verses.text: But what was this to ten thousand talents?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:66
verses.text: And so let us be ready to forgive all the trespasses which are committed against us, if we desire to be forgiven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:67
verses.text: For if we consider our sins, and reckon up what we do in deed, what by the eye, what by the ear, what by thought, what by numberless movements; I know not whether we so much as sleep without a talent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:68
verses.text: And therefore do we daily beg, daily knock at the ears of God by prayer, daily prostrate ourselves and say, "Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our 			 debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:69
verses.text: What debts of thine? All, or a certain part? Thou wilt answer, All.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:70
verses.text: So then do thou with thy debtor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:71
verses.text: This then is the rule thou layest down, this the condition thou speakest of; this the covenant and agreement thou dost mention when thou prayest, saying, "Forgive us, as we forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:72
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:73
verses.text: What then, Brethren, is the meaning of "seventy times seven"? Hear, for it is a great mystery, a wonderful sacrament.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:74
verses.text: When the Lord was baptized, the Evangelist St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:75
verses.text: Luke has in that place commemorated His generations in the regular order, series, and line in which they had come down to that generation in which Christ was born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:76
verses.text: Matthew begins at Abraham, and comes down to Joseph in a descending order; but Luke begins to reckon in an ascending order.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:77
verses.text: Why does the one reckon in a descending, and the other in an ascending order? Because Matthew set forth the generation of Christ by which He came down to us; and so he began to reckon when Christ was born in a descending order.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:78
verses.text: Whereas, because Luke begins to reckon when Christ was baptized; in this is the beginning of ascension, he begins to reckon in an ascending order, and in his reckoning he has completed seventy-seven generations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:79
verses.text: With whom did he begin his reckoning? Observe with whom? He began to reckon from Christ up to Adam himself, who was the first sinner, and who begat us with the bond of sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:80
verses.text: He reckoned up to Adam, and so there are reckoned seventy-seven generations; that is, from Christ up to Adam and from Adam up to Christ are the aforesaid seventy-seven generations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:81
verses.text: So then if no generation was omitted, there is no exemption of any trespass which ought not to be forgiven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:82
verses.text: For therefore did 			 he reckon up his seventy-seven generations, which number the Lord mentioned as to the forgiveness of sins; since he begins to reckon from the baptism, wherein all sins are remitted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:84
verses.text: And, Brethren, observe in this a yet greater mystery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:85
verses.text: In the number seventy-seven is a mystery of the remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:86
verses.text: So many are the generations found to be from Christ to Adam.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:87
verses.text: Now then, ask with somewhat more careful diligence for the secret meaning of this number, and enquire into its hidden meaning; with more careful diligence knock, that it may be opened unto thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:88
verses.text: Righteousness consists in the observance of the Law of God: true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:89
verses.text: For the Law is set forth in ten precepts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:90
verses.text: Therefore it was that the servant in the parable 			 "owed ten thousand talents".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:91
verses.text: This is that memorable Decalogue written by the finger of God, and delivered to the people by Moses, the servant of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:92
verses.text: He "owed" then "ten thousand talents;" which signifies all sins, with reference to the number of the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:93
verses.text: And the other "owed a hundred denarii;" derived equally from the same number.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:94
verses.text: For a hundred times a hundred make ten thousand; and ten times ten make a hundred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:95
verses.text: And the one "owed ten thousand talents," and the other ten 			 times ten denarii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:96
verses.text: For there was no departure from the number of the law, and in both numbers you will find every kind of sin included.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:97
verses.text: Both are debtors, and both implore and beg for pardon; but the wicked, ungrateful servant would not repay what he had received, would not grant the mercy which had been undeservedly accorded to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:98
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:99
verses.text: Consider then, Brethren; every man begins from Baptism; he goes out free, the "ten thousand talents" are forgiven him; and when he goes out, he will soon find some fellow-servant his debtor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:100
verses.text: Let him note then, what sin itself is; for the number eleven is the transgression of the law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:101
verses.text: For the law is ten, sin eleven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:102
verses.text: For the law is denoted by ten, sin by eleven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:103
verses.text: Why is sin denoted by eleven? Because to get to eleven, there is the transgression of the ten.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:104
verses.text: But the due limit is fixed in the law; and the transgression of it is sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:105
verses.text: Now when you have passed beyond the ten, you come to eleven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:106
verses.text: This high mystery was figured out when the tabernacle was commanded to be built.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:107
verses.text: There are many things mentioned there in number, which are a great mystery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:108
verses.text: Among the rest, curtains of haircloth were ordered to be made not ten, but eleven; because by haircloth is signified the confession of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:109
verses.text: Now what do you require more? Would you know how that all sins are contained in this number "seventy-seven"? Seven then is usually put for a whole; because in seven days the revolution of time is completed, and when the seventh is ended, it returns to the first again, that the same revolution may be continued.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:110
verses.text: In such revolutions whole ages pass away: yet there is no departure from the number seven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:111
verses.text: For He spoke of 			 all sins, when He said "seventy times seven;" for multiply that eleven seven times, and it makes seventy-seven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:112
verses.text: Therefore would He have all sins forgiven, for He marked them out by the number" seventy-seven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:113
verses.text: Let no one then retain against himself by refusing to forgive, lest it be retained against him, when he prayeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:114
verses.text: For God saith, "Forgive, and thou shalt be forgiven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:115
verses.text: For I have forgiven thee first; do thou at least forgive after that.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:116
verses.text: For if thou wilt not forgive, I will call 			 thee back, and put upon thee again all that I had remitted to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:117
verses.text: For the Truth doth not speak falsely; Christ neither deceiveth, nor is deceived, and He hath said at the close of the parable, "So likewise shall your Father which is in heaven do unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:118
verses.text: Thou findest a Father, imitate thy Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:119
verses.text: For if thou wilt not imitate Him, thou art devising to be disinherited.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:120
verses.text: "So likewise" then "shall My heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:121
verses.text: Say not with the tongue, "I forgive," and put off to forgive in the heart; for by His threat of vengeance God showeth thee thy punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:122
verses.text: God knoweth where thou speakest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:123
verses.text: Man can hear thy voice; God looketh into thy conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:124
verses.text: If thou sayest, I forgive; forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:125
verses.text: Better is it that thou shouldest be violent 			 in words, and forgive in the heart, than in words be soft, and in the heart relentless.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:126
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:127
verses.text: Now then unruly boys will beg, and take it hard to be beat taking exception against us when we wish to chastise them after this fashion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:128
verses.text: "I have sinned, but forgive me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:129
verses.text: Well, I have forgiven, and he sins again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:130
verses.text: "Forgive me," he cries, and I have forgiven him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:131
verses.text: He sins a third time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:132
verses.text: "Forgive me," he cries, and a third time I have forgiven him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:133
verses.text: Now then the fourth time let him be beat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:134
verses.text: And he will say, "What! have I tired you out to seventy-seven times?" Now if by such exceptions the severity of discipline sleep, upon the suppression of 			 discipline wickedness will rage with impunity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:135
verses.text: What then is to be done? Let us reprove with words, and if need be with scourges; but let us withal forgive the sin, and cast away the remembrance of it from the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:136
verses.text: For therefore did the Lord add, "from your hearts," that though through affection discipline be exercised, gentleness might not depart out of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:137
verses.text: For what is so kind and gentle as the surgeon with his knife? He that is to be cut cries, yet cut he is; he that is to be 			 cauterized cries, but cauterized he is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:138
verses.text: This is not cruelty; on no account let that surgeon's treatment be called cruelty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:139
verses.text: Cruel he is against the wounded part that the patient may be cured; for if the wound be softly dealt with, the man is lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:140
verses.text: Thus then would I advise, my Brethren, that we love our brethren, howsoever they may have sinned against us; that we let not affection toward them depart out of our hearts, and that when need is, we exercise discipline toward them; lest by the 			 relaxation of discipline, wickedness increase, and we begin to be accused on God's behalf, for it has been read to us, "Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:141
verses.text: Certainly, if one, as is the only true way, distinguishes the times, and so solves the question, all is true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:142
verses.text: If the sin be in secret, rebuke it in secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 32:143
verses.text: If the sin be public and open, rebuke it publicly that the sinner may be reformed; and "that others also may fear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:1
verses.text: Sermon XXXIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:2

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:5
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:6
verses.text: 17, "If thou wouldest enter into life, keep the commandments".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:8
verses.text: The Lord said to a certain young man, "If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:9
verses.text: He did not say, "If thou wilt enter into life eternal," but "If thou wilt enter into life;" laying down that as life, which is to be life eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:10
verses.text: Let us first then set forth the value of the love of this life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:11
verses.text: For even this present life, under whatever circumstances, is loved; and men fear and dread to end it of whatever kind it be; however full of trouble and misery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:12
verses.text: Hence may we see, hence consider, how the life eternal should be loved; when this life so miserable, 			 and which must sometime come to an end, is loved so much.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:13
verses.text: Consider, Brethren, how greatly should that life be loved, where thou wilt never end life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:14
verses.text: Thou dost love, it seems, this present life, where thou dost labour so much, hastest to and fro, art busy, sufferest fatigue; yea scarcely to be enumerated are the necessities of this miserable life; sowing, ploughing, clearing the ground, sailing, grinding, cooking, weaving; and after all these things thou hast to end thy 			 life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:15
verses.text: See the evils thou dost suffer in this miserable life, which thou lovest; and dost thou think that thou shalt always live, and never die? Temples, stones, marbles, joined so strongly together with iron and lead, fall into ruin for all their strength; and does a man suppose that he shall never die? Learn then, Brethren, to seek for eternal life, where you will not endure all this, but will reign with God for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:16
verses.text: "For he who wisheth life," as the Prophet says, "loveth to see good 			 days".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:17
verses.text: For in evil days death is rather wished for than life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:18
verses.text: Do we not hear and see men when they are involved in some tribulations and distresses, in law-suits or sicknesses and they see that they are in travail, do we not hear them saying nothing else but, "O God, send me death, hasten my days"? Yet when sickness comes, they run about, and physicians are fetched, and money and rewards are promised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:19
verses.text: Death himself says to thee, "Lo, here I am, whom but a little while ago thou 			 wert asking of the Lord, why wouldest thou fly from me now? I have found thee to be a self-deceiver, and a lover of this miserable life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:21
verses.text: But as concerning these days which we are passing now, the Apostle says, "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:22
verses.text: Are not these days indeed evil which we spend in this corruptible flesh, in or under so heavy a load of the corruptible body, amid so great temptations, amid so great difficulties, where there is but false pleasure, no security of joy, a tormenting fear, a greedy covetousness, a withering sadness? Lo, what evil days! yet no one is willing to end these same evil days, and hence men earnestly pray God that they may live long.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:23
verses.text: Yet what is it to live long, but to be long 			 tormented? What is it to live long, but to add evil days to evil days? When boys are growing up, it is as if days are being added to them; whereas they do not know that they are being diminished; and their very reckoning is false.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:24
verses.text: For as we grow in up, the number of our days rather diminishes than increases.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:25
verses.text: Appoint for any man at his birth, for instance, eighty years; every day he lives, he diminishes somewhat of that sum.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:26
verses.text: Yet silly men rejoice at the oft-recurring birthdays, both of 			 themselves and their children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:27
verses.text: O sensible man! If the wine in thy bottle is diminished, thou art sad; days art thou losing, and art thou glad? These days then are evil; and so much the more evil, in that they are loved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:28
verses.text: This world is so alluring, that no one is willing to finish a life of sorrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:29
verses.text: For the true, the blessed life is this, when we shall rise again, and reign with Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:30
verses.text: For the ungodly too shall rise again but to go into the fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:31
verses.text: Life then is there again, but that which is 			 blessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:32
verses.text: And blessed life there can be none but that which is eternal, where are "good days;" and those not many days, but one day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:33
verses.text: They are called "days" after the custom of this life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:34
verses.text: That day knows no rising, it knows no setting.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:35
verses.text: To that day there succeeds no to-morrow; because no yesterday precedes it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:36
verses.text: This day, or these days, and this life, this true life, have we in promise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:37
verses.text: It is then the reward of a certain work.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 33:38
verses.text: So if we love the reward, let us not fail in the work; and so 			 shall we reign with Christ for ever.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:1
verses.text: Sermon XXXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:2
verses.text: [LXXXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:5
verses.text: xix.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:6
verses.text: 17, "If thou wouldest enter into life, keep the commandments".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:8
verses.text: The Gospel lesson which has now sounded in our ears, Brethren, requires rather an attentive hearer and a doer, than an expositor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:9
verses.text: What is more clear than this light, "If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments"? What then have I to say but, "If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments"? Who is there that does not wish for life? and yet who is there that does wish to keep the commandments? If thou dost not wish to keep the commandments, why seekest thou after life? If thou art slow to the work, why dost thou hasten to the reward? The rich young man in the Gospel said that he had kept the commandments; then he heard the greater precepts, "If thou wilt be perfect, one thing 			 is lacking to thee, go sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor;" thou shalt not lose them, but "thou shalt have treasure in heaven; and come and follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:10
verses.text: For what shall it profit thee, if thou shalt do all the rest, and yet not follow Me?" But as ye have heard, "he went away" sad and "sorrowful; for he had great riches".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:11
verses.text: What he heard, have we heard also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:12
verses.text: The Gospel is Christ's voice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:13
verses.text: He sitteth in heaven; but He doth not cease to speak on earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:14
verses.text: Let us not be deaf, for He is crying out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:15
verses.text: Let us not be dead; for He is thundering.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:16
verses.text: If thou wilt not do the greater things, do at least the less.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:17
verses.text: If the burden of the 			 greater be too much for thee, at least take up the less.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:18
verses.text: Why art thou slow to both? why settest thyself against both? The greater are, "Sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor, and follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:19
verses.text: The less are, "Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shall not bear false witness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:20
verses.text: Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:21
verses.text: These do; why do I call to thee, to sell thy possessions, from whom I cannot gain, that thou wouldest keep from plundering what is another's? Thou hast heard, "Thou shalt not steal;" yet thou dost plunder.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:22
verses.text: Before the eyes of so great a Judge, I find thee not a thief only, but a plunderer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:23
verses.text: Spare thyself, have pity on thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:24
verses.text: This life yet allows thee respite, do not refuse correction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:25
verses.text: Yesterday thou wast a thief; be not so to-day too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:26
verses.text: Or if peradventure thou hast been so 			 to-day already, be not so to-morrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:27
verses.text: Put a stop sometime to thy evil doing, and so require good for a reward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:28
verses.text: Thou wouldest have good things, and wouldest not be good; thy life is a contradiction to thy desires.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:29
verses.text: If to have a good country-seat, is a great good: how great an evil must it be to have an evil soul!  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:30
verses.text: The rich man "went away sorrowful;" and the Lord said, "How hardly shall he that hath riches enter into the kingdom of heaven!" And by putting forth a comparison He showed the difficulty to be such that it was absolutely impossible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:31
verses.text: For every impossible thing is difficult; but not every difficult thing is impossible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:32
verses.text: As to how difficult it is, take heed to the comparison; "Verily I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:33
verses.text: A camel to go through the eye of a needle! If He had said a gnat, it would be impossible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:34
verses.text: And then when His disciples heard it, they were grieved and said, "If this be so, who then can be saved?" What rich man? Give ear then to Christ, ye poor, I am speaking to the people of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:35
verses.text: Ye are more of you poor than rich, do ye then at least receive what I say, yet give heed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:36
verses.text: Whosoever of you boast of your poverty, beware of pride, lest the humble rich surpass you; beware of impiety, lest the pious rich surpass you; beware of drunkenness, lest the sober rich surpass you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:37
verses.text: Do not glory of your poverty, if they must not glory of their riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:38
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:39
verses.text: And let the rich give ear, if indeed they are rich; let them give ear to the Apostle, "Charge the rich of this world," for there are who are the rich of another world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:40
verses.text: The poor are the rich of another world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:41
verses.text: The Apostles are the rich of another world, who said, "As having nothing, and yet possessing all things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:42
verses.text: So that ye may know of what poor he is speaking he added, "of this world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:43
verses.text: Let the "rich" then "of this world" give ear to the Apostle, "Charge," he says, "the rich of this world, that they be not proud in their conceits".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:44
verses.text: The first worm of riches is pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:45
verses.text: A consuming moth, which gnaws the whole, and reduces it even to dust.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:46
verses.text: "Charge them," therefore, "not to be proud in their conceits, nor to trust in the uncertainty of riches" (they are the Apostle's words), "but in the living God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:47
verses.text: A thief may take away thy gold; who can take away thy God? What hath the rich man, if he hath not God? What hath the poor man not, if he have God? Therefore he says, "Nor to trust in riches, but in the living God, who giveth us all 			 things richly to enjoy;" with which all things He giveth also Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:48
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:49
verses.text: If then they ought not to "trust in riches," not to confide in them, "but in the living God;" what are they to do with their riches? Hear what: "Let them be rich in good works".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:50
verses.text: What does this mean? Explain, O Apostle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:51
verses.text: For many are loth to understand what they are loth to practise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:52
verses.text: Explain, O Apostle; give none occasion to evil works by the obscurity of thy words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:53
verses.text: Tell us what thou dost mean by, "let them be rich in good works".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:54
verses.text: Let them hear and understand; let them not be suffered to excuse themselves; but rather let them begin to accuse themselves, and to say what we have just heard in the Psalm, "For I acknowledge my sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:55
verses.text: Tell us what this is, "let them be rich in good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:56
verses.text: Let them easily distribute".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:57
verses.text: And what is "let them easily distribute"? What! is this too not understood? "Let them easily distribute, let them communicate".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:58
verses.text: Thou hast, another hath not: communicate, that God may communicate to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:59
verses.text: Communicate here, and thou shalt communicate there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:60
verses.text: Communicate thy bread here, and thou shalt receive Bread there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:61
verses.text: What bread here? That which thou dost gather with sweat and toil, 			 according to the curse upon the first man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:62
verses.text: What Bread there? Even Him who said, "I am the Living Bread which came down from heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:63
verses.text: Here thou art rich, but thou art poor there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:64
verses.text: Gold thou hast, but thou hast not yet the Presence of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:65
verses.text: Lay out what thou hast, that thou mayest receive what thou hast not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:66
verses.text: "Let them be rich in good works, let them easily distribute, let them communicate".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:67
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:68
verses.text: Must they then lose all they have? He said, "Let them communicate," not "Let them give the whole".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:69
verses.text: Let them keep for themselves as much as is sufficient for them, let them keep more than is sufficient.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:70
verses.text: Let us give a certain portion of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:71
verses.text: What portion? A tenth? The Scribes and Pharisees gave tithes for whom Christ had not yet shed His Blood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:72
verses.text: The Scribes and Pharisees gave tithes; lest haply thou shouldest think thou art doing any great thing in breaking thy bread to the poor; and this is scarcely a thousandth part of thy means.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:73
verses.text: And yet I am not finding fault with this; do even this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:74
verses.text: So hungry and thirsty am I, that I am glad even of these crumbs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:75
verses.text: But yet I cannot keep back what He who died for us said whilst 			 He was alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:76
verses.text: "Except your righteousness exceed the righteousness of the Scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:77
verses.text: He does not deal softly with us; for He is a physician, He cuts to the quick.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:78
verses.text: "Except your righteousness exceed the righteousness of the Scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:79
verses.text: The Scribes and Pharisees gave the tenth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:80
verses.text: How is it with you? Ask yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:81
verses.text: Consider what you do, and with what means you do it; how much you give, how much you leave for yourselves; what you spend on mercy, what you reserve for luxury.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:82
verses.text: So then, "Let them 			 distribute easily, let them communicate, let them lay up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may hold on eternal life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:84
verses.text: I have admonished the rich; now hear, ye poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:85
verses.text: Ye rich, lay out your money; ye poor, refrain from plundering.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:86
verses.text: Ye rich, distribute your means; ye poor, bridle your desires.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:87
verses.text: Hear, ye poor, this same Apostle; "Godliness with sufficiency is a great getting".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:88
verses.text: Getting is the acquiring of gain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:89
verses.text: The world is yours in common with the rich; ye have not a house in common with the rich, but ye have the heaven in common, the light in common.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:90
verses.text: Seek only for a sufficiency, seek for what is enough, and do not wish for more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:91
verses.text: All the rest is a weight, rather than a help; a burden, rather than an honour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:92
verses.text: "Godliness with sufficiency is great gain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:93
verses.text: First is Godliness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:94
verses.text: Godliness is the worship of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:95
verses.text: "Godliness with sufficiency.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:96
verses.text: For we 			 brought nothing into this world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:97
verses.text: Didst thou bring anything hither? Nay, not even did ye rich bring anything.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:98
verses.text: Ye found all here, ye were born naked as the poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:99
verses.text: In both alike is the same bodily infirmity; the same infant crying, the witness of our misery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:100
verses.text: "For we brought nothing into this world" (he is speaking to the poor), "neither can we carry anything out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:101
verses.text: And having food and covering, let us be therewith content".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:102
verses.text: "For they who wish to be rich".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:103
verses.text: "Who wish to be," not who are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:104
verses.text: For they who are so, well and good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:105
verses.text: They have heard their lesson, that they be "rich in good works, that they distribute easily, that they communicate".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:106
verses.text: They have heard already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:107
verses.text: Do ye now hear who are not yet rich.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:108
verses.text: "They who wish to be rich, fall into temptation and a snare, and into many hurtful and foolish lusts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:109
verses.text: Do ye not fear? Hear what follows; "which drown men in destruction and 			 perdition".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:110
verses.text: Dost thou not now fear? "for avarice is the root of all evil"? Avarice is the wishing to be rich, not the being rich already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:111
verses.text: This is avarice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:112
verses.text: Dost thou not fear to be "drowned in destruction and perdition"? Dost thou not fear "avarice the root of all evil"? Thou pluckest up out of thy field the root of thorns, and wilt thou not pluck up out of thy heart the root of evil desires? Thou cleansest thy field from which thy body gets its fruit, and wilt thou not cleanse thy heart where thy God indwelleth? "For avarice is the root of 			 all evil, which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and entangled themselves in many sorrows".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:113
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:114
verses.text: Ye have now heard what ye must do, ye have heard what ye must fear, ye have heard how the kingdom of heaven may be purchased, ye have heard by what the kingdom of heaven may be hindered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:115
verses.text: Be ye all of one mind in obeying the word of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:116
verses.text: God made both the rich and poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:117
verses.text: Scripture says, "The rich and the poor meet together, the Lord is the Maker of them both".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:118
verses.text: The rich and the poor meet together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:119
verses.text: In what way, except in this present life? The rich and the poor are born alike.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:120
verses.text: Ye meet one another as ye walk on the way together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:121
verses.text: Do not thou oppress, nor thou defraud.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:122
verses.text: The one hath need, the other hath plenty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:123
verses.text: But "the Lord is the Maker of them both".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:124
verses.text: By him who hath, He helpeth him that needeth; by him who hath not, He proveth him that hath.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 34:125
verses.text: We have heard, we have spoken; let us fear, let us take heed, let us pray, let us 			 attain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:6

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:8
verses.text: The Gospel by the present lesson has reminded me to speak to you, Beloved, of the heavenly treasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:9
verses.text: For our God hath not, as unbelieving covetous men suppose, wished us to lose what we have: if what hath been enjoined us be properly understood, and piously believed, and devoutly received; He hath not enjoined us to lose, but rather shown a place where we may lay up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:10
verses.text: For no man can help thinking of his treasure, and following his riches 			 in a kind of journeying of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:11
verses.text: If then they are buried in the earth, his heart will seek the lowest earth; but if they are reserved in heaven, his heart will be above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:12
verses.text: If Christians therefore have the will to do what they know that they also make open profession of (not that all who hear know this; and I would that they who have known it, knew it not in vain); if then they have the will to "lift up the heart" above, let them lay up there, what they love; and though yet in the flesh on earth, let them dwell with Christ in heart; and as her Head went before the Church, so let the heart of the Christian go before him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:13
verses.text: As the members are to go where Christ the Head hath gone before, so shall each man at his rising again go where his heart hath now 			 gone before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:14
verses.text: Let us go hence then by that part of us which we may; our whole man will follow whither one part of us is gone before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:15
verses.text: Our earthly house must fall to ruin; our heavenly house is eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:16
verses.text: Let us move our goods beforehand, whither we are ourselves getting ready to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:17
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:18
verses.text: We have just heard a certain rich man seeking counsel from the "Good Master" as to the means of obtaining eternal life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:19
verses.text: Great was the thing he loved, and of little value was that he was unwilling to renounce.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:20
verses.text: And so in perverseness of heart, on hearing Him whom he had but now called "Good Master," through the overpowering love of what was valueless, he lost the possession of what was of great price.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:21
verses.text: If he had not wished to obtain eternal life, he would 			 not have asked counsel how to obtain eternal life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:22
verses.text: How is it then, Brethren, that he rejected the words of Him whom he had called "Good Master," drawn out for him as they were from the doctrine of the faith? What? Is He a Good Master before He teacheth, and when He hath taught, a bad one? Before He taught, He was called "Good".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:23
verses.text: He did not hear what he wished, but he did hear what was proper for him; he had come with longing, but he went away in sadness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:24
verses.text: What if He had told him, "Lose 			 what thou hast"? when he went away sad, because it was said, "Keep what thou hast securely".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:25
verses.text: "Go," saith He, "sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:26
verses.text: Art thou afraid, it may be, lest thou shouldest lose it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:27
verses.text: See what follows; "And thou shall have treasure in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:28
verses.text: Before now it may be thou hast set some young slave to guard thy treasures; thy God will be the guardian of thy gold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:29
verses.text: He who gave them on earth, will Himself keep them in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:30
verses.text: Perhaps he would not have hesitated to commit what he had to Christ, and was only sad because it was told him, "Give to the poor;" as though he would say in his heart, "Hadst 			 Thou said, Give it to Me, I will keep it in heaven for thee; I would not hesitate to give it to my Lord, the 'Good Master;' but now thou hast said, 'Give to the poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:31
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:32
verses.text: Let no one fear to lay out upon the poor, let no one think that he is the receiver whose hand he sees.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:33
verses.text: He receives it Who bade thee give it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:34
verses.text: And this I say not out of mine own heart, or by any human conjecture; hear Him Himself, who at once exhorteth thee, and giveth thee a title of security.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:35
verses.text: "I was an hungred," saith He, and ye gave Me meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:36
verses.text: And when after the enumeration of all their kind offices, they answered, "When saw we Thee an hungred?" He 			 answered, "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these of Mine, ye have done it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:37
verses.text: It is the poor man who begs, but He that is Rich receives.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:38
verses.text: Thou givest to one who will make away with it, He receiveth it Who will restore it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:39
verses.text: Nor will He restore only what He receiveth; He is pleased to borrow upon interest, He promiseth more than thou hast given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:40
verses.text: Give the rein now to thy avarice, imagine thyself an usurer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:41
verses.text: If thou wert an usurer indeed, thou wouldest be rebuked by the Church, confuted by the word of God, all thy brethren would execrate thee, as a cruel 			 usurer, desiring to wring gain from other's tears.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:42
verses.text: But now be an usurer, no one will hinder thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:43
verses.text: Thou art willing to lend to a poor man, who whenever he may repay thee will do it with grief; but lend now to a debtor who is well able to pay, and who even exhorteth thee to receive what he promiseth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:44
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:45
verses.text: Give to God, and press God for payment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:46
verses.text: Yea rather give to God, and thou wilt be pressed to receive payment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:47
verses.text: On earth indeed thou hadst to seek thy debtor; and he sought too, but only to find where he might hide himself from thy face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:48
verses.text: Thou hadst gone to the judge, and said, "Bid that my debtor be summoned;" and he on hearing this gets away, and cares not even to wish thee well, though to him perhaps in his need thou hadst given wealth by thy loan.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:49
verses.text: Thou hast one then on whom thou mayest well lay out thy money.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:50
verses.text: Give to Christ; He will of His own accord press thee to receive, whilst thou wilt even wonder that He hath received ought of thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:51
verses.text: For to them who are placed on His right hand He will first say, "Come, ye blessed of My Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:52
verses.text: "Come" whither? "Receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:53
verses.text: For what? "For I 			 was an hundred, and ye gave Me meat; I was thirsty, and ye gave Me drink; I was a stranger, and ye took Me in; naked, and ye clothed Me; I was sick and in prison, and ye visited Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:54
verses.text: And they will say, "Lord, when saw we Thee?" What doth this mean? The debtor presses to pay, and the creditors make excuses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:55
verses.text: But the trusty debtor will not let them suffer loss thereby.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:56
verses.text: "Do ye hesitate to receive? I have received, and are ye ignorant of it?" and He makes answer how He has received; "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these of Mine, ye have done it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:57
verses.text: "I received it not by Myself; but by Mine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:58
verses.text: What was given to them came to Me; be secure, ye have not lost it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:59
verses.text: Ye looked to those who were little able 			 to pay on earth; ye have One who is well able to pay in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:60
verses.text: I," He saith, "have received, I will repay".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:61
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:62
