verses.text: And what have I received, and what do I repay? "'I was an hungred,' He saith, 'and ye gave Me meat;' and the rest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:63
verses.text: I received earth, I will give heaven; I received temporal things, I will restore eternal; I received bread, I will give life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:64
verses.text: Yea, we may even say thus, "I have received bread, I will give Bread; I have received drink, I will give Drink; I have received houseroom, I will give a House; I was visited in sickness, I will give Health; I 			 was visited in prison, I will give Liberty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:65
verses.text: The bread which ye gave to My poor is consumed; the Bread which I will give both recruiteth the failing and doth not fail".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:66
verses.text: May He then give us Bread, He who is the living Bread which came down from heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:67
verses.text: When He shall give Bread, He will give Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:68
verses.text: For what didst thou intend when thou didst lend on usury? To give money, and to receive money; but to give a smaller sum, and to receive a larger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:69
verses.text: "I," saith God, "will give thee an exchange for the better for all that thou hast given Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:70
verses.text: For if thou wert to give a pound of silver, and to receive a pound of 			 gold, with how great joy wouldest thou be possessed? Examine and question avarice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:71
verses.text: "I have given a pound of silver, I receive a pound of gold!" What proportion is there between silver and gold! Much more then, what proportion is there between earth and heaven! And thy silver and gold thou wert to leave here below; whereas thou wilt not abide thyself for ever here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:72
verses.text: "And I will give thee something else, and I will give thee something more, and I will give thee something better; I will give 			 thee even that which will last for ever".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:73
verses.text: So then, Brethren, be our avarice restrained, that another, which is holy, may be enkindled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:74
verses.text: Evil altogether is her counsel, who hinders you from doing good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:75
verses.text: Ye are willing to serve an evil mistress, not owning a Good Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:76
verses.text: And sometimes two mistresses occupy the heart, and tear the slave asunder who deserves to be in slavery to such a double yoke.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:77
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:78
verses.text: Yes, sometimes two opposing mistresses have possession of a man, avarice and luxuriousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:79
verses.text: Avarice says, "Keep;" luxuriousness, says, "Spend".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:80
verses.text: Under two mistresses bidding and exacting diverse things what canst thou do? They have both their mode of address.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:81
verses.text: And when thou dost begin to be unwilling to obey them, and to take a step towards thy liberty; because they have no power to command, they use caresses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:82
verses.text: And their caresses are more to be guarded 			 against than their commands.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:83
verses.text: What says avarice? "Keep for thyself, keep for thy children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:84
verses.text: If thou shouldest be in want, no one will give to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:85
verses.text: Live not for the time present only; consult for the future".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:86
verses.text: On the other hand is luxuriousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:87
verses.text: Live whilst thou mayest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:88
verses.text: Do good to thine own soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:89
verses.text: Die thou must, and thou knowest not when; thou knowest not to whom thou shalt leave what thou hast, or who shall possess it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:90
verses.text: Thou art taking the bread out of thine own mouth, and perhaps after thy 			 death thine heir will not so much as place a cup of wine upon thy tomb; or if so be he place a cup, he will drink himself drunk with it, not a drop will come down to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:91
verses.text: Do well therefore to thine own soul, when and whilst thou canst".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:92
verses.text: Thus avarice did enjoin one thing; "Keep for thyself, consult for the future".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:93
verses.text: Luxuriousness another, "Do well to thine own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:94
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:95
verses.text: But O free man, called unto liberty, be weary, be weary of thy servitude to such mistresses as these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:96
verses.text: Acknowledge thy Redeemer, thy Deliverer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:97
verses.text: Serve Him, He enjoineth easier things, He enjoineth not things contrary one to another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:98
verses.text: I am bold further to say; avarice and luxuriousness did enjoin upon thee contrary things, so that thou couldest not obey them both; and one said, "Keep for thyself, and consult for the future;" the other said, "Spend freely, do well to 			 thine own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:99
verses.text: Now let thy Lord and thy Redeemer come forth, and He shall say the same, and yet no contrary things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:100
verses.text: If thou wilt not, His house hath no need of an unwilling servant.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:101
verses.text: Consider thy Redeemer, consider thy Ransom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:102
verses.text: He came to redeem thee, He shed His Blood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:103
verses.text: Dear He held thee whom He purchased at so dear a price.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:104
verses.text: Thou dost acknowledge Him who bought thee, consider from what He redeemeth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:105
verses.text: I say nothing of the other sins which lord it proudly over thee; for thou wast serving 			 innumerable masters.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:106
verses.text: I speak only of these two, luxuriousness and avarice, giving thee contrary injunctions, hurrying thee into different things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:107
verses.text: Deliver thyself from them, come to thy God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:108
verses.text: If thou wast the servant of iniquity, be now the servant of righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:109
verses.text: The words which they spake to thee, and the contrary injunctions they gave thee, the very same thou hearest now from thy Lord, yet are His injunctions not contrary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:110
verses.text: He doth not take away their words, but he taketh away their power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:111
verses.text: What did avarice say to thee? "Keep for thyself, consult for the future".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:112
verses.text: The word is not changed, but the man is changed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:113
verses.text: Now, if thou wilt, compare the counsellors.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:114
verses.text: The one is avarice, the other righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:115
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:116
verses.text: Examine these contrary injunctions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:117
verses.text: "Keep for thyself," says avarice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:118
verses.text: Suppose thou art willing to obey her, ask her where thou art to keep? Some well-defended place she will show thee, walled chamber, or iron chest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:119
verses.text: Well, use all precautions; yet peradventure some thief in the house will burst open the secret places; and whilst thou art taking precautions for thy money, thou wilt be in fear of thy life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:120
verses.text: It may be whilst thou art keeping up thy store, he whose mind 			 is set to plunder them, has it even in his thoughts to kill thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:121
verses.text: Lastly, even though by various precautions thou shouldest defend thy treasure and thy clothes against thieves; defend them still against the rust and moth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:122
verses.text: What canst thou do then? Here is no enemy without to take away thy goods, but one within consuming them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:123
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:124
verses.text: No good counsel then has avarice given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:125
verses.text: See she has enjoined thee to keep, yet has not found a place where thou mayest keep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:126
verses.text: Let her give also her next advice, "Consult for the future".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:127
verses.text: For what future? for a few and those uncertain days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:128
verses.text: She says, "Consult for the future," to a man who, it may be, will not live even till to-morrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:129
verses.text: But suppose him to live as long as avarice thinks he will, not as long as she can prove, or assure him, or have any 			 confidence about, but suppose him to live as long as she thinks, that he grow old and so come to his end: when he is even now bent double with old age, and leaning on his stick for support, still is he seeking gain, and hears avarice saying still, "Consult for the future".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:130
verses.text: For what future? When he is even at his last breath she speaks.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:131
verses.text: She says, "for thy children's sake".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:132
verses.text: Would that at least we did not find the old men who had no children avaricious.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:133
verses.text: Yet to these even, to such as 			 these even, who cannot even excuse their iniquity by any empty show of natural affection, she ceases not to say, "Consult for the future".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:134
verses.text: But it may be that these will soon blush for themselves; so let us look to those who have children, whether they are certain that their children will possess what they shall leave? Let them observe in their lifetime the children of other men, some losing what they had by the unjust violence of others, others by their own wickedness consuming what they possessed; and they remain in poor estate, who 			 were the children of rich men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:135
verses.text: Cease then to be the home-born slaves of avarice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:136
verses.text: But a man will say, "My children will possess this".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:137
verses.text: It is uncertain; I do not say, it is false, but at best, it is uncertain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:138
verses.text: But now suppose it to be certain, what dost thou wish to leave them? What thou hast gotten for thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:139
verses.text: Assuredly what thou hast gotten was not left thee, yet thou hast it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:140
verses.text: If thou hast been able to get possession of what was not left to thee, then will they also be able to get what 			 thou shalt not leave to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:141
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:142
verses.text: Thus have the counsels of avarice been refuted; but now let the Lord say the same words, now let righteousness speak: the words will be the same, but not the same the meaning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:143
verses.text: "Keep for thyself," saith the Lord, "consult for the future".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:144
verses.text: Now ask Him, "Where shall I keep?" "Thou shalt have treasure in heaven, where no thief approacheth, nor moth corrupteth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:145
verses.text: Against what an enduring future shalt thou keep it! "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:146
verses.text: And of how many days this kingdom is, the end of the passage shows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:147
verses.text: For after He had said of those on the left hand, "So these shall go away into everlasting burning;" of those on the right hand He saith, "but the righteous into life eternal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:148
verses.text: This is "consulting for the future".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:149
verses.text: A future which has no future beyond it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:150
verses.text: Those days without an end are called both "days," and "a day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:151
verses.text: For one when he was speaking of those days, saith, "That I may dwell in the house of the Lord for length of days".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:152
verses.text: And they are called a day, "This day have I begotten thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:153
verses.text: Now those days are one day; because there is no time, in it; that day is neither preceded by a yesterday, nor succeeded by a to-morrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:154
verses.text: So then let us "consult for the future:" the words indeed which avarice said to thee are not different in terms from this, yet by them is avarice overthrown.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:155
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:156
verses.text: One thing may yet be said, "But what am I to do about my children?" Hear on this point also the counsel of thy Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:157
verses.text: If thy Lord should say to thee, "The thoughts of them concern Me more who did create, than thee who didst beget them," peradventure thou couldest have nothing to say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:158
verses.text: Yet thou wilt look upon that rich man who went away sorrowful, and was rebuked in the Gospel, and wilt say to thyself perhaps, "That rich man did evil in not selling all and giving to the poor, because he had no children; but I have children; I have those for whom I should be keeping something.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:159
verses.text: In this weakness too the Lord is ready to advise with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:160
verses.text: I would be bold to speak through His mercy; I would be bold to say 			 something, not of mine own imagining, but of His pity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:161
verses.text: Keep then for thy children too, but hear me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:162
verses.text: Suppose (such is man's condition) any one should lose one of his children; mark, Brethren, mark how that avarice has no excuse, either as respects this world or the world to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:163
verses.text: Such, I say, is man's condition; for it is not that I wish it, but we see instances.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:164
verses.text: Some Christian child has been lost: thou hast lost a Christian child; not that thou hast indeed lost 			 him, but hast sent him before thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:165
verses.text: For he is not gone quite away, but gone before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:166
verses.text: Ask thine own faith: surely thou too wilt go thither presently, where he hath gone before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:167
verses.text: It is but a short question I ask, which yet I suppose no one will answer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:168
verses.text: Does thy son live? Ask thy faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:169
verses.text: If he live then, why is his portion seized upon by his brothers? But thou wilt say, What, will he return and possess it? Let it then be sent to him whither he is gone before; he cannot come to his goods, his goods can go to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:170
verses.text: Consider only with Whom 			 he is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:171
verses.text: If any son were serving at the Court, and became the Emperor's friend, and were to say to thee, "Sell my portion, which is there, and send it to me;" wouldest thou find what to answer him? Well, thy son is now with the Emperor of all emperors, with the King of all kings, with the Lord of all lords; send to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:172
verses.text: I do not say thy son is in need himself; but his Lord with whom he is, is in need upon the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:173
verses.text: He vouchsafes to receive here, what He gives in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:174
verses.text: Do what some 			 avaricious men are wont to do, make out a conveyance, bestow upon those who are in pilgrimage, what thou mayest receive in thine own country.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:175
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:176
verses.text: But now I am not speaking at all of thyself, but of thy child.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:177
verses.text: Thou art hesitating to give what is thine own, yea, rather art hesitating to restore what is another's; surely thou art hereby convicted, that it was not for thy children that thou wast laying up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:178
verses.text: See, thou dost not give to thy children, seeing thou wilt even take away from thy children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:179
verses.text: From this child at all events wilt thou take away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:180
verses.text: Why is he unworthy to receive his part, because he is living 			 with One worthier than all? There would be reason in it, if he with whom thy son is living, were unwilling to receive it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:181
verses.text: Rich shalt thou now be for thine house, but that the house of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:182
verses.text: So far it is then from me to say to thee, "Give what thou hast;" that I am saying to thee, "Pay that thou owest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:183
verses.text: But thou wilt say, "His brothers will have it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:184
verses.text: O evil maxim, which may teach thy children to wish for their brother's death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:185
verses.text: If they shall be enriched by the property of their 			 deceased brother, take heed how they may watch for one another in thine house.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:186
verses.text: What then wilt thou do? Wilt thou divide his patrimony, and so give lessons of parricide?  13.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:187
verses.text: But I am unwilling to speak of the loss of a child, lest I seem to threaten calamities, which do befall men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:188
verses.text: Let us speak in some more happy and auspicious tone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:189
verses.text: I do not say then, thou wilt have one less; reckon rather that thou hast one more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:190
verses.text: Give Christ a place with thy children, be thy Lord added to thy family; be thy Creator added to thy offspring, be thy Brother added to the number of thy children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:191
verses.text: For though there is so great a distance, yet hath He 			 condescended to be a Brother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:192
verses.text: And though He be the Father's Only Son, He hath vouchsafed to have coheirs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:193
verses.text: Lo, how bountifully hath He given! why wilt thou give in such barren sort? Thou hast two children; reckon Him a third: thou hast three, let Him be reckoned as a fourth: thou hast five, let Him be called a sixth; thou hast ten, let Him be the eleventh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:194
verses.text: I will say no more; keep the place of one child for thy Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:195
verses.text: For what thou shalt give to thy Lord, will profit both thee and thy children; 			 whereas, what thou dost keep for thy children wrongly, will hurt both thee and them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:196
verses.text: Now thou wilt give one portion, which thou hast reckoned as one child's portion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:197
verses.text: Reckon that thou hast got one child more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:198
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:199
verses.text: What great demand is this, my Brethren? I give you counsel only; do I use violence? As saith the Apostle, "This I speak for your own profit, not that I may cast a snare upon you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:200
verses.text: I imagine, Brethren, that it is a light and easy thought for a father of children to suppose that he has one child more, and thereby to procure such an inheritance as thou mayest possess for ever, both thou and thy children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:201
verses.text: Avarice can say nothing against it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:202
verses.text: Ye have cried out in acclamation at these words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:203
verses.text: Turn your words rather against her; let her not overcome you; let her not have greater power in your hearts, than your Redeemer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:204
verses.text: Let her not have greater power in your 			 hearts, than He who exhorteth us to "lift up our hearts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:205
verses.text: And so now let us dismiss her.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:206
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:207
verses.text: What says luxuriousness? What? "Do well to thine own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:208
verses.text: See also the Lord says the same, "Do well to thine own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:209
verses.text: What luxuriousness was saying to thee, the same saith Righteousness to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:210
verses.text: But consider here again in what sense the words are used.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:211
verses.text: If thou wouldest do well to thine own soul, consider that rich man who wished to do well to his soul, after the counsel of luxuriousness and avarice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:212
verses.text: His "ground brought forth plentifully, and he had 			 no room where to bestow his fruits; and he said, What shall I do?" I have no room where to bestow my fruits; I have found out what to do; "I will pull down my" old "barns, and build new," and will fill them, "and say to my soul, Thou hast much goods; take thy pleasure".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:213
verses.text: Hear the counsel against luxuriousness; "Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee; and whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?" And whither must that soul which shall be required of him go? This night it shall be required, and shall go he knows not whither.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:214
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:215
verses.text: Consider that other luxurious, proud, rich man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:216
verses.text: He "feasted sumptuously every day, and was clothed in purple and fine linen;" and "the poor man laid at his gate full of sores, and desired" in vain "the crumbs from the rich man's table;" he fed the dogs with his sores, but he was not fed by the rich man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:217
verses.text: They both died; one of them was buried; of the other what is said? "He was carried by the Angels into Abraham's bosom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:218
verses.text: The rich man sees the poor man; yea rather it is now the poor man sees the rich; he longs for a drop of water on his tongue from his finger, from him who once longed for a crumb from his table.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:219
verses.text: Indeed their lot was changed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:220
verses.text: The dead rich man asks for this in vain: O let not us who are 			 alive hear it in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:221
verses.text: For he wished to return again to the world, and was not permitted; he wished one of the dead to be sent to his brethren, neither was this granted him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:222
verses.text: But what was said to him? "They have Moses and the Prophets;" and he said, "They will not hear except one go from the dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:223
verses.text: Abraham said to him, "If they hear not Moses and the Prophets, neither will they believe though one go from the dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:224
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:225
verses.text: What luxuriousness then said in a perverted sense concerning the giving of alms, and procuring rest for our souls against the time to come, that so we may "do well to our souls," Moses also and the Prophets have spoken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:226
verses.text: Let us give ear while we are alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:227
verses.text: Because there he will desire in vain to hear, who has despised these words when he heard them here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:228
verses.text: Are we expecting that one should rise even from the dead, and tell us to do well to our own souls? It has been 			 done already: thy father hath not risen again, but thy Lord hath risen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:229
verses.text: Hear Him, and accept good counsel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:230
verses.text: Spare not thy treasures, spend as freely as thou canst.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:231
verses.text: This was the voice of luxuriousness: it has become the Lord's Voice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:232
verses.text: Spend as freely as thou canst, do well to thy soul, lest this night thy soul be required.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:233
verses.text: Here then ye have in Christ's Name a discourse as I think on the duty of almsgiving.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 35:234
verses.text: This your voice now applauding, is then only well-pleasing to the Lord, if He see withal 			 your hands active in works of mercy.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:1
verses.text: Sermon XXXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:2
verses.text: [LXXXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:4
verses.text: ]  Delivered on the Lord's Day, on that which is written in the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:5
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:6
verses.text: 1, "The kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that was a householder, who went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:8
verses.text: Ye have heard out of the Holy Gospel a parable well suited to the present season, concerning the labourers in the vineyard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:9
verses.text: For now is the time of the material vintage.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:10
verses.text: Now there is also a spiritual vintage, wherein God rejoiceth in the fruit of His vineyard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:11
verses.text: For we cultivate God, and God cultivateth us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:12
verses.text: But we do not so cultivate God as to make Him any better thereby.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:13
verses.text: For our cultivation is the labour of the heart, not of the hands.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:14
verses.text: He cultivateth us as the husbandman doth his field.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:15
verses.text: In then that He cultivateth us, He maketh us better; because so doth the husbandman make his field better by cultivating it, and the very fruit He seeketh in us is, that we may cultivate Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:16
verses.text: The culture He exerciseth on us is, that He ceaseth not to root out by His Word the evil seeds from our hearts, to open our heart, as it were, by the plough of His Word, to plant the seed of His precepts, to wait for the fruit of piety.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:17
verses.text: For when we have so received that culture into our heart, as to cultivate Him well, we are not ungrateful to our Husbandman, but render the fruit wherein He rejoiceth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:18
verses.text: And our fruit doth not make Him the richer, but us the happier.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:19
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:20
verses.text: See then; hear how, as I have said, "God cultivateth us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:21
verses.text: For that we cultivate God, there is no need to be proved to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:22
verses.text: For all men have this on their tongue, that men cultivate God, but the hearer feels a kind of awe, when he hears that God cultivates man; because it is not after the ordinary usage of men to say, that God cultivateth men, but that men cultivate God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:23
verses.text: We ought therefore to prove to you, that God also doth cultivate men; lest perchance we be 			 thought to have spoken a word contrary to sound doctrine, and men dispute in their heart against us, and as not knowing our meaning, find fault with us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:24
verses.text: I have determined therefore to show you, that God doth also cultivate us; but as I have said already, as a field, that He may make us better.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:25
verses.text: Thus the Lord saith in the Gospel, "I am the Vine, ye are the branches, My Father is the Husbandman".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:26
verses.text: What doth the Husbandman do? I ask you who are husbandmen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:27
verses.text: I suppose he cultivates his field.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:28
verses.text: If then God the Father be a Husbandman, He hath a field; and His field He cultivateth, and from it He expecteth fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:29
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:30
verses.text: Again, He "planted a vineyard," as the Lord Jesus Christ Himself saith, "and let it out to husbandmen, who should render Him the fruit in the proper season.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:31
verses.text: And He sent His servants to them to ask for the hire of the vineyard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:32
verses.text: But they treated them despitefully, and killed some," and contemptuously refused to render the fruits.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:33
verses.text: "He sent others also," they suffered the like treatment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:34
verses.text: And then the Householder, the Cultivator of His field, and the Planter, and Letter out of His vineyard, said; "I will send Mine Only Son, it may be they will at least reverence Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:35
verses.text: And so He saith, "He sent His Own Son also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:36
verses.text: They said among themselves, This is the heir, come, let us kill Him, and the inheritance shall be ours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:37
verses.text: And they 			 killed Him, and cast Him out of the vineyard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:38
verses.text: When the Lord of the vineyard cometh, what will He do to those wicked husbandmen? They answered, He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out His vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render Him the fruits in their seasons".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:39
verses.text: The vineyard was planted when the law was given in the hearts of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:40
verses.text: The Prophets were sent, seeking fruit, even their good life: the Prophets were treated despitefully by them, and were killed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:41
verses.text: Christ also was sent, the Only Son of the Householder; and they killed Him who was the Heir, and so lost the inheritance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:42
verses.text: Their evil counsel turned out contrary to their designs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:43
verses.text: They killed Him that they might possess the inheritance; and because they killed Him, they lost it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:44
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:45
verses.text: Ye have just heard too the parable out of the Holy Gospel; that "the kingdom of heaven is like unto a householder, which went out to hire labourers into His vineyard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:46
verses.text: He went out in the morning," and hired those whom he found, and agreed with them for a denarius as their hire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:47
verses.text: He "went out again at the third hour, and found others," and brought them to the labour of the vineyard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:48
verses.text: "And the sixth and ninth hour he did likewise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:49
verses.text: He went out also at the 			 eleventh hour," near the end of the day, "and found some idle and standing still, and he said to them, Why stand ye here?" Why do ye not work in the vineyard? They answered, "Because no man hath hired us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:50
verses.text: "Go ye also," said He, "and whatsoever is right I will give you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:51
verses.text: His pleasure was to fix their hire at a denarius.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:52
verses.text: How could they who had only to work one hour dare hope for a denarius? Yet they congratulated themselves in the hope that they should receive something.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:53
verses.text: So then these were brought in even for one hour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:54
verses.text: At the end of the day he ordered the hire to be paid to all, from the last to the first.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:55
verses.text: Then he began to pay at those who had come in at the eleventh hour, and he commanded a denarius to be given them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:56
verses.text: When they who had come at 			 the first hour saw that the others had received a denarius, which he had agreed for with themselves "they hoped that they should have received more:" and when their turn came, they also received a denarius.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:57
verses.text: "They murmured against the good man of the house, saying, Behold, thou hast made us who have borne the burning and heat of the day, equal and like to those who have laboured but one hour in the vineyard".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:58
verses.text: And "the good man," returning a most just answer to one of them, said, 			 "Friend, I do thee no wrong;" that is, "I have not defrauded thee, I have paid thee what I agreed for with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:59
verses.text: "I have done thee no wrong," for I have paid thee what I agreed for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:60
verses.text: To this other it is my will not to render a payment, but to bestow a gift.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:61
verses.text: "Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?" If I had taken from any one what did not belong to me, rightly I might be blamed, as fraudulent and unjust: if I had not paid any 			 one his due, rightly might I be blamed as fraudulent, and as withholding what belonged to another; but when I pay what is due, and give besides to whom I will, neither can he to whom I owed find fault, and he to whom I gave ought to rejoice the more".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:62
verses.text: They had nothing to answer; and all were made equal; "and the last became first, and the first last;" by equality of treatment, not by inverting their order.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:63
verses.text: For what is the meaning of, "the last were first, and the first last"? That both the first and last received the same.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:64
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:65
verses.text: How is it that he began to pay at the last? Are not all, as we read, to receive together? For we read in another place of the Gospel, that He will say to those whom He shall set on the right hand, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:66
verses.text: If all then are to receive together, how do we understand in this place, that they received first who began to work at the eleventh hour, and they last who were hired at the first hour? If I shall be able so to speak, as to reach your understanding, God be thanked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:67
verses.text: For to Him ought ye to render thanks, who distributeth to you by me; for nought of my own do I distribute.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:68
verses.text: If ye ask me, for example, which of the two has received first, he who has received after one hour, or he 			 who after twelve hours; every man would answer that he who has received after one hour, has received before him who received after twelve hours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:69
verses.text: So then though they all received at the same hour, yet because some received after one hour, others after twelve hours, they who received after so short a time are said to have received first.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:70
verses.text: The first righteous men, as Abel, and Noe, called as it were at the first hour, will receive together with us the blessedness of the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:71
verses.text: Other 			 righteous men after them, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all of their age, called as it were at the third hour, will receive together with us the blessedness of the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:72
verses.text: Other righteous men, as Moses, and Aaron, and whosoever with them were called as it were at the sixth hour, will receive together with us the blessedness of the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:73
verses.text: After them the Holy Prophets, called as it were at the ninth hour, will receive together with us the same blessedness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:74
verses.text: In the end 			 of the world all Christians, called as it were at the eleventh hour, will receive with the rest the blessedness of that resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:75
verses.text: All will receive together; but consider those first men, after how long a time do they receive it? If then those first receive after a long time, we after a short time; though we all receive together, yet we seem to have received first, because our hire will not tarry long in coming.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:76
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:77
verses.text: In that hire then shall we be all equal, and the first as the last, and the last as the first; because that denarius is life eternal, and in the life eternal all will be equal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:78
verses.text: For although through diversity of attainments the saints will shine, some more, some less; yet as to this respect, the gift of eternal life, it will be equal to all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:79
verses.text: For that will not be longer to one, and shorter to another, which is alike everlasting; that which hath no end will have no end either for thee or me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:80
verses.text: After one sort in that life will be wedded chastity, after another virgin purity; in one sort there will be the fruit of good works, in another sort the crown of martyrdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:81
verses.text: One in one sort, and another in another; yet in respect to the living for ever, this man will not live more than that, nor that than this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:82
verses.text: For alike without end will they live, though each shall live in his own brightness: and the denarius in the parable is that life eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:83
verses.text: Let not him then who has received after a long time murmur against him who has received after a short time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:84
verses.text: To the first, it is a payment; to the other, a free gift; yet the same thing is given alike to 			 both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:85
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:86
verses.text: There is also something like this in this present life, and besides that solution of the parable, by which they who were called at the first hour are understood of Abel and the righteous men of his age, and they at the third, of Abraham and the righteous men of his age, and they at the sixth, of Moses and Aaron and the righteous men of their age, and they at the eleventh, as in the end of the world, of all Christians; besides this solution of the parable, the parable 			 may be seen to have an explanation in respect even of this present life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:87
verses.text: For they are as it were called at the first hour, who begin to be Christians fresh from their mother's womb; boys are called as it were at the third, young men at the sixth, they who are verging toward old age, at the ninth hour, and they who are called as if at the eleventh hour, are they who are altogether decrepit; yet all these are to receive the one and the same denarius of eternal life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:88
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:89
verses.text: But, Brethren, hearken ye and understand, lest any put off to come into the vineyard, because he is sure, that, come when he will, he shall receive this denarius.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:90
verses.text: And sure indeed he is that the denarius is promised him; but this is no injunction to put off.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:91
verses.text: For did they who were hired into the vineyard, when the householder came out to them to hire whom he might find, at the third hour for instance, and did hire them, did they say to him, "Wait, we are not going 			 thither till the sixth hour"? or they whom he found at the sixth hour, did they say, "We are not going till the ninth hour"? or they whom he found at the ninth hour, did they say, "We are not going till the eleventh? For he will give to all alike; why should we fatigue ourselves more than we need?" What He was to give, and what He was to do, was in the secret of His own counsel: do thou come when thou art called.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:92
verses.text: For an equal reward is promised to all; but as to this appointed hour of 			 working, there is an important question.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:93
verses.text: For if, for instance, they who are called at the sixth hour, at that age of life that is, in which as in the full heat of noon, is felt the glow of manhood's years; if they, called thus in manhood, were to say, "Wait, for we have heard in the Gospel that all are to receive the same reward, we will come at the eleventh hour, when we shall have grown old, and shall still receive the same.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:94
verses.text: Why should we add to our labour?" it would be answered them 			 thus, "Art not thou willing to labour now, who dost not know whether thou shalt live to old age? Thou art called at the sixth hour; come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:95
verses.text: The Householder hath it is true promised thee a denarius, if thou come at the eleventh hour, but whether thou shalt live even to the seventh, no one hath promised thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:96
verses.text: I say not to the eleventh, but even to the seventh hour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:97
verses.text: Why then dost thou put off him that calleth thee, certain as thou art of the reward, but uncertain of the day? Take heed then lest 			 peradventure what he is to give thee by promise, thou take from thyself by delay".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:98
verses.text: Now if this may rightly be said of infants as belonging to the first hour, if it may be rightly said of boys as belonging to the third, if it may be rightly said of men in the vigour of life, as in the full-day heat of the sixth hour; how much more rightly may it be said of the decrepit? Lo, already is it the eleventh hour, and dost thou yet stand still, and art thou yet slow to come?  9.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:99
verses.text: But perhaps the Householder hath not gone out to call thee? If he hath not gone out, what mean our addresses to you? For we are servants of his household, we are sent to hire labourers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:100
verses.text: Why standest thou still then? Thou hast now ended the number of thy years; hasten after the denarius.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:101
verses.text: For this is the "going out" of the Householder, the making himself known; forasmuch as he that is in the house is hidden, he is not seen by those who are without; 			 but when he "goeth out" of the house, he is seen by those without.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:102
verses.text: So Christ is in secret, as long as He is not known and acknowledged; but when He is acknowledged, He hath gone out to hire labourers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:103
verses.text: For now He hath come forth from a hidden place, to be known of men: everywhere Christ is known, Christ is preached; all places whatsoever under the heaven proclaim aloud the glory of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:104
verses.text: He was in a manner the object of derision and contempt among the Jews, He appeared in low estate and 			 was despised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:105
verses.text: For He hid His Majesty, and manifested His infirmity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:106
verses.text: That in Him which was manifested was despised, and that which was hidden was not known.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:107
verses.text: "For had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:108
verses.text: But is He still to be despised now that He sitteth in heaven, if He were despised when He was hanging on the tree? They who crucified Him wagged their head, and standing before His Cross, as though they had attained the fruit of their cruel rage, they said in mockery, "If He be the Son of God, let Him come down from the Cross.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:109
verses.text: He saved others, Himself He cannot save".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:110
verses.text: He came not down, because He lay hid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:111
verses.text: For with far greater ease could He have come down from the Cross, who had power to rise again from the grave.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:112
verses.text: He showed forth an example of patience for our instruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:113
verses.text: He delayed His power, and was not acknowledged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:114
verses.text: For He had not then gone out to hire labourers, He had gone out, He had not made Himself known.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:115
verses.text: On the third day He rose again, He showed Himself to His disciples, ascended into heaven, and sent the Holy Ghost on the fiftieth 			 day after the resurrection, the tenth after the ascension.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:116
verses.text: The Holy Ghost who was sent filled all who were in one room, one hundred and twenty men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:117
verses.text: They "were filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with the tongues of all nations;" now was the calling manifest, now He went out to hire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:118
verses.text: For now the power of truth began to be made known to all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:119
verses.text: For then even one man having received the Holy Ghost, spake by himself with the tongues of all nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:120
verses.text: But now in the Church oneness itself, as one man speaks in the tongues of all nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:121
verses.text: For what tongue has not the Christian religion reached? to what limits does it not extend? Now is there no one "who hideth himself from the heat thereof;" 			  and delay is still ventured by him who stands still at the eleventh hour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:122
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:123
verses.text: It is plain then, my Brethren, it is plain to all, do ye hold it fast, and be sure of it, that whensoever any one turns himself to the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, from a useless or abandoned way of life, all that is past is forgiven him, and as though all his debts were cancelled, a new account is entered into with him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:124
verses.text: All is entirely forgiven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:125
verses.text: Let no one be anxious in the thought that there remains anything which is not forgiven him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:126
verses.text: But on the other hand, let no one rest in a perverse security.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:127
verses.text: For these two things are the death of souls, despair, and perverse hope.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:128
verses.text: For as a good and right hope saveth, so doth a perverse hope deceive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:129
verses.text: First, 			 consider how despair deceiveth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:130
verses.text: There are men, who when they begin to reflect on the evils they have done, think they cannot be forgiven; and whilst they think they cannot be forgiven, forthwith they give up their souls to ruin, and perish through despair, saying in their thoughts, "Now there is no hope for us; for such great sins as we have committed cannot be remitted or pardoned us; why then should we not satisfy our lusts? Let us at least fill up the pleasure of the time present, seeing 			 we have no reward in that which is to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:131
verses.text: Let us do what we list, though it be not lawful; that we may at least have a temporal enjoyment, because we cannot attain to the receiving an eternal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:132
verses.text: In saying such things they perish through despair, either before they believe at all, or when Christians already, they have fallen by evil living into any sins and wickednesses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:133
verses.text: The Lord of the vineyard goeth forth to them, and by the Prophet Ezekial knocketh, and calleth to them in their despair, and as they turn their backs to Him that calleth them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:134
verses.text: "In whatsoever day a man shall turn from his most wicked way, I will forget all his 			 iniquities".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:135
verses.text: If they hear and believe this voice, they are recovered from despair, and rise up again from that very deep and bottomless gulf, wherein they had been sunk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:136
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:137
verses.text: But these must fear, lest they fall into another gulf, and they die through a perverse hope, who could not die through despair.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:138
verses.text: For they change their thoughts, which are far different indeed from what they were before, but not less pernicious, and begin again to say in their hearts, "If in whatever day I turn from my most evil way, the merciful God, as He truly promiseth by the Prophet, will forget all my iniquities, why should I turn to-day and not to-morrow? Let 			 this day pass as yesterday, in excess of guilty pleasure, in the full flow of licentiousness, let it wallow in deadly delights; to-morrow I shall 'turn myself,' and there will be an end to it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:139
verses.text: One may answer thee, An end of what? Of mine iniquities, thou wilt say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:140
verses.text: Well, rejoice indeed, that to-morrow there will be an end of thine iniquities.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:141
verses.text: But what if before to-morrow thine own end shall be? So then thou dost well indeed to rejoice that God hath promised thee 			 forgiveness for thine iniquities, if thou art converted; but no one has promised thee to-morrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:142
verses.text: Or if perchance some astrologer hath promised it, it is a far different thing from God's promise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:143
verses.text: Many have these astrologers deceived, in that they have promised themselves advantages, and have found only losses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:144
verses.text: Therefore for the sake of these again whose hope is wrong, doth the Householder go forth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:145
verses.text: As He went forth to those who had despaired wrongly, and were lost in their despair, and called 			 them back to hope; so doth He go forth to these also who would perish through an evil hope; and by another book He saith to them, "Make no tarrying to turn to the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:146
verses.text: As He had said to the others, "In whatsoever day a man shall turn from his most wicked way, I will forget all his iniquities," and took despair away from them, because they had now given up their soul to perdition, despairing of forgiveness by any means; so doth He go forth to these also who have a mind to perish through hope and delay; and speaketh to them, and chideth them, "Make no tarrying to turn to the Lord, and put not off from day to day; for suddenly shall the 			 wrath of the Lord come forth, and in the day of vengeance He will destroy thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:147
verses.text: Therefore put not off, shut not against thyself what now is open.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:148
verses.text: Lo, the Giver of forgiveness openeth the door to thee; why dost thou delay? Thou oughtest to rejoice, were He to open after ever so long a time to thy knocking; thou hast not knocked, yet doth He open, and dost thou remain outside? Put not off then.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:149
verses.text: Scripture saith in a certain place, as touching works of mercy, "Say not, Go, and come again, and 			 to-morrow I will give; when thou canst do the kindness at once; for thou knowest not what may happen on the morrow".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:150
verses.text: Here then is a precept of not putting off being merciful to another, and wilt thou by putting off be cruel against thine own self? Thou oughtest not to put off to give bread, and wilt thou put off to receive forgiveness? If thou dost not put off in showing pity towards another, "pity thine own soul also in pleasing God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:151
verses.text: Give alms to thine own soul also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:152
verses.text: Nay I do not say, give to it, but thrust not back His Hand that would give to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:153
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:154
verses.text: But men continually injure themselves exceedingly in their fear to offend others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:155
verses.text: For good friends have much influence for good, and evil friends for evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:156
verses.text: Therefore it was not the Lord's will to choose first senators, but fishermen, to teach us for our own salvation to disregard the friendship of the powerful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:157
verses.text: O signal mercy of the Creator! For He knew that had He chosen the senator, he would say, "My rank has been chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:158
verses.text: If He had first made choice of 			 the rich man, he would say, "My wealth has been chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:159
verses.text: If He had first made choice of an emperor, he would say, "My power has been chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:160
verses.text: If the orator he would say, "My eloquence has been chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:161
verses.text: If of the philosopher, he would say, "My wisdom has been chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:162
verses.text: Meanwhile He says, let these proud ones be put off awhile, they swell too much.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:163
verses.text: Now there is much difference between substantial size and swelling; both indeed are large, but both are not alike sound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:164
verses.text: Let them then, 			 He says, be put off, these proud ones, they must be cured by something solid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:165
verses.text: First give Me, He says, this fisherman.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:166
verses.text: "Come, thou poor one, follow Me; thou hast nothing, thou knowest nothing, follow Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:167
verses.text: Thou poor and ignorant one, follow Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:168
verses.text: There is nothing in thee to inspire awe, but there is much in thee to be filled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:169
verses.text: To so copious a fountain an empty vessel should be brought.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:170
verses.text: So the fisherman left his nets, the fisherman received grace, and became a divine orator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:171
verses.text: See what the Lord did, of whom the Apostle says, "God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty, and base things of the world hath God chosen, yea and things which are not, as if they were, 			 that those things which are may be brought to nought".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:172
verses.text: And so now the fishermen's words are read, and the necks of orators are brought down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:173
verses.text: Let all empty winds then be taken away, let the smoke be taken away which vanishes as it mounts; let them be utterly despised when the question is of this salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:174
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:175
verses.text: If any one in a city had some bodily sickness, and there was in that place some very skilful physician who was an enemy to the sick man's powerful friends; if any one, I say, in a city were labouring under some dangerous bodily sickness; and there was in the same city a very skilful physician, an enemy as I said, of the sick man's powerful friends, and they were to say to their friend, "Do not call him in, he knows nothing;" and they were to say this not 			 from any judgment of their mind, but through dislike of him; would he not for his own safety's sake remove from him the groundless assertions of his powerful friends, and with whatever offence to them, in order that he might live but a few days longer, call that physician in, whom common report had given out as most skilful to drive away the disease of his body? Well, the whole race of mankind is sick, not with diseases of the body, but with sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:176
verses.text: There lies one great patient from East to West throughout the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:177
verses.text: To cure this great patient came the Almighty Physician down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:178
verses.text: He humbled Himself even to mortal flesh, 			 as it were to the sick man's bed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:179
verses.text: Precepts of health He gives, and is despised; they who do observe them are delivered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:180
verses.text: He is despised, when powerful friends say, "He knows nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:181
verses.text: If He knew nothing, His power would not fill the nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:182
verses.text: If He knew nothing, He would not have been, before He was with us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:183
verses.text: If He knew nothing, He would not have sent the Prophets before Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:184
verses.text: Are not those things which were foretold of old, fulfilled now? Does not this Physician 			 prove the power of His art by the accomplishment of His promises? Are not deadly errors overturned throughout the whole world; and by the threshing of the world lusts subdued? Let no one say, "The world was better aforetime than now; ever since that Physician began to exercise His art, many dreadful things we witness here".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:185
verses.text: Marvel not at this? Before that any were in course of healing, the Physician's residence seemed clean of blood; but now rather as seeing what thou dost, shake off all vain delights, and come to the Physician, it is the time of healing, not of pleasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:186
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:187
verses.text: Let us then think, Brethren, of being cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:188
verses.text: If we do not yet know the Physician, yet let us not like frenzied men be violent against Him, or as men in a lethargy turn away from Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:189
verses.text: For many through this violence have perished, and many have perished through sleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:190
verses.text: The frenzied are they who are made mad for want of sleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:191
verses.text: The lethargic are they who are weighed down by excessive sleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:192
verses.text: Men are to be found of both these kinds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:193
verses.text: Against this Physician it is the 			 will of some to be violent, and forasmuch as He is Himself sitting in heaven, they persecute His faithful ones on earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:194
verses.text: Yet even such as these He cureth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:195
verses.text: Many of them having been converted from enemies have become friends, from persecutors have become preachers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:196
verses.text: Such as these were the Jews, whom, though violent as men in frenzy against Him while He was here, He healed, and prayed for them as He hung upon the Cross.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:197
verses.text: For He said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:198
verses.text: Yet many of them when their fury was calmed, their frenzy as it were got under, came to know God, and Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:199
verses.text: When the Holy Ghost was sent after the Ascension, they were converted to Him whom they crucified, and as believers drunk in the Sacrament His Blood, which in their violence they shed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:200
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:201
verses.text: Of this we have examples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:202
verses.text: Saul persecuted the members of Jesus Christ, who is now sitting in heaven; grievously did he persecute them in his frenzy, in the loss of his reason, in the transport of his madness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:203
verses.text: But He with one word, calling to him out of heaven, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me?" struck down the frantic one, raised him up whole, killed the persecutor, quickened the preacher.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:204
verses.text: And so again many lethargic ones are healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:205
verses.text: For to such are they like, who are not violent against Christ, nor malicious against Christians, but who in their delay are only dull and heavy with drowsy words, are slow to open their eyes to the light, and are annoyed with those who would arouse them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:206
verses.text: "Get away from me," says the heavy, lethargic man, "I pray thee, get away from 			 me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:207
verses.text: Why? "I wish to sleep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:208
verses.text: But you will die in consequence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:209
verses.text: He through love of sleep will answer, "I wish to die".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:210
verses.text: And Love from above calls out "I do not wish it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:211
verses.text: Often does the son exhibit this loving affection to an aged father, though he must needs die in a few days; and is now in extreme old age.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:212
verses.text: If he sees that he is lethargic, and knows from the physician that he is oppressed with a lethargic complaint, who tells him "Arouse your father, do not let him sleep, if you 			 would save his life"! Then will the son come to the old man, and beat, and squeeze, or pinch, or prick him, or give him any uneasiness, and all through his dutiful affection to him; and will not allow him to die at once, die though he soon must from very age; and if his life is thus saved, the son rejoices that he has now to live some few days more with him who must soon depart to make way for him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:213
verses.text: With how much greater affection then ought we to be importunate with our friends, with whom we may live not a few days in this world, but in God's presence for ever! Let them then love us, and do what they hear us say, and worship Him, whom we also worship, that they may receive what we also hope for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 36:214
verses.text: "Let us turn to the Lord," etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:1
verses.text: Sermon XXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:2
verses.text: [LXXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:5
verses.text: xx.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:6
verses.text: 30, about the two blind men sitting by the way side, and crying out, "Lord, have mercy on us, Thou Son of David".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:8
verses.text: Ye know, Holy Brethren, full well as we do, that our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ is the Physician of our eternal health; and that to this end He took the weakness of our nature, that our weakness might not last for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:9
verses.text: For He assumed a mortal body, wherein to kill death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:10
verses.text: And, "though He was crucified through weakness," as the Apostle saith, "yet He liveth by the power of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:11
verses.text: They are the words too of the same Apostle; "He dieth no more, and death shall have no more dominion over Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:12
verses.text: These things, I say, are well known to your faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:13
verses.text: And there is also this which follows from it, that we should know that all the miracles which He did on the body, avail to our instruction, that we may from them perceive that which is not to pass away, nor to have any end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:14
verses.text: He restored to the blind those eyes which death was sure sometime to close; He raised Lazarus to life who was to die again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:15
verses.text: And whatever He did for the health of bodies, He did it not to 			 this end that they should be for ever; whereas at the last He will give eternal health even to the body itself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:16
verses.text: But because those things which were not seen, were not believed; by means of these temporal things which were seen, He built up faith in those things which were not seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:17
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:18
verses.text: Let no one then, Brethren, say that our Lord Jesus Christ doeth not those things now, and on this account prefer the former to the present ages of the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:19
verses.text: In a certain place indeed the same Lord prefers those who "do not see, and yet believe," to them who see and therefore believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:20
verses.text: For even at that time so irresolute was the infirmity of His disciples, that they thought that He whom they saw to have risen again must be handled, in order that they might believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:21
verses.text: It was not enough for their eyes that they had seen Him, unless their hands also were applied to His limbs, and the scars of His recent wounds were touched; that that disciple who was in doubt, might cry out suddenly when he had touched and recognised the 			 scars, "My Lord and my God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:22
verses.text: The scars manifested Him who had healed all wounds in others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:23
verses.text: Could not the Lord have risen again without the scars? Yes, but He knew the wounds which were in the hearts of His disciples, and to heal them He had preserved the scars on His own Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:24
verses.text: And what said the Lord to him who now confessed and said, "My Lord and my God"? "Because thou hast seen," He said, "thou hast believed; blessed are they who do not see, and yet believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:25
verses.text: Of whom spake He, Brethren, but 			 of us? Not that He spake only of us, but of those also who shall come after us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:26
verses.text: For after a little while when He had departed from the sight of men, that faith might be established in their hearts, whosoever believed, believed, though they saw Him not, and great has been the merit of their faith; for the procuring of which faith they brought only the movement of a pious heart, and not the touching of their hands.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:27
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:28
verses.text: These things then the Lord did to invite us to the faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:29
verses.text: This faith reigneth now in the Church, which is spread throughout the whole world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:30
verses.text: And now He worketh greater cures, on account of which He disdained not then to exhibit those lesser ones.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:31
verses.text: For as the soul is better than the body, so is the saving health of the soul better than the health of the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:32
