verses.text: The blind body doth not now open its eyes by a miracle of the Lord, but the blinded heart openeth its eyes 			 to the word of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:33
verses.text: The mortal corpse doth not now rise again, but the soul doth rise again which lay dead in a living body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:34
verses.text: The deaf ears of the body are not now opened; but how many have the ears of their heart closed, which yet fly open at the penetrating word of God, so that they believe who did not believe, and they live well, who did live evilly, and they obey, who did not obey; and we say, "Such a man is become a believer;" and we wonder when we hear of them whom once we had 			 known as hardened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:35
verses.text: Why then dost thou marvel at one who now believes, who is living innocently, and serving God; but because thou dost behold him seeing, whom thou hadst known to be blind; dost behold him living, whom thou hadst known to be dead; dost behold him hearing, whom thou hadst known to be deaf? For consider that there are who are dead in another than the ordinary sense, of whom the Lord spake to a certain man who delayed to follow the Lord, because he wished to bury his father; "Let 			 the dead," said He, "bury their dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:36
verses.text: Surely these dead buriers are not dead in body; for if this were so, they could not bury dead bodies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:37
verses.text: Yet doth he call them dead; where, but in the soul within? For as we may often see in a household, itself sound and well, the master of the same house lying dead; so in a sound body do many carry a dead soul within; and these the Apostle arouses thus, "Awake, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:38
verses.text: It is the Same who giveth light to the blind, that awakeneth the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:39
verses.text: For it is with His voice that the cry is made by the Apostle to the dead, "Awake, thou that sleepest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:40
verses.text: And the blind will be enlightened with light, when he shall have risen again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:41
verses.text: And how many deaf men did the Lord see before His eyes, when He said, "He that hath ears to hear, let him hear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:42
verses.text: For who was standing before Him without his bodily ears? What other ears then did He seek for, but those of the inner man?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:43
verses.text: Again, what eyes did He look for when He spake to those who saw indeed, but who saw only with the eyes of the flesh? For when Philip said to Him, "Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us;" he understood indeed that if the Father were shown him, it might well suffice him; but how would the Father suffice him whom He that was equal to the Father sufficed not? And why did He not suffice? Because He was not seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:44
verses.text: And why was He not seen? Because the eye whereby He might be seen was not yet whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:45
verses.text: For this, namely, that the Lord was seen in the flesh with the outward eyes, not only the disciples who honoured Him saw, but also the Jews who 			 crucified Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:46
verses.text: He then who wished to be seen in another way, sought for other eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:47
verses.text: And therefore it was that to him who said, "Show us the Father, and it sufficeth us;" He answered, "Have I been so long time with you; and yet hast thou not known Me, Philip? He who hath seen Me, hath seen the Father also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:48
verses.text: And that He might in the mean while heal the eyes of faith, he has first of all instructions given him regarding faith, that so he might attain to sight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:49
verses.text: And lest Philip should think that he was to conceive of God under the same form in which he then saw the Lord Jesus Christ in the body, he immediately subjoined; "Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me?" He had already said, "He who hath seen Me, hath seen the Father also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:50
verses.text: But Philip's eye was not yet sound enough to see the Father, nor consequently to see the Son who is Himself Coequal with the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:51
verses.text: And so Jesus Christ took in hand to cure, and with the medicines and salve of faith to strengthen the eyes of his mind, which as yet were weak and unable to behold so great a light, and He said, "Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me?" Let 			 not him then who cannot yet see what the Lord will one day show him, seek first to see what he is to believe; but let him first believe that the eye by which he is to see may be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:52
verses.text: For it was only the form of the servant which was exhibited to the eyes of servants; because if "He who thought it not robbery to be equal with God," could have been now seen as equal with God by those whom He wished to be healed, He would not have needed to "empty Himself, and to take the form of a servant".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:53
verses.text: But because there was no way whereby God could be seen, but whereby man could be seen, there was; therefore He who was God was made man, that that which was seen might heal that whereby He was not seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:54
verses.text: For He saith Himself in another place, "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:55
verses.text: Philip might of course have answered and said, "Lord, lo, I see Thee; is the Father such as I see Thee to be? forasmuch as Thou hast said, 'He who hath seen Me, hath seen the Father also'?" But before Philip answered thus, or perhaps before he so much as thought it, when the Lord had said, "He who hath seen Me, hath seen the Father also;" He immediately added, "Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me?" For with that eye he could, not 			 yet see either the Father, or the Son who is equal with the Father; but that his eye might be healed for seeing, he was to be anointed unto believing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:56
verses.text: So then before thou seest what thou canst not now see, believe what as yet thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:57
verses.text: "Walk by faith," that thou mayest attain to sight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:58
verses.text: Sight will not gladden him in his home whom faith consoleth not by the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:59
verses.text: For so says the Apostle, "As long as we are in the body, we are in pilgrimage from the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:60
verses.text: And he subjoins immediately why we are still "in pilgrimage," though we have now believed; "For we walk by faith," He says, "not by sight".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:61
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:62
verses.text: Our whole business then, Brethren, in this life is to heal this eye of the heart whereby God may be seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:63
verses.text: To this end are celebrated the Holy Mysteries; to this end is preached the word of God; to this end are the moral exhortations of the Church, those, that is, that relate to the correction of manners, to the amendment of carnal lusts, to the renouncing the world, not in word only, but in a change of life: to this end is directed the whole aim of the Divine and Holy 			 Scriptures, that that inner man may be purged of that which hinders us from the sight of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:64
verses.text: For as the eye which is formed to see this temporal light, a light though heavenly, yet corporeal, and manifest, not to men only, but even to the meanest animals (for for this the eye is formed, to see this light); if anything be thrown or fall into it, whereby it is disordered, is shut out from this light; and though it encompass the eye with its presence, yet the eye turns itself away from, and is 			 absent from it; and through its disordered condition is not only rendered absent from the light which is present, but the light to see which it was formed, is even painful to it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:65
verses.text: So the eye of the heart too when it is disordered and wounded turns away from the light of righteousness, and dares not and cannot contemplate it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:66
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:67
verses.text: And what is it that disorders the eye of the heart? Evil desire, covetousness, injustice, worldly concupiscence, these disorder, close, blind the eye of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:68
verses.text: And yet when the eye of the body is out of order, how is the physician sought out, what an absence of all delay to open and cleanse it, that that may be healed whereby this outward light is seen! There is running to and fro, no one is still, no one loiters, if even the smallest straw fall into the eye.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:69
verses.text: And 			 God it must be allowed made the sun which we desire to see with sound eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:70
verses.text: Much brighter assuredly is He who made it; nor is the light with which the eye of the mind is concerned of this kind at all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:71
verses.text: That light is eternal Wisdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:72
verses.text: God made thee, O man, after His own image.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:73
verses.text: Would He give thee wherewithal to see the sun which He made, and not give thee wherewithal to see Him who made thee, when He made thee after His own image? He hath given thee this also; both hath He given thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:74
verses.text: But much thou dost love these outward eyes, and despisest much that interior eye; it thou dost carry about bruised and wounded.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:75
verses.text: Yea, it would be a punishment to thee, if thy Maker should wish to manifest Himself unto thee; it would be a punishment to thine eye, before that it is cured and healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:76
verses.text: For so Adam in paradise sinned, and hid himself from the face of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:77
verses.text: As long then as he had the sound heart of a pure conscience, he rejoiced at the presence of God; when that eye was wounded by sin, 			 he began to dread the Divine light, he fled back into the darkness, and the thick covert of the trees, flying from the truth, and anxious for the shade.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:78
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:79
verses.text: Therefore, my Brethren, since we too are born of him, and as the Apostle says, "In Adam all die;" for we were all at first two persons if we were loth to obey the physician, that we might not be sick; let us obey Him now, that we may be delivered from sickness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:80
verses.text: The physician gave us precepts, when we were whole; He gave us precepts that we might not need a physician.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:81
verses.text: "They that are whole," He saith, "need not a physician, but they that are sick".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:82
verses.text: When whole we despised these precepts, and by experience have felt how to our own destruction we despised His precepts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:83
verses.text: Now we are sick, we are in distress, we are on the bed of weakness; yet let us not despair.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:84
verses.text: For because we could not come to the Physician, He hath vouchsafed to come Himself to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:85
verses.text: Though despised by man when he was whole, He did not despise him when he was stricken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:86
verses.text: He did not leave off to give other precepts to the weak, who would not keep the first 			 precepts, that he might not be weak; as though He would say, "Assuredly thou hast by experience felt that I spake the truth when I said, Touch not this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:87
verses.text: Be healed then now at length, and recover the life thou hast lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:88
verses.text: Lo, I am bearing thine infirmity; drink thou the bitter cup.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:89
verses.text: For thou hast of thine own self made those my so sweet precepts which were given to thee when whole, so toilsome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:90
verses.text: They were despised and so thy distress began; cured thou canst not be, except thou drink the bitter 			 cup, the cup of temptations, wherein this life abounds, the cup of tribulation, anguish, and sufferings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:91
verses.text: Drink then," He says, "drink, that thou mayest live".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:92
verses.text: And that the sick man may not make answer, "I cannot, I cannot bear it, I will not drink;" the Physician, all whole though he be, drinketh first, that the sick man may not hesitate to drink.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:93
verses.text: For what bitterness is there in this cup, which He hath not drunk? If it be contumely; He heard it first when He drove out the devils, 			 "He hath a devil, and by Beelzebub He casteth out devils".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:94
verses.text: Whereupon in order to comfort the sick, He saith, "If they have called the Master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of His household?" If pains are this bitter cup, He was bound and scourged and crucified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:95
verses.text: If death be this bitter cup, He died also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:96
verses.text: If infirmity shrink with horror from any particular kind of death, none was at that time more ignominious than the death of the cross.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:97
verses.text: For it was not in vain that the Apostle, when setting forth His obedience, added, "Made obedient unto death, even the death of the cross".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:98
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:99
verses.text: But because He designed to honour His faithful ones at the end of the world, He hath first honoured the cross in this world; in such wise that the princes of the earth who believe in Him have prohibited any criminal from being crucified; and that cross which the Jewish persecutors with great mockery prepared for the Lord, even kings His servants at this day bear with great confidence on their foreheads.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:100
verses.text: Only the shameful nature of the death which our Lord 			 vouchsafed to undergo for us is not now so apparent, Who, as the Apostle says, "was made a curse for us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:101
verses.text: And when as He hung, the blindness of the Jews mocked Him, surely He could have come down from the Cross, who if He had not so willed, had not been on the Cross; but it was a greater thing to rise from the grave than to come down from the Cross.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:102
verses.text: Our Lord then in doing these Divine, and in suffering these human things, instructs us by His Bodily miracles and Bodily patience, that we may believe, and be made whole to behold those things invisible which the eye of the body hath 			 no knowledge of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:103
verses.text: With this intent then He cured these blind men of whom the account has just now been read in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:104
verses.text: And consider what instruction He has by their cure conveyed to the man who is sick within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:105
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:106
verses.text: Consider the issue of the thing, and the order of the circumstances.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:107
verses.text: Those two blind men sitting by the way side cried out as the Lord passed by, that He would have mercy upon them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:108
verses.text: But they were restrained from crying out by the multitude which was with the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:109
verses.text: Now do not suppose that this circumstance is left without a mysterious meaning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:110
verses.text: But they overcame the crowd who kept them back by the great perseverance of their cry, that their voice might reach the Lord's 			 ears; as though He had not already anticipated their thoughts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:111
verses.text: So then the two blind men cried out that they might be heard by the Lord, and could not be restrained by the multitudes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:112
verses.text: The Lord "was passing by," and they cried out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:113
verses.text: The Lord "stood still," and they were healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:114
verses.text: For "the Lord Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will ye that I shall do unto you? They say unto Him, That our eyes may be opened".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:115
verses.text: The Lord did according to their faith, He recovered their eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:116
verses.text: If we have now understood by the sick, the deaf, the dead, the sick, and deaf, and dead, within; let us look out in this place also for the blind within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:117
verses.text: The eyes of the heart are clossd; "Jesus passeth by" that we may cry out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:118
verses.text: What is, "Jesus passeth by"? Jesus is doing things which last but for a time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:119
verses.text: What is "Jesus passeth by"? Jesus doeth things which pass by.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:120
verses.text: Mark and see how many things of His 			 have "passed by".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:121
verses.text: He was born of the Virgin Mary; is He being born always? As an infant was He suckled; is He suckled always? He ran through the successive ages of life unto man's full estate; doth He grow in body always? Boyhood succeeded to infancy, to boyhood youth, to youth man's full stature in several passing successions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:122
verses.text: Even the very miracles which He did are "passed by," they are read and believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:123
verses.text: For because these miracles are written that so they might be read, they 			 "passed by" when they were being done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:124
verses.text: In a word, not to dwell long on this, He was Crucified: is He hanging on the Cross always? He was Buried, He Rose again, He Ascended into heaven; "now He dieth no more, death shall no more have dominion over Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:125
verses.text: And His Divinity abideth ever, yea, the Immortality of His Body now shall never fail.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:126
verses.text: But nevertheless all those things which were wrought by Him in time have "passed by;" and they are written to be read, and they are preached to be believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:127
verses.text: In all these things then, "Jesus passeth by".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:128
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:129
verses.text: And what are "the two blind men by the way side," but the two people to cure whom Jesus came? Let us show those two people in the Holy Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:130
verses.text: It is written in the Gospel, "Other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also must I bring, that there may be one fold and One Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:131
verses.text: Who then are the two people? One the people of the Jews, and the other of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:132
verses.text: "I am not sent," He saith, "but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:133
verses.text: To whom did He say this? To the disciples; when that woman of Canaan who confessed herself to be a dog, cried out that she might be found worthy of the crumbs from the master's table.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:134
verses.text: And because she was found worthy, now were the two people to whom He had come made manifest: the Jewish people, to wit, of whom He said, "I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel;" and the people of the Gentiles, whose type this woman exhibited whom He had first rejected, saying, "It is not meet to cast the children's bread to the dogs;" and to whom when she said, "Truth, Lord, yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their 			 master's table;" He answered, "O woman, great is thy faith, be it unto thee even as thou wilt".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:135
verses.text: For of this people also was that centurion of whom the same Lord saith, "Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:136
verses.text: Because he had said, "I am not worthy that Thou shouldest come under my roof, but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:137
verses.text: So then the Lord even before His Passion and Glorification pointed out two people, the one to whom He had come because of the promises to the Fathers; and the other whom for His mercy's sake He did not reject; that it might be fulfilled which had been promised to Abraham, "In thy seed shall all nations be blessed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:138
verses.text: Wherefore also the Apostle after the Lord's Resurrection and Ascension, when He was despised by the Jews, went to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:139
verses.text: Not that he was silent however towards the Churches which consisted of Jewish believers; "I was unknown," he says, "by face unto the Churches of Judaea which were in Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:140
verses.text: But they heard only that he which persecuted us in times past, now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed, and they glorified God in me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:141
verses.text: So again Christ is called the "Corner Stone who made both one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:142
verses.text: For a corner joins two walls which come from different sides together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:143
verses.text: And what was so different as the circumcision and uncircumcision, having one wall from Judaea, the other from the Gentiles? But they are joined together by the corner stone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:144
verses.text: "For the stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:145
verses.text: There is no corner in a building, except when two walls coming from different directions meet together, and are joined in a kind of unity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:146
verses.text: The "two blind men" then crying out unto the Lord were these two walls according to the figure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:147
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:148
verses.text: Attend now, dearly Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:149
verses.text: The Lord was "passing by," and the blind men "cried out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:150
verses.text: What is "was passing by"? As we have already said, He was doing works which "passed by".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:151
verses.text: Now upon these passing works is our faith built up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:152
verses.text: For we believe on the Son of God, not only in that He is the word of God, by whom all things were made; for if He had always continued "in the form of God, equal with God," and had not "emptied Himself in taking the form of a servant," the blind men would not even have perceived Him, that they might be able to cry out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:153
verses.text: But when He wrought passing works, that is, "when He humbled Himself, having become obedient unto death, 			 even the death of the cross," the "two blind men cried out, Have mercy on us, thou Son of David".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:154
verses.text: For this very thing that He David's Lord and Creator, willed also to be David's Son, He wrought in time, He wrought "passing by".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:155
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:156
verses.text: Now what is it, Brethren, "to cry out" unto Christ, but to correspond to the grace of Christ by good works? This I say, Brethren, lest haply we cry aloud with our voices, and in our lives be dumb.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:157
verses.text: Who is he that crieth out to Christ, that his inward blindness may be driven away by Christ as He is "passing by," that is, as He is dispensing to us those temporal sacraments, whereby we are instructed to receive the things which are eternal? Who is he that crieth out unto Christ? Whoso despiseth the world, crieth out unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:158
verses.text: Whoso 			 despiseth the pleasures of the world, crieth out unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:159
verses.text: Whoso saith not with his tongue, but with his life, "The world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world," crieth out unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:160
verses.text: Whoso "disperseth abroad and giveth to the poor, that his righteousness may endure for ever," crieth out unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:161
verses.text: For let him that hears, and is not deaf to the sound, "sell that ye have, and give to the poor; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not;" let him as he hears the sound as it were of Christ's footsteps "passing by," cry out in response to this in his blindness, that is, let him do these things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:162
verses.text: Let his voice be in his actions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:163
verses.text: Let him begin to despise the world, to distribute to the poor his goods, to esteem as nothing worth what other men love, let him disregard injuries, not seek to be avenged, let him give his "cheek to the smiter," let him pray for his enemies; if any "one have taken away his 			 goods," let "him not ask for them again;" if he "have taken anything from any man, let him restore fourfold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:164
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:165
verses.text: When he shall begin to do all this, all his kinsmen, relations, and friends will be in commotion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:166
verses.text: They who love this world, will oppose him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:167
verses.text: What madness this! you are too extreme: what! are not other men Christians? This is folly, this is madness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:168
verses.text: And other such like things do the multitude cry out to prevent the blind from crying out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:169
verses.text: The multitude rebuked them as they cried out; but did not overcome their cries.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:170
verses.text: Let them who wish to be healed understand what they have to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:171
verses.text: Jesus is now also "passing by;" let them who are by the way side cry out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:172
verses.text: These are they "who know God with their lips, but their heart is far from Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:173
verses.text: These are by the way side, to whom as blinded in heart Jesus gives His precepts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:174
verses.text: For when those passing things which Jesus did are recounted, Jesus is always represented to us as "passing by".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:175
verses.text: For even unto the end of the world there will not be wanting "blind men sitting by the way side".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:176
verses.text: Need then there is that they who sit by the way side should cry out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:177
verses.text: The multitude that was with the Lord would repress the crying of those who were seeking for recovery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:178
verses.text: Brethren, do ye see my meaning? For I know not how to 			 speak, but still less do I know how to be silent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:179
verses.text: I will speak then, and speak plainly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:180
verses.text: For I fear "Jesus passing by" and "Jesus standing still;" and therefore I cannot keep silence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:181
verses.text: Evil and lukewarm Christians hinder good Christians who are truly earnest, and wish to do the commandments of God which are written in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:182
verses.text: This multitude which is with the Lord hinders those who are crying out, hinders those that is who are doing well, that they may not by perseverance be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:183
verses.text: But let them cry out, and not faint; let them not be led away as if by the authority of numbers; let them not imitate those who became Christians before them, who live evil lives themselves, and are jealous of the good deeds of others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:184
verses.text: Let them not 			 say, "Let us live as these so many live".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:185
verses.text: Why not rather as the Gospel ordains? Why dost thou wish to live according to the remonstrances of the multitude who would hinder thee, and not after the steps of the Lord, "who passeth by"? They will mock, and abuse, and call thee back; do thou cry out till thou reach the ears of Jesus.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:186
verses.text: For they who shall persevere in doing such things as Christ hath enjoined, and regard not the multitudes that hinder them, nor think much of their appearing to 			 follow Christ, that is of their being called Christians; but who love the light which Christ is about to restore to them, more than they fear the uproar of those who are hindering them; they shall on no account be separated from Him, and Jesus will "stand still," and make them whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:187
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:188
verses.text: For how are our eyes made whole? That as by faith we perceive Christ "passing by" in the temporal economy, so we may attain to the knowledge of Him as "standing still" in His unchangeable Eternity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:189
verses.text: For then is the eye made whole when the knowledge of Christ's Divinity is attained.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:190
verses.text: Let your love apprehend this; attend ye to the great mystery which I am to speak of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:191
verses.text: All the things which were done by our Lord Jesus Christ in time, graft faith in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:192
verses.text: We believe on the Son of God, not on the Word only, "by which all things were made;" but on this very Word, "made flesh that He might dwell among us," who was born of the Virgin Mary, and the rest which the Faith contains, and which are represented to us that Christ might "pass by," and that the blind, hearing His footsteps as He 			 "passeth by," might by their works "cry out," by their life exemplifying the profession of their faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:193
verses.text: But now in order that they who cry out may be made whole, "Jesus standeth still".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:194
verses.text: For he saw Jesus now "standing still" who says, "Though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we Him no more".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:195
verses.text: For he saw Christ's Divinity as far as in this life is possible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:196
verses.text: There is then in Christ the Divinity and the Humanity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:197
verses.text: The Divinity "standeth still," the Humanity "passeth by".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:198
verses.text: What means, The Divinity "standeth still"? It changeth not, is not shaken, doth not depart away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:199
verses.text: For He did not so come to us, as to depart from the Father; nor did He so ascend as to change His place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:200
verses.text: When He assumed Flesh, it changed place; but God assuming Flesh, seeing He is not in 			 place, doth not change His place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:201
verses.text: Let us then be touched by Christ "standing still," and so our eyes be made whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:202
verses.text: But whose eyes? The eyes of those who "cry out" when He is "passing by;" that is, who do good works through that faith, which hath been dispensed in time, to instruct us in our infancy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:203
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:204
verses.text: Now what thing more precious can we have than the eye made whole? They rejoice who see this created light which shines from heaven, or even that which is given out from a lamp.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:205
verses.text: And how wretched do they seem, who cannot see this light? But wherefore do I speak, and talk of all these things, but to exhort you all to "cry out," when Jesus "passeth by".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:206
verses.text: I hold up this light which perhaps ye do not see as an object of love to you, Holy Brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:207
verses.text: Believe, 			 whilst as yet ye see not; and "cry out" that ye may see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:208
verses.text: How great is thought to be the unhappiness of men, who do not see this bodily light? Does any one become blind; immediately it is said; "God is angry with him, he has committed some wicked deed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:209
verses.text: So said Tobias' wife to her husband.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:210
verses.text: He cried out because of the kid, lest it had come of theft; he did not like to hear the sound of any stolen thing in his house; and she, maintaining what she had done, reproached her husband; and 			 when he said, "Restore it if it be stolen;" she answered insultingly, "Where are thy righteous deeds?" How great was her blindness who maintained the theft; and how clear a light he saw, who commanded the stolen thing to be restored! She rejoiced outwardly in the light of the sun; he inwardly in the light of Righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:211
verses.text: Which of them was in the better light?  16.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:212
verses.text: It is to the love of this light that I would exhort you, Beloved; that ye would cry out by your works, when the Lord "passeth by;" let the voice of faith sound out, that "Jesus standing still," that is, the Unchangeable, Abiding Wisdom of God, and the Majesty of the Word of God, "by which all things were made," may open your eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:213
verses.text: The same Tobias in giving advice to his son, instructed him to this, to cry out; that is, he instructed him to good 			 works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:214
verses.text: He told him to give to the poor, charged him to give alms to the needy, and taught him, saying, "My son, alms suffereth not to come into darkness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:215
verses.text: The blind gave counsel for receiving and gaining light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:216
verses.text: "Alms," saith he, "suffereth not to come into darkness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:217
verses.text: Had his son in astonishment answered him, "What then, father, hast thou not given alms, that thou now speakest to me in blindness; art not thou in darkness, and yet thou dost say to me, "Alms suffereth not to come into darkness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:218
verses.text: But no, he knew well what the light was, concerning which he gave his son instruction, he knew well what he saw in the inner 			 man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:219
verses.text: The son held out his hand to his father, to enable him to walk on earth; and the father to the son, to enable him to dwell in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:220
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:221
verses.text: To be brief; that I may conclude this Sermon, Brethren, with a matter which touches me very nearly, and gives me much pain, see what crowds there are which "rebuke the blind as they cry out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:222
verses.text: But let them not deter you, whosoever among this crowd desire to be healed; for there are many Christians in name, and in works ungodly; let them not deter you from good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:223
verses.text: Cry out amid the crowds that are restraining you, and calling you back, and insulting you, 			 whose lives are evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:224
verses.text: For not only by their voices, but by evil works, do wicked Christians repress the good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:225
verses.text: A good Christian has no wish to attend the public shows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:226
verses.text: In this very thing, that he bridles his desire of going to the theatre, he cries out after Christ, cries out to be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:227
verses.text: Others run together thither, but perhaps they are heathens or Jews? Ah! indeed, if Christians went not to the theatres, there would be so few people there, that they would go away for very shame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:228
verses.text: So then 			 Christians run thither also, bearing the Holy Name only to their condemnation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:229
verses.text: Cry out then by abstaining from going, by repressing in thy heart this worldly concupiscence; hold on with a strong and persevering cry unto the ears of the Saviour, that Jesus may "stand still" and heal thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:230
verses.text: Cry out amidst the very crowds, despair not of reaching the ears of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:231
verses.text: For the blind men in the Gospel did not cry out in that quarter, where no crowd was, that so they might be heard in that direction, where there was no impediment from persons hindering them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:232
verses.text: Amidst the very crowds they cried out; and yet the Lord 			 heard them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:233
verses.text: And so also do ye even amidst sinners, and sensual then, amidst the lovers of the vanities of the world, there cry out that the Lord may heal you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:234
verses.text: Go not to another quarter to cry out unto the Lord, go not to heretics, and cry out unto Him there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:235
verses.text: Consider, Brethren, how in that crowd which was hindering them from crying out, even there were they who cried out made whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:236
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:237
verses.text: For observe this too, Holy Brethren, what it is to persevere in crying out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:238
verses.text: I will speak of what many as well as myself have experienced in Christ's name; for the Church does not cease to give birth to such as these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:239
verses.text: When any Christian has begun to live well, to be fervent in good works, and to despise the world; in this newness of his life he is exposed to the animadversions and contradictions of cold Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:240
verses.text: But if he persevere, and get the better of 			 them by his endurance, and faint not in good works; those very same persons who before hindered will now respect him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:241
verses.text: For they rebuke, and hinder, and withstand him so long as they have any hope that he will yield to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:242
verses.text: But if they shall be overcome by their perseverance who make progress, they turn round and begin to say, "He is a great man, a holy man, happy he to whom God hath given such grace".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:243
verses.text: Now do they honour him, they congratulate and bless and laud him; just as that multitude did which was with the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:244
verses.text: They first hindered the blind men that they might not cry out; but when 			 they continued to cry so as to attain to be heard, and to obtain the Lord's mercy, that same multitude now says, "Jesus calleth you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:245
verses.text: And they who a little before "rebuked them that they should hold their peace," use now the voice of exhortation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:246
verses.text: Now he only is not called by the Lord who is not in labour in this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:247
verses.text: But who is there in this life who is not in labour through his sins and iniquities? But if all labour, it is said to all, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:248
verses.text: Now if this is said to all, why ascribest thou thy miscarriage to Him that so inviteth thee? Come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:249
verses.text: His house is not too narrow for thee; the kingdom of God is possessed equally by all, and wholly by each one; it is not diminished by the increasing number of those who possess it, because it is not divided.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:250
verses.text: And that which is possessed by many with one heart, is whole and entire for each one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:251
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:252
verses.text: Yet in the mysterious sense of this passage, Brethren, we recognise what is expressed most plainly in other places of the sacred books, that there are within the Church both good and bad, as I often express it, wheat and chaff.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:253
verses.text: Let no one leave the floor before the time, let him bear with the chaff in the time of threshing, let him bear with it in the floor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:254
verses.text: For in the barn he will have none of it to bear with.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:255
verses.text: The Winnower will come, who shall divide the bad 			 from the good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:256
verses.text: There will then be a bodily separation too, which a spiritual separation now precedes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:257
verses.text: In heart be always separated from the bad, in body be united with them for a time, only with caution.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:258
verses.text: Yet be not negligent in correcting those who belong to you, who in any way appertain to your charge, by admonition, or instruction, by exhortation, or by threats.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:259
verses.text: Do it, in whatsoever way ye can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:260
verses.text: And because ye find in Scripture and in the examples of Saints, whether of those who lived before 			 or after the coming of the Lord in this life, that the bad do not defile the good in unity with them, do not on this account become slow in the correction of the bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:261
verses.text: In two ways the bad will not defile thee; if thou consent not to him, and if thou reprove him; this is, not to communicate with him, not to consent to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:262
verses.text: For there is a communication, when an agreement either of the will or of the approbation is joined to his deed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:263
verses.text: This the Apostle teaches us, when he says, "Have no 			 communication with the unfruitful works of darkness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:264
verses.text: And because it was a small matter not to consent, if negligence in correction accompanied it, he says, "But rather reprove them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:265
verses.text: See how he comprehended both at once, "Have no communication, but rather reprove them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:266
verses.text: What is, "Have no communication"? Do not consent to them, do not praise them, do not approve them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:267
verses.text: What is, "But rather reprove them"? Find fault with, rebuke, repress them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:268
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:269
verses.text: But then in the correction and repressing of other men's sins, one must take heed, that in rebuking another he do not lift up himself; and that sentence of the Apostle must be thought of, "Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth, take heed lest he fall".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:270
verses.text: Let the voice of chiding sound outwardly in tones of terror, let the spirit of love and gentleness be maintained within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:271
verses.text: "If a man be overtaken in a fault," as the same Apostle says, "ye which are spiritual restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:272
verses.text: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so shall ye fulfil the law of Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:273
verses.text: And again in another place, "The servant of the Lord must not strive, but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth; and that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are held captive by him at his will".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:274
verses.text: So then be neither consenting to evil, so as to approve of it; nor negligent so as not to reprove it; nor proud so as to reprove it in a tone of insult.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:275
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:276
verses.text: But whoso forsaketh unity, violateth charity; and whosoever violateth charity, how great gifts soever he have, he is nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:277
verses.text: "If he speak with the tongues of men and of angels; if he knew all mysteries, if he have all faith, so as to remove mountains, if he distribute all his goods to the poor, if he give his body to be burned, and have not charity; it is nothing; it profiteth him nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:278
verses.text: He possesseth all things to no useful end, who hath not that one thing by which he may use all these things well.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:279
verses.text: So then let us embrace charity, "studying to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:280
verses.text: Let not those seduce us who understand the Scriptures in a carnal manner, and who in making a bodily separation, are separated themselves by a spiritual sacrilege from the good corn of the Church which is spread over the whole world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:281
verses.text: For throughout the whole world hath the good seed been sown.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:282
verses.text: That good Sower, the Son of Man, hath scattered the good seed not in Africa only, but everywhere.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:283
verses.text: But the enemy hath sown tares upon it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:284
verses.text: Yet what saith the Householder? "Let both grow 			 together until the harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:285
verses.text: Grow where? In the field, of course.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:286
verses.text: What is the field? Is it Africa? No! What is it then? Let us not interpret it ourselves, let the Lord speak; let us not suffer any one to make his guess at his own pleasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:287
verses.text: For the disciples said to the Master, "Declare unto us the parable of the tares".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:288
verses.text: And the Lord declared it: "The good seed," said He, "are the children of the Kingdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:289
verses.text: But the tares are the children of the wicked one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:290
verses.text: Who sowed them? "The enemy that sowed 			 them," said He," is the devil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:291
verses.text: What is the field? "The field," said He, "is this world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:292
verses.text: What is the harvest? "The harvest," said He, "is the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:293
verses.text: Who are the reapers? "The reapers," said He, "are the Angels".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:294
verses.text: Is Africa the world? Is this present time the harvest? Is Donatus the reaper? Look then for the harvest throughout the whole world, throughout the whole world "grow unto the harvest," throughout the whole world bear with the tares even 			 until the harvest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:295
verses.text: Let not perverse men seduce you, that chaff so light, which flies out of the floor before the coming of the Winnower; let them not seduce you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:296
verses.text: Hold them fast even to this single parable of the tares, and suffer them not to speak of anything else.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:297
verses.text: This man, one will say, surrendered the Scriptures; no, not so: but this other man surrendered them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:298
verses.text: Whosoever it might be who has surrendered them, has their faithlessness made void the faithfulness of God? What is "the faithfulness of God"? That which He promised to Abraham, saying, "In thy seed shall all nations be blessed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:299
verses.text: What is the faithfulness of God? "Let both grow together until the harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:300
verses.text: Grow where? Throughout the field.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:301
verses.text: What is throughout the field? Throughout the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:302
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:303
verses.text: Here they say; "It is true both kinds did once grow throughout the world, but the good wheat is diminished, and confined to this our country, and our small communion".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:304
verses.text: But the Lord doth not allow thee to interpret as thou wilt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:305
verses.text: He who explaineth this parable Himself, shutteth thy mouth, thy sacrilegious, profane, and ungodly mouth, that is counter to thine own interests, while thou runnest counter to the testator, even as he calleth thee to the inheritance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:306
verses.text: How doth He shut thy mouth? by saying, "Let both grow together until the harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:307
verses.text: If the harvest hath come already, let us believe that the wheat has been diminished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:308
verses.text: Though not even then shall it be diminished, but gathered up into the barn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:309
verses.text: For so He saith, "Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into My barn".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:310
verses.text: If then they grow until the harvest, and after the harvest are gathered in, how are they diminished, thou wicked, thou ungodly one? I grant that in comparison with the tares and chaff the 			 wheat is less in quantity; still "both grow together until the harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:311
verses.text: For "when iniquity aboundeth, the love of many waxeth cold;" the tares and the chaff multiply.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:312
verses.text: But because throughout the whole world wheat cannot be wanting, which "by enduring unto the end shall be saved, both grow together until the harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:313
verses.text: And if because of the abundance of the wicked it is said, "When the Son of Man cometh, thinkest thou, shall He find faith on the earth?" and by this denomination are signified all those who by transgression of the law imitate him to whom it was said," Earth thou art, and unto earth shalt thou return;" yet because of the abundance of the good also, and because of him to whom it was said, "Thy seed shall be as the stars of heaven, and as the sand of the sea;" is that also written, "Many shall come from the East and West, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, in the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:314
verses.text: "Both" then "grow together until the harvest," and both the tares or chaff have their passages in the Scriptures, and the wheat theirs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:315
verses.text: And they who do not understand them, confound them and are themselves confounded; and in their blind desire they make such an uproar, that they will not be silenced even by the clear manifestation of the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:316
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:317
verses.text: See, they say, the Prophet says, "Depart ye, go ye out from thence, and touch no unclean thing;" how then for peace sake should we bear with the wicked, from whom we are commanded to "go out and depart that we touch not the unclean thing"? We understand that "departure" spiritually, they corporally.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:318
verses.text: For I also cry out with the Prophet (for however mean a vessel I am, God maketh use of me to minister to you); I also cry out and say to you, "Depart ye, go ye out from thence, and touch not the unclean thing;" but with the touch of the heart, not of the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:319
verses.text: For 			 what is it to "touch the unclean thing," but to consent to sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:320
verses.text: And what is it to "go out from thence," but to do what appertaineth to the rebuking of the wicked, as far as can be done, according to each one's grade and condition, with the maintenance of peace? Thou art displeased at a man's sin, thou hast not "touched the unclean thing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:321
verses.text: Thou hast reproved, rebuked, admonished him, hast administered, if the case required it, a suitable discipline, and such as doth not violate unity; then thou hast "gone out from thence".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:322
verses.text: Now consider the actions of the Saints, lest perhaps this should seem to be an interpretation of my own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:323
verses.text: As Saints have understood these words, so surely ought they to be 			 understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:324
verses.text: "Go ye out from them," says the Prophet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:325
verses.text: I will first maintain this meaning of the words from their customary use, and will afterwards show that that meaning is not my own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:326
verses.text: It often happens that men are accused; and when they are accused they defend themselves, and when the accused defends himself with good reason and justice, the hearers say, "He has got out of this".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:327
verses.text: Got out; whither has he gone? He abides still in the place where he was, yet has he "got out of this".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:328
verses.text: How has he got out of it? By the good account he has rendered, and by his most satisfactory defence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:329
verses.text: This is what the holy Apostles did when they "shook off the dust from their feet" against those who did not receive the message of peace which was sent to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:330
verses.text: That watchman, "got out from thence," to whom it was I said, "I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:331
verses.text: For it was told him "If thou warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, nor from his way, that wicked one shall die in his iniquity, and thou shalt deliver thy soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:332
verses.text: This if he do, he "goes out from him," not by a bodily separation, but by the defence of his own work.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:333
verses.text: For he did what it was his duty to do; though the other, whose duty it was to obey, obeyed not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:334
verses.text: This then is that, "Go ye out from thence".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:335
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:336
verses.text: So cried Moses and Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:337
verses.text: Let us see then if they acted thus, if they left the people of God, and betook themselves to other nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:338
verses.text: How many and vehement rebukes did Jeremiah utter against the sinners, and wicked ones of his people.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:339
verses.text: Yet he lived amongst them, he entered into the same temple with them, celebrated the same mysteries; he lived in that congregation of wicked men, but by his crying out "he went out from them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:340
verses.text: This is "to go out from them;" this is not "to touch the unclean thing," the not consenting to them in will, and the not sparing them in word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:341
verses.text: What shall I say of Jeremiah, of Isaiah, of Daniel, and Ezekiel, and the rest of the prophets, who did not retire from the wicked people, lest they should desert the good who were mingled with that people, among whom themselves were 			 able to be such as they were? When Moses himself, Brethren, was receiving the law in the mount, the people below made an idol.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:342
verses.text: The people of God, the people who had been led through the waves of the Red Sea which gave way to them, and overwhelmed their enemies who followed after, after so many signs and miracles displayed in plagues upon the Egyptians even unto death, and for "their" protection unto deliverance, yet demanded an idol, obtained an idol by force, made an idol, adored an idol, sacrificed unto an idol.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:343
verses.text: God showeth His servant what the people had done, and saith that He will destroy 			 them from before His Face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:344
verses.text: Moses maketh intercession for them as he was about to return to this people; yet had he a good opportunity of retiring and "going out from them," as these persons understand it, that he might "not touch the unclean thing," might not live among them; but he did not so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:345
verses.text: And that he might not seem to have acted thus from necessity rather than from love, God offered him another people; so that He might destroy these: "I will make of thee," He said, "a great 			 nation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:346
verses.text: But he did not accept it; he cleaveth to the sinners, he prayeth for the sinners.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:347
verses.text: And how does he pray? O signal proof of love, my Brethren! How does he pray? Mark that, as it were, mother's fondness, of which I have often spoken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:348
verses.text: When God threatened the sacrilegious people, Moses' tender heart trembled, and on their behalf he opposed himself to the wrath of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:349
verses.text: "Lord," he says, "if Thou wilt forgive their sin, forgive; but if not, blot me out of Thy book 			 which Thou hast written".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:350
verses.text: With what a father's and mother's fondness, yet with what assurance said he this, as he considered at once the justice and the mercy of God; that in that He is just, He would not destroy the righteous man; and that in that He is merciful, He would pardon the sinners.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:351
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:352
verses.text: It is now surely plain to your discernment, in what manner all such testimonies of the Scriptures are to be received; so that when Scripture says, that we must depart from the wicked, we are bid to understand this in no other sense, but that we depart in heart; lest by the separation from the good, we commit a greater evil than we shrink from in the union of the wicked, as these Donatists have done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:353
verses.text: But if they were truly good, and so had reproved the wicked, and not rather being themselves wicked, had defamed 			  the good, they would for peace sake bear with any, be they who they might, seeing they have received the Maximianists as sound, whom they condemned before as lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:354
verses.text: Undoubtedly the Prophet has said plainly, "Depart ye, go ye out from thence, and touch not the unclean thing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:355
verses.text: But that I may understand what he said, I pay attention to what he did.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:356
verses.text: By his own deeds he explains his words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:357
verses.text: He said, "Depart ye".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:358
verses.text: To whom did he say so? To the righteous of course.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:359
verses.text: From whom did he bid them depart? From sinners and wicked men of course.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:360
verses.text: I ask then, did he depart from such himself? I find that 			 he did not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:361
verses.text: So then he understood it in another sense.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:362
verses.text: For surely he would be the first to do what he enjoined.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:363
verses.text: He departed from them in heart, he rebuked and reproved them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:364
verses.text: By keeping himself from consenting to them, he "did not touch the unclean thing;" but by rebuking them he "went out" free in the sight of God; and to him God neither imputeth his own sins, because he sinned not; nor the sins of others, because he approved them not; nor negligence, because he kept not silence; nor 			 pride, because he continued in unity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 37:365
verses.text: So then, my Brethren, how many soever ye have among you, who are still weighed down by the love of the world, covetous, or perjured persons, adulterers, spectacle hunters, consulters of astrologers, of fanatics, of soothsayers, of augurs and diviners, drunkards, sensualists, whatever there is of bad that ye know ye have among you; show your disapprobation of it all as far as ye are able, that ye may in heart "depart;" and reprove them, that ye may "go 			 out from them;" and consent not to them, that "ye touch not the unclean thing".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:1
verses.text: Sermon XXXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:2
verses.text: [LXXXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:5
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:6
verses.text: 19, where Jesus dried up the fig-tree; and on the words, Luke xxiv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:7
verses.text: 28, where He made a pretence as though He would go further.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:9
verses.text: The lesson of the Holy Gospel which has just been read, has given us an alarming warning, lest we have leaves only, and have no fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:10
verses.text: That is, in few words, lest words be present and deeds be wanting.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:11
verses.text: Very terrible! Who does not fear when in this lesson he sees with the eyes of the heart the withered tree, withered at that word being spoken to it, "Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever"? Let the fear work amendment, and the amendment bring forth fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:12
verses.text: For without doubt, the Lord Christ foresaw that a certain tree would deservedly become withered, because it would have leaves, and would have no fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:13
verses.text: That tree is the synagogue, not that which was called, but that which was reprobate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:14
verses.text: For out of it also was called the people of God, who in sincerity and truth waited in the Prophets for the salvation of God, Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:15
verses.text: And forasmuch as it waited in faith, it 			 was thought worthy to know Him when He was present.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:16
verses.text: For out of it came the Apostles, out of it came the whole multitude of those who went before the ass of the Lord, and said, "Hosanna to the Son of David, blessed is He that cometh in the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:17
verses.text: There was a great company then of believing Jews, a great company of those who believed in Christ before He shed His Blood for them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:18
verses.text: For it was not in vain that the Lord Himself had come to none "but to the lost sheep of the house of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:19
verses.text: But in others, after He was crucified, and was now exalted into heaven, He found the fruit of repentance; and these He did not make to wither, but cultivated them in His field, and watered them with His word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:20
verses.text: Of this number were those four thousand Jews who believed, after that the disciples and those who were with them, filled with the Holy Ghost, spake with the tongues of all nations, and in that diversity of tongues announced in a way beforehand, that the Church should be throughout all nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:21
verses.text: They believed at that time, and "they were the lost sheep of the house of Israel;" but because "the Son of Man had come to seek and to save that which was lost," He found these also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:22
verses.text: But they lay hid here and there among thorns, as though wasted and dispersed by the wolves; and because they lay hid among thorns, He did not come to find them, save when torn by the thorns of His Passion; yet come He did, He found, He redeemed them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:23
verses.text: They had slain, not Him so much, as themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:24
verses.text: They were saved by Him who was slain for them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:25
verses.text: For, as the Apostles spake, they were pricked; they were pricked in conscience, who had pricked Him with the spear; and being pricked they sought for counsel, received it when it was given, repented, found grace, and believing drunk that Blood which in their fury they had shed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:26
verses.text: But they who have remained in this bad and barren race, even unto this day, and shall remain unto the end, were figured in that tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:27
verses.text: You come to them at this day, and find with them all the writings of the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:28
verses.text: But these are but leaves; Christ 			 is an hungred, and He seeketh for fruit; but findeth no fruit among them, because He doth not find Himself among them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:29
verses.text: For He hath no fruit, who hath not Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:30
verses.text: And he hath not Christ, who holdeth not to Christ's unity, who hath not charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:31
verses.text: And so by this chain he hath no fruit who hath not charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:32
verses.text: Hear the Apostle, "Now the fruit of the Spirit is charity;" so setting forth the praise of this cluster, that is, of this fruit; "The fruit of the Spirit," he says, "is charity, 			  joy, peace, long-suffering".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:33
verses.text: Do not wonder at what follows, when charity leads the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:34
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:35
verses.text: Accordingly, when the disciples marvelled at the withering of the tree, He set forth to them the value of faith, and said to them, "If ye have faith, and doubt not;" that is, if in all things ye have trust in God; and do not say, "God can do this, this He cannot do;" but rely on the omnipotence of the Almighty; "ye shall not only do this, but also if ye shall say to this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea, it shall be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:36
verses.text: And all things whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:37
verses.text: Now we read that miracles were wrought by the disciples, yea rather by the Lord through the disciples; for, "without Me," He says, "ye can do nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:38
verses.text: The Lord could do many things without the disciples, but the disciples nothing without the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:39
verses.text: He who could make even the disciples themselves, was not certainly assisted by them to make them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:40
verses.text: We read then of the Apostles' miracles, but we nowhere read of a tree being withered by them, nor of a mountain removed into the sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:41
verses.text: Let us enquire therefore where this was done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:42
verses.text: For the words of the Lord could not be without effect.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:43
verses.text: If ye are thinking of "trees" and "mountains" in their ordinary and familiar sense, it has not been done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:44
verses.text: But if ye think of that tree of which He spake, 			 and of that mountain of the Lord of which the Prophet said, "In the last days the mountain of the Lord's house shall be manifest;" if ye think of it, and understand it thus, it has been done, and done by the Apostles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:45
verses.text: The tree is the Jewish nation, but I say again, that part of it which was reprobate, not that which was called; that tree which we have spoken of is the Jewish nation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:46
verses.text: The mountain, as the prophetic testimony hath taught us, is the Lord Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:47
verses.text: The withered tree is the Jewish nation reft of the honour of Christ; the sea is this world with all the nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:48
