verses.text: Now see the Apostles speaking to 			 this tree which was about to be withered away, and casting the mountain into the sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:49
verses.text: In the Acts of the Apostles they speak to the Jews who gainsay and resist the word of truth, that is, who have leaves and have no fruit, and they say to them, "It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye have put it from you" (for ye use the words of the Prophets, yet do not acknowledge Him whom the Prophets foretold, that is, ye have leaves only), "lo, we 			 turn to the Gentiles".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:50
verses.text: For this also was foretold by the Prophets; "Behold, I have given Thee for a light of the Gentiles, that Thou mayest be My salvation unto the end of the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:51
verses.text: See then, the tree hath withered away; and Christ hath been removed unto the Gentiles, the mountain into the sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:52
verses.text: For how should not the tree wither away which is planted in that vineyard, of which it was said, "I will command my clouds that they rain no rain upon it"?  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:53
verses.text: Now that in order to convey this truth the Lord acted prophetically, I mean that, as concerning this tree, it was not His will merely to exhibit a miracle, but that by the miracle He conveyed the intimation of something to come, there are many things which teach and persuade us, yea even against our wills force us to believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:54
verses.text: In the first place, what fault in the tree was it that it had no fruit, when even if it had no fruit at the proper season, that is, the 			 season of its fruit, it would not assuredly be any fault in the tree; for the tree as being without sense and reason could not be to blame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:55
verses.text: But to this is added, that as we read it in the narrative of the other Evangelist who expressly mentions this, "it was not the time for that fruit".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:56
verses.text: For that was the time when the fig-tree shoots forth its tender leaves, which come, we know, before the fruit; and this we prove, because the day of the Lord's Passion was at hand, and we know at what time He suffered; and if we did not know it, we ought of course to give credit to the Evangelist who says, "The time of figs was not yet".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:57
verses.text: So then if it was only a miracle that was to have been set forth, and not something to be prophetically figured, it 			 would have been much more worthy of the clemency and mercy of the Lord, to have made green again any tree He might find withered; as He healed the sick, as He cleansed the lepers, as He raised the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:58
verses.text: But then contrariwise, as though against the ordinary rule of His clemency, He found a green tree, not yet bearing fruit out of its proper season, but still not refusing the hope of fruit to its dresser, and He withered it away; as though He would say to us, "I have no delight in the withering 			 away of this tree, but thus I would convey to you, that I have not designed to do this without any cause for it, but only because I desired thereby to convey to you a lesson you might the more regard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:59
verses.text: It is not this tree that I have cursed, it is not on a tree without sense that I have inflicted punishment, but I have made thee fear, whosoever thou art that dost consider the matter, that thou mightest not despise Christ when He is an hungered, that thou mightest love rather to be enriched with 			 fruit, than to be overshadowed by leaves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:60
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:61
verses.text: This one thing is that which the Lord intimates that He designed to signify by what He did.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:62
verses.text: What else is there? He cometh to the tree being hungry, and seeketh fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:63
verses.text: Did He not know that it was not the time for it? What the cultivator of the tree knew, did not its Creator know? He seeketh on the tree then for fruit which it had not yet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:64
verses.text: Doth He really seek for it, or rather make a pretence of seeking it? For if He really sought it, He was mistaken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:65
verses.text: But this be 			 far from Him, to be mistaken! He made then a pretence of seeking it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:66
verses.text: Fearing to allow this, that he maketh a pretence, thou dost confess that He was mistaken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:67
verses.text: Again, thou dost turn away from the idea of His being mistaken, and so run into that of His making a pretence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:68
verses.text: We are parched up between the two.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:69
verses.text: If we are parched, let us beg for rain, that we may grow green, lest in saying anything unworthy of the Lord, we rather wither away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:70
verses.text: The Evangelist indeed says, "He came to the tree, and found 			 no fruit on it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:71
verses.text: "He found none," would not be said of Him, unless He had either really sought for it, or made a pretence of seeking, though He knew that there was none there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:72
verses.text: Wherefore we do not hesitate, let us by no means say that Christ was mistaken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:73
verses.text: What then? shall we say He made a pretence? Shall we say this? How shall we get out of this difficulty? Let us say what, if the Evangelist had not said of the Lord in another place, we should not of ourselves dare to say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:74
verses.text: Let us say what 			 the Evangelist has written, and when we have said, let us understand it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:75
verses.text: But in order that we may understand it, let us first believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:76
verses.text: For, "unless ye believe," says the Prophet, "ye shall not understand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:77
verses.text: The Lord Christ after His Resurrection, was walking in the way with two of His disciples, by whom He was not yet recognised, and with whom He joined company as a third traveller.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:78
verses.text: They came to the place whither they were going, and the Evangelist says, "But He made a pretence as though He would have gone further".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:79
verses.text: But they kept Him, saying, in the spirit of a courteous kindness, that it was already drawing toward evening, and praying Him to tarry there with them; being received and entertained by them, He breaketh Bread, and is known of them in blessing and breaking of the Bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:80
verses.text: So then, let us not now fear to say, that He made a pretence of seeking, if He made a pretence of going further.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:81
verses.text: But here there arises another question.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:82
verses.text: Yesterday I insisted at some length on the truth which is in the Apostles; how then do we find any "pretence" in the Lord Himself? Therefore, Brethren, I must tell you, and teach you according to my poor abilities, which the Lord giveth me for your benefit, and must convey to you what ye may hold as a rule in the interpretation of all Scripture.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:83
verses.text: Everything that is said or done is to be understood either in its literal signification, or else it signifies something figuratively; or at least contains both of these at once, both its own literal interpretation, and a figurative signification also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:84
verses.text: Thus I have set forth three things, examples of them must now be given; and from whence, but from the Holy Scriptures? It is said in its literal acceptation, that the Lord suffered, that He rose again, and ascended into heaven; that we shall rise again at the end of the world, that we shall reign with Him for ever, if we do not despise Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:85
verses.text: Take all this as spoken literally, and look not out for figures; as it is expressed, so it really is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:86
verses.text: And so also with divers actions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:87
verses.text: The Apostle went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, the Apostle actually did this, it actually took place, it was an action peculiar to himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:88
verses.text: It is a fact which he tells you; a simple fact according to its literal meaning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:89
verses.text: "The stone which the builders refused, is become the Head of the corner," is spoken in a figure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:90
verses.text: If we take "the stone" literally, what "stone did the builders refuse, which became the Head of the corner"? If we take "the stone" literally, of what corner is this "stone" become the Head? If we admit that it was figuratively expressed, and take it figuratively, the Corner-stone is Christ: the head of the corner, is the Head of the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:91
verses.text: Why is the Church the Corner? Because she has called the Jews from one 			 side, and the Gentiles from another, and these two walls as it were coming from different quarters, and meeting together in one, she has bound together by the grace of her peace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:92
verses.text: For, "He is our peace, who hath made both one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:93
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:94
verses.text: Ye have heard instances of a literal expression, and a literal action, and of a figurative expression; ye are waiting for an instance of a figurative action.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:95
verses.text: There are many such, but meanwhile, as is suggested by this mention of the corner-stone, when Jacob anointed the stone which he had placed at his head as he slept, and in his sleep saw a mysterious dream, ladders rising from the earth to heaven, and Angels ascending and descending, and the Lord standing upon the ladder, he understood what it was designed to figure, and took the stone for a figure of Christ, to prove to us thereby that he was no stranger to the understanding of that vision and revelation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:96
verses.text: Do not wonder then that he anointed it, for Christ received His Name from "the anointing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:97
verses.text: Now this Jacob was said in the Scripture to be "a man without guile".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:98
verses.text: And this Jacob ye know was called Israel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:99
verses.text: Accordingly in the Gospel, when the Lord saw Nathanael, He said, "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:100
verses.text: And that Israelite not yet knowing who it was that talked with him, answered, "Whence knewest Thou me?" And the Lord said to him, "When thou wast under the fig-tree I saw thee;" as though he would say, When thou wast in the shadow of sin, I predestinated thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:101
verses.text: And Nathanael, because he remembered that he had been under the fig-tree, where the Lord was not, acknowledged His Divinity, and answered, "Thou art the Son of God, Thou art the King of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:102
verses.text: He who had been under the fig-tree was not made a withered fig-tree; he acknowledged Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:103
verses.text: And the Lord said unto him, "Because I said, When thou wast under the fig-tree I saw thee, believest 			 thou? thou shall see greater things than these".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:104
verses.text: What are these "greater things"? "Verily I say unto you" (for he "is an Israelite in whom is no guile;" remember Jacob in whom was no guile; and recollect of what he is speaking, the stone at his head, the vision in his sleep, the ladder from earth to heaven, the Angels ascending and descending; and so see what it is that the Lord would say to "the Israelite without guile"); "Verily I say unto you, Ye shall see heaven 			 opened" (hear, thou guileless Nathanael, what guileless Jacob saw); "ye shall see heaven opened, and Angels ascending and descending" (unto whom?) "unto the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:105
verses.text: Therefore was He, as the Son of Man, anointed on the head; for "the head of the woman is the man, and the Head of the man is Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:106
verses.text: Now observe, He did not say, "ascending from the Son of Man, and descending to the Son of Man," as if He were only above; but "ascending and descending unto the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:107
verses.text: Hear the Son of Man crying out from above, "Saul, Saul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:108
verses.text: Hear the Son of Man from below, "Why persecutest thou Me?"  6.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:109
verses.text: Ye have heard an instance of a literal expression, as "that we shall rise again;" of a literal action, as that, according as it is said, "Paul went up to Jerusalem to see Peter".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:110
verses.text: "The stone which the builders refused," is a figurative expression; "the anointed stone" which was at Jacob's head, is a figurative action.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:111
verses.text: There is now due to your expectation an example made out of both together, something which is at once a literal fact, and which also signifies something else figured by it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:112
verses.text: "We know that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a free-woman;" this was literally a fact, not only a story, but a fact; are ye looking for that which was figured in it? "These are the two Testaments".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:113
verses.text: That then which is spoken figuratively, is a sort of fiction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:114
verses.text: But since it has some real event represented by it, and the very figure itself has its ground of truth, it escapes all imputation of falsehood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:115
verses.text: "The sower went out to sow his seed; and as he sowed, some fell by the way side, some fell upon stony places, some fell among 			 thorns, and some fell upon good ground".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:116
verses.text: Who went out "to sow," or when went he out, or upon what "thorns," or "stones" or "way side" or in what field did he sow? If we receive this as a fictitious story, we understand it in a figurative sense; it is fictitious.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:117
verses.text: For if any sower really went out, and did cast the seed in these different places, as we have heard, it were no fiction, and so no falsehood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:118
verses.text: But now though it be a fiction, yet it is no falsehood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:119
verses.text: Why? Because the fiction has some further 			 signification, it deceives thee not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:120
verses.text: It requires only one to understand it, and does not lead any one into error.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:121
verses.text: And thus Christ wishing to convey this lesson to us, sought for fruit, and hereby set forth to us a figurative, and no deceiving fiction; a fiction therefore worthy of praise, not of blame; not one by the examination of which we might run into what was false; but by the diligent investigation of which we might discover what is true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:122
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:123
verses.text: I see that one may say, Explain to me; what did that signify, that "He made a pretence of going further"? For if it had no further meaning, it is a deceit, a lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:124
verses.text: We must then according to our rules of exposition, and distinctions, tell you what this "pretence of going further," signified; "He made a pretence of going further," and is kept back from going further.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:125
verses.text: In so far then as the Lord Christ being as they supposed absent in respect 			 of His Bodily presence, was thought to be really absent, He will as it were "go further".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:126
verses.text: But hold Him fast by faith, hold Him fast at the breaking of Bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:127
verses.text: What shall I say more? Have ye recognised Him? If so, then have ye found Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:128
verses.text: I must not speak any longer on this Sacrament.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:129
verses.text: They who put off the knowledge of this Sacrament, Christ goeth further from them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 38:130
verses.text: Let them then hold It fast, let them not let Him go; let them invite Him to their home, and so they are invited to heaven.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:1
verses.text: Sermon XL.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:2
verses.text: [XC.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:5
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:6
verses.text: 2, etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:7
verses.text: , about the marriage of the king's son; against the Donatists, on charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:8
verses.text: Delivered at Carthage in the Restituta.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:9
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:10
verses.text: All the faithful know the marriage of the king's son, and his feast, and the spreading of the Lord's Table is open to them all who will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:11
verses.text: But it is of importance to each one to see how he approaches, even when he is not forbidden to approach It.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:12
verses.text: For the Holy Scriptures teach us that there are two feasts of the Lord; one to which the good and evil come, the other to which the evil come not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:13
verses.text: So then the feast, of which we have just now heard when the Gospel was being read, has both good and evil guests.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:14
verses.text: All who excused themselves from this feast are evil; but not all those who entered in are good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:15
verses.text: You 			 therefore who are the good guests at this feast do I address, who have in your minds the words, "He that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh judgment to himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:16
verses.text: All you who are such do I address, that ye look not for the good without, that ye bear with the evil within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:17
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:18
verses.text: I do not doubt that ye wish to hear, Beloved, who they are of whom I have spoken in my address, that they should not look for the good without, and should bear with the evil within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:19
verses.text: If all within are evil, whom do I address? If all within are good, whom did I advise them to bear with being evil? Let me first then with the Lord's assistance get out of this difficulty as best I can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:20
verses.text: If you consider good perfectly and strictly speaking, none is good but God Alone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:21
verses.text: Ye have the Lord saying most plainly, "Why callest thou Me good? there is none Good but One, that is, God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:22
verses.text: How then can that marriage feast have good and bad guests, if "none is good but God Alone"? In the first place ye ought to know, that after a certain sort we are all evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:23
verses.text: Yes, doubtless after a certain sort are we all evil; but after no sort are we all good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:24
verses.text: For can we compare ourselves with the Apostles, to whom the Lord Himself said, "If ye then being evil know how to give good gifts unto your children?" If we consider the Scriptures, there was but one evil one among the twelve Apostles, with reference to whom the Lord said in a certain place, "And ye are clean, but not all".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:25
verses.text: But yet in addressing them all together, He said, "If ye being evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:26
verses.text: Peter heard this, John heard this, Andrew heard this, all the rest of the eleven Apostles heard it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:27
verses.text: What did they hear? "If ye being evil know how to give good gifts unto your children; how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask Him?" When they heard that they were evil, they were in despair; but when they heard that God in heaven was their Father, they 			 revived.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:28
verses.text: "Ye being evil;" what then is due to the evil, but punishment? "How much more shall your Father which is in heaven?" What is due to children but reward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:29
verses.text: In the name of "evil" is the dread of punishment; in the name of "children" is the hope of heirs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:31
verses.text: According to a certain respect then they were evil, who after another respect were good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:32
verses.text: For to them to whom it is said, "Ye being evil know how to give good gifts unto your children;" is added immediately, "How much more shall your Father which is in heaven?" He is then the Father of the evil, but not of those who are to be left so; because He is the Physician of them who are to be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:33
verses.text: According to a certain sort then they were evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:34
verses.text: And yet those 			 guests of the Householder at the King's marriage, were not I suppose of that number of whom it was said, "they invited good and bad," that they should be reckoned among the number of the bad, who we have heard were shut out in his person who was found not to have a wedding garment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:35
verses.text: According to a certain respect, I repeat they were bad, who yet were good; and according to a certain respect they were good, who yet were bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:36
verses.text: Hear John according to what respect they were bad: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:37
verses.text: Behold after what respect they were bad: because they had sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:38
verses.text: According to what respect were they good? "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:39
verses.text: If then we should say, on the principle of this interpretation which ye have now heard me bring, as I think, out of the sacred Scriptures, viz.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:40
verses.text: that the same men are both after a certain manner, good, and after a certain manner bad; if we should wish to receive according to this sense the words, "they invited good and bad," the same persons, that is, at once good and bad; if we should wish so to receive them, we are not permitted so to do, by reason of 			 that one who was found "not having a wedding garment," and who was not merely "cast forth," so as to be deprived of that feast, but so as to be condemned in the punishment of everlasting darkness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:41
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:42
verses.text: But one will say, What of one man? what strange, what great matter is it, if one among the crowd "not having a wedding garment" crept in unperceived to the servants of the Householder? Could it be said because of that one, "they invited good and bad"? Attend therefore, my Brethren, and understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:43
verses.text: That one man represented one class; for they were many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:44
verses.text: Here some diligent hearer may answer me, and say, "I have no wish for you to tell me your guesses; I 			 wish to have it proved to me that that one represented many".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:45
verses.text: By the Lord's present help, I will prove it clearly; nor will I search far, that I may be able to prove it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:46
verses.text: God will assist me in His own words in this place, and will furnish you by my ministry with a plain proof of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:47
verses.text: "The Master of the house came in to see the guests".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:48
verses.text: See, my Brethren, the servants' business was only to invite and bring in the good and bad; see that it is not said, that the servants took notice of the guests, and found among them a man which had not on a wedding garment, and spoke to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:49
verses.text: This is not written.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:50
verses.text: The Master of the house saw him, the Master of the house discovered, the Master of the house inspected, the Master of the house separated him out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:51
verses.text: It was not right to pass over this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:52
verses.text: But I have undertaken to 			 establish another point, how that that one signifies many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:53
verses.text: "The Master of the house" then "came in to see the guests, and He found there a man which had not on a wedding garment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:54
verses.text: And He saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:55
verses.text: For He who questioned him was One, to whom he could give no feigned reply.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:56
verses.text: The garment that was looked for is in the heart, not on the body; for had it been put on externally, it could not have been concealed even from the servants.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:57
verses.text: Where that wedding garment must be put on, hear in the words, "Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:58
verses.text: Of that garment the Apostle speaks, "If so be that we shall be found clothed, and not naked".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:59
verses.text: Therefore was he discovered by the Lord, who escaped the notice of the servants.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:60
verses.text: Being questioned, he is speechless: he is bound, cast out, and condemned one by many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:61
verses.text: I have said, Lord, that Thou teachest us that in this Thou dost give warning to all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:62
verses.text: Recollect then with me, my Brethren, the words which ye have heard, and ye will at once discover, at once determine, that that one was many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:63
verses.text: True it was one man whom the Lord questioned, to one He said, "Friend, how camest thou 			 in hither?" It was one who was speechless, and of that same one was it said, "Bind him hand and foot, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:64
verses.text: Why? "For many are called, but few chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:65
verses.text: How can any one gainsay this manifestation of the truth? "Cast him," He saith, "into outer darkness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:66
verses.text: "Him," that one man assuredly, of whom the Lord saith, "for many are called, but few chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:67
verses.text: So then it is the few who are not cast out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:68
verses.text: He was it is true but one man "who had not the wedding garment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:69
verses.text: Cast him out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:70
verses.text: But why is he cast out? "For many are called, but few chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:71
verses.text: Leave alone the few, cast out the many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:72
verses.text: It is true, that man was but one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:73
verses.text: Yet undoubtedly that one not only was many, but those many in numbers far surpassed the number of the good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:74
verses.text: For the good are many also; but in comparison of the bad, they are few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:75
verses.text: In the crop there is much wheat; compare it with the chaff, and the grains of corn are few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:76
verses.text: The same persons considered in themselves are many, in comparison with the bad are few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:77
verses.text: How do we prove that in themselves they are many? "Many shall come from the East and from the West".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:78
verses.text: Whither shall they come? To that 			 feast, into which both good and bad enter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:79
verses.text: But speaking of another feast, He subjoined, "and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:80
verses.text: That is the feast to which the bad shall not approach.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:81
verses.text: Be that feast which now is, received worthily, that we may attain to the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:82
verses.text: The same then are many, who are also few; in themselves many; in comparison with the bad few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:83
verses.text: Therefore what saith the Lord? He found one, and said, "Let the many be cast out, the few remain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:84
verses.text: For to say, "many are called, but few chosen," is nothing else than to show plainly who in this present feast are accounted to be such, as to be 			 brought to that other feast, where no bad men shall come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:85
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:86
verses.text: What is it then? I would not that ye all who approach the Lord's Table which is in this life, should be with the many who are to be shut out, but with the few who are to be reserved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:87
verses.text: And how shall ye be able to attain to this? Take "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:88
verses.text: Ye will say, "Explain this 'wedding garment' to us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:89
verses.text: Without a doubt, that is the garment which none but the good have, who are to be left at the feast, reserved unto that other feast 			 to which no bad man approaches, who are to be brought safely thither by the grace of the Lord; these have "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:90
verses.text: Let us then, my Brethren, seek for those among the faithful who have something which bad men have not, and this will be "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:91
verses.text: If we speak of sacraments, ye see how that these are common to the bad and good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:92
verses.text: Is it Baptism? Without Baptism it is true no one attaineth to God; but not every one that hath Baptism attaineth to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:93
verses.text: I cannot 			 therefore understand Baptism, the Sacrament itself that is, to be "the wedding garment;" for this garment I see in the good, I see in the bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:94
verses.text: Peradventure it is the Altar, or That which is received at the Altar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:95
verses.text: But no; we see that many eat, and "eat and drink judgment to themselves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:96
verses.text: What is it then? Is it fasting? The wicked fast also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:97
verses.text: Is it running together to the Church? The wicked run thither also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:98
verses.text: Lastly, is it miracles? Not only do the good and bad perform them, but sometimes 			 the good perform them not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:99
verses.text: See, among the ancient people Pharaoh's magicians wrought miracles, the Israelites did not; among the Israelites, Moses only and Aaron wrought them; the rest did not, but saw, and feared, and believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:100
verses.text: Were the magicians of Pharaoh who did miracles, better men than the people of Israel who could not do them, and yet that people were the people of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:101
verses.text: In the Church itself, hear the Apostle, "Are all prophets? Have all the gifts of healing? Do all speak with tongues?"  6.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:102
verses.text: What is that "wedding garment" then? This is the wedding garment: "Now the end of the commandment," says the Apostle, "is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:103
verses.text: This is "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:104
verses.text: Not charity of any kind whatever; for very often they who are partakers together of an evil conscience seem to love one another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:105
verses.text: They who commit robberies together, who love the hurtful arts of sorceries, and the stage together, who join together in the shout of the chariot race, or the wild beast fight; these very often love one another; but in these there is no "charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith 			 unfeigned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:106
verses.text: The wedding garment" is such charity as this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:107
verses.text: "Though I speak with the tongues of men and of Angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, and a tinkling cymbal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:108
verses.text: Tongues have come in alone, and it is said to them, "How came ye in hither not having a wedding garment?" "Though," said he, "I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:109
verses.text: See, these are the miracles of men who very often have not "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:110
verses.text: "Though," he says, "I have all these, and have not Christ, I am 			 nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:111
verses.text: Is then "the gift of prophecy" nothing? is then "the knowledge of mysteries" nothing? It is not that these are nothing; but "I," if I have them, "and have not charity, am nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:112
verses.text: How many good things profit nothing without this one good thing! If then I have not charity, though I bestow alms freely upon the poor, though I have come to the confession of Christ's Name even unto blood and fire, these things may be done even through the love of glory, and so are vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:113
verses.text: Because then they may be done even from the love of glory, and so be vain, 			 and not through the rich charity of a godly affection, he names them all also in express terms, and do thou give ear to them; "though I distribute all my goods for the use of the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:114
verses.text: This then is "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:115
verses.text: Question yourselves; if ye have it, ye may be without fear in the Feast of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:116
verses.text: In one and the same man there exist two things, charity and desire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:117
verses.text: Let charity be born in thee, if it be yet unborn, and if it be born, be it nourished, fostered, increased.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:118
verses.text: But as to that desire, though in this life it cannot be utterly extinguished; "for if we say that we have no sin we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us;" 			  but in so far as desire is in us, so far we are not without sin: let charity increase, desire decrease; that the one, that is, charity, may one day be perfected, and desire be consumed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:119
verses.text: Put on "the wedding garment:" you I address, who as yet have it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:120
verses.text: Ye are already within, already do ye approach to the Feast, and still have ye not yet the garment to do honour to the Bridegroom; "Ye are yet seeking your own things, not the things which are Jesus Christ's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:121
verses.text: For "the wedding garment" is taken in honour of the union, the union, that is, of the Bridegroom to the Bride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:122
verses.text: Ye know the Bridegroom; it is Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:123
verses.text: Ye know the Bride; it is the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:124
verses.text: Pay honour to the Bride, pay honour to the Bridegroom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:125
verses.text: If ye pay due honour to them both, ye will be their children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:126
verses.text: Therefore in this make progress.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:127
verses.text: Love the Lord, and so learn to love yourselves; that when by loving the Lord ye shall have loved yourselves, ye may securely love your neighbour as yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:128
verses.text: For when I find a man that does not love himself, how shall I commit his neighbour whom he should love as himself to him? And who is there, you will say, 			 who does not love himself? Who is there? See, "He that loveth iniquity hateth his own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:129
verses.text: Does he love himself, who loves his body, and hates his soul to his own hurt, to the hurt of both his body and soul? And who loves his own soul? He that loveth God with all his heart and with all his mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:130
verses.text: To such an one I would at once entrust his neighbour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:131
verses.text: "Love your neighbour as yourselves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:132
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:133
verses.text: One may say, "Who is my neighbour?" Every man is your neighbour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:134
verses.text: Had we not all the same two parents? Animals of every species are neighbours one to the other, the dove to the dove, the leopard to the leopard, the asp to the asp, the sheep to the sheep, and is not man neighbour to man? Call to mind the ordering of the creation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:135
verses.text: God spake, the waters brought forth swimming creatures, great whales, fish, birds, and such like things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:136
verses.text: Did all the birds come of 			 one bird? Did all vultures come of one vulture? Did all doves come of one dove? Did all snakes come of one snake? or all gilt-heads of one gilt-head? or all sheep of one sheep? No, the earth assuredly brought forth all these kinds together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:137
verses.text: But when it came to man, the earth did not bring forth man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:138
verses.text: One father was made for us; not even two, father and mother: one father, I say, was made for us, not even two, father and mother; but out of the one father came the one mother; the one father came from none, but was made by God, and the one mother came out of him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:139
verses.text: Mark then the nature of our race: we flowed out of one fountain; 			 and because that one was turned to bitterness, we all became from a good, a wild olive tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:140
verses.text: And so grace came also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:141
verses.text: One begat us unto sin and death, yet as one race, yet as neighbours one to another, yet as not merely like, but related to each other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:142
verses.text: There came One against one; against the one who scattered, One who gathereth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:143
verses.text: Thus against the one who slayeth, is the One who maketh alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:144
verses.text: "For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:145
verses.text: Now as whosoever is born of the first, dieth; so whosoever believeth in Christ is made alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:146
verses.text: Provided, that is, that he have "the wedding garment," and be invited as one who is to remain, and not to be cast out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:147
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:148
verses.text: So then, my Brethren, have charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:149
verses.text: I have explained it to be this garment, this "wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:150
verses.text: Faith is praised, it is plain, it is praised: but what kind of faith this is, the Apostle distinguishes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:151
verses.text: For certain who boasted of faith, and had not a good conversation, the Apostle James rebukes and says, "Thou believest there is one God, thou doest well; the devils also believe and tremble".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:152
verses.text: Call to mind with me whereupon Peter was praised, whereupon called blessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:153
verses.text: Was it because he said, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God"? He who pronounced Him blessed, regarded not the sound of the words, but the affection of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:154
verses.text: For would ye know that Peter's blessedness lay not in these words? The devils also said the same.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:155
verses.text: "We know Thee who Thou art, the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:156
verses.text: Peter confessed Him to be "the Son of God;" the devils confessed Him to be "the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:157
verses.text: "Distinguish, my lord, distinguish between the two".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:158
verses.text: I do make a plain distinction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:159
verses.text: Peter spake in love, the devils from fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:160
verses.text: And again Peter says, "I am with Thee, even unto death".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:161
verses.text: The devils say, "What have we to do with Thee?" So then thou who art come to the feast, glory not of faith only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:162
verses.text: Distinguish well the nature of this faith; and then in thee is recognised "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:163
verses.text: Let the Apostle make the distinction, let him teach us; "neither circumcision availeth anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:164
verses.text: Tell us, what faith? do not even the devils believe and tremble? I will tell thee, he says, and listen, I will now draw the distinction, "But faith which worketh by love".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:165
verses.text: What faith, then, and of what kind? "That which worketh by love".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:166
verses.text: "Though I have all knowledge," he says, "and all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:167
verses.text: Have faith with love; for love without faith ye cannot have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:168
verses.text: This I warn, this I exhort, this in the 			 name of the Lord I teach you, Beloved, that ye have faith with love; for ye may possibly have faith without love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:169
verses.text: I do not exhort you to have faith, but love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:170
verses.text: For ye cannot have love without faith; the love I mean of God and your neighbour; whence can it come without faith? How doth he love God, who doth not believe on God? How doth the fool love God, "who saith in his heart, there is no God"? Possible it is that ye may believe that Christ hath come and not love Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:171
verses.text: But it is not possible that ye should love Christ, and yet say that Christ hath not come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:172
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:173
verses.text: So then, have faith with love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:174
verses.text: This is the "wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:175
verses.text: Ye who love Christ, love one another, love your friends, love your enemies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:176
verses.text: Let not this be hard to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:177
verses.text: What then do ye lose thereby, when ye gain so much? What? dost thou ask of God as some great favour, that thine enemy may die? This is not "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:178
verses.text: Turn thy thoughts to the Bridegroom Himself hanging upon the Cross for thee, and praying to His Father for His enemies; 			 "Father," saith He, "forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:179
verses.text: Thou hast seen the Bridegroom speaking thus; see too the friend of the Bridegroom, a guest "with the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:180
verses.text: Look at the blessed Stephen, how he rebukes the Jews as though in rage and resentment, "Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye have resisted the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:181
verses.text: Which of the Prophets have not your fathers killed?" Thou hast heard how severe he is with his tongue.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:182
verses.text: And at once thou art prepared to speak against any one; and I would it were against him who offendeth God, and not who offendeth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:183
verses.text: One offendeth God, and thou dost not rebuke him; he offendeth thee, and thou criest out; where is that "wedding garment"? Ye have heard therefore how Stephen was severe; now hear how he loved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:184
verses.text: He offended those whom he was rebuking, and was stoned by them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:185
verses.text: And as he was being overwhelmed and bruised to death by the hands of his furious persecutors 			 on every side, and the blows of the stones, he first said, "Lord Jesus Christ, receive my spirit".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:186
verses.text: Then after he had prayed for himself standing, he bent the knee for them who were stoning him, and said, "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge; let me die in my body, but let not these die in their souls.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:187
verses.text: And when he had said this, he fell asleep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:188
verses.text: After these words he added no more; he spake them and departed; his last prayer was for his enemies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:189
verses.text: Learn ye hereby to have "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:190
verses.text: So do thou too bend the knee, and beat thy forehead against the ground, and as thou art about to approach the Table of the Lord, the Feast of the Holy Scriptures, do not say, "O that mine enemy might die! Lord, if I have deserved ought of Thee, slay mine enemy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:191
verses.text: Because if so be that thou sayest so, dost thou not fear lest 			 He should answer thee, "If I should choose to slay thine enemy, I should first slay thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:192
verses.text: What! dost thou glory because thou hast now come invited hither? Think only what thou wast but a little while ago.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:193
verses.text: Hast thou not blasphemed Me? hast thou not derided Me? didst thou not wish to wipe out My Name from off the earth? Yet now thou dost applaud thyself because thou hast come invited hither! If I had slain thee when thou wast Mine enemy, how could I have made thee My friend? Why, by thy wicked 			 prayers dost thou teach Me to do, what I did not in thine own case?" Yea rather God saith to thee, "Let me teach thee to imitate Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:194
verses.text: When I was hanging on the Cross, I said, 'Forgive them, for they know not what they do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:195
verses.text: ' This lesson I taught My brave soldier.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:196
verses.text: Be thou My recruit against the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:197
verses.text: In no other way wilt thou fight at all unconquerably, unless thou dost pray for thine enemies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:198
verses.text: Yet by all means ask this, yea ask this very thing, ask that thou mayest persecute thine enemy; but ask it with discernment; distinguish well what thou askest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:199
verses.text: See, a man is thine enemy; answer me, what is it in him which is at enmity with thee? Is it in this, that he is a man, that he is at enmity with 			 thee? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:200
verses.text: What then? That he is evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:201
verses.text: In that he is a man, in that he is that I made him, he is not at enmity with thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:202
verses.text: He saith to thee, "I did not make man evil; he became evil by disobedience, who obeyed the devil rather than God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:203
verses.text: What he has made himself, is at enmity with thee; in that he is evil, he is thine enemy; not in that he is a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:204
verses.text: For I hear the word "man," and "evil;" the one is the name of nature, the other of sin; the sin I cure; and the nature I preserve".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:205
verses.text: And so thy God saith to thee, "See, I do avenge thee, I do slay thine enemy; I take away that which makes him evil, I preserve that which constitutes him a man: now if I shall have made him a good man, have 			 I not slain thine enemy, and made him thy friend?" So ask on what thou art asking, not that the men may perish, but that these their enmities may perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:206
verses.text: For if thou pray for this, that the man may die; it is the prayer of one wicked man against another; and when thou dost say, "Slay the wicked one," God answereth thee, "Which of you?"  10.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:207
verses.text: Extend your love then, and limit it not to your wives and children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:208
verses.text: Such love is found even in beasts and sparrows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:209
verses.text: Ye know the sparrows and the swallows how they love their mates, how together they hatch their eggs, and nourish their young together, by a sort of free and natural kindliness, and with no thought of a return.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:210
verses.text: For the sparrow does not say, "I will nourish my young, that when I am grown old, they may feed me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:211
verses.text: He has no such thought; he loves and feeds them, for the love of them; displays the affection of a parent, and looks for no return.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:212
verses.text: And so, I know, I am sure, do ye love your children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:213
verses.text: "For the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:214
verses.text: Yea upon this plea it is that many of you excuse your covetousness, that ye are getting for your children, and are laying by for them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:215
verses.text: But I say, extend your love, let this love grow; for to love wives and children, is not yet that "wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:216
verses.text: Have faith to Godward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:217
verses.text: First love God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:218
verses.text: Extend yourselves out to God; and whomsoever ye shall be able, draw on to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:219
verses.text: There is thine enemy: let him be drawn to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:220
verses.text: There is a son, a wife, a servant; let them be all drawn to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:221
verses.text: There is a stranger; let him be drawn to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:222
verses.text: There is an enemy; let him be drawn to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:223
verses.text: Draw, draw on 			 thine enemy; by drawing him on he shall cease to be thine enemy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:224
verses.text: So let charity be advanced, so be it nourished, that being nourished it may be perfected; so be "the wedding garment" put on; so be the image of God, after which we were created, by this our advancing, engraven anew in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:225
verses.text: For by sin was it bruised, and worn away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:226
verses.text: How is it bruised? how worn away? When it is rubbed against the earth? And what is, "When it is rubbed against the earth"? When it is worn by earthly lusts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:227
verses.text: For 			 "though man  walketh in this image, yet is he disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:228
verses.text: Truth is looked for in God's image, not vanity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:229
verses.text: By the love of the truth then be that image, after which we were created, engraven anew, and His Own tribute rendered to our Caesar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:230
verses.text: For so ye have heard from the Lord's answer, when the Jews tempted Him, as He said, "Why tempt ye Me, ye hypocrites; show Me the tribute money," that is, the impress and superscription of the image.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:231
verses.text: Show me what ye pay, what ye get ready, what is exacted of you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:232
verses.text: And "they showed Him a denarius;" and "He asked whose image and superscription it had".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:233
verses.text: They answered, "Caesar's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:234
verses.text: So Caesar looks for his own image.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:235
verses.text: It is not Caesar's will that what he ordered to be made should be lost to him, and it is not surely God's will that what He hath made should be lost to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:236
verses.text: Caesar, my Brethren, did not make the 			 money; the masters of the mint make it; the workmen have their orders, he issues his commands to his ministers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:237
verses.text: His image was stamped upon the money; on the money was Caesar's image.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:238
verses.text: And yet he requires what others have stamped; he puts it in his treasures; he will not have it refused him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:239
verses.text: Christ's coin is man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 39:240
verses.text: In him is Christ's image, in him Christ's Name, Christ's gifts, Christ's rules of duty.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:1
verses.text: Sermon XLI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:2
verses.text: [XCI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:5
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:6
verses.text: 42, where the Lord asks the Jews whose son they said David was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:8
verses.text: When the Jews were asked (as we have just now heard out of the Gospel when it was being read), how our Lord Jesus Christ, whom David himself called his Lord was David's Son, they were not able to answer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:9
verses.text: For what they saw in the Lord, that they knew.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:10
verses.text: For He appeared to them as the Son of man; but as the Son of God He was hidden.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:11
verses.text: Hence it was, that they believed that He could be overcome, and that they derided Him as He hung upon the 			 Tree, saying, "If He be the Son of God, let Him come down from the Cross, and we will believe on Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:12
verses.text: They saw one part of what He was, they knew not the other, "For had they known Him, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:13
verses.text: Yet they knew that the Christ was to be the Son of David.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:14
verses.text: For even now they hope that He will come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:15
verses.text: They know not that He is come already, but this their ignorance is voluntary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:16
verses.text: For even if they did not acknowledge Him on the tree, they ought not to have failed to acknowledge Him on His Throne.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:17
verses.text: For in whose Name are all nations called and blessed, but in His whom they think not to have been the Christ? For this Son of David, that is, "of the seed of David according to the 			 flesh," is the Son of Abraham.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:18
verses.text: Now if it was said to Abraham, "In thy seed shall all nations be blessed;" and they see now that in our Christ are all nations blessed, why wait they for what is already come, and fear not that which is yet to come? for our Lord Jesus Christ, making use of a prophetic testimony to assert His authority, called Himself "the Stone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:19
verses.text: Yea such a stone, "that whosoever shall stumble against it shall be shaken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it shall grind him to powder".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:20
verses.text: For when this stone is stumbled against, it lieth low; by lying low, it "shaketh" him that stumbleth against it; being lifted on high, by its coming down it "grindeth" the proud "to powder".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:21
verses.text: Already therefore are the Jews "shaken" by that stumbling; it yet remains that by His Glorious Advent they should be "ground to powder" also, unless peradventure whilst they are yet alive, they acknowledge Him that they die not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:22
verses.text: For God is patient, and inviteth them day 			 by day to the Faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:23
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:24
verses.text: But when the Jews could not answer the Lord proposing a question, and asking "whose Son they said Christ was;" and they answered, "the Son of David;" He goes on with the further question put to them, "How then doth David in spirit call Him Lord, saying, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on My right hand till I make Thine enemies My footstool.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:25
verses.text: If David then," He saith, "in spirit call Him Lord, how is He his Son?" He did not say, "He is not his Son, but how is He his son?" When he saith "How," it is a word not of negation, but of enquiry; as though He should say to them, "Ye say well indeed that Christ is David's Son, but David himself doth call Him Lord; whom he then calleth Lord, how is He his Son?" Had the Jews been instructed in the Christian faith, which we hold; had they not closed their hearts against the Gospel, had they wished to have 			 spiritual life in them, they would, as instructed in the faith of the Church, have made answer to this question and said, "Because in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God and the Word was God:" see how He is David's Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:26
verses.text: But because "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us;" see how He is David's Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:27
verses.text: But as being ignorant, they were silent, nor when they shut their mouths did they open their ears, that what they could not answer when questioned, they might after instruction know.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:28
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:29
verses.text: But seeing that is a great thing to know the mystery how He is David's Son and David's Lord: how one Person is both Man and God; how in the form of Man He is less than the Father, in the form of God equal with the Father; how again He saith, on the one hand, "The Father is greater than I;" and on the other, "I and My Father are one;" seeing this is a great mystery, our conduct must be fashioned, that it may be comprehended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:30
verses.text: For to the unworthy is it closed up, it is opened to those who are meet for it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:31
verses.text: It is not with stones, or clubs, or the fist, or the heel, that we knock unto the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:32
verses.text: It is the life which knocks, it is to the life that it is opened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:33
verses.text: The seeking is with the heart, the asking is with the heart, the knocking is with the heart, the opening is to the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:34
verses.text: Now that heart which asks rightly, and knocks and seeks rightly, 			 must be godly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:35
verses.text: Must first love God for His Own sake (for this is godliness); and not propose to itself any reward which it looks for from Him other than God Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:36
verses.text: For than Him is there nothing better.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:37
verses.text: And what precious thing can he ask of God, in whose sight God Himself is lightly esteemed? He giveth earth, and thou rejoicest, thou lover of the earth, who art thyself become earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:38
verses.text: If when He giveth earthly goods, thou dost rejoice, how much more oughtest thou to rejoice when He giveth thee 			 Himself, who made heaven and earth? So then God must be loved for His own sake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:39
verses.text: For the Devil not knowing what was passing in the heart of holy Job, brought this as a great charge against him, saying, "Doth Job worship God for His Own sake".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:40
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:41
verses.text: So then if the adversary brought this charge, we ought to fear lest it be brought against us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:42
verses.text: For with a very slanderous accuser have we to deal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:43
verses.text: If he seek to invent what is not, how much more will he seek to object what really is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:44
verses.text: Nevertheless let us rejoice, that ours is such a Judge, as cannot be deceived by our accuser.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:45
verses.text: For if we had a man for our judge, the enemy might invent for him what he would.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:46
verses.text: For none is more subtle in invention than the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:47
verses.text: For he 			 it is who at this time also invents all false accusations against the saints.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:48
verses.text: He knows his accusations can have no avail with God, and so He scatters them among men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:49
verses.text: Yet what does this profit him, seeing the Apostle says, "Our glorying is this, the testimony of our conscience?" Yet think ye that he does not invent these false charges with aught of subtlety? Yes, well he knows what evil he shall work thereby, if the watchfulness of faith resist him not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:50
verses.text: For for this reason scatters he his evil charges against the good, that the weak may think that there are no good, and so may give themselves up to be hurried along, and made a prey of by their lusts, whilst they say within themselves, "For who is there that keeps the commandments of God, or who is 			 there that preserves chastity?" and whilst he thinks that no one does, he himself becomes that no one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:51
verses.text: This then is the devil's art.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:52
verses.text: But such a man was Job, that he could not invent any such charge against him; for his life was too well known and manifest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:53
verses.text: But because he had great riches, he brought that against him, which if it had any existence, might lie in the heart, and not appear in the conduct.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:54
verses.text: He worshipped God, he gave alms; and with what heart he did this none knew, no not the 			 Devil himself; but God had known.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:55
verses.text: God giveth His testimony to His own servant; the Devil calumniates the servant of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:56
verses.text: He is allowed to be tried, Job is proved, the Devil is confounded.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:57
verses.text: Job is found to worship God for His Own sake, to love Him for His Own sake; not because He gave him ought, but because He did not take away Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:58
verses.text: For he said, "The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so is it done, blessed be the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:59
verses.text: The fire of temptation approached him; but it found him gold, not stubble; it cleared away the dross from it, but did not reduce it to ashes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:60
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:61
verses.text: Because then, in order to understand the mystery of God, how Christ is both man and God, the heart must be cleansed: and it is cleansed by a good conversation, by a pure life, by chastity, and sanctity, and love, and by "faith, which worketh by love" (now all this that I am speaking of, is, as it were, the tree which hath its root in the heart; for it is only from the root of the heart that actions proceed; in which if thou plant desire, thorns spring forth; if thou plant charity, good fruit): the Lord, after that question which He had proposed to the Jews, when they were not able to answer it, immediately went on to speak of good actions, that He might show why they were unworthy to understand what He asked them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:62
verses.text: For when 			 those proud and wretched men were not able to answer, they ought of course to have said, "we do not know; Master, tell us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:63
verses.text: But no: they were speechless at the proposing of the question, and they opened not their mouth to seek instruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:64
verses.text: And so the Lord in reference to their pride said immediately, "Beware of the Scribes which love the chief seats in the synagogues, and the first rooms at feasts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:65
verses.text: Not because they hold them, but because they love them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:66
verses.text: For in these words he accused their heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:67
verses.text: Now none can accuse the heart, but He who can inspect it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:68
verses.text: For meet it is that to the servant of God, who holds some post of honour in the Church, the first place should be assigned; because if it were not given him, it were evil for him who refuses to give it; but yet it is no good to him to whom it is given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:69
verses.text: It is meet and right then that in the congregation of Christians their 			 Prelates should sit in eminent place, that by their very seat they may be distinguished, and that their office may be duly marked; yet not so that they should be puffed up for their seat; but that they should esteem it a burden, for which they are to render an account.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:70
verses.text: But who knows whether they love this, or do not love it? This is a matter of the heart, it can have no other judge but God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:71
verses.text: Now the Lord Himself warned His disciples, that they should not fall into this leaven; as He 			 calls it in another place, "Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:72
verses.text: And when they supposed that He said this to them because they had brought no bread; He answered them, "Have ye forgotten how many thousands were filled with the five loaves? Then understood they," it is said, "that He called their doctrine leaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:73
verses.text: For these present temporal good things they loved, but they neither feared the evil things eternal, nor loved the good things eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:74
verses.text: And so their hearts being closed, they could not understand what the Lord asked them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:75
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:76
verses.text: But what then has the Church of God to do, that it may be able to understand what it has first obtained grace to believe? It must make the mind capacious for receiving what shall be given it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:77
verses.text: And that this may be done, that the mind, that is, may be capacious, our Lord God suspends His promises, He has not taken them away.
