verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:78
verses.text: Therefore does He suspend them, that we may stretch out ourselves; and therefore do we stretch ourselves out, that we may grow; and therefore do we grow, that we may reach them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:79
verses.text: Behold the Apostle Paul stretching himself out unto these suspended promises: 			 "Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:80
verses.text: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do; forgetting those things which are behind, and stretching forth unto those things which are before, I press earnestly toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:81
verses.text: He was running on the earth; the prize hung suspended from heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:82
verses.text: He ran then on the earth; but in spirit he ascended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:83
verses.text: Behold him thus stretching himself out, behold him hanging forth after the suspended prize.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:84
verses.text: "I press on," he says, "for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:85
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:86
verses.text: We must journey on then, yet for this no need of anointing the feet, or looking out for beasts, or providing a vessel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:87
verses.text: Run with the heart's affection, journey on with love, ascend by charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:88
verses.text: Why seekest thou for the way? Cleave unto Christ, who by Descending and Ascending hath made Himself the Way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:89
verses.text: Dost thou wish to ascend? Hold fast to Him that ascendeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:90
verses.text: For by thine own self thou canst not rise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:91
verses.text: "For no man hath ascended up to heaven, but He that came 			 down from heaven, even the Son of Man which is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:92
verses.text: If no one ascendeth but He that descended, that is, the Son of Man, our Lord Jesus, dost thou wish to ascend also? Be then a member of Him who Only hath ascended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:93
verses.text: For He the Head, with all the members, is but One Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:94
verses.text: And since no one can ascend, but he who in His Body is made a member of Him; that is fulfilled, "that no man hath ascended, but He that descended".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:95
verses.text: For thou canst not say, "Lo, why hath Peter, for instance, ascended, why hath Paul ascended, why have the 			 Apostles ascended, if no one hath ascended, but He that descended?" The answer to this is, "What do Peter, and Paul, and the rest of the Apostles, and all the faithful, what do they hear from the Apostle? 'Now ye are the Body of Christ, and members in particular.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:96
verses.text: ' If then the Body of Christ and His members belong to One, do not thou make two of them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:97
verses.text: For He left 'father and mother, and clave to his wife, that two might be one flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:98
verses.text: ' He left His Father, in that here He did not show Himself as equal with the Father; but 'emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:99
verses.text: ' He left His mother also, the synagogue of which He was born after the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:100
verses.text: He clave to His Wife, that is, to His Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:101
verses.text: Now in the place where Christ Himself brought forward this testimony, He showed that the marriage bond might not be dissolved: 'Have ye not read,' said He, 'that God which made them at the beginning, made them male and female; and said, They twain shall be in one flesh? What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:102
verses.text: ' 			  And what is the meaning of 'They twain shall be in one flesh'? He goes on to say; 'Wherefore they are no more twain but one flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:103
verses.text: ' Thus 'no man hath ascended, but He that descended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:104
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:105
verses.text: For that ye may know, that the Bridegroom and the Bride are One according to the Flesh of Christ, not according to His Divinity (for according to His Divinity we cannot be what He is; seeing that He is the Creator, we the creature; He the Maker, we His work; He the Framer, we framed by Him; but in order that we might be one with Him in Him, He vouchsafed to be our Head, by taking of us flesh wherein to die for us); that ye may know then that this 			 whole is One Christ, He said by Isaiah, "He hath bound a mitre on me as a bridegroom, and clothed me with ornaments as a bride".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:106
verses.text: He is then at once the Bridegroom and the Bride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:107
verses.text: That is, the Bridegroom in Himself as the Head, the Bride in the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:108
verses.text: "For they twain," saith He, "shall be in one flesh; so now they are no more twain, but one flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:109
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:110
verses.text: Seeing then that we are of His members, in order that we may understand this mystery as I have said, Brethren, let us live holily, let us love God for His Own sake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:111
verses.text: Now He who showeth to us while in our pilgrimage the form of a servant, reserveth for those that reach their country the form of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:112
verses.text: With the form of a servant hath He laid down the way, with the form of God He hath prepared the home.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:113
verses.text: Seeing then that it is a hard matter for us to comprehend this, 			 but no hard matter to believe it; for Isaiah says, "Unless ye believe ye shall not understand;" let us "walk by faith as long as we are in pilgrimage from the Lord, till we come to sight where we shall see face to face".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:114
verses.text: As walking by faith, let us do good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:115
verses.text: In these good works, let there be a free love of God for His Own sake, and an active love of our neighbour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:116
verses.text: For we have nothing we can do for God; but because we have something we may do for our neighbour, we shall by our good offices to the needy, gain His favour who is the source of all abundance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:117
verses.text: Let every one then do what he can for others; let him freely bestow upon the needy of his superfluity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:118
verses.text: One has money; let him feed the poor, let him clothe the naked, let him build a church, let him do with his money all the good he can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:119
verses.text: Another has good counsel; let him guide his neighbour, let him by the light of holiness drive away the darkness of doubting.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:120
verses.text: Another has learning; let him draw out of this store of the Lord, let him minister food to his fellow-servants, 			 strengthen the faithful, recall the wandering, seek the lost, do all the good he can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:121
verses.text: Something there is, which even the poor may deal out to one another; let one lend feet to the lame, another give his own eyes to guide the blind; another visit the sick, another bury the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:122
verses.text: These are things which all may do, so that in a word it would be hard to find one who has not some means of doing good to others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 40:123
verses.text: And last of all comes that important duty which the Apostle speaks of; "Bear ye one 			 another's burdens, and so shall ye fulfil the law of Christ".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:1
verses.text: Sermon XLII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:2
verses.text: [XCII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:4
verses.text: ]  On the same words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:5
verses.text: xxii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:7
verses.text: The question which was proposed to the Jews, Christians ought to solve.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:8
verses.text: For the Lord Jesus Christ, who proposed it to the Jews, did not solve it Himself, to the Jews, I mean, He did not, but to us He hath solved it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:9
verses.text: I will put you in remembrance, Beloved, and ye will find that He hath solved it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:10
verses.text: But first consider the knot of the question.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:11
verses.text: He asked the Jews what they "thought of Christ, whose Son He was to be;" for they too look for 			 the Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:12
verses.text: They read of Him in the Prophets, they expected Him to come, when He was come they killed Him; for where they read that Christ would come, there did they read that they should kill Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:13
verses.text: But His future coming they hoped for in the Prophets; for they did not see their future crime.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:14
verses.text: He therefore so questioned them about the Christ, not as if about One who was unknown to them, or whose Name they had never heard, or whose coming they had never hoped for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:15
verses.text: For they err in that even yet 			 they hope for Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:16
verses.text: And we indeed hope for Him too; but we hope for Him as One who is to come as Judge, not to be judged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:17
verses.text: For the Holy Prophets prophesied both, that He should come first to be judged unrighteously, that He should come afterwards to judge with righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:18
verses.text: "What think ye," then, saith he, "of Christ? whose Son is He? They answered Him, The Son of David".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:19
verses.text: And this was entirely according to the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:20
verses.text: But He said, "How then doth David in spirit call Him Lord, saying, The Lord said unto My Lord, Sit Thou on My right hand, till I make Thine enemies Thy footstool.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:21
verses.text: If David then in spirit call Him Lord, how is He his Son?"  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:22
verses.text: Here then is need of a caution, lest Christ be thought to have denied that He was the Son of David.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:23
verses.text: He did not deny that He was the Son of David, but He enquired the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:24
verses.text: "Ye have said that Christ is the Son of David, I do not deny it; but David calls Him Lord; tell me how is He his Son, who is also his Lord; tell me how?" They did not tell Him, but were silent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:25
verses.text: Let us then tell by the explanation of Christ Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:26
verses.text: Where? By His Apostle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:27
verses.text: But first, whereby do we 			 prove that Christ hath Himself explained it? The Apostle says, "Would ye receive a proof of Christ who speaketh in me?" So then in the Apostle hath He vouchsafed to solve this question.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:28
verses.text: In the first place, what said Christ speaking by the Apostle to Timothy? "Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my Gospel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:29
verses.text: See, Christ is the Son of David.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:30
verses.text: How is He also David's Lord? Tell us, O Apostle: "who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:31
verses.text: Acknowledge David's Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:32
verses.text: If thou acknowledge David's Lord, our Lord, the Lord of heaven and earth, the Lord of the Angels, equal with God, in the form of God, how is He David's Son? Mark what follows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:33
verses.text: The Apostle shows thee David's Lord by saying, "Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to 			 be equal with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:34
verses.text: And how is He David's Son? "But He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men; and being found in fashion as a man, He humbled Himself, having become obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:35
verses.text: Wherefore God also hath highly exalted Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:36
verses.text: Christ "of the seed of David," the Son of David, rose again because "He emptied Himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:37
verses.text: How did He "empty Himself"? By taking that which He was not, not by losing that which He was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:38
verses.text: He "emptied Himself," He "humbled himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:39
verses.text: Though He was God, He appeared as man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:40
verses.text: He was despised as He walked on earth, He who made the heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:41
verses.text: He was despised as though a mere man, as though of no power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:42
verses.text: Yea, not despised only, but slain moreover.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:43
verses.text: He was that stone that lay 			 on the ground, the Jews stumbled against it, and were shaken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:44
verses.text: And what doth He Himself say? "Whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be shaken, but on whomsoever it shall fall, it shall grind him to powder".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:45
verses.text: First, He lay low, and they stumbled against Him; He shall come from above, and He will "grind" them that have been shaken "to powder".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:46
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:47
verses.text: Thus have ye heard that Christ is both David's Son, and David's Lord: David's Lord always, David's Son in time: David's Lord, born of the substance of His Father, David's Son, born of the Virgin Mary, conceived by the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:48
verses.text: Let us hold fast both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:49
verses.text: The one of them will be our eternal habitation, the other is our deliverance from our present exile.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:50
verses.text: For unless our Lord Jesus Christ had vouchsafed to become man, man had perished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:51
verses.text: He was made that 			 which He made, that what He made might not perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:52
verses.text: Very Man, Very God; God and man whole Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:53
verses.text: This is the Catholic faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:54
verses.text: Whoso denieth that Christ is God is a Photinian; whoso denieth that Christ is man is a Manichaean.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:55
verses.text: Whoso confesseth that Christ is God equal with the Father and very man, that He truly suffered, truly shed His blood (for the Truth would not have set us free, if He had given a false price for us); whoso confesseth both, is a Catholic.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:56
verses.text: He hath the country, he hath the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:57
verses.text: He hath the country, "In the beginning was the Word;" He hath the country, "Being in the form of God, He thought it not robbery to be equal with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:58
verses.text: He hath the way, "The Word was made flesh;" He hath the way, "He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:59
verses.text: He is the home whither we are going, He is the way whereby we go.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 41:60
verses.text: Let us by Him go unto Him, and we shall not go astray.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:1
verses.text: Sermon XLIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:2
verses.text: [XCIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:5
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:6
verses.text: 1, "then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:8
verses.text: Ye who were present yesterday remember my promise; which with the Lord's assistance is to be made good to-day, not to you only, but to the many others also who have come together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:9
verses.text: It is no easy question, who the ten virgins are, of whom five are wise, and five foolish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:10
verses.text: Nevertheless, according to the context of this passage which I have wished should be read again to you to-day, Beloved, I do not think, as far as the Lord vouchsafes to 			 give me understanding, that this parable or similitude relates to those women only who by a peculiar and more excellent sanctity are called Virgins in the Church, whom by a more usual term we are wont also to call, "The Religious;" but if I mistake not this parable relates to the whole Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:11
verses.text: But though we should understand it of those only who are called "the Religious," are they but ten? God forbid that so great a company of virgins should be reduced to so small a number! But perhaps one may say, "But what if though they be so many in outward profession, yet in truth they are so few, that scarce ten can be found!" It is not so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:12
verses.text: For if he had meant that the good virgins only should be understood by the ten, He would not have represented five foolish ones 			 among them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:13
verses.text: For if this is the number of the virgins which are called, why are the doors of the great house shut against five?  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:14
verses.text: So then let us understand, dearly Beloved, that this parable relates to us all, that is, to the whole Church together, not to the Clergy only of whom we spoke yesterday; nor to the laity only; but generally to all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:15
verses.text: Why then are the Virgins five and five? These five and five virgins are all Christian souls together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:16
verses.text: But that I may tell you what by the Lord's inspiration I think, it is not souls of every sort, but such souls as have the Catholic faith, and seem to have good works in the Church of God; and yet even of them, "five are wise, and five are foolish".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:17
verses.text: First then let us see why they are called 			 "five," and why "virgins," and then let us consider the rest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:18
verses.text: Every soul in the body is therefore denoted by the number five, because it makes use of five senses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:19
verses.text: For there is nothing of which we have perception by the body, but by the five folded gate, either by the sight, or the hearing, or the smelling, or the tasting, or the touching.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:20
verses.text: Whoso then abstaineth from unlawful seeing, unlawful hearing, unlawful smelling, unlawful tasting, and unlawful touching, by reason of his uncorruptness hath gotten the name of virgin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:21
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:22
verses.text: But if it be good to abstain from the unlawful excitements of the senses, and on that account every Christian soul has gotten the name of virgin; why are five admitted and five rejected? They are both virgins, and yet are rejected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:23
verses.text: It is not enough that they are virgins; and that they have lamps.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:24
verses.text: They are virgins, by reason of abstinence from unlawful indulgence of the senses; they have lamps, by reason of good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:25
verses.text: Of which good works the Lord saith, "Let 			 your works shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:26
verses.text: Again He saith to His disciples, "Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:27
verses.text: In the "girded loins" is virginity; in the "burning lamps" good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:28
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:29
verses.text: The title of virginity is not usually applied to married persons: yet even in them there is a virginity of faith, which produces wedded chastity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:30
verses.text: For that you may know, Holy Brethren, that every one, every soul, as touching the soul, and that uncorruptness of faith by which abstinence from things unlawful is practised, and by which good works are done, is not unsuitably called "a virgin;" the whole Church which consists of virgins, and boys, and married men 			 and married women, is by one name called a Virgin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:31
verses.text: Whence prove we this? Hear the Apostle saying, not to the religious women only but to the whole Church together; "I have espoused you to One Husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:32
verses.text: And because the devil, the corrupter of this virginity, is to be guarded against, after the Apostle had said, "I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ;" he subjoined, "But I fear, lest as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:33
verses.text: Few have virginity in the body; in the heart all ought to have it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:34
verses.text: If then abstinence from what is unlawful be good, whereby it has received the name of virginity, and good works are praiseworthy, which are signified by the lamps; why are five admitted and five rejected? If there be a virgin, and one who carries lamps, who yet is not admitted; where shall he see himself, who neither preserveth a virginity from things unlawful, and who not wishing to have good works walketh in 			 darkness?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:35
verses.text: Of these then, my Brethren, yea, of these let us the rather treat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:36
verses.text: He who will not see what is evil, he who will not hear what is evil, he that turneth away his smell from the unlawful fumes, and his taste from the unlawful food of the sacrifices, he who refuseth the embrace of another man's wife, breaketh his bread to the hungry, bringeth the stranger into his house, clotheth the naked, reconcileth the litigious, visiteth the sick, burieth the dead; he surely 			 is a virgin, surely he hath lamps.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:37
verses.text: What seek we more? Something yet I seek.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:38
verses.text: What seekest thou yet, one will say? Something yet I seek; the Holy Gospel hath set me on the search.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:39
verses.text: It hath said that even of these, virgins, and carrying lamps, some are wise and some foolish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:40
verses.text: By what do we see this? By what make the distinction? By the oil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:41
verses.text: Some great, some exceedingly great thing doth this oil signify.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:42
verses.text: Thinkest thou that it is not charity? This we say as searching out what it is; we hazard no 			 precipitate judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:43
verses.text: I will tell you why charity seems to be signified by the oil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:44
verses.text: The Apostle says, "I show unto you a way above the rest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:45
verses.text: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of Angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:46
verses.text: This, that is "charity," is "that way above the rest," which is with good reason signified by the oil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:47
verses.text: For oil swims above all liquids.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:48
verses.text: Pour in water, and pour in oil upon it, the oil will swim above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:49
verses.text: Pour in oil, pour in water upon it, the oil will swim above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:50
verses.text: If you keep the usual order, it will be uppermost; if you change the order, it will be uppermost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:51
verses.text: "Charity never falleth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:52
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:53
verses.text: What is it then, Brethren? Let us treat now of the five wise and the five foolish virgins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:54
verses.text: They wished to go to meet the Bridegroom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:55
verses.text: What is the meaning of "to go and meet the Bridegroom"? To go with the heart, to be waiting for his coming.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:56
verses.text: But he tarried.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:57
verses.text: "While he tarries, they all slept".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:58
verses.text: What is "all"? Both the foolish and the wise, "all slumbered and slept".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:59
verses.text: Think we is this sleep good? What is this sleep? Is it that at the 			 tarrying of the Bridegroom, "because iniquity aboundeth, the love of many waxeth cold"? Are we to understand this sleep so? I like it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:60
verses.text: I will tell you why.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:61
verses.text: Because among them are the wise virgins; and certainly when the Lord said, "Because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold;" He went on to say, "But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:62
verses.text: Where would ye have those wise virgins be? Are they not among those that "shall endure unto the end"? They would not be admitted within at all, Brethren, for any other reason, than because they have "endured unto the end".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:63
verses.text: No coldness of love then crept over them, in them love did not wax cold; but preserves its glow even unto the end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:64
verses.text: And because it glows even unto the end, therefore are the gates of the Bridegroom opened to them; therefore are they told to enter in, 			 as that excellent servant, "Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:65
verses.text: What then is the meaning of they "all slept"? There is another sleep which no one escapes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:66
verses.text: Remember ye not the Apostle saying, "But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep," that is, concerning them which are dead? For why are they called "they which are asleep," but because they are in their own day? Therefore "they all slept".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:67
verses.text: Thinkest thou that because one is wise, he has not therefore to die? Be the virgin foolish, or be she wise, all suffer equally the sleep of death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:68
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:69
verses.text: But men continually say to themselves, "Lo, the day of judgment is coming now, so many evils are happening, so many tribulations thicken; behold all things which the Prophets have spoken, are well-nigh fulfilled; the day of judgment is already at hand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:70
verses.text: They who speak thus, and speak in faith, go out as it were with such thoughts to "meet the Bridegroom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:71
verses.text: But, lo! war upon war, tribulation upon tribulation, earthquake upon earthquake, famine upon famine, 			 nation against nation, and still the Bridegroom comes not yet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:72
verses.text: Whilst then He is expected to come, all they who are saying, "Lo, He is coming, and the Day of Judgment will find us here," fall asleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:73
verses.text: Whilst they are saying this, they fall asleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:74
verses.text: Let each one then have an eye to this his sleep, and persevere even unto his sleep in love; let sleep find him so waiting.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:75
verses.text: For suppose that he has fallen asleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:76
verses.text: "Will not He who falls asleep afterwards rise again?" 			  Therefore "they all slept;" both of the wise and the foolish virgins in the parable, it is said, "they all slept".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:77
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:78
verses.text: "Lo, at midnight there was a cry made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:79
verses.text: What is, "at midnight"? When there is no expectation, no belief at all of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:80
verses.text: Night is put for ignorance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:81
verses.text: A man makes as it were a calculation with himself: "Lo, so many years have passed since Adam, and the six thousand years are being completed, and then immediately according to the computation of certain expositors, the Day of Judgment will come;" yet these calculations come and pass away, and still the coming of the Bridegroom is delayed, and the virgins who had 			 gone to meet him sleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:82
verses.text: And, lo, when He is not looked for, when men are saying, "The six thousand years were waited for, and, lo, they are gone by, how then shall we know when He will come?" He will come at midnight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:83
verses.text: What is, "will come at midnight"? Will come when thou art not aware.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:84
verses.text: Why will He come when thou art not aware of it? Hear the Lord Himself, "It is not for you to know the times or the seasons which the Lord hath put in His own power".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:85
verses.text: "The day of the Lord," says the Apostle, "will come as a thief in the night".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:86
verses.text: Therefore watch thou by night that thou be not surprised by the thief.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:87
verses.text: For the sleep of death—will ye, or nill ye—it will come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:88
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:89
verses.text: "But when that cry was made at midnight".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:90
verses.text: What cry was this, but that of which the Apostle says, "In the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump"? "For the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed"? And so when the cry was made at midnight, "Behold, the Bridegroom cometh;" what follows? "Then all those virgins arose".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:91
verses.text: What is, "they" all arose? "The hour will come," said the Lord Himself, "when all that are in the graves shall hear His voice, and shall come forth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:92
verses.text: Therefore at the last trumpet they all arose.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:93
verses.text: "Now those wise virgins had brought oil with them in their vessels; but the foolish brought no oil with them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:94
verses.text: What is the meaning of "brought no oil with them in their vessels"? What is "in their vessels"? In their hearts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:95
verses.text: Whence the Apostle says, "Our glorying is this, the testimony of our conscience".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:96
verses.text: There is the oil, the precious oil; this oil is of the gift of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:97
verses.text: Men can put oil into their vessels, but they cannot create the olive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:98
verses.text: See, I have oil; but didst thou create the oil? It is of the gift of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:99
verses.text: Thou hast oil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:100
verses.text: Carry it with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:101
verses.text: What is "carry it with thee"? Have it within, there please thou God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:102
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:103
verses.text: For, lo, those "foolish virgins, who brought no oil with them," wish to please men by that abstinence of theirs whereby they are called virgins, and by their good works, when they seem to carry lamps.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:104
verses.text: And if they wish to please men, and on that account do all these praiseworthy works, they do not carry oil with them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:105
verses.text: Do you then carry it with thee, carry it within where God seeth; there carry the testimony of thy conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:106
verses.text: For he who walks to 			 gain the testimony of another, does not carry oil with him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:107
verses.text: If thou abstain from things unlawful, and doest good works to be praised of men; there is no oil within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:108
verses.text: And so when men begin to leave off their praises, the lamps fail.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:109
verses.text: Observe then, Beloved, before those virgins slept, it is not said that their lamps were extinguished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:110
verses.text: The lamps of the wise virgins burned with an inward oil, with the assurance of a good conscience, with an inner glory, with an inmost charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:111
verses.text: Yet the lamps of the 			 foolish virgins burned also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:112
verses.text: Why burnt they then? Because there was yet no want of the praises of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:113
verses.text: But after that they arose, that is in the resurrection from the dead, they began to trim their lamps, that is, began to prepare to render unto God an account of their works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:114
verses.text: And because there is then no one to praise, every man is wholly employed in his own cause, there is no one then who is not thinking of himself, therefore were there none to sell them oil; so their lamps began to fail, and 			 the foolish betook themselves to the five wise, "give us of your oil, for our lamps are going out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:115
verses.text: They sought for what they had been wont to seek for, to shine that is with others' oil, to walk after others' praises.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:116
verses.text: "Give us of your oil, for our lamps are going out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:117
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:118
verses.text: But they say, "Not so, lest there be not enough for us and you, but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:119
verses.text: This was not the answer of those who give advice, but of those who mock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:120
verses.text: And why mock they? Because they were wise, because wisdom was in them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:121
verses.text: For they were not wise by ought of their own; but that wisdom was in them, of which it is written in a certain book, she shall say to those that despised her, when they have fallen upon the evils which she threatened them; "I will laugh over your destruction".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:122
verses.text: What wonder then is it, that the wise mock the foolish virgins? And what is this mocking?  12.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:123
verses.text: "Go ye to them that sell, and buy for yourselves:" ye who never were wont to live well, but because men praised you, who sold you oil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:124
verses.text: What means this, "sold you oil"? "Sold praises".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:125
verses.text: Who sell praises, but flatterers? How much better had it been for you not to have acquiesced in flatterers, and to have carried oil within, and for a good conscience-sake to have done all good works; then might ye say, "The righteous shall correct me in mercy, and reprove me, but the oil of the sinner shall not fatten 			  my head".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:126
verses.text: Rather, he says, let the righteous correct me, let the righteous reprove me, let the righteous buffet me, let the righteous correct me, than the "oil of the sinner fatten mine head".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:127
verses.text: What is the oil of the sinner, but the blandishments of the flatterer?  13.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:128
verses.text: "Go ye" then "to them that sell," this have ye been accustomed to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:129
verses.text: But we will not give to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:130
verses.text: Why? "Lest there be not enough for us and you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:131
verses.text: What is, "lest there be not enough"? This was not spoken in any lack of hope, but in a sober and godly humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:132
verses.text: For though the good man have a good conscience; how knows he, how He may judge who is deceived by no one? He hath a good conscience, no sins conceived in the heart solicit 			  him, yet, though his conscience be good, because of the daily sins of human life, he saith to God, "forgive us our debts;" seeing he hath done what comes next, "as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:133
verses.text: He hath broken his bread to the hungry from the heart, from the heart hath clothed the naked; out of that inward oil he hath done good works, and yet in that judgment even his good conscience trembleth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:134
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:135
verses.text: See then what this, "Give us oil," is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:136
verses.text: They were told "Go ye rather to them that sell".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:137
verses.text: In that ye have been used to live upon the praises of men, ye do not carry oil with you; but we can give you none; "lest there be not enough for us and you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:138
verses.text: For scarcely do we judge of ourselves, how much less can we judge of you? What is "scarcely do we judge of ourselves"? Because, "When the righteous King sitteth on the throne, who will glory that his 			 heart is pure?"  It may be thou dost not discover anything in thine own conscience; but He who seeth better, whose Divine glance penetrateth into deeper things, discovereth it may be something, He seeth it may be something, He discovereth something.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:139
verses.text: How much better mayest thou say to Him, "Enter not into judgment with Thy servant"? Yea, how much better, "Forgive us our debts"? Because it shall be also said to thee because of those torches, because of those lamps; "I was hungry, and ye gave Me meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:140
verses.text: What then? did not the foolish virgins do so too? Yea, but they did it not before Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:141
verses.text: How then did they do it? As the Lord forbiddeth, who said, "Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men to be seen of them, otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven: and when ye 			 pray, be not as the hypocrites, for they love to pray, standing in the streets, that they may be seen of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:142
verses.text: Verily I say unto you, they have received their reward".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:143
verses.text: They have bought oil, they have given the price; they have bought it, they have not been defrauded of men's praises, they have sought men's praises, and have had them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:144
verses.text: These praises of men aid them not in the judgment day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:145
verses.text: But the other virgins, how have they done? "Let your works shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:146
verses.text: He did not say, "may glorify you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:147
verses.text: For thou hast no oil of thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:148
verses.text: Boast thyself and say, I have it; but from Him, "for what hast thou that thou hast not received?" So then in this way acted the one, and in that the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:149
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:150
verses.text: Now it is no wonder, that "while they are going to buy," while they are seeking for persons by whom to be praised, and find none; while they are seeking for persons by whom to be comforted, and find none; that the door is opened, that "the Bridegroom cometh," and the Bride, the Church, glorified then with Christ, that the several members may be gathered together into their whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:151
verses.text: "And they went in with Him into the marriage, and the door was shut".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:152
verses.text: Then the foolish virgins came afterwards; but had they bought any oil, or found any from whom they might buy it? Therefore they found the doors shut; they began to knock, but too late.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:153
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:154
verses.text: It is said, and it is true, and no deceiving saying, "Knock, and it shall be opened unto you;" but now when it is the time of mercy, not when it is the time of judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:155
verses.text: For these times cannot be confounded, since the Church sings to her Lord of "mercy and judgment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:156
verses.text: It is the time of mercy; repent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:157
verses.text: Canst thou repent in the time of judgment? Thou wilt be then as those virgins, against whom the door was shut.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:158
verses.text: "Lord, Lord, open to us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:159
verses.text: What! did they not repent, that they had brought no oil with them? Yes, but what profiteth them their late repentance, when the true wisdom mocked them? Therefore "the door was shut".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:160
verses.text: And what was said to them? "I know you not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:161
verses.text: Did not He know them, who knoweth all things? What then is, "I know 			 you not?"  I refuse, I reject you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:162
verses.text: In my art I do not acknowledge you, my art knoweth not vice; now this is a marvellous thing, it doth not know vice, and it judgeth vice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:163
verses.text: It doth not know it in the practice of it; it judgeth by reproving it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:164
verses.text: Thus then, "I know you not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:165
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:166
verses.text: The five wise virgins came, and "went in".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:167
verses.text: How many are ye, my Brethren, in the profession of Christ's Name! let there be among you the five wise, but be not five such persons only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:168
verses.text: Let there be among you the five wise, belonging to this wisdom of the number five.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:169
verses.text: For the hour will come, and come when we know not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:170
verses.text: It will come at midnight, Watch ye.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:171
verses.text: Thus did the Gospel close; "Watch, for ye know neither the day nor the hour".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:172
verses.text: But if we are all to sleep, how shall we watch? Watch with the heart, watch with faith, watch with hope, watch with charity, watch with good works; and then, when thou shalt sleep in thy body, the time will come that thou shalt rise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:173
verses.text: And when thou shalt have risen, make ready the lamps.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:174
verses.text: Then shall they go out no more, then shall they be renewed with the inner oil of conscience; then shall that Bridegroom fold thee in His spiritual embrace, then shall He bring thee into His House where thou shall never sleep, where thy lamp can never be extinguished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 42:175
verses.text: But at present we are in labour, and our lamps flicker amid the winds and temptations of this life; but only let our flame burn strongly, that the wind of temptation may increase the fire, rather than put it out.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:1
verses.text: Sermon XLIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:2
verses.text: [XCIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Matt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:5
verses.text: xxv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:6
verses.text: 24, etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:7
verses.text: , where the slothful servant who would not put out the talent he had received, is condemned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:9
verses.text: My lords, my brethren, and fellow bishops have deigned to visit us and gladden us by their presence; but I know not why they are unwilling to assist me, when wearied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:10
verses.text: I have said this to you, Beloved, in their hearing, that your hearing may in a manner intercede for me with them, that when I ask them they also may discourse unto you in their turn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:11
verses.text: Let them dispense what they have received, let them vouchsafe to work rather than excuse 			 themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:12
verses.text: Be pleased, however, to hear from me, fatigued though I be and have difficulty in speaking, a few words only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:13
verses.text: For we have besides a record of God's mercies vouchsafed through a holy Martyr, which we must give willing audience to altogether.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:14
verses.text: What is it then? what shall I say unto you? Ye have heard in the Gospel both the due recompense of the good servants, and the punishment of the bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:15
verses.text: And the whole wickedness of that servant who was reprobate and severely condemned, was that he would not put out his money to use.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:16
verses.text: He kept the entire sum he had received; but the Lord looked for profit from it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:17
verses.text: God is coveteous with regard to our salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:18
verses.text: If he who did not put out to use is so condemned, what must they look for who lose what they have received? We then are the dispensers, we put out, ye receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:19
verses.text: We look 			 for profit; do ye live well.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:20
verses.text: For this is the profit in our dealings with you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:21
verses.text: But do not think that this office of putting out to use does not belong to you also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:22
verses.text: Ye cannot execute it indeed from this elevated seat, but ye can wherever ye chance to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:23
verses.text: Wherever Christ is attacked, defend Him; answer murmurers, rebuke blasphemers, from their fellowship keep yourselves apart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:24
verses.text: So do ye put out to use, if ye make gain of any.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:25
verses.text: Discharge our office in your own houses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:26
verses.text: A 			 bishop is called from hence, because he superintends, because he takes care and attends to others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:27
verses.text: To every man then, if he is the head of his own house, ought the office of the Episcopate to belong, to take care how his household believe, that none of them fall into heresy, neither wife, nor son, nor daughter, nor even his slave, because he has been bought at so great a price.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:28
verses.text: The Apostolic teaching has set the master over the slave, and put the slave under the master; 			  nevertheless Christ gave the same price for both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:29
verses.text: Do not neglect then the least of those belonging to you, look after the salvation of all your household with all vigilance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 43:30
verses.text: This if ye do, ye put out to use; ye will not be slothful servants, ye will not have to fear so horrible a condemnation.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:1
verses.text: Sermon XLV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:2
verses.text: [XCV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Mark viii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:5
verses.text: 5, etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:6
verses.text: , where the miracle of the seven loaves is related.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:8
verses.text: In expounding to you the Holy Scriptures, I as it were break bread for you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:9
verses.text: Do ye in hunger receive it, and break forth with a fulness of phrase from the heart; and ye who are rich in your banquet, be not meagre in good works and deeds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:10
verses.text: What I deal out to you is not mine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:11
verses.text: What ye eat, I eat; what ye live upon, I live upon.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:12
verses.text: We have in heaven a common store-house; for from thence comes the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:13
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:14
verses.text: The "seven loaves" signify the seven-fold operation of the Holy Spirit; the "four thousand men," the Church established on the four Gospels; "the seven baskets of fragments," the perfection of the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:15
verses.text: For by this number very constantly is perfection figured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:16
verses.text: For whence is that which is said, "seven times in a day will I praise thee"? Does a man sin who does not praise the Lord so often? What then is "seven times will I praise," but "I will never cease from praise"? For he who says "seven times," signifies all time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:17
verses.text: Whence in this world there are continual revolutions of seven days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:18
verses.text: What then is "seven times in a day will I praise Thee," but what is said in another place, "His praise shall always be in my mouth"? With reference to this perfection, John writes to seven Churches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:19
verses.text: The Apocalypse is a book of St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:20
verses.text: John the Evangelist; and he writes "to seven Churches".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:21
verses.text: Be ye hungered; own ye these baskets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:22
verses.text: For those fragments were not lost; but seeing that ye too belong to the Church, they have surely profited you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:23
verses.text: In that I explain this to you, I minister to Christ; and when ye hear peaceably, ye "sit down".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:24
verses.text: I in my body sit, but in my heart I am standing, and ministering to you in anxiety; lest peradventure, not the food, but the vessel offend any of you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:25
verses.text: Ye know the feast of God, ye have often heard it, that it is for the heart, not for the belly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:26
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:27
verses.text: Of a truth four thousand men were filled by seven loaves; what is more wonderful than this! Yet even this were not enough, had not seven baskets also been filled with the fragments that remained.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:28
verses.text: O great mysteries! they were works, and the works spake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:29
verses.text: If thou understand these doings, they are words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:30
verses.text: And ye too belong to the four thousand, because ye live under the fourfold Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:31
verses.text: To this number the children and women did not belong.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:32
verses.text: For so it is said, "And 			 they that did eat were four thousand men, excepting women and children".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:33
verses.text: As though the void of understanding, and the effeminate were without number.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:34
verses.text: Yet let even these eat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:35
verses.text: Let them eat: it may be the children will grow, and will be children no more; it may be the effeminate will be amended, and become chaste.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:36
verses.text: Let them eat; we dispense, we deal out to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:37
verses.text: But who these are, God inspecteth His feast, and if they do not amend themselves, He who knew how to invite them thither, knoweth also how to separate them from the rest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:38
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:39
verses.text: Ye know it, dearly Beloved; call to mind the parable of the Gospel, how that the Lord came in to inspect the guests at a certain feast of His.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:40
verses.text: The Master of the house who had invited them, as it is written, "found there a man which had not on a wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:41
verses.text: For to the marriage had that Bridegroom invited them who is "fair in beauty above the children of men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:42
verses.text: That Bridegroom became deformed because of His deformed spouse, that he might make her fair.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:43
verses.text: How did the Fair One become deformed? If I do not prove it, I am blaspheming.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:44
verses.text: The testimony of his fair beauty the Prophet gives me, who saith, "Thou art fair in beauty above the children of men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:45
verses.text: The testimony of his deformity another Prophet gives me, who saith, "We saw Him, and He had no grace, nor beauty; but His countenance was marred, and His whole look deformed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:46
verses.text: O Prophet, who saidst, "Thou art fair in beauty above the children of men;" thou art contradicted; another Prophet cometh out against thee, and saith, "Thou speakest falsely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:47
verses.text: We have seen Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:48
verses.text: What is this that thou sayest, 'Thou art fair in beauty above the children of men? We have seen Him, and He had no grace nor beauty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:49
verses.text: '" Are then these two Prophets at disagreement in the Corner-stone of peace? Both spake of Christ, both spake of the Cornerstone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:50
verses.text: In the corner 			 the walls unite.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:51
verses.text: If they do not unite, it is not a building, but a ruin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:52
verses.text: No, the Prophets agree, let us not leave them in strife.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:53
verses.text: Yea, rather let us understand their peace; for they know not how to strive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:54
verses.text: O Prophet, who saidst, "Thou art fair in beauty above the children of men;" where didst thou see Him? Answer me, answer where didst thou see Him? "Being in the form of God, He thought it not robbery to be equal with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:55
verses.text: There I saw Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:56
verses.text: Dost thou doubt that He who is "equal with God" is "fair in beauty above the children of men"? Thou hast answered; now let him answer who said, "We saw Him, and He had no grace, nor beauty".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:57
verses.text: Thou hast said so; tell us where didst thou see Him? He begins from the other's words; where the other ended, there he begins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:58
verses.text: Where did he end? "Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:59
verses.text: Lo, where he saw Him who was 			 "fair in beauty above the children of men;" do thou tell us,where thou sawest that "He had no grace nor beauty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:60
verses.text: But He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men, and found in fashion as a man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:61
verses.text: Of His deformity he still further says; "He humbled Himself, having become obedient unto death even the death of the cross".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:62
verses.text: Lo, where I saw Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:63
verses.text: Therefore are they both in peaceful concord, both are at peace together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:64
verses.text: What is more "fair" than God? What more "deformed" than the Crucified?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:65
verses.text: So then this Bridegroom, "fair in beauty above the children of men," became deformed that He might make His Spouse fair to whom it is said, "O thou beauteous among women," of whom it is said, "Who is this that cometh up, whitened" with the brightness of light, not the colouring of falsehood! He then who called them to the wedding, found a man who had not a wedding garment, and He said unto him, "Friend, how camest thou in hither, not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:66
verses.text: For he found not what to answer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:67
verses.text: And the Master of the house Who had invited him said, "Bind him hands and feet, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:68
verses.text: For so small a fault, so great a punishment? For great it is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:69
verses.text: It is called a small fault not to have "the wedding garment;" small, but only by those who do not understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:70
verses.text: How would He have been so incensed, how would He have so judged, to cast him, on account of the wedding garment which he had not, "bound hands and feet into outer darkness, where was weeping and gnashing of teeth," unless it had been a very grievous fault, not to have "the wedding garment"? I say 			 this; seeing ye have been invited through me; for though He invited you, He invited you by my ministry.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:71
verses.text: Ye are all at the feast, have the wedding garment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:72
verses.text: I will explain what it is, that ye may all have it, and if any one now hears me who has it not, let him, before the Master of the house comes and inspects His guests, be changed for the better, let him receive "the wedding garment," and so sit down in all assurance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:73
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:74
verses.text: For in truth, dearly Beloved, he who was cast forth from the feast, does not signify one man; far from it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:75
verses.text: They are many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:76
verses.text: And the Lord Himself who put forth this parable, the Bridegroom Himself, who calleth together to the feast, and quickeneth whom He calleth, He hath Himself explained to us, that that man does not denote one man, but many, there, in that very place, in the same parable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:77
verses.text: I do not go far for this, I find the explanation there, there I break the 			 bread, and set it before you to be eaten.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:78
verses.text: For He said, when he who had not "the wedding garment was cast out thence into outer darkness," He said and added immediately, "for many are called, but few chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:79
verses.text: Thou hast cast forth one man from hence, and Thou sayest, "for many are called, but few chosen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:80
verses.text: Without doubt the chosen are not cast forth; and they were the few guests who remained; and the "many" were represented in that one, because that one who hath not "the wedding garment" is the body of the wicked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:81
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:82
verses.text: What is "the wedding garment"? Let us search for it in the Holy Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:83
verses.text: What is "the wedding garment"? Without doubt it is something which the bad and good have not in common; let us discover this, and we shall discover "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:84
verses.text: Among the gifts of God, what have not the good and bad in common? That we are men and not beasts, is a gift of God; but this is common to good and bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:85
verses.text: That the light from heaven rises upon us, that the rain descends from the cloud, the fountains flow, the fields yield their fruit; these are gifts, but common to the good and bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:86
verses.text: Let us go to the marriage feast, let us leave the others without, who being called come not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:87
verses.text: Let us consider the guests themselves, that is, Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:88
verses.text: Baptism is a gift of God, the good 			 and bad have it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:89
verses.text: The Sacraments of the Altar the good and bad receive together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:90
verses.text: Saul prophesied for all his wickedness, and in his rage against a holy and most righteous man, even while he was persecuting him, he prophesied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:91
verses.text: Are the good only said to believe? "The devils also believe and tremble".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:92
verses.text: What shall I do? I have sifted all, and have not yet come to "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:93
verses.text: I have unfolded my envelopings, I have considered all, or almost all, and have not yet come to that garment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:94
verses.text: The Apostle Paul in a certain place has brought me a great collection of excellent things; he has laid them open before me, and I have said to him, "Show me, if so be thou hast found among them that 'wedding garment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:95
verses.text: '" He begins to unfold them one by one, and to say, "Though I speak with the tongues of men and of Angels, though I have all knowledge, and the gift of prophecy, and all faith, so that I could remove mountains; though I distribute all my goods to the poor, and give my body to be burned".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:96
verses.text: Precious garments! nevertheless, there is not yet here that "wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:97
verses.text: Now bring out to us "the wedding garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:98
verses.text: Why dost thou keep us in suspense, O Apostle? Peradventure prophecy is a gift of God which both good and bad have not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:99
verses.text: "If," says He, "I have not charity, nothing profiteth me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:100
verses.text: See "the wedding garment;" put it on, ye guests, that ye may sit down securely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:101
verses.text: Do not say; "we are too poor to have that garment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:102
verses.text: Clothe others, and ye are 			 clothed yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:103
verses.text: It is winter, clothe the naked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:104
verses.text: Christ is naked; and He will give you that "wedding garment" whosoever have it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:105
verses.text: Run to Him, beseech Him; He knoweth how to sanctify His faithful ones, He knoweth how to clothe His naked ones.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:106
verses.text: That ye may be able as having "the wedding garment" to be free from the fear of the outer darkness, and the binding of your members and hands and feet; let not your works fail.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:107
verses.text: If they fail, with hands bound what canst thou do? with feet 			 bound, whither wilt thou fly? Keep then that "wedding garment," put it on, and so sit down in security, when He comes to inspect.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 44:108
verses.text: The Day of Judgment will come; He is now giving a long space, let him who erewhile was naked now be clothed.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:1
verses.text: Sermon XLVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:2
verses.text: [XCVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Mark viii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:5
verses.text: 34 , "If any man would come after me, let him deny himself," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:6
verses.text: And on the words 1 John ii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:7
verses.text: 15 , "if any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:9
verses.text: Hard and grievous does that appear which the Lord hath enjoined, that "whosoever will come after Him, must deny himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:10
verses.text: But what He enjoineth is not hard or grievous, who aideth us that what He enjoineth may be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:11
verses.text: For both is that true which is said to Him in the Psalm, "Because of the words of Thy lips I have kept hard ways".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:12
verses.text: And that is true which He said Himself, "My yoke is easy, and My burden is light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:13
verses.text: For whatsoever is hard in what is enjoined us, charity makes easy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:14
verses.text: We know what great things love itself can do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:15
verses.text: Very often is this love even abominable and impure; but how great hardships have men suffered, what indignities and intolerable things have they endured, to attain to the object of their love? whether it be a lover of money who is called covetous; or a lover of honour, who is called ambitious; or a lover of beautiful women, who is called voluptuous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:16
verses.text: And who could 			 enumerate all sorts of loves? Yet consider what labour all lovers undergo, and are not conscious of their labours; and then does any such one most feel labour, when he is hindered from labour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:17
verses.text: Since then the majority of men are such as their loves are, and that there ought to be no other care for the regulation of our lives, than the choice of that which we ought to love; why dost thou wonder, if he who loves Christ, and who wishes to follow Christ, for the love of Him denies himself? For if by 			 loving himself man is lost, surely by denying himself he is found.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:18
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:19
verses.text: The first destruction of man, was the love of himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:20
verses.text: For if he had not loved himself, if he had preferred God to himself, he would have been willing to be ever subject unto God; and would not have been turned to the neglect of His will, and the doing his own will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:21
verses.text: For this is to love one's self, to wish to do one's own will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:22
verses.text: Prefer to this God's will; learn to love thyself by not loving thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:23
