verses.text: For that ye may know that it is a vice to love one's self, 			 the Apostle speaks thus, "For men shall be lovers of their own selves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:24
verses.text: And can he who loves himself have any sure trust in himself? No; for he begins to love himself by forsaking God, and is driven away from himself to love those things which are beyond himself; to such a degree that when the aforesaid Apostle had said," Men shall be lovers of their own selves," he subjoined immediately, "lovers of money".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:25
verses.text: Already thou seest that thou art without.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:26
verses.text: Thou hast begun to love thyself: stand in thyself if thou canst.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:27
verses.text: Why goest thou without? Hast thou, as being rich in money, become a lover of money? Thou hast begun to love what is without thee, thou hast lost thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:28
verses.text: When a man's love then goes even away from himself to those things which are without, he begins to share the vanity of his vain desires, and prodigal as it were to spend his strength.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:29
verses.text: He is dissipated, exhausted, without resource or strength, he feeds swine; and wearied with this office of feeding swine, he at last remembers what he was, and 			 says, "How many hired servants of my Father's are eating bread, and I here perish with hunger!" But when the son in the parable says this, what is said of him, who had squandered all he had on harlots, who wished to have in his own power what was being well kept for him with his father; he wished to have it at his own disposal, he squandered all, he was reduced to indigence: what is said of him? "And when he returned to himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:30
verses.text: If "he returned to himself," he had gone away from himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:31
verses.text: Because he had fallen from himself, had gone away from himself, he returns 			 first to himself, that he may return to that state from which he had fallen away by falling from himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:32
verses.text: For as by falling away from himself, he remained in himself; so by returning to himself, he ought not to remain in himself, lest he again go away from himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:33
verses.text: Returning then to himself, that he might not remain in himself, what did he say? "I will arise and go to my Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:34
verses.text: See, whence he had fallen away from himself, he had fallen away from his Father; he had fallen away from himself, he had gone away from himself to those things which are without.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:35
verses.text: He returns to himself, and goes to his Father, where he may keep himself in all security.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:36
verses.text: If then he had gone away from himself, let him also in returning to himself, from whom he had gone away, that he may "go to his Father," deny himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:37
verses.text: What is "deny himself"? Let him not trust in himself, 			 let him feel that he is a man, and have respect to the words of the prophet, "Cursed is every one that putteth his hope in man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:38
verses.text: Let him withdraw himself from himself, but not towards things below.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:39
verses.text: Let him withdraw himself from himself, that he may cleave unto God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:40
verses.text: Whatever of good he has, let him commit to Him by whom he was made; whatever of evil he has, he has made it for himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:41
verses.text: The evil that is in him God made not; let him destroy what himself has done, who has been thereby undone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:42
verses.text: "Let him deny himself," He saith, "and take up his cross, and follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:43
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:44
verses.text: And whither must the Lord be followed? Whither He is gone, we know; but a very few days since we celebrated the solemn memorial of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:45
verses.text: For He has risen again, and ascended into heaven; thither must He be followed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:46
verses.text: Undoubtedly we must not despair of it, because He hath Himself promised us, not because man can do anything.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:47
verses.text: Heaven was far away from us, before that our Head had gone into heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:48
verses.text: But now why should we despair, if we are members of that Head? Thither 			 then must He be followed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:49
verses.text: And who would be unwilling to follow Him to such an abode? Especially seeing that we are in so great travail on earth with fears and pains.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:50
verses.text: Who would be unwilling to follow Christ thither, where is supreme felicity, supreme peace, perpetual security? Good is it to follow Him thither: but we must see by what way we are to follow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:51
verses.text: For the Lord Jesus did not say the words we are engaged in, when He had now risen from the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:52
verses.text: He had not yet suffered, He had still to come 			 to the Cross, had to come to His dishonouring, to the outrages, the scourging, the thorns, the wounds, the mockeries, the insults, Death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:53
verses.text: Rough as it were is the way; it makes thee to be slow; thou hast no mind to follow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:54
verses.text: But follow on.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:55
verses.text: Rough is the way which man has made for himself, but what Christ hath trodden in His passage is worn smooth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:56
verses.text: For who would not wish to go to exaltation? Elevation is pleasing to all; but humility is the step to it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:57
verses.text: Why dost thou put out thy foot beyond thee? 			 Thou hast a mind to fall, not to ascend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:58
verses.text: Begin by the step, and so thou hast ascended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:59
verses.text: This step of humility those two disciples were loth to have an eye to, who said, "Lord, bid that one of us may sit at Thy right hand, and the other at the left in Thy kingdom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:60
verses.text: They sought for exaltation, they did not see the step.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:61
verses.text: But the Lord showed them the step.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:62
verses.text: For what did He answer them? "Ye who seek the hill of exaltation, can ye drink the cup of humiliation?" And therefore He does not say simply, "Let him deny himself, and follow Me" howsoever: but He said more, "Let him take up his cross, and follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:63
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:64
verses.text: What is, "Let him take up his cross"? Let him bear whatever trouble he has; so let him follow Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:65
verses.text: For when he shall begin to follow Me in conformity to My life and precepts, he will have many to contradict him, he will have many to hinder him, he will have many to dissuade him, and that from among those who are even as it were Christ's companions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:66
verses.text: They who hindered the blind men from crying out were walking with Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:67
verses.text: Whether therefore they be threats or caresses, or whatsoever hindrances there be, if thou wish to follow, turn them into thy cross, bear it, carry it, do not give way beneath it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:68
verses.text: There seems to be an exhortation to martyrdom in these words of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:69
verses.text: If there be persecution, ought not all things to be despised in consideration of Christ? The world is loved; but let Him be preferred by whom the world was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:70
verses.text: Great is the world; but greater is He by 			 whom the world was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:71
verses.text: Fair is the world; but fairer is He by whom the world was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:72
verses.text: Sweet is the world; but sweeter is He by whom the world was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:73
verses.text: Evil is the world; and good is He by whom the world was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:74
verses.text: How shall I be able to explain and unravel what I have said? May God help me? For what have I said? what have ye applauded? See, it is but a question, and yet ye have already applauded.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:75
verses.text: How is the world evil, if He by whom the world was made is good? Did not God make all things, 			 "and behold they were very good"? Does not Scripture at each several work of creation testify that God made it good, by saying, "And God saw that it was good," and at the end summed them all up together thus how that God had made them, "And behold they were very good"?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:76
verses.text: How then is the world evil, and He good by whom the world was made? How? "Since the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:77
verses.text: The world was made by Him, the heaven and earth and all things that are in them: "the world knew Him not," the lovers of the world; the lovers of the world and the despisers of God; this "world knew Him not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:78
verses.text: So then the world is evil, because they are evil who prefer the world to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:79
verses.text: And He is good who made the world, the heaven, and earth, and sea, and themselves who love the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:80
verses.text: For this only, that they love the world and do not love God, He made not in them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:81
verses.text: But themselves, all that appertains to their nature He made; what appertains to guiltiness, He made not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:82
verses.text: This is that I said a little while ago, "Let man efface what he has made, and so will he be well-pleasing to Him who made Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:84
verses.text: For there is among men themselves a good world also; but one that has been made good from being evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:85
verses.text: For the whole world if you take the word "world" for men, putting aside (what we call the world) the heaven and earth and all things that in them are; if you take the world for men, the whole world did he who first sinned make evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:86
verses.text: The whole mass was corrupted in the root.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:87
verses.text: God made man good; so runs the Scripture, "God made man upright; and men themselves 			 found out many cogitations".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:88
verses.text: Run from these "many" to One, gather up thy scattered things into one: flow on together, fence thyself in, abide with One; go not to many things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:89
verses.text: There is blessedness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:90
verses.text: But we have flowed away, have gone on to perdition: we were all born with sin, and to that sin wherein we were born have we too added by our evil living, and the whole world has become evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:91
verses.text: But Christ came, and He chose that which He made, not what He found; for He found all evil, and by His grace He made 			 them good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:92
verses.text: And so was made another "world;" and the "world" now persecutes the "world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:93
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:94
verses.text: What is the "world" which persecutes? That of which it is said to us, "Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:95
verses.text: If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:96
verses.text: For all that is in the world, is the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, which is not of the Father, but of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:97
verses.text: And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever," 			  even as God abideth for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:98
verses.text: Lo! I have spoken of two "worlds," the "world" which persecutes, and that which it persecutes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:99
verses.text: What is the "world" which persecutes? "All that is the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, which is not of the Father, but of the world;" and "the world passeth away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:100
verses.text: Lo, this is the "world" which persecutes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:101
verses.text: What is the "world" which it persecutes? "He that doeth the will of God 			 abideth for ever," even as God abideth for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:102
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:103
verses.text: But see, that which persecutes is called the "world;" let us prove whether that also which suffers persecution is called "the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:104
verses.text: What! Art thou deaf to the voice of Christ who speaketh, or rather to Holy Scripture which testifieth, "God was in Christ reconciling the world unto Himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:105
verses.text: "If the world hate you, know ye that it first hated Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:106
verses.text: See, the "world" hates.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:107
verses.text: What does it hate but the "world"? What "world"? "God was in Christ reconciling the world unto Himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:108
verses.text: The condemned "world" persecutes; the reconciled "world" suffers persecution.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:109
verses.text: The condemned "world" is all that is without the Church; the reconciled "world" is the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:110
verses.text: For He says, "The Son of Man came not to judge the world, but that the world through Him may be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:111
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:112
verses.text: Now in this world, holy, good, reconciled, saved, or rather to be saved, and now saved in hope, "for we are saved in hope;" in this world, I say, that is in the Church which wholly follows Christ, He hath said as of universal application, "Whosoever will follow Me, let him deny himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:113
verses.text: For it is not that the virgins ought to give ear to this, and the married women ought not; or that the widows ought, and the women who still have their husbands ought not; or that monks ought, and the married men ought not; or that the clergy ought, and the laymen ought not: but let the 			 whole Church, the whole body, all the members, distinguished and distributed throughout their several offices, follow Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:114
verses.text: Let the whole Church follow Him, that only Church, let the dove follow Him, let the spouse follow Him, let her who has been redeemed and endowed with the Bridegroom's blood, follow Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:115
verses.text: There virgin purity hath its place; there widowed continence hath its place; married chastity there hath its place; but adultery hath no place of its own there; and no place there hath 			 lasciviousness, unlawful and meet for punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:116
verses.text: But let these several members which have their place there, in their kind and place and measure, "follow Christ;" let them "deny themselves;" that is, let them presume nothing of themselves: let them "take up their cross," that is, let them in the world endure for Christ's sake whatever the world may bring upon them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:117
verses.text: Let them love Him, who Alone doth not deceive, who Alone is not deceived, Alone deceiveth not; let them love Him, 			 for that is true which He doth promise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:118
verses.text: But because He doth not give at once, faith wavers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:119
verses.text: Hold on, persevere, endure, bear delay and thou hast borne the cross.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:120
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:121
verses.text: Let not the virgin say, "I shall alone be there".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:122
verses.text: For Mary shall not be there alone but the widow Anna shall be there also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:123
verses.text: Let not the woman which hath an husband say, "The widow will be there, not I;" for it is not that Anna will be there, and Susanna not be there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:124
verses.text: But by all means let them who would be there prove themselves hereby, that they who have here a lower place envy not, but love in others the better place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:125
verses.text: For, for instance, my Brethren, 			 that ye may understand me; one man has chosen a married life, another a life of continence; if he who has chosen the married life, has adulterous lusts, he has "looked back;" he has lusted after that which is unlawful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:126
verses.text: He too who would wish afterwards to return from continence to a married life, has "looked back;" he has chosen what is in itself lawful, yet he has "looked back".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:127
verses.text: Is marriage then to be condemned? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:128
verses.text: Marriage is not to be condemned; but see whither he had come who 			 has chosen it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:129
verses.text: He had already got before it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:130
verses.text: When he was living as a young man in voluptuousness, marriage was before him; he was making his way towards it; but when he had chosen continence, marriage was behind him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:131
verses.text: "Remember," saith the Lord, "Lot's wife".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:132
verses.text: Lot's wife, by looking behind, remained motionless.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:133
verses.text: To whatever point then any one has been able to reach, let him fear to "look back" from thence; and let him walk in the way, let him "follow Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:134
verses.text: "Forgetting those things which are behind, and stretching forth unto those things which are before, let him by an earnest inward intention press on toward the prize of the calling of God in Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 45:135
verses.text: Let those that are married regard the unmarried as above themselves; let them acknowledge that they are better; let them in them love what themselves have not; and let them in them love Christ.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:1
verses.text: Sermon XLVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:2
verses.text: [XCVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Mark xiii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:5
verses.text: 32, "But of that day or that hour knoweth no one, not even the angels in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:7
verses.text: The advice, Brethren, which ye have just heard Scripture give, when it tells us to watch for the last day, every one should think of as concerning his own last day; lest haply when ye judge or think the last day of the world to be far distant, ye slumber with respect to your own last day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:8
verses.text: Ye have heard what Jesus said concerning the last day of this world, "That neither the Angels of heaven, nor the Son knew it, but the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:9
verses.text: Where indeed there is a great difficulty, lest understanding this in a carnal way, we think that the Father knoweth anything which the Son knoweth not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:10
verses.text: For indeed when He said, "the Father knoweth it;" He said this because in the Father the Son also knoweth it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:11
verses.text: For what is there in a day which was not made by the Word, by whom the day was made? Let no one then search out for the last Day, when it is to be; but let us watch all by our good lives, lest the last day of any 			 one of us find us unprepared, and such as any one shall depart hence on his last day, such he be found in the last day of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:12
verses.text: Nothing will then assist thee which thou shalt not have done here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:13
verses.text: His own works will succour, or his own works will overwhelm every one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:14
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:15
verses.text: And how have we in the Psalm sung unto the Lord, "Lord, have mercy on me, for man hath trodden me down"? He is called a man who lives after the manner of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:16
verses.text: For it is said to them who live after God, "Ye are gods, and ye are all the children of the Most High".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:17
verses.text: But to the reprobate, who were called to be the sons of God, and who wished rather to be men, that is, to live after the manner of men, he says, "But ye shall die like men, and fall as one of the princes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:18
verses.text: For that man is mortal, ought to avail for his instruction, not for boasting.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:19
verses.text: Whereupon does a worm that is to die on the morrow boast himself? I speak to your love, Brethren; proud mortals ought to be made blush by the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:20
verses.text: For he, though proud, is yet immortal; he is a spirit, though a malignant one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:21
verses.text: The last day is kept in store for him at the end as his punishment; nevertheless he is not subject to the death to which we are subject.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:22
verses.text: But man heard the sentence, "Thou 			 shalt surely die".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:23
verses.text: Let him make a good use of his punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:24
verses.text: What is that I have said, "Let him make a good use of his punishment"? Let him not by that from which he received his punishment fall into pride; let him acknowledge that he is mortal, and let it break down his elation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:25
verses.text: Let him hear it said to him, "Why is earth and ashes proud?" Even if the devil is proud, he is not "earth and ashes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:26
verses.text: Therefore was it said, "But ye shall die like men, and shall fall as one of the princes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:27
verses.text: Ye do not consider that ye are mortals, and ye are proud as the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:28
verses.text: Let man then make a good use of his punishment, Brethren; let him make a good use of his evil, that he may make advancement to his good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:29
verses.text: Who does not know, that the necessity of our dying is a punishment; and the more grievous, that we know not when? The punishment is certain, the hour uncertain; and of that punishment alone are we certain in the ordinary course of human affairs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:31
verses.text: All else of ours, both good and evil, is uncertain; death alone is certain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:32
verses.text: What is this that I say? A child is conceived, perhaps it will be born, perhaps it will be an untimely birth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:33
verses.text: So it is uncertain: Perhaps he will grow up, perhaps he will not grow up; perhaps he will grow old, perhaps he will not grow old; perhaps he will be rich, perhaps poor; perhaps he will be distinguished, perhaps abased; perhaps he will have children, perhaps he will not; perhaps he 			 will marry, perhaps not; and so on, whatever else among good things you may name.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:34
verses.text: Now look too at the evils of life: Perhaps he will have sickness, perhaps he will have not; perhaps he will be stung by a serpent, perhaps not; perhap he will be devoured by a wild beast, perhaps he will not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:35
verses.text: And so look at all evils; everywhere is there a "perhaps it will be," and "perhaps it will not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:36
verses.text: But canst thou say, "Perhaps he will die," and "perhaps he will not die"? 			  As when medical men examine an illness, and ascertain that it is fatal, they make this announcement; "He will die, he will not get over this".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:37
verses.text: So from the moment of a man's birth, it may be said, "He will not get over this".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:38
verses.text: When he is born he begins to be ailing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:39
verses.text: When he dies, he ends indeed this ailment: but he knows not whether he does not fall into a worse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:40
verses.text: The rich man in the Gospel had ended his voluptuous ailment, he came to a tormenting one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:41
verses.text: But the poor man 			 ended his ailment, and arrived at perfect health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:42
verses.text: But he made choice in this life of what he was to have hereafter; and what he reaped there, he sowed here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:43
verses.text: Therefore while we live we ought to watch, and to make choice of that which we may possess in the world to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:44
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:45
verses.text: Let us not love the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:46
verses.text: It overwhelms its lovers, it conducts them to no good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:47
verses.text: We must rather labour in it that it seduce us not, than fear lest it should fall.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:48
verses.text: Lo, the world falleth; the Christian standeth firm; because Christ doth not fall.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:49
verses.text: For wherefore saith the Lord, "Rejoice, for that I have overcome the world"? We might answer Him if we pleased, "'Rejoice,' yes do Thou rejoice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:50
verses.text: If Thou 'hast overcome,' do thou rejoice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:51
verses.text: Why should we?" Why doth He say to us, "Rejoice;" but because it is for us that He hath overcome, for us hath fought? For wherein fought He? In that He took man's nature upon Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:52
verses.text: Take away His birth of a virgin, take away that He emptied Himself, "taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men, and found in fashion as a man;" 			  take away this, and where is the combat, where the contest? where the trial? where the victory, which no battle has preceded? "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:53
verses.text: All things were made by Him, and without Him was nothing made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:54
verses.text: Could the Jews have crucified this Word? Could those impious men have mocked this Word? Could this Word have been buffeted? Could this Word have been crowned with thorns? But that He might suffer all this, "the Word was made flesh;" and after He had suffered all this, by rising again He "overcame".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:55
verses.text: So then He hath "overcome" for us, to whom He hath shown the assurance of His resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:56
verses.text: Thou sayest then to God, "Have mercy upon me, O Lord, for man hath trodden me down".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:57
verses.text: Do not "tread down" thyself, and man will not overcome thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:58
verses.text: For, lo, some powerful man alarms thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:59
verses.text: By what does he alarm thee? "I will spoil thee, will condemn, will torture, will kill thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:60
verses.text: And thou criest, "Have mercy upon me, O Lord, for man hath trodden me down".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:61
verses.text: If thou say the truth, and mark thyself well, one dead "treads thee down," because thou art afraid of the threats of a man; and man "treads thee down," because thou wouldest not be afraid, 			 unless thou wert a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:62
verses.text: What is the remedy then? O man, cleave to God, by whom thou wast made a man; cleave fast to Him, put thy affiance in Him, call upon Him, let Him be thy strength.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:63
verses.text: Say to Him, "In Thee, O Lord, is my strength".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 46:64
verses.text: And then thou shalt sing at the threatenings of men; and what thou shalt sing hereafter, the Lord Himself telleth thee, "I will hope in God, I will not fear what man can do unto me".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:1
verses.text: Sermon XLVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:2
verses.text: [XCVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke vii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:5
verses.text: 2, etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:6
verses.text: ; on the three dead persons whom the Lord raised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:8
verses.text: The miracles of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ make indeed an impression on all who hear of, and believe them; but on different men in different ways.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:9
verses.text: For some amazed at His miracles done on the bodies of men, have no knowledge to discern the greater; whereas some admire the more ample fulfilment in the souls of men at the present time of those things which they hear of as having been wrought on their bodies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:10
verses.text: The Lord Himself saith, 			 "For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom He will".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:11
verses.text: Not of course that the Son "quickeneth" some, the Father others; but the Father and the Son "quicken" the same; for the Father doeth all things by the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:12
verses.text: Let no one then who is a Christian doubt, that even at the present time the dead are raised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:13
verses.text: Now all men have eyes, wherewith they can see the dead rise again in such sort, as the son of that widow rose, of whom we have just read out of the Gospel; but those eyes wherewith men see the dead in heart rise again, all men have not, save those who have risen already in heart themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:14
verses.text: It is a greater miracle to raise again one who is to live for ever, than to raise one who must die again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:16
verses.text: The widowed mother rejoiced at the raising again of that young man; of men raised again in spirit day by day does Mother Church rejoice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:17
verses.text: He indeed was dead in the body but they in soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:18
verses.text: His visible death was bewailed visibly; their death invisible was neither enquired into nor perceived.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:19
verses.text: He sought them out who had known them to be dead; He Alone knew them to be dead, who was able to make them alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:20
verses.text: For if the Lord had not come to raise the dead, the Apostle 			 would not have said, "Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:21
verses.text: You hear of one asleep in the words, "Rise, thou that sleepest;" but understand it of one dead when you hear, "And arise from the dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:22
verses.text: Thus they who are even dead in the body are often said to be asleep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:23
verses.text: And certainly they all are but asleep, in respect of Him who is able to awaken them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:24
verses.text: For in respect of thee, a dead man is dead indeed, seeing he will not awake, beat or prick or tear him as thou wilt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:25
verses.text: But in respect of Christ, he was but asleep to whom it was said, "Arise," and he arose forthwith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:26
verses.text: No one can as easily awaken another in bed, as Christ can in the tomb.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:27
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:28
verses.text: Now we find that three dead persons were raised by the Lord "visibly," thousands "invisibly".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:29
verses.text: Nay, who knows even how many dead He raised visibly? For all the things that He did are not written.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:30
verses.text: John tells us this, "Many other things Jesus did, the which if they should be written, I suppose that the whole world could not contain the books".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:31
verses.text: So then there were without doubt many others raised: but it is not without a meaning that the three are expressly recorded.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:32
verses.text: For our Lord Jesus Christ would that those things which He did on the body should be also spiritually understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:33
verses.text: For He did not merely do miracles for the miracles' sake; but in order that the things which He did should inspire wonder in those who saw them, and convey truth to them who understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:34
verses.text: As he who sees letters in an excellently written 			 manuscript, and knows not how to read, praises indeed the transcriber's hand, and admires the beauty of the characters; but what those characters mean or signify he does not know; and by the sight of his eyes he is a praiser of the work, but in his mind has no comprehension of it; whereas another man both praises the work, and is capable of understanding it; such an one, I mean, who is not only able to see what is common to all, but who can read also; which he who has never learned cannot.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:35
verses.text: So they who saw Christ's miracles, and understood not what they meant, and what they in a manner 			 conveyed to those who had understanding, wondered only at the miracles themselves; whereas others both wondered at the miracles, and attained to the meaning of them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:36
verses.text: Such ought we to be in the school of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:37
verses.text: For he who says that Christ only worked miracles, for the miracles' sake, may say too that He was ignorant that it was not the time for fruit, when He sought figs upon the fig-tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:38
verses.text: For it was not the time for that fruit, as the Evangelist testifies; and yet being hungry He sought for fruit upon the tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:39
verses.text: Did not Christ know, what any peasant knew? What the dresser of the tree knew, did not the tree's Creator know? So then when being hungry He sought fruit on the tree, He signified that He was hungry, and seeking after something else than this; and He found that tree without fruit, but full of leaves, and He cursed it, and it 			 withered away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:40
verses.text: What had the tree done in not bearing fruit? What fault of the tree was its fruitlessness? No; but there are those who through their own will are not able to yield fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:41
verses.text: And barrenness is "their" fault, whose fruitfulness is their will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:42
verses.text: The Jews then who had the words of the Law, and had not the deeds, were full of leaves, and bare no fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:43
verses.text: This have I said to persuade you, that our Lord Jesus Christ performed miracles with this view, that by those miracles He might signify 			 something further, that besides that they were wonderful and great, and divine in themselves, we might learn also something from them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:44
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:45
verses.text: Let us then see what He would have us learn in those three dead persons whom He raised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:46
verses.text: He raised again the dead daughter of the ruler of the synagogue, for whom when she was sick petition was made to Him, that He would deliver her from her sickness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:47
verses.text: And as He is going, it is announced that she is dead; and as though He would now be only wearying Himself in vain, word was brought to her father, "Thy daughter is dead, why weariest thou the Master any further?" 			  But He went on, and said to the father of the damsel, "Be not afraid, only believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:48
verses.text: He comes to the house, and finds the customary funeral obsequies already prepared, and He says to them, "Weep not, for the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:49
verses.text: He spake the truth; she was asleep; asleep, that is, in respect of Him, by whom she could be awakened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:50
verses.text: So awakening her, He restored her alive to her parents.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:51
verses.text: So again He awakened that young man, the widow's son, by whose case I have been now reminded to speak with you, Beloved, on this subject, as He Himself shall vouchsafe to give me power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:52
verses.text: Ye have just heard how he was awakened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:53
verses.text: The Lord "came nigh to the city; and behold there was a dead man being carried out" already beyond the gate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:54
verses.text: Moved with compassion, for that the mother, a widow and bereaved of her only son, was weeping, He did what ye have heard, saying, "Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:55
verses.text: He that was dead arose, and 			 began to speak, and He restored him to his mother".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:56
verses.text: He awakened Lazarus likewise from the tomb.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:57
verses.text: And in that case when the disciples with whom He was speaking knew that he was sick, He said (now "Jesus loved him"), "Our friend Lazarus sleepeth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:58
verses.text: They thinking of the sick man's healthful sleep; say, "Lord, if he sleep he is well".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:59
verses.text: "Then said Jesus," speaking now more plainly, I tell you, "our friend Lazarus is dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:60
verses.text: And in both He said the truth; "He is dead in respect of you, he is asleep in respect of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:61
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:62
verses.text: These three kinds of dead persons, are three kinds of sinners whom even at this day Christ doth raise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:63
verses.text: For that dead daughter of the ruler of the synagogue was within in the house, she had not yet been carried out from the secresy of its walls into public view.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:64
verses.text: There within was she raised, and restored alive to her parents.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:65
verses.text: But the second was not now indeed in the house, but still not yet in the tomb, he had been carried out of the walls, but not committed to the 			 ground.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:66
verses.text: He who raised the dead maiden who was not yet carried out, raised this dead man who was now carried out, but not yet buried.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:67
verses.text: There remained a third case, that He should raise one who was also buried; and this He did in Lazarus.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:68
verses.text: There are then those who have sin inwardly in the heart, but have it not yet in overt act.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:69
verses.text: A man, for instance, is disturbed by any lust.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:70
verses.text: For the Lord Himself saith, "Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her, hath committed adultery with her already in 			 his heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:71
verses.text: He has not yet in body approached her, but in heart he has consented; he has one dead within, he has not yet carried him out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:72
verses.text: And as it often happens, as we know, as men daily experience in themselves, when they hear the word of God, as it were the Lord saying, "Arise;" the consent unto sin is condemned, they breathe again unto saving health and righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:73
verses.text: The dead man in the house arises, the heart revives in the secret of the thoughts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:74
verses.text: This resurrection of a dead 			 soul takes place within, in the retirement of the conscience, as it were within the walls of the house.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:75
verses.text: Others after consent proceed to overt act, carrying out the dead as it were, that that which was concealed in secret, may appear in public.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:76
verses.text: Are these now, who have advanced to the outward act, past hope? Was it not said to the young man in the Gospel also, "I say unto thee, Arise"? Was he not also restored to his mother? So then he too who has committed the open act, if haply admonished 			 and aroused by the word of truth, he rise again at the Voice of Christ, is restored alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:77
verses.text: Go so far he could, perish for ever he could not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:78
verses.text: But they who by doing what is evil, involve themselves even in evil habit, so that this very habit of evil suffers them not to see that it is evil, become defenders of their evil deeds; are angry when they are found fault with; to such a degree, that the men of Sodom of old said to the righteous man who reproved their abominable design, "Thou art come to 			 sojourn, not to give laws".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:79
verses.text: So powerful in that place was the habit of abominable filthiness, that profligacy now passed for righteousness, and the hinderer of it was found fault with rather than the doer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:80
verses.text: Such as these pressed down by a malignant habit, are as it were buried.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:81
verses.text: Yea, what shall I say, Brethren? In such sort buried, as was said of Lazarus, "By this time he stinketh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:82
verses.text: That heap placed upon the grave, is this stubborn force of habit, whereby the soul is pressed down, and is not suffered either to rise, or breathe again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:84
verses.text: Now it was said, "He hath been dead four days".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:85
verses.text: So in truth the soul arrives at that habit, of which I am speaking by a kind of four-fold progress.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:86
verses.text: For there is first the provocation as it were of pleasure in the heart, secondly consent, thirdly the overt act, fourthly the habit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:87
verses.text: For there are those who so entirely throw off things unlawful from their thoughts, as not even to feel any pleasure in them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:88
verses.text: There are those who do feel the pleasure, and do not consent to them; death is not yet perfected, but in a certain sort 			 begun.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:89
verses.text: To the feeling of pleasure is added consent; now at once is that condemnation incurred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:90
verses.text: After the consent, progress is made unto the open act; the act changes into a habit; and a sort of desperate condition is produced, so as that it may be said, "He hath been dead four days, by this time he stinketh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:91
verses.text: Therefore, the Lord came, to whom of course all things were easy; yet He found in that case as it were a kind of difficulty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:92
verses.text: He "groaned" in the spirit, He showed that there is need of much and loud remonstrance to raise up those who have grown hard by habit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:93
verses.text: Yet at the voice of the Lord's cry, the bands of necessity were burst asunder.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:94
verses.text: The powers of hell trembled, and Lazarus is restored alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:95
verses.text: For the Lord delivers even from evil habits those who "have been dead four days;" for this man in the Gospel, "who had been dead four days," was asleep only in respect of Christ whose will it was to raise him 			 again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:96
verses.text: But what said He? Observe the manner of his arising again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:97
verses.text: He came forth from the tomb alive, but he could not walk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:98
verses.text: And the Lord said to the disciples; "Loose him, and let him go".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:99
verses.text: "He" raised him from death, "they" loosed him from his bonds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:100
verses.text: Observe how there is something which appertaineth to the special Majesty of God who raiseth up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:101
verses.text: A man involved in an evil habit is rebuked by the word of truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:102
verses.text: How many are rebuked, and give no ear! Who is it then who deals within with him who does give ear? Who breathes life into him within? Who is it who drives away the unseen death, gives the life unseen? After rebukes, after remonstrances, are not men 			 left alone to their own thoughts, do they not begin to turn over in their minds how evil a life they are living, with how very bad a habit they are weighed down? Then displeased with themselves, they determine to change their life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:103
verses.text: Such have risen again; they to whom what they have been is displeasing have revived: but though reviving, they are not able to walk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:104
verses.text: These are the bands of their guilt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:105
verses.text: Need then there is, that whoso has returned to life should be loosed, and let go.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:106
verses.text: This office hath 			 He given to the disciples to whom He said, "Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:107
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:108
verses.text: Let us then, dearly Beloved, in such wise hear these things, that they who are alive may live; they who are dead may live again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:109
verses.text: Whether it be that as yet the sin has been conceived in the heart, and not come forth into open act; let the thought be repented of, and corrected, let the dead within the house of conscience arise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:110
verses.text: Or whether he has actually committed what he thought of; let not even thus his case be despaired of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:111
verses.text: The dead within has not arisen, let him 			 arise when "he is carried out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:112
verses.text: Let him repent him of his deed, let him at once return to life; let him not go to the depth of the grave, let him not receive the load of habit upon him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:113
verses.text: But peradventure I am now speaking to one who is already pressed down by this hard stone of his own habit, who is already laden with the weight of custom, who "has been in the grave four days already, and who stinketh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:114
verses.text: Yet let not even him despair; he is dead in the depth below, but Christ is exalted on 			 high.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:115
verses.text: He knows how by His cry to burst asunder the burdens of earth, He knows how to restore life within by Himself, and to deliver him to the disciples to be loosed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:116
verses.text: Let even such as these repent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:117
verses.text: For when Lazarus had been raised again after the four days, no foul smell remained in him when he was alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 47:118
verses.text: So then let them who are alive, still live; and let them who are dead, whosoever they be, in which kind soever of these three deaths they find themselves, see to it that they rise again at 			 once with all speed.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:1
verses.text: Sermon XLIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:2
verses.text: [XCIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke vii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:5
verses.text: 37, "And behold, a woman who was in the city, a sinner," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:6
verses.text: On the remission of sins, against the Donatists.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:8
verses.text: Since I believe that it is the will of God that I should speak to you on the subject whereof we are now reminded by the words of the Lord out of the Holy Scriptures, I will by His assistance deliver to you, Beloved, a Sermon touching the remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:9
verses.text: For when the Gospel was being read, ye gave most earnest heed, and the story was reported, and represented before the eyes of your heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:10
verses.text: For ye saw, not with 			 the body, but with the mind, the Lord Jesus Christ "sitting at meat in the Pharisee's house," and when invited by him, not disdaining to go.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:11
verses.text: Ye saw too a "woman" famous in the city, famous indeed in ill fame, "who was a sinner," without invitation force her way into the feast, where her Physician was at meat, and with an holy shamelessness seek for health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:12
verses.text: She forced her way then, as it were unseasonably as regarded the feast, but seasonably as regarded her expected blessing; for she well knew under how severe a disease she was labouring, and she knew that He 			 to whom she had come was able to make her whole; she approached then, not to the Head of the Lord, but to His Feet; and she who had walked long in evil, sought now the steps of Uprightness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:13
verses.text: First she shed tears, the heart's blood; and washed the Lord's Feet with the duty of confession.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:14
verses.text: She wiped them with her hair, she kissed, she anointed them: she spake by her silence; she uttered not a word, but she manifested her devotion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:16
verses.text: So then because she touched the Lord, in watering, kissing, washing, anointing His feet; the Pharisee who had invited the Lord Jesus Christ, seeing He was of that kind of proud men of whom the Prophet Isaiah says, "Who say, Depart far from me, touch me not, for I am clean;" thought that the Lord did not know the woman.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:17
verses.text: This he was thinking with himself, and saying in his heart, "This man if He were a prophet, would have known what woman this is that" hath approached His feet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:18
verses.text: He supposed that He did not know her, because He repelled her not, because He did not forbid her to approach Him, because He suffered Himself to be touched by her, sinner as she was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:19
verses.text: For whence knew he, that He did not know her? But what if He did know, O thou Pharisee, 			 inviter and yet derider of the Lord! Thou dost feed the Lord, yet by whom thou art to be fed thyself, thou dost not understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:20
verses.text: Whereby knowest thou, that the Lord did not know what that woman had been, save because she was permitted to approach Him, save because by His sufferance she kissed His Feet, save because she washed, save because she anointed them? For these things a woman unclean ought not to be permitted to do with the Feet that are clean? So then had such a woman approached that 			 Pharisee's feet, he would have been sure to say what Isaiah says of such; "Depart from me, touch me not, for I am clean".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:21
verses.text: But she approached the Lord in her uncleanness, that she might return clean: she approached sick, that she might return whole: she approached Him, confessing, that she might return professing Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:23
verses.text: For the Lord heard the thoughts of the Pharisee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:24
verses.text: Let now the Pharisee understand even by this, whether He was not able to see her sins, who could hear his thoughts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:25
verses.text: So then He put forth to the man a parable concerning two men, who owed to the same creditor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:26
verses.text: For He was desirous to heal the Pharisee also, that He might not eat bread at his house for nought; He hungered after him who was feeding Him, He wished to reform him, to slay, to eat him, to pass him over 			 into His Own Body; just as to that woman of Samaria, He said, "I thirst".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:27
verses.text: What is, "I thirst"? I long for thy faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:28
verses.text: Therefore are the words of the Lord in this parable spoken; and there is this double object in them, both that that inviter might be cured together with those who ate at the table with Him, who alike saw the Lord Jesus Christ, and were alike ignorant of Him, and that that woman might have the assurance her confession merited, and not be pricked any more with the stings of her conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:29
verses.text: "One," said He, "owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty; He forgave them both: which loved him most?" He to whom the parable 			 was proposed answered, what of course common reason obliged him to answer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:30
verses.text: "I suppose, Lord, he to whom he forgave most.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:31
verses.text: Then turning to the woman he said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest Me no water for My feet: she hath washed My feet with tears, and wiped them with her hairs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:32
verses.text: Thou gavest Me no kiss: this woman since the time she came in, hath not ceased to kiss My feet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:33
verses.text: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed My feet 			 with ointment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:34
verses.text: Therefore I say, her many sins are forgiven her, for she loved much.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:35
verses.text: But to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:36
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:37
verses.text: Here arises a difficulty which must in real truth be resolved, and which requires your fixed attention, Beloved, lest haply my words may not be equal to the removing and clearing of the whole obscurity of it by reason of the stress of time; especially as this flesh of mine exhausted by its heat, now longs to be recruited, and demanding its due, and clogging the eagerness of the soul gives proof of that which is said, "The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh 			 is weak".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:38
verses.text: Cause there is for fear, yea great cause for fear, lest by these words of the Lord, there steal over the minds of those who understand them not aright, who indulge their fleshly lusts, and are loth to be brought away from them into liberty, that sentiment which, even as the Apostles preached, sprung up in the tongues of slanderous men, of whom the Apostle Paul says, "And as some affirm that we say, Let us do evil that good may come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:39
verses.text: For a man may say, "If 'he to whom little is forgiven, loveth little;' and he to whom more is forgiven, loveth more; and it is better to love more, than to love less; it is right that we should sin much, and owe much which we may desire to be forgiven us, that so we may love Him the more who forgiveth us our large debts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:40
verses.text: For that woman in the Gospel who was a sinner, in the same proportion as she owed more, loved the more Him who forgave her her debts, as the Lord 			 Himself saith, 'Her many sins are forgiven her, for she loved much.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:41
verses.text: ' Now why did she love much, but because she owed much? And afterwards He added and subjoined, 'But to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:42
verses.text: ' Is it not better," he may say, "that much should be forgiven me, than less, that thereupon I may love my Lord the more"? Ye see no doubt the great depth of this difficulty; ye see it, I am sure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:43
verses.text: Ye see too my stress of time; yes, this also do ye see and 			 feel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:44
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:45
verses.text: Accept then a few words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:46
verses.text: If I shall not do justice to the magnitude of the question, lay up for a time what I shall say at present, and hold me a debtor for some future time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:47
verses.text: Suppose now two men, that by the clearer force of examples ye may think upon what I have proposed to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:48
verses.text: One of them is full of sins, has lived most wickedly for a length of time; the other of them has committed but few sins; they come both to grace, are both baptized, they enter debtors, they go out free; more has been forgiven to one, less to the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:49
verses.text: I ask, how much does each love? If I shall find 			 that he loves most, to whom the most sins have been forgiven, it is to his greater advantage that he has sinned much, his much iniquity was to his greater advantage, that so his love might not be lukewarm.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:50
verses.text: I ask the other how much he loves, I find less; for if I find that he too loves, as much as the other, to whom much has been forgiven, how shall I make answer to the words of the Lord, how shall that be true which the Truth hath said, "To whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little"? 			 "See," a man says, "but little has been forgiven me, I have not sinned much; yet I love as much as he, to whom much has been forgiven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:51
verses.text: Dost thou speak truth, or Christ? Has thy lie been forgiven thee to this end, that thou shouldest fix the charge of lying on Him who forgave thee? If little has been forgiven thee, thou lovest little.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:52
verses.text: For if but little has been forgiven thee, and thou lovest very much, thou contradictest Him who said, "To whom little is forgiven, the same loveth 			 little".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:53
verses.text: Therefore I give the more credit to Him, who knoweth thee better than thou dost know thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:54
verses.text: If thou dost suppose that but little hath been forgiven thee, it is certain that thou lovest but little.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:55
verses.text: "What then," says he, "ought I to do? Ought I to commit many sins, that there may be many which He shall be able to forgive me, that I may be able to love more?" It presses me sore, but may the Lord, who hath proposed this saying of truth to us, deliver me out of this 			 strait.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:56
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:57
verses.text: This was spoken on account of that Pharisee who thought that he had either no sins, or but few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:58
verses.text: Now unless he had had some love, he would not have invited the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:59
verses.text: But how little was it! He gave Him no kiss, not so much as water for His Feet, much less tears; he did not honour Him with any of those offices of respect, with which that woman did, who well knew what need she had of being cured, and by whom she might be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:60
verses.text: O Pharisee, therefore dost thou love 			 but little, because thou dost fondly think that but little is forgiven thee; not because little really is forgiven thee, but because thou thinkest that that which is forgiven is but little.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:61
verses.text: "What then?" he says; "Am I who have never committed murder, to be reckoned a murderer? Am I who have never been guilty of adultery, to be punished for adultery? Or are these things to be forgiven me, which I have never committed?" See: once more suppose two persons, and let us speak to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:62
verses.text: One 			 comes with supplication, a sinner covered over with thorns as a hedgehog, and timid exceedingly as a hare.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:63
verses.text: But the rock is the hedgehog's and the hare's refuge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:64
verses.text: He comes then to the Rock, he finds refuge, he receives succour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:65
verses.text: The other has not committed many sins; what shall we do for him that he may love much? what shall we persuade him? Shall we go against the words of the Lord, "To whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little"? Yes, most truly so, to whom little is really forgiven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:66
verses.text: But O thou who sayest that thou hast not committed many sins: why hast thou not? by whose guidance? God be thanked, that by your movement and 			 voice ye have made signs that ye have understood me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:67
verses.text: Now then, as I think, the difficulty has been solved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:68
verses.text: The one has committed many sins, and so is made a debtor for many; the other through God's guidance has committed but few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:69
verses.text: To Him to whom the one ascribes what He hath forgiven, does the other also ascribe what he hath not committed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:70
verses.text: Thou hast not been an adulterer in that past life of thine, which was full of ignorance, when as yet thou wast not enlightened, as yet discerned not good 			 and evil, as yet believed not on Him, who was guiding thee though thou didst not know Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:71
verses.text: Thus doth thy God speak to thee: "I was guiding thee for Myself, I was keeping thee for Myself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:72
verses.text: That thou mightest not commit adultery, no enticers were near thee; that no enticers were near thee, was My doing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:73
verses.text: Place and time were wanting; that they were wanting again, was My doing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:74
verses.text: Or enticers were nigh thee, and neither place nor time was wanting; that thou mightest not consent, it 			 was I who alarmed thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:75
verses.text: Acknowledge then His grace, to whom thou also owest it, that thou hast not committed the sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:76
verses.text: The other owes me what was done, and thou hast seen forgiven him; and thou owest to me what thou hast not done".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:77
verses.text: For there is no sin which one man commits, which another man may not commit also, if He be wanting as a Director, by whom man was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:78
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:79
verses.text: Now then seeing I have resolved this profound difficulty, as best I could in so short a space of time (or if I have not resolved it yet, let me be held, as I have already said, a debtor for the rest); let us now rather consider briefly that question of the remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:80
verses.text: Christ was supposed to be but a man both by him who invited Him, and by them who sat as guests at the table with Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:81
verses.text: But that woman who was a sinner had seen something more than this in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:82
verses.text: For why did she all those things, but that her sins might be forgiven her? She knew then that He was able to forgive sins; and they knew that no man was able to forgive them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:83
verses.text: And we must believe that they all, they who were at the table, that is, and that woman who approached to the Feet of the Lord, all knew that no man could forgive sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:84
verses.text: Forasmuch then as they all knew this; she who believed that He could forgive sins, understood Him to be more than man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:85
verses.text: So when He had said to the woman, 			 "Thy sins are forgiven thee;" they immediately said, "Who is this that forgiveth sins also?" Who is this, whom the woman who was a sinner already knew? Thou who sittest at the table as if in sound health, knowest not thy Physician; because it may be through a stronger fever thou hast even lost thy reason.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:86
verses.text: For thus the frantic patient as he laughs is bewailed by those who are in health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:87
verses.text: Nevertheless, ye do well to know, and hold fast that truth; yea, hold it fast, that no man is able to 			 forgive sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:88
verses.text: This woman who believed that she could be forgiven by Christ, believed Christ not to be man only, but God also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:89
verses.text: "Who," say they, "is this that forgiveth sins also?" And the Lord did not tell them as they said, "Who is this?" "It is the Son of God, the Word of God;" He did not tell them this, but suffering them to abide for a while still in their former opinion, He really solved the question which had excited them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:90
verses.text: For He who saw them at the table, heard their 			 thoughts, and turning to the woman, He said, "Thy faith hath made thee whole".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:91
verses.text: Let these who say, "Who is this that forgiveth sins also?" who think me to be but a man, think me but a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:92
verses.text: For thee "thy faith hath made thee whole".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:93
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:94
verses.text: The Good Physician not only cured the sick then present, but provided also for them who were to be hereafter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:95
verses.text: There were to be men in after times, who should say, "It is I who forgive sins, I who justify, I who sanctify, I who cure whomsoever I baptize".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:96
verses.text: Of this number are they who say, "Touch me not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:97
verses.text: Yes, so thoroughly are they of this number, that lately, in our conference, as ye may read in the records of it, when a place was offered them by the commissary, that they should sit with us, they thought it right to answer, "It is told us in Scripture with such not to sit," lest of course by the contact of the seats, our contagion (as they think) should reach to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:98
verses.text: See if this is not, "Touch me not, for I am clean".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:99
verses.text: But on another day, when I had a better opportunity, I represented to them this most wretched vanity, when there was a question concerning the Church, how that the evil in it do not contaminate the good: I 			 answered them, because they would not on this account sit with us, and said that they had been so advised by the Scripture of God, seeing forsooth that it is written, "I have not sat in the council of vanity;" I said, "If ye will not sit with us, because it is written, 'I have not sat in the council of vanity;' why have ye entered this place with us, since it is written in the following words, 'And with them that do iniquity I will not enter in'?" So then in that they say, "Touch me not, for I am clean," they are like to that Pharisee, who had invited the Lord, and who thought that He did not know the woman, simply because He did not hinder her from touching His 			 Feet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:100
verses.text: But in another respect the Pharisee was better, because whereas he supposed Christ to be but a man, he did not believe that by a man sins could be forgiven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:101
