verses.text: There was shown then a better understanding in Jews than heretics.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:102
verses.text: What said the Jews? "'Who is this that forgiveth sins also?' Does any man dare to usurp this to himself?" What on the other hand says the heretic? "It is I who forgive, I cleanse, I sanctify".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:103
verses.text: Let not me, but Christ, answer him: "O man, when I was thought 			 by the Jews to be but a man, I gave forgiveness of sins to faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:104
verses.text: (It is not I, but Christ who answereth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:105
verses.text: ) And thou, O heretic, mere man as thou art, dost say, "Come, O woman, I will make thee whole".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:106
verses.text: Whereas when I was thought to be but a man, I said, "Go, woman, thy faith hath made thee whole".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:107
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:108
verses.text: They answer, "knowing not," as the Apostle says, "either what they speak, or whereof they affirm:" they answer and say, "If men do not forgive sins, then that is false which Christ saith, 'Whatsoever ye shall loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:109
verses.text: '" But thou dost not know why this is said, and in what sense this is said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:110
verses.text: The Lord was about to give to men the Holy Spirit, and He wished it to be understood that sins are forgiven to His faithful by His Holy Spirit, and not by men's deserts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:111
verses.text: For what art thou, O man, but an invalid who hast need of healing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:112
verses.text: Wouldest thou make thyself my physician? Together with me, seek the Physician.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:113
verses.text: For that the Lord might show this more plainly, that sins are forgiven by the Holy Spirit, 			 which He hath given to His faithful ones, and not by men's deserts, after He had risen from the dead, He saith in a certain place, "Receive ye the Holy Ghost;" and when He had said, "Receive ye the Holy Ghost," He subjoined immediately, "Whosesoever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them;" that is, the Spirit remits them, not ye.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:114
verses.text: Now the Spirit is God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:115
verses.text: God therefore remits, not ye.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:116
verses.text: But what are ye in regard to the Spirit? "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?" And again, "Know ye not that your bodies are the temples of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God?" So then God dwelleth in His holy temple, that is in His holy faithful ones, in His Church; by them doth He remit sins; because they are living temples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:117
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:118
verses.text: But He who remitteth by man, can also remit even without man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:119
verses.text: For He who is able to give by another, hath no less the power to give by Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:120
verses.text: To some He gave by the ministry of John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:121
verses.text: By whom did He give to John himself? With good reason, as God wished to show this, and to attest this truth, when certain in Samaria had had the Gospel preached to them, and had been baptized, and baptized by Philip the Evangelist, one of the seven deacons that were first chosen, they did not receive the Holy Ghost, though they had been baptized.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:122
verses.text: Tidings were brought to the disciples who were at Jerusalem, and they came to Samaria, in order that they who had been baptized, might by imposition of their hands receive the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:123
verses.text: And so it was; "They came and laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:124
verses.text: For the Holy Ghost was at that time given in such sort, that He even visibly showed Himself to have been given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:125
verses.text: For they who received Him spake with the tongues of all nations; to signify that the Church among the nations was to speak in the tongues of all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:126
verses.text: So then they received the Holy Ghost, and He appeared evidently to be in them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:127
verses.text: Which when Simon saw, supposing that this power was of men, he wished it might be his also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:128
verses.text: What he thought to be of men, he wished to buy of 			 men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:129
verses.text: "How much money," says he, "will ye take of me, that by imposition of my hands the Holy Ghost may be given?" Then Peter says to him with execration, "Thou hast neither part nor lot in this faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:130
verses.text: For thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:131
verses.text: Thy money perish with thee; and the rest which he spake in the same place suitably to the occasion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:132
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:133
verses.text: Now why I have wished to bring this subject before you, give heed, Dearly Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:134
verses.text: It was meet that God should first show that He worketh by the ministry of men; but afterwards by Himself, lest men should think, as Simon thought, that it was man's gift, and not God's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:135
verses.text: Though the disciples themselves knew this well already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:136
verses.text: For there were one hundred and twenty men collected together, when without the imposition of any hand the Holy Ghost came upon them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:137
verses.text: For who had laid hands on them at that time? And yet He came, and filled them first.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:138
verses.text: After that offence of Simon, what did God do? See Him teaching, not by words but by things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:139
verses.text: That same Philip, who had baptized the men, and the Holy Ghost had not come upon them, unless the Apostles had met together and laid their hands upon them, baptized the officer, that is, the eunuch of queen 			 Candace, who had worshipped in Jerusalem, and returning thence was reading in his chariot Isaiah the Prophet, and understood it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:140
verses.text: Philip being admonished went up to his chariot, explained the Scripture, unfolded the faith, preached Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:141
verses.text: The eunuch believed on Christ, and said when they came unto a certain water, "See water, who doth hinder me to be baptized? Philip said to him, Dost thou believe on Jesus Christ? He answered, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:142
verses.text: Immediately he went down with him into the water".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:143
verses.text: When the mystery and sacrament of Baptism had been accomplished, that the gift of the Holy Ghost might not be thought to be of men, there was no waiting, as in the other case, for the Apostles to come, but the Holy Ghost came forthwith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:144
verses.text: Thus was Simon's thought destroyed, lest in such a thought he might have followers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:145
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:146
verses.text: Again, another more wonderful example.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:147
verses.text: Peter came to Cornelius the centurion, to a Gentile man, uncircumcised: he began to preach Christ Jesus both to him, and to those who were with him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:148
verses.text: "While Peter was yet speaking," I do not say, when as yet he had not laid on his hands, but when he had not even yet baptized them, and when they who were with Peter were in doubt whether the uncircumcised ought to be baptized (for there had arisen an offence between the Jews who believed, and those who had been brought to the faith from among the Gentiles, between the Jews, that is, and the Christians who were baptized though uncircumcised), that God might take away this question, "while Peter was 			 speaking, the Holy Ghost came," filled Cornelius, filled them who were with him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:149
verses.text: And by this very attestation of so great a thing, as it were a loud voice came to Peter, "Why dost thou doubt of water? Already I am here".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:150
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:151
verses.text: So then let every soul which is to be delivered from her manifold wickedness by the grace of the Lord, to be cleansed as it were in the Church from her filthy prostitution, believe with all assurance, approach the Feet of the Lord, seek His Footsteps, confess in pouring out tears upon them, and wipe them with her hair.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:152
verses.text: The Feet of the Lord are the preachers of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:153
verses.text: The woman's hair is all superfluous possessions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:154
verses.text: Let her wipe the Feet with her hair, yea 			 by all means wipe them, let her do works of mercy; and when she has wiped them, let her kiss them, let her receive peace, that she may have love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:155
verses.text: She has approached to such an one, has been baptized by such an one as the Apostle Paul: from him let her hear, "Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:156
verses.text: But she has been baptized by another, by one "who seeks his own things, not the things which are Jesus Christ's:" let her hear from the Lord, "Do what they say, but do not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:157
verses.text: So let her assurance be in Him, whether she meet with a good Evangelist, or with one who acts not as he speaks.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 48:158
verses.text: For she hears from the Lord with firm assurance, "O woman, go thy way, thy faith hath made thee whole".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:1
verses.text: Sermon L.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:2
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke ix.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:5
verses.text: 57, etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:6
verses.text: , where the case of the three persons is treated of, of whom one said, "I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest," and was disallowed: another did not dare to offer himself, and was aroused; the third wished to delay, and was blamed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:8
verses.text: Give ye ear to that which the Lord hath given me to speak on the lesson of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:9
verses.text: For we have read, that the Lord Jesus acted differently, when one man offered himself to follow Him, and was disallowed; another did not dare this, and was aroused; a third put off, and was blamed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:10
verses.text: For the words, "Lord, I will follow Thee whithersoever Thou goest," what is so prompt, what so active, what so ready, and what so fitly disposed to so great a good, as this "following the Lord whithersoever He should go"? Thou wonderest at this, saying, "How is this, that one so ready found no favour with the Good Master and Lord Jesus Christ, though He was inviting disciples to give them the kingdom of Heaven?" But inasmuch as He was such a Master as could see beforehand things to come, we understand, Brethren, that this man, if he 			 had followed Christ, would have been sure to "seek his own things, not the things which are Jesus Christ's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:11
verses.text: For He hath said Himself, "Not every one that saith unto Me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:12
verses.text: And of such was this man, nor did he know himself so well as the Physician knew him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:13
verses.text: For if he saw himself to be a dissembler now, if he had known himself at this time to be full of duplicity and guile, then he did not know with Whom he was speaking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:14
verses.text: For He it is of whom the Evangelist says, "He had no need that any one should testify to Him of man, for He Himself knew what was in man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:15
verses.text: What then did He answer? "Foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man hath not where to lay His Head".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:16
verses.text: But where hath He not? In thy faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:17
verses.text: For in thy heart foxes have holes, thou art full of guile; in thy heart birds of the air have nests; thou art lifted up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:18
verses.text: Full of guile and self-elation as thou art, thou shalt not follow Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:19
verses.text: How can a guileful man follow Simplicity?  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:20
verses.text: And then forthwith to another who was silent, and said nothing, and promised nothing, He saith, "Follow Me!" As much evil as He saw in the other, so much good saw He in this man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:21
verses.text: "Follow Me," Thou sayest to one who hath no wish for it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:22
verses.text: Lo, here is a man quite ready, "I will follow Thee whithersoever Thou goest;" and yet Thou sayest to another who hath no such wish, "Follow thou Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:23
verses.text: "The first," saith He, "I decline, because I see in him holes, I see nests".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:24
verses.text: "But then why dost Thou press this other, whom Thou dost challenge to follow Thee, and he makes excuses? Lo, Thou dost even force him, and he doth not come; Thou dost exhort him, and he doth 			 not follow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:25
verses.text: For what doth he say? 'I will go first to bury my father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:26
verses.text: '" The faith of his heart showed itself to the Lord; but his dutiful affection made him delay.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:27
verses.text: But the Lord Christ when He is preparing men for the Gospel, will have no excuse from this carnal and temporal affection interfere.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:28
verses.text: It is true that both the law of God prescribes these duties, and the Lord Himself reproves the Jews, because they destroyed this very commandment of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:29
verses.text: And the Apostle 			 Paul has in his Epistle laid it down, and said, "This is the first commandment with promise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:30
verses.text: What? "Honour thy father and thy mother".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:31
verses.text: God of a surety spake it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:32
verses.text: This young man then wished to obey God, and to bury his father; but it is place, and time, and circumstance, which is in this case to give way to place, and time, and circumstance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:33
verses.text: A father must be honoured, but God must be obeyed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:34
verses.text: He that begat us must be loved, but He that created us must be preferred.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:35
verses.text: "I am calling thee," saith He, "to My Gospel; I have need of thee for another work: this is a greater work than that which thou wishest to be 			 doing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:36
verses.text: 'Let the dead bury their dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:37
verses.text: ' Thy father is dead: there are other dead men to bury the dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:38
verses.text: Who are the dead who bury the dead? Can a dead man be buried by dead men? How can they lay him out, if they are dead? How can they carry him, if they are dead? How can they bewail him, if they are dead? Yet they do lay him out, and carry, and bewail him, and they are dead; because they are unbelievers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:39
verses.text: That which is written in the Song of Songs is a lesson to us, when the Church says, "Set in order love in 			 me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:40
verses.text: What is, "Set in order love in me"? Make the proper degrees, and render to each what is his due.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:41
verses.text: Do not put what should come before, below that which should come after it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:42
verses.text: Love your parents, but prefer God to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:43
verses.text: Mark the mother of the Maccabees, "'My sons, I know not how ye appeared in my womb.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:44
verses.text: ' Conceive you I could, give you birth I could; but 'form you I could not:' hear Him therefore, prefer Him to me: trouble not yourselves, that I must remain here without you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:45
verses.text: Thus she commanded them, and they followed her.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:46
verses.text: What this mother taught her children, did the Lord Jesus Christ teach him to whom He said, "Follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:47
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:48
verses.text: See now how another disciple presented himself, to whom no one said anything: he said, "Lord, I will follow Thee, but I will first go to bid them farewell which are at my house".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:49
verses.text: I suppose this is his meaning, "Let me tell my friends, lest haply they seek me as usual".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:50
verses.text: And the Lord said, "No man putting his hand on the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:51
verses.text: The East calls thee, and thou art looking toward the west.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:52
verses.text: In this lesson we learn this, that the Lord chooses whom He will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:53
verses.text: But He chooses them, as the Apostle says, both according to His Own grace, and according to their righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:54
verses.text: For such are the words of the Apostle; "Attend," he says, "to what Elias saith: Lord, they have killed Thy Prophets, they have overthrown Thine altars, and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:55
verses.text: But what saith the answer of God to him? 			 I have reserved to Myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee before Baal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:56
verses.text: Thou thinkest that thou art the only servant who is working faithfully: there are others too who fear Me, and they not few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:57
verses.text: For I have "seven thousand" there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:58
verses.text: And then he added, "Even so then at this present time also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:59
verses.text: For some Jews believed, though the most were reprobate; like him who carried holes for foxes in his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:60
verses.text: "Even so then," saith he, "at this present time also, there is a remnant saved through the election of grace:" that is, there is the same 			 Christ even now, as then, who also then said to that Elias, "I have reserved to Myself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:61
verses.text: What is, "I have reserved to Myself"? I have chosen them, because I saw their hearts that they trusted in Me, and not in themselves, nor in Baal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:62
verses.text: They are not changed, they are as they were made by Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:63
verses.text: And thou who art speaking, except thou hadst placed thy trust in Me, where wouldest thou be? Except thou wert replenished by My grace, wouldest not thou too be bowing the knee before Baal? But thou 			 art replenished by My grace; because thou hast not put thy trust at all in thine own strength, but wholly in My grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:64
verses.text: Do not therefore glory in this, as to suppose thou hast no fellow-servants in thy service; there are others whom I have chosen, as I have chosen thee, those, namely, who put their trust in Me; as the Apostle says, "Even now also a remnant is saved through the election of grace".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:66
verses.text: Beware, O Christian, beware of pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:67
verses.text: For though thou art a follower of the saints, ascribe it always wholly to grace; for that there should be any "remnant" in thee, the grace of God hath brought to pass, not thine own deserts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:68
verses.text: For the Prophet Isaiah again having this remnant in view, had said already, "Except the Lord of Hosts had left us a seed, we should have become as Sodom, and should have been like unto Gomorrah".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:69
verses.text: "So then," says the Apostle, "at this present time also a remnant is saved through the election of grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:70
verses.text: But if by grace," says he, "then is it no more of works" (that is, "be now no more lifted up upon thine own deserts"); "otherwise grace is no more grace".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:71
verses.text: For if thou dost build on thine own work; then is a reward rendered unto thee, not grace freely bestowed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:72
verses.text: But if it be grace, it is gratuitously given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:73
verses.text: I ask thee then, O sinner, "Dost thou believe in Christ?" Thou sayest, "I do believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:74
verses.text: "What dost thou believe? That all thy sins may be forgiven thee freely through Him?" Then hast thou what thou hast believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:75
verses.text: O grace gratuitously given! And thou, righteous man, what dost thou believe, that thou canst not keep thy 			 righteousness without God? That thou art righteous then, impute it wholly to His mercy; but that thou art a sinner, ascribe it to thine own iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:76
verses.text: Be thou thine own accuser, and He will be thy gracious Deliverer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:77
verses.text: For every crime, wickedness, or sin comes of our own negligence, and all virtue and holiness come of God's gracious goodness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 49:78
verses.text: "Let us turn to the Lord".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:1
verses.text: Sermon LI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:2
verses.text: [CI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:5
verses.text: 2, "The harvest truly is plenteous," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:7
verses.text: By the lesson of the Gospel which has just been read, we are reminded to search what that harvest is of which the Lord says, "The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:8
verses.text: Pray ye the Lord of the harvest, that He would send forth labourers into His harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:9
verses.text: Then to His twelve disciples, whom He also named Apostles, He added other seventy-two, and sent them all, as appears from His words, to the harvest then ready.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:10
verses.text: What then was that harvest? For that harvest was not among these Gentiles, among whom there had been nothing sown.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:11
verses.text: It remains therefore that we understand that this harvest was among the people of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:12
verses.text: It was to that harvest that the Lord of the harvest came, to that harvest He sent reapers; but to the Gentiles He 			 sent not reapers, but sowers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:13
verses.text: Understand we then that it was harvest among the people of the Jews, sowing time among the peoples of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:14
verses.text: For out of that harvest were the Apostles chosen, where now that the harvest was, the corn was already ripe; for there had the Prophets sown.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:15
verses.text: Delightful it is to take a view of God's husbandry, and to feel delight in His gifts, and the labourers in His field.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:16
verses.text: For in this husbandry did he labour, who said, "I laboured more than they all".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:17
verses.text: But the strength to labour was given him by the Lord of the harvest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:18
verses.text: Therefore he added, "Yet it is not I, but the grace of God which is with me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:19
verses.text: For that he was employed in this husbandry he clearly enough shows, where he says, "I have planted, Apollos watered".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:20
verses.text: But this Apostle, from Saul, becoming Paul, that is, from being proud, the least of all (for the name of Saul is derived from Saul; but Paul is little; whence in a way interpreting his own name, he says, "I am the least of the Apostles": this Paul I say, the little, and the least, sent unto the Gentiles, says that he was sent particularly to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:21
verses.text: He himself so writes, we read, believe, preach it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:22
verses.text: He then in his Epistle to the Galatians says, that having been now called by the Lord Jesus, he came to Jerusalem, and "communicated the Gospel" unto the Apostles, that their right hands were given to him, the sign of harmony, the sign of agreement, that what they had learnt from him differed in no respect from them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:23
verses.text: Afterwards he says that it was agreed between him and them, that he should go to the Gentiles, and they unto the circumcision, he as a sower, they as reapers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:24
verses.text: So also with good reason, though they knew it not, did the Athenians give him his name.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:25
verses.text: For as they heard the word from him, they said, "Who is 			 this sower of words?"  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:26
verses.text: Attend then and be it your delight with me to take a view of the husbandry of God and the two harvests in it, the one already past, the other yet to come; the one already past among the people of the Jews, the one yet to come among the peoples of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:27
verses.text: Let us prove this; and whereby, but by the Scripture of God, the Lord of the harvest? See we have it said there in this present lesson, "The harvest is great, but the labourers are few.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:28
verses.text: Pray ye the Lord 			 of the harvest, that He would send forth labourers into His harvest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:29
verses.text: But because in that harvest there were to be gainsaying and persecuting Jews, He says, "Behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:30
verses.text: Let us show something clearer still touching this harvest in the Gospel according to John, where the Lord sat as He was wearied at the well, great mysteries indeed were transacted, but the time is too short to treat of them all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:31
verses.text: But give ye ear to that which relates to the present subject.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:32
verses.text: For we have undertaken to show a harvest among the people, among whom the Prophets preached; for therefore were they sowers, that the Apostles might be reapers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:33
verses.text: A woman of Samaria talks with the Lord Jesus, and when the Lord among other things had told her how God ought to be worshipped, she says, "We know that Messias cometh who is called 			 Christ, and He will teach us all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:34
verses.text: And the Lord saith to her, I that speak with thee am He".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:35
verses.text: Believe what thou hearest; why dost thou make search for what thou seest? "I that speak with thee am He".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:36
verses.text: But as to what she had said, "We know that the Messias will come," whom Moses and the Prophets have announced, "who is called Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:37
verses.text: The harvest was already in the ear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:38
verses.text: When it had yet to grow it had received the Prophets as sowers, now that it was come to ripeness it waited for the Apostles as reapers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:39
verses.text: Presently as she heard this 			 she believed and left her water-pot, and ran in haste, and began to announce the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:40
verses.text: The disciples at that time had gone to buy bread; who on their return found the Lord talking with the woman, and they marvelled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:41
verses.text: Yet did they not dare to say to Him, "What or why talkest Thou with her?" They had astonishment in themselves, they repressed their boldness in their heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:42
verses.text: To this Samaritan woman then the Name of Christ was nothing new, she was already waiting for His coming, already did she believe that He would come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:43
verses.text: Whence had she believed it, if Moses had not sown? But hear this more expressly noted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:44
verses.text: The Lord then said to His disciples, "Ye say that the summer is yet far distant, lift up your eyes, and see the fields white already to harvest" 			  And then He adds, "Others have laboured, and ye are entered into their labours".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:45
verses.text: Abraham laboured, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, the Prophets laboured in sowing; at the Lord's coming the harvest was found ripe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:46
verses.text: The reapers sent with the scythe of the Gospel, carried the sheaves into the Lord's floor, where Stephen was to be threshed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:47
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:48
verses.text: But here comes in that Paul, and he is sent to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:49
verses.text: And this he does not conceal in setting forth the grace, which he had specially and peculiarly received.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:50
verses.text: For he says in his Scriptures, that he was sent to preach the Gospel where Christ had not been named.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:51
verses.text: But because that first harvest was past already, and all the Jews who remained are no harvest, let us consider that harvest which we ourselves are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:52
verses.text: For it has been sown by Apostles and Prophets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:53
verses.text: The Lord Himself sowed it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:54
verses.text: For He was in the Apostles, seeing that Christ also Himself reaped it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:55
verses.text: For they are nothing without Him; He is perfect without them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:56
verses.text: For He saith Himself to them, "For without Me, ye can do nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:57
verses.text: What then doth Christ from henceforth sowing among the Gentiles say? "A sower went out to sow".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:58
verses.text: "There" are reapers "sent out" to reap, "here" an unwearied sower "went out" to sow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:59
verses.text: For what fear did it cause him, that "some seed fell on the way side, and some on rocky places, and some among thorns"? If he had been afraid of these unmanageable grounds, he would never have got to the good ground.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:60
verses.text: What is it to us, what affair of ours is it to be disputing now of the Jews, and talking of the chaff? this only concerns us, that we be not "the way side," nor "the rock," nor "the thorns," but "the good ground".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:61
verses.text: Be our heart well-prepared, that from it may come the "thirty," or the "sixty fold," or the thousand, and the "hundred fold;" some more, some less; but all is wheat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:62
verses.text: Let it not be "the 			 way side," where the enemy as a bird may take away the seed trodden down by the passers by.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:63
verses.text: Let it not be "the rock," where the shallow soil makes it spring up immediately, so that it cannot bear the sun.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:64
verses.text: Let it not be the "thorns," the lusts of this world, the anxieties of an ill-ordered life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:65
verses.text: For what is worse than that anxiety of life, which doth not suffer one to attain unto Life? What more miserable, than by caring for life, to lose Life? What more unhappy, than by fearing death, to fall into death? Let the thorns be rooted up, the field prepared, the seeds put in, let them grow unto the harvest, let the barn be longed for, not the fire feared.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:66
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:67
verses.text: My place accordingly it is, whom with all my unworthiness the Lord hath appointed to be a labourer in His field, to say these things to you, to sow, to plant, to water, yea to dig round about some trees, and to apply the basket of dung; belongeth it to me to do these things faithfully; to you to receive them faithfully; to the Lord to aid me in my labour, and you in your belief, all of us labouring, but in Him overcoming the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:68
verses.text: What then belongs to your place I have already said; now I wish to say what belongs to ours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:69
verses.text: But peradventure it seems to some of you, that it is something superfluous which I have declared that I wish to say, and speaking within themselves they are saying in thought, "O 			 that he would now let us go! He has said already what belongs to our place, as to that which belongs to his, what is that to us?" I think it is better that in a reciprocal and mutual love, we should belong to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:70
verses.text: Ye are now indeed of one family, we of the same family are dispensers, it is true, but we all belong to one Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:71
verses.text: Nor what I give, do I give of mine own; but of His from whom I also receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:72
verses.text: For if I should give of mine own, I shall give a lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:73
verses.text: "For he that speaketh a lie, 			 speaketh of his own".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:74
verses.text: So then ye ought to give ear to that which belongs to the duty of the dispenser, whether it be that ye may have joy in yourselves, if ye find yourselves to be such, or whether it be that ye may be even in this very thing instructed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:75
verses.text: For how many are there among this people who shall some day be dispensers! I too was once where ye now are; and I who am seen now to be measuring out to my fellowservants their food from this higher place, a few years since in a lower place was 			 receiving food with my fellow-servants.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:76
verses.text: I am speaking now a Bishop to lay-men; but I know that in speaking to them I am speaking to many who will some day be bishops also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:77
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:78
verses.text: Let us see then how we must understand what the Lord enjoined on them whom He sent to preach the Gospel, and let us consider in our mind this prepared harvest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:79
verses.text: "Carry," He saith, "neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes; and salute no man by the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:80
verses.text: And into whatsoever house ye enter, say, Peace be to this house.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:81
verses.text: If the Son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it; if not, it shall return to you again".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:82
verses.text: If it hath "rested," hath the other lost it? This be far from the mind of Saints! So then this is not to be taken in a carnal sense; and hence it may be neither are the "purse," nor "shoes," nor "scrip;" nor above all that, where if we take it simply without examination, pride seems to be enjoined us, that we "salute no man by the way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:84
verses.text: Let us give heed to our Lord, our True Example and Succour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:85
verses.text: Let us prove that He is our Succour; "Without Me ye can do nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:86
verses.text: Let us prove that He is our Example; "Christ," says Peter, "suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow His steps".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:87
verses.text: Our Lord Himself had bags in the way, and these bags He entrusted to Judas.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:88
verses.text: It is true He suffered from the thief; but I as desiring to learn of my Lord say, "O Lord, Thou didst suffer from the thief, whence hadst Thou that of which he could take away? Me, a wretched and infirm man Thou hast admonished not even to carry a purse; Thou didst carry bags, and hadst that in which Thou couldest suffer from the thief.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:89
verses.text: If Thou hadst not carried them, neither could he have found 			 anything to take away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:90
verses.text: What remains, but that he here saith to me, "Understand what that thou hearest, 'Carry no purse,' means? What is a purse? Money shut up, that is, concealed wisdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:91
verses.text: What is, 'Carry no purse? Be not wise within your own selves only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:92
verses.text: Receive ye the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:93
verses.text: ' It should be a fountain in thee, not a purse; from whence distribution is made to others, not where it is itself shut in".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:94
verses.text: And the scrip is the same as the purse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:95
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:96
verses.text: What are "the shoes"? The shoes which we use, are the skins of dead beasts, the coverings of our feet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:97
verses.text: By this then are we bidden to renounce dead works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:98
verses.text: This Moses was admonished of in a figure, when the Lord speaking to him said, "Loose thy shoes from off thy feet; for the place wherein thou standest is holy ground".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:99
verses.text: What ground is so holy as the Church of God? In it therefore let us stand, let us loose our shoes, let us, that is, renounce dead works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:100
verses.text: For as touching these shoes, wherewith we walk, the same my Lord again assures me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:101
verses.text: For if He had not been shod Himself, John would not have said of Him, "I am not worthy to unloose the latchet of His shoes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:102
verses.text: Be there obedience then, let not a haughty severity steal over us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:103
verses.text: "I," says one, "fulfil the Gospel, because I walk with naked feet".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:104
verses.text: Well, thou canst do it, I cannot.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:105
verses.text: But let us both keep that which we both receive together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:106
verses.text: How? Let us glow with charity, let us love one another; and so it shall be, that I will love your strength, and thou shall bear my weakness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:107
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:108
verses.text: But what thinkest thou, who dost not choose to understand in what sense these words are used, and who art forced by thy perverse interpretation to slander even the Lord Himself as to the "bags" and "shoes;" what thinkest thou? Does it please thee then, that as we meet our friends in the way, we should neither pay them our salutations if they are our betters, nor return the salutations of our inferiors? What, dost thou fulfil the Gospel, because thou art saluted, and art silent? But thus thou wilt not be like to the traveller going on the way, but to the milestone pointing out the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:109
verses.text: Let us then lay aside this coarse interpretation, and understand aright the words of the Lord, "and salute no man by the way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:110
verses.text: For it is not without a cause that we are enjoined this, nor would He mislike us to do what He enjoined.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:111
verses.text: What then is, "Salute no man by the way"? It might indeed be even simply taken thus, that He has commanded us to do what He enjoins with all speed; and that His words "Salute no man by the way," are as though He had said, "Put all other things by, till ye accomplish 			 what has been enjoined you;" according to that style of speaking by which expressions are wont to be exaggerated in the custom of conversation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:112
verses.text: Nor need we go far; in the same discourse a little while afterwards He says, "And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shall be thrust down to hell".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:113
verses.text: What is, "exalted to heaven"? Did the walls of that city touch the clouds, or reach to the stars? But what is "exalted to heaven"? Thou seemest thyself to be surpassing happy, surpassing powerful, thou art exceeding proud.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:114
verses.text: As then for the sake of exaggeration this was said, "Thou art exalted unto heaven" to that city, which was not exalted, nor rose up unto heaven; so to express haste hyperbolically was it said, "So run, so do what I have enjoined you, that 			 travellers by the way may not in the least retard you; but disregarding all things else, hasten to the end set before you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:115
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:116
verses.text: But there is another more recondite meaning in these words which it is not difficult to understand, which respects more particularly myself and all dispensers, and you too who are hearers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:117
verses.text: He that salutes, wishes salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:118
verses.text: For so the ancients in their letters wrote thus, "Such a one sends salvation to another".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:119
verses.text: Salutation derives its name from this salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:120
verses.text: What then is, "Salute no man by the way"? They who "salute by the way," do so "by occasion".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:121
verses.text: I see that ye have quickly understood me, yet for all that I must not finish yet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:122
verses.text: For ye have not all understood so quickly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:123
verses.text: I have seen that some understand by their voice, I see more asking for something 			 further by their silence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:124
verses.text: But seeing that we are talking of the way, let us walk as it were in the way: ye quick ones, wait for the slow, and walk evenly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:125
verses.text: What then did I say, He "who salutes by the way," salutes only by occasion? He was not going to him whom he salutes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:126
verses.text: He was about one thing, another came in his way; he was seeking one thing, he found across his path some other thing to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:127
verses.text: What then is it to "salute by occasion"? "By occasion" to announce salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:128
verses.text: Now what else 			 is it to announce salvation, but to preach the Gospel? If then thou dost preach, do it by love, and not "by occasion".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:129
verses.text: There are men then, who though "they seek their own things," yet preach no other Gospel; of whom the Apostle says with sighing, "For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:130
verses.text: And these "saluted," that is announced salvation, they preached the Gospel; but they sought some other thing, and therefore they saluted only "by occasion".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:131
verses.text: And what is this? If thou art such an one, whosoever thou art, thou doest it; nay not all of you who do it are such, but it may be that some of you who do it are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:132
verses.text: But if thou art such, it is not that thou doest it, but it is done by thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:133
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:134
verses.text: For such as these did the Apostle suffer; yet did he not enjoin them so to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:135
verses.text: And these do something, or something is done by them; they seek something else, yet they preach the word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:136
verses.text: Care not what the preacher seeks after; be it thy will to hold fast what he preaches; but let his intention be no concern of thine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:137
verses.text: Hear the word of salvation from his mouth, from his mouth hold fast this salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:138
verses.text: Be not thou the judge of his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:139
verses.text: If thou seest that he is 			 seeking after other things, what is that to thee? Hear Him who is Salvation; "What they say, do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:140
verses.text: He has given thee assurance who hath said, "What they say, do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:141
verses.text: Do they evil? "Do not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:142
verses.text: Do they good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:143
verses.text: They do not "salute by the way," they do not preach the Gospel by occasion; "be ye followers of them, even as they also are of Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:144
verses.text: A good man preaches to thee; pluck the grape from the vine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:145
verses.text: A bad man preaches to thee, pluck the grape as it hangs in the hedge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:146
verses.text: The cluster has grown on the vine-branch entangled among the thorns, but it has not grown from the thorns.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:147
verses.text: By all means when thou seest any such thing as this and art hungry, be careful as thou pluckest it, lest when thou puttest forth thy hand to the grape, thou be torn by the thorns.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:148
verses.text: This is what I say; in such wise hear what is good, as that thou 			 imitate not the evil of the character.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:149
verses.text: Let him preach "by occasion," salute by the way; it will injure him because he has not given ear to the precept of Christ, "Salute no man by the way;" it will not injure thee, who, whether thou dost hear of salvation from a passer by, or from one who comes direct to thee, dost hold fast that salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:150
verses.text: Hear the Apostle, who as I have said already gives us to understand this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:151
verses.text: "What then?" "So that in every way, whether by occasion or in truth, Christ is preached; and herein I do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:152
verses.text: For I know that this shall turn to my salvation through your prayer".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:153
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:154
verses.text: Let then such as these, the Apostles of Christ, the preachers of the Gospel, who "salute not by the way," that is, who do not seek or do any other thing, but who in genuine charity preach the Gospel, let them come into the house, and say, "Peace to this house".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:155
verses.text: They speak not with the mouth only; they pour out that of which they are full; they preach peace, and they have peace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:156
verses.text: They are not as those of whom it was said, "Peace, Peace, and there is no 			 peace".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:157
verses.text: What is, "Peace, Peace, and there is no peace"? They preach it, but they have it not; they praise it and they love it not; they say, and do not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:158
verses.text: But yet do thou receive the peace, "whether by occasion or in truth Christ be preached".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:159
verses.text: Whoso then is full of peace, and salutes, saying, "Peace to this house, if the son of peace be there, his peace shall rest upon him; if not," for peradventure there is no one of peace there, yet he who saluted has lost nothing, "it 			 shall return," says he, "to you again".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:160
verses.text: It shall return to thee, though it never departed from thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 50:161
verses.text: For this He would mean to say, It profiteth thee that thou hast declared it, it hath not profited him at all who hath not received it; thou hast not lost thy reward, because he hath remained empty; it is rendered thee for thy good will, it is rendered thee for the charity which thou hast bestowed, He will render it to thee who hath given thee assurance of it by that Angelic voice, "Peace 			 on earth to men of good will".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:1
verses.text: Sermon LII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:2
verses.text: [CII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:5
verses.text: 16, "He that rejecteth you rejecteth me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:7
verses.text: What our Lord Jesus Crist at that time spake to His disciples was put in writing, and prepared for us to hear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:8
verses.text: And so we have heard His words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:9
verses.text: For what profit would it be to us if He were seen, and were not heard? And now it is no hurt, that He is not seen, and yet is heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:10
verses.text: He saith then, "He that despiseth you, despiseth Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:11
verses.text: If to the Apostles only He said, "He that despiseth you, despiseth Me;" do ye despise us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:12
verses.text: But if His word reach to us, and He hath called us, and set us in their place, see that ye despise not us, lest the wrong ye shall do unto us reach to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:13
verses.text: For if ye fear not us, fear Him who said, "He that despiseth you, despiseth Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:14
verses.text: But why do we, who are unwilling to be despised by you, speak to you, except that we may have joy of your good conversation? Let your good works 			 be the solace of our perils.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:15
verses.text: Live well, that ye may not die ill.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:17
verses.text: And in these words which I have spoken, "Live well, that ye may not die ill," do not think of those who it may be have lived evilly, and have died in their beds; and the pomp of their funeral has been displayed, and they have been laid in costly coffins, in sepulchres prepared with exceeding beauty and labour; nor because each one of you perhaps is saying, "I should wish so to die," do ye think that it is a vain thing I have chosen to say; when I said that I 			 would that ye should live well, that ye may not die ill? On the other hand, the case of some one, it may be, occurs to you, who has both lived well, and according to the opinion of men has died ill; perhaps he has died from the fall of a house, has died by shipwreck, has died by wild beasts; and each carnal man is saying in his heart, "What good is it to live well? See this man has so lived, and in this wise has he died".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:18
verses.text: "Return therefore to your heart;" and if ye are faithful ones, ye 			 will find Christ there; He speaketh to you there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:19
verses.text: For I cry aloud, but He in silence giveth more instruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:20
verses.text: I speak by the sound of words; He speaketh within by the fear of the thoughts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:21
verses.text: May He then engraft my word in your heart; for I have taken upon me to say, "Live well, that ye may not die ill".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:22
verses.text: See, for faith is in your hearts, and Christ dwelleth there, and it is His place to teach what I desire to give utterance to.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:23
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:24
verses.text: Remember that rich and that poor man in the Gospel; "the rich man clothed in purple and fine linen," and crammed with daily feastings; and the poor man "lying before" the rich man's gate, hungry, and looking for "the crumbs from his table, full of sores, licked" by "dogs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:25
verses.text: Remember, I say; and whence do ye remember, but because Christ is there in your hearts? Tell me, what have ye asked Him within, and what hath He answered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:26
verses.text: For he goes on to say, "It came to pass that that poor man died, and was carried by the Angels into Abraham's bosom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:27
verses.text: The rich man also died, and was buried in hell.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:28
verses.text: And being in torments he lifted up his eyes, and saw Lazarus resting in Abraham's bosom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:29
verses.text: Then he cried, saying, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send 			 Lazarus that he may dip his finger in water, and drop it on my tongue, for I am tormented in this flame".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:30
verses.text: Proud in the world, in hell a beggar! For that poor man did attain to his crumbs; but the other attained not to the drop of water.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:31
verses.text: Of these two then, tell me, which died well, and which died ill? Do not ask the eyes, return to the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:32
verses.text: For if ye ask the eyes, they will answer you falsely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:33
verses.text: For vastly splendid, and disguised with much worldly show, are the honours which could be paid to that rich man in his death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:34
verses.text: What crowds of mourning slaves and handmaids might there be! what pompous train of 			 dependants! what splendid funeral obsequies! what costliness of burial! I suppose he was overwhelmed with spices.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:35
verses.text: What shall we say then, Brethren, that he died well, or died ill? If ye ask the eyes, he died very well; if ye enquire of your inner Master, he died most ill.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:36
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:37
verses.text: If then those haughty men who keep their own goods to themselves, and bestow none of them upon the poor, die in this way; how do they die who plunder the goods of others? Therefore have I said with true reason, "Live well, that ye die not ill," that ye die not as that rich man died.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:38
verses.text: Nothing proves an evil death, but the time after death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:39
verses.text: On the other hand, look at that poor man; not with the eyes, for so ye will err; let faith look at him, let the heart see 			 him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:40
verses.text: Set him before your eyes lying on the ground, "full of sores, and the dogs" coming and "licking his sores".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:41
verses.text: Now when ye recall him before your eyes in this guise, immediately ye loathe him, ye turn your face away, and stop your nostrils: see then with the eyes of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:42
verses.text: "He died, and was carried by the Angels into Abraham's bosom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:43
verses.text: The rich man's family was seen bewailing him; the Angels were not seen rejoicing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:44
verses.text: What then did Abraham answer the rich man? "Son, 			 remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst good things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:45
verses.text: Thou thoughtest nothing good, but what thou hadst in this life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:46
verses.text: Thou hast received them; but those days are past; and thou hast lost the whole; and thou hast remained behind to be tormented in hell".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:47
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:48
verses.text: Opportune then was it, Brethren, that those words should be spoken to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:49
verses.text: Have respect unto the poor, whether lying on the ground, or walking; have respect unto the poor, do good works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:50
verses.text: Ye who are wont so to do, do it still and ye who are not wont to do so, do it now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:51
verses.text: Let the number of those who do good works increase; since the number of the faithful increases also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:52
verses.text: Ye do not yet see how great is the good ye do; for so the husbandman also sees not 			 the crop when he sows, but he trusts the ground.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:53
verses.text: Wherefore dost thou not trust God? Our harvest will come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 51:54
verses.text: Think, that we are busy in travail now, are working in travail now, but sure to receive, as it is written, "They went on and wept as they cast their seed; but they shall surely come with exultation, bringing their sheaves with them".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:1
verses.text: Sermon LIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:2
verses.text: [CIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:5
verses.text: 38, "And a certain woman named Martha received him into her house," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:7
verses.text: The words of our Lord Jesus Christ which have just been read out of the Gospel, give us to understand, that there is some one thing for which we must be making, when we toil amid the manifold engagements of this life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:8
verses.text: Now we make for this as being yet in pilgrimage, and not in our abiding place; as yet in the way, not yet in our country; as yet in longing, not yet in enjoyment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:9
verses.text: Yet let us make for it, and that without sloth and without 			 intermission, that we may some time be able to reach it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:10
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:11
verses.text: Martha and Mary were two sisters, true kinswomen both, not only in blood, but in religion also; both clave to the Lord, both with one heart served the Lord when He was present in the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:12
verses.text: Martha received Him, as strangers are usually received.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:13
verses.text: Yet it was the handmaid received her Lord, the sick her Saviour, the creature her Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:14
verses.text: And she received Him to be fed in the body, herself to be fed in spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:15
verses.text: For the Lord was pleased to "take on Him the form of a 			 servant," and "having taken the form of a servant" in it to be fed by servants, by reason of His condescension, not His condition.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:16
verses.text: For this truly was condescension, to allow Himself to be fed by others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:17
verses.text: He had a body, wherein He might hunger indeed and thirst; but do ye not know that when He hungered in the wilderness Angels ministered to Him? So then, in that He was pleased to be fed, He showed favour to them that fed Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:18
verses.text: And what marvel is this, seeing He showed this same favour to the widow as touching the Holy Elias, whom He had before fed by the ministry of a raven? Did He fail in His power of feeding him, when He sent him to the widow? By no means.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:19
verses.text: He did not fail in His power of feeding him, when He sent him to the widow; but He designed to bless the religious widow, by means of her pious office paid to His servant.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:20
verses.text: Thus then was the Lord received as a guest, "who came unto His own, and His own received Him not: but as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God:" adopting servants, and making them brethren; redeeming captives, and making them co-heirs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:21
verses.text: Yet let none of you, as perhaps may be the case, say, "O blessed they who obtained the grace to receive Christ into their own house!" Do not grieve, do not murmur, that thou wert born in times when thou seest the Lord no more in the flesh; He has not taken this blessedness from thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:22
verses.text: "Forasmuch," says He, "as ye have done it unto the least of Mine, ye have done unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:23
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:24
verses.text: These few words, as the shortness of the time allowed me, would I speak concerning the Lord who was pleased to be fed in the flesh, while He feedeth in the spirit: let us now come to the subject which I have proposed concerning unity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:25
verses.text: Martha, who was arranging and preparing to feed the Lord, was occupied about much serving.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:26
verses.text: Mary her sister chose rather to be fed by the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:27
verses.text: She in a manner deserted her sister who was toiling about much serving, and she sat 			 herself at the Lord's feet, and in stillness heard His word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:28
verses.text: Her most faithful ear had heard already; "Be still, and see that I am the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:29
verses.text: Martha was troubled, Mary was feasting; the one was arranging many things, the other had her eyes upon the One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:30
verses.text: Both occupations were good; but yet as to which was the better, what shall we say? We have One whom we may ask, let us give ear together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:31
verses.text: Which was the better, we heard now when the lesson was read, and let us hear again as I repeat it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:32
verses.text: Martha appeals to her Guest, lays the request of her pious complaints before the Judge, that her sister had deserted her, and 			 neglected to assist her when she was so busied in her serving.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:33
verses.text: Without any answer from Mary, yet in her presence, the Lord gives judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:34
verses.text: Mary preferred as in repose to commit her cause to the Judge, and had no mind to busy herself in making answer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:35
verses.text: For if she were to be getting ready words to answer, she must remit her earnest attention to hear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:36
verses.text: Therefore the Lord answered, who was in no difficulty for words, in that He was the Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:37
verses.text: What then did He say? "Martha, Martha".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:38
verses.text: The repetition of the name is a token of love, or perhaps of exciting attention; she is named twice, that she might give the more attentive heed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:39
verses.text: "Martha, Martha," hear: "Thou art occupied about many things: but one thing is needful;" for so meaneth unum opus est, not "one work," that is, one single work, but one is needful, is expedient, is necessary, which one thing Mary had chosen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:40
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:41
verses.text: Consider, Brethren, this "one thing," and see if even in multitude itself anything pleases, but "this oneness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:42
verses.text: See how great a number, through God's mercy, ye are: who could bear you, if ye did not mind "one thing"? Whence in this many is this quiet? Give oneness, and it is a people; take oneness away, and it is a crowd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:43
verses.text: For what is a crowd, but a disordered multitude? But give ear to the Apostle: "Now I beseech you, brethren".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:44
verses.text: He was speaking 			 to a multitude; but he wished to make them all "one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:45
verses.text: "Now I beseech you, brethren, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no schisms among you; but that ye be perfected in the same mind, and in the same knowledge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:46
verses.text: And in another place, "That ye be of one mind, thinking one thing, doing nothing through strife or vainglory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:47
verses.text: And the Lord prays to the Father touching them that are His: "that they may be one even as We are One".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:48
verses.text: And in the Acts of the Apostles; "And the multitude of them that believed were of one soul, and of one heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:49
verses.text: Therefore, "Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt His Name in one together".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:50
verses.text: For one thing is necessary, that celestial Oneness, the Oneness in which the Father, and the Son, and Holy Spirit are One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:51
verses.text: See how the praise of Unity is commended to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:52
verses.text: Undoubtedly our God is Trinity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:53
verses.text: The Father is not the Son the Son is not the Father, the Holy Spirit is neither the Father, nor the Son, but the Spirit of both; and yet these Three are not Three Gods, nor Three Almighties; but One God, Almighty, the whole Trinity is one God; because One thing is necessary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:54
verses.text: To this one thing nothing brings us, except 			 being many we have one heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:55
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:56
verses.text: Good are ministrations done to the poor, and especially the due services and the religious offices done to the saints of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:57
verses.text: For they are a payment, not a gift, as the Apostle says, "If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we shall reap your carnal things?" Good are they, we exhort you to them, yea by the word of the Lord we build you up, "be not slow to entertain" the saints.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:58
verses.text: Sometimes, they who were not aware of it, by entertaining those whom they knew not, have entertained angels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:59
verses.text: These things are good; yet better is that thing which Mary hath chosen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:60
verses.text: For the one thing hath manifold trouble from necessity; the other hath sweetness from charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:61
verses.text: A man wishes when he is serving, to meet with something; and sometimes he is not able: that which is lacking is sought for, that which is at hand is got ready; and the mind is distracted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:62
verses.text: For if Martha had been sufficient for these things, she would not have demanded her sister's help.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:63
verses.text: These things are 			 manifold, are diverse, because they are carnal, because they are temporal; good though they be, they are transitory.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:64
verses.text: But what said theLord to Martha? "Mary hath chosen that better part".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:65
verses.text: Not thou a bad, but she a better.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:66
verses.text: Hear, how better; "which shall not be taken away from her".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:67
verses.text: Some time or other, the burden of these necessary duties shall be taken from thee: the sweetness of truth is everlasting.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:68
