verses.text: "That which she hath chosen shall not be taken away from her".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:69
verses.text: It is not taken away, but yet it is increased.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:70
verses.text: In this life, that is, is it increased, in the other life it will be perfected, never shall it be "taken away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:71
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:72
verses.text: Yea, Martha, blessed in thy good serving, even thou (with thy leave would I say it) seekest this reward for all thy labour—quiet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:73
verses.text: Now thou art occupied about much serving, thou hast pleasure in feeding bodies which are mortal, though they be the bodies of Saints; but when thou shalt have got to that country, wilt thou find there any stranger whom thou mayest receive into thine house? wilt thou find the hungry, to whom thou mayest break thy bread? or the 			 thirsty, to whom thou mayest hold out thy cup? the sick whom thou mayest visit? the litigious, whom thou mayest set at one? the dead, whom thou mayest bury? None of all these will be there, but what will be there? What Mary hath chosen; there shall we be fed, and shall not feed others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:74
verses.text: Therefore there will that be in fulness and perfection which Mary hath chosen here; from that rich table, from the word of the Lord did she gather up some crumbs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:75
verses.text: For would ye know what will be there? The Lord 			 Himself saith of His servants: "Verily I say unto you, that He will make them to sit down to meat, and will pass by and serve them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:76
verses.text: What is "to sit down to meat," but to "be still"? What is, "to sit down to meat," but to rest? What is, "He will pass by and serve them"? First, He passeth by, and so serveth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:77
verses.text: And where? In that heavenly Banquet, of which he saith, "Verily I say unto you, Many shall come from the East and West, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:78
verses.text: There will the Lord feed us, but first He passeth on from hence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:79
verses.text: For (as ye should know) the Pasch is by interpretation Passing-over.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:80
verses.text: The Lord came, He did divine things, He suffered human things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:81
verses.text: Is He still spit upon? Is He still struck with the palm of the hand? Is He still crowned with thorns? Is He still scourged? Is He still crucified? Is He still wounded with a spear? "He hath passed by".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:82
verses.text: And so too the Gospel tells us, when He kept the 			 Paschal feast with His disciples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:83
verses.text: What says the Gospel? "But when the hour was come that Jesus should pass out of this world unto the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 52:84
verses.text: Therefore did He pass, that He might feed us; let us follow, that we may be fed.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:1
verses.text: Sermon LIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:2
verses.text: [CIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:4
verses.text: ]  Again, on the words of the Gospel, Luke x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:5
verses.text: 38, etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:6
verses.text: , about Martha and Mary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:8
verses.text: When the holy Gospel was being read, we heard that the Lord was received by a religious woman into her house, and her name was Martha.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:9
verses.text: And while she was occupied in the care of serving, her sister Mary was sitting at the Lord's Feet, and hearing His Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:10
verses.text: The one was busy, the other was still; one was giving out, the other was being filled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:11
verses.text: Yet Martha, all busy as she was in that occupation and toil of serving, appealed to the Lord, and 			 complained of her sister, that she did not help her in her labour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:12
verses.text: But the Lord answered Martha for Mary; and He became her Advocate, who had been appealed to as Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:13
verses.text: "Martha," He saith, "thou art occupied about many things, when one thing is necessary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:14
verses.text: Mary hath chosen the better part, which shall not be taken from her".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:15
verses.text: For we have heard both the appeal of the appellant, and the sentence of the Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:16
verses.text: Which sentence answered the appellant, defended the other's cause.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:17
verses.text: For Mary was intent on the sweetness of the Lord's word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:18
verses.text: Martha was intent, how she might feed the Lord; Mary intent how she might be fed by the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:19
verses.text: By Martha a feast was being prepared for the Lord, in whose feast Mary was even now delighting herself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:20
verses.text: As Mary then was listening with sweet pleasure to His most sweet word, 			 and was feeding with the most earnest affection, when the Lord was appealed to by her sister, how, think we, did she fear, lest the Lord should say to her, "Rise and help thy sister"? For by a wondrous sweetness was she held; a sweetness of the mind which is doubtless greater than that of the senses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:21
verses.text: She was excused, she sat in greater confidence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:22
verses.text: And how excused? Let us consider, examine, investigate it thoroughly as we can, that we may be fed also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:23
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:24
verses.text: For what, do we imagine that Martha's serving was blamed, whom the cares of hospitality had engaged, who had received the Lord Himself into her house? How could she be rightly blamed, who was gladdened by so great a guest? If this be true, let men give over their ministrations to the needy; let them choose for themselves "the better part, which shall not be taken from" them; let them give themselves wholly to the word, let them long after the sweetness of doctrine; be occupied about the saving knowledge; let it be no care to them, what stranger is in the street, who there is that wants bread, or clothing, or to be visited, to be redeemed, to be buried; let works of mercy cease, earnest heed be given to knowledge only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:25
verses.text: If this be "the better part," why do not all do this, when we have the Lord Himself for our defender in this behalf? For we do not fear in this matter, 			 lest we should offend His justice, when we have the support of His judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:26
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:27
verses.text: And yet it is not so; but as the Lord spake so it is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:28
verses.text: It is not as thou understandest; but it is as thou oughtest to understand it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:29
verses.text: So mark; "Thou art occupied about many things, when one thing is needful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:30
verses.text: Mary hath chosen the better part".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:31
verses.text: Thou hast not chosen a bad part; but she a better.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:32
verses.text: And how better? Because thou art "about many things," she about "one thing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:33
verses.text: One is preferred to many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:34
verses.text: For one does not come from many, but many from one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:35
verses.text: The things which were made, are many, He who made them is One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:36
verses.text: The heaven, the earth, the sea, and all things that in them are, how many are they! Who could enumerate them? who conceive their vast number? Who made all these? God made them all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:37
verses.text: Behold, "they are very good".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:38
verses.text: Very good are the things He made; how much better is He who made them! Let us consider then our "occupations about many things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:39
verses.text: Much serving is necessary for the refreshment of our bodies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:40
verses.text: Wherefore is this? Because we hunger, and thirst.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:41
verses.text: Mercy is necessary for the miserable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:42
verses.text: Thou breakest bread to the hungry; because thou hast found an hungry man; take hunger away; to whom dost thou break bread? Take houseless wandering away; to whom dost thou show hospitality? Take nakedness away; to whom dost thou furnish clothes? Let there be no sickness; whom dost thou visit? No captivity; whom dost thou redeem? No quarrelling; whom dost thou reconcile? No death; whom dost thou bury? In that world to come, these evils will not be; therefore these services will not be either.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:43
verses.text: Well then did Martha, as touching the bodily—what shall I call it, want, or will, of the Lord?—minister to His mortal flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:44
verses.text: But 			 who was He in that mortal flesh? "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God:" see what Mary was listening to! "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us:" see to whom Martha was ministering! Therefore "hath Mary chosen the better part, which shall not be taken from her".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:45
verses.text: For she chose that which shall abide for ever; "it shall not be taken from her".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:46
verses.text: She wished to be occupied about "one thing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:47
verses.text: She understood already, "But it is good for me to cleave to the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:48
verses.text: She sat at the feet of our Head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:49
verses.text: The more lowlily she sat, the more amply did she receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:50
verses.text: For the water flows together to the low hollows of the valley, runs down from the risings of the hill.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:51
verses.text: The Lord then did not blame Martha's work, but distinguished between their services.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:52
verses.text: "Thou art occupied about many things; yet one thing is needful".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:53
verses.text: Already hath Mary chosen this for herself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:54
verses.text: The labour of manifoldness passeth away, and the love of unity abideth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:55
verses.text: Therefore what 			 she hath chosen, "shall not be taken from her".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:56
verses.text: But from thee, that which thou hast chosen (of course this follows, of course this is understood) from thee, that which thou hast chosen shall be taken away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:57
verses.text: But to thy blessedness shall it be taken away, that that which is better may be given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:58
verses.text: For labour shall be taken away from thee, that rest may be given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:59
verses.text: Thou art still on the sea, she is already in port.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:60
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:61
verses.text: Ye see then, dearly Beloved, and, as I suppose, ye understand already, that in these two women, who were both well pleasing to the Lord, both objects of His love, both disciples; ye see, I say (and an important thing it is which whosoever understand, understand hereby, a thing which, even those of you who do not understand ought to give ear to, and to know), that in these two women the two lives are figured, the life present, and the life to come, the life of 			 labour, and the life of quiet, the life of sorrow, and the life of blessedness, the life temporal, and the life eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:62
verses.text: These are the two lives: do ye think of them more fully.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:63
verses.text: What this life contains, I speak not of a life of evil, or iniquity, or wickedness, or luxuriousness, or ungodliness; but of labour, and full of sorrows, by fears subdued, by temptations disquieted: even this harmless life I mean, such as was suitable for Martha: this life I say, examine as best ye can; and as I have 			 said, think of it more fully than I speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:64
verses.text: But a wicked life was far from that house, and was neither with Martha nor with Mary; and if it ever had been, it fled at the Lord's entrance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:65
verses.text: There remained then in that house, which had received the Lord, in the two women the two lives, both harmless, both praiseworthy; the one of labour, the other of ease; neither vicious, neither slothful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:66
verses.text: Both harmless, both, I say, praiseworthy: but one of labour, the other of ease: neither vicious, which the 			 life of labour must beware of; neither slothful, which the life of ease must beware of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:67
verses.text: There were then in that house these two lives, and Himself, the Fountain of life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:68
verses.text: In Martha was the image of things present, in Mary of things to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:69
verses.text: What Martha was doing, that we are now; what Mary was doing, that we hope for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:70
verses.text: Let us do the first well, that we may have the second fully.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:71
verses.text: For what of it have we now? How far have we it? As long as we are here, how much of it is there that we have? For in 			 some measure are we employed in it now, and ye too when removed from business, and laying aside domestic cares, ye meet together, stand, listen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:72
verses.text: In so far as ye do this, ye are like Mary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:73
verses.text: And with greater facility do ye do that which Mary doeth, than I who have to distribute.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:74
verses.text: Yet if I say ought, it is Christ's; therefore doth it feed you, because it is Christ's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:75
verses.text: For the Bread is common to us all, of which I too live as well as you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:76
verses.text: "But now we live, if ye, Brethren, stand fast in the 			 Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:77
verses.text: I would not that ye should stand fast in us, but in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 53:78
verses.text: "For neither is he that planteth anything, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:1
verses.text: Sermon LV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:2
verses.text: [CV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:5
verses.text: 5, "Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:7
verses.text: We have heard our Lord, the Heavenly Master, and most faithful Counsellor exhorting us, who at once exhorteth us to ask, and giveth when we ask.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:8
verses.text: We have heard Him in the Gospel exhorting us to ask instantly, and to knock even after the likeness of intrusive importunity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:9
verses.text: For He has set before us, for the sake of example, "If any of you had a friend, and were to ask of him at night for three loaves, when a friend out of his way had come to him, and he had nothing to set before him; and he were to answer that he was now at rest, and his servants with him, and that he must not be disturbed by his entreaties; but the other were to be instant and persevering in knocking, and not being alarmed in modesty to depart, but compelled by necessity to continue on; that he would rise, though not for friendship's sake, at least for the other's importunity, and would give him as 			 many as he wished".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:10
verses.text: And how many did he wish? He wished for no more than three.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:11
verses.text: To this parable then, the Lord adjoined an exhortation, and urged us earnestly to ask, seek, knock, till we receive what we ask, and seek, and knock for, making use of an example from a contrary case; as of that "judge who neither feared God, nor regarded man," and yet when a certain widow besought him day by day, overcome by her importunity, he gave her that which he could not in kindness give her, against his will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:12
verses.text: But our Lord Jesus Christ, who is in the midst of us a Petitioner, with God a Giver, would not surely exhort us so strongly to ask, if He were not willing to give.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:13
verses.text: Let then the slothfulness of men be put to shame; He is more willing to give, than we to receive; He is more willing to show mercy, than we to be delivered 			 from misery; and doubtless if we shall not be delivered, we shall abide in misery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:14
verses.text: For the exhortation He giveth us, He giveth only for our own sakes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:16
verses.text: Let us awake, and believe Him who exhorteth us, obey Him who promiseth us, and rejoice in Him who giveth unto us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:17
verses.text: For peradventure, some time or other some friend out of his way has come to us too, and we have found nothing to set before him; and under the experience of this necessity, we have received both for ourselves and him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:18
verses.text: For it cannot be, but that some one of us hath fallen in with a friend who asked him something, which he could not answer; and then he 			 has discovered that he has it not, when he is pressed to give it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:19
verses.text: A friend has come to thee "out of the way," out, that is, of the life of this world, in which all men are passing along as strangers, and no one abides here as possessor; but to every man it is said, "Thou hast been refreshed, pass on, go on thy way, give place to the next comer".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:20
verses.text: Or perhaps from an evil "way," that is, from an evil life, some friend of thine wearied out, and not finding the truth, by the hearing and perceiving of which he may be made happy, but exhausted amid all the lust and poverty of the world, comes to thee, as to a Christian, and says, "Give me an account of this, make me a Christian".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:21
verses.text: And he asks what it may be thou didst not know through the simplicity of thy faith; and so thou hast not whereby to recruit him in his 			 hunger, and reminded thus thou discoverest thine own indigence; and when thou wishest to teach thou art forced to learn; and whilst thou dost blush before him who asked thee, as not finding in thyself what he was seeking for, thou art compelled to seek, that thou mayest be thought worthy to find.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:23
verses.text: And where shouldest thou seek.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:24
verses.text: Where but in the books of the Lord? Peradventure what he has asked is contained in the book, but it is obscure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:25
verses.text: Perhaps the Apostle has declared it in some Epistle: declared it in such wise, that thou canst read, but canst not understand it: thou art not permitted to pass on.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:26
verses.text: For the interrogator urges thee; Paul himself, or Peter, or any of the Prophets thou art not allowed to ask.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:27
verses.text: For this family is now at rest with their Lord, and 			 intense is the ignorance of this life, that is, it is midnight, and thy hungry friend is urgent upon thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:28
verses.text: A simple faith haply sufficed thee, him it suffices not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:29
verses.text: Is he then to be abandoned? Is he to be cast out of thy house? Therefore unto the Lord Himself, unto Him with whom the family is at rest, knock by prayer, ask, be instant.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:30
verses.text: He will not, as that friend in the parable, arise and give thee as overcome by importunity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:31
verses.text: He wisheth to give; thou for thy knocking hast not yet received; knock 			 on; He wisheth to give.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:32
verses.text: And what He wisheth to give, He deferreth, that thou mayest long the more for it when deferred, lest if given quickly it should be lightly esteemed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:33
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:34
verses.text: But when thou hast gotten the three loaves, that is, to feed on and understand the Trinity, thou hast that whereby thou mayest both live thyself, and feed others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:35
verses.text: Now thou needest not fear the stranger who comes out of his way to thee, but by taking him in mayest make him a citizen of the household: nor needest thou fear lest thou come to the end of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:36
verses.text: That Bread will not come to an end, but it will put an end to thine indigence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:37
verses.text: It is Bread, God the Father, and it is 			 Bread, God the Son, and it is Bread, God the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:38
verses.text: The Father Eternal, the Son Coeternal with Him, and the Holy Ghost Coeternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:39
verses.text: The Father Unchangeable, the Son Unchangeable, the Holy Ghost Unchangeable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:40
verses.text: The Father Creator, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:41
verses.text: The Father the Shepherd and the Giver of life, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:42
verses.text: The Father the Food and Bread eternal, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:43
verses.text: Learn, and teach; live thyself, and feed others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:44
verses.text: God who giveth to thee, giveth 			 thee nothing better than Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:45
verses.text: O thou greedy one, what else wast thou seeking for? Or if thou seek for aught else, what will suffice thee whom God doth suffice not?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:46
verses.text: But necessary it is that thou have charity, that thou have faith, that thou have hope; that that which is given may be sweet unto thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:47
verses.text: And these same, faith, hope, charity, are three.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:48
verses.text: And these too are gifts of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:49
verses.text: For faith we have received from Him; "As God," saith he, "hath distributed to every one the measure of faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:50
verses.text: And hope we have received from Him, to whom it is said, "Wherein Thou hast caused me to hope".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:51
verses.text: And charity we have received from Him, of whom it is said, "The charity of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost, which hath been given to us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:52
verses.text: Now these three are likewise in some measure different; but all gifts of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:53
verses.text: For "there abide these three, faith, hope, charity; but the greatest of these is charity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:54
verses.text: In those loaves it is not said that any one loaf was greater than the others; but simply that three loaves were asked for, and were given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:55
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:56
verses.text: See other three things: "Who is there of you, whom if his son ask a loaf, will he give him a stone? Or who is there of you of whom if his son ask a fish, will he give him a serpent? or if he ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion? If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him!" Let us then again consider these three things, if haply there be not here those three, "faith, hope, charity; but the greatest of these is charity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:57
verses.text: Set down then these three things, a loaf, a fish, an egg; the greatest of these is a loaf.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:58
verses.text: Therefore in these three things do we well understand charity by "the loaf".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:59
verses.text: On which account He has opposed a stone to a loaf; because hardness is contrary to charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:60
verses.text: By "a fish" we understand faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:61
verses.text: A certain holy man has 			 said, and we are glad to say it too; "The 'good fish' is a godly faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:62
verses.text: It lives amidst the waves, and is not broken or dissolved by the waves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:63
verses.text: Amidst the temptations and tempests of this world, liveth godly faith; the world rages, yet it is uninjured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:64
verses.text: Observe only that serpent is contrary to faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:65
verses.text: For My faith is she betrothed to whom it is said in the Song of Songs, "Come from Lebanon, My spouse, coming and passing over to Me from the beginning of faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:66
verses.text: Therefore betrothed too, because faith is the beginning of betrothal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:67
verses.text: For something is promised by the bridegroom, and by this plighted faith is he held bound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:68
verses.text: Now to the fish the Lord opposed the serpent, to faith the devil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:69
verses.text: Wherefore to this betrothed one does the Apostle say, "I have betrothed you to One Husband, to present you a chaste virgin to Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:70
verses.text: And, "I fear lest as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds also should be corrupted from 			 the purity which is in Christ;" that is, which is in the faith of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:71
verses.text: For he says, "That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:72
verses.text: Therefore let not the devil corrupt our faith, let him not devour the fish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:73
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:74
verses.text: There remains hope, which, as I think, is compared to an egg.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:75
verses.text: For hope has not yet arrived at attainment; and an egg is something, but not yet the chicken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:76
verses.text: So then quadrupeds give birth to young ones, but birds to the hope of young.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:77
verses.text: Hope therefore exhorts us to this, to despise things present, to wait for things to come; "forgetting those things which are behind," let us, with the Apostle," reach forth unto those things which are before".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:78
verses.text: For so he says; "But one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, reaching forth unto those things which are before, I follow on earnestly unto the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:79
verses.text: Nothing then is so hostile to hope, as to "look back," to place hope, that is, in those things which flit by and pass away; but in those things should we place it, which are not yet given, but which sometime will be given, and will never pass away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:80
verses.text: But when the 			 world is deluged by trials, as it were the sulphureous rain of Sodom, the example of Lot's wife must be feared.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:81
verses.text: For she "looked behind;" and in the spot where she looked behind, there did she remain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:82
verses.text: She was turned into salt, that she might season the wise by her example.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:83
verses.text: Of this hope the Apostle Paul speaketh thus; "For we are saved in hope; but hope that is seen is not hope; for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for: but if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:84
verses.text: For what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:85
verses.text: It is an egg, and not as yet the chicken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:86
verses.text: And it is covered with a shell; it is not seen because it is covered; let it be with patience waited for; let it feel the warmth, that it may come to life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:87
verses.text: Press on, "reach forth unto the things which are before, forget the past.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:88
verses.text: For the things which are seen, are temporal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:89
verses.text: Not looking back," says he, "at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:90
verses.text: For the things which are seen are temporal; but the things 			 which are not seen are eternal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:91
verses.text: Unto those things which are not seen then extend thy hope, wait, endure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:92
verses.text: Look not back.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:93
verses.text: Fear "the scorpion" for thine "egg".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:94
verses.text: See how he wounds with the tail, which he has behind him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:95
verses.text: Let not then the "scorpion" crush thine "egg," let not this world crush thy hope (so to say) with its poison, therefore against thee, because behind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:96
verses.text: How loudly does the world talk to thee, what an uproar does it make behind thy back, that thou mayest look back! that is, that thou 			 mayest place thy hope in present things (and yet not even present, for they cannot be called present which have no fixedness), and mayest turn thy mind away from that which Christ hath promised, and not yet given, but who, seeing He is faithful, will give it, and mayest be content to look for rest in a perishing world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:97
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:98
verses.text: For this cause does God mingle bitternesses with the felicities of earth, that another felicity may be sought, in whose sweetness there is no deceit; yet by these very bitternesses does the world endeavour to turn thee away from thy longing pursuit after the things "which are before," and to turn thee back.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:99
verses.text: For these bitternesses, for these tribulations dost thou murmur and say, "See, all things are perishing in Christian times".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:100
verses.text: What 			 complaint is this! God hath not promised me that these things shall not perish; Christ hath not promised me this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:101
verses.text: The Eternal hath promised things eternal: if I believe, from a mortal, I shall be made eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:102
verses.text: What noise is this, O world impure! what murmuring is this! Why art thou trying to turn me back? Perishing as thou art, thou wishest to detain me; what wouldest thou do, if thou hadst any permanence? Whom wouldest thou not beguile by thy sweetness, if with all thy bitternesses thou dost impose thy false nourishment upon us? For me, if I have hope, if I hold fast my hope, my "egg" has not been wounded by the "scorpion".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:103
verses.text: "I will bless the Lord at all times, His praise shall be ever in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:104
verses.text: Be the world prosperous, or be the world turned upside down; "I will bless the Lord," who made the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:105
verses.text: Yes, verily, I will bless Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:106
verses.text: Be it well with me according to the flesh, or be it ill according to the flesh, "I will bless the Lord at all times, His praise shall be ever in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:107
verses.text: For if I bless when it is well, and blaspheme when it is ill with me; I have received the "scorpion's" sting, being pricked "I have looked back;" which be far from us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:108
verses.text: "The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away: it is done, as the Lord pleased; blessed be the name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:109
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:110
verses.text: The city which has given us birth according to the flesh still abideth, God be thanked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:111
verses.text: O that it may receive a spiritual birth, and together with us pass over unto eternity! If the city which has given us birth according to the flesh abide not, yet that which has given us birth according to the Spirit abides for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:112
verses.text: "The Lord doth build up Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:113
verses.text: Has He by sleeping brought His building to ruin, or by not keeping it, let the enemy into it? "Except the Lord keep the city, he that keepeth it waketh but in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:114
verses.text: And what "city"? "He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:115
verses.text: What is Israel, but the seed of Abraham? What the seed of Abraham, but Christ? "And to thy seed," he says, "which is Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:116
verses.text: And to us what says he? "But ye are Christ's, therefore Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:117
verses.text: "In thy seed," saith He, "shall all nations be blessed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:118
verses.text: The holy city, the faithful city, the city on earth a sojourner, hath its foundation in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:119
verses.text: O faithful one, do not corrupt thy hope, do not lose thy charity, "gird up thy loins," light, and hold out thy lamps before thee; "wait for the Lord, when He will return from the wedding".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:120
verses.text: Why art thou alarmed, because the kingdoms of the earth are perishing? Therefore hath a heavenly kingdom been promised thee, that thou mightest not perish with the kingdoms of the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:121
verses.text: For it was foretold, foretold distinctly, that they should perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:122
verses.text: For we cannot deny that it was foretold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:123
verses.text: Thy Lord for whom thou art waiting, hath told thee, "Nation shall rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:124
verses.text: The kingdoms of the earth have their changes; He will come of whom it is said, "and of His kingdom there shall be no end".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:125
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:126
verses.text: They who have promised this to earthly kingdoms have not been guided by truth, but have lied through flattery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:127
verses.text: A certain poet of theirs has introduced Jupiter speaking, and he says of the Romans;  To them no bounds of empire I assign,  Nor term of years to their immortal line.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:128
verses.text: Most certainly truth makes no such answer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:129
verses.text: This empire which thou hast given "without term of years," is it on earth, or in heaven? On earth assuredly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:130
verses.text: And even if it were in heaven, yet "heaven and earth shall pass away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:131
verses.text: Those things shall pass away which God hath Himself made; how much more rapidly shall that pass away which Romulus founded! Perhaps if we had a mind to press Virgil on this point, and tauntingly to ask him why he said it; he would take us aside privately, and say to us, "I know this as well as you, but what could I do who was selling words to the Romans, if by this kind of flattery I did not promise something which was false? And yet even in this very instance I have been 			 cautious, when I said, 'I assigned to them an empire without term of years,' I introduced their Jupiter to say it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:132
verses.text: I did not utter this falsehood in my own person, but put upon Jupiter the character of untruthfulness: as the god was false, the poet was false.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:133
verses.text: For would ye know that I well knew the truth of it? In another place, when I did not introduce this stone, called Jupiter, but spoke in my own person, I said,  'Th' impending ruin of the Roman state.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:134
verses.text: '  See how I spoke of the impending ruin of the state.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:135
verses.text: I spoke of its impending ruin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:136
verses.text: I did not suppress it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:137
verses.text: When he spoke in truth he was not silent as to its ruin; when in flattery, he promised that it should abide for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:138
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:139
verses.text: Let us not then faint, my Brethren: an end there will be to all earthly kingdoms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:140
verses.text: If that end be now, God knoweth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:141
verses.text: For peradventure it is not yet, and we, through some infirmity, or mercifulness, or misery, are wishing that it may not be yet; nevertheless will it not therefore some day be? Fix your hope in God, desire the things eternal, wait for the things eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:142
verses.text: Ye are Christians, Brethren, we are all Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:143
verses.text: Christ did not come down into 			 the flesh that we might live softly; let us endure rather than love the things present; manifest is the harm of adversity, deceitful is the soft blandishment of prosperity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:144
verses.text: Fear the sea, even when it is a calm.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:145
verses.text: On no account let us hear in vain, "Let us lift up our hearts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:146
verses.text: Why place we our hearts in the earth, when we see that the earth is being turned upside down? We cannot but exhort you, that ye may have something to say and answer in defence of your hope against the deriders and 			 blasphemers of the Christian name.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:147
verses.text: Let no one by his murmuring turn you back from waiting for the things to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:148
verses.text: All who by reason of these adversities blaspheme our Christ, are the "scorpion's" tail.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:149
verses.text: Let us put our egg under the wings of that Hen of the Gospel, which crieth out to that false and abandoned city, "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen her chickens, and thou wouldest not!" Let it not be said to us, "How often would I, and thou wouldest not!" For that hen is the Divine Wisdom; but assumed flesh to accommodate Itself to its chickens.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:150
verses.text: See the hen with feathers bristling, with wings hanging down, with voice broken, and tremulous, and faint, and languid, accommodating herself to her little ones.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:151
verses.text: Our egg then, that is, our hope, let us place beneath the wings of this Hen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:152
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:153
verses.text: Ye have noticed, it may be, how a hen will tear a scorpion in pieces.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:154
verses.text: O then that the Hen of the Gospel would tear in pieces and devour these blasphemers, creeping out of their holes, and inflicting hurtful stings, would pass them over into Her Body, and turn them into an egg.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:155
verses.text: Let them not be angry; we seem to be excited; but we do not return curses for curses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:156
verses.text: "We are cursed, and we bless, being defamed, we entreat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:157
verses.text: But "let him not speak of Rome, it is said of me: O that he would hold his tongue about Rome;" as though I were insulting it, and not rather entreating the Lord for it, and exhorting you all, unworthy as I am.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:158
verses.text: Be it far from me to insult it! The Lord avert this from my heart, and from the grief of my conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:159
verses.text: Have we not had many brethren there? have we not still? Does not a large portion of the pilgrim city Jerusalem live there? has it not endured there temporal 			 afflictions? but it has not lost the things eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:160
verses.text: What can I say then, when I speak of Rome, but that is false, which they say of our Christ, that He is Rome's destroyer, and that the gods of wood and stone were her defenders? Add what is more costly, "gods of brass".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:161
verses.text: Add what is costlier still, "of silver and gold:" the "idols of the nations are silver and gold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:162
verses.text: He did not say, "stone;" he did not say, "wood;" he did not say, "clay;" but, what they value highly, "silver and gold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:163
verses.text: Yet these silver and golden idols "have eyes, and see not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:164
verses.text: The gods of gold, of wood, are as regards their costliness unequal; but as to "having eyes, and seeing not," they are equal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:165
verses.text: See to what sort of guardians learned men have entrusted Rome, to those "who have eyes, and see not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:166
verses.text: Or if they were able to preserve Rome, why did they first perish themselves? They say; "Rome perished at the same time".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:167
verses.text: Nevertheless they perished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:168
verses.text: "No," they say, "they did not perish themselves, but their statues".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:169
verses.text: Well, how then 			 could they keep your houses, who were not able to keep their own statues? Alexandria once lost such gods as these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:170
verses.text: Constantinople some time since, ever since it was made a grand city, for it was made so by a Christian Emperor, lost its false gods; and yet it has increased, and still increases, and remains.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:171
verses.text: And remain it will, as long as God pleases.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:172
verses.text: For we do not to this city either promise an eternal duration because we say this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:173
verses.text: Carthage remains now in its possession of the Name of Christ, 			 yet once on a time its goddess Caelestis was overthrown; because celestial she was not, but terrestrial.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:174
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:175
verses.text: And that which they say is not true, that immediately on losing her gods Rome has been taken and ruined.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:176
verses.text: It is not true at all; their images were overthrown before; and even so were the Goths with Rhadagaisus conquered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:177
verses.text: Remember, my Brethren, remember; it is no long time since, but a few years, call it to mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:178
verses.text: When all the images in the city of Rome had been overthrown, Rhadagaisus king of the Goths came with a large army, much more numerous than that of Alaric was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:179
verses.text: Rhadagaisus was a Pagan; he sacrificed to Jupiter every day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:180
verses.text: Everywhere it was announced, that Rhadagaisus did not cease from sacrificing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:181
verses.text: Then said they all, "Lo, we do not sacrifice, he does sacrifice, we, who are 			 not allowed to sacrifice must be conquered by him who does sacrifice".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:182
verses.text: But God making proof that not even temporal deliverance, nor the preservation of these earthly kingdoms, consist in these sacrifices, Rhadagaisus, by the Lord's help, was marvellously overcome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:183
verses.text: Afterwards came other Goths who did not sacrifice, they came, who though they were not Catholics in the Christian faith, were yet hostile and opposed to idols, and they took Rome; they conquered those who 			 put their trust in idols, who were still seeking after the idols they had lost, and desiring still to sacrifice to the lost gods.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:184
verses.text: And amongst them too were some of our brethren, and these were afflicted also: but they had learnt to say, "I will bless the Lord at all times".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:185
verses.text: They were involved in the afflictions of their earthly kingdom: but they lost not the kingdom of heaven; yea, rather, they were made the better for obtaining it through the exercise of tribulations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:186
verses.text: And if they did not in their tribulations blaspheme, they came out as sound vessels from the furnace, and were filled with the blessing of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:187
verses.text: Whereas those blasphemers, who follow and long after earthly things, who place their hope in earthly things, when these they have 			 lost, whether they will or no, what shall they retain? where shall they abide? Nothing without, nothing within; an empty coffer, an emptier conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 54:188
verses.text: Where is their rest? where their salvation? where their hope? Let them then come, let them give over blaspheming, let them learn to adore; let the scorpions with their stings be devoured by the Hen, let them be turned into His body who makes them pass over into it; let them on earth be exercised, in heaven be crowned.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:1
verses.text: Sermon LVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:2
verses.text: [CVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:5
verses.text: 39, "Now do ye Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the platter," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:7
verses.text: Ye have heard the holy Gospel, how the Lord Jesus in that which He said to the Pharisees, conveyed doubtless a lesson to His own disciples, that they should not think that righteousness consists in the cleansing of the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:8
verses.text: For every day did the Pharisees wash themselves in water before they dined; as if a daily washing could be a cleansing of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:9
verses.text: Then He showed what sort of persons they were.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:10
verses.text: He told them who saw them; for He saw 			 not their faces only but their inward parts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:11
verses.text: For that ye may know this, that Pharisee, to whom Christ made answer, thought within himself, he uttered nothing aloud, yet the Lord heard him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:12
verses.text: For within himself he blamed the Lord Christ, because He had so come to his feast without having washed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:13
verses.text: He was thinking, the Lord heard, therefore He answered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:14
verses.text: What then did He answer? "Now do ye Pharisees wash the outside of the platter; but within ye are full of guile and ravening".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:15
verses.text: What! is this to come to a feast! how did He not spare the man by whom He had been invited? Yea rather by rebuking He did spare him, that being reformed He might spare him in the judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:16
verses.text: And what is it that He showeth to us? That Baptism also which is conferred once for all, cleanses by faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:17
verses.text: Now faith is within, not without.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:18
verses.text: Wherefore it is said and read in the Acts of the Apostles, "Cleansing their hearts by faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:19
verses.text: And the Apostle Peter thus speaks in his Epistle; "So too hath He given you a similitude from Noah's ark, how that eight souls were saved by water".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:20
verses.text: And then he added, "So also in a like figure will baptism save us, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:21
verses.text: "This answer of a good conscience" did the Pharisees despise, and washed "that which was without;" within they continued full of pollution.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:23
verses.text: And what did He say to them after this? "But rather give alms, and behold all things are clean unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:24
verses.text: See the praise of alms, do, and prove it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:25
verses.text: But mark awhile; this was said to the Pharisees.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:26
verses.text: These Pharisees were Jews, the choice men as it were of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:27
verses.text: For those of most consideration and learning were then called Pharisees.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:28
verses.text: They had not been washed by Christ's Baptism; they had not yet believed on Christ, the Only-begotten Son of God, who walked among them, yet was not acknowledged by them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:29
verses.text: How then doth He say to them, "Give alms, and behold all things are clean 			 unto you"? If the Pharisees had paid heed to Him, and given alms, at once according to His word "all things would have been clean to them;" what need then was there for them to believe on Him? But if they could not be cleansed, except by believing on Him, who "cleanseth the heart by faith;" what means, "Give alms, and behold all things are clean unto you"? Let us carefully consider this, and peradventure He Himself explains it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:31
verses.text: When He had spoken thus, doubtless they thought that they did give alms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:32
verses.text: And how did they give them? They tithed all they had, they took away a tenth of all their produce, and gave it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:33
verses.text: It is no easy matter to find a Christian who doth as much.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:34
verses.text: See what the Jews did.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:35
verses.text: Not wheat only, but wine, and oil; nor this only, but even the most trifling things, cummin, rue, mint, and anise, in obedience to God's precept, they tithed all; put aside, that is, a tenth part, and gave alms of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:36
verses.text: I suppose then that they recalled this to mind, and thought that the Lord Christ was speaking to no purpose, as if to those who did not give alms; whereas they knew their own doings, how that they tithed, and gave alms of the minutest and most trifling of their produce.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:37
verses.text: They mocked Him within themselves as He spake thus, as if to men who did not give alms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:38
verses.text: The Lord knowing 			 this, immediately subjoined, "But woe unto you, Scribes and Pharisees, who tithe mint, and cummin, and rue, and all herbs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:39
verses.text: That ye may know, I am aware of your alms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:40
verses.text: Doubtless these tithes are your alms; yea even the minutest and most trifling of your fruits do ye tithe; "Yet ye leave the weightier matters of the law, judgment and charity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:41
verses.text: Mark.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:42
verses.text: Ye have "left judgment and charity," and ye tithe herbs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:43
verses.text: This is not to do alms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:44
verses.text: "These," saith He, "ought ye to do, and not to leave the other undone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:45
verses.text: Do what? "Judgment and charity, justice and mercy;" and "not to leave the other 			 undone".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:46
verses.text: Do these; but give the preference to the others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:47
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:48
verses.text: If this be so, why did He say to them, "Do alms, and behold all things are clean unto you"? What is, "Do alms"? Do mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:49
verses.text: What is, "Do mercy"? If thou understand, begin with thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:50
verses.text: For how shouldest thou be merciful to another, if thou art cruel to thyself? "Give alms, and all things are clean unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:51
verses.text: Do true alms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:52
verses.text: What is alms? Mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:53
verses.text: Hear the Scripture; "Have mercy on thine own soul, pleasing God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:54
verses.text: Do alms, "Have mercy on thine own soul, pleasing God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:55
verses.text: Thine own soul is a beggar before thee, return to thy conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:56
verses.text: Whosoever thou art, who art living in wickedness or unbelief, return to thy conscience; and there thou findest thy soul in beggary, thou findest it needy, thou findest it poor, thou findest it in sorrow, nay perhaps thou dost not find it in need, but dumb through its neediness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:57
verses.text: For if it beg, it "hungereth after righteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:58
verses.text: Now when thou findest 			 thy soul in such a state (all this is within, in thy heart), first do alms, give it bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:59
verses.text: What bread? If the Pharisee had asked this question, the Lord would have said to him, "Give alms to thine own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:60
verses.text: For this He did say to him; but he did not understand it, when He enumerated to them the alms which they were used to do, and which they thought were unknown to Christ; and He saith to them, "I know that ye do this, 'ye tithe mint and anise, cummin and rue;' but I am speaking of 			 other alms; ye despise 'judgment and charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:61
verses.text: ' In judgment and charity give alms to thine own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:62
verses.text: What is "in judgment"? Look back, and discover thyself; mislike thyself, pronounce a judgment against thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:63
verses.text: And what is charity? "Love the Lord God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind; love thy neighbour as thyself:" and thou hast done alms first to thine own soul, within thy conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:64
verses.text: Whereas if thou neglect this alms, give what thou wilt, give how much thou wilt; reserve of thy goods not a tenth, but a half; give nine parts, and leave but one for thine own self: thou doest nothing, when thou doest not alms to thine own soul, and art poor in thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:65
verses.text: Let thy soul have its food, that it perish not by famine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:66
verses.text: Give her bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:67
verses.text: What bread, thou wilt say? He speaketh with thee Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:68
verses.text: If 			 thou wouldest hear, and understand, and believe the Lord, He would say to thee Himself, "I am the Living Bread which came down from heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:69
verses.text: Wouldest thou not first give this Bread to thine own soul, and do alms unto it? If then thou believest, thou oughtest so to do, that thou mayest first feed thine own soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:70
verses.text: Believe in Christ, and the things which are within shall be cleansed; and what is without shall be clean also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 55:71
verses.text: "Let us turn to the Lord," etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:1
verses.text: Sermon LVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:2
verses.text: [CVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:5
verses.text: 15, "And he said unto them, take heed, and keep yourselves from all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:7
verses.text: I doubt not but that ye who fear God, do hear His word with awe, and execute it with cheerfulness; that what He hath promised, ye may at present hope for, hereafter receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:8
verses.text: We have just now heard the Lord Christ Jesus, the Son of God, giving us a precept.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:9
verses.text: The Truth, who neither deceiveth, nor is deceived, hath given us a precept; let us hear, fear, beware.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:10
verses.text: What is this precept then: "I say unto you, Beware of all covetousness"? 			  What is, "of all covetousness"? What is, "of all"? Why did He add, "of all"? For He might have spoken thus, "Beware of covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:11
verses.text: It suited Him to add, "of all;" and to say, "Beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:12
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:13
verses.text: Why He said this, the occasion as it were out of which these words arose, is shown to us in the holy Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:14
verses.text: A certain man appealed to Him against his brother, who had taken away all his patrimony, and gave not back his proper portion to his brother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:15
verses.text: Ye see then how good a case this appellant had.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:16
verses.text: For he was not seeking to take by violence another's, but was seeking only for his own which had been left him by his parents; these was he demanding back by his appeal to 			 the judgment of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:17
verses.text: He had an unrighteous brother; but against an unrighteous brother had he found a righteous Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:18
verses.text: Ought he then in so good a cause to lose that opportunity? Or who would say to his brother, "Restore to thy brother his portion," if Christ would not say it? Would that judge be likely to say it, whom perhaps his richer and extortionate brother might corrupt by a bribe? Forlorn then as he was, and despoiled of his father's goods, when he had found 			 such and so great a Judge he goes up to Him, he appeals to, he beseeches Him, he lays his cause before Him in few words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:19
verses.text: For what occasion was there to set forth his cause at length, when he was speaking to Him who could even see the heart? "Master," he says, "speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:20
verses.text: The Lord did not say to him, "Let thy brother come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:21
verses.text: No, He neither sent for him to be present, nor in his presence did He say to him who had appealed to Him, "Prove what thou wast saying".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:22
verses.text: He asked for half an inheritance, he asked for half an inheritance on earth; the Lord offered him a whole inheritance in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:23
verses.text: The Lord gave more than asked for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:24
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:25
verses.text: "Speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:26
verses.text: Just case, short case.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:27
verses.text: But let us hear Him who at once gives judgment and instruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:28
verses.text: "Man," He saith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:29
verses.text: "O man;" for seeing thou valuest this inheritance so highly, what art thou but a man? He wished to make him something more than man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:30
verses.text: What more did He wish to make him, from whom He wished to take covetousness away? What more did He wish to make him? I will tell you, "I have said, Ye 			 are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:31
verses.text: Lo, what He wished to make him, to reckon him that hath no covetousness among the "gods".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:32
verses.text: "Man, who made Me a divider among you?" So the Apostle Paul His servant, when he said, "I beseech you, brethren, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no schisms among you," was unwilling to be a divider.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:33
verses.text: And afterwards he thus admonished them who were running after his name, and dividing Christ: "Every one of you saith, I am of Paul, and I of Apollos, and I of Cephas, and I of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:34
verses.text: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?" Judge then, how wicked are those men, who would have Him to be divided, who would not be a divider.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:35
verses.text: "Who," saith He, "hath made Me a divider among you?"  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:36
verses.text: Thou hast petitioned for a kindness; hear counsel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:37
verses.text: "I say unto you, Beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:38
verses.text: "Perhaps," he would say, "thou wouldest call him covetous and greedy, if he were seeking another's goods; but I say, seek not even thine own greedily or covetously".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:39
verses.text: This is "Of all, beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:40
verses.text: A heavy burden this! If by any chance this burden be imposed on them that are weak; let Him be sought unto, that He who imposes it, may vouchsafe to give us strength.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:41
verses.text: For it is not a thing to be lightly regarded, my Brethren, when our Lord, our Redeemer, 			 our Saviour, who died for us, who gave His Own Blood as our ransom, to redeem us, our Advocate and Judge; it is no light matter when He saith, "Beware".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:42
verses.text: He knoweth well how great the evil is; we know it not, let us believe Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:43
verses.text: "Beware," saith He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:44
verses.text: Wherefore? of what? "of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:45
verses.text: I am but keeping what is mine own, I am not taking away another's; "Beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:46
verses.text: Not only is he covetous, who plunders the goods of others; but he is covetous too, who 			 greedily keeps his own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:47
verses.text: But if he is so blamed who greedily keeps his own; how is he condemned who plunders what is another's! "Beware," He saith, "of all covetousness: For a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:48
verses.text: He that stores up great abundance, how much does he take therefrom to live? When he has taken it, and in a way separated in thought sufficient to live upon from it, let him consider for whom the rest remains; lest haply when thou 			 keepest wherewith to live, thou art gathering only wherewith to die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:49
verses.text: Behold Christ, behold truth, behold severity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:50
verses.text: "Beware," saith truth: "Beware," saith severity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:51
verses.text: If thou love not the truth, fear severity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:52
verses.text: "A man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:53
verses.text: Believe Him, He doth not deceive thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:54
verses.text: On the other hand, thou sayest, "Yea, 'a man's life' does 'consist in the abundance of the things which he possesses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:55
verses.text: '" He doth not deceive 			 thee; thou deceivest thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:56
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:57
verses.text: Out of this occasion then, when that appellant was seeking his own portion, not desiring to plunder another's, arose that sentence of the Lord, wherein He said not, "Beware of covetousness;" but added, "of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:58
verses.text: Nor was this all: He giveth another example of a certain rich man, "whose ground had turned out well".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:59
verses.text: "There was," He saith, "a certain rich man, whose ground had turned out well".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:60
verses.text: What is, "had turned out well"? The ground which he possessed had brought forth a great produce.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:61
verses.text: How great? So that he could not find where to bestow it: suddenly, through his abundance he became straitened—this old covetous man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:62
verses.text: For how many years had already passed away, and yet those barns had been enough? So great then was the produce, that the accustomed places were not sufficient.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:63
verses.text: And the wretched man sought counsel, not as to how he should lay the 			 additional produce out, but how he should store it up; and in thinking he discovered an expedient.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:64
verses.text: He seemed as it were wise in his own eyes, by the discovery of this expedient.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:65
verses.text: Knowingly did he think of it, wisely hit upon it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:66
verses.text: What was this he wisely hit upon? "I will destroy," he says, "my" old "barns, and will build new ones greater, and will fill them; and I will say to my soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:67
verses.text: What wilt thou say to thy soul? "Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for 			 many years, take thine ease, eat, drink, be merry".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:68
verses.text: This did the wise discoverer of this expedient say to his soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:69
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:70
verses.text: "And God," who doth not disdain to speak even with fools, "said unto him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:71
verses.text: Some of you may peradventure say, And how did God speak with a fool? O, my Brethren, with how many fools does He speak here, when the Gospel is read! When it is read, are not they who hear and do not, fools? What then did the Lord say? For he, I repeat, thought himself wise by the discovery of his expedient.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:72
verses.text: "Thou fool," He saith; "Thou fool," who seemest wise unto thyself; "Thou fool," who hast said to thy soul, "Thou hast much goods laid up for many years: 			 to-day is thy soul required of thee!" Thy soul to which thou hast said, "Thou hast much goods," to-day is "required," and hath no good at all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:73
verses.text: Let it then despise these goods, and be herself good, that when she is "required," she may depart in assured hope.
