verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:74
verses.text: For what is more perverse than a man who wishes to have "much goods," and does not wish to be good himself? Unworthy art thou to have them, who dost not wish to be what thou dost wish to have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:75
verses.text: For dost thou wish to have a bad country house? No indeed, but a good one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:76
verses.text: Or a bad wife? No, but a good one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:77
verses.text: Or a bad hood? Or even a bad shoe? And why a bad soul only? He did not in this place say to this fool who was thinking on vain things, building barns, and who had no regard to the wants of the poor; He did not say to him, "To-day shall thy soul be hurried away to hell:" He said no such thing as this, but "is required of thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:78
verses.text: "I do not tell thee whither thy soul shall go; yet hence, where thou art laying up for it such store of things, must it depart, whether thou wilt or no".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:79
verses.text: Lo, "thou fool," thou hast thought to fill thy new and greater barns, as if there was nothing to be done with what thou hast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:80
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:81
verses.text: But peradventure he was not yet a Christian.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:82
verses.text: Let us hear then, Brethren, to whom as believers the Gospel is read, by whom He who spake these things, is worshipped, whose mark is borne by us on our forehead, and is held in the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:83
verses.text: For of very great concernment is it where a man hath the mark of Christ, whether in the forehead, or both in the forehead and the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:84
verses.text: Ye have heard to-day the words of the holy prophet Ezekiel, how that before God sent one to 			 destroy the ungodly people, He first sent one to mark them, and said to him, "Go and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and moan for the sins of my people that are done in the midst of them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:85
verses.text: He did not say, "which are done without them;" but "in the midst of them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:86
verses.text: Yet they "sigh and moan;" and therefore are they "marked on the forehead:" in the forehead of the inner man, not the outer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:87
verses.text: For there is a forehead in the face, there is a forehead in the conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:88
verses.text: So it happens that when the inner forehead is stricken, the outer grows red; either red with shame, or pale with fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:89
verses.text: So then there is a forehead of the inner man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:90
verses.text: There were they "marked" that they might not 			 be destroyed; because though they did not correct the sins which were "done in the midst of them," yet they sorrowed for them, and by that very sorrow separated themselves; and though separated in God's sight, they were mixed with them in the eyes of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:91
verses.text: They are "marked" secretly, are not hurt openly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:92
verses.text: Afterwards the Destroyer is sent, and to him it is said, "Go, lay waste, spare neither young nor old, male nor female, but come not near those who have the mark on their forehead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:93
verses.text: How great security is granted to you, my Brethren, who among this people are sighing, and moaning for the iniquities which are being done in the midst of you, and who do them not!  8.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:94
verses.text: But that ye may not commit iniquities, "beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:95
verses.text: I will tell you in its full extent, what is "of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:96
verses.text: In matter of lust he is covetous, whom his own wife suffices not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:97
verses.text: And idolatry itself is called covetousness; because again in matter of divine worship he is covetous, whom the one and true God suffices not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:98
verses.text: What but the covetous soul makes for itself many gods? What but the covetous soul makes to itself false martyrs? "Beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:99
verses.text: Lo, thou lovest thine own goods, and dost boast thyself in that thou seekest not the goods of others; see what evil thou doest in not hearing Christ, who saith, "Beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:100
verses.text: See thou dost love thine own goods, thou dost not take away the goods of others; thou hast the fruits of thy labour, they are justly thine; thou hast been left an heir, some one whose good graces thou hast attained has given it to thee; thou 			 hast been on the sea, and in its perils, hast committed no fraud, hast sworn no lie, hast acquired what it hath pleased God thou shouldest; and thou art keeping it greedily as in a good conscience, because thou dost not possess it from evil sources, and dost not seek what is another's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:101
verses.text: Yet if thou give not heed to Him who hath said, "Beware of all covetousness," hear how great evils thou wilt be ready to do for thine own goods' sake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:102
verses.text: Lo, for example, it hath 			 chanced to thee to be made a judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:103
verses.text: Thou wilt not be corrupted, because thou dost not seek the goods of others; no one giveth thee a bribe and says, "Give judgment against my adversary".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:104
verses.text: This be far from thee, a man, who seekest not the things of others, how couldest thou be persuaded to do this? Yet see what evil thou wilt be ready to do for thine own goods' sake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:105
verses.text: Peradventure he that wishes thee to judge evilly, and pronounce sentence for him against his adversary is a powerful man, and 			 able to bring up false accusation against thee, that thou mayest lose what thou hast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:106
verses.text: Thou dost reflect, and think upon his power, think of thine own goods thou art keeping, which thou dost love: not which thou hast possessed, but in whose power rather thou art thyself unhappily fixed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:107
verses.text: This thy bird-lime, by reason of which thou hast not the wings of virtue free, thou dost look to; and thou sayest within thine own self, "I am offending this man, he has much influence in the world; he will suggest evil accusations against me, and I shall be outlawed, and lose all I have".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:108
verses.text: Thus thou wilt give unrighteous judgment, not when thou seekest another's, but when thou keepest thine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:109
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:110
verses.text: Give me a man who has given ear to Christ, give me a man who has heard with fear "Beware of all covetousness;" and let him not say to me, "I am a poor man, a plebeian of mean estate, one of the common people, how can I hope ever to be a judge? I am in no fear of this temptation, the peril of which thou hast placed before mine eyes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:111
verses.text: Yet lo, even this poor man I will tell what he ought to fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:112
verses.text: Some rich and powerful person calls thee to give false witness for 			 him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:113
verses.text: What wilt thou be doing now? Tell me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:114
verses.text: Thou hast a good little property of thine own; thou hast laboured for it, hast acquired, and kept it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:115
verses.text: That person requires of thee; "Give false witness for me, and I will give thee so and so much".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:116
verses.text: Thou who seekest not the things of others, sayest, "That be far from me: I do not seek for what it has not pleased God to give me, I will not receive it; depart from me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:117
verses.text: "Hast thou no wish to receive what I give? I will take away what thou hast 			 already".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:118
verses.text: See now prove thyself, question now thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:119
verses.text: Why dost thou look at me? Look inward on thine own self, look at thine own self within, examine thine own self within; sit down before thine own self, and summon thine own self before thee, and stretch thyself upon the rack of God's commandment, and torment thyself with His fear, and deal not softly with thyself; answer thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:120
verses.text: Lo, if any one were to threaten thee with this, what wouldest thou do? "I will take away from 			 thee what with so great labour thou hast acquired, if thou wilt not give false witness for me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:121
verses.text: Give him that; "Beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:122
verses.text: "O my servant," He will say to thee, "whom I have redeemed and made free, whom from a servant I have adopted to be a brother, whom I have set as a member in My Body, give ear to Me: He may take away what thou hast acquired, Me he shall not take away from thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:123
verses.text: Art thou keeping thine own goods, that thou mayest not perish? What, have I not said 			 unto thee, 'Beware of all covetousness'?"  10.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:124
verses.text: Lo, thou art in confusion, tossed to and fro; thy heart as a ship is shaken about by tempests.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:125
verses.text: Christ is asleep: awake Him, that sleepeth, and thou shalt be exposed no more to the raging of the storm.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:126
verses.text: Awake Him, who was pleased to have nothing here, and thou hast all, who came even to the Cross for thee, whose "Bones" as He was naked and hanging "were numbered" by them that mocked Him; and "beware of all covetousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:127
verses.text: Covetousness of money is not 			 all; "beware of covetousness" of life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:128
verses.text: A dreadful covetousness, covetousness much to be feared.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:129
verses.text: Sometimes a man will despise what he has, and say, "I will not give false witness; I will not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:130
verses.text: You tell me, I will take away what thou hast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:131
verses.text: Take away what I have; you do not take away what I have within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:132
verses.text: For he was not left a poor man, who said, 'The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away; it is done as it pleased the Lord; blessed' therefore 'be the Name of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:133
verses.text: Naked came I out of my 			 mother's womb, naked shall I return to the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:134
verses.text: ' Naked outwardly, well-clothed within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:135
verses.text: Naked as regards these rags, these corruptible rags outwardly, clothed within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:136
verses.text: With what? 'Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:137
verses.text: '" But what if he say to thee, when thou hast despised the things which thou possessest, what if he say to thee, "I will kill thee"? If thou have given ear to Christ, answer him, "Wilt Thou kill me? Better that thou shouldest kill my body, than that I by a false tongue should kill my soul! What canst thou do to me? Thou wilt kill my body; my soul will depart at liberty, to receive again at the end of the world even this very body she hath despised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:138
verses.text: What canst thou do to me 			 then? Whereas if I should give false witness for thee, with thy tongue do I kill myself; and not in my body do I kill myself; 'For the mouth that lieth killeth the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:139
verses.text: '" But peradventure thou dost not say so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:140
verses.text: And why dost thou not say so? Thou wishest to live; thou wishest to live longer than God hath appointed for thee? Dost thou then "beware of all covetousness"? So long was it God's will that thou shouldest live, till this person came to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:141
verses.text: It may be that he will kill thee, to make a martyr of thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:142
verses.text: Entertain then no undue desire of life; and so thou wilt not have an eternity of death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:143
verses.text: Ye see how that 			 covetousness everywhere, when we wish for more than is necessary, causes us to sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 56:144
verses.text: Beware we of all covetousness, if we would enjoy eternal wisdom.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:1
verses.text: Sermon LVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:2
verses.text: [CVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:5
verses.text: 35 , "Let your loins be girded about, and your lamps burning; and be ye yourselves like," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:6
verses.text: And on the words of the 34th Psalm, v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:7
verses.text: 12 , "what man is he that desireth life," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:9
verses.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ both came to men, and went away from men, and is to come to men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:10
verses.text: And yet He was here when He came, nor did He depart when He went away, and He is to come to them to whom He said, "Lo, I am with you, even unto the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:11
verses.text: According to the "form of a servant" then, which He took for our sakes, was He born at a certain time, and was slain, and rose again, and now "dieth no more, neither shall death have any more dominion over Him;" but according to His Divinity, wherein He was equal to the Father, was He already in this world, and "the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:12
verses.text: On this point ye have just heard the Gospel, what admonition it has given us, putting us on our guard, and wishing us to be unencumbered and prepared to await the end; that after these last things, which are to be feared in this world, that rest may succeed which hath no end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:13
verses.text: Blessed are they who shall be partakers of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:14
verses.text: For then shall they be in security, who are not in security now; and again then shall they fear, who will not fear now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:15
verses.text: Unto this waiting, and for this hope's sake, have we been made Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:16
verses.text: Is not our hope not of this world? Let us then not love the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:17
verses.text: From the love of this world have we been called away, that we may hope for and love 			 another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:18
verses.text: In this world ought we to abstain from all unlawful desires, to have, that is, "our loins girded;" and to be fervent and to shine in good works, that is, to have "our lights burning".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:19
verses.text: For the Lord Himself said to His disciples in another place of the Gospel, "No man lighteth a candle and putteth it under a bushel, but on a candlestick, that it may give light unto all that are in the house".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:20
verses.text: And to show of what He was speaking, He subjoined and said, "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:21
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:22
verses.text: Therefore He would that "our loins should be girded, and our lights burning".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:23
verses.text: What is, "our loins girded"? "Depart from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:24
verses.text: What is to "burn"? What is to have our "lights burning"? It is this, "And do good".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:25
verses.text: What is that which He said afterwards, "And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their Lord, when He will return from the wedding:" except that which follows in that Psalm, "Seek after peace, and ensue it"? These three things, that is, "abstaining from evil, and doing good," and the hope of everlasting reward, are recorded in the Acts of the Apostles, where it is written, that Paul taught them of "temperance and righteousness," and the hope of eternal life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:26
verses.text: To temperance belongs, "let your loins be girded".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:27
verses.text: To righteousness, "and your lights burning".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:28
verses.text: To the hope of eternal life, the waiting for the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:29
verses.text: So then, "depart from evil," this is temperance, these are the loins girded: "and do good," this is righteousness, these are the "lights burning;" "seek peace, and ensue it," this is the waiting for the world to come: therefore, "Be ye like unto men that wait for their 			 Lord, when He will come from the wedding".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:31
verses.text: Having then these precepts and promises, why seek we on earth for "good days," where we cannot find them? For I know that ye do seek them, when ye are either sick, or in any of the tribulations, which in this world abound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:32
verses.text: For when life draws towards its close, the old man is full of complaints, and with no joys.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:33
verses.text: Amid all the tribulations by which mankind is worn away, men seek for nothing but "good days," and wish for a long life, which here they cannot have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:34
verses.text: For even a man's long life is narrowed within so short a span to the wide extent of all ages, as if it were but one drop to the whole sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:35
verses.text: What then is man's life, even that which is called a long one? They call that a long life, which even in this world's course is short; and as I have said, groans abound even unto the decrepitude of old age.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:36
verses.text: This at the most is but brief, and of short duration; and yet how eagerly is it sought by men, with how great diligence, with how great toil, with 			 how great carefulness, with how great watchfulness, with how great labour do men seek to live here for a long time, and to grow old.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:37
verses.text: And yet this very living long, what is it but running to the end? Thou hadst yesterday, and thou dost wish also to have to-morrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:38
verses.text: But when this day and to-morrow are passed, thou hast them not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:39
verses.text: Therefore thou dost wish for the day to break, that that may draw near to thee whither thou hast no wish to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:40
verses.text: Thou makest some annual festival with thy 			 friends, and hearest it there said to thee by thy well-wishers, "Mayest thou live many years," thou dost wish that what they have said, may come to pass.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:41
verses.text: What? Dost thou wish that years and years may come, and the end of these years come not? Thy wishes are contrary to one another; thou dost wish to walk on, and dost not wish to reach the end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:42
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:43
verses.text: But if, as I have said, there is so great care in men, as to desire with daily, great and perpetual labours, to die somewhat later: with how great cause ought they to strive, that they may never die? Of this, no one will think.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:44
verses.text: Day by day "good days" are sought for in this world, where they are not found; yet no one wishes so to live, that he may arrive there where they are found.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:45
verses.text: Therefore the same Scripture admonishes us, and says, "Who is the man that 			 wisheth for life, and loveth to see good days?" Scripture so asked the question, as that It knew well what answer would be given It; knowing that all men would "seek for life and good days".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:46
verses.text: In accordance with their desire It asked the question, as if the answer would be given It from the heart of all, "I wish it;" It said thus, "Who is the man that wisheth for life, and loveth to see good days?" Just as even at this very hour in which I am speaking to you, when ye heard me say, "Who is the man that wisheth 			 for life, and loveth to see good days?" ye all answered in your heart, "I".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:47
verses.text: For so do I too, who am speaking with you, "wish for life and good days;" what ye seek, that do I seek also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:48
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:49
verses.text: Just as if gold were necessary for us all, and we all, I as well as you, were wishing to get at the gold, and there was some anywhere in a field of yours, in a place subject to your power, and I were to see you searching for it, and were to say to you, "What are ye searching for?" ye were to answer me, "Gold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:50
verses.text: And I were to say to you, "Ye are searching for gold, and I am searching for gold too: what ye are searching for, I am searching for; but ye are not 			 searching for it where we can find it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:51
verses.text: Listen to me then, where we can find it; I am not taking it away from you, I am showing you the spot;" yea, let us all follow Him, who knows where what we are seeking for, is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:52
verses.text: So now too seeing that ye desire "life and good days," we cannot say to you, "Do not desire 'life and good days;'" but this we say, "Do not seek for 'life and good days' here in this world, where 'good days' cannot be".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:53
verses.text: Is not this life itself like unto 			 death? Now these days here hasten and pass away: for to-day has shut out yesterday; tomorrow only rises that it may shut out to-day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:54
verses.text: These days themselves have no abiding; wherefore wouldest thou abide with them? Your desire then whereby ye wish for "life and good days," I not only do not repress, but I even more strongly inflame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:55
verses.text: By all means "seek" for "life, seek for good days;" but let them be sought there, where they can be found.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:56
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:57
verses.text: For would ye with me hear His counsel, who knoweth where "good days" and where "life" is? Hear it not from me, but together with me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:58
verses.text: For One says to us, "Come, ye children, hearken unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:59
verses.text: And let us run together, and stand, and prick up our ears, and with our hearts understand the Father, who hath said, "Come, ye children, hearken unto Me, I will teach you the fear of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:60
verses.text: And then follows what he would teach us, and to what end the fear of the Lord is useful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:61
verses.text: "Who is the man that wisheth life, and loveth to see good days?" We all answer, "We wish it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:62
verses.text: Let us listen then to what follows, "Refrain thy tongue from evil, and thy lips that they speak no guile".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:63
verses.text: Now say, "I wish it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:64
verses.text: Just now when I said, "Who is the man that wisheth for life, and loveth to see good days?" we all answered, "I".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:65
verses.text: Come then, let some one now answer "I".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:66
verses.text: So then, "Refrain thy tongue from evil, and thy lips that they speak no guile".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:67
verses.text: Now say, "I".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:68
verses.text: Wouldest thou then have "good days" and "life," and wouldest thou not "refrain thy tongue from evil, and thy lips that they speak no guile"? Alert to the reward, slow to the 			 work! And to whom if he does not work is the reward rendered? I would that in thy house thou wouldest render the reward even to him that does work! For to him that works not, I am sure thou dost not render it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:69
verses.text: And why? Because thou owest nothing to him that does not work! And God hath a reward proposed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:70
verses.text: What reward? "Life and good days," which life we all desire, and unto which days we all strive to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:71
verses.text: The promised reward He will give us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:72
verses.text: What reward? "Life and good days".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:73
verses.text: And what 			 are "good days"? Life without end, rest without labour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:74
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:75
verses.text: Great is the reward He hath set before us: in so great a reward as is set before us, let us see what He hath commanded us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:76
verses.text: For enkindled by the reward of so great a promise, and by the love of the reward, let us make ready at once our strength, our sides, our arms, to do His bidding.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:77
verses.text: Is it as if He were to command us to carry heavy burdens, to dig something it may be, or to raise up some machine? No, no such laborious thing hath He enjoined thee, but hath 			 enjoined thee only to "refrain" that member which amongst all thy members thou dost move so quickly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:78
verses.text: "Refrain thy tongue from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:79
verses.text: It is no labour to erect a building, and is it a labour to hold in the tongue? "Refrain thy tongue from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:80
verses.text: Speak no lie, speak no revilings, speak no slanders, speak no false witnesses, speak no blasphemies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:81
verses.text: "Refrain thy tongue from evil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:82
verses.text: See how angry thou art, if any one speaks evil of thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:83
verses.text: As thou art angry with another, when he speaks 			 evil of thee; so be thou angry with thyself, when thou speakest evil of another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:84
verses.text: "Let thy lips speak no guile".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:85
verses.text: What is in thine heart within, be that spoken out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:86
verses.text: Let not thy breast conceal one thing, and thy tongue utter another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:87
verses.text: "Depart from evil, and do good".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:88
verses.text: For how should I say, "Clothe the naked," to him who up to this time would strip him that is clothed? For he that oppresses his fellow-citizen, how can he take in the stranger? So then in proper order, first "depart from 			 evil," and "do good;" first "gird up thy loins," and then "light the lamp".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:89
verses.text: And when thou hast done this, wait in assured hope for "life and good days".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 57:90
verses.text: "Seek peace, and ensue it;" and then with a good face wilt thou say unto the Lord, "I have done what Thou hast bidden, render me what Thou hast promised".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:1
verses.text: Sermon LIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:2
verses.text: [CIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:5
verses.text: 56, 58, "Ye know how to interpret the face of the Earth and the Heaven," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:6
verses.text: ; and of the words, "for as thou art going with thine adversary before the magistrate, on the way give diligence to be quit of him," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:8
verses.text: We have heard the Gospel, and in it the Lord reproving those who knew how to discern the face of the sky, and know not how to discover the time of faith, the kingdom of heaven which is at hand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:9
verses.text: Now this He said to the Jews; but His words reach even unto us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:10
verses.text: Now the Lord Jesus Christ Himself began the preaching of His Gospel in this way; "Repent ye, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:11
verses.text: In like manner too John the Baptist and His forerunner began thus; "Repent ye, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:12
verses.text: And now the Lord rebuketh those who would not repent, when "the kingdom of heaven was at hand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:13
verses.text: "The kingdom of heaven," as He saith Himself, "will not come with observation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:14
verses.text: And again He saith, "The kingdom of heaven is within you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:15
verses.text: Let every one then wisely receive the admonitions of the Master, that he may not lose the season of the mercy of the Saviour, which is now being dealt out, as long as the human race is spared.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:16
verses.text: For to this end is man spared, that he may be converted, and that he may not be to be condemned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:17
verses.text: God only knoweth when the end of the world shall come: nevertheless now is the time of faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:18
verses.text: Whether the end of the world shall find any of us here, I know not; and perhaps it will not find us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:19
verses.text: Our time is very near to each one of us, seeing we are 			 mortal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:20
verses.text: We walk in the midst of chances.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:21
verses.text: If we were made of glass, we should have to fear chances less than we have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:22
verses.text: What is more fragile than a vessel of glass? And yet it is kept, and lasts for ages.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:23
verses.text: For though the chances of a fall are feared for the vessel of glass, yet there is no fear of fever or old age for it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:24
verses.text: We then are more fragile and more infirm; because all the chances which are incessant in human things, we doubtless through our frailness are in daily dread of; and if these 			 chances come not, yet time goes on; a man avoids this stroke, can he avoid his end? he avoids accidents which happen from without, can that which is born within be driven away? Again, now the entrails engender worms, now some other disease attacks on a sudden; lastly, let a man be spared ever so long, at last when old age comes, there is no way of putting off that.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:25
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:26
verses.text: Wherefore let us give ear to the Lord, let us do within ourselves what He hath enjoined.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:27
verses.text: Let us see who that adversary is, of whom He hath put us in fear, saying, "If thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, give diligence in the way to be delivered from him; lest haply he deliver thee to the magistrate, and the magistrate to the officer, and thou be cast into prison, from whence thou shalt not come out, till thou payest the very last farthing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:28
verses.text: Who is this "adversary"? If the devil; we have been delivered from him already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:29
verses.text: What a price was given for us that we might be redeemed from him! Of which the Apostle says, speaking of this our redemption, "Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:30
verses.text: We have been redeemed, we have renounced the devil; how shall we "give diligence to be delivered from him," that he make us not, as sinners, his captives again? But this is not the "adversary" of whom the Lord gives us warning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:31
verses.text: For in another place another Evangelist has so expressed it, that if we join both expressions together, and compare both expressions of the two Evangelists with each other, we shall soon understand who this adversary is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:32
verses.text: For see, what did Luke 			 say here? "When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, give diligence in the way to be delivered from him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:33
verses.text: But the other Evangelist has expressed this same thing thus: "Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:34
verses.text: All the rest is alike: "Lest haply the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:35
verses.text: Both Evangelists have explained this alike.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:36
verses.text: One said, "Give diligence in the way to be delivered from him;" the other said, "Agree with him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:37
verses.text: For thou wilt not be able to "be delivered from him," unless thou "agree with him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:38
verses.text: Wouldest thou "be delivered from him? Agree with him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:39
verses.text: But what? is it the devil with whom the Christian ought to "agree"?  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:40
verses.text: Let us then seek out this "adversary," with whom we ought to "agree, lest he deliver us to the judge, and the judge to the officer;" let us seek him out, "and agree with him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:41
verses.text: If thou sin, the word of God is thine adversary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:42
verses.text: For example, it is a delight to thee perchance to be drunken; it says to thee, "Do it not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:43
verses.text: It is a delight to thee to frequent the spectacles, and such triflings; it says to thee, "Do it not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:44
verses.text: It is a delight to thee to commit adultery; the word of God saith to thee, "Do it not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:45
verses.text: In what sins soever thou wouldest do thine own will, it saith to thee, "Do it not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:46
verses.text: It is the adversary of thy will, till it become the author of thy salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:47
verses.text: O how goodly, how 			 useful an "adversary"! It does not seek our will, but our advantage.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:48
verses.text: It is our "adversary," as long as we are our own adversaries.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:49
verses.text: As long as thou art thine own enemy, thou hast the word of God thine enemy; be thine own friend, and thou art in agreement with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:50
verses.text: "Thou shalt do no murder;" give ear, and thou hast "agreed" with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:51
verses.text: "Thou shalt not steal;" give ear, and thou hast "agreed" with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:52
verses.text: "Thou shalt not commit adultery;" give ear, and thou hast "agreed" 			 with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:53
verses.text: "Thou shalt not give false witness;" give ear, and thou hast "agreed" with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:54
verses.text: "Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife;" give ear, and thou hast agreed with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:55
verses.text: "Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's goods;" give ear, and thou hast "agreed" with it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:56
verses.text: In all these things thou hast agreed with this "thine adversary," and what hast thou lost to thyself? Not only hast thou lost nothing; but thou hast even found thyself, who hadst been lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:57
verses.text: "The way," is this life; if we shall "agree with the adversary," if we shall come to terms with him; when "the way" is ended, we shall not fear the "judge, the officer, the prison.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:58
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:59
verses.text: When is "the way" ended? It is not ended at the same hour to all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:60
verses.text: Each several man hath his hour when he shall end his "way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:61
verses.text: This life is called "the way;" when thou hast ended this life, thou hast ended "the way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:62
verses.text: We are going on, and the very living is advancing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:63
verses.text: Unless peradventure ye imagine that time advances, and we stand still! It cannot be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:64
verses.text: As time advances, we too advance; and years do not come to us, but rather go away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:65
verses.text: Greatly are men 			 mistaken when they say, "This boy has little good sense yet, but years will come on him, and he will be wise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:66
verses.text: Consider what thou sayest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:67
verses.text: "Will come on him," thou hast said; "I will show that they go away," whereas thou sayest, "they come on".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:68
verses.text: And hear how easily I prove it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:69
verses.text: Let us suppose that we have known the number of his years from his birth; for instance (that we may wish him well) he has to live fourscore years, he is to arrive at old age.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:70
verses.text: Write down fourscore years.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:71
verses.text: One 			 year he has lived; how many hast thou in the total? how many hast thou down? Fourscore! Deduct one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:72
verses.text: He has lived ten; seventy remain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:73
verses.text: He has lived twenty; sixty remain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:74
verses.text: Yet surely, it will be said, they did come; what can this mean? Our years come that they may depart; they come, I say that they may go.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:75
verses.text: For they do not come, that they may abide with us, but as they pass through us, they wear us out, and make us less and less strong.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:76
verses.text: Such is "the way" into which we have come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:77
verses.text: What then have 			 we to do with that "adversary," that is, with the word of God? "Agree with him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:78
verses.text: For thou knowest not when "the way" may be ended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:79
verses.text: When "the way" is ended, there remain "the judge," and "the officer," and "the prison".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:80
verses.text: But if thou maintain a good will to "thine adversary," and "agree with him;" instead of a "judge," shalt thou find a father, instead of a cruel "officer," an Angel taking thee away into Abraham's bosom, instead of a "prison," 			 paradise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 58:81
verses.text: How rapidly hast thou changed all things "in the way," because thou hast "agreed with thine adversary"!.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:1
verses.text: Sermon LX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:2
verses.text: [CX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xiii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:5
verses.text: 6, where we are told of the fig-tree, which bare no fruit for three years; and of the woman which was in an infirmity eighteen years; and on the words of the ninth Psalm, v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:6
verses.text: 19, "Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail: let the nations be judged in thy sight".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:8
verses.text: Touching "the fig-tree" which had its three years' trial, and bare no fruit, and "the woman which was in an infirmity eighteen years," hearken to what the Lord may grant me to say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:9
verses.text: The fig-tree is the human race.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:10
verses.text: And the three years are the three times; one before the Law, the second under the Law, the third under grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:11
verses.text: Now there is nothing unsuitable in understanding by "the fig-tree" the human 			 race.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:12
verses.text: For when the first man sinned, he covered his nakedness with fig-leaves; covered those members, from which we derive our birth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:13
verses.text: For what before his sin should have been his glory, after sin became his shame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:14
verses.text: So before that, "they were naked, and were not ashamed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:15
verses.text: For they had no reason to blush, when no sin had gone before; nor could they blush for their Creator's works, because they had not yet mingled any evil work of their own with the good works of their Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:16
verses.text: For they had not yet eaten of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, of which they had been forbidden to eat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:17
verses.text: After then that they had eaten and sinned, the human race sprang from them; that is, man from man, debtor from debtor, mortal from mortal, sinner from sinner.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:18
verses.text: In this "tree" then he entitles those, who through the whole range of time would not bear fruit; and for this cause the axe was hanging over the unfruitful tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:19
verses.text: The gardener intercedes for it, punishment is deferred, that help may be administered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:20
verses.text: Now the gardener who intercedes, is every saint who within the Church prays for those who are without the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:21
verses.text: And what does he pray? "Lord, let it alone this year also;" that is, in this time of grace, spare the sinners, spare the 			 unbelievers, spare the barren, spare the unfruitful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:22
verses.text: "I will dig about it, and put a basket of dung about it; if it bear fruit, well; but if not, thou shalt come and cut it down".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:23
verses.text: "Thou shalt come:" When? Thou shalt come in judgment, when Thou shalt come to judge the quick and dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:24
verses.text: Meanwhile they are spared.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:25
verses.text: But what is the "digging"? What is the "digging about it," but the teaching lowliness and repentance? For a ditch is low ground.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:26
verses.text: The basket of dung understand in its good effects.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:27
verses.text: It is filthy, but it produces fruit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:28
verses.text: The gardener's filth is the sinner's sorrows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:29
verses.text: They who repent, repent in filthy robes; if, that is, they understand 			 aright, and repent in truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:30
verses.text: To this tree then is it said, "Repent ye, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:31
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:32
verses.text: What is that "woman who was in an infirmity eighteen years"? In six days God finished His works.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:33
verses.text: Three times six are eighteen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:34
verses.text: What the "three years" then in "the tree" signified, that do the "eighteen years" in this woman.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:35
verses.text: She was bent down, she could not look up; because in vain did she hear, "Up with your hearts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:36
verses.text: But the Lord made her straight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:37
verses.text: There is hope then, for the children, that is, even until the day of judgment come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:38
verses.text: Man ascribes 			 much to himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:39
verses.text: Yet what is man? A righteous man is something great.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:40
verses.text: But yet a righteous man is righteous only by the grace of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:41
verses.text: "For what is man, save that thou art mindful of him?" Wouldest thou see what man is? "All men are liars".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:42
verses.text: We have chanted, "Arise, Lord; let not man prevail".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:43
verses.text: What is, "let not man prevail"? Were not the Apostles men? Were not Martyrs men? The Lord Jesus Himself, without ceasing to be God, vouchsafed to be Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:44
verses.text: What then is, "Arise, Lord; let not man prevail"? If "all men are liars; arise," Truth, "let not" falsehood "prevail".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:45
verses.text: If man then would be anything good, it must not be of anything of his own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:46
verses.text: For if he should wish to be anything of his own he will be "a liar".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:47
verses.text: If he would wish to be true, he must be 			 so of that which is from God, not of anything of his own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:48
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:49
verses.text: Therefore, "Arise, Lord; let not man prevail".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:50
verses.text: So much did lying prevail before the flood, that after the flood only eight men remained.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:51
verses.text: By them the earth was again replenished with lying men, and out of them was elected the people of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:52
verses.text: Many miracles were wrought, divine benefits imparted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:53
verses.text: They were brought right through to the land of promise, delivered from Egyptian bondage: Prophets were raised up among them, they received the temple, they received the priesthood, they received the anointing, they received the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:54
verses.text: Yet of this very people was it said afterwards, "The strange children have lied unto 			 me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:55
verses.text: At last He was sent who had been promised afore by the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:56
verses.text: "Let not man prevail," even the more, because that God was made Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:57
verses.text: But even He, though He did divine works, was despised, though He showed forth so many acts of mercy, He was apprehended, He was scourged, He was hanged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:58
verses.text: Thus far "did man prevail," to apprehend the Son of God, to scourge the Son of God, to crown the Son of God with thorns, to hang the Son of God upon the tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:59
verses.text: So far "did man 			 prevail:" how far, but up to the time that having been taken down from the tree, He was laid in the sepulchre? If He had remained there, man would have "prevailed" indeed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:60
verses.text: But this prophecy addresses the very Lord Jesus Himself, saying, "Arise, Lord, let not man prevail".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:61
verses.text: O Lord, Thou hast vouchsafed to come in the flesh, the Word made Flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:62
verses.text: The Word above us, the Flesh among us, the Word-flesh between God and Man: Thou didst choose a virgin to be born from according to the flesh, when Thou wast to be conceived, Thou didst find a Virgin; when Thou wast born, Thou didst leave a Virgin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:63
verses.text: But Thou wast not acknowledged; Thou wast Seen, and yet wast hidden.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:64
verses.text: Infirmity was seen, Power was hidden.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:65
verses.text: All this was done, that Thou mightest shed that Blood, which is our Price.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:66
verses.text: Thou didst so great miracles, didst give health to the weaknesses of the sick, 			 didst show forth many acts of mercy, and receivedst evil for good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:67
verses.text: They mocked Thee, Thou didst hang upon the tree; the ungodly wagged their heads before Thee, and said, "If Thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:68
verses.text: Hadst Thou then lost Thy power, or rather wast Thou showing forth Thy Patience? and yet they mocked Thee, and yet they derided Thee, yet, when Thou wast slain, they went away as if victorious.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:69
verses.text: Lo, Thou art laid in the sepulchre: "Arise, Lord, let not man prevail".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:70
verses.text: "Let not" the ungodly enemy "prevail, let not" the blind Jew "prevail".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:71
verses.text: For when Thou wert crucified, the Jew in his blindness seemed to himself to have "prevailed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:72
verses.text: "Arise, Lord, let not man 			 prevail".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:73
verses.text: It is done, yea, it is done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:74
verses.text: And now what remains, but that "the nations be judged in thy sight"? For He hath risen again, as ye know, and ascended into heaven; and from thence He shall come to judge the quick and the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:75
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:76
verses.text: Ah! unfruitful tree, mock not, because thou art yet spared; the axe is delayed, be not thou secure; He will come and thou shalt be cut down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:77
verses.text: Believe that He will come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:78
verses.text: All these things which now ye see, once were not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:79
verses.text: Once the Christian people were not over the whole world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:80
verses.text: It was read of in prophecy, not seen in the earth; now it is both read and seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:81
verses.text: Thus was the Church herself completed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:82
verses.text: It was not said to her, "See, O daughter, and hear;" but, "Hear and see".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:83
verses.text: Hear the predictions, see the completions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:84
verses.text: As then, my beloved Brethren, Christ had once not been born of a Virgin, but His birth was promised, and He was born; He had once not done His miracles, they were promised, and He did them: He had not yet suffered, it was promised, and so it came to pass: He had not risen again, it was foretold, and so fulfilled: His Name was not throughout the world, it was foretold, and so fulfilled: the idols were not destroyed and broken down, it 			 was foretold, and so fulfilled: heretics had not assailed the Church, it was foretold, and so fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:85
verses.text: So also the Day of Judgment is not yet, but seeing it hath been foretold, it shall be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:86
verses.text: Can it be that He who in so many things hath shown Himself true, should be false touching the Day of Judgment? He hath given us a bond of His promises.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:87
verses.text: For God hath made Himself a debtor, not by owing ought, that is, not by borrowing; but by promising.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:88
verses.text: We cannot therefore say to Him, "Give back what Thou hast received".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:89
verses.text: Since "who hath first given to Him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again?" We cannot say to Him, "Give what Thou hast received;" but we say without scruple, "Give what Thou hast promised".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:90
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:91
verses.text: For hence it is that we are bold to say, day by day, "Thy kingdom come;" that when His kingdom comes, we too may reign with Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:92
verses.text: Which hath been promised to us in these words; "Then will I say unto them, Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:93
verses.text: But assuredly only if we shall have done what follows in that place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:94
verses.text: "For I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:95
verses.text: He made these promises to our fathers; but He hath given us a security, for us too to read.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:96
verses.text: If He who hath vouchsafed to give us this security, were to make a reckoning with us and say, "Read my debts, the debts, that is, of my promises, and reckon up what I have already paid, and reckon also what I still owe; see how many I have paid already; and what I owe is but little; will ye for that little that remains, think Me an untrustworthy promiser?" What should we have to answer against this most evident truth? Let him then who is barren repent, 			 and bear "fruit worthy of repentance".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:97
verses.text: He that is bent down, who looks only on the earth, rejoices in earthly happiness, who thinks this the only happy life, where he may be happy, and who believes no other can be; whosoever he be that is so bent down, let him be made straight; if he cannot by himself, let him call upon God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 59:98
verses.text: For was that woman made straight by herself? Woe had it been for her, if He had not stretched out His Hand.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:1
verses.text: Sermon LXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:2
verses.text: [CXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xiii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:5
verses.text: 21 and 23, where the kingdom of God is said to be "like unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal;" and of that which is written in the same chapter, "Lord, are they few that are saved?"  1.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:6
verses.text: "The three measures of meal" of which the Lord spake, is the human race.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:7
verses.text: Recollect the deluge; three only remained, from whom the rest were to be re-peopled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:8
verses.text: Noe had three sons, by them was repaired the human race.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:9
verses.text: That holy "woman who hid the leaven," is Wisdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:10
verses.text: Lo, the whole world crieth out in the Church of God, "I know that the Lord is great".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:11
verses.text: Yet doubtless there are but few who are saved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:12
verses.text: Ye remember a question which was lately set before us out of the Gospel, "Lord," it was said, "are there few that be saved?" What said the Lord to this? He did not say, "Not few, but many are they who are saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:13
verses.text: He did not say this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:14
verses.text: But what said He, when He had heard, "Are there few that be saved? Strive to enter by the strait gate".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:15
verses.text: When thou hearest then, "Are there few that be saved?" the Lord confirmed what He heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:16
verses.text: Through the "strait gate" but "few" can "enter".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:17
verses.text: In another place He saith Himself, "Strait and narrow is the way which leadeth unto life, and few there be that go thereby: but broad and spacious is the way that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which walk thereby".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:18
verses.text: Why rejoice we in great numbers? Give ear to me, ye "few".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:19
verses.text: I know that ye are "many," who hear me, yet but "few" of you hear to obey.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:20
verses.text: I see the floor, I look for the corn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:21
verses.text: And hardly is the corn seen, when the floor is being threshed; but the time is coming, that it shall be winnowed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:22
verses.text: But few then are saved in comparison of the many that shall perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:23
verses.text: For these same "few" will constitute in themselves a great mass.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:24
verses.text: When the Winnower shall come with His fan in 			 His Hand, "He will cleanse His floor, and lay up the wheat into the garner; but the chaff He will burn with unquenchable fire".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:25
verses.text: Let not the chaff scoff at the wheat; in this He speaketh truth, and deceiveth no one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:26
verses.text: Be ye then in yourselves among many a many, few though ye be in comparison of a certain many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:27
verses.text: So large a mass is to come out of this floor, as to fill the garner of heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:28
verses.text: For the Lord Christ would not contradict Himself, who hath said, "Many there are who enter in by the narrow gate, many who go to ruin through the wide gate;" contradict Himself, who hath in another place said, "Many 			 shall come from the East and West".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:29
verses.text: "Many" then are the "few;" both "few" and "many".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:30
verses.text: Are the "few" one sort, and the "many" another? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:31
verses.text: But the "few" are themselves the "many;" "few" in comparison of the lost, "many in the society of the Angels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:32
verses.text: Hearken, dearly Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:33
verses.text: The Apocalypse hath this written; "After this I beheld of all languages, and nations, and tribes, a great multitude, which no man can number, coming with white robes and palms".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:34
verses.text: This is the mass of the saints.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:35
verses.text: With how much clearer voice will the floor say, when it has been fanned, separated from the crowd of ungodly, and evil, and false Christians, when those who "press" and do not "touch" (for a certain woman in the Gospel "touched," the crowd "pressed" Christ), shall have been severed unto everlasting fire; when all they then, who are to be damned shall have been separated off, with how great assurance will the purified mass, 			 standing at the Right Hand, fearing now for itself the admixture of no evil men, nor the loss of any of the good, now about to reign with Christ, say, "I know that the Lord is great"!  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:36
verses.text: If then, my Brethren (I am speaking to the corn), if they acknowledge what I say, predestined unto life eternal, let them speak by their works, not by their voices.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:37
verses.text: I am constrained to speak to you, what I ought not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:38
verses.text: For I ought to find in you matter of praise, not to seek subjects for admonition.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:39
verses.text: Yet see I will say but a few words, I will not dwell upon it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:40
verses.text: Acknowledge the duty of hospitality, thereby some have attained unto God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:41
verses.text: Thou takest in some stranger, whose 			 companion in the way thou thyself also art; for strangers are we all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:42
verses.text: He is a Christian who, even in his own house and in his own country, acknowledges himself to be a stranger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:43
verses.text: For our country is above, there we shall not be strangers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:44
verses.text: For every one here below, even in his own house, is a stranger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:45
verses.text: If he be not a stranger, let him not pass on from hence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:46
verses.text: If pass on he must, he is a stranger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:47
verses.text: Let him not deceive himself, a stranger he is; whether he will or not, he is a stranger.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:48
verses.text: And he leaves 			 that house to his children, one stranger to other strangers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:49
verses.text: Why? If thou wert at an inn, wouldest thou not depart when another comes? The same thou doest even in thine own house.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:50
verses.text: Thy father left a place to thee, thou wilt some day leave it to thy children.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:51
verses.text: Neither dost thou abide here, as one who is to abide always, nor to those who are so to abide, wilt thou leave it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:52
verses.text: If we are all passing away, let us do something which cannot pass away, that when we shall have passed away, and have come 			 thither whence we may not pass away, we may find our good works there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:53
verses.text: Christ is the keeper, why dost thou fear lest thou shouldest lose what thou spendest on the poor? "Let us turn to the Lord," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:54
verses.text: And after the Sermon.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:55
verses.text: I suggest to you, Beloved, what ye know already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:56
verses.text: To-morrow breaks the anniversary day of the venerable lord Aurelius' ordination; he asks and admonishes you, dear Brethren, by my humble ministry, that ye would be so good as to meet together with all devotion at the basilica of Faustus.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 60:57
verses.text: Thanks be to God.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:1
verses.text: Sermon LXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:2
verses.text: [XCII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xiv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:5
verses.text: 16, "A certain man made a great supper," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:6
verses.text: Delivered in the basilica Restituta.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:8
verses.text: Holy lessons have been set forth before us, to which we should both give ear, and upon which by the Lord's help I would deliver some observations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:9
verses.text: In the Apostolic lesson thanks are rendered unto the Lord for the faith of the Gentiles, of course, because it was His work.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:10
verses.text: In the Psalm we have said, "O God of hosts, turn us, and show us Thy Face, and we shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:11
verses.text: In the Gospel we have been called to a supper; yea, rather others have been called, we not called, but led; not only led, but even forced.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:12
verses.text: For so have we heard, that "a certain Man made a great supper".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:13
verses.text: Who is this Man, but "the Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus"? He sent that those who had been invited might come, for the hour was now come, that they should come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:14
verses.text: Who are they who had been invited, but those who had been called by the Prophets who were sent before? When? Of old, ever since the Prophets were sent, they invited to Christ's supper.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:15
verses.text: They were sent then to the people of Israel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:16
verses.text: Often were they sent, often did they call men, to come at the hour of supper.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:17
verses.text: But they received those who invited them, refused the supper.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:18
verses.text: What 			 means "they received those who invited them, refused the supper"? They read the Prophets and killed Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:19
verses.text: But when they killed Him, then though they knew it not, they prepared a Supper for us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:20
verses.text: When the Supper was now prepared, when Christ had been offered up, when the Supper of the Lord, which the faithful know, had been set forth after the resurrection of Christ, and established by His Hands and Mouth, were the Apostles sent to them, to whom the Prophets had been sent before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:21
verses.text: "Come ye 			 to the supper".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:23
verses.text: They who would not come made excuses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:24
verses.text: And how did they excuse themselves? There were three excuses: "One said, I have bought a farm, and I go to see it; have me excused.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:25
verses.text: Another said, I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I go to prove them; I pray thee have me excused.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:26
verses.text: A third said, I have married a wife, have me excused; I cannot come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:27
verses.text: Do we suppose that these are not the excuses, which hinder all men, who decline to come to this supper? Let us look into them, discuss, find them out; but only that we may beware.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:28
verses.text: In the purchase of the farm, the spirit of domination is marked out; therefore pride is rebuked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:29
verses.text: For men are delighted to have a farm, to hold, to possess it, to have men in it under them, to have dominion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:30
verses.text: An evil vice, the first vice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:31
verses.text: For the first man wished to have dominion, in that he would not 			 that any should have dominion over him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:32
verses.text: What is to have dominion, but to take pleasure in one's own power? There is a greater power, let us submit ourselves to it, that we may be able to be safe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:33
verses.text: "I have bought a farm, have me excused".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:34
verses.text: Having discovered pride, he would not come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:35
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:36
verses.text: "Another said, I have bought five pairs of oxen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:37
verses.text: Would it not have been enough, "I have bought oxen"? Something beyond doubt there is, which by its very obscurity challenges us to seek out, and understand; and in that it is shut, He exhorteth us to knock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:38
verses.text: The five pairs of oxen are the senses of this body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:39
verses.text: There are numbered five senses of this body, as is known to all; and they who, it may be, do not consider it, will doubtless perceive it on being reminded 			 of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:40
verses.text: There are then found to be five senses of this body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:41
verses.text: In the eyes is the sight, the hearing in the ears, the smell in the nose, the taste in the mouth, the touch in all the members.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:42
verses.text: We have perception of white and black, and things coloured in whatever way, light and dark, by the sight.
