verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:43
verses.text: Harsh and musical sounds, we have perception of by the hearing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:44
verses.text: Of sweet and offensive smells, we have perception by the smell.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:45
verses.text: Of things sweet and bitter by the taste.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:46
verses.text: Of things hard and soft, smooth and 			 rough, warm and cold, heavy and light, by the touch.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:47
verses.text: They are five, and they are pairs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:48
verses.text: Now that they are pairs, is seen most easily in the case of the three first senses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:49
verses.text: There are two eyes, two ears, two nostrils; see three pairs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:50
verses.text: In the mouth, that is in the sense of taste, a certain doubling is found, because nothing affects the taste, unless it is touched by the tongue and the palate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:51
verses.text: The pleasure of the flesh which pertains to the touch, has this doubling in a less obvious way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:52
verses.text: For there 			 is both an outer and an inner touch.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:53
verses.text: And so it too is double.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:54
verses.text: Why are they called pairs of oxen? Because by these senses of the body, earthly things are sought for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:55
verses.text: For oxen turn up the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:56
verses.text: So there are men far off from faith, given up to earthly things, occupied in the things of the flesh; who will not believe anything but what they attain to by the five senses of their body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:57
verses.text: In those five senses do they lay down for themselves the rules of their whole will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:58
verses.text: "I will not believe," says 			 one, "anything but what I see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:59
verses.text: See, here is what I know, and am sure of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:60
verses.text: Such a thing is white, or black, or round, or square, or coloured so and so; this I know, am sensible of, have a hold of; nature itself teaches it me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:61
verses.text: I am not forced to believe what you cannot show me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:62
verses.text: Or it is a voice: I perceive that it is a voice; it sings well, it sings ill, it is sweet, it is harsh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:63
verses.text: I know, I know this, it has come to me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:64
verses.text: There is a good or a bad smell: I know, I perceive it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:65
verses.text: This is sweet, this is 			 bitter; this is salt, this insipid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:66
verses.text: I know not what you would tell me more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:67
verses.text: By the touch I know what is hard, what is soft; what is smooth, what is rough; what is warm, and what cold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:68
verses.text: What more would you show me?"  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:69
verses.text: By such an impediment was our Apostle Thomas held back, who as to the Lord Christ, the resurrection that is of Christ, would not believe even his own eyes only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:70
verses.text: "Unless," says he, "I put my fingers into the places of the nails and wounds, and unless I put my hand into His side, I will not believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:71
verses.text: And the Lord who could have risen again without any vestige of a wound, kept the scars, that they might be touched by the doubting Apostle, and the wounds of his heart be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:72
verses.text: And yet as designing to call to His supper others, against the excuse of "the five pairs of oxen," He said, "Blessed they who do not see, and believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:73
verses.text: We, my Brethren, who have been called to this supper, have not been kept back by "these five pairs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:74
verses.text: For we have not in this age desired to see the Face of the Lord's Body, nor have we longed to hear the Voice proceeding out of the mouth of that Body; we have not sought in Him for any passing odour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:75
verses.text: A certain "woman anointed Him with most costly ointment," that "house was filled with the odour;" but we were not there; lo, we did not smell, yet we believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:76
verses.text: He gave to the disciples the Supper consecrated by His Own Hands; but we did not sit down at that Feast, and yet we daily eat this same Supper by faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:77
verses.text: And do not think it strange that in that supper which He gave with His Own Hand, one was present without faith: the faith that appeared, afterwards was more than a compensation for that faithlessness then.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:78
verses.text: Paul was not there who believed, Judas was there who 			 betrayed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:79
verses.text: How many now too in this same Supper, though they saw not then that table, nor beheld with their eyes, nor tasted with their mouths, the bread which the Lord took in His Hands, yet because it is the same as is now prepared, how many now also in this same Supper, "eat and drink judgment to themselves"?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:80
verses.text: But whence arose an occasion, so to say, to the Lord, to speak of this supper? One of them that sat at meat with Him (for He was at a feast, whither He had been invited), had said, "Blessed are they who eat bread in the kingdom of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:81
verses.text: He sighed as though after distant things, and the Bread Himself was sitting down before him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:82
verses.text: Who is the Bread of the kingdom of God, but He who saith, "I am the Living Bread which came down from heaven"? Do not get thy mouth ready, but thine heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:83
verses.text: On this occasion it was that the parable of this supper was set forth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:84
verses.text: Lo, we believe in Christ, we receive Him with faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:85
verses.text: In receiving Him we know what to think of.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:86
verses.text: We receive but little, and we are nourished in heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:87
verses.text: It is not then what is seen, but what is believed, that feeds us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:88
verses.text: Therefore we too have not sought for that outward sense; nor have we said, "Let them believe who have seen with their eyes, and handled with their 			 hands the Lord Himself after His resurrection, if what is said be true; we do not touch Him, why should we believe?" If we were to entertain such thoughts, we should be kept back from the supper by those "five pairs of oxen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:89
verses.text: That ye may know, Brethren, that not the gratification of these five senses, which softens and ministers pleasure, but a kind of curiosity was denoted, He did not say, "'I have bought five pairs of oxen,' and I go to feed them;" but, "I go to prove them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:90
verses.text: He who wishes to "prove" by "the pairs of oxen," does not wish to be in doubt, just as St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:91
verses.text: Thomas by these "pairs" did not wish to be in doubt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:92
verses.text: "Let me see, let me touch, let me put in my fingers".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:93
verses.text: "'Behold,' saith the Lord, 'put in thy fingers along My Side, and be not unbelieving.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:94
verses.text: ' For thy sake have I been slain; at the place which thou wishest to touch, have I shed My Blood, that I might redeem thee; and dost thou still doubt of Me, unless thou touch Me? Behold, this too I grant; behold, this too I show thee; touch, and believe; find out the place of My wound, heal the wound of thy doubting".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:95
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:96
verses.text: "The third said, I have married a wife".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:97
verses.text: This is the pleasure of the flesh, which is a hindrance to many: and I would that it were so only without, and not within! There are men who say, "There is no happiness for a man, if he have not the pleasures of the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:98
verses.text: These are they whom the Apostle censures, saying, "'Let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we shall die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:99
verses.text: ' Who hath risen to this life from the other? Who hath ever told us what goes on there? We take away with us, what in the time present makes our happiness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:100
verses.text: He that speaks thus, "has married a wife," attaches himself to the flesh, places his delight in the pleasures of the flesh, excuses himself from the supper; let him look well to it that he die not by an inward famine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:101
verses.text: Attend to John, the holy Apostle and Evangelist; "Love not the world, neither the things that are in 			 the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:102
verses.text: O ye who come to the Supper of the Lord, "Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:103
verses.text: He did not say, "Have not;" but, "Love not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:104
verses.text: Thou hast had, possessed, loved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:105
verses.text: The love of earthly things, is the bird-lime of the spirit's wings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:106
verses.text: Lo, thou hast desired, thou hast stuck fast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:107
verses.text: "Who will give thee wings as of a dove?" When wilt thou fly, whither thou mayest in deed, seeing thou hast perversely wished to rest here, where thou hast to thy hurt stuck fast? "Love not the world," is the divine trumpet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:108
verses.text: By the voice of this trumpet unceasingly is it proclaimed to the compass of the earth, and to the whole world, "Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:109
verses.text: Whosoever loveth the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:110
verses.text: For all that is in the 			 world, is the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the ambition of life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:111
verses.text: He begins at the last with which the Gospel ends.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:112
verses.text: He begins at that, at which the Gospel made an end.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:113
verses.text: "The lust of the flesh, I have married a wife.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:114
verses.text: The lust of the eyes, I have bought five pairs of oxen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:115
verses.text: The ambition of life, I have bought a farm".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:116
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:117
verses.text: Now these senses are denoted by the mention of the eyes only, the whole by a part, because the pre-eminence in the five senses belongs to the eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:118
verses.text: Wherefore though sight belongs peculiarly to the eyes, we are accustomed to use the word "seeing" through all the five senses.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:119
verses.text: How? In the first place, in relation to the eyes themselves we say; "See how white it is, look and see how white it is:" this has relation to the eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:120
verses.text: Hear and see how musical it is! 			 Could we say conversely, "Hear and see how white it is"? This expression, "see," runs through all the senses; whereas the distinguishing expression of the other senses does not in its turn run through it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:121
verses.text: "Mark and see how musical; smell and see how agreeable it is; taste and see how sweet it is; touch and see how soft it is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:122
verses.text: And yet surely since they are senses, we should rather say thus; "Hear and be sensible how musical it is; smell and be sensible how agreeable it is; taste and be sensible how sweet it is; touch and be sensible how hot it is; handle and be sensible how smooth it is; handle and be sensible how 			 soft it is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:123
verses.text: But we say none of these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:124
verses.text: For thus the Lord Himself after His resurrection when He appeared to His disciples, and when though they saw Him they still wavered in faith supposing that they saw a spirit, said, "Why do ye doubt, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? See My Hands and My Feet".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:125
verses.text: It is not enough to say, "See;" He saith, "Touch, and handle, and see".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:126
verses.text: "Look and see, handle and see; with the eyes alone see, and see by all the senses".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:127
verses.text: Because He was looking for the inner sense of faith, He offered Himself to the outward senses of the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:128
verses.text: We have made no attainment in the Lord by these outward senses, we have heard with our ears, have believed with our heart; and this hearing not from His mouth, but from the mouth of His preachers, from their mouths who were already at the supper, and who by the pouring forth of what they there drunk in invited us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:129
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:130
verses.text: Let us away then with vain and evil excuses, and come we to the supper by which we may be made fat within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:131
verses.text: Let not the puffing up of pride keep us back, let it not lift us up, nor unlawful curiosity scare us, and turn us away from God; let not the pleasure of the flesh hinder us from the pleasure of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:132
verses.text: Let us come, and be filled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:133
verses.text: And who came but the beggars, the "maimed," the "halt," the "blind"? But there came not thither the rich, and the 			 whole, who walked, as they thought, well, and saw acutely; who had great confidence in themselves, and were therefore in the more desperate case, in proportion as they were more proud.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:134
verses.text: Let the beggars come, for He inviteth them, "who, though He was rich, for our sakes became poor, that we beggars through His poverty might be enriched".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:135
verses.text: Let the maimed come, "for they that are whole need not a physician, but they that are in evil case".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:136
verses.text: Let the halt come who may say to Him, "Set in order my steps in Thy paths".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:137
verses.text: Let the blind come who may say, "Enlighten mine eyes, that I may never sleep in death".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:138
verses.text: Such as these came at the hour, when those who had been first invited, had been rejected for their own excuses: they came at the hour, they entered in from the streets and lanes of the city.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:139
verses.text: And the servant "who had been sent," brought answer, "Lord, it is done as Thou hast commanded, and yet there is room".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:140
verses.text: "Go out," saith He, "into the highways and hedges, and compel those whom thou shalt find to come in".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:141
verses.text: Whom thou shalt find wait not till they choose to come, compel them to come in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:142
verses.text: I have prepared a great supper, a great house, I cannot suffer any place to be vacant in it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:143
verses.text: The Gentiles came from the streets and lanes: let the heretics come from the hedges, here they shall find peace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:144
verses.text: For those who make hedges, their object is to make divisions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:145
verses.text: Let them be drawn away from the hedges, let them be plucked up from among the thorns.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:146
verses.text: They have stuck fast in the hedges, they are 			 unwilling to be compelled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:147
verses.text: Let us come in, they say, of our own good will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:148
verses.text: This is not the Lord's order, "Compel them," saith he, "to come in".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 61:149
verses.text: Let compulsion be found outside, the will arise within.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:1
verses.text: Sermon LXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:2
verses.text: [CXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xvi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:5
verses.text: 9, "Make to yourselves friends by means of the mammon of unrighteousness," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:7
verses.text: Our duty is to give to others the admonitions we have received ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:8
verses.text: The recent lesson of the Gospel has admonished us to make friends of the mammon of iniquity, that they too may "receive" those who do so "into everlasting habitations".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:9
verses.text: But who are they that shall have everlasting habitations, but the Saints of God? And who are they who are to be received by them into everlasting habitations, but 			 they who serve their need, and minister cheerfully to their necessities? Accordingly let us remember, that in the last judgment the Lord will say to those who shall stand on His right hand, "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat;" and the rest which ye know.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:10
verses.text: And upon their enquiring when they had afforded these good offices to Him, He answered, "When ye did it to one of the least of Mine, ye did it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:11
verses.text: These least are they who receive into everlasting habitations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:12
verses.text: This He said to them on the right hand, because they did so: and the contrary He said to them on the left, because they would not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:13
verses.text: But what have they on the right hand who did so, received, or rather, what are they to receive? "Come," says He, "ye blessed of My Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:14
verses.text: For I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:15
verses.text: When ye did it to one of the 			 least of Mine, ye did it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:16
verses.text: Who then are these least ones of Christ? They are those who have left all they had, and followed Him, and have distributed whatever they had to the poor; that unencumbered and without any worldly fetter they might serve God, and might lift their shoulders free from the burdens of the world, and winged as it were aloft.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:17
verses.text: These are the least.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:18
verses.text: And why the least? Because lowly, because not puffed up, not proud.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:19
verses.text: Yet weigh them in the scales, these least ones, and thou wilt find them 			 a heavy weight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:21
verses.text: But what means it, that He says they are "friends of the mammon of iniquity"? What is "the mammon of iniquity"? First, what is "mammon"? For it is not a Latin word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:22
verses.text: It is a Hebrew word, and cognate to the Punic language.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:23
verses.text: For these languages are allied to one another by a kind of nearness of signification.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:24
verses.text: What the Punics call mammon, is called in Latin, "lucre".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:25
verses.text: What the Hebrews call mammon, is called in Latin, "riches".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:26
verses.text: That we may express the whole then in Latin, our Lord Jesus Christ says this, "Make to yourselves friends of the riches of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:27
verses.text: Some, by a bad understanding of this, plunder the goods of others, and bestow some of that upon the poor, and so think that they do what is enjoined them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:28
verses.text: For they say, "To plunder the goods of others, is the mammon of iniquity; to spend some of it, especially on the poor 			 saints, this is to make friends with the mammon of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:29
verses.text: This understanding of it must be corrected, yea, must be utterly effaced from the tablets of your heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:30
verses.text: I would not that ye should so understand it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:31
verses.text: Give alms of your righteous labours: give out of that which ye possess rightfully.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:32
verses.text: For ye cannot corrupt Christ your Judge, that He should not hear you together with the poor, from whom ye take away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:33
verses.text: For if thou wert to despoil any one who was weak, thyself being stronger and of greater 			 power, and he were to come with thee to the judge, any man you please on this earth, who had any power of judging, and he were to wish to plead his cause with thee; if thou wert to give anything of the spoil and plunder of that poor man to the judge, that he might pronounce judgment in thy favour; would that judge please even thee? True, he has pronounced judgment in thy favour, and yet so great is the force of justice, that he would displease even thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:34
verses.text: Do not then represent God to thyself as 			 such an one as this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:35
verses.text: Do not set up such an idol in the temple of thine heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:36
verses.text: Thy God is not such as thou oughtest not to be thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:37
verses.text: If thou wouldest not judge so, but wouldest judge justly; even so thy God is better than thou: He is not inferior to thee: He is more just, He is the fountain of justice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:38
verses.text: Whatsoever good thou hast done, thou hast gotten from Him; and whatsoever good thou hast given vent to, thou hast drunk in from Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:39
verses.text: Dost thou praise the vessel, because it hath something from Him, and blame the fountain? Do not give alms out of usury and increase.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:40
verses.text: I am speaking to the faithful, am speaking to those to whom we distribute the body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:41
verses.text: Be in fear and amend yourselves: that I may not have hereafter to say, Thou doest so, and thou too doest so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:42
verses.text: Yet I trow, that if I should do so, ye ought not to be angry with me, but with yourselves, that ye may amend 			 yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:43
verses.text: For this is the meaning of the expression in the Psalm, "Be ye angry, and sin not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:44
verses.text: I would have you be angry, but only that ye may not sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:45
verses.text: Now in order that ye may not sin, with whom ought ye to be angry but with yourselves? For what is a penitent man, but a man who is angry with himself? That he may obtain pardon, he exacts punishment from himself; and so with good right says to God, "Turn Thine eyes from my sins, for I acknowledge my sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:46
verses.text: If thou acknowledgest it, then He will pardon it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:47
verses.text: Ye then who have done so wrongly, do so no more: it is not lawful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:48
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:49
verses.text: But if ye have done so already, and have such money in your possession, and have filled your coffers thereby, and were heaping up treasure by these means: what ye have comes of evil, now then add not evil to it, and make to yourselves friends of the mammon of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:50
verses.text: Had Zacchaeus what he had from good sources? Read and see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:51
verses.text: He was the chief of the publicans, that is, he was one to whom the public taxes were paid in: by this he had his wealth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:52
verses.text: He had oppressed many, had taken from many, and so had heaped much together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:53
verses.text: Christ entered into his house, and salvation came upon his house; for so said the Lord Himself, "This day is salvation come to this house".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:54
verses.text: Now mark the method of this salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:55
verses.text: First he was longing to see the Lord, because he was little in stature: but when the crowd hindered him, he got up into a sycamore tree, and saw Him as He passed by.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:56
verses.text: But Jesus saw him, and said, "Zacchaeus, come down, I must abide at thy house".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:57
verses.text: Thou art hanging there, but I will not keep thee in suspense.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:58
verses.text: I will not, that is, put thee off.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:59
verses.text: Thou didst wish to see Me as I passed by, to-day shalt thou find Me dwelling at thy house.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:60
verses.text: So 			 the Lord went in unto him, and he, filled with joy, said, "The half of my goods I give to the poor".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:61
verses.text: Lo, how swiftly he runs, who runs to make friends of the mammon of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:62
verses.text: And lest he should be held guilty on any other account, he said, "If I have taken anything from any man, I" will "restore fourfold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:63
verses.text: He inflicted sentence of condemnation on himself, that he might not incur damnation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:64
verses.text: So then, ye who have anything from evil sources, do good therewith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:65
verses.text: Ye who have not, wish 			 not to acquire by evil means.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:66
verses.text: Be thou good thyself, who doest good with what is evilly acquired: and when with this evil thou beginnest to do any good, do not remain evil thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:67
verses.text: Thy money is being converted to good, and dost thou thyself continue evil?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:68
verses.text: There is indeed another way of understanding it; and I will not withhold it too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:69
verses.text: The mammon of iniquity is all the riches of this world, from whatever source they come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:70
verses.text: For howsoever they be heaped together, they are the mammon of iniquity, that is, the riches of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:71
verses.text: What is, "they are the riches of iniquity"? It is money which iniquity calls by the name of riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:72
verses.text: For if we seek for the true riches, they are different from these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:73
verses.text: In these Job abounded, 			 naked as he was, when he had a heart full to Godward, and poured out praises like most costly gems to his God, when he had lost all he had.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:74
verses.text: And from what treasure did he this, if he had nothing? These then are the true riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:75
verses.text: But the other sort are called riches by iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:76
verses.text: Thou dost possess these riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:77
verses.text: I blame it not: an inheritance has come to thee, thy father was rich, and he left it to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:78
verses.text: Or thou hast honestly acquired them: thou hast a house full of the fruit of just labour; I blame it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:79
verses.text: Yet even thus do not call them riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:80
verses.text: For if thou dost call them riches, thou wilt love them: and if thou love 			 them, thou wilt perish with them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:81
verses.text: Lose, that thou be not lost: give, that thou mayest gain: sow, that thou mayest reap.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:82
verses.text: Call not these riches, for "the true" they are not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:83
verses.text: They are full of poverty, and liable ever to accidents.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:84
verses.text: What sort of riches are those, for whose sake thou art afraid of the robber, for whose sake thou art afraid of thine own servant, lest he should kill thee, and take them away, and fly? If they were true riches, they would give thee security.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:85
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:86
verses.text: So then those are the true riches, which when we have them, we cannot lose.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:87
verses.text: And lest haply thou shouldest fear a thief because of them, they will be there where none can take them away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:88
verses.text: Hear thy Lord, "Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where no thief approacheth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:89
verses.text: Then will they be riches, when thou hast removed them hence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:90
verses.text: As long as they are in the earth, they are not riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:91
verses.text: But the world calls them riches, iniquity calls them so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:92
verses.text: God calls them therefore the mammon of iniquity, because iniquity calls them riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:93
verses.text: Hear the Psalm, "O Lord, deliver me out of the hand of strange children, whose mouth hath spoken vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:94
verses.text: Whose sons are as new plants, firmly rooted from their youth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:95
verses.text: Their daughters decked out, adorned round about after the similitude of a temple.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:96
verses.text: Their storehouses full, flowing out from this into that.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:97
verses.text: Their oxen fat, their sheep fruitful, multiplying in their goings forth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:98
verses.text: There is no breach of wall, nor going forth, no crying out in their streets".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:99
verses.text: Lo, what sort of happiness the Psalmist has described: but hear what is the case with them whom he has set forth as children of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:100
verses.text: "Whose mouth hath spoken vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of iniquity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:101
verses.text: Thus has he set them forth, and said that their happiness is only upon the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:102
verses.text: And what did he add? "They are happy the people that hath these things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:103
verses.text: But who called them so? "Strange children," aliens from the race, and belonging not to the 			 seed of Abraham: they "called the people happy that hath these things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:104
verses.text: Who called them so? "They whose mouth hath spoken vanity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:105
verses.text: It is a vain thing then to call them happy who have these things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:106
verses.text: And yet they are called so by them, "whose mouth hath spoken vanity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:107
verses.text: By them the "mammon of iniquity" of the Gospel is called riches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:108
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:109
verses.text: But what sayest thou? Seeing that these "strange children" that they "whose mouth hath spoken vanity," have "called the people happy that hath these things," what sayest thou? These are false riches, show me the true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:110
verses.text: Thou findest fault with these, show me what thou praisest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:111
verses.text: Thou wishest me to despise these, show me what to prefer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:112
verses.text: Let the Psalmist speak himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:113
verses.text: For he who said, "they called the people happy that hath these things," 			 gives us such an answer, as if we had said to him, that is, to the Psalmist himself, "Lo, this thou hast taken away from us, and nothing hast thou given us: lo, these, lo, these we despise; whereby shall we live, whereby shall we be happy? For they who have spoken, they will undertake to answer for themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:114
verses.text: For they have 'called' men 'who have' riches 'happy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:115
verses.text: ' But what sayest thou?" As if he had been thus questioned, he makes answer and says, They call the rich happy: but I say, "Happy are the people whose is the Lord their God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:116
verses.text: Thus then thou hast heard of the true riches, make friends of the mammon of iniquity, and thou shalt be "a happy people, whose is the Lord their God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:117
verses.text: At times we go along the way, and see very pleasant and 			 productive estates, and we say, "Whose estate is that?" We are told, "such a man's;" and we say, "Happy man!" We "speak vanity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:118
verses.text: Happy he whose is that house, happy he whose that estate, happy he whose that flock, happy he whose that servant, happy he whose is that household.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:119
verses.text: Take away vanity if Thou wouldest hear the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:120
verses.text: "Happy he whose is the Lord" his "God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:121
verses.text: For not he who has that estate is happy: but he whose is that "God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:122
verses.text: But in order to declare most 			 plainly the happiness of possessions, thou sayest that thy estate has made thee happy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:123
verses.text: And why? Because thou livest by it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:124
verses.text: For when thou dost highly praise thine estate, thou sayest thus, "It finds me food, I live by it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:125
verses.text: Consider whereby thou dost really live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:126
verses.text: He by whom thou livest, is He to whom thou sayest, "With Thee is the fountain of life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:127
verses.text: "Happy is the people whose God is the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:128
verses.text: O Lord my God, O Lord our God, make us happy by Thee, that we may come unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:129
verses.text: We wish not to be happy from gold, or silver, or land, from these earthly, and most vain, and transitory goods of this perishable life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:130
verses.text: Let not "our mouth speak vanity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:131
verses.text: Make us happy by Thee, seeing that we shall never lose Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:132
verses.text: When we shall once have gotten Thee, we shall neither lose Thee, nor be lost ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:133
verses.text: Make us happy by Thee, 			 because "Happy is the people whose is the Lord their God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:134
verses.text: Nor will God be angry if we shall say of Him, He is our estate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:135
verses.text: For we read that "the Lord is the portion of my inheritance".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:136
verses.text: Grand thing, Brethren, we are both His inheritance, and He is ours, seeing that we both cultivate His service and He cultivateth us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:137
verses.text: It is no derogation to His honour that He cultivateth us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:138
verses.text: Because if we cultivate Him as our God, He cultivateth us as His field.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:139
verses.text: And, (that ye may know that He doth cultivate us) hear Him whom He hath sent to us: "I," saith He, "am the vine, ye are the branches, My Father is the Husbandman".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:140
verses.text: Therefore He doth cultivate us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:141
verses.text: But if we yield fruit, He prepares for us His garner.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:142
verses.text: But if under the attention of so great a hand we will be barren, and for good fruit bring forth thorns, I am loth to say what follows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:143
verses.text: Let us make an end with a theme of joy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 62:144
verses.text: "Let us turn then to the Lord," etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:1
verses.text: Sermon LXIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:2
verses.text: [CXIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xvii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:5
verses.text: 3, "If thy brother sin, rebuke him," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:6
verses.text: , touching the remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:7
verses.text: Delivered at the Table of St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:8
verses.text: Cyprian, in the presence of Count Boniface.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:9
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:10
verses.text: The Holy Gospel which we heard just now as it was being read, has admonished touching the remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:11
verses.text: And on this subject must ye be admonished now by my discourse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:12
verses.text: For we are ministers of the word, not our own word, but the word of our God and Lord, whom no one serves without glory, whom no one despises without punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:13
verses.text: He then the Lord our God, who abiding with the Father made us, and having been made for us, re-made us, He 			 the Lord our God Jesus Christ Himself says to us what we have heard just now in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:14
verses.text: "If," He saith, "thy brother shall sin against thee, rebuke him, and if he shall repent, forgive him; and if he shall sin against time seven times in a day, and shall come and say, I repent, forgive him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:15
verses.text: He would not have "seven times in a day" otherwise understood than "as often as may be," lest haply he sin eight times, and thou be unwilling to forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:16
verses.text: What then is "seven times"? Always, as often as he shall sin and repent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:17
verses.text: For this, "Seven times in a day will I praise thee," is the same as in another Psalm, "His praise shall always be in my mouth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:18
verses.text: And there is the strongest reason why seven times should be put for that which is always: for the whole course of time revolves in a circle of seven coming and returning days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:19
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:20
verses.text: Whosoever then thou art that hast thy thoughts on Christ, and desirest to receive what He hath promised, be not slow to do that which He hath enjoined.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:21
verses.text: Now what hath He promised? "Eternal life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:22
verses.text: And what hath He enjoined? That pardon be given to thy brother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:23
verses.text: As if He had said to thee, "Do thou, O man, give pardon to a man, that I, who am God, may come unto thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:24
verses.text: But that I may pass over, or rather pass by for a while, those more exalted divine 			 promises in which our Creator engages to make us equal with His Angels, that we may with Him, and in Him, and by Him, live without end; not to speak of this just now, dost thou not wish to receive of thy God this very thing, which thou art commanded to give thy brother? This very thing, I say, which thou art commanded to give thy brother, dost thou not wish to receive from thy Lord? Tell me if thou wishest it not; and so give it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:25
verses.text: What is this, but that thou shouldest forgive him that asks 			 thee, if thou require to be forgiven? But if thou have nothing to be forgiven thee, I dare to say, be unwilling to forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:26
verses.text: Though I ought not even to say this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:27
verses.text: Though thou have nothing to be forgiven thee, forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:28
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:29
verses.text: Thou art just on the point of saying to me, "But I am not God, I am a man, a sinner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:30
verses.text: God be thanked that thou dost confess thou hast sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:31
verses.text: Forgive then, that they may be forgiven thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:32
verses.text: Yet the Lord Himself our God exhorteth us to imitate Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:33
verses.text: In the first place God Himself, Christ, exhorteth us, of whom the Apostle Peter said, "Christ hath suffered for us, leaving you an example that ye should follow His steps, who did no sin, neither was guile, found in 			 His mouth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:34
verses.text: He then verily had no sin, yet did He die for our sins, and shed His Blood for the remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:35
verses.text: He took upon Him for our sakes what was not His due, that He might deliver us from what was due to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:36
verses.text: Death was not due to Him, nor life to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:37
verses.text: Why? Because we were sinners.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:38
verses.text: Death was not due to Him, nor life to us; He received what was not due to Him, He gave what was not due to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:39
verses.text: But since we are speaking of the remission of sins, lest ye should think it too high a thing 			 to imitate Christ, hear the Apostle saying, "Forgiving one another, even as God in Christ hath forgiven you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:40
verses.text: "Be ye therefore imitators of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:41
verses.text: They are the Apostle's words, not mine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:42
verses.text: Is it indeed a proud thing to imitate God? Hear the Apostle, "Be ye imitators of God as dearly beloved children".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:43
verses.text: Thou art called a child: if thou refuse to imitate Him, why seekest thou His inheritance?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:44
verses.text: This would I say even if thou hadst no sin which thou mightest desire to be forgiven thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:45
verses.text: But as it is, whosoever thou art, thou art a man; though thou be righteous, thou art a man; be thou layman, or monk, or clerk, or Bishop, or Apostle, thou art a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:46
verses.text: Hear the Apostle's voice, "If we shall say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:47
verses.text: He, that famous John and an Evangelist, he whom the Lord Christ loved beyond all the rest, who lay on His breast, he says, "If we shall say".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:48
verses.text: He did not say, "If ye shall say that ye have no sin," but "if we shall say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:49
verses.text: He joined himself in the guilt, that he might be joined in the pardon also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:50
verses.text: "If we shall say".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:51
verses.text: Consider who it is that says, "If we shall say that we have no sin, we deceive 			 ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:52
verses.text: But if we shall confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all iniquity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:53
verses.text: How does He cleanse? By forgiving, not as though He found nothing to punish, but as finding something to forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:54
verses.text: So then, Brethren, if we have sins, let us forgive them that ask us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:55
verses.text: Let us not retain enmities in our heart against another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:56
verses.text: For the retaining of enmities more than anything corrupts this heart of ours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:57
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:58
verses.text: I would then that thou shouldest forgive, seeing that I find thee asking forgiveness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:59
verses.text: Thou art asked, forgive: thou art asked, and thou wilt ask thyself; thou art asked, forgive; thou wilt ask to be forgiven; for, lo, the time of prayer will come: I have thee fast in the words thou wilt have to speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:60
verses.text: Thou wilt say, "Our Father, which art in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:61
verses.text: For thou wilt not be in the number of children, if thou shalt not say, "Our Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:62
verses.text: So then thou wilt 			 say, "Our Father, which art in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:63
verses.text: Follow on; "Hallowed be Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:64
verses.text: Say on, "Thy kingdom come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:65
verses.text: Follow still on, "Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:66
verses.text: See what thou addest next, "Give us this day our daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:67
verses.text: Where are thy riches? So thou art a beggar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:68
verses.text: Nevertheless in the mean while (it is the point I am speaking of), say what is next after, "Give us this day our daily bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:69
verses.text: Say what follows this: "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:70
verses.text: Now thou hast come to my words, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:71
verses.text: By what right? by what covenant? on what condition? on what express stipulation? "As we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:72
verses.text: It is but a small thing that thou dost not forgive; yea thou dost more, thou 			 liest unto God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:73
verses.text: The condition is laid down, the law fixed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:74
verses.text: "Forgive as I forgive".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:75
verses.text: Therefore He does not forgive, unless thou forgivest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:76
verses.text: "Forgive as I forgive".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:77
verses.text: Thou wishest to be forgiven when thou askest, forgive him that asks of thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:78
verses.text: He that is skilled in heaven's laws has dictated these prayers: He does not deceive thee; ask according to the tenor of His heavenly voice: say, "Forgive us, as we also forgive," and do what thou sayest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:79
verses.text: He that lies in his prayers, loses the benefit he seeks: he that lies in his prayers, both loses his cause, and finds his punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:80
verses.text: And if any one lies to the emperor, he is convicted of his lie at his coming: but when thou liest in prayer, thou by thy very prayer art convicted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:81
verses.text: For God does not seek for witness as regards thee to convict thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:82
verses.text: He who dictated the prayers to thee, is thine Advocate: if thou liest, He is a witness against thee: if thou dost not amend thyself, He will be thy Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:83
verses.text: So then both say it, and do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:84
verses.text: For if thou say it not, thou wilt not obtain making thy requests contrary to the law; but if thou say it and do it not, thou wilt be further guilty of lying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:85
verses.text: There is no means of evading that verse, save by fulfilling what we say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:86
verses.text: Can we blot this 			 verse out of our prayer? Would ye that clause, "Forgive us our debts," should be there, and that we should blot out what follows, "As we also forgive our debtors"? Thou shalt not blot it out, lest thou be first blotted out thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:87
verses.text: So then in this prayer thou sayest, "Give," and thou sayest, "Forgive:" that thou mayest receive what thou hast not, and may be forgiven what thou hast done amiss.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:88
verses.text: So then thou wishest to receive, give; thou wishest to be forgiven, forgive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:89
verses.text: It is a 			 brief summary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:90
verses.text: Hear Christ Himself in another place, "Forgive, and ye shall be forgiven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:91
verses.text: What will ye forgive? What others have sinned against you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:92
verses.text: What shall ye be forgiven? What ye have sinned yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:93
verses.text: "Forgive".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:94
verses.text: "Give, and there shall be given you what ye desire," eternal life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 63:95
verses.text: Support the temporal life of the poor man, sustain the poor man's present life, and for this so small and earthly seed ye shall receive for harvest life eternal, Amen.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:1
verses.text: Sermon LXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:2
verses.text: [CXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xviii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:5
verses.text: 1,"They ought always to pray, and not to faint," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:6
verses.text: And on the two who went up into the temple to pray: and of the little children who were presented unto Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:8
verses.text: The lesson of the Holy Gospel builds us up unto the duty of praying and believing, and of not putting our trust in ourselves, but in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:9
verses.text: What greater encouragement to prayer than the parable which is proposed to us of the unjust judge? For an unjust judge, who feared not God, nor regarded man, yet gave ear to a widow who besought him, overcome by her importunity, not inclined thereto by kindness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:10
verses.text: If he then heard her prayer, who hated to be asked, how must He hear who exhorts us to ask? When therefore by this comparison from a contrary case the Lord had taught that "men ought always to pray and not to faint," He added and said, "Nevertheless, when the Son of Man shall come, thinkest thou that He shall find faith on the earth?" If faith fail, prayer perishes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:11
verses.text: For who prays for that which he does not believe? Whence also the blessed Apostle, when he exhorted to prayer, said, "Whosoever shall call upon the Name of the Lord, shall be saved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:12
verses.text: And in order to show that faith is the fountain of prayer, he went on and said, "How then shall they call on Him in whom they have not believed?" So then that we may pray, let us believe; and that this same faith whereby we pray fail not, let us pray.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:13
verses.text: Faith pours out prayer, and the pouring out of prayer obtains the strengthening of faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:14
verses.text: Faith, I say, pours out prayer, the pouring out of prayer obtains strengthening even for faith itself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:15
verses.text: For that faith might not fail in temptations, therefore did the Lord say," Watch and pray, lest ye enter into temptation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:16
verses.text: "Watch," He saith, "and pray, lest ye enter into temptation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:17
verses.text: What is to "enter into temptation," but to depart from faith? For so far temptation advances as faith gives way: and so far temptation gives way, as faith advances.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:18
verses.text: For that you may know, Beloved, more plainly, that the Lord said, "Watch and pray, lest ye enter into temptation," as touching faith lest it should fail and perish; He said in the same place of the Gospel, "This night hath Satan desired 			 to sift  you as wheat, and I have prayed for thee, Peter, that thy faith fail not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:19
verses.text: He that defendeth prayeth, and shall not he pray who is in peril? For in the words of the Lord, "when the Son of Man shall come, thinkest thou that He shall find faith on the earth?" He spoke of that faith, which is perfect.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:20
verses.text: For it is scarce found on the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:21
verses.text: Lo! this Church of God is full: and who would come hither, if there were no faith? But who would not remove mountains, if there were full faith? Look at the very Apostles: they would not have left all they had, have 			 trodden under foot this world's hope, and followed the Lord, if they had not had great faith; and yet if they had full faith, they would not have said to the Lord, "Increase our faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:22
verses.text: See again, that man confessing both of himself (behold faith, yet not full faith), who when he had presented to the Lord his son to be cured of an evil spirit, and was asked whether he believed, answered and said, "Lord, I believe, help Thou mine unbelief".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:23
verses.text: "Lord," says he, "I believe," I believe; therefore there was faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:24
verses.text: But "help Thou mine unbelief," therefore there was not full faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:25
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:26
verses.text: But inasmuch as faith belongs not to the proud, but to the humble, "He spake this parable unto certain who seemed to themselves to be righteous, and despised others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:27
verses.text: Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:28
verses.text: The Pharisee said, God, I thank Thee that I am not as the rest of men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:29
verses.text: He might at least have said, "as many men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:30
verses.text: What does, "as the rest of men," mean, but all except himself? "I," he says, "am just, the rest are sinners".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:31
verses.text: "I am not as the rest of men, unjust, extortioners, adulterers".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:32
verses.text: And, lo, from thy neighbour, the publican, thou takest occasion of greater pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:33
verses.text: "As," he says, "this publican".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:34
verses.text: "I," he says, "am alone, he is of the rest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:35
verses.text: "I am not," says he, "such as he is, through my righteous 			 deeds, whereby I have no unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:36
verses.text: "I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:37
verses.text: In all his words seek out for any one thing that he asked of God, and thou wilt find nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:38
verses.text: He went up to pray: he had no mind to pray to God, but to laud himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:39
verses.text: Nay, it is but a small part of it, that he prayed not to God, but lauded himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:40
verses.text: More than this he even mocked him that did pray.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:41
verses.text: "But the Publican stood afar off;" and yet he was in deed near to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:42
verses.text: The consciousness of his heart kept him off, piety brought him close.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:43
verses.text: "But the Publican stood afar off:" yet the Lord regarded him near.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:44
verses.text: "For the Lord is high, yet hath He respect unto the lowly".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:45
verses.text: But "those that are high" as was this Pharisee, "He knoweth afar off".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:46
verses.text: "The high" indeed "God knoweth afar off," but He doth not pardon them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:47
verses.text: Hear still more the humility of the Publican.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:48
verses.text: It is but a small matter that he stood afar off; "he did not even lift up his eyes unto heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:49
verses.text: He looked not, that he might be looked upon.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:50
verses.text: He did not dare to look upwards, his conscience pressed him down: but hope lifted him up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:51
verses.text: Hear again, "he smote his breast".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:52
verses.text: He 			 punished himself: wherefore the Lord spared him for his confession.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:53
verses.text: "He smote his breast, saying, Lord, be merciful to me a sinner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:54
verses.text: See who he is that prays.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:55
verses.text: Why dost thou marvel that God should pardon, when he acknowledges his own sin? Thus thou hast heard the case of the Pharisee and Publican; now hear the sentence; thou hast heard the proud accuser, thou hast heard the humble criminal; hear now the Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:56
verses.text: "Verily I say unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:57
verses.text: The Truth saith, God saith, the Judge saith it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:58
verses.text: "Verily I say unto you, That Publican went down from the temple justified rather than that Pharisee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:59
verses.text: Tell us, Lord, the cause.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:60
verses.text: Lo! I see that the publican goes down from the temple justified rather than the Pharisee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:61
verses.text: I ask why? Dost thou ask why? Hear why.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:62
verses.text: "Because every one that exalteth himself shall be abased, and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:63
verses.text: Thou hast heard the sentence, beware of its evil cause.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:64
verses.text: In other words, thou hast heard the sentence, beware of pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:66
verses.text: Let now those ungodly babblers, whosoever they be, who presume on their own strength, let them hear and see these things: let them hear who say, God made me a man, I make myself just.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:67
verses.text: O thou who art worse and more detestable than the Pharisee! The Pharisee in the Gospel did indeed call himself just, but yet he gave thanks to God for it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:68
verses.text: He called himself just, but yet he gave God thanks.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:69
verses.text: "I thank Thee, O God, that I am not as the rest of men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:70
verses.text: "I thank 			 Thee, O God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:71
verses.text: He gives God thanks, that he is not as the rest of men: and yet he is blamed as being proud and puffed up; not in that he gave God thanks, but in that he desired as it were no more to be added unto him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:72
verses.text: "I thank thee that I am not as the rest of men, unjust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:73
verses.text: So then thou art just; so then thou askest for nothing; so then thou art full already; so then the life of man is not a trial upon earth; so then thou art full already; so then thou aboundest already, so then thou hast no ground for saying, "Forgive us our debts!" What must his case be then who impiously impugns grace, if he is blamed who give thanks proudly?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:74
verses.text: And, lo, after the case had been stated, and the sentence pronounced, little children also came forth, yea, rather, are carried and presented to be touched.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:75
verses.text: To be touched by whom, but the Physician? Surely, it will be said, they must be whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:76
verses.text: To whom are the infants presented to be touched? To whom? To the Saviour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:77
verses.text: If to the Saviour, they are brought to be saved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:78
verses.text: To whom, but to Him "who came to seek and to save what was lost".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:79
verses.text: How were they lost? As far as concerns them personally, I see that they are without fault, I am seeking for their guiltiness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:80
verses.text: Whence is it? I listen to the Apostle, "By one man sin entered into the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:81
verses.text: By one man," he says, "sin entered into the world, and death by sin, and so death passed upon all men by him in whom all sinned".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:82
verses.text: Let then the little children come, let them come: let the Lord be heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:83
verses.text: "Suffer little children to come unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:84
verses.text: Let the little ones come, let the sick come to the Physician, the lost to their Redeemer: let them come, let no man hinder them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:85
verses.text: In the branch they have not yet committed any evil, but they are ruined in their root.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:86
verses.text: "Let the Lord bless the small with the great".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:87
verses.text: Let the Physician touch both small and great.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:88
verses.text: The cause of the little ones we commend to their elders.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:89
verses.text: Speak ye for them who are mute, pray for them who weep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:90
verses.text: If ye are not their elders to no purpose, be ye their guardians: defend them who are not able yet to manage their own cause.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:91
verses.text: Common is the loss, let the finding be common: we were lost all together, together be we found in Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:92
verses.text: Uneven is the desert, but common is the grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:93
verses.text: They have no evil 			 but what they have drawn from the source: they have no evil but what they have derived from the first original.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:94
verses.text: Let not them keep them off from salvation, who to what they have so derived have added much more evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:95
verses.text: The elder in age is the elder in iniquity too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:96
verses.text: But the grace of God effaces what thou hast derived, effaces too what thou hast added.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 64:97
verses.text: For, "where sin abounded, grace hath superabounded".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:1
verses.text: Sermon LXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:2
verses.text: [CXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, Luke xxiv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:5
verses.text: 36, "He himself stood in the midst of them, and saith unto them, peace be unto you," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:7
verses.text: The Lord appeared to His disciples after His resurrection, as ye have heard, and saluted them, saying, "Peace be unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:8
verses.text: This is peace indeed, and the salutation of salvation: for the very word salutation has received its name from salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:9
verses.text: And what can be better than that Salvation Itself should salute man? For Christ is our Salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:10
verses.text: He is our Salvation, who was wounded for us, and fixed by nails to the tree, and being taken down from the tree, was laid in the sepulchre.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:11
verses.text: And from the sepulchre He arose, with His wounds healed, His scars kept.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:12
verses.text: For this He judged expedient for His disciples, that His scars should be kept, where by the wounds of their hearts might be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:13
verses.text: What wounds? The wounds of unbelief.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:14
verses.text: For He appeared to their eyes, exhibiting real flesh, and they thought they saw a spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:15
verses.text: It is no light wound, this wound of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:16
verses.text: Yea, they have made a malignant heresy who have abided in this wound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:17
verses.text: But do we suppose that the disciples had not been wounded, because they were so quickly healed? Only, Beloved, suppose, if they had continued in this wound, to think that the Body which had been buried, could not rise again, but that a spirit in the image of a body, deceived the eyes of men: 			 if they had continued in this belief, yea, rather in this unbelief, not their wounds, but their death would have had to be bewailed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:18
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:19
verses.text: But what said the Lord Jesus? "Why are ye troubled, and why do thoughts ascend into your hearts?" If thoughts ascend into your heart, the thoughts come from the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:20
verses.text: But it is good for a man, not that a thought should ascend into his heart, but that his heart should itself ascend upwards, where the Apostle would have believers place their hearts, to whom he said, "If ye be risen with Christ, mind those things which are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:21
verses.text: Seek those things which are above, not the things which are upon the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:22
verses.text: For ye are dead, 			 and your life is hid with Christ in God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:23
verses.text: When Christ your life shall appear, then shall ye also appear with Him in glory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:24
