verses.text: In what glory? The glory of the resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:25
verses.text: In what glory? Hear the Apostle saying of this body, "It is sown in dishonour, it shall rise in glory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:26
verses.text: This glory the Apostles were unwilling to assign to their Master, their Christ, their Lord: they did not believe that His Body could rise from the sepulchre: they thought Him to be a Spirit, though they saw His flesh, and they believed not their very eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:27
verses.text: Yet we believe them who preach but do not show Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:28
verses.text: Lo, they believed not Christ who showed Himself to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:29
verses.text: Malignant wound! Let the remedies for these scars come forth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:30
verses.text: "Why are ye troubled, and why do thoughts ascend 			 into your hearts? See My hands and My feet," where I was fixed with the nails.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:31
verses.text: "Handle and see".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:32
verses.text: But ye see, and yet do not see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:33
verses.text: "Handle and see".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:34
verses.text: What? "That a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:35
verses.text: When He had thus spoken," so it is written, "He showed them His hands and His feet".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:36
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:37
verses.text: "And while they were yet in hesitation, and wondered for joy".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:38
verses.text: Now there was joy already, and yet hesitation continued.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:39
verses.text: For a thing incredible had taken place, yet taken place it had.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:40
verses.text: Is it at this day a thing incredible, that the Body of the Lord rose again from the sepulchre? The whole cleansed world has believed it; whoso has not believed it, has remained in his uncleanness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:41
verses.text: Yet at that time it was incredible: and persuasion was addressed not to the eyes only, but to the hands also, that by the bodily senses faith might descend into their heart, and that faith so descending into their heart might be preached throughout the world to them who neither saw nor touched, and yet without doubting believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:42
verses.text: "Have ye," saith He, "anything to eat?" How much doeth the good 			 Builder still to build up the edifice of faith? He did not hunger, yet He asked to eat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:43
verses.text: And He ate by an act of His power, not through necessity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:44
verses.text: So then let the disciples acknowledge the verity of His body, which the world has acknowledged at their preaching.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:45
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:46
verses.text: If haply there be any heretics who still in their hearts maintain that Christ exhibited Himself to sight, but that Christ's was not very flesh; let them now lay aside that error, and let the Gospel persuade them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:47
verses.text: We do but blame them for entertaining this conceit: He will damn them if they shall persevere in it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:48
verses.text: Who art thou who dost not believe that a body laid in the sepulchre could rise again? If thou art a Manichee, who dost not believe that He was 			 crucified either, because thou dost not believe that He was even born, thou declarest that all that He showed was false.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:49
verses.text: He showed what was false, and dost thou speak the truth? Thou dost not lie with thy mouth, and did He lie in His body? Lo thou dost suppose that He appeared unto the eyes of men what He really was not, that He was a spirit, not flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:50
verses.text: Hear Him: He loves thee, let Him not condemn thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:51
verses.text: Hear Him speaking: lo, He speaks to thee, thou unhappy one, He speaks to thee, "Why art 			 thou troubled, and why do thoughts ascend into thine heart?" "See," saith He, "My hands and My feet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:52
verses.text: Handle and see, because a spirit hath not flesh and bones as ye see Me have".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:53
verses.text: This spake the Truth, and did He deceive? It was a body then, it was flesh; that which had been buried, appeared.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:54
verses.text: Let doubting perish, and meet praise ensue.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:55
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:56
verses.text: He showed himself then to the disciples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:57
verses.text: What is "Himself"? The Head of His Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:58
verses.text: The Church was foreseen by Him as in thee to be throughout the world, by the disciples it was not yet seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:59
verses.text: He showed the Head, He promised the Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:60
verses.text: For what did He add next? "These are the words which I spake to you, while I was yet with you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:61
verses.text: What is this, "While I was yet with you"? Was He not with them then when He was speaking to them? What is, "when I was yet with you"? was with you as mortal, which now I am not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:62
verses.text: I was with you when I had yet to die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:63
verses.text: What is, "with you"? With you who were to die, Myself to die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:64
verses.text: Now I am no more with you: for I am with those who are to die, Myself to die no more for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:65
verses.text: This then is what I said to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:66
verses.text: What? "That all things must be fulfilled which are written in 			 the Law, and in the Prophets, and in the Psalms concerning Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:67
verses.text: I told you that all things must be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:68
verses.text: "Then opened He their understanding".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:69
verses.text: Come then, O Lord, employ Thy keys, open, that we may understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:70
verses.text: Lo, Thou dost tell all things, and yet are not believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:71
verses.text: Thou art thought to be a spirit, art touched, art rudely handled, and yet they who touch Thee hesitate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:72
verses.text: Thou dost admonish them out of the Scriptures, and yet they understand Thee not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:73
verses.text: Their hearts are closed, open, and enter in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:74
verses.text: He did so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:75
verses.text: "Then opened He their understanding".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:76
verses.text: Open, O Lord, yea, open the heart of him who is in doubt concerning Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:77
verses.text: Open "his" understanding who believes that Christ was a phantom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:78
verses.text: "Then opened He their understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:79
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:80
verses.text: And "He said unto them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:81
verses.text: What? "That thus it behoved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:82
verses.text: That thus it is written, and thus it behoved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:83
verses.text: What? "That Christ should suffer, and rise from the dead the third day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:84
verses.text: And this they saw, they saw Him suffering, they saw Him hanging, they saw Him with them alive after His resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:85
verses.text: What then did they not see? The Body, that is, the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:86
verses.text: Him they saw, her they saw not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:87
verses.text: They saw the Bridegroom, the Bride yet lay hid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:88
verses.text: Let him promise her too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:89
verses.text: "Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:90
verses.text: This is the Bridegroom, what of the Bride? "And that repentance and remission of sins should 			 be preached in His Name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:91
verses.text: This the disciples did not yet see: they did not yet see the Church throughout all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:92
verses.text: They saw the Head, and they believed the Head touching the Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:93
verses.text: By this which they saw, they believed that which they saw not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:94
verses.text: We too are like to them: we see something which they saw not, and something we do not see which they did see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:95
verses.text: What do we see, which they saw not? The Church throughout all nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:96
verses.text: What do we not see, which they saw? Christ present in 			 the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:97
verses.text: As they saw Him, and believed concerning the Body, so do we see the Body; let us believe concerning the Head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:98
verses.text: Let what we have respectively seen help us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:99
verses.text: The sight of Christ helped them to believe the future Church: the sight of the Church helps us to believe that Christ has risen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:100
verses.text: Their faith was made complete, and ours is made complete also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:101
verses.text: Their faith was made complete from the sight of the Head, ours is made complete by the sight of the Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:102
verses.text: Christ was made known to them 			 "wholly," and to us is He so made known: but He was not seen "wholly" by them, nor by us has He been "wholly" seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:103
verses.text: By them the Head was seen, the Body believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:104
verses.text: By us the Body has been seen, the Head believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:105
verses.text: Yet to none is Christ lacking: in all He is complete, though to this day His Body remains imperfect.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:106
verses.text: The Apostles believed; through them many of the inhabitants of Jerusalem believed; Judaea believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:107
verses.text: Samaria believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:108
verses.text: Let the members be added on, the building added on to the 			 foundation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:109
verses.text: "For no other foundation can any man lay," says the Apostle, "than that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:110
verses.text: Let the Jews rage madly, and be filled with jealousy: Stephen be stoned, Saul keep the raiment of them who stone him, Saul, one day to be the Apostle Paul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:111
verses.text: Let Stephen be killed, the Church of Jerusalem dispersed in confusion: out of it go forth burning brands, and spread themselves and spread their flame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:112
verses.text: For in the Church of Jerusalem, as it were burning brands were set on fire by the Holy Spirit, when they had all one soul, and one heart to God-ward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:113
verses.text: When Stephen was stoned, that pile suffered persecution: the brands were dispersed, and the world was set on fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:114
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:115
verses.text: And then intent on his furious schemes, that Saul received letters from the chief of the priests, and began his journey in his cruel rage, breathing out slaughter, thirsting for blood, to drag bound and to hurry off to punishment whomsoever he could, and from every quarter that he could, and to satiate himself with the shedding of their blood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:116
verses.text: But where was God, where was Christ, where He that had crowned Stephen? Where, but in heaven? Let Him now look on Saul, 			 and mock him in his fury, and call from heaven, "'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me?' I am in heaven, and thou in earth, and yet thou persecutest Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:117
verses.text: Thou dost not touch the body, but my members thou art treading down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:118
verses.text: Yet what art thou doing? What art thou gaining? 'It is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:119
verses.text: ' Kick as thou wilt, thou only distressest thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:120
verses.text: Lay aside thy fury then, recover soundness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:121
verses.text: Lay aside evil counsel, seek after good succour".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:122
verses.text: By that voice he was struck to the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:123
verses.text: Who was struck to the earth? The persecutor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:124
verses.text: Lo, by that 			 one word was he overcome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:125
verses.text: After what wast thou going, after what was thy fury carrying thee? Those whom thou wast seeking out, now thou followest; whom thou wast persecuting, now for them thou sufferest persecution.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:126
verses.text: He rises up the preacher, who was struck to the earth, the persecutor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:127
verses.text: He heard the Lord's voice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:128
verses.text: He was blinded, but in the body only, that he might be enlightened in heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:129
verses.text: He was brought to Ananias, catechised on sundry points, baptized, and so came forth an Apostle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:130
verses.text: Speak 			 then, preach, preach Christ, spread His doctrine, O thou goodly leader of the flock, but lately a wolf.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:131
verses.text: See him, mark him, who once was raging.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:132
verses.text: "But for me, God forbid that I should glory, save in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world has been crucified to me and I to the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:133
verses.text: Spread the Gospel: scatter with thy mouth what thou hast conceived in thine heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:134
verses.text: Let the nations hear, let the nations believe; let the nations multiply, let the Lord's empurpled spouse spring forth from the blood of Martyrs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:135
verses.text: And from her how many have come already, how many members have cleaved to the Head, and cleave to Him still and believe! They were baptized, and others shall be baptized, and after them shall others come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:136
verses.text: Then I say, at the end of the world shall the 			 stones be joined to the foundation, living stones, holy stones, that at the end the whole edifice may be built by that Church, yea by this very Church which now sings the new song, while the house is in building.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:137
verses.text: For so the Psalm itself says, "When the house was in building after the captivity;" and what says it, "Sing unto the Lord a new song, sing unto the Lord all the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:138
verses.text: How great a house is this! But when does it sing the new song? When it is in building.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:139
verses.text: When is it dedicated? At the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:140
verses.text: Its foundation has been already dedicated, because He hath ascended into heaven, and dieth no more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 65:141
verses.text: When we too shall have risen to die no more, then shall we be dedicated.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:1
verses.text: Sermon LXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:2
verses.text: [CXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John i.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:5
verses.text: 1, "In the beginning was the word, and the word was with God, and the word was God," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:6
verses.text: Against the Arians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:8
verses.text: The section of the Gospel which has been read, most dearly beloved brethren, looketh for the pure eye of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:9
verses.text: For from John's Gospel we have understood our Lord Jesus Christ according to His Divinity for the creating of the whole creation, and according to His Humanity for the recovery of the creature fallen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:10
verses.text: Now in this same Gospel we find what sort and how great a man was John, that from the dignity of the dispenser it may be 			 understood of how great a price is the Word which could be announced by such a man; yea, rather how without price is That which surpasseth all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:11
verses.text: For any purchasable thing is either equal to the price, or it is below it, or it exceeds it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:12
verses.text: When any one procures a thing for as much as it is worth, the price is equal to the thing which is procured; when for less, it is below it; when for more, it exceeds it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:13
verses.text: But to the Word of God nothing can either be equalled, or to exchange can anything be 			 below It, or above It.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:14
verses.text: For all things can be below the Word of God, for that "all things were made by Him;" yet are they not in such wise below, as if they were the price of the Word, that any one should give something to receive That.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:15
verses.text: Yet if we may say so, and if any principle or custom of speaking admit this expression, the price for procuring the Word, is the procurer himself, who will have given himself for himself to This Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:16
verses.text: Accordingly when we buy anything we look out for something to give, that for the price we give we may have the thing we wish to buy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:17
verses.text: And that which we 			 give is without us; and if it was with us before, what we give becomes without us, that that which we procure may be with us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:18
verses.text: Whatever price the purchaser may find it, it must needs be such as that he gives what he has, and receives what he has not; yet so that he from whom the price goes himself remains, and that for which he gives the price is added to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:19
verses.text: But whoso would procure this Word, whoso would have it, let him not seek for anything without himself to give, let 			 him give himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:20
verses.text: And when he shall have done this, he doth not lose himself, as he loseth the price when he buys anything.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:21
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:22
verses.text: The Word of God then is set forth before all men; let them who can, procure It, and they can who have a godly will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:23
verses.text: For in That Word is peace; and "peace on earth is to men of good will".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:24
verses.text: So then whoso will procure it, let him give himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:25
verses.text: This is as it were the price of the Word, if so it may in any way be said, when he that giveth doth not lose himself, and gaineth the Word for which he giveth himself, and gaineth himself too in the Word to whom he giveth himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:26
verses.text: And what giveth he to the Word? Not ought that is any other's than His, for whom he giveth himself; but what by the Same Word was made, that is given back to Him to be remade; "All things were 			 made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:27
verses.text: If all things, then of course man too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:28
verses.text: If the heaven, and earth, and sea, and all things that are therein, if the whole creation; of course more manifestly he, who being made after the image of God by the Word was made man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:29
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:30
verses.text: I am not now, brethren, discussing how the words, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God," can be understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:31
verses.text: After an ineffable sort it may be understood; it cannot by the words of man he made to be understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:32
verses.text: I am treating of the Word of God, and telling you why It is not understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:33
verses.text: I am not now speaking to make It understood, but I tell you what hinders It from being understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:34
verses.text: For He is a certain Form, a Form not formed, but the Form of all things formed; a Form unchangeable, without failure, without decay, without thee, without place, surpassing all things, 			 being in all things, as at once a kind of foundation in which they are, and a Head-stone under which they are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:35
verses.text: If you say that all things are in Him, you lie not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:36
verses.text: For This Word is called the Wisdom of God; and we have it written, "In Wisdom hast Thou made all things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:37
verses.text: Lo, then in Him are all things: and yet in that He is God, under Him are all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:38
verses.text: I am showing how incomprehensible is what has been read; yet it has been read, not that it should be comprehended by man, but that man should sorrow that he comprehends it not, and find out whereby he is hindered from comprehending, and remove those hindrances, and, himself changed from worse to better, aspire after the perception of the unchangeable Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:39
verses.text: For the Word doth not advance or 			 increase by the addition of those who know It; but is Entire, if thou abide; Entire, if thou depart; Entire, when thou dost return; abiding in Itself, and renewing all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:40
verses.text: It is then the Form of all things, the Form unfashioned, without thee, as I have said, and without space.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:41
verses.text: For whatsoever is contained in space, is circumscribed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:42
verses.text: Every form is circumscribed by bounds; it hath limits wherefrom and whereunto it reaches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:43
verses.text: Again, what is contained in place, and has extension in a sort of bulk 			 and space, is less in its parts than in the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:44
verses.text: God grant that ye may understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:45
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:46
verses.text: Now from the bodies which are day by day before our eyes, which we see, which we touch, among which we live, we are able to judge how that every body hath a form in space.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:47
verses.text: Now everything which occupies a certain space, is less in its parts than in its whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:48
verses.text: The arm, for instance, is a part of the human body; of course the arm is less than the whole body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:49
verses.text: And if the arm be less, it occupies a smaller space.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:50
verses.text: So again the head, in that it is a part of the body, is 			 contained in less space, and is less than the whole body of which it is the head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:51
verses.text: So all things which are in space, are less in their several parts than in the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:52
verses.text: Let us entertain no such idea, no such thought concerning That Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:53
verses.text: Let us not form our conceptions of spiritual things from the suggestion of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:54
verses.text: That Word, That God, is not less in part than in the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:55
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:56
verses.text: But thou art not able to conceive of any such thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:57
verses.text: Such ignorance is more pious than presumptuous knowledge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:58
verses.text: For we are speaking of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:59
verses.text: It is said, "And the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:60
verses.text: We are speaking of God; what marvel, if thou do not comprehend? For if thou comprehend, He is not God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:61
verses.text: Be there a pious confession of ignorance, rather than a rash profession of knowledge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:62
verses.text: To reach to God in any measure by the mind, is a great blessedness; but to comprehend Him, is altogether impossible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:63
verses.text: God is an object for the mind, He is to be understood; a body is for the eyes, it is to be seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:64
verses.text: But thinkest thou that thou comprehendest a body by the eye? Thou canst not at 			 all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:65
verses.text: For whatever thou lookest at, thou dost not see the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:66
verses.text: If thou seest a man's face, thou dost not see his back at the time thou seest the face; and when thou seest the back, thou dost not at that time see the face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:67
verses.text: Thou dost not then so see, as to comprehend; but when thou seest another part which thou hadst not seen before, unless memory aid thee to remember that thou hast seen that from which thou dost withdraw, thou couldest never say that thou hadst 			 comprehended anything even on the surface.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:68
verses.text: Thou handlest what thou seest, turnest it about on this side and that, or thyself dost go round it to see the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:69
verses.text: In one view then thou canst not see the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:70
verses.text: And as long as thou turnest it about to see it, thou art but seeing the parts; and by putting together that thou hast seen the other parts, thou dost fancy that thou seest the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:71
verses.text: But this must not be understood as the sight of the eyes, but the activity of the memory.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:72
verses.text: What then can be 			 said, Brethren, of that Word? Lo, of the bodies which are before our eyes we say they cannot comprehend them by a glance; what eye of the heart then comprehendeth God? Enough that it reach to Him if the eye be pure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:73
verses.text: But if it reach, it reacheth by a sort of incorporeal and spiritual touch, yet it doth not comprehend; and that, only if it be pure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:74
verses.text: And a man is made blessed by touching with the heart That which ever abideth Blessed; and that is this Very Everlasting Blessedness, and that 			 Everlasting Life, whereby man is made to live; that Perfect Wisdom, whereby man is made wise; that Everlasting Light, whereby man becomes enlightened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:75
verses.text: And see how by this touch thou art made what thou wast not, thou dost not make that thou touchest be what it was not before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:76
verses.text: I repeat it, there grows no increase to God from them that know Him, but to them that know Him, from the knowledge of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:77
verses.text: Let us not suppose, dearly beloved Brethren, that we confer any benefit on God, because I have said 			 that we give Him in a manner a price.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:78
verses.text: For we do not give Him aught whereby He can be increased, Who when thou fallest away, is Entire, and when thou returnest, abideth Entire, ready to make Himself seen that He may bless those who turn to Him, and punish those with blindness who turn away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:79
verses.text: For by this blindness, as the beginning of punishment, doth He first execute vengeance on the soul that turns away from Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:80
verses.text: For whoso turns away from the True Light, that is from God, is at once made blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:81
verses.text: He is not yet sensible of his punishment, but he hath it already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:82
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:83
verses.text: Accordingly, dearly beloved brethren, let us understand that the Word of God is incorporeally, inviolably, unchangeably, without temporal nativity, yet born of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:84
verses.text: Do we think that we can any how persuade certain unbelievers that that is not it, consistent with the truth, which is said by us according to the Catholic faith,which is contrary to the Arians, by whom the Church of God hath been often tried, forasmuch as carnal men receive with greater ease what they have 			 been accustomed to see? For some have dared to say, "The Father is greater than the Son, and precedes Him in thee;" that is, the Father is greater than the Son, and the Son is less than the Father, and is preceded by the Father in thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:85
verses.text: And they argue thus; "If He was born, of course the Father was before His Son was born to Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:86
verses.text: Attend; may He be with me, whilst your prayers assist me, and with godly heed desire to receive what He may give, what He may suggest to me; may He be with 			 me, that I may be able in some sort to explain what I have begun.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:87
verses.text: Yet, brethren, I tell you before I begin, if I shall not be able to explain it, do not suppose that it is the failure of the proof, but of the man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:88
verses.text: Accordingly I exhort and entreat you to pray; that the mercy of God may be with me, and make the matter be so explained by me, as is meet for you to hear, and for me to speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:89
verses.text: They then say thus; "If He be the Son of God, He was born".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:90
verses.text: This we confess.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:91
verses.text: For He would not be a Son, 			 if He were not born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:92
verses.text: It is plain, the faith admits it, the Catholic Church approves it, it is truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:93
verses.text: They then go on; "If the Son was born to the Father, the Father was before the Son was born to Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:94
verses.text: This the faith rejects, Catholic ears reject it, it is anathematized, whoso entertains this conceit is without, he belongs not to the fellowship and society of the saints.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:95
verses.text: Then says he, "Give me an explanation, how the Son could be born to the Father, and yet be coeval with Him of whom He 			 was born?"  7.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:96
verses.text: And what can we do, brethren, when we are conveying lessons of spiritual things to carnal men; even if so be we ourselves too are not carnal, when we intimate these spiritual truths to carnal men, to men accustomed to the idea of earthly nativities, and seeing the order of these creatures, where succession and departure separates off in age them that beget and them that are begotten? For after the father the son is born, to succeed the father, who in time of 			 course must die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:97
verses.text: This do we find in men, this in other animals, that the parents are first, the children after them in time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:98
verses.text: Through this custom of observation they desire to transfer carnal things to spiritual, and by their intentness on carnal things are more easily led into error.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:99
verses.text: For it is not the reason of the hearers which follows those who preach such things, but custom which even entangles themselves, that they do preach such things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:100
verses.text: And what shall we do? Shall we keep silence? Would 			 that we might! For perchance by silence something might be thought of worthy of the unspeakable subject.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:101
verses.text: For whatsoever cannot be spoken, is unspeakable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:102
verses.text: Now God is unspeakable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:103
verses.text: For if the Apostle Paul saith, that he "was caught up even unto the third heaven, and that he heard unspeakable words;" how much more unspeakable is He, who showed such things, which could not be spoken by him to whom they were shown? So then, brethren, it were better if we could keep silence, and say, "This the faith contains; so we believe; thou art not able to receive it, thou art but a babe; thou must patiently endure till thy wings be grown, lest when thou wouldest fly without wings, it should not be the free course of liberty, but the fall of temerity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:104
verses.text: What do they say against this? "O if he had anything to say, he would say it to me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:105
verses.text: This is the mere excuse of one who is at fault.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:106
verses.text: He is overcome by the truth, who does not choose to answer".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:107
verses.text: He to whom this is said, if he make no answer, though he be not conquered in himself is yet conquered in the wavering brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:108
verses.text: For the weak brethren hear it, and they think that there is really nothing to be said; and perhaps they 			 think right that there is nothing to be said, yet not that there is nothing to be felt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:109
verses.text: For a man can express nothing which he cannot also feel; but he may feel something which he cannot express.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:110
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:111
verses.text: Nevertheless, saving the unspeakableness of that Sovereign Majesty, lest when we shall have produced certain similitudes against them, any one should think that we have by them arrived at that which cannot be expressed or conceived by babes (and if it can be at all even by the more advanced, it can only be in part, only in a riddle, only "through a glass;" but not as yet, "face to face"), let us too produce certain similitudes against them, whereby they may be refuted, not "it" comprehended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:112
verses.text: For when we say that it may very possibly happen, that it may be understood, that He may both be born, and yet Coeternal with Him of whom He was born, in order to refute this, and prove it as it were to be false, they bring forth similitudes against us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:113
verses.text: From whence? From the creatures, and they say to us, "Every man of course was before he begat a son, he is greater 			 in age than his son; and so a horse was before he begat his foal, and a sheep, and the other animals".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:114
verses.text: Thus do they bring similitudes from the creatures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:115
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:116
verses.text: What! must we labour too, that we may find resemblances of those things which we are establishing? And what if I should not find any, might I not rightly say, "The Nativity of the Creator hath, it may be, no resemblance of itself among the creatures? For as far as He surpasseth the things which are here, in that He is there, so far doth He surpass the things which are born here, in that He was born there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:117
verses.text: All things here have their being from God; and yet what is to 			 be compared with God? So all things which are born here, are born by His agency.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:118
verses.text: And so perhaps there is no resemblance of His Nativity found, as there is none found whether of His Substance, Unchangeableness, Divinity, Majesty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:119
verses.text: For what can be found here like these? If then it chance that no resemblance of His Nativity either be found, am I therefore overwhelmed, because I have not found resemblances to the Creator of all things, when desiring to find in the creature what is like the 			 Creator?"  10.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:120
verses.text: And in very truth, Brethren, I am not likely to discover any temporal resemblances which I can compare to eternity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:121
verses.text: But as to those which thou hast discovered, what are they? What hast thou discovered? That a father is greater in time than his son; and therefore thou wouldest have the Son of God to be less in time than the Eternal Father, because thou hast found that a son is less than a father born in time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:122
verses.text: Find me an eternal father here, and thou hast found a 			 resemblance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:123
verses.text: Thou findest a son less than a father in time, a temporal son less than a temporal father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:124
verses.text: Hast thou found me a temporal son younger than eternal father? Seeing then that in Eternity is stability, but in time variety; in Eternity all things stand still, in time one thing comes, another succeeds; thou canst find a son of lesser age succeeding his father in the variety of time, for that he himself succeeded to his father also, not a son born in time to a father eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:125
verses.text: How then, 			 Brethren, can we find in the creature aught coeternal, when in the creature we find nothing eternal? Do thou find an eternal father in the creature, and I will find a coeternal son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:126
verses.text: But if thou find not an eternal father, and the one surpasses the other in thee; it is sufficient, that for a resemblance I find something coeval.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:127
verses.text: For what is coeternal is one thing what is coeval another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:128
verses.text: Every day we call them coeval who have the same measure of times; the one is not preceded by the other in time, 			 yet they both whom we call coeval once began to "be".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:129
verses.text: Now if I shall be able to discover something which is born coeval with that of which it is born; if two coeval things can be discovered, that which begets, and that which is begotten; we discover in this case things coeval, let us understand in the other things coeternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:130
verses.text: If here I shall find that a thing begotten hath begun to be ever since that which begets began to be, we may understand at least that the Son of God did not begin to 			 be, ever since He that begat Him did not begin to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:131
verses.text: Lo, brethren, perhaps we may discover something in the creature, which is born of something else, and which yet began to be at the same time as that of which it is born began to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:132
verses.text: In the latter case, the one began to be when the other began to be; in the former the one did not begin to be, ever since the other began not to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:133
verses.text: The first then is coeval, the second coeternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:134
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:135
verses.text: I suppose that your holiness has understood already what I am saying, that temporal things cannot be compared to eternal; but that by some slight and small resemblance, things coeval may be with things coeternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:136
verses.text: Let us find accordingly two coeval things; and let us get our hints as to these resemblances from the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:137
verses.text: We read in the Scriptures of Wisdom, "For she is the Brightness of the Everlasting Light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:138
verses.text: Again we read, "The unspotted 			 Mirror of the Majesty of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:139
verses.text: Wisdom Herself is called, "The Brightness of the Everlasting Light," is called, "The Image of the Father;" from hence let us take a resemblance, that we may find two coeval things, from which we may understand things coeternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:140
verses.text: O thou Arian, if I shall find that something that begets does not precede in time that which it begat, that a thing begotten is not less in time than that of which it is begotten; it is but just that thou concede to me, that these coeternals may 			 be found in the Creator, when coevals can be found in the creature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:141
verses.text: I think that this indeed occurs already to some brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:142
verses.text: For some anticipated me as soon as I said, "For She is the Brightness of the Everlasting Light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:143
verses.text: For the fire throws out light, light is thrown out from the fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:144
verses.text: If we ask which comes from which, every day when we light a candle are we reminded of some invisible and indescribable thing, that the candle as it were of our understanding may be lighted in this night of 			 the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:145
verses.text: Observe him who lights a candle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:146
verses.text: While the candle is not lighted, there is as yet no fire, nor any brightness which proceedeth from the fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:147
verses.text: But I ask, saying, "Does the brightness come from the fire, or the fire from the brightness?" Every soul answers me (for it has pleased God to sow the beginnings of understanding and wisdom in every soul); every soul answers me, and no one doubts, that that brightness comes from the fire, not the fire from the brightness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:148
verses.text: Let us then look 			 at the fire as the father of that brightness; for I have said before that we are looking for things coeval, not coeternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:149
verses.text: If I desire to light a candle, there is as yet no fire there, nor yet that brightness; but immediately that I have lighted it, together with the fire comes forth the brightness also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:150
verses.text: Give me then here a fire without brightness, and I believe you that the Father ever was without the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:151
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:152
verses.text: Attend; The matter has been explained by me as so great a matter could be, by the Lord helping the earnestness of your prayers, and the preparation of your heart, ye have taken in as much as ye were able to receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:153
verses.text: Yet these things are ineffable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:154
verses.text: Do not suppose that anything worthy of the subject has been spoken, if it only be for that things carnal are compared with coeternal, things temporal with things abiding ever, things subject to extinction to things immortal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:155
verses.text: But inasmuch as the Son is said also to be the Image of the Father, let us take from this too a sort of resemblance, though in things very different, as I have said before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:156
verses.text: The image of a man looking into a glass is thrown out from the glass.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:157
verses.text: But this cannot assist us for the clearing of that which we are endeavouring in some sort to explain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:158
verses.text: For it is said to me, "A man who looks into a glass of course, 'was' already, and was born before that.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:159
verses.text: The image came out only as soon as he looked 			 at himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:160
verses.text: For a man who looks in a glass, 'was' before he came to the glass".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:161
verses.text: What then shall we find, from which we may be able to draw out such a resemblance, as we did from the fire and the brightness? Let us find one from a very little thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:162
verses.text: You know without any difficulty how water often throws out the images of bodies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:163
verses.text: I mean, when any one is passing, or standing still along the water, he sees his own image there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:164
verses.text: Let us suppose then something born on the water's side, as a 			 shrub, or an herb, is it not born together with its image? As soon as ever it begins to be, its image begins to be with it, it does not precede in its birth its own image; it cannot be showed to me that anything is born upon the water's side, and that its image has appeared afterwards, whereas it first appeared without its image; but it is born together with its image; and yet the image comes from it, not it from the image.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:165
verses.text: It is born then together with its image, and the shrub and its image 			 begin to be together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:166
verses.text: Dost thou not confess that the image is begotten of that shrub, not the shrub of the image? So then thou dost confess that the image is from that shrub.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:167
verses.text: Accordingly that which begets and that which is begotten began to "be" together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:168
verses.text: Therefore they are coeval.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:169
verses.text: If the shrub had been always, the image from the shrub would have been always too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:170
verses.text: Now that which has its being from something else, is of course born of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:171
verses.text: It is possible then that one that begets might always 			 be, and always be together with that which was born of him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:172
verses.text: For here it was that we were in perplexity and trouble, how the Eternal Nativity might be understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:173
verses.text: So then the Son of God is so called on this principle, that there is the Father also, that He hath One from whom He derives His Being; not on this, that the Father is first in time, and the Son after.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:174
verses.text: The Father always was, the Son always from the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:175
verses.text: And because whatever "is" from another thing, is born, therefore the Son was 			 always born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:176
verses.text: The Father always was, the image from Him always was; as that image of the shrub was born of the shrub, and if the shrub had always been, the image would also have always been born from the shrub.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:177
verses.text: Thou couldest not find things begotten coeternal with the eternal begetters, but thou hast found things born coeval with those that begat them in time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:178
verses.text: I understand the Son coeternal with the Eternal who begat Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:179
verses.text: For what with regard to things of time is coeval, with regard 			 to things eternal is coeternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:180
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:181
verses.text: Here there is somewhat for you to consider, Brethren, as a protection against blasphemies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:182
verses.text: For it is constantly said, "See thou hast produced certain resemblances; but the brightness which is thrown out from the fire, shines less brilliantly than the fire itself, and the image of the shrub has less proper subsistence, than that shrub of which it is the image.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:183
verses.text: These instances have a resemblance, but they have not a thorough equality: wherefore they do not seem to be of the same substance".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:184
verses.text: What then shall we say, if any one say, "The Father then is to the Son, such as the brightness is to the fire, and the image to the shrub"? See I have understood the Father to be eternal; and the Son to be coeternal with Him; nevertheless say we that He is as the brightness which is 			 thrown out from and is less brilliant than the fire, or as the image which is reflected from and has less real existence than the shrub? No, but there is a thorough equality.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:185
verses.text: "I do not believe it," he will say, "because thou hast not discovered a resemblance".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:186
verses.text: Well then, believe the Apostle, because he was able to see what I have said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:187
verses.text: For he says, "He thought it not robbery to be equal with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:188
verses.text: Equality is perfect likeness in every way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:189
verses.text: And what said he? "Not robbery".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:190
verses.text: Why? Because that is robbery which belongs to another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:191
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:192
verses.text: Yet from these two comparisons, these two kinds, we may perhaps find in the creature a resemblance whereby we may understand how the Son is both coeternal with the Father, and in no respect less than He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:193
verses.text: But this we cannot find in one kind of resemblances singly: let us join both kinds together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:194
verses.text: How both kinds? One, of which they themselves give instances of resemblances, and the other, of which we gave.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:195
verses.text: For they gave instances of resemblances from those things 			 which are born in time, and are preceded in time by them of whom they are born, as man of man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:196
verses.text: He that is born first is greater in time; but yet man and man, that is of the same substance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:197
verses.text: For man begets a man, and a horse a horse, and a sheep a sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:198
verses.text: These beget after the same substance, but not after the same time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:199
verses.text: They are diverse in time, but not in nature diverse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:200
verses.text: What then do we praise here in this nativity? The equality of nature surely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:201
verses.text: But what is wanting? The equality of time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:202
verses.text: Let us 			 retain the one thing which is praised here, that is, the equality of nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:203
verses.text: But in the other kind of resemblances, which we gave from the brightness of the fire and the image of the shrub, you find not an equality of nature, you do find an equality of time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:204
verses.text: What do we praise here? Equality of time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:205
verses.text: What is wanting? Equality of nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:206
verses.text: Join the things which you praise together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:207
verses.text: For in the creatures there is wanting something which you praise, in the Creator nothing can be wanting: because what 			 you find in the creature, came forth from the Hand of the Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:208
verses.text: What then is there in things coeval? Must not that be given to God which you praise here in? But what is wanting must not be attributed to that Sovereign Majesty, in the which there is no defect.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:209
verses.text: See I offer to you things begetting coeval with things begotten: in these you praise the equality of time, but find fault with the inequality of nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:210
verses.text: What you find fault with, do not attribute to God; what you praise, attribute to Him; so from this kind of resemblances you attribute to Him instead of a cotemporaneousness a coeternity, that the Son may be coeternal with Him of whom He was born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:211
verses.text: But from the other kind of resemblances, which itself too is a creature of God, and ought to praise the Creator, what do you praise in them? Equality of nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:212
verses.text: You had before assigned coeternity by reason of the first 			 distinction; by reason of this last, assign equality; and the nativity of the same substance is complete.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:213
verses.text: For what is more mad, my brethren, than that I should praise the creature in anything which does not exist in the Creator? In man I praise equality of nature, shall I not believe it in Him who made man? That which is born of man is man; shall not that which is born of God, be That which He is of whom He was born? Converse have I none with works which God hath not made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:214
verses.text: Let then all the 			 works of the Creator praise Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:215
verses.text: I find in the one case a cotemporaneousness, I get at the knowledge of a coeternity in the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:216
verses.text: In the first I find an equality of nature, I understand an equality of substance in the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:217
verses.text: In this then that is "wholly," which in the other case is found in the several parts, and several things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:218
verses.text: It is then "wholly" here altogether, and not only what is in the creature; I find it wholly here, but as being in the Creator, in so much higher a way, in that 			 the one is visible, the Other Invisible; the one temporal, the Other Eternal; the one changeable, the Other Unchangeable; the one corruptible, the Other Incorruptible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:219
verses.text: Lastly, in the case of men themselves, what we find, man and man, are two men; here the Father and the Son are One God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:220
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:221
verses.text: I render unspeakable thanks to our Lord God, that He hath vouchsafed, at your prayers, to deliver my infirmity from this most perplexed and difficult place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:222
verses.text: Yet above all things remember this, that the Creator transcends indescribably whatever we could gather from the creature, whether by the bodily senses, or the thought of the mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:223
verses.text: But wouldest thou with the mind reach Him? Purify thy mind, purify thine heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:224
verses.text: Make clean the eye whereby That, 			 whatever It be, may be reached.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:225
verses.text: For "blessed are the clean in heart, for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:226
verses.text: But whilst the heart was not cleansed, what could be provided and granted more mercifully by Him, than that That Word of whom we have spoken so great and so many things, and yet have spoken nothing worthy of Him; that That Word, "by whom all things were made," should become that which we are, that we might be able to attain to That which we are not? For we are not God; but with the mind or the interior eye of the heart we can see God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:227
verses.text: Our eyes dulled by sins, blinded, 			 enfeebled by infirmity, desire to see; but we are in hope, not yet in possession.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:228
verses.text: We are the children of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:229
verses.text: This saith John, who says, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God;" he who lay on the Lord's Breast, who drew in these secrets from the Bosom of His Heart; he says, "Dearly beloved, we are the children of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be; we know that, when He shall appear, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:230
verses.text: This is promised us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:231
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:232
verses.text: But in order that we may attain, if we cannot yet see God the Word, let us hear the Word made Flesh; seeing we are carnal, let us hear the Word Incarnate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:233
verses.text: For for this cause came He, for this cause took upon Him our infirmity, that thou mightest be able to receive the strong words of a God bearing thy weakness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:234
verses.text: And He is truly called "milk".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:235
verses.text: For He giveth milk to infants, that He may give the meat of wisdom to them of riper years.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:236
verses.text: Suck then now with 			 patience, that thou mayest be fed to thy heart's most eager wish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:237
verses.text: For how is even the milk, wherewith infants are suckled, made? Was it not solid meat on the table? But the infant is not strong enough to eat the meat which is on the table; what does the mother do? She turns the meat into the substance of her flesh, and makes milk of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:238
verses.text: Makes for us what we may be able to take.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:239
verses.text: So the Word was made Flesh, that we little ones, who were indeed as infants with respect to food, might be nourished by milk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:240
verses.text: But there is this difference; that when the mother makes the food turned into flesh milk, the food is turned into milk; whereas the Word abiding Itself unchangeably assumed Flesh, that there might be, as it were, a tissue of the two.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:241
verses.text: What He is, He did not 			 corrupt or change, that in thy fashion, He might speak to thee, not transformed and turned into man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:242
verses.text: For abiding unalterable, unchangeable, and altogether inviolable, He became what thou art in respect of thee, what He is in Himself in respect of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:243
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:244
verses.text: For what doth He say Himself to the infirm, to the end that recovering that sight, they may be able in some measure to reach the Word by whom all things were made? "Come unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:245
verses.text: Take My yoke upon you, and learn of Me, that I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:246
verses.text: What doth the Master, the Son of God, the Wisdom of God, by whom all things were made, proclaim? He calleth the human race, and saith, "Come unto Me, all ye that labour, and learn of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:247
verses.text: Thou wast thinking haply that the Wisdom of God would say, "Learn how I have made the heavens and the stars; how all things also were numbered in Me before they were made, how by virtue of unchangeable principles your very hairs were numbered".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:248
verses.text: Didst thou think that Wisdom would say these things, and such as these? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:249
verses.text: But first that.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:250
verses.text: "That I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:251
verses.text: Lo, see here what ye can comprehend, brethren; it is surely a little thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:252
verses.text: We are making our way to great things, let us receive the little things, and we shall be great.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:253
verses.text: Wouldest thou comprehend the height of God? First comprehend the lowliness of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:254
verses.text: Condescend to be humble for thine own sake, seeing that God 			 condescended to be humble for thy sake too; for it was not for His own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:255
verses.text: Comprehend then the lowliness of Christ, learn to be humble, be loth to be proud.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:256
verses.text: Confess thine infirmity, lie patiently before the Physician; when thou shalt have comprehended His lowliness, thou risest with Him; not as though He should rise Himself in that He is the Word; but thou rather, that He may be more and more comprehended by thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:257
verses.text: At first thou didst understand falteringly and hesitatingly; afterwards thou wilt 			 understand more surely and more clearly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:258
verses.text: He doth not increase, but thou makest progress, and He seemeth as it were to rise with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:259
verses.text: So it is, brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:260
verses.text: Believe the commandments of God, and do them, and He will give you the strength of understanding.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:261
verses.text: Do not put the last first, and, as it were, prefer knowledge to the commandments of God; lest ye be only the lower, and none the more firmly rooted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:262
verses.text: Consider a tree; first it strikes downwards, that it may grow up on high; fixes its root low in the ground, that it may extend its top to heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:263
verses.text: Does it make an effort to grow except from humiliation? And wouldest thou without charity comprehend these transcendent matters, shoot toward the heaven without a root? This were a ruin, 			 not a growing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 66:264
verses.text: With "Christ" then "dwelling in your hearts by faith, be ye rooted and grounded in charity, that ye may be filled with all the fulness of God".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:1
verses.text: Sermon LXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:2
verses.text: [CXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:4
verses.text: ]  On the same words of the Gospel, John i.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:5
verses.text: , "In the beginning was the word," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:7
verses.text: All ye who are looking for a man's many words, understand the One Word of God, "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:8
verses.text: Now, "In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:9
verses.text: But, "The Word was," since we have heard, "In the beginning God made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:10
verses.text: Acknowledge we in Him the Creator; for Creator is He who made; and the creature what He made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:11
verses.text: For no creature which was made "was," as God the Word "was," by whom it was made, always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:12
verses.text: Now when we heard "The Word was," with whom was It? We understand the Father who did not make nor create the Same Word, but begat Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:13
verses.text: For, "In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:14
verses.text: Whereby 			 made He them? "The Word was, and the Word was with God;" but what kind of Word? Did it sound and so pass away? Was it a mere thought, and motion of the mind? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:15
verses.text: Was it suggested by memory, and uttered? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:16
verses.text: What kind of Word then? Why dost thou look for many words from me? "The Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:17
verses.text: When we hear, "The Word was God," we do not make a second God; but we understand the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:18
verses.text: For the Word is the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:19
verses.text: Lo, the Son, and What but God? For "The Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:20
verses.text: What the Father? God of course.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:21
verses.text: If the Father is God and the Son God, do we make two Gods? God forbid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:22
verses.text: The Father is God, the Son God; but the 			 Father and the Son One God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:23
verses.text: For the Only Son of God was not made, but born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:24
verses.text: "In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth;" but the Word was of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:25
verses.text: Was the Word therefore made by the Father? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:26
verses.text: "All things were made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:27
verses.text: If by Him all things were made, was He too made by Himself? Do not imagine that He by whom thou hearest all things were made was Himself made among all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:28
verses.text: For if He were made Himself, all things were not made by Him, but Himself was made among the rest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:29
verses.text: You say, "He was made;" what, by Himself? Who can make himself? If then He was made, how by Him were all things made? See, Himself too was made, as you say, not I, for that He was begotten, I do not deny.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:30
verses.text: If then you 			 say that He was made, I ask by what, by whom? By Himself? Then He "was," before He was made, that He might make Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:31
verses.text: But if all things were made by Him, understand that He was not Himself made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:32
verses.text: If thou art not able to understand, believe, that thou mayest understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:33
verses.text: Faith goes before; understanding follows after; since the Prophet says, "Unless ye believe, ye shall not understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:34
verses.text: The Word was".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:35
verses.text: Look not for time in Him, by whom times were made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:36
verses.text: "The Word was".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:37
verses.text: But you say, "There was a time that the Word was not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:38
verses.text: You say falsely; nowhere do you read this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:39
verses.text: But I do read for you, "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:40
verses.text: What look you for before the beginning? But if you should be able to find anything before the beginning, this will be the beginning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:41
verses.text: He is mad who looks for anything before the beginning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:42
verses.text: What then doth he say was before the 			 beginning? "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:43
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:44
verses.text: But you will say, "The Father both 'was,' and was before the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:45
verses.text: What are you looking for? "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:46
verses.text: What you find, understand; seek not for what you are not able to find.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:47
verses.text: Nothing is before the beginning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:48
verses.text: "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:49
verses.text: The Son is the Brightness of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:50
verses.text: Of the Wisdom of the Father, which is the Son, it is said, "For He is the brightness of the Everlasting Light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:51
verses.text: Are you seeking for a Son without a Father? Give me a light without brightness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:52
