verses.text: If there was a time when the Son was not, the Father was a light obscure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:53
verses.text: For how was He not an obscure Light, if It had no brightness? So then the Father always, the Son always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:54
verses.text: If the Father always, the Son always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:55
verses.text: Do you ask of me, whether the Son were born? I answer, "born".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:56
verses.text: For He would not be a Son if not born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:57
verses.text: So when I say, the Son always was, I say in fact was always born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:58
verses.text: And who 			 understands, "Was always born"? Give me an eternal fire, and I will give thee an eternal brightness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:59
verses.text: We bless God who hath given to us the holy Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:60
verses.text: Be ye not blind in the brightness of the light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:61
verses.text: Brightness is engendered of the Light, and yet the Brightness is Coeternal with the Light that engenders It.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:62
verses.text: The Light always, its Brightness always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:63
verses.text: It begat Its Own Brightness; but was it ever without Its Brightness? Let God be allowed to beget an eternal Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:64
verses.text: I pray you hear of whom we 			 are speaking; hear, mark, believe, understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:65
verses.text: Of God are we speaking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:66
verses.text: We confess and believe the Son coeternal with the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:67
verses.text: But you will say, "When a man begets a Son, he that begets is the elder, and he that is begotten the younger".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:68
verses.text: It is true; in the case of men, he that begets is the elder, and he that is begotten, the younger, and he arrives in time to his father's strength.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:69
verses.text: But why, save that whilst the one grows, the other grows old? Let the father 			 stand still a while, and in his growing the son will follow on him, and you will see him equal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:70
verses.text: But see, I give you whereby to understand this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:71
verses.text: Fire engenders a coeval brightness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:72
verses.text: Among men you only find sons younger, fathers older; you do not find them coeval: but as I have said, I show you brightness coeval with its parent fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:73
verses.text: For fire begets brightness, yet is it never without brightness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:74
verses.text: Since then you see that the brightness is coeval with its fire, suffer God to beget a Coeternal Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:75
verses.text: Whoso understandeth, let him rejoice: but whoso understandeth not, let him believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 67:76
verses.text: For the word of the Prophet cannot be disannulled; "Unless ye believe, ye shall not understand".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:1
verses.text: Sermon LXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:2
verses.text: [CXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:4
verses.text: ]  On the same words, John i.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:5
verses.text: "In the beginning was the word," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:7
verses.text: That our Lord Jesus Christ in seeking lost man was made Man, our preaching has never withholden, and your faith has ever retained; and moreover, that this our Lord, who for our sakes was made Man, was always God with the Father, and always will be, yea rather always Is; for where there is no succession of time, there is no "hath been" and "will be".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:8
verses.text: For that of which it is said, "it hath been," is now no more; that of which it 			 is said, "it will be," is not yet; but He always is, because He truly "is," that is, is unchangeable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:9
verses.text: For the Gospel lesson has just now taught us a high and divine mystery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:10
verses.text: For this beginning of the Gospel St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:11
verses.text: John poured forth for that he drank it in from the Lord's Breast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:12
verses.text: For ye remember, that it has been very lately read to you, how that this St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:13
verses.text: John the Evangelist lay in the Lord's Bosom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:14
verses.text: And wishing to explain this clearly, he says, "On the Lord's Breast;" that we might understand what he meant, by "in the Lord's bosom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:15
verses.text: For what, think we, did he drink in who was lying on the Lord's Breast? Nay, let us not think, but drink; for we too have just now heard what we may drink in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:17
verses.text: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:18
verses.text: O glorious preaching! O the result of the full feast of the Lord's Breast! "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:19
verses.text: Why seekest thou for what was before It? "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:20
verses.text: If the Word had been made (for made indeed that was not by which all things were made); if the Word had been made, the Scripture would have said, "In the beginning God made the Word;" as it is said in Genesis, "In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:21
verses.text: God then did not in the beginning make the Word; because, "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:22
verses.text: This Word which was in the beginning, where was It? Follow on, "And the Word was with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:23
verses.text: But from our daily hearing the words of men we are wont to think lightly of this name of "Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:24
verses.text: In this case do not think lightly of the Name of "Word;" "The Word was God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:25
verses.text: The same," that is the Word, "was in the beginning with God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:26
verses.text: All things were made by Him, and without 			 Him was nothing made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:27
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:28
verses.text: Extend your hearts, help the poverty of my words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:29
verses.text: What I shall be able to express, give ear to; on what I shall not be able to express, meditate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:30
verses.text: Who can comprehend the abiding Word? All our words sound, and pass away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:31
verses.text: Who can comprehend the abiding Word, save He who abideth in Him? Wouldest thou comprehend the abiding Word? Do not follow the current of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:32
verses.text: For this flesh is indeed a current; for it has none abiding.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:33
verses.text: As it were from a kind of secret fount 			 of nature men are born, they live, they die; or whence they come, or whither they go, we know not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:34
verses.text: It is a hidden water, till it issue from its source; it flows on, and is seen in its course; and again it is hidden in the sea.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:35
verses.text: Let us despise this stream flowing on, running, disappearing, let us despise it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:36
verses.text: "All flesh is grass, and all the glory of flesh is as the flower of grass.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:37
verses.text: The grass withereth, the flower falleth away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:38
verses.text: Wouldest thou endure? "But the word of the Lord endureth for 			 ever".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:39
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:40
verses.text: But in order to succour us, "The Word was made Flesh, and dwelt among us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:41
verses.text: What is, "The Word was made Flesh"? The gold became grass.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:42
verses.text: It became grass for to be burned; the grass was burned, but the gold remained; in the grass It perisheth not, yea, It changed the grass.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:43
verses.text: How did It change it? It raised it up, quickened it, lifted it up to heaven, and placed it at the right Hand of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:44
verses.text: But that it might be said, "And the Word was made Flesh, and dwelt among us," let us recollect awhile what went before.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:45
verses.text: "He came unto His Own, and His 			 Own received Him not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:46
verses.text: But as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:47
verses.text: "To become," for they "were" not; but He "was" Himself in the beginning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:48
verses.text: "He gave them" then "power to become the sons of God, to them that believe in His Name; who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:49
verses.text: Lo, born they are, in whatever age of the flesh they may be; ye see infants; see and rejoice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:50
verses.text: Lo, they are born; but they are born of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:51
verses.text: Their mother's womb is the water of baptism.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:52
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:53
verses.text: Let no man in poorness of soul entertain this conceit, and turn over such most beggarly thoughts in his mind, and say to himself, "How 'in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God: all things were made by Him;' and lo, 'the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us?'" Hear why it was done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:54
verses.text: "To those" we know "who believed on Him He hath given power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:55
verses.text: Let not those then to whom He hath given 			 power to become the sons of God, think it impossible to become the sons of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:56
verses.text: "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:57
verses.text: Do not imagine that it is too great a thing for you to become the sons of God; for your sakes He became the Son of man, who was the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:58
verses.text: If He was made, that He might be less, who was more; can He not bring it to pass, that of that less which we were, we may be something more? He descended to us, and shall not we ascend to Him? For us He accepted our death, 			 and shall He not give us His Life? For thee He suffered thy evil things, and shall He not give thee His good things?  6.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:59
verses.text: "But how," one will say, "can it be, that the Word of God, by whom the world is governed, by whom all things both were, and are created, should contract Himself into the womb of a Virgin; should abandon the world, and leave the Angels, and be shut up in one woman's womb?" Thou skillest not to conceive of things divine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:60
verses.text: The Word of God (I am speaking to thee, O man, I am speaking to thee of the omnipotence of the Word of God) could surely do all, seeing that 			 the Word of God is omnipotent, at once remain with the Father, and come to us; at once in the flesh come forth to us, and lay concealed in Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:61
verses.text: For He would not the less have been, if He had not been born of flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:62
verses.text: He "was" before His own flesh; He created His Own mother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:63
verses.text: He chose her in whom He should be conceived, He created her of whom He should be created.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:64
verses.text: Why marvellest thou? It is God of whom I am speaking to thee: "The Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:66
verses.text: I am treating of the Word, and perchance the word of men may furnish somewhat like; though very unequal, far distant, in no way comparable, yet something which may convey a hint to you by way of resemblance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:67
verses.text: Lo, the word which I am speaking to you, I have had previously in my heart: it came forth to thee, yet it has not departed from me; that began to be in thee, which was not in thee; it continued with me when it went forth to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:68
verses.text: As then my word was brought 			 forth to thy sense, yet did not depart from my heart; so That Word came forth to our senses, yet departed not from His Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:69
verses.text: My word was with me, and it came forth into a voice: the Word of God was with the Father, and came forth into Flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:70
verses.text: But can I do with my voice that which He could do with His Flesh? For I am not master of my voice as it flies; He is not only master of His Flesh, that It should be born, live, act; but even when dead He raised It up, and exalted unto the Father the Vehicle as it were in which He came forth to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:71
verses.text: You may call the Flesh of Christ a Garment, you may call It a Vehicle, and as perchance Himself vouchsafed to teach us, you may call It His Beast; for on this beast He raised him who had been wounded by robbers; lastly, as He said Himself more expressly, you may call It a Temple; This Temple knows death no more, Its seat is at the right Hand of the Father: in This Temple shall He come to judge the quick and dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:72
verses.text: What He hath by precept taught, He hath by example manifested.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:73
verses.text: What He hath in His own Flesh shown, that oughtest thou to hope for in thy flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:74
verses.text: This is faith; hold fast what as yet thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 68:75
verses.text: Need there is, that by believing thou abide firm in that thou seest not; lest 			 when thou shalt see, thou be put to shame.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:1
verses.text: Sermon LXX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:2
verses.text: [CXX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:4
verses.text: ]  On the same words of John i.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:5
verses.text: , "In the beginning was the word," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:7
verses.text: The beginning of John's Gospel, "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:8
verses.text: Thus he begins, this he saw, and transcending the whole creation, mountains, air, the heavens, the stars, Thrones, Dominions, Principalities, Powers, all Angels, and Archangels, transcending all; he saw the Word in the beginning, and drank It in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:9
verses.text: He saw above every creature, he drank in from the Lord's breast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:10
verses.text: For this same St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:11
verses.text: John the Evangelist is he whom Jesus specially loved; insomuch that he lay on His Breast at supper.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:12
verses.text: There was this secret, that therefrom might be 			 drunk in, what in the Gospel was to be poured forth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:13
verses.text: Happy they who hear and understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:14
verses.text: Of the next degree of blessedness are they who though they understand not, believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:15
verses.text: For how great a thing it is to see This Word of God, who can explain in human words?  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:16
verses.text: Lift up your hearts, my Brethren, lift them up as best ye can; whatsoever occurs to you from the idea of any body whatsoever, reject.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:17
verses.text: If the Word of God occurs to you under the idea of the light of this sun, expand, extend how you will, set no bounds in your thought to that light; it is nothing to the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:18
verses.text: Whatsoever of this sort the mind conceives, is less in one part than in the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:19
verses.text: Of theWord conceive as Whole everywhere.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:20
verses.text: Understand ye what I say; 			 because of my stress of time I am limiting myself as much as I can for your sakes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:21
verses.text: Understand ye what I say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:22
verses.text: Lo, this light from heaven, which is called by the name of the sun, when it comes forth, it enlightens the earth, unfolds the day, develops forms, distinguishes colours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:23
verses.text: Great blessing it is, great gift of God to all mortal men; let His works magnify Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:24
verses.text: If the sun is so beauteous, what more beauteous than the sun's Maker? And yet look, Brethren; lo, he pours his rays through the 			 whole earth; penetrates open places, the closed resist him; he sends his light through windows; can he also through a wall? To the Word of God all is open, from the Word of God nothing is hid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:25
verses.text: Observe another difference, how far from the Creator is the creature, especially the bodily creature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:26
verses.text: When the sun is in the East, it is not in the West.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:27
verses.text: Its light indeed shed from that vast body reaches even to the West; but itself is not there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:28
verses.text: When it begins to set, then it will be there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:29
verses.text: When it 			 rises, it is in the East; when it sets it is in the West.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:30
verses.text: By these operations of his, it has given name to those quarters.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:31
verses.text: Because it is in the East when it rises at the East, it has made it be called the Rising Sun; because it is at the West when it sets at the West, it has made it be called the Setting Sun.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:32
verses.text: At night it is nowhere seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:33
verses.text: Is the Word of God so? When It is in the East, is It not in the West; or when It is in the West, is It not in the East? or does It ever leave the earth, and go 			 under or behind the earth? It is Whole everywhere.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:34
verses.text: Who can in words explain this? Who see it? By what means of proof shall I establish to you what I say? I am speaking as a man, it is to men I speak; I am speaking as one weak, to men weaker am I speaking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:35
verses.text: And yet, my brethren, I am bold to say that I do in some sort see what I am saying to you, though "through a glass," or "darkly," I do in some sort understand even within my heart a word touching this thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:36
verses.text: But it seeks to go forth to 			 you, and finds no meet vehicle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:37
verses.text: The vehicle of the word is the sound of the voice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:38
verses.text: What I am saying within mine own self I seek to say to you, and words fail.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:39
verses.text: For I wish to speak of the Word of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:40
verses.text: How great a Word, what kind of Word? "All things were made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:41
verses.text: See the works, and stand in awe of the Worker.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:42
verses.text: "All things were made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:43
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:44
verses.text: Return with me, O human infirmity, return, I say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:45
verses.text: Let us comprehend these human things if we can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:46
verses.text: We are men, I who speak, I am a man, and to men I speak, and utter the sound of my voice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:47
verses.text: I convey the sound of my voice to men's ears, and by the sound of my voice I somehow through the ear lay up understanding also in the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:48
verses.text: Let us then speak on this point what and how we can, let us comprehend it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:49
verses.text: But if we have not ability to comprehend even this, in 			 respect of the Other what are we? Lo, ye are listening to me; I am speaking a word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:50
verses.text: If any one goes out from us, and is asked outside what is being done here, he answers, "The Bishop is speaking a word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:51
verses.text: I am speaking a word of the Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:52
verses.text: But what a word, of what a Word? A mortal word, of the Word Immortal; a changeable word, of the Word Unchangeable; a passing word of the Word Eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:53
verses.text: Nevertheless, consider my word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:54
verses.text: For I have told you already, the Word of God is Whole everywhere.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:55
verses.text: See, I 			 am speaking a word to you; what I say reaches to all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:56
verses.text: Now that what I am saying might come to you all, did ye divide what I say? If I , were to feed you, to wish to fill not your minds, but your bodies, and to set loaves before you to be satisfied therewith; would ye not divide my loaves among you? Could my loaves come to every one of you? If they came to one only, the rest would have none.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:57
verses.text: But now see, I am speaking, and ye all receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:58
verses.text: Nay, not only all receive, but all receive it whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:59
verses.text: It 			 comes whole to all, to each whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:60
verses.text: O the marvels of my word! What then is the Word of God? Hear again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:61
verses.text: I have spoken; what I have spoken, has gone forth to you, and has not gone away from me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:62
verses.text: It has reached to you, and has not been separated from me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:63
verses.text: Before I spake, I had it, and ye had not; I spake, and ye began to have, and I lost nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:64
verses.text: O the marvel of my word! What then is the Word of God? From little things form conjectures of things great.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:65
verses.text: Consider earthly things, laud the heavenly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:66
verses.text: I 			 am a creature, ye are creatures; and such great miracles are done with my word in my heart, in my mouth, in my voice, in your ears, in your hearts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:67
verses.text: What then is the Creator? O Lord, hear us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:68
verses.text: Make us, for that Thou hast made us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:69
verses.text: Make us good, for that Thou hast made us enlightened men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:70
verses.text: These white-robed, enlightened ones hear Thy word by me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:71
verses.text: For enlightened by Thy grace they stand before Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:72
verses.text: "This is the day which the Lord hath made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 69:73
verses.text: Only let them labour, let them pray for this, that when these days shall have gone by, they may not become darkness, who have been made the light of the wonders and the blessings of God.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:2
verses.text: [CXXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John i.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:5
verses.text: 10, "The world was made through him," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:7
verses.text: By the Lord "was the world made, and the world knew Him not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:8
verses.text: What world was made by Him, what world knew Him not? For it is not the same world that was made by Him, which knew Him not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:9
verses.text: What is the world that was made by Him? The heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:10
verses.text: How did not the heaven know Him, when at His Passion the sun was darkened? How did not the earth know Him, when as He hung upon the Cross, it quaked? But "the world knew Him not," whose Prince he is, of whom it is said, "Behold, the prince of this world cometh, and findeth nothing in 			 me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:11
verses.text: Wicked men are called the world; unbelieving men are called the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:12
verses.text: They have gotten their name from that they love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:13
verses.text: By the love of God we are made gods; so by the love of the world, we are called the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:14
verses.text: But "God was in Christ reconciling the world unto Himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:15
verses.text: "The world" then "knew Him not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:16
verses.text: What? "all men?"  2.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:17
verses.text: "He came unto His Own, and His Own received Him not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:18
verses.text: All things are His, but they are called His Own, from among whom His mother was, among whom He had taken Flesh, to whom He had sent before the heralds of His advent, to whom He had given the law, whom He had delivered from the Egyptian bondage, whose father Abraham according to the flesh He elected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:19
verses.text: For He said truth, "Before Abraham was, I am".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:20
verses.text: He did not say, "Before Abraham was," or "before Abraham was made, I was made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:21
verses.text: For "in the beginning the Word was," not, "was made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:22
verses.text: So then "He came unto His Own," He came to the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:23
verses.text: "And His Own received Him not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:24
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:25
verses.text: "But as many as received Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:26
verses.text: For of course the Apostles were there, who "received Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:27
verses.text: There were they who carried branches before His beast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:28
verses.text: They went before and followed after, and spread their garments, and cried with a loud voice, "Hosanna to the Son of David, Blessed is He That cometh in the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:29
verses.text: Then said the Pharisees unto Him, "Restrain the children, that they cry not out so unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:30
verses.text: And He said, "If these shall hold their peace, the stones will cry out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:31
verses.text: Us He saw when He spake these words; "If these shall hold their peace, the stones will cry out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:32
verses.text: Who are stones, but they who worship stones? If the Jewish children shall hold their peace, the elder and the younger Gentiles shall cry out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:33
verses.text: Who are the stones, but they of whom speaketh that very John, who came "to bear witness of the Light"? For when he saw these self-same Jews priding themselves on their birth from Abraham, he said to them, "O generation of vipers".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:34
verses.text: They called themselves the children of Abraham; and he addressed them, "O generation of vipers".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:35
verses.text: Did he do Abraham wrong? God forbid! He gave them a name from their character.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:36
verses.text: For that if they were the children of Abraham, they would imitate Abraham; as He too telleth them who say to Him, "We be free, and were never in bondage to any man; we have Abraham for our father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:37
verses.text: And He said, "If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the deeds of Abraham.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:38
verses.text: Ye wish to kill 			 Me, because I tell you the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:39
verses.text: This did not Abraham".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:40
verses.text: Ye were of his stock, but ye are a degenerate stock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:41
verses.text: So then what said John? "O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?" Because they came to be baptized with the baptism of John unto repentance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:42
verses.text: "Who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:43
verses.text: And say not in your hearts, We have Abraham to our father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:44
verses.text: For God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:45
verses.text: For God is able of these stones which he saw in the Spirit; to them he spake; he foresaw us; "For God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:46
verses.text: Of what stones? "If these shall hold their peace, the stones will cry out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:47
verses.text: Ye have just now heard, and cried out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:48
verses.text: It is fulfilled, "The stones shall cry out".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:49
verses.text: For from among the Gentiles we came, in our forefathers we worshipped stones.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:50
verses.text: Therefore are we called dogs too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:51
verses.text: Call to mind what that woman heard 			 who cried out after the Lord, for she was a Canaanitish woman, a worshipper of idols, the handmaid of devils.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:52
verses.text: What said Jesus to her? "It is not good to take the children's bread, and to cast it to dogs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:53
verses.text: Have ye never noticed, how dogs will lick the greasy stones? So are all the worshippers of images.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:54
verses.text: But grace has come to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:55
verses.text: "But as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:56
verses.text: See ye have here some just now born: to them hath He "given power to become the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:57
verses.text: To whom hath He given it? "To them that believe in His Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:58
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:59
verses.text: And how do they become the sons of God? "Who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of man, nor of the will of the flesh, but of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:60
verses.text: Having received power to become the sons of God, they are born of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:61
verses.text: Mark then: They are born of God, "not of blood," like their first birth, like that wretched birth, issuing out of wretchedness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:62
verses.text: But they who are born of God, what were they? whereby were they first born? Of blood; of the joint blood of the male and female, of the carnal union of male and female, from this were they born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:63
verses.text: From whence now? They are born of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:64
verses.text: The first birth of the male and female; the 			 second birth of God and the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:66
verses.text: Lo, they are born of God; whereby is it brought to pass that they should be born of God, who were first born of men? Whereby is it brought to pass, whereby? "And the Word was made Flesh, that It might dwell among us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:67
verses.text: Wondrous exchange; He made Flesh, they spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:68
verses.text: What is this? What condescension is here, my brethren! Lift up your minds to the hope and comprehension of better things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:69
verses.text: Give not yourselves up to worldly desires.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:70
verses.text: "Ye have been bought with a Price;" for your sakes the Word was made Flesh; for your sakes He who was the Son of God, was made the Son of man: that ye who were the sons of men, might be made sons of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:71
verses.text: What was He, what was He made? What were ye, what were ye made? He was the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:72
verses.text: What was He made? The Son of man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:73
verses.text: Ye were the sons of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:74
verses.text: What were ye made? The sons of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:75
verses.text: He shared with us our evil things, to give us His good things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:76
verses.text: But even in that He was made the Son of man, He is different much 			 from us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:77
verses.text: We are the sons of men by the lust of the flesh; He the Son of man by the faith of a virgin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:78
verses.text: The mother of any other man whatever conceives by a carnal union; and every one is born of human parents, his father and his mother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:79
verses.text: But Christ was born of the Holy Ghost, and the Virgin Mary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:80
verses.text: He came to us, but from Himself departed not far; yea from Himself as God He departed never; but added what He was to our nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:81
verses.text: For He came to that which He was not, He did not lose what He was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:82
verses.text: He was 			 made the Son of man; but did not cease to be the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:83
verses.text: Hereby the Mediator, in the middle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:84
verses.text: What is, "in the middle"? Neither up above, nor down below.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:85
verses.text: How neither up above, nor down below? Not above, since He is Flesh; not below, since He is not a sinner.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:86
verses.text: But yet in so far as He is God, above always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:87
verses.text: For He did not so come to us, as to leave the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 70:88
verses.text: From us He went, and did not leave us; to us will He come again, and will not leave Him.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:2
verses.text: [CXXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John i.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:5
verses.text: 48,"When thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:7
verses.text: What we have heard said by the Lord Jesus Christ to Nathanael, if we understand it aright, does not concern him only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:8
verses.text: For our Lord Jesus saw the whole human race under the fig-tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:9
verses.text: For in this place it is understood that by the fig-tree He signified sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:10
verses.text: Not that it always signifies this, but as I have said in this place, in that fitness of significancy, in which ye know that the first man, when he sinned, covered himself with fig 			 leaves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:11
verses.text: For with these leaves they covered their nakedness when they blushed for their sin; and what God had made them for members, they made for themselves occasions of shame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:12
verses.text: For they had no need to blush for the work of God; but the cause of sin preceded shame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:13
verses.text: If iniquity had not gone before, nakedness would never have been put to the blush.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:14
verses.text: For "they were naked, and were not ashamed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:15
verses.text: For they had committed nothing to be ashamed for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:16
verses.text: But why have I said all this? That we may understand that by the fig-tree sin is signified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:17
verses.text: What then is, "when thou wast under the fig-tree, I saw thee"? When thou wast under sin, I saw thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:18
verses.text: And Nathanael looking back upon what had occurred, remembered that he had been under a fig-tree, where Christ was not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:19
verses.text: He was not there, that is, by His Bodily Presence; but by His knowledge in the Spirit where is He not? And because he knew that he was under the fig-tree alone, where the Lord Christ was not; when He said to him, "When thou wast under the fig-tree, I saw thee;" he both acknowledged the Divinity in Him, and cried out, 			 "Thou art the King of Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:21
verses.text: The Lord said, "Because I said unto thee, I saw thee when thou wast under the fig-tree, marvellest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:22
verses.text: What are these greater things? And He said, "Ye shall see heaven open, and the Angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:23
verses.text: Let us call to mind the old story written in the sacred Book.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:24
verses.text: I mean in Genesis.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:25
verses.text: When Jacob slept at a certain place, he put a stone at his head; and in his sleep he saw a ladder reaching from earth even unto heaven; and the Lord was resting upon it; and Angels were ascending and descending by it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:26
verses.text: This did Jacob see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:27
verses.text: A man's dream would not have been recorded, had not some great mystery been figured in it, had not some great prophecy been to be understood in that vision.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:28
verses.text: Accordingly, Jacob himself, because he understood what he 			 had seen, placed a stone there, and anointed it with oil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:29
verses.text: Now ye recognise the anointing; recognise The Anointed also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:30
verses.text: For He is "the Stone which the builders rejected; He was made the Head of the corner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:31
verses.text: He is the Stone of which Himself said, "Whosoever shall stumble against This Stone shall be shaken; but on whomsoever That Stone shall fall, It will crush him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:32
verses.text: It is stumbled against as It lies on the earth; but It will fall on him, when He shall come from on high to judge the quick and dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:33
verses.text: Woe to the Jews, for that when Christ lay low in His humility, they stumbled against Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:34
verses.text: "This Man," say they, "is not of God, because He breaketh the sabbath day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:35
verses.text: "If He be the Son of God, let Him come down from the cross".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:36
verses.text: Madman, the Stone lies on the ground, and so thou deridest It.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:37
verses.text: But since thou dost deride It, thou art blind; since thou art blind, thou stumblest; since thou stumblest, thou art shaken; since thou hast been shaken by It as It now lies on the ground, hereafter shall thou be crushed by It as It fails from above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:38
verses.text: Therefore Jacob anointed the stone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:39
verses.text: Did he make an idol of it? He showed a meaning in it, but did not adore it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:40
verses.text: Now then give ear, attend to this Nathanael, by the occasion of whom the Lord Jesus hath been pleased to explain to us Jacob's vision.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:41
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:42
verses.text: Ye that are well instructed in the school of Christ, know that this Jacob is Israel too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:43
verses.text: They are two names; for they are one man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:44
verses.text: His first name Jacob, which is by interpretation supplanter, he received when he was born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:45
verses.text: For when those twins were born, his brother Esau was born first; and the hand of the younger was found on the elder's foot.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:46
verses.text: He held his brother's foot who preceded him in his birth, and himself came after.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:47
verses.text: And because of this occurrence, because he held his brother's heel, he was called Jacob, that is, Supplanter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:48
verses.text: And afterwards, when he was returning from Mesopotamia, the Angel wrestled with him in the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:49
verses.text: What comparison can there be between an Angel's and a man's strength? Therefore it is a mystery, a sacrament, a prophecy, a figure; let us therefore understand it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:50
verses.text: For consider the manner of the struggle too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:51
verses.text: While he wrestleth, Jacob prevailed against the Angel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:52
verses.text: Some high meaning is here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:53
verses.text: And when the man had prevailed against the Angel, he kept hold of Him; yes, the man kept hold of Him whom he had conquered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:54
verses.text: And said to Him, "I will not let Thee go, except Thou bless 			 me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:55
verses.text: When the conqueror was blessed by the Conquered, Christ was figured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:56
verses.text: So then that Angel, who is understood to be the Lord Jesus, saith to Jacob, "Thou shalt not be any more called Jacob, but Israel shall thy name be," which is by interpretation, "Seeing God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:57
verses.text: After this He touched the sinew of his thigh, the broad part, that is, of the thigh, and it dried up; and Jacob became lame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:58
verses.text: Such was He who was conquered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:59
verses.text: So great power had this Conquered One, as to touch the thigh, and make lame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:60
verses.text: It was then with His Own will that He was conquered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:61
verses.text: For He "had power to lay down" His strength, "and He had power to take It up".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:62
verses.text: He is not angry at being conquered, for He is not angry at being crucified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:63
verses.text: For He even blessed him, saying, "Thou shalt not be called Jacob, but Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:64
verses.text: Then the "supplanter" was made "the seer of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:65
verses.text: And He touched, as I have said, his thigh, and made him lame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:66
verses.text: Observe in Jacob the people of the Jews, those thousands who followed and went before the Lord's beast, who in concert with the Apostles worshipped the Lord, and cried out, "Hosanna to the Son of 			 David, Blessed is He that cometh in the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:67
verses.text: Behold Jacob blessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:68
verses.text: He has continued lame until now in them who are at this day Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:69
verses.text: For the broad part of the thigh signifies the multitude of increase.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:70
verses.text: Of whom the Psalm, when it prophesied that the Nations should believe, speaketh, saying, "A people whom I have not known, hath served Me; by the hearing of the ear it hath obeyed Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:71
verses.text: I was not there, and I was heard; here I was, and I was killed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:72
verses.text: "A people whom I have not known, hath served Me; by the hearing of the ear it hath obeyed Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:73
verses.text: Therefore, "faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:74
verses.text: And it goes on, "The strange children have lied unto Me;" concerning the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:75
verses.text: "The strange children have lied unto Me, the strange children have faded away and have halted from their paths".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:76
verses.text: I have pointed out Jacob to you, Jacob blessed and Jacob lame.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:77
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:78
verses.text: But as arising out of this occasion, this must not be passed over, which may haply of itself perplex some of you; with what design is it, that when this Jacob's grandfather Abraham's name was changed (for he too was first called Abram, and God changed his name, and said, "Thou shall not be called Abram, but Abraham"); from that time he was not called Abram.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:79
verses.text: Search in the Scriptures, and you will see that before he received another name, he was called only Abram; after he received it, he was called only Abraham.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:80
verses.text: But this Jacob, when he received another name, heard the same words, "Thou shalt not be called Jacob, but Israel shalt thou be called".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:81
verses.text: Search the Scriptures, and see how that he was always called both, both Jacob and Israel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:82
verses.text: Abram after he had received another name, was called only Abraham.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:83
verses.text: Jacob after he had received another name, was called both Jacob and Israel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:84
verses.text: The name of Abraham was to be developed in this world; for here he was made the father of many nations, whence he received his name.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:85
verses.text: But the name of Israel relates to another world, where we shall see God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:86
verses.text: Therefore the people 			 of God, the Christian people in this present time, is both Jacob and Israel, Jacob in fact, Israel in hope.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:87
verses.text: For the younger people is called the Supplanter of its brother the elder people.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:88
verses.text: What! have we supplanted the Jews? No, but we are said to be their supplanters, for that for our sakes they were supplanted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:89
verses.text: If they had not been blinded, Christ would not have been crucified; His precious Blood would not have been shed; if that Blood had not been shed, the world would not have been redeemed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:90
verses.text: Because then their blindness hath profited us, therefore hath the elder brother been supplanted by the younger, and the younger is called the Supplanter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:91
verses.text: But how long shall this be?  5.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:92
verses.text: The time will come, the end of the world will come, and all Israel shall believe; not they who now are, but their children who shall then be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:93
verses.text: For these present walking in their own ways, will go to their own place, will pass on to everlasting damnation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:94
verses.text: But when they shall have been made all one people, that shall come to pass which we sing, "I shall be satisfied when Thy glory shall be manifested".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:95
verses.text: When the promise which is made to us, that we "see face to face," shall come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:96
verses.text: "Now we see through a glass darkly," and "in part;" but when both people, now purified, now raised again, now crowned, now changed into an immortal form, and into everlasting incorruption, shall see God face to face, and Jacob shall be no more, but there shall be Israel only; then shall the Lord see him in the person of this holy Nathanael, and shall say, "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:97
verses.text: When thou dost hear, "Behold an Israelite indeed;" let Israel come into thy mind; when Israel shall come into thy mind, let his dream come into thy mind, in which he saw a ladder from earth even to heaven, the Lord standing upon it, the Angels of God ascending and descending.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:98
verses.text: This dream did Jacob see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:99
verses.text: But after this he was called Israel; that is, some little time after as he came from Mesopotamia, and on his journey.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:100
verses.text: If then Jacob saw the ladder, and he is also called 			 Israel; and this Nathanael is an "Israelite indeed in whom is no guile;" therefore when he wondered because the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:101
verses.text: said to him, "I saw thee under the fig-tree;" did He say to him, "Thou shalt see greater things than these".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:102
verses.text: And so He announced to him Jacob's dream.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:103
verses.text: To whom did He announce it? To him whom He called "an Israelite, in whom was no guile".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:104
verses.text: As if He had said, "His dream, by whose name I have called thee, shall be manifested in thee; make no haste to wonder, "thou shalt see greater things than these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:105
verses.text: Ye shall see heaven open, and the Angels of God ascending and descending unto the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:106
verses.text: See what Jacob saw; see why Jacob anointed the stone with oil; see why Jacob prophetically signified and prefigured the Anointed One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:107
verses.text: For that action was a prophecy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:108
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:109
verses.text: Now I know what you are waiting for; I understand what you would hear from me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:110
verses.text: This too will I briefly declare, as the Lord enableth me; "ascending and descending unto the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:111
verses.text: How—if they descend to Him, He is here; if they ascend to Him, He is above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:112
verses.text: But if they ascend to Him, and descend toHim, He is at once above and here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:113
verses.text: It cannot any way possibly be, that they should ascend to Him, and descend to Him, unless He be both there whither they 			 ascend, and here whither they descend—How do we prove that He is both there, and that He is here? Let Paul, who was first Saul, answer us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:114
verses.text: He found it by experience, when he was first a persecutor, and afterwards became a preacher; first Jacob, afterwards Israel; who was himself too "of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:115
verses.text: In him let us see Christ above, Christ below.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:116
verses.text: First, the very Voice of the Lord from heaven shows this; "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" What! had Paul ascended into heaven? Had Paul so much as cast a stone into heaven? He was persecuting the Christians, binding them, haling them to be put to death, searching them out in every place where they lay hid, when they were found on no consideration sparing them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:117
verses.text: To whom the Lord Christ saith, "Saul, Saul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:118
verses.text: Whence crieth He? From heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:119
verses.text: Therefore He is above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:120
verses.text: "Why persecutest thou Me?" Therefore He is below.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:121
verses.text: Thus have I explained all, though briefly, yet as 			 well as I could to you, Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:122
verses.text: I have ministered to you according to my duty, and now for your duty, do ye think upon the poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 71:123
verses.text: Let us turn to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:2
verses.text: [CXXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John ii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:5
verses.text: 2, "and Jesus also was bidden, and his disciples, to the marriage".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:7
verses.text: Ye know, Brethren, for ye have learnt it as believing in Christ, and continually too do we by our ministry impress it upon you, that the humility of Christ is the medicine of man's swollen pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:8
verses.text: For man would not have perished, had he not been swollen up through pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:9
verses.text: For "pride," as saith the Scripture, "is the beginning of all sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:10
verses.text: Against the beginning of sin, the beginning of righteousness was necessary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:11
verses.text: If then pride be the beginning of all sin, whereby should the swelling of pride be cured, had not God vouchsafed to humble Himself? Let man blush to be proud, seeing that God hath humbled Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:12
verses.text: For when man is told to humble himself, he disdains it; and when men are injured, it is pride that makes them wish to be avenged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:13
verses.text: Forasmuch as they disdain to humble themselves, they wish to be avenged; as if 			 another's punishment could be any profit to any man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:14
verses.text: One who has been hurt and suffered wrong wishes to be avenged; he seeks his own remedy from another's punishment, and gains a great torment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:15
verses.text: The Lord Christ therefore vouchsafed to humble Himself in all things, showing us the way; if we but think meet to walk thereby.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:17
verses.text: Among His other acts, lo, the Virgin's Son comes to the marriage; who being with the Father instituted marriage.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:18
verses.text: As the first woman, by whom came sin, was made of a man without a woman; so the Man by whom sin was done away, was made of a woman without a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:19
verses.text: By the first we fell, by the other we rise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:20
verses.text: And what did He at this marriage? Of water He made wine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:21
verses.text: What greater sign of power? He who had power to do such things, vouchsafed to be in need.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:22
verses.text: He who made of 			 water wine could also have of stones made bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:23
verses.text: The power was the same; but then the devil tempted Him, therefore Christ did it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:24
verses.text: For ye know that when the Lord Christ was tempted, the devil suggested this to Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:25
verses.text: For He was an hungred, since this too He vouchsafed to be, since this too made part of His Humiliation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:26
verses.text: The Bread was hungry, as the Way fainted, as saving Health was wounded, as the Life died.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:27
verses.text: When then He was an hungred as ye know, the tempter said to Him, "If Thou be the Son 			 of God, command that these stones be made bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:28
verses.text: And He made answer to the tempter, teaching thee to answer the tempter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:29
verses.text: For to this end does the general fight, that the soldiers may learn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:30
verses.text: What answer did He make? "Man doth not live by bread alone, but by every word of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:31
verses.text: And He did not make bread of the stones, who of course could as easily have done it, as He made of water wine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:32
verses.text: For it is an exercise of the same power to make bread of stone; but He did it not, that He might despise the tempter's will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:33
verses.text: For no otherwise is the tempter overcome, but by being despised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:34
verses.text: And when He had overcome the devil's temptation, "Angels came and ministered to Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:35
verses.text: He then who had so great power, why did He not do the one, and do the other? Read, yea, recollect what thou hast just heard, when He did this, when, that is, He made of the water wine; what did the Evangelist add? "And His disciples believed on Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:36
verses.text: Would the devil on the other occasion have believed on Him?  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:37
verses.text: He then who could do so great things, was hungry, and athirst, was wearied, slept, was apprehended, beaten, crucified, slain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:38
verses.text: This is the way; walk by humility, that thou mayest come to eternity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:39
verses.text: Christ-God is the Country whither we go; Christ-Man is the Way whereby we go.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:40
verses.text: To Him we go, by Him we go; why fear we lest we go astray? He departed not from the Father; and came to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:41
verses.text: He sucked the breasts, and He contained the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:42
verses.text: He lay in the manger, and He fed 			 the Angels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:43
verses.text: God and Man, the same God who is Man, the same Man who is God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:44
verses.text: But not God in that wherein He is Man, God, in that He is the Word; Man, in that the Word was made Flesh; by at once continuing to be God, and by assuming man's Flesh; by adding what He was not, not losing what He was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:45
verses.text: Therefore henceforward, having now suffered in this His humiliation, dead, and buried, He has now risen again, and ascended into heaven, there He is, and sitteth at the right Hand of the Father: and here 			 He is needy in His poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:46
verses.text: Yesterday too I set this forth to your Affection by occasion of what He said to Nathanael, "Thou shalt see a greater thing than this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:47
verses.text: For I say unto you, Ye shall see Heaven open, and the Angels of God ascending and descending unto the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:48
verses.text: We searched out what this meant, and spake at some length; must we recapitulate the same to-day? Let those who were present remember; yet I will briefly run over it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:49
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:50
verses.text: He would not say, "ascending unto the Son of Man," unless He were above; He would not say, "descending unto the Son of Man," unless He were also below.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:51
verses.text: He is at once above, and below; above in Himself, below in His; above with the Father, below in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:52
verses.text: Whence also was that Voice to Saul, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me?" He would not say, "Saul, Saul," unless that He was above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:53
verses.text: But Saul was not persecuting Him above.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:54
verses.text: He then who was above would not have said, "Why persecutest thou me?" unless He were below also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:55
verses.text: Fear Christ above; recognise Him below.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:56
verses.text: Have Christ above bestowing His bounty, recognise Him here in need.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:57
verses.text: Here He is poor, there He is rich.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:58
verses.text: That Christ is poor here, He tells us Himself for me, "I was an hungred, I was thirsty, I was naked, I was a stranger, I was in 			 prison".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:59
verses.text: And to some He said, "Ye have ministered unto Me," and to some He said, "Ye have not ministered unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:60
verses.text: Lo, we have proved Christ poor; that Christ is Rich, who knows not? And even here it was a property of these riches to turn the water into wine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:61
verses.text: If he who has wine is rich, how rich is He who maketh wine? So then Christ is rich and poor; as God, rich; as Man, poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:62
verses.text: Yea rich too now as Very Man He hath ascended into heaven, sitteth at the right 			 Hand of the Father; yet still He is poor and hungry here, thirsty, and naked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:63
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:64
verses.text: What art thou? Rich, or poor? Many tell me, I am poor; and they tell the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:65
verses.text: I recognise some poor having something, and some having want.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:66
verses.text: But some have much gold and silver.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:67
verses.text: O that they would acknowledge themselves poor! Poor they will acknowledge themselves, if they acknowledge the poor about them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:68
verses.text: For how is it? How much soever thou hast, thou rich man whosoever thou art, thou art God's beggar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:69
verses.text: The hour of prayer comes, and there I prove thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:70
verses.text: Thou makest 			 thy petition.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:71
verses.text: How art thou not poor, who makest thy petition? I say more, Thou makest petition for bread.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:72
verses.text: Wilt thou not have to say, "Give us our daily bread"? Thou, who askest for daily bread, art thou poor, or rich? And yet Christ saith to thee, "Give Me of that which I have given thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:73
verses.text: For what didst thou bring here, when thou camest hither? All things that I created, thyself created hast found here; nothing didst thou bring, nothing shalt thou take away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:74
verses.text: Why wilt thou not give Me of Mine Own? For thou art full, and the poor man is empty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:75
verses.text: Look at your first origin; naked were ye both born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:76
verses.text: Thou too then wast born naked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:77
verses.text: Great 			 store hast thou found here; didst thou bring ought with thee? I ask for Mine Own; give, and I will repay.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:78
verses.text: Thou hast found Me a bountiful giver, make Me at once thy debtor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:79
verses.text: It is not enough to say, 'Thou hast found Me a bountiful giver, make Me at once thy debtor;' let Me regard thee as lending upon interest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:80
verses.text: Thou givest me but little, I will repay more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:81
verses.text: Thou givest me earthly things, I will repay heavenly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:82
verses.text: Thou givest me temporal things, I will restore eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 72:83
verses.text: I will restore thee to 			 thyself, when I shall have restored thee unto Me".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:2
verses.text: [CXXXIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John viii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:5
verses.text: 31, "If ye abide in my word, then are ye truly my disciples," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:7
verses.text: Ye know well, Beloved, that we all have One Master, and are fellow disciples under Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:8
verses.text: Nor are we your masters, because we speak to you from this higher spot; but He is the Master of all, who dwelleth in us all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:9
verses.text: He just now spake to us all in the Gospel, and said to us, what I also am saying to you; but He saith it of us, as well of us as of you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:10
verses.text: "If ye shall continue in My word," not of course in my word 			 who am now speaking to you; but in His who spake just now out of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:11
verses.text: "If ye shall continue in My word," saith He, "ye are My disciples indeed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:12
verses.text: To be a disciple, it is not enough to come, but to continue.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:13
verses.text: He doth not therefore say, "If ye shall hear My word;" or, "If ye shall come to My word;" or, "If ye shall praise My word;" but observe what He said, "If ye shall continue in My word, ye are My disciples indeed, and ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall free you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:14
verses.text: What shall we say, Brethren? To continue in the word of God, is it toilsome, or is it not? If it be toilsome, look at the great reward; if it be not toilsome, thou receivest the reward for nought.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:15
verses.text: Continue we then in Him who continueth in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:16
verses.text: We, if we continue not in Him, fall; but He if He continue not in us, hath not on that account lost an habitation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:17
