verses.text: For He skilleth to continue in Himself, who never leaveth Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:18
verses.text: But for man, God forbid that he should continue in 			 himself who hath lost himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:19
verses.text: So then we continue in Him through indigence; He continueth in us through mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:21
verses.text: Now then seeing it hath been set forth what we ought to do, let us see what we are to receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:22
verses.text: For He hath appointed a work, and promised a reward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:23
verses.text: What is the work? "If ye shall continue in Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:24
verses.text: A short work; short in description, great in execution.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:25
verses.text: "If ye shall build on the Rock".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:26
verses.text: O how great a thing is this, Brethren, to build on the Rock, how great is it! "The floods came, the winds blew, the rain descended, and beat upon that house, and it fell not; for it was founded upon a rock".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:27
verses.text: What then is to continue in the word of God, but not to yield to any temptations? The reward, what is it? "Ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall free you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:28
verses.text: Bear with me, for ye perceive that my voice is feeble; assist me by your calm attention.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:29
verses.text: Glorious reward! "Ye shall know the truth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:30
verses.text: Here one may haply say, "And what doth it profit me to know the truth?" "And the truth shall free you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:31
verses.text: If the truth have no charms for you, let freedom have its charms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:32
verses.text: In the usage of the Latin tongue, the expression, "to be free," is used in two senses; and chiefly we are accustomed to hear this word in this sense, that whosoever is free may be understood to escape some danger, to be rid of some 			 embarrassment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:33
verses.text: But the proper signification of "to be free," is "to be made free;" just as "to be saved," is "to be made safe;" "to be healed," is, "to be made whole;" so "to be freed," is "to be made free".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:34
verses.text: Therefore I said, "If the truth have no charms for you, let freedom have its charms".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:35
verses.text: This is expressed more evidently in the Greek language, nor can it be there understood in any other sense.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:36
verses.text: And that ye may know that in no other sense can it be 			 understood; when the Lord spake, the Jews answered, "We were never in bondage to any man; how sayest thou the Truth shall free you?" That is, "the Truth shall make you free," how sayest thou to us, who were never in bondage to any man? "How," say they, "dost Thou promise them freedom, who as Thou seest never bare the hard yoke of bondage?"  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:37
verses.text: They heard what they ought; but they did not what they ought.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:38
verses.text: What did they hear? Because I said, "The truth shall free you;" ye turned your thoughts upon yourselves, that ye are not in bondage to man, and ye said, "We were never in bondage to any man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:39
verses.text: Every one," Jew and Greek, rich and poor, the man in authority and private station, the emperor and the beggar, "Every one that committeth sin is the servant of sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:40
verses.text: "Every one," saith He, "that committeth sin is the servant of sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:41
verses.text: If men but acknowledge their bondage, they will see from whence they may obtain freedom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:42
verses.text: Some free-born man has been taken captive by the barbarians, from a free man is made a slave; another hears, and pities him, considers how that he has money, becomes his ransomer, goes to the barbarians, gives money, ransoms the man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:43
verses.text: And he has indeed restored freedom, if he have taken away iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:44
verses.text: But what man 			 has ever taken away iniquity from another man? He who was in bondage with the barbarians, has been redeemed by his ransomer; and great difference there is between the ransomer and the ransomed; yet haply are they fellow-slaves under the lordship of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:45
verses.text: I ask him that was ransomed, "Hast thou sin?" "I have," he says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:46
verses.text: I ask the ransomer, "Hast thou sin?" "I have," he says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:47
verses.text: So then neither do thou boast thyself that thou hast been ransomed, nor thou uplift thyself that thou 			 art his ransomer; but fly both of you to the True Deliverer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:48
verses.text: It is but a small part of it, that they who are under sin, are called servants; they are even called dead; what a man is afraid of captivity bringing upon him, iniquity has brought on him already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:49
verses.text: For what? because they seem to be alive, was He then mistaken who said, "Let the dead bury their dead"? So then all under sin are dead, dead servants, dead in their service, servants in their death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:50
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:51
verses.text: Who then freeth from death and from bondage, save He, who is "Free among the dead"? Who is "Free among the dead," save He who among sinners is without sin? "Lo, the prince of the world cometh," saith our Redeemer Himself, our Deliverer, "Lo, the prince of the world cometh, and shall find nothing in Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:52
verses.text: He holds fast those whom he hath deceived, whom he hath seduced, whom he hath persuaded to sin and death; "in Me shall he find nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:53
verses.text: Come, Lord, Redeemer come, come; let the captive acknowledge thee, him that leadeth captive flee thee; be Thou my Deliverer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:54
verses.text: Lost as I was, He hath found me in Whom the devil findeth nothing that cometh of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:55
verses.text: The prince of this world findeth in Him Flesh, he findeth it but what kind of Flesh? A mortal Flesh, which he can seize, 			 which he can crucify, which he can kill.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:56
verses.text: Thou art mistaken, O deceiver, the Redeemer is not deceived; thou art mistaken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:57
verses.text: Thou seest in the Lord a mortal Flesh, it is not flesh of sin, it is the likeness of flesh of sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:58
verses.text: "For God sent His Son in the likeness of flesh of sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:59
verses.text: True Flesh, mortal Flesh; but not flesh of sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:60
verses.text: "For God sent His Son in the likeness of flesh of sin, that by sin He might condemn sin in the Flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:61
verses.text: "For God sent His Son in the likeness of flesh of sin;" in Flesh, but not in flesh of sin; but "in the likeness of flesh of sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:62
verses.text: For what purpose? "That by sin," of which assuredly there was none in Him, "He might condemn sin in the flesh; that the righteousness of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:63
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:64
verses.text: If then it was "the likeness of flesh of sin," not flesh of sin, how, "That by sin He might condemn sin in the flesh"? So a likeness is wont to receive the name of that thing of which it is a likeness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:65
verses.text: The word man is used for a real man; but if you show a man painted on the wall, and enquire what it is, it is answered, "A man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:66
verses.text: So then Flesh having the likeness of flesh of sin, that it might be a sacrifice for sin, is called "sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:67
verses.text: The same 			 Apostle says in another place, "He made Him to be sin for us, who knew no sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:68
verses.text: "Him who knew no sin:" Who is He who knew no sin, but He That said, "Behold the prince of the world cometh, and shall find nothing in me? Him who knew no sin, made He sin for us;" even Christ Himself, who knew no sin, God made sin for us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:69
verses.text: What does this mean, Brethren? If it were said, "He made sin upon Him," or, "He made Him to have sin;" it would seem intolerable; how do we tolerate what is said, "He made Him sin," that Christ Himself should be sin? They who are acquainted with the Scriptures of the Old Testament recognise what I am saying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:70
verses.text: For it is not an expression once used, but repeatedly, 			 very constantly, sacrifices for sins are called "sins".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:71
verses.text: A goat, for instance, was offered for sin, a ram, anything; the victim itself which was offered for sin was called "sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:72
verses.text: A sacrifice for sin then was called "sin;" so that in one place the Law says, "That the Priests are to lay their hands upon the sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:73
verses.text: "Him" then, "who knew no sin, He made sin for us;" that is, "He was made a sacrifice for sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:74
verses.text: Sin was offered, and sin was cancelled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:75
verses.text: The Blood of the Redeemer was shed, and the debtor's bond was cancelled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:76
verses.text: This is the "Blood, That was shed for many for the remission of sins".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:77
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:78
verses.text: What meaneth this then thy senseless exultation, O thou that didst hold me captive, for that my Deliverer had mortal Flesh? See, if He had sin; if thou hast found anything of thine in Him, hold Him fast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:79
verses.text: "The Word was made Flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:80
verses.text: The Word is the Creator, the Flesh His creature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:81
verses.text: What is there here of thine, O enemy? And the Word is God, and His Human Soul is His creature, and His Human Flesh His creature, and the Mortal Flesh of God is His creature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:82
verses.text: Seek for sin here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:83
verses.text: But what art thou seeking? The Truth saith, "The prince of this world shall come, and shall find nothing in Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:84
verses.text: He did not therefore not find Flesh, but nothing of his own, that is, no sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:85
verses.text: Thou didst deceive the innocent, thou madest them guilty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:86
verses.text: Thou didst slay the Innocent; thou destroyedst Him from whom thou hadst nothing due, render back what thou didst hold fast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:87
verses.text: Why then didst thou exult for a short hour, because thou didst find in Christ mortal Flesh? It was thy trap: whereupon thou didst rejoice, thereby hast thou been taken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:88
verses.text: Wherein thou didst exult that thou hadst found 			 something, therein thou sorrowest now that thou hast lost what thou didst possess.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:89
verses.text: Therefore, brethren, let us who believe in Christ, continue in His word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:90
verses.text: For if we shall continue in His word, we are His disciples indeed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:91
verses.text: For not those twelve only, but all we who continue in His word are His disciples indeed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:92
verses.text: And "we shall know the Truth, and the Truth shall free us;" that is, Christ the Son of God who hath said, "I am the Truth," shall make you free, that is, shall free you, not from barbarians, but from the devil; not from the captivity of the body, but from the iniquity of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:93
verses.text: It is He Only who freeth in such wise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:94
verses.text: Let no one call himself free, lest he remain a slave.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 73:95
verses.text: Our soul shall not remain in bondage, for that day by day our debts are forgiven.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:2
verses.text: [CXXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:4
verses.text: ]  Again in John v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:5
verses.text: 2 , etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:6
verses.text: , on the five porches, where lay a great multitude of impotent folk, and of the pool of Siloa.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:8
verses.text: Subjects strange neither to your ears nor hearts are now repeated: yet do they revive the affections of the hearer, and by repetition in some sort renew us: nor is it wearisome to hear what is well known already, for the words of the Lord are always sweet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:9
verses.text: The exposition of the sacred Scriptures is as the sacred Scriptures themselves: though they be well known, yet are they read to impress the remembrance of them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:10
verses.text: And so the exposition of 			 them, though it be well known, is nevertheless to be repeated, that they who have forgotten it may be reminded, or they who chanced not to hear it may hear; and that with those who do retain what they are used to hear, it may by the repetition be brought to pass that they shall not be able to forget it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:11
verses.text: For I remember that I have already spoken to you, Beloved, on this lesson of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:12
verses.text: Yet to repeat the same explanation to you is not wearisome, even as it was not wearisome to repeat the 			 same Lesson to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:13
verses.text: The Apostle Paul saith in a certain Epistle, "To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not wearisome, but for you it is necessary".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:14
verses.text: So too with myself to say the same things to you, to me is not wearisome, but for you it is safe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:16
verses.text: The five porches in which the infirm folk lay signify the Law, which was first given to the Jews and to the people of Israel by Moses the servant of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:17
verses.text: For this Moses the minister of the Law wrote five books.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:18
verses.text: In relation therefore to the number of the books which he wrote, the five porches figured the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:19
verses.text: But because the Law was not given to heal the infirm, but to discover and to manifest them; for so saith the Apostle, "For if there had been a 			 law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the Law; But the Scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe;" therefore in those porches the sick folk lay, but were not cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:20
verses.text: For what saith he? "If there had been a law given which could have given life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:21
verses.text: Therefore those porches which figured the Law could not cure the sick.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:22
verses.text: Some one will say to me, "Why then was it given?" The Apostle Paul hath himself explained: "Scripture," saith he, "hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:23
verses.text: For these folk who were 			 sick, thought themselves to be whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:24
verses.text: They received the Law, which they were not able to fulfil; they learnt in what disease they were, and they implored the Physician's aid; they wished to be cured because they came to know they were in distress, which they would not have known if they had not been unable to fulfil the Law which had been given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:25
verses.text: For man thought himself innocent, and from this very pride of false innocence became more mad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:26
verses.text: To tame this pride then and to lay it bare, the Law 			 was given; not to deliver the sick, but to convince the proud.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:27
verses.text: Attend then, Beloved; to this end was the Law given, to discover diseases, not to take them away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:28
verses.text: And so then those sick folk who might have been sick in their own houses with greater privacy, if those five porches had not existed, were in those porches set forth to the eyes of all men, but were not by the porches cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:29
verses.text: The Law therefore was useful to discover sins, because that man being made more abundantly guilty by the 			 transgression of the Law, might, having tamed his pride, implore the help of Him That pitieth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:30
verses.text: Attend to the Apostle; "The Law entered that sin might abound; but where sin abounded, grace hath much more abounded".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:31
verses.text: What is, "The Law entered that sin might abound"? As in another place he saith, "For where there is no law, there is no transgression".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:32
verses.text: Man may be called a sinner before the Law, a transgressor he cannot.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:33
verses.text: But when he hath sinned, after that he hath received the Law, he is found not only a sinner, but a transgressor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:34
verses.text: Forasmuch then as to sin is added transgression, therefore "hath sin abounded".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:35
verses.text: And when sin abounds, human pride learns at length to submit itself, and to confess to God, and to say "I am weak".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:36
verses.text: To say to those words of the Psalm which none but the humbled soul saith, "I said, Lord, be 			 merciful unto me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:37
verses.text: Let the weak soul then say this that is at least convinced by transgression, and not cured, but manifested by the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:38
verses.text: Hear too Paul himself showing thee, both that the Law is good, and yet that nothing but the grace of Christ delivereth from sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:39
verses.text: For the Law can prohibit and command; apply the medicine, that that which doth not allow a man to fulfil the Law, may be cured, it cannot, but grace only doeth that.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:40
verses.text: For the Apostle saith, "For I delight in the Law of God after the 			 inner man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:41
verses.text: That is, I see now that what the Law blames is evil, and what the Law commands is good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:42
verses.text: "For I delight in the Law of God after the inner man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:43
verses.text: I see another law in my members resisting the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity in the law of sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:44
verses.text: This derived from the punishment of sin, from the propagation of death, from the condemnation of Adam, "resists the law of the mind, and brings it into captivity in the law of sin which is in the members".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:45
verses.text: He was 			 convinced; he received the Law, that he might be convinced: see now what profit it was to him that he was convinced.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:46
verses.text: Hear the following words, "Wretched man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:47
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:48
verses.text: Give heed then.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:49
verses.text: Those five porches were significative of the Law, bearing the sick, not healing them; discovering, not curing them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:50
verses.text: But who did cure the sick? He that descended into the pool.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:51
verses.text: And when did the sick man descend into the pool? When the Angel gave the sign by the moving of the water.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:52
verses.text: For thus was that pool sanctified, for that the Angel came down and moved the water.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:53
verses.text: Men saw the water; and from the motion of the troubled water they understood the 			 presence of the Angel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:54
verses.text: If any one then went down, he was cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:55
verses.text: Why then was not that sick man cured? Let us consider his own words; "I have no man," he says, "when the water is moved, to put me into the pool, but while I am coming, another steppeth down".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:56
verses.text: Couldest not thou then step down afterwards, if another step down before thee? Here it is shown us, that only one was cured at the moving of the water.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:57
verses.text: Whosoever stepped down first, he alone was cured: but whoever stepped down afterwards, at that moving of the water was not cured, but waited till it was moved again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:58
verses.text: What then does this mystery mean? For it is not without a meaning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:59
verses.text: Attend, Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:60
verses.text: Waters are put in the Apocalypse for a figure of peoples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:61
verses.text: For when in the Apocalypse John saw many waters, he asked what it meant, and it was told him that they were peoples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:62
verses.text: The water then of the pool signified the people of the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:63
verses.text: For as that people was held in by the five books of Moses in the Law, so that water too was enclosed by five porches.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:64
verses.text: When was the water troubled? When the people of the Jews was troubled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:65
verses.text: And when was the people of the Jews troubled, but when the Lord Jesus Christ came? The Lord's Passion was the troubling of the water.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:66
verses.text: For the Jews were troubled when the Lord suffered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:67
verses.text: See, what was just 			 now read had relation to this troubling.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:68
verses.text: "The Jews wished to kill Him, not only because He did these things on the sabbaths, but because He called Himself the Son of God, making Himself equal with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:69
verses.text: For Christ called Himself the Son after one manner, in another was it said to men, "I said, Ye are Gods, and ye are all children of the Most High".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:70
verses.text: For if He had made Himself the Son of God in such sort as any man whatever may be called the son of God (for by the grace of God men are called sons of God); the Jews would not have been enraged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:71
verses.text: But because they understand Him to call Himself the Son of God in another way, according to that, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God;" and according to what the Apostle saith, "Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God;" they saw a man, and they were enraged, because He made Himself equal with God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:72
verses.text: But He well knew that He was equal, but wherein they saw not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:73
verses.text: For that which they saw they wished to crucify; by That which they saw not, they were judged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:74
verses.text: What did the Jews see? What the Apostles also saw, when Philip said, "Show us the Father, and it sufficeth us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:75
verses.text: But what did the Jews not see? What not even the Apostles saw, when the Lord answered, "Have I been so long time with you, and yet have ye not known Me? He that seeth Me, seeth the Father also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:76
verses.text: Because then the Jews were not able to see This in Him, they held Him for a proud and ungodly man, making Himself equal with God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:77
verses.text: Here was a troubling, the water was troubled, the Angel had come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:78
verses.text: For the Lord is called also the "Angel of the Great Counsel," in that He is the messenger of the Father's will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:79
verses.text: For Angel in Greek is in Latin "messenger".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:80
verses.text: So you have the Lord saying that He announces to us the kingdom of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:81
verses.text: He then had come, the "Angel of the Great Counsel," but the Lord of all the Angels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:82
verses.text: "Angel" on this account, because He took Flesh; the "Lord of Angels," in that by "Him all things were made, and without Him was nothing made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:83
verses.text: For if all things, Angels too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:84
verses.text: And therefore Himself was not made, because by Him all things were made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:85
verses.text: Now what was made, was not made without the operation of the Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:86
verses.text: But the flesh which became the mother of Christ, could not have been born, if it had not been created by the Word, which was afterwards born of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:87
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:88
verses.text: The Jews then were troubled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:89
verses.text: What is this? "Why doeth He these things on the sabbath days?" And especially at those words of the Lord, "My Father worketh hitherto, and I work".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:90
verses.text: Their carnal understanding of this, that God rested on the seventh day from all His works, "troubled them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:91
verses.text: For this is written in Genesis, and most excellently written it is, and on the best reasons.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:92
verses.text: But they thinking that God as it were rested from fatigue on the seventh day after all, and that He therefore blessed it, because on it He was refreshed from His weariness, did not in their foolishness understand, that He who made all things by the Word, could not be wearied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:93
verses.text: Let them read, and tell me how could God be wearied, who said, "Let it be made, and it 			 was made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:94
verses.text: To-day if a man could so do, as God did, how would he be wearied? He said, "Let there be light, and the light was made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:95
verses.text: Again, "Let there be a firmament, and it was made:" if indeed He said, and it was not done, He was wearied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:96
verses.text: In another place briefly, "He spake, and they were made; He commanded, and they were created".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:97
verses.text: He then who worketh thus, how doth He labour? But if He labour not, how doth He rest? But in that sabbath, in which it is said that God rested from all His works, in the Rest of God our rest was signified; because the sabbath of this world shall be, when the six ages shall have passed away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:98
verses.text: The six days as it were of the world are passing away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:99
verses.text: One day hath passed away, from Adam unto Noe; another from the deluge unto Abraham; the third from Abraham unto David; the fourth from 			 David unto the carrying away into Babylon; the fifth from the carrying away into Babylon unto the advent of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:100
verses.text: Now the sixth day is in passing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:101
verses.text: We are in the sixth age, in the sixth day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:102
verses.text: Let us then be reformed after the image of God, because that on the sixth day man was made after the image of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:103
verses.text: What formation did then, let reformation do in us, and what creation did there, let creating-anew do in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:104
verses.text: After this day in which we now are, after this age, the rest which is promised to the saints and prefigured in those days, shall come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:105
verses.text: Because in very truth too, after all things which He made in the world, He hath made nothing new in creation afterwards.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:106
verses.text: The creatures themselves shall be transformed and changed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:107
verses.text: For since the creatures were 			 fashioned, nothing more has been added.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:108
verses.text: But nevertheless, if He who made did not rule the world, what is made would fall to ruin: He cannot but administer that which He hath made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:109
verses.text: Because then nothing hath been added to the creation, He is said to have rested from all His works; but because He doth not cease to govern what He made, rightly did the Lord say, "My Father worketh even hitherto".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:110
verses.text: Attend, Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:111
verses.text: He finished, He is said to have rested; for He finished His works, and hath added 			 no more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:112
verses.text: He governeth what He hath made; therefore He doth not cease to work.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:113
verses.text: But with the same facility that He made, with the same doth He govern.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:114
verses.text: For do not suppose, brethren, that when He created He did not labour, and that He laboureth in that He governeth: as in a ship, they labour who build the ship, and they who manage it labour too; for they are men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:115
verses.text: For with the same facility wherewith "He spake and they were made," with the same facility and judgment doth He govern all things by 			 the Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:116
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:117
verses.text: Let us not, because human affairs seem to be in disorder, fancy that there is no governance of human affairs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:118
verses.text: For all men are ordered in their proper places; but to every man it seems as though they have no order.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:119
verses.text: Do thou only look to what thou wouldest wish to be; for as thou shalt wish to be, the Master knoweth where to place thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:120
verses.text: Look at a painter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:121
verses.text: Before him are placed various colours, and he knows where to set each colour on.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:122
verses.text: Questionless the sinner hath chosen to be the black colour; does not then the Artist know where to place him? How many parts does the painter finish off with the colour of black? how many ornaments does he make of it? With it he makes the hair, the beard, the eye-brows; he makes the face of white only.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:123
verses.text: Look then to that which thou wouldest wish to be; take no care where He may order thee who cannot err, He knoweth where to place thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:124
verses.text: For so we see it happen by the common laws of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:125
verses.text: Some man, for instance, has chosen to be a house-breaker: the law of 			 the judge knows that he has acted contrary to the law: the law of the judge knows where to place him; and orders him most properly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:126
verses.text: He indeed has lived evilly; but not evilly has the law ordered him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:127
verses.text: From a house-breaker he will be sentenced to the mines; from the labour of such how great works are constructed? That condemned man's punishment is the city's ornament.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:128
verses.text: So then God knoweth where to place thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:129
verses.text: Do not think that thou art disturbing the counsel of God, if thou art minded to be 			 disorderly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:130
verses.text: Doth not He who knew how to create, know how to order thee? Good were it for thee to strive for this, to be set in a good place.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:131
verses.text: What was said of Judas by the Apostle? "He went unto his own place".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:132
verses.text: By the operation of course of Divine Providence, because by an evil will he chose to be evil, but God did not by ordering evil make it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:133
verses.text: But because that evil man himself chose to be a sinner, he did what he would, and suffered what he would not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:134
verses.text: In that he did what he would, his sin is discovered; in that he suffered what he would not, the order of God is praised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:135
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:136
verses.text: Wherefore have I said all this? That ye, brethren, may understand what was most excellently said by the Lord Jesus Christ, "My Father worketh even hitherto".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:137
verses.text: In that He doth not abandon the creature which He made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:138
verses.text: And He said, "As He worketh, so do I also work".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:139
verses.text: In this He at once signified that He was equal with God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:140
verses.text: "My Father," saith He, "worketh hitherto, and I work".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:141
verses.text: Their carnal sense touching the rest was troubled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:142
verses.text: For they thought that the Lord being wearied rested, that He should work no more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:143
verses.text: They hear, "My Father worketh even hitherto:" they are troubled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:144
verses.text: "And I work:" He hath made Himself equal with God: they are troubled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:145
verses.text: But be not alarmed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:146
verses.text: The water is troubled, now the sick man is to be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:147
verses.text: What meaneth this? Therefore are they troubled, that the Lord may suffer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:148
verses.text: The Lord doth suffer, the precious Blood is shed, the sinner is redeemed, grace is given to the sinner, to him that saith, "Wretched man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death? The grace of God, through Jesus Christ our Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:149
verses.text: But how is he cured? If he step down.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:150
verses.text: For that pool was so made, that men should go down, and not come up to it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:151
verses.text: For there might be pools of such a kind, so constructed, that men must go up to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:152
verses.text: But why was this made in such a way that men must go down to it? Because the Lord's Passion searches for the humble.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:153
verses.text: Let the humble go down, let him not be proud, if he wishes to be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:154
verses.text: But why was it but "one"? Because the Church is only One throughout the world, unity is 			 saved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:155
verses.text: When then one is made whole, unity is signified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:156
verses.text: By one understand unity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:157
verses.text: Depart not then from unity, if thou wouldest not be without a part in this saving cure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:158
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:159
verses.text: What then does it mean that the man was in infirmity thirty-eight years? I know, brethren, that I have spoken of this already; but even those who read forget, how much more they who hear but seldom? Attend therefore for a little while, Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:160
verses.text: In the number forty, the accomplishment of righteousness is figured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:161
verses.text: The accomplishment of righteousness, in that we live here in labour, in toil, in self-restraint, in fastings, in watchings, in tribulations; this is the exercise of righteousness, to bear this present time, and to fast as it were from this world; not from the food of the body, which we do but seldom; but from the love of the world, which we ought to do always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:162
verses.text: He then fulfils the law 			 who abstains from this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:163
verses.text: For he cannot love that which is eternal, unless he shall cease to love that which is temporal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:164
verses.text: Consider a man's love: think of it as, so to say, the hand of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:165
verses.text: If it is holding anything, it cannot hold anything else.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:166
verses.text: But that it may be able to hold what is given to it, it must leave go what it holds already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:167
verses.text: This I say, see how expressly I say it; "Whoso loveth the world cannot love God; he hath his hand engaged".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:168
verses.text: God saith to him, "Hold what I 			 give".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:169
verses.text: He will not leave go what he was holding; he cannot receive what is offered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:170
verses.text: Have I said a man should not possess ought? If he is able, if perfection require this of him, let him not possess.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:171
verses.text: If hindered by any necessity he is not able, let him possess, not be possessed; let him hold, not be held; let him be the lord of his possessions, not the slave; as saith the Apostle "However, brethren, the time is short; it remaineth that both they that have wives, be as though they had not; 			 and they who buy, as though they possessed not; and they who rejoice, as though they rejoiced not; and they who weep, as though they wept not; and they who use this world, as though they used it not; for the fashion of this world passeth away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:172
verses.text: I would have you be without carefulness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:173
verses.text: What is, "Do not love what thou dost possess in this world"? Let it not hold thine hand fast, by which God must be held.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:174
verses.text: Let not thy love be engaged, whereby thou canst make thy way to God, and cleave to Him who created thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:175
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:176
verses.text: Thou wilt say and make answer to me, "Yea, God knows that I possess innocently what I have".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:177
verses.text: Temptation proves thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:178
verses.text: There is a troubling of thy possessions, and thou dost blaspheme.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:179
verses.text: It is but lately we were in such a case.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:180
verses.text: There is a troubling of thy possessions, and thou art not found what thou wast, and dost show that there is one thing in thy mouth to-day, and another in thy mouth yesterday.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:181
verses.text: And I would that thou wouldest only defend thine own even with 			 vehemence; and not try to usurp with audacity another's; and what is worse, to escape reprehension, maintain that what is another's is thine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:182
verses.text: But why need I say more? This I advise, this I say, Brethren, and as a brother advise; God bids, and I admonish because I am admonished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:183
verses.text: He alarmeth me, who doth not allow me to keep silence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:184
verses.text: He exacteth of me what He hath given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:185
verses.text: For He hath given it to be laid out, not to be kept up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:186
verses.text: And if I should keep it and hide it, He saith to me, 			 "Thou wicked and slothful servant, wherefore gavest thou not My money to the exchangers, that at My coming I might require it with usury?" And what will it profit me that I have lost nothing of that which I received? That is not enough for my Lord, He is covetous; but God's covetousness is our salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:187
verses.text: He is covetous, He looketh for His own money, He gathereth in His Own image.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:188
verses.text: "Thou shouldest have given," saith He, "the money to the exchangers, that at My coming I might require it with usury".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:189
verses.text: And if by any chance forgetfulness should make me fail of admonishing you, the temptations and tribulations 			 at least which we are suffering, would be an admonition to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:190
verses.text: Ye have heard at least the word of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:191
verses.text: Blessed be the Lord and His glory.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:192
verses.text: For ye are here gathered together, and are hanging on the word of God's minister.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:193
verses.text: Turn not your attention to our flesh, by which the word is given out to you; for hungry men regard not the meanness of the dish, but the preciousness of the food.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:194
verses.text: God is proving you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:195
verses.text: Ye are gathered together, ye praise the word of God; temptation will prove in what manner ye 			 hear it: ye will have the active business of life whereby your true character will be shown.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:196
verses.text: For so he who to-day is shouting with railings, was yesterday a ready listener.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:197
verses.text: Therefore I forewarn; therefore I tell you, therefore I do not withhold it, my Brethren, that the time of questioning will come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:198
verses.text: For the Lord maketh question of the righteous and of the ungodly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:199
verses.text: This you know ye have sung, this have we sung together; "The Lord maketh question of the righteous and the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:200
verses.text: And what 			 follows? "But he that loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:201
verses.text: And in another place, "Into the thoughts of the ungodly there shall be questioning made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:202
verses.text: God doth not make question of thee there, where I question thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:203
verses.text: I question thy tongue, God questioneth thy thoughts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:204
verses.text: For He knoweth how thou dost hear, and He knoweth how to require, Who ordereth me to give.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:205
verses.text: He hath wished me to be a dispenser, the requiring He hath reserved to Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:206
verses.text: To admonish, to teach, to rebuke, is ours; but to save, and to crown, or to condemn, and to cast into hell, is not ours; "But the Judge shall deliver to the officer, and the officer to the 			 prison.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:207
verses.text: Verily I say unto thee, thou shalt not go out thence, till thou payest the last farthing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:208
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:209
verses.text: Let us then return to our subject.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:210
verses.text: The perfection of righteousness is shown by the number forty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:211
verses.text: What is it to fulfil the number forty? To restrain one's self from the love of this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:212
verses.text: Restraint from temporal things, that they be not loved to our destruction, is, as it were, fasting from this world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:213
verses.text: Therefore the Lord fasted forty days, and Moses, and Elias.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:214
verses.text: He then who gave His servants the power to fast forty days, could He not fast eighty or 			 a hundred? Why then did He not will to fast more than He had given His servants to do, but because in this number forty is the mystery of fasting, the restraint from this world? What is this to say? What the Apostle says; "The world is crucified to me, and I to the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:215
verses.text: He then fulfils the number forty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:216
verses.text: And what doth the Lord show? That because Moses did this, this Elias, this Christ, that this both the Law, and the Prophets, and the Gospel, teach; that thou mayest not think that there is one thing in the Law, another in the Prophets, another in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:217
verses.text: All Scripture teacheth thee nothing else, but restraint from the love of the world, that thy love may speed on to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:218
verses.text: As a figure that the Law teaches this, Moses fasted forty days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:219
verses.text: As a 			 figure that the Prophets teach it, Elias fasted forty days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:220
verses.text: As a figure that the Gospel teaches it, the Lord fasted forty days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:221
verses.text: And therefore in the mount too these three appeared, the Lord in the middle, Moses and Elias at the sides.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:222
verses.text: Wherefore? Because the Gospel itself receives testimony from the Law and the Prophets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:223
verses.text: But why in the number forty is the perfection of righteousness? In the Psalter it is said, "O God, I will sing a new song unto Thee, upon a psaltery of ten strings will I sing praises unto Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:224
verses.text: Which signifies the ten precepts of the Law, which the Lord came not to destroy, but to fulfil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:225
verses.text: And the Law itself throughout the whole world, it is evident, hath four quarters, the East, and West, South, and North, as the Scripture saith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:226
verses.text: And hence the vessel which bare all the emblematic animals, which was exhibited to Peter, when he was told, "Kill and eat," that it might be shown that the Gentiles should believe and enter into the body of the Church, just as what we eat entereth into our body, and which was let down from heaven by four corners (these are the four quarters of the world), showed that the whole world should believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:227
verses.text: Therefore in the number forty is restraint from the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:228
verses.text: This is the fulfilling of the Law: now the fulfilling of the Law is charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:229
verses.text: And therefore before the Pasch we fast forty days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:230
verses.text: For this time 			 before the Pasch is the sign of this our toilsome life, wherein, in toils, and cares, and continence, we fulfil the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:231
verses.text: But afterwards we celebrate the Pasch, that is, the days of the Lord's resurrection signifying our own resurrection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:232
verses.text: Therefore fifty days are celebrated; because the reward of the denarius is added to the forty, and it becomes fifty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:233
verses.text: Why is the reward a denarius? Have ye not read, how that they who were hired into the vineyard, whether at the first, or sixth, or the last 			 hour, could only receive the denarius? When to our righteousness shall be added its reward, we shall be in the number fifty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:234
verses.text: Yea, and then shall we have none other occupation, save to praise God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:235
verses.text: And therefore throughout those days we say, "Hallelujah".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:236
verses.text: For Halleluiah is the praise of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:237
verses.text: In this frail estate of mortality, in this fortieth number here, as though before the resurrection, let us groan in prayers, that we may sing praises then.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:238
verses.text: Now is the time of longing, then will be the time of embracing and 			 enjoying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:239
verses.text: Let us not faint in the time of forty, that we may joy in the time of fifty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:240
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:241
verses.text: Now who is he that fulfilleth the Law, but he that hath charity? Ask the Apostle, "Charity is the fulfilling of the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:242
verses.text: For all the Law is fulfilled in one word, in that which is written, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:243
verses.text: But the commandment of charity is twofold; "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:244
verses.text: This is the great commandment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:245
verses.text: The other is like it; Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:246
verses.text: They are the words of the Lord in the Gospel: "On these two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:247
verses.text: Without this twofold love the Law cannot be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:248
verses.text: As long as the Law is not fulfilled, there is infirmity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:249
verses.text: Therefore he had two short, who was infirm thirty and eight years.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:250
verses.text: What means, "had two short"? He did not fulfil these two commandments.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:251
verses.text: What doth it profit that the rest is fulfilled, if those are not fulfilled? Hast thou thirty-eight? If thou have not those two, the rest will profit thee nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:252
verses.text: Thou hast two short, without which the rest avail not, if thou 			 have not the two commandments which conduct unto salvation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:253
verses.text: "If I speak with the tongues of men and angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:254
verses.text: And if I know all mysteries, and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:255
verses.text: And if I distribute all my substance, and if I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:256
verses.text: They are the Apostle's words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:257
verses.text: All those things therefore which he mentioned are as it were the thirty-eight years; but because charity was not there, there was infirmity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:258
verses.text: From that infirmity who then shall make whole, but He who came to give charity? "A new commandment I give unto you, that ye love one another".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:259
verses.text: And because He came to give charity, and charity fulfilleth the Law, with good reason said He, "I came not to destroy the Law, but to fulfil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:260
verses.text: He cured the sick man, and told him to carry his couch, and go unto his house.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:261
verses.text: And so too He said to the sick of the palsy whom He cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:262
verses.text: What is it to carry our couch? The pleasure of our flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:263
verses.text: Where we lie in infirmity, is as it were our bed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:264
verses.text: But they who are cured master and carry it, are not by this flesh mastered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:265
verses.text: So then, thou whole one, master the frailness of thy flesh, that in the sign of the forty days' fast from this world, thou mayest fulfill the number forty, for that He hath made that sick man whole, "Who came not to destroy the Law, but to fulfil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:266
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:267
verses.text: Having heard this, direct your heart to Godward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:268
verses.text: Do not deceive yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:269
verses.text: Ask yourselves then when it is well with you in the world ; then ask yourselves, whether ye love the world, or whether ye love it not; learn to let it go before ye are let go yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:270
verses.text: What is to let it go? Not heartily to love it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:271
verses.text: Whilst there is yet something with thee which thou must one day lose, and either in life or death let it go, it cannot be with thee always; whilst I say it 			 is yet with thee, loosen thy love; be prepared for the will of God, hang upon God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:272
verses.text: Hold thee fast to Him, whom thou canst not lose against thy will, that if it chance thee to lose these temporal things, thou mayest say, "The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away, as it hath pleased the Lord, so is it done, blessed be the Name of the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:273
verses.text: But if it chance, and God so wills it, that the things thou hast be with thee even to the last: for thy detachment from this life thou receivest the denarius, the fifty, and the perfection of blessedness cometh to pass in thee, when thou shalt sing Hallelujah.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:274
verses.text: Having these things which I have now brought forward in your memory, may they avail to overthrowing your love of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:275
verses.text: Evil is its friendship, deceitful, it makes a man the enemy of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:276
verses.text: Soon, in one single 			 temptation, a man offendeth God, and becometh His enemy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:277
verses.text: Nay not then becometh His enemy; but is then discovered to have been His enemy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:278
verses.text: For when he was loving and praising Him, he was an enemy; but he neither knew it himself, nor did others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:279
verses.text: Temptation came, the pulse is touched, and the fever discovered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:280
verses.text: So then brethren, the love of the world, and the friendship of the world, make men the enemies of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:281
verses.text: And it does not make good what it promises, it is a liar, and deceiveth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:282
verses.text: Therefore men 			 never cease hoping in this world, and who attains to all he hopes for? But whereunto soever he attains, what he has attained to is forthwith disesteemed by him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:283
verses.text: Other things begin to be desired, other fond things are hoped for; and when they come, whatsoever it is that comes to thee, is disesteemed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:284
verses.text: Hold thee fast then to God, for He can never be of light esteem, for nothing is more beautiful than He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:285
verses.text: For for this cause are these things disesteemed, because they cannot stand, because they are 			 not what He is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:286
verses.text: For nought, O soul, sufficeth thee, save He who created thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:287
verses.text: Whatsoever else thou apprehendest is wretched; for He Alone can suffice thee who made thee after His Own likeness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:288
verses.text: Thus it was expressly said, "Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:289
verses.text: There only can there be security; and where security can be, there in a certain sort will be insatiable satiety.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 74:290
verses.text: For thou wilt neither be so satiated, as to wish to depart; nor will anything be wanting, as though thou couldest suffer want.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:2
verses.text: [CXXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:5
verses.text: 19 , "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father doing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:7
verses.text: The mysteries and secrets of the kingdom of God first seek for believing men, that they may make them understanding.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:8
verses.text: For faith is understanding's step; and understanding faith's attainment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:9
verses.text: This the Prophet expressly says to all who prematurely and in undue order look for understanding, and neglect faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:10
verses.text: For he says, "Unless ye believe, ye shall not understand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:11
verses.text: Faith itself then also hath a certain light of its own in the Scriptures, in Prophecy, in the Gospel, in the Lessons of the Apostles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:12
verses.text: For all these things which are read to us in this present time, are lights in a dark place, that we may be nourished up unto the day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:13
verses.text: The Apostle Peter says, "We have a more sure word of prophecy, whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day-star arise in your hearts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:14
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:15
verses.text: Ye see then, Brethren, how exceedingly unregulated and disordered in their haste are they who like immature conceptions seek an untimely birth before the birth; who say to us, "Why dost thou bid me believe what I do not see? Let me see something that I may believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:16
verses.text: Thou biddest me believe whilst yet I see not; I wish to see, and by seeing to believe, not by hearing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:17
verses.text: Let the Prophet speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:18
verses.text: "Unless ye believe, ye shall not understand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:19
verses.text: Thou wishest to ascend, 			 and dost forget the steps.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:20
verses.text: Surely, out of all order.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:21
verses.text: O man, if I could show thee already what thou mightest see, I should not exhort thee to believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:23
verses.text: Faith then, as it has been elsewhere defined, is "the firm support of those who hope, the evidence of things which are not seen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:24
verses.text: If they are not seen, how are they evidenced to be? What! Whence are these things which thou seest, but from That which thou seest not? To be sure thou dost see somewhat that thou mayest believe somewhat, and from that thou seest, mayest believe what thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:25
verses.text: Be not ungrateful to Him who hath made thee see, whereby thou mayest be able to believe what as yet thou canst not see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:26
verses.text: God hath given thee eyes in the body, reason in the heart; arouse the reason of the heart, 			 wake up the interior inhabitant of thine interior eyes, let it take to its windows, examine the creature of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:27
verses.text: For there is one within who sees by the eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:28
verses.text: For when thy thoughts within thee are on any other subject, and the inhabitant within is turned away, the things which are before thine eyes thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:29
verses.text: For to no purpose are the windows open, when he who looks through them is away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:30
verses.text: It is not then the eyes that see, but some one sees by the eyes; awake him, arouse him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:31
verses.text: For this hath 			 not been denied thee; God hath made thee a rational animal, set thee over the cattle, formed thee after His Own image.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:32
verses.text: Oughtest thou to use them as the cattle do; only to see what to add to thy belly, not to thy soul? Stir up, I say, the eye of reason, use thine eyes as a man should, consider the heaven and earth, the ornaments of the heaven, the fruitfulness of the earth, the flight of the birds, the swimming of the fish, the virtue of the seeds, the order of the seasons; consider the works, and seek for the Author; take a view of what thou seest, and seek Him whom thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:33
verses.text: Believe on Him whom thou seest not, because of these things which thou seest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:34
verses.text: And lest thou think that it is with mine own words that I have exhorted thee; hear the Apostle saying, "For the invisible things of God from the creation of the world are clearly seen by those things which are made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:35
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:36
verses.text: These things thou disregardedst, nor didst look upon them as a man, but as an irrational animal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:37
verses.text: The Prophet cried out to thee, and cried in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:38
verses.text: "Be ye not like to horse and mule, which have no understanding".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:39
verses.text: These things I say thou didst see, and disregard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:40
verses.text: God's daily miracles were disesteemed, not for their easiness, but their constant repetition.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:41
verses.text: For what is more difficult to understand than a man's birth, that one who was in existence should by dying depart into darkness, and that one who was not, by being born should come forth to light? What so marvellous, what so difficult to comprehend? But with God easy to be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:42
verses.text: Marvel at these things, awake; at His unusual works, thou canst wonder, are they greater than those which thou art accustomed to see? Men wondered that our Lord God Jesus Christ filled so many thousands with five loaves; and they do not wonder that through a few grains the whole earth is filled with crops.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:43
verses.text: When the water was made wine, men saw it, and were amazed; what else takes place with the rain along the root of the vine? He did the one, He does the other; the one that thou mayest be fed, the other that thou mayest wonder.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:44
verses.text: But both are wonderful, for both are the works of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:45
verses.text: Man sees unusual things, and wonders; whence is the man himself who wonders? where was he? whence came he forth? whence the fashion of his body? whence the distinction of his limbs? whence that beautiful form? from what 			 beginnings? what contemptible beginnings? And he wonders at other things, when he the wonderer is himself a great wonder.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:46
verses.text: Whence then are these things which thou seest but from Him whom thou seest not? But as I had begun to say, because these things were disesteemed by thee, He came Himself to do unusual things, that in these usual ones too thou mightest acknowledge thy Creator.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:47
verses.text: He came to Whom it is said, "Renew signs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:48
verses.text: To Whom it is said, "Show forth Thy marvellous mercies".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:49
verses.text: For dispensing them He ever was; He dispensed them, and no one marvelled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:50
verses.text: Therefore came He a Little one to the little, He came a Physician to the sick, who was able to come when He would, to return when He would, to do whatsoever He would, to judge as He would.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:51
verses.text: And this, His will, is very righteousness; yea what He willeth, I say, is very righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:52
verses.text: For that is not unrighteous which He willeth, nor can that be right which He willeth not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:53
verses.text: He came to raise the dead, men 			 marvelling that He restored a man to the light who was in light already, He who day by day bringeth forth to the light those who were not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:54
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:55
verses.text: These things He did, yet was He despised by the many, who considered not so much what great things He did, as how small He was; as though they said within themselves, "These are divine things, but He is a man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:56
verses.text: Two things then thou seest, divine works, and a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:57
verses.text: If divine works cannot be wrought but by God, take heed lest in This Man God lie concealed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:58
verses.text: Attend, I say, to what thou seest, believe what thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:59
verses.text: He hath not abandoned thee, who hath called thee 			 to believe; though He enjoin thee to believe that which thou canst not see: yet hath He not given thee up to see nothing whereby thou mayest be able to believe what thou dost not see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:60
verses.text: Is the creation itself a small sign, a small indication of the Creator? He also came, He did miracles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:61
verses.text: Thou couldest not see God, a man thou couldest; so God was made Man, that in One thou mightest have both what to see, and what to believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:62
verses.text: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was 			 with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:63
verses.text: Thus thou hearest, and as yet seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:64
verses.text: Lo, He comes, lo, He is born, lo, He comes forth of a woman, who made man and woman.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:65
verses.text: He who made man and woman was not made by man and woman.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:66
verses.text: For thou wouldest peradventure have been likely to despise Him for being born, the manner of His birth canst thou not despise; for He ever was before that He was born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:67
verses.text: Lo, I say, He took a Body, He was clothed in Flesh, He came forth from the womb.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:68
verses.text: Dost thou now see? seest thou now, I say? I ask as to the Flesh, but I point out as to That Flesh; something thou seest, and something thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:69
