verses.text: Lo, in this very Birth, there are at once two things, one which thou mayest see, and another thou mayest not see; but so that by this which thou seest, thou mayest believe that which thou seest not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:70
verses.text: Thou hadst begun to despise, because thou seest Him who was born; believe what thou dost not see, that He was born of a virgin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:71
verses.text: "How trifling a person," says one, "is he who was born!" But how great is He who was of a virgin born! And He who was born of a virgin brought thee a temporal miracle; He was not born of a father, of any man, I mean, His father, yet was He born of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:72
verses.text: But let it not seem impossible to thee, that He was born by His mother only, Who made man before father and mother.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:73
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:74
verses.text: He brought thee then a temporal miracle, that thou mayest seek and admire Him who is Eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:75
verses.text: For He "who came forth as a Bridegroom out of His chamber," that is, out of the virgin's womb, where the holy nuptials were celebrated of the Word and the Flesh: He brought, I say, a temporal miracle; but He is Himself eternal, He is coeternal with the Father, He it is, who "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:76
verses.text: He did for thee whereby thou mightest be cured, that thou mightest be able to see what thou didst not see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:77
verses.text: What thou despisest in Christ, is not yet the contemplation of him that is made whole, but the medicine of the sick.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:78
verses.text: Do not hasten to the vision of the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:79
verses.text: The Angels see, the Angels rejoice, the Angels feed Thereon and live; Whereon they feed faileth not, nor is their food minished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:80
verses.text: In the thrones of glory, in the regions of the heavens, in the parts which are above 			 the heavens, the Word is seen by the Angels, and is their Joy; is their Food, and endureth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:81
verses.text: But in order that man might eat Angel's Bread, the Lord of Angels became Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:82
verses.text: This is our Salvation, the Medicine of the infirm, the Food of the whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:84
verses.text: And He spake to men, and said what ye have now heard, "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:85
verses.text: Is there now any one, think we, that understandeth this? Is there any one, think we, in whom the eye-salve of the flesh hath now its effect to the discerning in any fashion the brightness of the Divinity? He hath spoken, let us speak too; He, because the Word; we, because of the Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:86
verses.text: And why speak we, howsoever we do it, of the Word? Because we were made by the Word after the likeness of the Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:87
verses.text: As far then as we are capable of, as far as we can be partakers of that 			 ineffableness, let us also speak, and let us not be contradicted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:88
verses.text: For our faith hath gone before, so that we may say, "I believed, therefore have I spoken".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:89
verses.text: I speak then that which I believe; whether or no I also see, or howsoever I see; He seeth rather; ye cannot see it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:90
verses.text: But when I shall have spoken, whether he who sees what I speak of, believe that I see too what I have spoken of, or whether he believe it not, what is that to me? Let him only really see, and let him believe what he will of me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:91
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:92
verses.text: "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:93
verses.text: Here rises up an error of the Arians; but it rises up that it may fall; because it is not humbled, that it may rise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:94
verses.text: What is it which hath set thee off? Thou wouldest say that the Son is less than the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:95
verses.text: For thou hast heard, "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:96
verses.text: From this thou wouldest have the Son called less; it is this I know, I know it is this hath set thee off; believe that He is not less, thou canst not as yet see it, believe, this is what I was saying a little while ago.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:97
verses.text: "But how," you will say, "am I to believe against His own words"? He saith Himself, "The Son 			 can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:98
verses.text: Attend too to that which follows; "For what things soever the Father doeth, the same also doeth the Son likewise;" He did not say, "such things," Beloved, consider a while, that ye cause not confusion to yourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:99
verses.text: There is need of a tranquil heart, a godly and devout faith, a religious earnest attention; attend, not to me the poor vessel, but to Him who putteth the bread in the vessel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:100
verses.text: Attend then a while.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:101
verses.text: For in all that I have said above in exhorting you to faith, that the mind imbued with faith may be capable of understanding, all that has been said has had a pleasing, glad, and easy sound, has cheered your minds, ye have followed it, ye have 			 understood what I said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:102
verses.text: But what I am now about to say I hope there are some who will understand; yet I fear that all will not understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:103
verses.text: And seeing that God hath by the lesson of the Gospel proposed to us a subject to speak upon, and we cannot avoid that which the Master hath proposed; I fear lest haply they who will not understand, who perhaps will be the greater number, should think that I have spoken to them in vain; but yet because of those who will understand, I do not speak in vain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:104
verses.text: Let 			 him who understandeth rejoice, let him who doth not understand bear it patiently; what he doth not understand, let him bear, and that he may understand, let him bear delay.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:105
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:106
verses.text: He doth not say then, "What things soever the Father doeth, such doeth the Son:" as if the Father doeth some things, and the Son others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:107
verses.text: For it did seem as though He had meant this when He said above, "The Son doeth nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:108
verses.text: Mark; He did not there either say, "But what He heareth the Father enjoin;" but, "what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:109
verses.text: If then we consult the carnal understanding, or sense rather, He hath 			 set before Him as it were two workmen, the Father and the Son, the Father working without seeing any, the Son working from seeing the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:110
verses.text: This is still a carnal view.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:111
verses.text: Nevertheless, in order to understand those things which are higher, let us not decline these lower and mean things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:112
verses.text: First, let us set something before our eyes in this way; let us suppose there are two workmen, father and son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:113
verses.text: The father has made a chest, which the son could not make, unless he saw the father making it: he keeps his mind on the 			 chest which the father has made, and makes another chest like it, not the same.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:114
verses.text: I put off for a while the words which follow, and now I ask the Arian; "Dost thou understand it in the sense of this supposition? Hath the Father done something, which when the Son saw Him do, He too hath done something like it? For do the words by which thou art perplexed seem to have this meaning?" Now He doth not say, "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He heareth the Father enjoin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:115
verses.text: But He 			 saith, "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:116
verses.text: See, if thou understand it thus; the Father hath done something, and the Son attendeth that He may see what He Himself too hath to do; and that, some other thing like that which the Father had done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:117
verses.text: This which the Father hath done, by whom hath He done it? If not by the Son, if not by the Word, thou hast incurred the charge of blasphemy against the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:118
verses.text: "For all things were made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:119
verses.text: So then what the Father had done, He had done by the Word; if by the Word He had done it, He had done it by the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:120
verses.text: Who then is that other who attends, that He may do some other thing which he seeth the Father do? Ye have not been wont to say that the Father hath two sons: there is One, One Only-Begotten of Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:121
verses.text: But through His mercy, Alone as regards His Divinity and not Alone as regards the inheritance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:122
verses.text: The Father hath made coheirs with His Only Son; not begotten them like 			 Him of His Own Substance, but adopted them by Him out of His Own family.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:123
verses.text: For "we have been called," as Holy Scripture testifieth, "into the adoption of sons".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:124
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:125
verses.text: What then sayest thou? It is the Only Son Himself That speaketh; the Only-Begotten Son speaketh in the Gospel: the Word Himself hath given us the words, we have heard Himself saying, "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:126
verses.text: Now then the Father doeth that the Son may see what to do; and nevertheless the Father doeth nothing but by the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:127
verses.text: Assuredly thou art confused, thou heretic, assuredly thou art confused; but thy confusion is 			 as from taking hellebore, that thou mayest be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:128
verses.text: Even now thou canst not find thine own self, thou dost even thyself condemn thine own judgment and thy carnal view, I think.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:129
verses.text: Put behind thee the eyes of the flesh, raise up what eyes thou hast in thine heart, behold things divine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:130
verses.text: They are men's words it is true thou hearest, and by a man, by the Evangelist, by the Gospel thou hearest men's words, as a man; but it is of the Word of God thou hearest, that thou mayest hear what is human, 			 come to know what is Divine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:131
verses.text: The Master hath given trouble, that He might instruct; hath sown a difficulty, that He might excite an earnest attention.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:132
verses.text: "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:133
verses.text: It might follow that He should say, "For what things soever the Father doeth, the like doeth the Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:134
verses.text: This He doth not say; but, "What things soever the Father doeth, the same doeth the Son likewise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:135
verses.text: The Father doeth not some things, the Son other things; because all things that the Father doeth, He doeth by the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:136
verses.text: The Son raised Lazarus; did not the Father raise him? The Son gave sight to the blind man; did not the Father give him sight? The Father by the Son in the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:137
verses.text: It is the Trinity; but the Operation of the Trinity is One, the Majesty One, the Eternity One, the Coeternity One, and the Works the Same.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:138
verses.text: The Father doth not create some men, the Son others, the Holy Ghost others; the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost create one and the same man; and the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost, One God, createth him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:139
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:140
verses.text: You observe a Plurality of Persons, but acknowledge the Unity of the Divinity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:141
verses.text: For because of the Plurality of Persons it was said, "Let Us make man after Our image and likeness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:142
verses.text: He did not say, "I will make man, and do Thou attend when I am making him, that Thou too mayest be able to make another".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:143
verses.text: "Let Us make," He saith; I hear the Plurality; "after Our image;" again I hear the Plurality.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:144
verses.text: Where then is the Singularity of the Divinity? Read what follows, "And God made man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:145
verses.text: It is said, "Let Us make man;" and it is not said, "The Gods made man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:146
verses.text: The Unity is understood in that it was said, "God made man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:147
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:148
verses.text: Where then is that carnal view? Be it confounded, hidden, brought to nought; let the Word of God speak to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:149
verses.text: Even now as godly men, as believing already, as already imbued with faith, and having gotten some attainment of understanding, turn we to the Word Himself, to the Fountain of light, and let us say together, "O Lord, the Father doeth ever the same things as Thou; for that whatsoever the Father doeth, by Thee He doeth it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:150
verses.text: We have heard that Thou art the Word in the beginning; we have not seen, but believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:151
verses.text: There too have we heard what follows, that 'all things were made by Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:152
verses.text: ' All things then that the Father doeth, He doeth by Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:153
verses.text: Therefore Thou doest the same things as the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:154
verses.text: Why then didst Thou wish to say, 'The Son can do nothing of Himself'? For I see a certain equality in Thee with the Father, in that I hear, 'What things soever the Father doeth, the same doeth the Son;' I recognise an equality, hereby I understand, and comprehend as far as I am able, 'I and My Father are One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:155
verses.text: ' What meaneth it, that Thou canst do nothing, but what Thou seest the Father do? What meaneth this?"  13.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:156
verses.text: Peradventure He would say to me, yea say to us all: "Now as to this that I have said, 'The Son can do nothing, but what He seeth the Father do;' My 'Seeing' how dost thou understand? My 'Seeing,' what is it? Put aside for a while the form of the servant which He took for thy sake.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:157
verses.text: For in that servant's form our Lord had eyes and ears in the Flesh, and that human form was the same figure of a Body, such as we bear, the same outlines of members.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:158
verses.text: That Flesh had come from Adam: but He was not as Adam.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:159
verses.text: So then the Lord walking whether on the earth or in the sea, as it pleased Him, as He would, for whatever He would, He could; looked at what He would; He fixed His eyes, He saw; He turned away His eyes, and did not see; who followed was behind Him, whoso could be seen, before Him; with the eyes of His Body, He saw only what was before Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:160
verses.text: But from His Divinity nothing was hid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:161
verses.text: Put aside, put aside, I say, for a while the form of the 			 servant, look at the Form of God in which He was before the world was made; in which He was equal to the Father; hereby receive and understand what He saith to thee, 'Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:162
verses.text: ' There see Him if thou canst, that thou mayest be able to see what His 'Seeing' is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:163
verses.text: "In the beginning was the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:164
verses.text: How doth the Word see? Hath the Word eyes, or are our eyes found in Him, the eyes not of the flesh, but the eyes of godly hearts? For, "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:165
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:166
verses.text: Christ thou seest Man and God; He doth manifest to thee the Man, God He reserveth for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:167
verses.text: Now see how He reserveth God for thee, who doth manifest Himself to thee as Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:168
verses.text: "Whoso loveth Me," saith He, "keepeth My commandments; whoso loveth Me shall be loved of My Father, and I will love him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:169
verses.text: And as if it were asked, "What wilt Thou give to him whom Thou lovest?" "And I will manifest Myself," saith He, "to him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:170
verses.text: What meaneth this, Brethren? He whom they saw already, promised that He would manifest Himself to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:171
verses.text: To whom? Those by whom He was seen, or those also by whom He was not seen? Thus speaking to a certain Apostle, who asked to see the Father, that it might suffice him, and said, "Show us the Father, and it sufficeth us" 			 —Then He standing before this servant's eyes, in the form of a servant, reserving for his eyes when deified the Form of God, saith to him, "Have I been so long time with you, and have ye not known Me? He that seeth Me, seeth the Father also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:172
verses.text: Thou askest to see the Father; see Me, thou seest Me, and dost not see Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:173
verses.text: Thou seest what for thee I have assumed, thou dost not see What I have reserved for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:174
verses.text: Give ear to My commandments, purify thine eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:175
verses.text: "For whoso loveth Me, keepeth My commandments, and I will love him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:176
verses.text: To him as keeping My commandments, 			 and by My commandments made whole will I manifest Myself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:177
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:178
verses.text: If then, Brethren, we are not able to see what the "Seeing" of the Word is, whither are we going? what Vision it may be with too great haste are we requiring? why are we wishing to have shown us what we are not able to see? These things accordingly are spoken of which we desire to see, not as what we are able already to comprehend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:179
verses.text: For if thou seest the "Seeing" of the Word, peradventure in that thou seest the "Seeing" of the Word, thou wilt see the 			 Word Himself; that the Word may not be one thing, the "Seeing" of the Word another, lest there be Therein anything joined, and coupled, and double, and compacted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:180
verses.text: For It is something Simple, of a Simplicity ineffable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:181
verses.text: Not as with a man, the man is one thing, the man's seeing another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:182
verses.text: For sometimes a man's seeing is extinguished, and the man remains.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:183
verses.text: This it is of which I said that I was about to say something which all would not be able to understand; the Lord even grant that some may 			 have understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:184
verses.text: My Brethren, to this end doth He exhort us, that we may see, that the "Seeing" of the Word is beyond our powers; for they are small; be they nourished, perfected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:185
verses.text: Whereby? By the commandments.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:186
verses.text: What commandments? "He that loveth Me, keepeth My commandments".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:187
verses.text: What commandments? For already do we wish to increase, to be strengthened, perfected, that we may see the "Seeing" of the Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:188
verses.text: Tell us, Lord, now what commandments? "A new commandment I give unto you, that ye love one another".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:189
verses.text: This charity then, Brethren, let us draw from the plentifulness of the Fountain, let us receive it; be nourished by it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:190
verses.text: Receive thou that whereby thou mayest be able to receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:191
verses.text: Let charity give thee birth, let charity nourish thee; charity bring thee to perfection, charity strengthen thee; that thou mayest see this "Seeing" of the Word, that the Word is not one thing and His "Seeing" another, but that the "Seeing" of the Word is the Very Word Himself; and so perhaps thou wilt soon understand that that which is said, "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do," is as 			 if He had said, "The Son would not be, if He had not been born of the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 75:192
verses.text: Let this suffice, Brethren; I know that I have said that which perhaps, if meditated upon, may develop itself to many, which oftentimes when expressed in words may chance to be obscured.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:2
verses.text: [CXXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:5
verses.text: 25 ,"Verily, verily, I say unto you, the hour cometh, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the son of God; and they that hear shall live,"etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:6
verses.text: ; and on the words of the apostle, "things which eye saw not," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:7
verses.text: , 1 Cor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:8
verses.text: ii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:9
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:10
verses.text: Our hope, Brethren, is not of this present time, nor of this world, nor in that happiness whereby men are blinded that forget God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:11
verses.text: This ought we above all things to know, and in a Christian heart hold fast, that we were not made Christians for the good things of the present time, but for something else which God at once promiseth, and man doth not yet comprehend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:12
verses.text: For of this good it is said, "That eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, 			 neither hath it entered into the heart of man, what things God hath prepared for them that love Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:13
verses.text: Because then this good, so great, so excellent, so ineffable, fell not in with man's understanding, it required God's promise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:14
verses.text: For what hath been promised him, man blind of heart doth not now comprehend; nor can it be shown to him at present, what he will one day be to whom the promise is given.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:15
verses.text: For so an infant child, if he could understand the words of one speaking, when himself could neither speak, nor walk, nor do anything, but feeble as we see he is, unable to stand, 			  requiring the assistance of others, were able only to understand him who should speak to him and tell him, "Lo, as thou seest me walking, working, speaking, after a few years thou shall be as I am;" as he considered himself and the other, though he would see what was promised; yet considering his own feebleness, would not believe, and yet he would see what was promised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:16
verses.text: But with us infants, as it were, lying in this flesh and feebleness, that which is promised is at once 			 great and is not seen; and so faith is aroused whereby we believe that we do not see that we may attain to see what we believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:17
verses.text: Whosoever derideth this faith, so as to think that he is not to believe in that he doth not see; when that shall come which he believed not, is put to shame: being confounded is separated, being separated, is condemned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:18
verses.text: But whoso shall have believed, is put aside at the right hand, and shall stand with great confidence and joy among those to whom it shall be said, "Come, blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom which hath been prepared for you from 			 the beginning of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:19
verses.text: But the Lord made an end when He spake these words, thus, "These shall go into everlasting burning, but the righteous into life eternal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:20
verses.text: This is the life eternal which is promised us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:21
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:22
verses.text: Because men love to live on this earth, life is promised them; and because they exceedingly fear to die, eternal life is promised them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:23
verses.text: What dost thou love? To live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:24
verses.text: This shalt thou have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:25
verses.text: What dost thou fear? To die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:26
verses.text: Thou shalt not suffer it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:27
verses.text: This seemed to be enough for human infirmity, that it should be said, "Thou shalt have eternal life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:28
verses.text: This the mind of man can comprehend, by its present condition it can in some sort comprehend what is to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:29
verses.text: But by the 			 imperfection of its present condition how far can it comprehend it? Because he lives, and does not wish to die; he loves eternal life, he wishes to live always, never to die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:30
verses.text: But they who shall be tormented in punishments, have even a wish to die, and cannot.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:31
verses.text: It is no great thing then to live long, or to live for ever; but to live blessedly is a great thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:32
verses.text: Let us love eternal life, and hereby may we know how greatly we ought to labour for eternal life, when we see men who love the present 			 life, which lasts but for a time and must be brought to an end, labour so for it, that when the fear of death comes, they will do whatever they can, not to put away, but to put off death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:33
verses.text: How does a man labour, when death threatens, by flight, by concealment, by giving all he has, and redeeming himself, by toil, by endurance of torments and uneasinesses, by calling in physicians, and whatever else a man can do? See, how that after exhausting all his labour and his means, he is but able to 			 contrive to live a little longer; to live always, he is not able.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:34
verses.text: If then men strive with so great labour, with so great efforts, so great a cost, such earnestness, such watchfulness, such carefulness, that they may live a little longer; how should they strive that they may live for ever? And if they are called wise, who by all means strive to put off death, and live a few days, that they lose not a few days: how foolish are they who so live as to lose the day eternal!  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:35
verses.text: This then only can be promised us, that this gift of God may in whatever measure be sweet to us, from this which we have at present; seeing that it is of His gift we have it, that we live, that we are in health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:36
verses.text: When then eternal life is promised, let us set before our eyes a life of such a kind, as to remove from it everything unpleasant which we suffer here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:37
verses.text: For it is easier for us to find what is not there, than what is there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:38
verses.text: Lo, here we live; we shall live there 			 also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:39
verses.text: Here we are in health when we are not sick, and there is no pain in the body; there we shall be in health also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:40
verses.text: And when it is well with us in this life, we suffer no scourge; we shall suffer none there also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:41
verses.text: Suppose then a man here below living, in sound health, suffering no scourge; if any one were to grant him that he should be for ever so, and that this good estate should never cease, how greatly would he rejoice? how greatly be transported? how would he not contain himself in joy 			 without pain, without torment, without end of life? If God had promised us this only, which I have mentioned, which I have just now in such words as I was able, described and set forth; at what a price ought it to be purchased if it were to be sold, how great a sum ought to be given to buy it? Would all that thou hadst suffice, even though thou shouldest possess the whole world? And yet it is to be sold; buy it if thou wilt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:42
verses.text: And be not much disquieted for a thing so great, because of the 			 largeness of the price.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:43
verses.text: Its price is no more than what thou hast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:44
verses.text: Now to procure any great and precious thing, thou wouldest get ready gold, or silver, or money, or any increase of cattle, or fruits, which might be produced in thy possessions, to buy this I know not what great and excellent thing, whereby to live in this earth happily.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:45
verses.text: Buy this too, if thou wilt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:46
verses.text: Do not look for what thou hast, but for what thou art.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:47
verses.text: The price of this thing is thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:48
verses.text: Its price is what thou art thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:49
verses.text: Give 			 thine own self, and thou shalt have it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:50
verses.text: Why art thou troubled? why disquieted? What? Art thou going to seek for thine own self, or to buy thyself? Lo, give thine own self as thou art, such as thou art to that thing, and thou shalt have it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:51
verses.text: But you will say, "I am wicked, and perhaps it will not accept me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:52
verses.text: By giving thyself to it, thou wilt be good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:53
verses.text: The giving thyself to this faith and promise, this is to be good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:54
verses.text: And when thou shalt be good, thou wilt be the price of this thing; and shalt 			 have, not only what I have mentioned, health, safety, life, and life without end; thou shalt not only have this, I will take away other things yet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:55
verses.text: There shall there be no weariness, and sleeping; there shall there be no hunger, and thirst; there shall there be no growing, and growing old; because there shall be no birth either where the numbers remain entire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:56
verses.text: The number that is there is entire; nor is there any need for it to be increased, seeing there is no chance of diminution there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:57
verses.text: Lo, how 			 many things have I taken away, and I have not yet said what shall be there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:58
verses.text: Lo, already there is life, and safety; no scourge, no hunger, no thirst, no failing, none of these; and yet I have not said, "what eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, nor hath ascended into the heart of man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:59
verses.text: For if I have said it, it is false that is written, "Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither hath it ascended into the heart of man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:60
verses.text: For whence should it ascend into my heart, that I should say "that 			 which hath not ascended into the heart of man"? It is believed, and not seen; not only not seen, but not even expressed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:61
verses.text: How then is it believed, if it is not expressed? Who believes what he doth not hear? But if he hear it that he may believe, it is expressed; if expressed, it is thought of; if thought of and expressed, then it entereth into the ears of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:62
verses.text: And because it would not be expressed if it were not thought of, it hath ascended also into the heart of man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:63
verses.text: Lo, already 			 the mere proposing of so great a thing disturbs us, that we cannot put it forth clearly in words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:64
verses.text: Who then can explain the thing itself?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:65
verses.text: Let us attend to the Gospel; just now the Lord was speaking, and let us do what He said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:66
verses.text: "He that believeth in Me," saith He, "passeth from death unto life, and cometh not into judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:67
verses.text: Verily I say unto you, that the hour shall come, and now is, when the dead shall hear the Voice of the Son of God, and they that hear shall live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:68
verses.text: For as the Father hath life in Himself, so hath He given to the Son to have life in Himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:69
verses.text: By begetting Him He gave it; in that He begat, He gave it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:70
verses.text: For the Son is of the Father, not the Father of the Son; but the Father is the Father of the Son, and the Son is the Son of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:71
verses.text: I say the Son is begotten of the Father, not the Father of the Son; and the Son was always, always therefore begotten.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:72
verses.text: Who can comprehend this "always begotten"? For when any man hears of one begotten, it occurs to him; "Therefore there was a time, when he who was begotten was 			 not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:73
verses.text: What say we then? Not so; there was no time before the Son, for that "all things were made by Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:74
verses.text: If all things were made by Him, times also were made by Him; how could times be before the Son, by whom times were made? Take away then all times, the Son was with the Father always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:75
verses.text: If the Son were with the Father always, and yet the Son, He was begotten always; if begotten always, He who was begotten was always with Him That begat Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:76
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:77
verses.text: You will say, "This have I never seen, one begetting, and always with him whom he begat; but he that begat came first, and he that was begotten followed in time".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:78
verses.text: You say well, "I have never seen this;" for this appertains to "that which eye hath not seen".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:79
verses.text: Do you ask how it may be expressed? It cannot be expressed; "For the ear hath not heard, neither hath it ascended unto the heart of man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:80
verses.text: Be it believed and adored, when we believe, we adore; 			 when we adore, we grow; when we grow, we comprehend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:81
verses.text: For as yet whilst we are in this flesh, as long as we are absent from the Lord, we are, with respect to the Holy Angels who see these things, infants to be suckled by faith, hereafter to be fed by sight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:82
verses.text: For so saith the Apostle, "As long as we are in the body we are absent from the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:83
verses.text: For we walk by faith, not by sight".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:84
verses.text: We shall some day come to sight, which is thus promised us by John in his Epistle; "Dearly beloved, we are the sons of God, and it hath not yet appeared what we shall be".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:85
verses.text: We are the sons of God now by grace, by faith, by the Sacrament, by the Blood of Christ, by the redemption of the Saviour; "We are the sons of God, and it hath not yet appeared what we shall be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:86
verses.text: We know that when He shall appear, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:87
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:88
verses.text: Lo, unto the comprehending of what are we being nourished up; lo, unto the embracing and the feeding on what are we being nourished up; yet so as that that which is fed on is not diminished, and he that feedeth is supported.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:89
verses.text: For now food supports us by eating it; but the food which is eaten, is diminished; but when we shall begin to feed on Righteousness, to feed on Wisdom, to feed on that Food Immortal, we are at once supported, and That Food is not diminished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:90
verses.text: For if the eye knows how to feed on light, and yet doth not diminish the light; for the light will be no less because it is seen by more; it feeds the eyes of more, and yet is as great as it was before: both they are fed, and it is not diminished; if God hath granted this to the light which He hath made for the eyes of the flesh, what is He Himself, the Light for the eyes of the heart? If then any choice food were praised to thee, on which thou wast to dine, thou wouldest prepare the stomach; God is praised to thee, prepare the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:91
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:92
verses.text: Behold what thy Lord saith to thee: "The hour shall come," saith He, "and now is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:93
verses.text: "The hour shall come," yea, that very hour, "now is, when"—what? "when the dead shall hear the Voice of the Son of God, and they that shall hear shall live".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:94
verses.text: They then that shall not hear, shall not live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:95
verses.text: What is, "They that shall hear"? They that shall obey.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:96
verses.text: What is, "They that shall hear"? They that shall believe and obey, they shall live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:97
verses.text: So then 			 before they believed and obeyed, they lay dead; they walked, and were dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:98
verses.text: What availed it to them, that they walked, being dead? And yet if any among them were to die a bodily death, they would run, get ready the grave, wrap him up, carry him out, bury him, the dead, the dead; of whom it is said, "Let the dead bury their dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:99
verses.text: Such dead as these are in such wise raised by the Word of God, as to live in faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:100
verses.text: They who were dead in unbelief, are aroused by the Word.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:101
verses.text: Of this hour said the Lord, "The hour shall come, and now is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:102
verses.text: For with His Own Word did He raise them that were dead in unbelief; of whom the Apostle says, "Arise thou that sleepest, and rise up from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:103
verses.text: This is the resurrection of hearts, this is the resurrection of the inner man, this is the resurrection of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:104
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:105
verses.text: But this is not the only resurrection, there remains a resurrection of the body also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:106
verses.text: Whoso riseth again in soul, riseth again in body to his blessedness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:107
verses.text: For in soul all do not rise again; in body all are to rise again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:108
verses.text: In soul, I say, all do not rise again; but they that believe and, obey; for, "They that shall hear shall live".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:109
verses.text: But as the Apostle says, "All men have not faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:110
verses.text: If then all men have not faith, all men do not rise again in soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:111
verses.text: When thy hour of the resurrection of the body shall come, all shall rise again; be they good or bad, all shall rise again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:112
verses.text: But whoso first riseth again in soul, to his blessedness riseth again in body; whoso doth not first rise again in soul, riseth again in body to his curse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:113
verses.text: Whoso riseth again in soul, riseth again in body unto life; whoso riseth not again in soul, riseth again in body unto punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:114
verses.text: Seeing 			 then that the Lord hath impressed upon us this resurrection of souls, unto which we ought all to hasten, and to labour that we may live therein, and living persevere even unto the end, it remained for Him to impress upon us the resurrection of bodies also, which is to be at the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:115
verses.text: Now hear how He hath impressed this too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:116
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:117
verses.text: When He had said, "Verily I say unto you, The hour shall come, and now is, when the dead," that is, the unbelievers, "shall hear the Voice of the Son of God," that is, the Gospel, "and they that shall hear," that is, that shall obey, "shall live," that is, shall be justified, and shall be unbelievers no longer; when, I say, He had said this, forasmuch as He saw that we had need to be instructed as to the resurrection of the flesh also, and were 			 not to be left thus, He went on and said, "For as the Father hath life in Himself, so hath He given to the Son to have life in Himself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:118
verses.text: This refers to the resurrection of souls, to the quickening of souls.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:119
verses.text: Then He added, "And hath given Him power to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:120
verses.text: This Son of God, is Son of Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:121
verses.text: For if the Son of God had continued the Son of God, and had not been made the Son of Man, He would not have delivered the sons of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:122
verses.text: He who had made 			 man, was Himself made that which He made, that what He made might not perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:123
verses.text: But He was in such wise made the Son of Man, as to continue the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:124
verses.text: For He was made Man by assuming that which He was not, not by losing That which He was; continuing God, He was made Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:125
verses.text: He took thee, He was not consumed in thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:126
verses.text: As such then came He to us, the Son of God, and Son of Man, the Maker and the Made, the Creator and the Created; the Creator of His mother, Created of His mother; such came He to 			 us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:127
verses.text: In respect of His being the Son of God, He saith, "The hour shall come, and now is, when the dead shall hear the Voice of the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:128
verses.text: He did not say, "Of the Son of Man;" for He was impressing the truth, wherein He is equal to the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:129
verses.text: "And they that shall hear shall live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:130
verses.text: For as the Father hath life in Himself, so hath He given to the Son to have life in Himself;" not by participation, but in our God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:131
verses.text: But He, the Father, hath life in Himself; and He begat such a Son as 			 should have life in Himself; not be made a partaker of life, but Himself be Life, of which life we should be partakers; that is, should have life in Himself, and Himself be Life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:132
verses.text: But that He should be made the Son of Man, He took from us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:133
verses.text: Son of God in Himself; that He should be the Son of Man, He took from us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:134
verses.text: Son of God of That which is His Own, Son of Man of ours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:135
verses.text: That which is the less, took He from us; That which is the more, gave He to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:136
verses.text: For thus He died in that He is the Son of Man, 			 not in that He is the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:137
verses.text: Yet the Son of God died; but He died in respect to the flesh, not in respect to "the Word which was made flesh, and dwelt among us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:138
verses.text: So then in that He died, He died of that which was ours; in that we live, we live of That which is His.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:139
verses.text: He could not die of That which was His own, nor could we live of that which is our own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:140
verses.text: As God then, as the Only-Begotten, as equal with Him who begat Him, did the Lord Jesus impress this upon us, that if we hear, we shall live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:141
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:142
verses.text: But, saith He, "He hath given Him power to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:143
verses.text: So then that Form is to come to judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:144
verses.text: The Form of Man is to come to judgment; therefore He said, "He hath given Him power to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:145
verses.text: The Judge here shall be the Son of Man; here shall That Form judge which was judged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:146
verses.text: Hear and understand: the Prophet had said this already, "They shall look on Him whom they 			 pierced".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:147
verses.text: That Very Form shall they see which they smote with a spear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:148
verses.text: He shall sit as Judge, Who stood at the judge's seat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:149
verses.text: He shall condemn the real criminals, Who was made a criminal falsely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:150
verses.text: He shall come Himself, That Form shall come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:151
verses.text: This you find in the Gospel too; when before the eyes of His disciples He was going into heaven, they stood and looked on, and the Angelic voice spake, "Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:152
verses.text: "This Jesus shall come in 			 like manner as ye see Him going into heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:153
verses.text: What is, "shall come in like manner"? Shall come in this Very Form.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:154
verses.text: For "He hath given Him power to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:155
verses.text: Now see on what principle this was behoveful and right, that they who were to be judged might see the Judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:156
verses.text: For they who were to be judged were both good and bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:157
verses.text: "But blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:158
verses.text: It remained that in the Judgment the Form of the servant should be manifested both to good and bad, the Form of God be reserved for the good alone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:159
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:160
verses.text: For what is it that the good are to receive? Behold I am now expressing that which I did not express a little above; and yet in expressing I do not express it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:161
verses.text: For I said that there we shall be in sound health, shall be safe, shall be living, shall be without scourges, without hunger and thirst, without failing, without loss of our eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:162
verses.text: All this I said; but what we shall have more, I said not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:163
verses.text: We shall see God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:164
verses.text: Now this will be so great, yea so great a thing 			 will it be, that in comparison of it, all the rest is nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:165
verses.text: I said that we shall be living, that we shall be safe and sound, that we shall suffer no hunger and thirst, that we shall not fall into weariness, that sleep will not oppress us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:166
verses.text: All this, what is it to that happiness, whereby we shall see God? Because then God cannot be now manifested as He is, whom nevertheless we shall see; therefore, "what eye hath not seen, nor ear heard," this the good shall see, this shall the godly see, this the merciful shall see, this shall the faithful see, this shall they see who shall have a good lot in the resurrection of the body, for that they have had a good obedience in the resurrection of the heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:167
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:168
verses.text: Shall then the wicked man see God too? of whom Isaiah saith, "Let the ungodly be taken away, that he see not the Glory of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:169
verses.text: Both the ungodly and the godly then shall see that Form; and when the sentence, "Let the ungodly be taken away that he see not the Glory of God," shall have been pronounced; it remains that as to the godly and the good, that be fulfilled which the Lord Himself promised, when He was here in the flesh, and seen not by the good only, but by the evil also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:170
verses.text: He spake amongst the good and evil, and was seen of all, as God, hidden, as Man, manifested; as God ruling men, as Man 			 appearing among men: He spake, I say, among them, and said, "Whoso loveth Me, keepeth My commandments; and he that loveth Me, shall be loved of My Father, and I will love him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:171
verses.text: And as if it were said to Him, And what wilt Thou give him? And "I will," He saith, "manifest Myself to him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:172
verses.text: When did He say this? When He was seen by men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:173
verses.text: When did He say this? When He was seen even by them, by whom He was not loved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:174
verses.text: How then was He to manifest Himself to them that loved Him, save in Such a Form, as they who loved Him then saw not? Therefore, seeing that the Form of God was being reserved, the Form of man manifested; by the Form of man, speaking to 			 men, conspicuous and visible, He manifested Himself to all, both good and bad, He reserved Himself for them that loved Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:175
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:176
verses.text: When is He to manifest Himself to them that love Him? After the resurrection of the body, when "the ungodly shall be taken away that he see not the Glory of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:177
verses.text: For then "when He shall appear, we shall be like Him; for we shall see Him as He is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:178
verses.text: This is life eternal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:179
verses.text: For all that we said before is nothing to that life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:180
verses.text: That we live, what is it? That we are in health, what is it? That we shall see God, is a great thing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:181
verses.text: This is life eternal; this Himself hath said, "But this is life eternal, that they may know Thee the Only True God, and Jesus Christ whom Thou hast sent".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:182
verses.text: This is life eternal, that they may know, see, comprehend, acquaint themselves with what they had believed, may perceive that which they were not yet able to comprehend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:183
verses.text: Then may the mind see what "eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither hath it ascended into the heart of man;" this shall be said to them at the end, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom which hath been prepared for you from the beginning of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:184
verses.text: Those wicked ones then shall go into everlasting burning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:185
verses.text: But the righteous, whither? Into life eternal? What is life eternal? "This is life eternal, that they may know Thee, the Only True God, and Jesus Christ, whom Thou hast sent".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:186
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:187
verses.text: Speaking then of the future resurrection of the body, and not leaving us thus, He saith, "He hath given Him power to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:188
verses.text: Marvel not at this, for the hour shall come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:189
verses.text: He did not add in this place, "and now is;" because this hour shall be hereafter, because this hour shall be at the end of the world, because this shall be the last hour, shall be at the last trump.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:190
verses.text: "Marvel not at this," because I have said, 			 "He hath given Him power to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:191
verses.text: Marvel not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:192
verses.text: For this reason have I said this, because it behoves Him as Man to be judged by men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:193
verses.text: And what men shall He judge? Those whom He finds alive? Not only those, but what? "The hour shall come, when they that are in the graves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:194
verses.text: How did He express those that are dead in the flesh? "They who are in the graves," whose corpses lie buried, whose ashes are covered up, whose bones are dispersed, whose flesh is flesh no more, and yet is entire to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:195
verses.text: "The hour shall come, when all that are in the graves shall hear His Voice, and shall come forth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:196
verses.text: Be they good or bad, they shall hear the Voice, and shall come forth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:197
verses.text: All the bands of the grave shall be burst asunder; all that was lost, yea rather was thought to be lost shall be restored.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:198
verses.text: For if God made man who was not, can He not re-fashion that which was?  15.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:199
verses.text: I suppose when it is said, "God shall raise the dead again," no incredible thing is said for it is of God, not of man, that it is said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:200
verses.text: It is a great thing which shall be done, yea, an incredible thing that shall be done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:201
verses.text: But let it not be incredible, for see, who It is That doeth it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:202
verses.text: He it is said shall raise thee, Who created thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:203
verses.text: Thou wast not, and thou art; and once made, shalt thou not be? God forbid thou shouldest think so! God did something more 			 marvellous when He made that which was not; and nevertheless He did make that which was not; and shall it be disbelieved that He is able to re-fashion that which was, by those very persons whom He made what they were not? Is this the return we make to God, we who were not, and were made? Is this the return we make Him, that we will not believe that He is able to raise again what He hath made? Is this the return which His creature renders Him? "Have I therefore," God saith to thee, "made 			 thee, O man, before thou wast, that thou shouldest not believe Me, that thou shalt be what thou wast, who hast been able to be what thou wast not?" But you will say, "Lo, what I see in the tomb, is dust, ashes, bones; and shall this receive life again, skin, substance, flesh, and rise again? what? these ashes, these bones, which I see in the tomb?" Well.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:204
verses.text: At least thou seest ashes, thou seest bones in the tomb; in thy mother's womb there was nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:205
verses.text: This thou seest, ashes at least there 			 are, and bones; before that thou wast, there was neither ashes, nor bones; and yet thou wast made, when thou wast not at all; and dost thou not believe that these bones (for in whatever state, of whatever kind they are, yet they are), shall receive the form again which they had, when thou hast received what thou hadst not? Believe; for if thou shalt believe this, then shall thy soul be raised up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:206
verses.text: And thy soul shall be raised up "now;" "The hour shall come, and now is;" then to thy 			 blessing shall thy flesh rise again, "when the hour shall come, that all that are in the graves shall hear His Voice, and shall come forth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:207
verses.text: For thou must not at once rejoice, because thou dost hear "and come forth;" hear what follows, "They that have done good unto the resurrection of life; but they that have done evil unto the resurrection of damnation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 76:208
verses.text: Turning to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:2
verses.text: [CXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:5
verses.text: 31 ,"If I bear witness of myself," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:6
verses.text: ; and on the words of the apostle, Galatians v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:7
verses.text: 16 , "Walk by the spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:8
verses.text: For the flesh lusteth," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:9
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:10
verses.text: We have heard the words of the holy Gospel; and this that the Lord Jesus saith, "If I bear witness of Myself, My witness is not true," may perplex some.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:11
verses.text: How then is not the witness of the Truth true? Is it not Himself who hath said, "I am the Way, and the Truth, and the Life"? Whom then are we to believe, if we must not believe the Truth? For of a surety he is minded to believe nothing but falsehood, who does not choose to believe the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:12
verses.text: So then this was spoken on their principles, that you should understand it thus, and gather this meaning from these words; "If I bear witness of Myself, My witness is not true," that is, as ye think.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:13
verses.text: For He knew well that His Own witness of Himself was true; but for the sake of the weak, and hard of belief, 			 and without understanding, the Sun looked out for lamps.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:14
verses.text: For their weakness of sight could not bear the dazzling brightness of the Sun.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:15
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:16
verses.text: Therefore was John sought for to bear witness to the Truth; and ye have heard what He said; "Ye came unto John; he was a burning and a shining lamp, and ye were willing for a season to rejoice in his light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:17
verses.text: This lamp was prepared for their confusion, for of this was it said so long time before in the Psalms, "I have prepared a lamp for Mine Anointed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:18
verses.text: What! a lamp for the Sun! "His enemies will I clothe with confusion: but upon Himself shall my sanctification flourish".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:19
verses.text: And hence they were in a certain place confounded by means of this very John, when the Jews said to the Lord, "By what authority doest Thou these things? Tell us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:20
verses.text: To whom He answered, "Do ye tell Me too, The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?" They heard, and held their peace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:21
verses.text: For they thought at once with themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:22
verses.text: "If we shall say, Of men: the people will stone us; for they hold John as a prophet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:23
verses.text: If we shall say, From heaven; He will say to 			 us, Why then have ye not believed him?" For John bare witness to Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:24
verses.text: So straitened in their hearts by their own questions, and taken in their own snares, they answered, "We do not know".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:25
verses.text: What else could the voice of darkness be? It is right indeed for a man when he does not know, to say, "I know not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:26
verses.text: But when he does know, and says, "I know not;" he is a witness against himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:27
verses.text: Now they knew well John's excellency, and that his baptism was from heaven; but they were unwilling to acquiesce in Him 			 to whom John bare witness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:28
verses.text: But when they said, "We do not know;" Jesus answered them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:29
verses.text: "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:30
verses.text: And they were confounded; and so was fulfilled, "I have prepared a lamp for Mine Anointed, His enemies will I clothe with confusion".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:31
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:32
verses.text: Are not Martyrs witnesses of Christ, and do they not bear witness to the truth? But if we think more carefully, when those Martyrs bear witness, He beareth witness to Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:33
verses.text: For He dwelleth in the Martyrs, that they may bear witness to the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:34
verses.text: Hear one of the Martyrs, even the Apostle Paul; "Would ye receive a proof of Christ, who speaketh in Me?" When John then beareth witness, Christ, who dwelleth in John, beareth witness to Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:35
verses.text: Let Peter bear witness, let Paul bear witness, let the rest of the Apostles bear witness, let Stephen bear witness, it is He who dwelleth in them all that beareth witness to Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:36
verses.text: For He without them is God, they without Him, what are they?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:37
verses.text: Of Him it is said, "He ascended up on high, He led captivity captive, He gave gifts unto men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:38
verses.text: What is, "He led captivity captive"? He conquered death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:39
verses.text: What is, "He led captivity captive"? The devil was the author of death, and the devil was himself by the Death of Christ led captive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:40
verses.text: "He ascended up on high".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:41
verses.text: What do we know higher than heaven? Visibly and before the eyes of His disciples He ascended into heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:42
verses.text: This we know, this we believe, this we confess.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:43
verses.text: "He gave gifts unto men".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:44
verses.text: What gifts? The Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:45
verses.text: He who giveth such a Gift, what is He 			 Himself? For great is God's mercy; He giveth a Gift equal to Himself; for His Gift is the Holy Spirit, and the Whole Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, is One God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:46
verses.text: What hath the Holy Spirit brought us? Hear the Apostle; "The love of God," saith he, "hath been shed abroad in our hearts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:47
verses.text: Whence, thou beggar, hath the love of God been shed abroad in thine heart? How, or wherein hath the love of God been shed abroad in the heart of man? "We have," saith he, "this treasure in earthen vessels".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:48
verses.text: Why in earthen vessels? "That the excellency of the power may be of God?" Finally, when he had said, "The love of God hath been shed abroad in our hearts;" that no man might think that he hath this love of God of himself, he added immediately, "By the Holy Spirit, who hath been given to us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:49
verses.text: Therefore, that thou mayest love God, let God dwell in thee, and love Himself in thee, that is, to His love let Him move thee, enkindle, enlighten, arouse thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:50
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:51
verses.text: For in this body of ours there is a struggle; as long as we live, we are in combat; as long as we are in combat, we are in peril; but, "in all these things we are conquerors through Him who loved us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:52
verses.text: Our combat ye heard of just now when the Apostle was being read.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:53
verses.text: "All the law," saith he, "is fulfilled in one word, even in this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:54
verses.text: This love is from the Holy Spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:55
verses.text: "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:56
verses.text: First see, if thou knowest yet how to love thyself; and then will I commit to thee the neighbour whom thou art to love as thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:57
verses.text: But if thou dost not yet know how to love thyself; I fear lest thou shouldest deceive thy neighbour as thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:58
verses.text: For if thou lovest iniquity, thou dost not love thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:59
verses.text: The Psalm is witness; "But whoso loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:60
verses.text: Now if thou hate thine own soul, what doth it profit thee that thou dost love thy flesh? If thou hate thine own soul and lovest thy flesh, thy flesh shall rise again; but only that thy soul may be tormented.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:61
verses.text: Therefore the soul must first be loved, which is to be subdued unto God, that this service may maintain its due order, the soul to God, the flesh to the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:62
verses.text: Wouldest thou that thy flesh should serve thy soul? Let thy soul serve God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:63
verses.text: Thou oughtest to be ruled, that thou 			 mayest be able to rule.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:64
verses.text: For so perilous is this struggle, that if thy Ruler forsake thee, ruin must ensue.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:66
verses.text: What struggle? "But if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:67
verses.text: But I say, Walk in the Spirit".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:68
verses.text: I am quoting the words of the Apostle, which have been just read out of his Epistle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:69
verses.text: "But I say, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lusts of the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:70
verses.text: "But I say, Walk in the Spirit, and the lusts of the flesh," he did not say, "Ye shall not have;" nor did he say, "Ye shall not do;" but, "Ye shall not fulfil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:71
verses.text: Now what this is, with the Lord's assistance, I will declare as I shall be able; give attention, that ye may understand, if ye are 			 walking in the Spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:72
verses.text: "But I say, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lusts of the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:73
verses.text: Let him follow on; if haply anything, as this which is here obscure, may be understood more easily by the sequel of his words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:74
