verses.text: For I said, that it was not without a meaning that the Apostle would not say, "Ye shall not have the lusts of the flesh;" nor again would even say," Ye shall not do the lusts of the flesh;" but said, "Ye shall not fulfil the 			 lusts of the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:75
verses.text: He hath set forth this struggle before us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:76
verses.text: In this battle are we occupied, if we are in God's service.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:77
verses.text: What then follows? "For the flesh lusteth against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:78
verses.text: For these are contrary the one to the other, so that ye do not the things that ye would".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:79
verses.text: This, if it be not understood, is with exceeding peril heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:80
verses.text: And therefore anxious as I am lest men by an evil interpretation should perish, I have undertaken with the Lord's assistance to explain these words to your affection.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:81
verses.text: We have leisure enough, we have begun early in the morning, the hour of dinner does not press; on this day, the sabbath that is, they that hunger after the word of God are wont especially to meet together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:82
verses.text: Hear and attend, I will speak with what 			 carefulness I can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:84
verses.text: What then is that which I said, "Is heard with peril if it be not understood"? Many overcome by carnal and damnable lusts, commit all sorts of crimes and impurities, and wallow in such abominable uncleanness, as it is a shame even to mention; and say to themselves these words of the Apostle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:85
verses.text: See what the Apostle has said, "So that we cannot do the things that ye would".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:86
verses.text: I would not do them, I am forced, I am compelled, I am overcome, "I do the things that I would not," as the Apostle says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:87
verses.text: "The flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh, so that ye cannot do the things that ye would".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:88
verses.text: You see with what peril this is heard, if it be not understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:89
verses.text: You see how it concerns the pastor's office, to open the closed fountains, and to minister to the thirsty sheep the pure, harmless water.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:90
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:91
verses.text: Be not willing then to be overcome when thou fightest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:92
verses.text: See what kind of war, what kind of battle, what kind of strife he hath set forth, within, within thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:93
verses.text: "The flesh lusteth against the Spirit".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:94
verses.text: If the Spirit lust not also against the flesh, commit adultery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:95
verses.text: But if the Spirit lust against the flesh, I see a struggle, I do not see a victory, it is a contest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:96
verses.text: "The flesh lusteth against the Spirit".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:97
verses.text: Adultery has its pleasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:98
verses.text: I confess that it 			 has its pleasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:99
verses.text: But, "The Spirit lusteth against the flesh:" Chastity too has its pleasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:100
verses.text: Therefore let the Spirit overcome the flesh; or by all means not be overcome by the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:101
verses.text: Adultery seeks the darkness, chastity desires the light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:102
verses.text: As thou wouldest wish to appear to others, so live; as thou wouldest wish to appear to men, even when beyond the eyes of men so live; for He who made thee, even in the darkness seeth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:103
verses.text: Why is chastity praised publicly by all? Why do not even 			 adulterers praise adultery? "Whoso" then "seeketh the truth, cometh to the light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:104
verses.text: But adultery has its pleasure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:105
verses.text: Be it contradicted, resisted, opposed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:106
verses.text: For it is not so that thou hast nothing wherewith to fight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:107
verses.text: Thy God is in thee, the good Spirit hath been given to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:108
verses.text: And notwithstanding this flesh of ours is permitted to lust against the spirit by evil suggestions and real delights.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:109
verses.text: Be that secured which the Apostle saith, "Let not sin reign in your mortal body".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:110
verses.text: He did not say, "Let it not be there".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:111
verses.text: It is there already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:112
verses.text: And this is called sin, because it has befallen us through the wages of sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:113
verses.text: For in Paradise the flesh did not lust against the spirit, nor was there this struggle there, where was peace only; but after the transgression, after that man was loth to serve God and was given up to himself; yet not so given up to himself as that he could so much as possess himself; but possessed by him, by whom deceived; the flesh began to lust against the Spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:114
verses.text: Now it is in the good that it lusteth against the Spirit; for in the bad it has nothing to lust 			 against.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:115
verses.text: For there doth it lust against the Spirit, where the Spirit is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:116
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:117
verses.text: For when he says, "The flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh;" do not suppose that so much hath been attributed to the spirit of man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:118
verses.text: It is the Spirit of God who fighteth in thee against thyself, against that which in thee is against thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:119
verses.text: For thou wouldest not stand to Godward; thou didst fall, wast broken; as a vessel when it falls from a man's hand to the ground, wast thou broken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:120
verses.text: And because thou wast broken, therefore art 			 thou turned against thyself; therefore art thou contrary to thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:121
verses.text: Let there be nought in thee contrary to thyself, and thou shalt stand in thine integrity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:122
verses.text: For that thou mayest know that this office appertaineth to the Holy Spirit; the Apostle saith in another place, "For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die; but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the flesh, ye shall live".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:123
verses.text: From these words man was at once uplifting himself, as though by his own spirit he were able to mortify the deeds of the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:124
verses.text: "If ye live after the flesh, ye shall die; but if through the Spirit ye do mortify the deeds of the flesh, ye shall live".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:125
verses.text: Explain to us, Apostle, through what spirit? For man also hath a spirit appertaining to his proper nature, whereby he is man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:126
verses.text: For man consists of body and spirit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:127
verses.text: And of this spirit of man it is said, "No man knoweth the 			 things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:128
verses.text: I see then that man himself hath his own spirit appertaining to his proper nature, and I hear thee saying, "But if through the Spirit ye do mortify the deeds of the flesh, ye shall live".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:129
verses.text: I ask, through what spirit; my own, or God's? For I hear thy words, and am still perplexed by this ambiguity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:130
verses.text: For when the word "spirit" is used, it is used sometimes of the spirit of a man, and of cattle, as it is written, that "all flesh which had in 			 itself the spirit of life, died by the flood".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:131
verses.text: And so the word spirit is spoken of cattle, and spoken of man too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:132
verses.text: Sometimes even the wind is called spirit; as it is in the Psalm, "Fire, hail, snow, frost, the spirit of the tempest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:133
verses.text: For as much then as the word "spirit" is used in many ways, by what spirit, O Apostle, hast thou said that the deeds of the flesh are to be mortified; by mine own, or by the Spirit of God? Hear what follows, and understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:134
verses.text: The difficulty is removed by the following words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:135
verses.text: For when he had said, "But if through the Spirit ye mortify the deeds of the flesh, ye shall live;" he added immediately, "For as many as are acted upon by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:136
verses.text: Thou dost act, if thou art acted upon, and actest well, if thou art acted upon by the Good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:137
verses.text: So then when he said to thee, "If through the Spirit ye mortify the deeds of the flesh, ye shall live;" and it was doubtful with thee of what spirit he had spoken, in the words following understand the Master, acknowledge the Redeemer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:138
verses.text: For That Redeemer hath given thee the Spirit Whereby thou mayest mortify the deeds of the 			 flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:139
verses.text: "For as many as are acted upon by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:140
verses.text: They are not the sons of God if they are not acted upon by the Spirit of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:141
verses.text: But if they are acted upon by the Spirit of God, they fight; because they have a mighty Helper.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:142
verses.text: For God doth not look on at our combattings as the people do at the gladiators.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:143
verses.text: The people may favour the gladiator, help him they cannot when he is in peril.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:144
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:145
verses.text: So then here to; "The flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:146
verses.text: And what means, "So that ye cannot do the things that ye would"? For here is the peril with one who understands it amiss.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:147
verses.text: Be it now my office to explain it, howsoever incompetent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:148
verses.text: "So that ye cannot do the things that ye would".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:149
verses.text: Attend, ye holy ones, whosoever ye are that are fighting.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:150
verses.text: To them that are battling do I speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:151
verses.text: They who are fighting, understand; he 			 that is not fighting, understands me not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:152
verses.text: Yea, he that is fighting, I will not say understands me, but anticipates me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:153
verses.text: What is the chaste man's wish? That no lust should rise up in his members at all opposed to chastity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:154
verses.text: He wisheth for peace, but as yet he hath it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:155
verses.text: For when we shall have come to that state, where there shall rise up no lust at all to be opposed, there will be no enemy for us to struggle with; nor is victory a matter for expectation there, for that there is triumphing over 			 the now vanquished foe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:156
verses.text: Hear of this victory, in the Apostle's own words; "This corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:157
verses.text: Now when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality; then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:158
verses.text: Hear the voices of them that triumph; "O death, where is thy contention? O death, where is thy sting?" Thou hast smitten, thou hast wounded, thou hast thrown down; but He hath been wounded for me who made me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:159
verses.text: O death, death, He who made me hath been wounded for me, and by His Death hath overcome thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:160
verses.text: And then in triumph shall they say, "O death, where is thy contention? O death, where is thy sting?"  11.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:161
verses.text: But now, when "the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh," is the contention of death; we do not what we would.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:162
verses.text: Why? Because we would that there should be no lusts, but we cannot hinder it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:163
verses.text: Whether we will or not, we have them; whether we will or not, they solicit, they allure, they sting, they disturb us, they will be rising.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:164
verses.text: They are repressed, not yet extinguished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:165
verses.text: How long does the flesh lust against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh? Will it be so, even when the man is dead? God forbid! Thou puttest off the flesh, how then shall thou draw the lusts of the flesh along with thee? Nay, if thou hast fought well, thou shall be received into rest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:166
verses.text: And from this rest, thou passest to be crowned, not condemned; that thou mayest 			 after it be brought to the Kingdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:167
verses.text: As long then as we live here, my brethren, so it is; so is it with us even who have grown old in this warfare, less mighty enemies it is true we have, but yet we have them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:168
verses.text: Our enemies are in a measure wearied out even now by age; but nevertheless, wearied though they be, they do not cease to harass by such excitements as they can the quiet of old age.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:169
verses.text: Sharper is the fight of the young; we know it well, we have passed through it: "The flesh" then 			 "lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; so that ye cannot do the things that ye would".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:170
verses.text: For what would ye, O holy men, and good warriors, and brave soldiers of Christ? what would ye? That there should be no evil lusts at all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:171
verses.text: But ye cannot help it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:172
verses.text: Sustain the war, hope for triumph.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:173
verses.text: For now in the meanwhile ye must fight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:174
verses.text: "The flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; so that ye cannot do the things that ye would;" that is, that there should be no lusts of the flesh at all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:175
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:176
verses.text: But do what ye are able; what the Apostle himself says in another place, which I had already begun to repeat; "Let not sin reign in your mortal body, to obey the desires thereof".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:177
verses.text: Lo, what I would not; evil desires arise; but obey them not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:178
verses.text: Arm thyself, assume the weapons of war.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:179
verses.text: The precepts of God are thy arms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:180
verses.text: If thou listen to me as thou shouldest, thou art armed even by that which I am speaking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:181
verses.text: "'Let not sin,' he says, 'reign in your mortal body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:182
verses.text: ' For as long as ye bear a mortal body, sin doth fight against you; but let it not reign".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:183
verses.text: What is, "Let it not reign"? That is, "to obey the desires thereof".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:184
verses.text: If ye begin to obey, it 			 reigns.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:185
verses.text: And what is it to obey, but to "yield your members as instruments of iniquity unto sin"? Nothing more excellent than this teacher.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:186
verses.text: What wouldest thou that I should yet explain to thee? Do what thou hast heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:187
verses.text: Yield not thy members instruments of iniquity unto sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:188
verses.text: God hath given thee power by His Spirit to restrain thy members.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:189
verses.text: Lust riseth up, restrain thy members; what can it do now that it hath risen? Restrain thou thy members; yield not thy members instruments of iniquity unto 			 sin; arm not thine adversary against thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:190
verses.text: Restrain thy feet, that they go not after unlawful things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:191
verses.text: Lust hath risen up, restrain thy members; restrain thine hands from all wickedness; restrain the eyes, that they wander not astray; restrain the ears, that they hear not the words of lust with pleasure; restrain the whole body, restrain the sides, restrain its highest and lowest parts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:192
verses.text: What can lust do? How to rise up, it knoweth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:193
verses.text: How to conquer, it knoweth not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:194
verses.text: By rising up constantly 			 without effect, it learns not even to rise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:195
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:196
verses.text: Let us then return to the words, which I had set forth out of the Apostle as obscure, and we shall now see them to be plain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:197
verses.text: For this I had set forth, that the Apostle did not say, "Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not have the lusts of the flesh;" because we must necessarily have them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:198
verses.text: Why then did he not say, "Ye shall not do the lusts of the flesh"? Because we do them; for we do lust.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:199
verses.text: The very lusting, is doing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:200
verses.text: But the Apostle says, "Now it is no 			 more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:201
verses.text: What then hast thou to beware of? This doubtless, that thou fulfil them not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:202
verses.text: A damnable lust hath risen up, it hath risen, made its suggestion; let it not be heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:203
verses.text: It burneth, and is not quieted, and thou wouldest that it should not burn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:204
verses.text: Where then is, "So that ye cannot do the things that ye would"? Do not give it thy members.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:205
verses.text: Let it burn without effect, and it will spend itself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:206
verses.text: In thee then these lusts are done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:207
verses.text: It must be confessed, they are done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:208
verses.text: And therefore he 			 said, "Ye shall not fulfil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:209
verses.text: Let them not then be fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:210
verses.text: Thou hast determined to do, thou hast fulfilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:211
verses.text: For thou hast fulfilled it, if thou determinest upon committing adultery, and dost not commit it, because no place hath been found, because no opportunity is given, because, it may be, she for whom thou seemest to be disturbed is chaste; lo, now she is chaste, and thou art an adulterer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:212
verses.text: Why? Because thou hast fulfilled lusts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:213
verses.text: What is, "hast fulfilled"? Hast determined in thy 			 mind upon committing adultery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:214
verses.text: If now, which God forbid, thy members too have wrought, thou hast fallen down headlong into death.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:215
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:216
verses.text: Christ raised up the daughter of the ruler of the synagogue who was dead in the house.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:217
verses.text: She was in the house, she had not yet been carried out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:218
verses.text: So is the man who hath determined on some wickedness in his heart; he is dead, but he lies within.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:219
verses.text: But if he has come as far as to the action of the members, he has been carried out of the house.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:220
verses.text: But the Lord raised also the young man, the widow's son, when he was being carried out dead beyond the gate of the city.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:221
verses.text: So then I venture to say, Thou hast determined in thine heart, if thou call thyself back from thy deed, thou wilt be cured before thou put it into action.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:222
verses.text: For if thou repent in thine heart, that thou hast determined on some bad and wicked and abominable and damnable thing; there where thou wast lying dead, within, so within hast thou arisen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:223
verses.text: But if thou have fulfilled, now hast thou been carried out; but thou hast One to say to thee, "Young man, I say unto thee, Arise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:224
verses.text: Even though thou have perpetrated it, repent thee, return at once, come not to the sepulchre.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:225
verses.text: But even here I find a third one dead, who was brought even to the sepulchre.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:226
verses.text: He has now upon him the weight of habit, a mass of earth presses him down exceedingly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:227
verses.text: For he has been practised much in unclean deeds, and is weighed down exceedingly by his immoderate habit.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:228
verses.text: Here too Christ crieth, "Lazarus, come forth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:229
verses.text: For a man of very evil habit "now stinketh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:230
verses.text: With good reason did Christ in that case cry out; and not cry out only, but with a loud Voice cried out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:231
verses.text: For at Christ's Cry even such as these, dead though they be, buried though they be, stinking though they be, yet even these shall rise again, they shall rise again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:232
verses.text: For of none that lieth dead need we despair under such a Raiser up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 77:233
verses.text: Turn we to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:2
verses.text: [CXXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John v.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:5
verses.text: 39 , "Ye search the Scriptures, because ye think that in them ye have eternal life," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:6
verses.text: Against the Donatists.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:8
verses.text: Give heed, Beloved, to the lesson of the Gospel which has just sounded in our ears, whilst I speak a few words as God shall vouchsafe to me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:9
verses.text: The Lord Jesus was speaking to the Jews, and said to them, "Search the Scriptures, in which ye think ye have eternal life, they testify of me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:10
verses.text: Then a little after He said, "I am come in My Father's Name, and ye have not received Me; if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:11
verses.text: Then a little after; "How can ye believe, who look for glory one from another, and seek not the glory which is of God only?" At last He saith, "I do not accuse you to the Father; there is one that accuseth you, Moses, in whom ye trust.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:12
verses.text: For had ye believed Moses, ye would haply believe Me also, for he wrote of Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:13
verses.text: But seeing ye believe not his words, how can ye believe Me?" At these sayings which have been set before us from divine inspiration, out of the reader's mouth, but by the Saviour's ministry, give ear to a few words, not to be estimated by their number, but to be duly weighed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:14
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:15
verses.text: For all these things it is easy to understand as touching the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:16
verses.text: But we must beware, lest, when we give too much attention to them, we withdraw our eyes from ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:17
verses.text: For the Lord was speaking to His disciples; and assuredly what He spake to them, He spake to us too their posterity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:18
verses.text: Nor to them only does what He said, "Lo, I am with you alway even unto the end of the world," apply, but even to all Christians that should be after them, and succeed them even unto the end of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:19
verses.text: Speaking then to them He said, "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:20
verses.text: They at that time thought that the Lord had said this, because they had brought no bread; they did not understand that "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees" meant, "beware of the doctrine of the Pharisees".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:21
verses.text: What was the doctrine of the Pharisees, but that which ye have now heard? "Seeking glory one of another, looking for glory one from another, and not seeking the glory which is of God only".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:22
verses.text: Of these the Apostle Paul thus speaks; "I bear them record that they 			 have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:23
verses.text: "They have," he says, "a zeal of God;" I know it, I am sure of it; I was once among them, I was such as they.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:24
verses.text: "They have," he says, "a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:25
verses.text: What is this, O Apostle, "not according to knowledge"? Explain to us what the knowledge is thou dost set forth, which thou dost grieve is not in them, and wouldest should be in us? He went on and subjoined and developed what he had set forth closed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:26
verses.text: What is, "They have a zeal 			 of God, but not according to knowledge? For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and wishing to establish their own, have not submitted themselves into the righteousness of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:27
verses.text: To be ignorant then of God's righteousness, and to wish to establish one's own, this is to "look for glory one from another, and not to seek the glory which is of God only".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:28
verses.text: This is the leaven of the Pharisees.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:29
verses.text: Of this the Lord bids beware.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:30
verses.text: If it is servants that He bids, and the Lord that bids, let us beware; lest we hear, "Why say ye to Me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?"  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:31
verses.text: Let us then leave a while the Jews to whom the Lord was then speaking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:32
verses.text: They are without, they will not listen to us, they hate the Gospel itself, they procured false witness against the Lord, that they might condemn Him when alive; other witness they bought with money against Him when dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:33
verses.text: When we say to them, "Believe on Jesus," they answer us, "Are we to believe on a dead man?" But when we add, "But He rose again;" they answer, "Not 			  at all;" His disciples stole Him away from the sepulchre.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:34
verses.text: The Jewish buyers love falsehood and despise the truth of the Lord, the Redeemer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:35
verses.text: What thou art saying, O Jew, thy parents bought for money; and this which they bought hath continued in thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:36
verses.text: Give heed rather to Him That bought thee, not to him who bought a lie for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:37
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:38
verses.text: But as I have said, let us leave these, and attend rather to these our brethren, with whom we have to do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:39
verses.text: For Christ is the Head of the Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:40
verses.text: The Head is in Heaven, the Body is on earth; the Head is the Lord, the Body His Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:41
verses.text: But ye remember it is said, "They shall be two in one flesh".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:42
verses.text: "This is a great mystery," says the Apostle, "but I speak in Christ and in the Church".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:43
verses.text: If then they are two in one flesh, they are two in one voice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:44
verses.text: Our Head the Lord Christ spake to the Jews these things which we heard, when the Gospel was being read, The Head to His enemies; let the Body too, that is, the Church, speak to its enemies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:45
verses.text: Ye know to whom it should speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:46
verses.text: What has it to say? It is not of myself that I have said, that the voice is one; because the flesh is one, the voice is one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:47
verses.text: Let us then say this to them; I am speaking with the voice of the 			 Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:48
verses.text: "O Brethren, dispersed children, wandering sheep, branches cut off, why do ye calumniate me? Why do ye not acknowledge me? "Search the Scriptures, in which ye think ye have eternal life, they testify of me;" to the Jews our Head saith, what the Body saith to you; "Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:49
verses.text: Why? Because ye do not "search the Scriptures, which testify of me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:50
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:51
verses.text: A testimony for the Head; "To Abraham and his seed were the promises made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:52
verses.text: He saith not, And to seeds, as of many, but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:53
verses.text: A testimony for the body unto Abraham, which the Apostle hath brought forward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:54
verses.text: "To Abraham were the promises made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:55
verses.text: As I live, saith the Lord, I swear by Myself, because thou hast obeyed My Voice, and hast not spared thine own beloved son for Me, that in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand of the sea, and in thy seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:56
verses.text: Thou hast here a testimony for the Head, and one for the Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:57
verses.text: Hear another, short, and almost in one sentence including a testimony for the Head and for the Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:58
verses.text: The Psalm was speaking of the Resurrection of Christ; "Be Thou exalted, O God, above the heavens".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:59
verses.text: And immediately for the Body; "And Thy glory above all the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:60
verses.text: Hear a testimony for the Head; "They digged My Hands and My Feet, they numbered all My Bones; and they looked and stared upon Me; they divided My garments among them, and cast lots upon My vesture".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:61
verses.text: Hear immediately a testimony for the Body, a few words after, "All the ends of the world shall remember themselves and be turned unto the Lord, and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship in His sight; for the kingdom is the Lord's, and He shall have dominion over the nations".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:62
verses.text: Hear for the Head; And "He is as a bridegroom coming forth out of His bride-chamber".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:63
verses.text: And in this same Psalm hear for the Body; "Their sound went out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:64
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:65
verses.text: These passages are for the Jews, and for these of our own brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:66
verses.text: Why so? Because these Scriptures of the Old Testament both the Jews receive, and these our brethren receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:67
verses.text: But Christ Himself, whom the others do not receive, let us see if these last receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:68
verses.text: Let Him speak Himself, speak both for Himself who is the Head, and for His Body which is the Church; for so in us the head speaks for the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:69
verses.text: Hear for the Head; He was risen from the dead, He found the 			 disciples hesitating, doubting, not believing for joy; He "opened their understanding that they might understand the Scriptures, and said to them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise again from the dead the third day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:70
verses.text: Thus for the Head; let Him speak for the Body too; "And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His Name throughout all nations, beginning at Jerusalem".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:71
verses.text: Let the Church then speak to her enemies, let her speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:72
verses.text: She does speak clearly, she is not silent: only let them give ear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:73
verses.text: Brethren, ye have heard the testimonies, now acknowledge me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:74
verses.text: "Search the Scriptures, in which ye hope ye have eternal life: they testify of me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:75
verses.text: What I have said is not of mine own, but of my Lord's; and notwithstanding, ye still turn away, still turn your backs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:76
verses.text: "How can ye believe me, who look for glory one from another, and seek not the glory 			 which is of God only? For being ignorant of God's righteousness, ye have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:77
verses.text: For being ignorant of God's righteousness, and wishing to establish your own, ye have not submitted yourselves to the righteousness of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:78
verses.text: What else is it to be ignorant of God's righteousness, and to wish to establish your own, but to say, "It is I who sanctify, it is I who justify; what I may have given is holy"? Leave to God what is God's; recognise, O man, what is man's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:79
verses.text: Thou art ignorant of God's righteousness, and wishest to establish thine own.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:80
verses.text: Thou dost wish to justify me; it is enough for thee that thou be justified with me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:81
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:82
verses.text: It is said of Antichrist, and all understand of him what the Lord said, "I am come in My Father's Name, and ye have not received Me; if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:83
verses.text: But let us hear John too; "Ye have heard that Antichrist cometh, and even now are there many Antichrists".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:84
verses.text: What is it in Antichrist that we are in horror of, but that he is to honour his own name, and to despise the Name of the Lord? What else doeth he that saith, "It is I that justify"? We answer him, "I came to Christ, not with my feet, but with my heart I came; where I heard the Gospel, there did I believe, there was I baptized; because I believed on Christ, I believed on God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:85
verses.text: Yet says he, "Thou art not clean".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:86
verses.text: "Why?" "Because I was not there".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:87
verses.text: "Tell me 			 why am not I cleansed, a man who was baptized in Jerusalem, who was baptized, for instance, among the Ephesians, to whom an Epistle you read was written, and whose peace you despise? Lo, to the Ephesians the Apostle wrote; a Church was founded, and remains even to this day; yea, remains in greater fruitfulness, remains in greater numbers, holds fast that which it received of the Apostle, 'If any man preach ought to you than that ye have received, let him be 			 accursed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:88
verses.text: '  What now? what dost thou say to me? Am I not clean? There was I baptized, am I not clean?" "No, even thou art not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:89
verses.text: "Why?" "Because I was not there".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:90
verses.text: "But He who is everywhere was there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:91
verses.text: He who is everywhere was there, in whose Name I believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:92
verses.text: Thou coming I know not whence, yea, rather not coming, but wishing that I should come to thee, fixed in this place, sayest to me, 'Thou wast not baptized duly, seeing I was not there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:93
verses.text: ' Consider who was there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:94
verses.text: What 			 was said to John? 'Upon whom thou shall see the Spirit descending like a dove, this is He which baptizeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:95
verses.text: ' Him hast thou seeking for thee; nay, for that thou hast grudged me who was baptized by Him, thou hast lost Him rather".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:96
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:97
verses.text: Understand then, my Brethren, our language and theirs, and look which ye would choose.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:98
verses.text: This is what we say; "Be we holy, God knoweth it; be we unrighteous, this again He knoweth better; place not your hope in us, whatsoever we be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:99
verses.text: If we be good, do as is written, 'Be ye imitators of me, as I also am of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:100
verses.text: ' But if we be bad, not even thus are ye abandoned, not even thus have ye remained without counsel: give ear to Him, saying, 'Do what they say; but do not what they do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:101
verses.text: '" Whereas they on the contrary say, "If we were not good, ye were lost".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:102
verses.text: Lo, here is "another that shall come in his own name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:103
verses.text: Shall my life then depend on thee, and my salvation be tied up in thee? Have I so forgotten my foundation? Was not Christ the Rock? Is it not that he that buildeth upon the rock, neither the wind nor the floods overthrow him? Come then, if thou wilt, with me upon the Rock, and do not wish to be to me for the rock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:104
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:105
verses.text: Let the Church then say those last words also, "If ye had believed Moses, ye would believe me also; for he wrote of me;" for that I am His body of whom he wrote.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:106
verses.text: And of the Church did Moses write.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:107
verses.text: For I have quoted the words of Moses "In thy seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:108
verses.text: Moses wrote this in the first book.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:109
verses.text: If ye believed Moses, ye would also believe Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:110
verses.text: Because ye despise Moses' words, it must needs be that ye despise the words of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:111
verses.text: "They have" there, saith He, "Moses and the Prophets, let them hear them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:112
verses.text: Nay, father Abraham, but if one went unto them from the dead," him they will hear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:113
verses.text: "And He said, If they hear not Moses and the Prophets, neither will they believe, if one rise again from the dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:114
verses.text: This was said of the Jews: was it therefore not said of heretics? He had risen from the dead, who said, "It behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise again from the dead the third day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:115
verses.text: This I believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:116
verses.text: I believe it, he says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:117
verses.text: Dost thou believe? Wherefore believest thou not what follows? In that thou believest, "It behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise again from the dead the third day;" this was spoken of the Head; believe also that which follows concerning the Church, 			 "That repentance and remission of sins should be preached throughout all nations".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:118
verses.text: Wherefore dost thou believe as touching the Head, and believest not as touching the Body? What hath the Church done to thee, that thou wouldest so to say behead her? Thou wouldest take away the Church's Head, and believe the Head, leave the Body as it were a lifeless trunk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:119
verses.text: It is all to no purpose that thou dost caress the Head, like any devoted servant.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:120
verses.text: He that would take off the head, doth his best to kill both the head and the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:121
verses.text: They are ashamed to deny Christ, yet 			 are they not ashamed to deny Christ's words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:122
verses.text: Christ neither we nor ye have seen with our eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:123
verses.text: The Jews saw, and slew Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:124
verses.text: We have not seen Him, and believe; His words are with us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:125
verses.text: Compare yourselves with the Jews: they despised Him hanging upon the Tree, ye despise Him sitting in heaven; at their suggestion Christ's title was set up, by your setting yourselves up, Christ's Baptism is effaced.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:126
verses.text: But what remains, Brethren, but that we pray even for the proud, that we pray even for the puffed up, who so extol themselves? Let us say to God on their behalf, "Let them know that the Lord is Thy Name; and" not "that" men, but "Thou Only art the Most High over all the earth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 78:127
verses.text: Let us turn to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:2
verses.text: [CXXX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John vi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:5
verses.text: 9 , where the miracle of the five loaves and the two fishes is related.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:7
verses.text: It was a great miracle that was wrought, dearly beloved, for five thousand men to be filled with five loaves and two fishes, and the remnants of the fragments to fill twelve baskets.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:8
verses.text: A great miracle: but we shall not wonder much at what was done, if we give heed to Him That did it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:9
verses.text: He multiplied the five loaves in the hands of them that brake them, who multiplieth the seeds that grow in the earth, so as that a few grains are sown, and 			 whole barns are filled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:10
verses.text: But, because he doth this every year, no one marvels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:11
verses.text: Not the inconsiderableness of what is done, but its constancy takes away admiration of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:12
verses.text: But when the Lord did these things, He spake to them that had understanding, not by words only, but even by the miracles themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:13
verses.text: The five loaves signified the five books of Moses' Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:14
verses.text: The old Law is barley compared to the Gospel wheat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:15
verses.text: In those books are great mysteries concerning Christ contained.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:16
verses.text: Whence He saith Himself, "If ye had believed Moses, ye would believe Me also; for 			 he wrote of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:17
verses.text: But as in barley the marrow is hid under the chaff, so in the veil of the mysteries of the Law is Christ hidden.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:18
verses.text: As those mysteries of the Law are developed and unfolded; so too those loaves increased when they were broken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:19
verses.text: And in this that I have explained to you, I have broken bread unto you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:20
verses.text: The five thousand men signify the people ordered under the five books of the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:21
verses.text: The twelve baskets are the twelve Apostles, who themselves too were filled with the fragments of the 			 Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:22
verses.text: The two fishes are either the two precepts of the love of God and our neighbour, or the two people of the circumcision and uncircumcision, or those two sacred personages of the king and the priest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:23
verses.text: As these things are explained, they are broken; when they are understood, they are eaten.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:24
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:25
verses.text: Let us turn to Him who did these things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:26
verses.text: He is Himself "The Bread which came down from heaven;" but Bread which refresheth the failing, and doth not fail; Bread which can be tasted, cannot be wasted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:27
verses.text: This Bread did the manna also figure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:28
verses.text: Wherefore it is said, "He gave them the Bread of heaven, man ate Angels' Bread".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:29
verses.text: Who is the Bread of heaven, but Christ? But in order that man might eat Angels' Bread, the Lord of Angels was made Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:30
verses.text: For if He had not been made Man, we should not have His Flesh; if we had not His Flesh, we should not eat the Bread of the Altar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:31
verses.text: Let us hasten to the inheritance, seeing we have hereby received a great earnest of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:32
verses.text: My brethren, let us long for the life of Christ, seeing we hold as an earnest the Death of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:33
verses.text: How shall He not give us His good things, 			 who hath suffered our evil things? In this our earth, in this evil world, what abounds, but to be born, to labour, and to die? Examine thoroughly man's estate, convict me if I lie: consider all men whether they are in this world for any other end than to be born, to labour, and to die? This is the merchandize of our country: these things here abound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:34
verses.text: To such merchandize did that Merchantman descend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:35
verses.text: And forasmuch as every merchant gives and receives; gives what he has, and receives what he 			 has not; when he procures anything, he gives money, and receives what he buys: so Christ too in this His traffic gave and received.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:36
verses.text: But what received He? That which aboundeth here, to be born, to labour, and to die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:37
verses.text: And what did He give? To be born again, to rise again, and to reign for ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:38
verses.text: O Good Merchant, buy us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:39
verses.text: Why should I say buy us, when we ought to give Thee thanks that Thou hast bought us? Thou dost deal out our Price to us, we drink Thy Blood; so dost thou deal out to us our Price.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:40
verses.text: And we read the Gospel, our title deed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:41
verses.text: We are Thy servants, we are Thy creatures: Thou hast made us, Thou hast redeemed us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:42
verses.text: Any one can buy his servant, create him he cannot; but the Lord hath both created and redeemed His servants; created them, that they might be; redeemed them, that they might not be captives ever.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:43
verses.text: For we fell into the hands of the prince of this world, who seduced Adam, and made him his servant, and began to possess us as his slaves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:44
verses.text: But the Redeemer came, and the seducer was overcome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:45
verses.text: And what did our Redeemer to him who held us captive? For our ransom he held out His Cross as a trap; he placed in It as a bait His Blood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:46
verses.text: He indeed had power to shed His Blood, he did not attain to drink it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:47
verses.text: And in that he shed the Blood of Him who was no debtor, he was commanded to render up the debtors; he shed the Blood of the Innocent, he was commanded to withdraw from the guilty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:48
verses.text: He verily shed His Blood to this end, that He might wipe out our sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:49
verses.text: That then whereby he held us fast was effaced by the Redeemer's Blood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:50
verses.text: For he only held us fast by the bonds of our own sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:51
verses.text: They were the captive's chains.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:52
verses.text: He came, He bound the strong one with the bonds of His 			 Passion; He entered into his house into the hearts, that is, of those where he did dwell, and took away his vessels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:53
verses.text: We are his vessels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:54
verses.text: He had filled them with his own bitterness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:55
verses.text: This bitterness too he pledged to our Redeemer in the gall.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:56
verses.text: He had filled us then as his vessels; but our Lord spoiling his vessels, and making them His Own, poured out the bitterness, filled them with sweetness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:57
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:58
verses.text: Let us then love Him, for He is sweet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:59
verses.text: "Taste and see that the Lord is sweet".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:60
verses.text: He is to be feared, but to be loved still more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:61
verses.text: He is Man and God; the One Christ is Man and God; as one man is soul and body: but God and Man are not two Persons.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:62
verses.text: In Christ indeed there are two substances, God and Man; but one Person, that the Trinity may remain, and that there be not a quaternity introduced by the addition of the human nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:63
verses.text: How then can it be that God should not have mercy upon us, for whose sake God was made Man? Much is that which He hath done already; more wonderful is that which He hath done, than what He hath promised; and by that which He hath done, ought we to believe what He hath promised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:64
verses.text: For that which He hath done, we should scarcely believe, unless we also saw it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:65
verses.text: Where do we see it? In the peoples that believe, in the multitude that has been brought 			 unto Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:66
verses.text: For that hath been fulfilled which was promised to Abraham; and from these things which we see, we believe what we do not see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:67
verses.text: Abraham was one single man, and to him was it said, "In thy seed shall all nations be blessed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:68
verses.text: If he had looked to himself, when would he have believed? He was one single man, and was now old; and he had a barren wife, and one who was so far advanced in age, that she could not conceive, even though she had not been barren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:69
verses.text: There was nothing at all from which any hope could be drawn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:70
verses.text: But he looked to Him 			 That gave the promise, and believed what he did not see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:71
verses.text: Lo, what he believed, we see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:72
verses.text: Therefore from these things which we see, we ought to believe what we see not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:73
verses.text: He begat Isaac, we saw it not; and Isaac begat Jacob, and this we did not see; and Jacob begat twelve sons, and them we saw not; and his twelve sons begat the people of Israel; this great people we see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:74
verses.text: I have now begun to mention those things which we do see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:75
verses.text: Of the people of Israel was born the Virgin Mary, and she gave birth to 			 Christ; and, lo, in Christ all nations are blessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:76
verses.text: What more true? more certain? more plain? Together with me, long after the world to come, ye who have been gathered together out of the nations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:77
verses.text: In this world hath God fulfilled His promise concerning the seed of Abraham.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:78
verses.text: How shall He not give us His eternal promises, whom He hath made to be Abraham's seed? For this the Apostle saith: "But if ye be Christ's" (they are the Apostle's words), "then are ye Abraham's seed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:79
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:80
verses.text: We have begun to be some great thing; let no man despise himself: we were once nothing; but we are something.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:81
verses.text: We have said unto the Lord, "Remember that we are dust;" but out of the dust He made man, and to dust He gave life, and in Christ our Lord hath He already brought this same dust to the Kingdom of Heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:82
verses.text: For from this dust took He flesh, from this took earth, and hath raised earth to heaven, He who made heaven and earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:83
verses.text: If then these two new things, not yet done, were set before us, and it were asked of us, "Which is the most wonderful, that He who is God should be made Man, or he who is man should be made a man of God? which is 			 the more wonderful? which the more difficult?" What hath Christ promised us? That which as yet we see not; that is, that we should be His men, and reign with Him, and never die? This is so to say with difficulty believed, that a man once born should arrive at that life, where he shall never die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:84
verses.text: This is what we believe with a heart well cleansed, cleansed, I mean, of the world's dust; that this dust close not up our eye of faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:85
verses.text: This it is that we are bid believe, that after we have been dead, we shall be even with our dead bodies in life, where we shall never die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:86
verses.text: Wonderful it is; but more wonderful is that which Christ hath done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:87
verses.text: For which is the more incredible, that man should live for ever, or that God should ever die? That men should receive life from God is the more credible; that God should receive death 			 from men I suppose is the more incredible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:88
verses.text: Yet this hath been brought to pass already: let us then believe that which is to be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:89
verses.text: If that which is the more incredible hath been brought to pass, shall He not give us that which is the more credible? For God hath power to make of men Angels, who hath made of earthy and filthy spawn, men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:90
verses.text: What shall we be? Angels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:91
verses.text: What have we been? I am ashamed to call it to mind; I am forced to consider it, yet I blush to tell it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:92
verses.text: What have we been? Whence did God make men? What were we before we were at all? We were nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:93
verses.text: When we were in our mother's wombs, what were we? It is enough that ye remember.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:94
verses.text: Withdraw your minds from the whence ye were made, and think of what ye are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:95
verses.text: Ye live; but so do herbs and trees live.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:96
verses.text: Ye have sensation, and so have cattle sensation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:97
verses.text: Ye are men, ye have got beyond the cattle, ye are superior to the cattle; for that ye understand how great things He hath done for you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:98
verses.text: Ye have life, ye have sensation, ye have understanding, ye are men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:99
verses.text: Now to this benefit what can be compared? Ye are Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:100
verses.text: For if we had not received this, what would it profit us, that we were men! So then we are Christians, we belong to Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:101
verses.text: For all the world's rage, it doth not break us; because we belong to Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:102
verses.text: For all the world's caresses, 			 it doth not seduce us; we belong to Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:103
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:104
verses.text: A great Patron have we found, Brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:105
verses.text: Ye know that men depend much upon their patrons.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:106
verses.text: A dependent of a man in power will make answer to any one who threatens him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:107
verses.text: "Thou canst do nothing to me, as long as my lord's head is safe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:108
verses.text: How much more boldly and surely may we say, "Thou canst do nothing to us, whilst our Head is safe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:109
verses.text: Forasmuch as our Patron is our Head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:110
verses.text: Whosoever depend upon any man as patron, are his dependents; we are the members of our Patron.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:111
verses.text: Let Him bear us in Himself, and let no man tear us away from Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:112
verses.text: Since 			 what labours soever we shall have endured in this world, all that passeth away, is nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:113
verses.text: The good things shall come which shall not pass away; by labours we arrive at them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:114
verses.text: But when we have arrived, no one teareth us away from them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:115
verses.text: The gates of Jerusalem are shut; they receive the bolts too, that to that city it may be said, "Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem, praise thy God, O Sion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:116
verses.text: For He hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates; He hath blessed thy children within 			 thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:117
verses.text: Who hath made thy borders peace".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:118
verses.text: When the gates are shut, and the bolts drawn, no friend goeth out, no enemy entereth in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 79:119
verses.text: There shall we have true and assured security, if here we shall not have abandoned the truth.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:2
verses.text: [CXXXI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John vi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:5
verses.text: 53 , "Except ye eat the flesh," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:6
verses.text: , and on the words of the apostles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:7
verses.text: And the Psalms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:8
verses.text: Against the Pelagians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:9
verses.text: Delivered at the Table of the Martyr St.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:10
verses.text: Cyprian, the 9th  of the Calends of October,—23 Sept.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:11
verses.text: , on the Lord's day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:12
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:13
verses.text: We have heard the True Master, the Divine Redeemer, the human Saviour, commending to us our Ransom, His Blood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:14
verses.text: For He spake to us of His Body and Blood; He called His Body Meat, His Blood Drink.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:15
verses.text: The faithful recognise the Sacrament of the faithful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:16
verses.text: But the hearers what else do they but hear? When therefore commending such Meat and such Drink He said, "Except ye shall eat My Flesh and drink My Blood, ye shall have no life in you;" 			  (and this that He said concerning life, who else said it but the Life Itself? But that man shall have death, not life, who shall think that the Life is false), His disciples were offended, not all of them indeed, but very many, saying within themselves, "This is an hard saying, who can hear it?" But when the Lord knew this in Himself, and heard the murmurings of their thought, He answered them, thinking though uttering nothing, that they might understand that they were heard, and might cease to entertain such thoughts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:17
verses.text: What then did He answer? "Doth this offend you?" "What then if ye shall see the Son of Man ascend up where He was before?" What meaneth this? "Doth this offend you?" "Do ye imagine that I am about to make divisions of this My Body which ye see; and to cut up My Members, and give them to you? 'What then if ye shall see the Son of Man ascend up where He was before?'" Assuredly, He who could ascend Whole could not be consumed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:18
verses.text: So then He both gave us of His Body and Blood a healthful refreshment, and briefly solved so great a question as to His Own Entireness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:19
verses.text: Let them then who eat, eat 			 on, and them that drink, drink; let them hunger and thirst; eat Life, drink Life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:20
verses.text: That eating, is to be refreshed; but thou art in such wise refreshed, as that that whereby thou art refreshed, faileth not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:21
verses.text: That drinking, what is it but to live? Eat Life, drink Life; thou shalt have life, and the Life is Entire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:22
verses.text: But then this shall be, that is, the Body and the Blood of Christ shall be each man's Life; if what is taken in the Sacrament visibly is in the truth itself eaten spiritually, drunk 			 spiritually.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:23
verses.text: For we have heard the Lord Himself saying, "It is the Spirit That quickeneth, but the flesh profiteth nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:24
verses.text: The words that I have spoken unto you, are Spirit and Life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:25
verses.text: But there are some of you," saith He, "that believe not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:26
verses.text: Such were they who said, "This is a hard saying, who can hear it?" It is hard, but only to the hard; that is, it is incredible, but only to the incredulous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:27
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:28
verses.text: But in order to teach us that this very believing is matter of gift, not of desert, He saith, "As I have said unto you, no man cometh unto Me, except it were given him of My Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:29
verses.text: Now as to where the Lord said this, if we call to mind the foregoing words of the Gospel, we shall find that He had said, "No man cometh unto Me, except the Father which hath sent Me draw him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:30
verses.text: He did not lead, but draw.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:31
verses.text: This violence is done to the heart, not the body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:32
verses.text: Why then dost thou marvel? Believe, and thou comest; love, and thou art drawn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:33
verses.text: Do not suppose here any rough and uneasy violence; it is gentle, it is sweet; it is the very sweetness that draweth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:34
verses.text: Is not a sheep drawn, when fresh grass is shown to it in its hunger? Yet I imagine that it is not bodily driven on, but fast bound by desire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:35
verses.text: In such wise do thou come too to Christ; do not conceive of 			 long journeyings; where thou believest, there thou comest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:36
verses.text: For unto Him, who is everywhere we come by love, not by sailing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:37
verses.text: But forasmuch as even in this kind of voyage, waves and tempests of divers temptations abound; believe on the Crucified; that thy faith may be able to ascend the Wood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:38
verses.text: Thou shalt not sink, but shalt be borne upon the Wood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:39
verses.text: Thus, even thus, amid the waves of this world did he sail, who said, "But God forbid that I should glory, save in the Cross of our Lord Jesus 			 Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:40
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:41
verses.text: But wonderful it is, that when Christ Crucified is preached, two hear, one despiseth, the other ascendeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:42
verses.text: Let him that despiseth, impute it to himself; let not him that ascendeth, arrogate it to himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:43
verses.text: For he hath heard from the True Master; "No man cometh unto Me, except it were given unto him of My Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:44
verses.text: Let him joy, that it hath been given; let him render thanks to Him who giveth it, with a humble, not an arrogant heart; lest what he 			 hath attained through humility, he lose through pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:45
verses.text: For even they who are already walking in this way of righteousness, if they attribute it to themselves, and to their own strength, perish out of it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:46
verses.text: And therefore Holy Scripture teaching us humility saith by the Apostle, "Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:47
verses.text: And lest hereupon they should attribute ought to themselves, because he said, "Work," he subjoined immediately, "For it is God who worketh in you both to will and to do of His good pleasure".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:48
