verses.text: "It is God who worketh in you;" therefore "with fear and trembling," make a valley, receive the rain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:49
verses.text: Low grounds are filled, high grounds are dried up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:50
verses.text: Grace is rain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:51
verses.text: Why dost thou marvel then, if "God resist the proud, and giveth grace unto the lowly"? Therefore, "with fear and trembling;" that is, with humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:52
verses.text: "Be not high-minded, but fear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:53
verses.text: Fear that thou mayest be filled; be not high-minded, lest thou be dried up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:54
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:55
verses.text: But you will say, "I am walking in this way already; once there was need for me to learn, there was need for me to know by the teaching of the law what I had to do: now I have the free choice of the will; who shall withdraw me from this way?" If thou read carefully, thou wilt find that a certain man began to uplift himself, on a certain abundance of his, which he had nevertheless received; but that the Lord in mercy, to teach him humility, took away what He 			 had given; and he was on a sudden reduced to poverty, and confessing the mercy of God in his recollection, he said, "In my abundance I said, I shall never be moved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:56
verses.text: "In my abundance I said".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:57
verses.text: But I said it, I who am a man said it; "All men are liars, I said".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:58
verses.text: Therefore, "in my abundance I said;" so great was the abundance, that I dared to say, "I shall never be moved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:59
verses.text: What next? "O Lord, in Thy favour Thou gavest strength to my beauty".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:60
verses.text: But "Thou turnedst away Thy Face from me, and I was troubled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:61
verses.text: "Thou hast shown me," saith he, "that that wherein I did abound, was of Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:62
verses.text: Thou hast shown me Whence I should seek, to Whom attribute what I had received, to Whom I ought to render thanks, to Whom I should run in my thirst, Whereby be filled, and with Whom keep that whereby I should be filled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:63
verses.text: 'For my strength will I keep to Thee;' whereby I am by Thy bounty filled, through Thy safe keeping I will not lose.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:64
verses.text: 'My strength will I keep to Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:65
verses.text: ' That Thou mightest show me this, 'Thou turnedst away Thy Face from me, and I was troubled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:66
verses.text: ' 'Troubled,' because dried up; dried up, because exalted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:67
verses.text: Say then thou dry and parched one, that thou mayest be filled again; 'My soul is as earth without water unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:68
verses.text: ' Say, 'My soul is as earth without water unto Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:69
verses.text: ' For Thou hast said, not the Lord, 'I shall never be moved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:70
verses.text: ' Thou hast said it, presuming on thine own strength; but it was not of thyself, and thou didst think as if it were".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:71
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:72
verses.text: What then doth the Lord say? "Serve ye the Lord in fear, and rejoice unto Him with trembling".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:73
verses.text: So the Apostle too, "Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:74
verses.text: For it is God who worketh in you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:75
verses.text: Therefore rejoice with trembling: "Lest at any time the Lord be angry".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:76
verses.text: I see that you anticipate me by your crying out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:77
verses.text: For you know what I am about to say, you anticipate it by crying out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:78
verses.text: And whence have ye this, but that He taught you to whom ye have by believing come? This then He saith; hear what ye know already; I am not teaching, but in preaching am 			 calling to your remembrance; nay, I am neither teaching, seeing that ye know already, nor calling to remembrance, seeing that ye remember, but let us say all together what together with us ye retain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:79
verses.text: "Embrace discipline, and rejoice," but, "with trembling," that, humble ye may ever hold fast that which ye have received.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:80
verses.text: "Lest at any time the Lord be angry;" with the proud of course, attributing to themselves what they have, not rendering thanks to Him, from whom they have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:81
verses.text: "Lest at any time the Lord be angry, and ye perish from the righteous way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:82
verses.text: Did he say, Lest at any time the Lord be angry, and ye come not into the righteous way"? Did he say, "Lest the Lord be angry, and He bring you not to the righteous way"? 			 or "admit you not into the righteous way? Ye are walking in it already, be not proud, lest ye even perish from it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:83
verses.text: 'And ye perish,' saith he, 'from the righteous way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:84
verses.text: '" "When His wrath shall be kindled in a short time" against you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:85
verses.text: At no distant time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:86
verses.text: As soon as thou art proud, thou losest at once what thou hadst received.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:87
verses.text: As though man terrified by all this were to say, "What shall I do then?" It follows, "Blessed are all they that trust in Him:" not in themselves, but in Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:88
verses.text: "By grace are we saved, not of ourselves, but it is the gift of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:89
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:90
verses.text: Peradventure ye are saying, "What does he mean, that he is so often saying this? A second and a third time he says it; and scarcely ever speaks, but when he says it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:91
verses.text: Would that I may not say it in vain! For men there are unthankful to grace, attributing much to poor and disabled nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:92
verses.text: True it is, when man was created he received great power of free-will; but he lost it by sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:93
verses.text: He fell into death, became infirm, was left in the way by the 			 robbers half dead; the Samaritan, which is by interpretation keeper, passing by lifted him up on his own beast; he is still being brought to the inn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:94
verses.text: Why is he lifted up? He is still in process of curing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:95
verses.text: "But," he will say, "it is enough for me that in baptism I received remission of all sins".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:96
verses.text: Because iniquity was blotted out, was therefore infirmity brought to an end? "I received," says he, "remission of all sins".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:97
verses.text: It is quite true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:98
verses.text: All sins were blotted out in the Sacrament of Baptism, all entirely, of words, deeds, thoughts, all were blotted out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:99
verses.text: But this is the 			 "oil and wine" which was poured in by the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:100
verses.text: Ye remember, beloved Brethren, that man who was wounded by the robbers, and half dead by the way, how he was strengthened, by receiving oil and wine for his wounds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:101
verses.text: His error indeed was already pardoned, and yet his weakness is in process of healing in the inn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:102
verses.text: The inn, if ye recognise it, is the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:103
verses.text: In the time present, an inn, because in life we are passing by: it will be a home, whence we shall never remove, when we shall have got in 			 perfect health unto the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:104
verses.text: Meanwhile receive we gladly our treatment in the inn, and weak as we still are, glory we not of sound health: lest through our pride we gain nothing else, but never for all our treatment to be cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:105
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:106
verses.text: "Bless the Lord, O my soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:107
verses.text: Say, yea say to thy soul, "Thou art still in this life, still bearest about a frail flesh, still "doth the corruptible body press down the soul;" still after the entireness of remission hast thou received the remedy of prayer; for still, whilst thy weaknesses are being healed, dost thou say, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:108
verses.text: Say then to thy soul, thou lowly valley, not an exalted hill; say to thy soul, "Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:109
verses.text: What benefits? Tell them, enumerate them, render thanks.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:110
verses.text: What benefits? "Who forgiveth all thine iniquities".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:111
verses.text: This took place in baptism.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:112
verses.text: What takes place now? "Who healeth all thy weaknesses".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:113
verses.text: This takes place now; I acknowledge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:114
verses.text: But as long as I am here, "the corruptible body presseth down the soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:115
verses.text: Say then also that which comes next, "Who redeemeth thy life from corruption".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:116
verses.text: After redemption from corruption, what remaineth? "When this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:117
verses.text: Where, O death, is thy contention?" There rightly, "O death, where is thy sting?" Thou seekest its place, and findest it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:118
verses.text: What is "the sting of death"? What is, "O death, where is thy sting?" Where is sin? Thou seekest, and it is nowhere.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:119
verses.text: For "the sting of death is sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:120
verses.text: They are the Apostle's words, not mine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:121
verses.text: Then shall it be said, "O death, where is thy sting?" Sin shall nowhere be, neither to surprise thee, nor to assault thee, nor to inflame thy conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:122
verses.text: Then it shall not be said, "Forgive us our debts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:123
verses.text: But what shall be said? "O Lord our God, give us peace: for Thou hast rendered all things unto us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:124
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:125
verses.text: Finally, after the redemption from all corruption, what remaineth but the crown of righteousness? This at least remaineth, but even in it, or under it, let not the head be swollen that it may receive the crown.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:126
verses.text: Hear, mark well the Psalm, how that crown will not have a swollen head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:127
verses.text: After he had said, "Who redeemeth thy life from corruption;" he saith, "Who crowneth thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:128
verses.text: Here thou wert ready at once to say, "'Crowneth thee,' is an acknowledgment of 			 my merits, my own excellence hath done it; it is the payment of a debt, not a gift".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:129
verses.text: Give ear rather to the Psalm.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:130
verses.text: For it is thou again that sayest this; and "all men are liars".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:131
verses.text: Hear what God saith; "Who crowneth thee with mercy and pity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:132
verses.text: Of His mercy He crowneth thee, of His pity He crowneth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:133
verses.text: For thou hadst no worthiness that He should call thee, and being called should justify thee, being justified glorify thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:134
verses.text: "The remnant is saved by the election of grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:135
verses.text: But if by grace, then is it no more of works; otherwise grace is no more grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:136
verses.text: For to him that worketh, the reward shall not be reckoned according to grace, but according to 			 debt".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:137
verses.text: The Apostle saith, "Not according to grace, but according to debt".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:138
verses.text: But "thee He crowneth with pity and mercy;" and if thy own merits have gone before, God saith to thee, "Examine well thy merits, and thou shalt see that they are My gifts".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:139
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:140
verses.text: This then is the righteousness of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:141
verses.text: As it is called, "The Lord's salvation," not whereby the Lord is saved, but which He giveth to them whom He saveth; so too the grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord is called the righteousness of God, not as that whereby the Lord is righteous, but whereby He justifieth those whom of ungodly He maketh righteous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:142
verses.text: But some, as the Jews in former times, both wish to be called Christians, and still ignorant of God's righteousness, desire to establish their own, even in our own times, in the times of open grace, the 			 times of the full revelation of grace which before was hidden; in the times of grace now manifested in the floor, which once lay hid in the fleece.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:143
verses.text: I see that a few have understood me, that more have not understood, whom I will by no means defraud by keeping silence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:144
verses.text: Gideon, one of the righteous men of old, asked for a sign from the Lord, and said, "I pray, Lord, that this fleece which I put in the floor be bedewed,and that the floor be dry".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:145
verses.text: And it was so; the fleece was bedewed, the whole floor was dry.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:146
verses.text: In the morning he wrung out the fleece in a basin; forasmuch as to the humble is grace given; and in a basin, ye know what the Lord did to His disciples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:147
verses.text: Again, he asked for another sign; "O Lord, I would," saith he, "that the fleece be dry, the floor bedewed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:148
verses.text: And it was so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:149
verses.text: Call to mind the time of the Old Testament, grace was hidden in a cloud, as the rain in the fleece.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:150
verses.text: Mark now the time of the New 			 Testament, consider well the nation of the Jews, thou wilt find it as a dry fleece; whereas the whole world, like that floor, is full of grace, not hidden, but manifested.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:151
verses.text: Wherefore we are forced exceedingly to bewail our brethren, who strive not against hidden, but against open and manifested grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:152
verses.text: There is allowance for the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:153
verses.text: What shall we say of Christians? Wherefore are ye enemies to the grace of Christ? Why rely ye on yourselves? Why unthankful? For why did Christ come? Was not nature 			 here before? Was not nature here, which ye only deceive by your excessive praise? Was not the Law here? But the Apostle says, "If righteousness come by the Law, then Christ is dead in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:154
verses.text: What the Apostle says of the Law, that say we of nature to these men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:155
verses.text: "If righteousness come by nature, then Christ is dead in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:156
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:157
verses.text: What then was said of the Jews, the same altogether do we see in these men now.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:158
verses.text: "They have a zeal of God: I hear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:159
verses.text: What is, "not according to knowledge"? "For being ignorant of God's righteousness, and wishing to establish their own, they have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:160
verses.text: My Brethren, share with me in my sorrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:161
verses.text: When ye find such as these, do not hide them; be there no such misdirected mercy in you; by all means, when ye find such, hide them not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:162
verses.text: Convince the gainsayers, and those who resist, bring to us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:163
verses.text: For already have two councils on this question been sent to the Apostolic see; and rescripts also have come from thence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:164
verses.text: The question has been brought to an issue; would that their error may sometime be brought to an issue too! Therefore do we advise that they may take heed, we teach that they may be instructed, we pray that they may be changed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 80:165
verses.text: Let us turn to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:2
verses.text: [CXXXII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John vi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:5
verses.text: 55 ,"For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:6
verses.text: He that eateth my flesh," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:8
verses.text: As we heard when the Holy Gospel was being read, the Lord Jesus Christ exhorted us by the promise of eternal life to eat His Flesh and drink His Blood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:9
verses.text: Ye that heard these words, have not all as yet understood them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:10
verses.text: For those of you who have been baptized and the faithful do know what He meant.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:11
verses.text: But those among you who are yet called Catechumens, or Hearers, could be hearers, when it was being read, could they be understanders too? 			 Accordingly our discourse is directed to both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:12
verses.text: Let them who already eat the Flesh of the Lord and drink His Blood, think What it is they eat and drink, lest, as the Apostle says, "They eat and drink judgment to themselves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:13
verses.text: But they who do not yet eat and drink, let them hasten when invited to such a Banquet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:14
verses.text: Throughout these days the teachers feed you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:15
verses.text: Christ daily feedeth you, That His Table is ever ordered before you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:16
verses.text: What is the reason.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:17
verses.text: O Hearers, that ye see the Table, and come not to the Banquet? And peradventure, just now when the Gospel was being read, ye said in your hearts, "We are thinking what it is that He saith, 'My Flesh is meat indeed, and My Blood is drink indeed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:18
verses.text: ' 			  How is the Flesh of the Lord eaten, and the Blood of the Lord drunk? We are thinking what He saith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:19
verses.text: Who hath closed it against thee, that thou dost not know this? There is a veil over it; but if thou wilt, the veil shall be taken away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:20
verses.text: Come to the profession, and thou hast resolved the difficulty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:21
verses.text: For what the Lord Jesus said, the faithful know well already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:22
verses.text: But thou art called a Catechumen, art called a Hearer, and art deaf.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:23
verses.text: For the ears of the booty thou hast open, seeing that thou hearest the words which were spoken; but the ears of the heart thou hast still closed, seeing thou understandest not what was spoken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:24
verses.text: I plead, I do not discuss it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:25
verses.text: Lo, Easter is at hand, give in thy name for baptism.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:26
verses.text: If the festivity arouse thee not, let the very curiosity induce thee: that thou mayest know the meaning of, Whoso eateth My Flesh and drinketh My Blood dwelleth in Me, and I in him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:27
verses.text: That thou mayest know with me what is meant, "Knock, and it shall be opened unto thee:" and as I say to thee, "Knock, and it shall be opened unto thee," so do I too knock, open thou to me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:28
verses.text: When I speak aloud to the ears, I knock at the breast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:29
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:30
verses.text: But if the Catechumens, my Brethren, are to be exhorted not to delay to approach to this so great grace of regeneration; what great care ought we to have in building up the faithful, that their approaching may profit them, and that they eat and drink not such a Banquet unto their own judgment? Now that they may not eat and drink unto judgment, let them live well.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:31
verses.text: Be ye exhorters, not by words, but by your conduct; that they who have not been baptized, may in such 			 wise hasten to follow you, that they perish not by imitating you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:32
verses.text: Do ye who are married keep the fidelity of the marriage-bed with your wives.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:33
verses.text: Render what you require.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:34
verses.text: As a husband thou requirest chastity from thy wife; give her an example, not words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:35
verses.text: Thou art the head, look where thou goest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:36
verses.text: For thou oughtest to go where it may not be dangerous for her to follow: yea, thou oughtest to walk thyself where thou wouldest have her follow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:37
verses.text: Thou requirest strength from the weaker sex; the lust of the 			 flesh ye have both of you: let him that is the stronger, be the first to conquer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:38
verses.text: And yet, which is to be lamented, many men are conquered by the women.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:39
verses.text: Women preserve chastity, which men will not preserve; and in that they preserve it not, would wish to appear men: as though he was in sex the stronger, only that the enemy might more easily subdue him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:40
verses.text: There is a struggle, a war, a combat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:41
verses.text: The man is stronger than the woman, the "man is the head of the woman".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:42
verses.text: The woman combats and overcomes; dost thou succumb to the enemy? The body stands firm, and does the head lie low? But those of you who have not yet wives, and who yet already approach to the Lord's Table, and eat the Flesh of Christ, and drink His Blood, if ye are about to marry, keep yourselves for your wives.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:43
verses.text: As ye would have them come to you, such ought they also to find you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:44
verses.text: What young man is there who would not wish to marry a chaste wife? And if he were to espouse a 			 virgin who would not desire she should be unpolluted? Thou lookest for one unpolluted, be unpolluted thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:45
verses.text: Thou lookest for one pure, be not thyself impure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:46
verses.text: For it is not that she is able, and thou art not able.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:47
verses.text: If it were not possible, then could not she be so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:48
verses.text: But, seeing that she can, let this teach thee, that it is possible.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:49
verses.text: And that she may have this power, God is her ruler.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:50
verses.text: But thou wilt have greater glory if thou shalt do it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:51
verses.text: Why greater glory? The vigilance of parents is a check to 			 her, the very modesty of the weaker sex is a bridle to her; lastly, she is in fear of the laws of which thou art not afraid.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:52
verses.text: Therefore it is then that thou wilt have greater glory if thou shalt do it; because if thou do it, thou fearest God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:53
verses.text: She has many things to fear besides God, thou fearest God alone.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:54
verses.text: But He whom thou fearest is greater than all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:55
verses.text: He is to be feared in public, He in secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:56
verses.text: Thou goest out, thou art seen; thou goest in, thou art seen; the lamp is lighted, He seeth thee; the 			 lamp is extinguished, He seeth thee; thou enterest into thy closet, He seeth thee; in the retirement of thine own heart, He seeth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:57
verses.text: Fear Him, Him whose care it is to see thee; and even by this fear be chaste.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:58
verses.text: Or if thou wilt sin, seek for some place where He may not see thee, and do what thou wouldest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:59
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:60
verses.text: But ye who have taken the vow already, chasten your bodies more strictly, and suffer not yourselves to loosen the reins of concupiscence even after those things which are permitted; that ye may not only turn away from an unlawful connection, but may despise even a lawful look.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:61
verses.text: Remember, in whichever sex ye are, whether men or women, that ye are leading on earth the life of Angels: "For the Angels are neither given in marriage, nor marry".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:62
verses.text: This shall we be, when we shall have risen again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:63
verses.text: How much better are ye, who before death begin to be what men will be after the resurrection! Keep your proper degrees, for God keepeth for you your honours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:64
verses.text: The resurrection of the dead is compared to the stars that are set in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:65
verses.text: "For star differeth from star in glory," as the Apostle says; "so also is the resurrection of the dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:66
verses.text: For after one manner virginity shall shine there, after another shall wedded chastity shine there, after another shall holy widowhood shine there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:67
verses.text: They shall shine diversely, but all shall be there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:68
verses.text: The brilliancy unequal, the heaven the same.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:69
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:70
verses.text: With your thoughts then on your degrees, and keeping your professions, approach ye to the Flesh of the Lord, approach to the Blood of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:71
verses.text: Whoso knoweth himself to be otherwise, let him not approach.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:72
verses.text: Be moved to compunction rather by my words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:73
verses.text: For they who know that they are keeping for their wives, what from their wives they require, they who know that they are in every way keeping continence, if this they have vowed to God, feel joy at my words; but they who 			 hear me say, "Whosoever of you are not keeping chastity, approach not to that Bread," are saddened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:74
verses.text: And I should have no wish to say this; but what can I do? Shall I fear man, so as to suppress the truth? What, if those servants do not fear the Lord, shall I therefore too not fear? as if I do not know that it is said, "'Thou wicked and slothful servant,' thou shouldest dispense, and I require".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:75
verses.text: Lo, I have dispensed, O Lord my God; lo, in Thy Sight, and in the sight of Thy Holy Angels, and of this Thy people, I have laid out Thy money; for I am afraid of Thy judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:76
verses.text: I have dispensed, do Thou require.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:77
verses.text: Though I should not say it, Thou wouldest do it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:78
verses.text: Therefore I rather say, I have dispensed, do Thou convert, do Thou spare.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:79
verses.text: Make them chaste who have been unchaste, that in Thy Sight we may rejoice together when the judgment 			 shall come, both he who hath dispensed and he to whom it hath been dispensed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:80
verses.text: Doth this please you? May it do so! Whosoever of you are unchaste, amend yourselves, whilst ye are alive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 81:81
verses.text: For I have power to speak the word of God, but to deliver the unchaste, who persevere in wickedness, from the judgment and condemnation of God, have I no power.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:2
verses.text: [CXXXIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel of John vii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:5
verses.text: 6 , etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:6
verses.text: , where Jesus said that He was not going up unto the feast, and notwithstanding went up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:8
verses.text: I Purpose by the Lord's assistance to treat of this section of the Gospel which has just been read; nor is there a little difficulty here, lest the truth be endangered, and falsehood glory.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:9
verses.text: Not that either the truth can perish, nor falsehood triumph.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:10
verses.text: Now hearken for a while what difficulty this lesson has; and being made attentive by the propounding of the difficulty, pray that I may be sufficient for its solution.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:11
verses.text: "The Jews' feast of tabernacles was at hand;" these it seems are the days which they observe even to this day, when they build huts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:12
verses.text: For this solemnity of theirs is called from the building of tabernacles; since σκηνὴ means a "tabernacle," σκηνοπηγία is the building of a tabernacle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:13
verses.text: These days were kept as feast days among the Jews; and it was called one feast day, not because it was over in one day, but because it was kept up by a continued festivity; just as the feast day of the Passover, and the feast day of unleavened 			 bread, and notwithstanding, as is manifest, that feast is kept throughout many days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:14
verses.text: This anniversary then was at hand in Judaea, the Lord Jesus was in Galilee, where He had also been brought up, where too He had relations and kinsfolk, whom Scripture calls "His brethren".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:15
verses.text: "His brethren, therefore," as we have heard it read, "said unto Him, Pass from hence, and go into Judaea; that Thy disciples also may see Thy works that Thou doest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:16
verses.text: For no man doeth anything in secret, and himself 			 seeketh to be known openly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:17
verses.text: If Thou do these things, manifest Thyself to the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:18
verses.text: Then the Evangelist subjoins, "For neither did His brethren believe in Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:19
verses.text: If then they did not believe in Him, the words they threw out were of envy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:20
verses.text: "Jesus answered them, My time is not yet come; but your time is alway ready.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:21
verses.text: The world cannot hate you; but Me it hateth, because I testify of it that the works thereof are evil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:22
verses.text: Go ye up to this feast day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:23
verses.text: I go not up to this feast day, for My time is not yet accomplished".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:24
verses.text: Then follows the Evangelist; "When He had said these words, He Himself stayed in Galilee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:25
verses.text: But when His brethren were gone up, then went He also up to the feast day, not openly, but as it were in secret".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:26
verses.text: Thus far is the extent of the difficulty, all the rest is clear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:27
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:28
verses.text: What then is the difficulty? what makes the perplexity? what is in peril? Lest the Lord, yea, to speak more plainly, lest the Truth Itself should be thought to have lied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:29
verses.text: For if we would have it thought that He lied, the weak will receive an authority for lying.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:30
verses.text: We have heard say that He lied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:31
verses.text: For those who think that He lied, speak thus, "He said that He should not go up to the feast day, and He went up".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:32
verses.text: In the first place then, let us, as far as in the 			 press of time we can, see whether he does lie, who says a thing and does it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:33
verses.text: For example, I have told a friend, "I will see you to-morrow;" some greater necessity occurs to hinder me; I have not on that account spoken falsely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:34
verses.text: For when I made the promise, I meant what I said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:35
verses.text: But when some greater matter occurred, which hindered the accomplishment of my promise, I had no design to lie, but I was not able to fulfil the promise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:36
verses.text: Lo, to my thinking I have used no labour to persuade you, but have merely suggested to your good sense, that he who promises something, and doeth it not, does not lie, if, that he do it not, something has occurred to hinder the fulfilment of his promise, not to be any proof of falsehood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:37
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:38
verses.text: But some one who hears me will say, "Canst thou then say this of Christ, that He either was not able to fulfil what He would, or that He did not know things to come?" Thou doest well, good is thy suggestion, right thy hint; but, O man, share with me my anxiety.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:39
verses.text: Dare we to say that He lies, Who we do not dare to say is weak in power? I for my part, to the best of my thinking, as far as according to my infirmity I am able to judge, would choose 			 that a man should be deceived in any matter rather than lie in any.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:40
verses.text: For to be deceived is the portion of infirmity, to lie of iniquity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:41
verses.text: "Thou hatest, O Lord," saith he, "all them that work iniquity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:42
verses.text: And immediately after, "Thou shalt destroy all them that speak a lie".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:43
verses.text: Either "iniquity" and "a lie" are upon a level; or, "Thou shalt destroy," is more than "Thou hatest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:44
verses.text: For he who is held in hatred, is not immediately punished by destruction.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:45
verses.text: But let that question be, whether there be ever a necessity to lie; for I am not now discussing that; it is a dark question, and has many lappings; I have not time to cut them, and to come to the quick.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:46
verses.text: Therefore let the treatment of it be deferred to some other time; for peradventure it will be cured by the Divine assistance without any words of mine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:47
verses.text: But attend and distinguish between what I have deferred, and what I wish to treat of to-day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:48
verses.text: Whether on any occasion one may lie, this difficult and most obscure question I defer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:49
verses.text: But whether Christ lied, whether the Truth spake anything false, this, being reminded of it by the Gospel lesson, have I undertaken 			 to-day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:50
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:51
verses.text: Now what the difference is between being deceived, and lying, I will briefly state.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:52
verses.text: He is deceived who thinks what he says to be true, and therefore says it, because he thinks it true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:53
verses.text: Now if this which he that is deceived says, were true, he would not be deceived; if it were not only true, but he also knew it to be true, he would not lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:54
verses.text: He is deceived then, in that it is false, and he thinks it true; but he only says it because he thinks it true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:55
verses.text: The error 			 lies in human infirmity, not in the soundness of the conscience.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:56
verses.text: But whosoever thinks it to be false, and asserts it as true, he lies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:57
verses.text: See, my Brethren, draw the distinction, ye who have been brought up in the Church, instructed in the Lord's Scriptures, not uninformed, nor simple, nor ignorant men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:58
verses.text: For there are among you men learned and erudite, and not indifferently instructed in all kinds of literature; and with those of you who have not learnt that literature which is called liberal, it is more that ye have been nourished up in the word of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:59
verses.text: If I labour in explaining what I mean, do ye aid me both by the attention of your hearing, and the thoughtfulness of your meditations.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:60
verses.text: Nor will ye aid, unless ye are aided.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:61
verses.text: Wherefore pray we mutually for one another, and look equally for our common Succour.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:62
verses.text: He is deceived, who whereas what he says is false, thinks it to be true; but he lies, who thinks a thing to be false, and gives it out as true, whether it be true or false.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:63
verses.text: Observe what I have added, "whether it be true or false;" yet he who thinks it to be false, and asserts it as true, lies; he aims to deceive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:64
verses.text: For what good is 			 it to him, that it is true? He all the while thinks it false, and says it as if it were true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:65
verses.text: What he says is true in itself, it is in itself true; with regard to him it is false, his conscience does not hold that which he is saying; he thinks in himself one thing to be true, he gives out another for truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:66
verses.text: His is a double heart, not single; he does not bring out that which he has in it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:67
verses.text: The double heart has long since been condemned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:68
verses.text: "With deceitful lips in a heart and a heart have they 			 spoken evil things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:69
verses.text: Had it been enough to say, "in the heart have they spoken evil things," where is the "deceitful lips"? What is deceit? When one thing is done, another pretended.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:70
verses.text: Deceitful lips are not a single heart; and because not a single heart, therefore "in a heart and a heart;" therefore "in a heart" twice, because the heart is double.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:71
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:72
verses.text: How then think we of the Lord Jesus Christ, that He lied? If it is a less evil to be deceived than to lie, dare we to say that He lies who we dare not to say is deceived? But He is neither deceived, nor doth He lie; but in very deed as it is written (for of Him is it understood, of Him ought it to be understood), "Nothing false is said unto the King, and nothing false shall proceed out of His mouth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:73
verses.text: If by King here he meant any man, let us prefer Christ the 			 King, to a man-king.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:74
verses.text: But if, which is the truer understanding of it, it is Christ of whom he spake, if I say, as is the truer understanding of it, it is Christ of whom he spake (for to Him indeed nothing false is said, in that He is not deceived; from His Mouth nothing false proceedeth, in that He doth not lie); let us look how we are to understand the section of the Gospel, and let us not make the pitfall of a lie, as it were, on heavenly authority.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:75
verses.text: But it is most absurd to be seeking to explain the truth, and to prepare a place for a lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:76
verses.text: What art thou teaching me, I ask thee, who art explaining this text to me, what wouldest thou teach me? I do not know whether you would dare to say, "Falsehood".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:77
verses.text: For if you should dare to say this, I turn away mine ears, and fasten them up with thorns, that if you should try to force your way, I might through their very pricking 			 make away without the explanation of the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:78
verses.text: Tell me what thou wouldest wish to teach me, and thou hast resolved the difficulty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:79
verses.text: Tell me, I pray thee; lo, here I am; mine ears are open, my heart is ready, teach me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:80
verses.text: But I ask, what? I will not travel through many things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:81
verses.text: What art thou going to teach me? Whatsoever learning thou art about to bring forward, whatsoever strength to show in disputation, tell me this one thing only, one of two things I ask; art thou going to 			 teach me truth or falsehood? What do we suppose he will answer lest one depart; lest while he is open-mouthed and making an effort to bring out his words, I forthwith leave him: what will he promise but truth? I am listening, standing, expecting, most earnestly expecting.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:82
verses.text: See here, he who promised that he will teach me truth, insinuates falsehood concerning Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:83
verses.text: How then shall he teach truth, who would say that Christ is false? If Christ is false, can I hope that thou wilt tell me the 			 truth?  6.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:84
verses.text: Consider again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:85
verses.text: What does he say? Hath Christ spoken falsely? Where, I ask thee? "Where He says, 'I go not up to the feast day;' and went up".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:86
verses.text: For my part, I should wish thoroughly to examine this place, if so be we may see that Christ did not speak falsely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:87
verses.text: Yea rather, seeing that I have no doubt that Christ did not speak falsely, I will either thoroughly examine this passage and understand it, or, not understanding it, I will defer it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:88
verses.text: Yet that Christ 			 spoke falsely will I never say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:89
verses.text: Grant that I have not understood it; I will depart in my ignorance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:90
verses.text: For better is it with piety to be ignorant, than with madness to pronounce judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:91
verses.text: Notwithstanding we are trying to examine, if so be by His assistance, who is the Truth, we may find something, and be found something ourselves, and this something will not be in the Truth a lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:92
verses.text: For if in searching I find a lie, I find not a something but a nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:93
verses.text: Let us then look where it is thou sayest that 			 Christ lied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:94
verses.text: He will say, "In that He said, 'I go not up to this feast,' and went up".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:95
verses.text: Whence dost thou know that He said so? What if I were to say, nay, not I, but any one, for God forbid that I should say it; what if another were to say, "Christ did not say this;" whereby dost thou refute him, whereby wilt thou prove it? Thou wouldest open the book, find the passage, point it out to the man, yea with great confidence force the book upon him if he resisted, "Hold it, mark, read, 			 it is the Gospel you have in your hands".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:96
verses.text: But why, I ask thee, why dost thou so rudely accost this feeble one? Do not be so eager; speak more composedly, more tranquilly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:97
verses.text: See, it is the Gospel I have in my hands; and what is there in it? He answers: "The Gospel declares that Christ said what thou deniest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:98
verses.text: And wilt thou believe that Christ said it, because the Gospel declares it? "Decidedly for that reason," says he.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:99
verses.text: I marvel exceedingly how thou shouldest say that Christ lieth, and the Gospel doth not lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:100
verses.text: But lest haply when I speak of the Gospel, thou 			 shouldest think of the book itself, and imagine the parchment and ink to be the Gospel, see what the Greek word means; Gospel is "a good messenger," or "a good message".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:101
verses.text: The messenger then doth not lie, and doth He who sent him, lie? This messenger, the Evangelist to wit, to give his name also, this John who wrote this, did he lie concerning Christ, or say the truth? Choose which you will, I am ready to hear you on either side.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:102
verses.text: If he spake falsely, you have no means of proving that 			 Christ spake those words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:103
verses.text: If he said the truth, truth cannot flow from the fountain of falsehood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:104
verses.text: Who is the Fountain? Christ: let John be the stream.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:105
verses.text: The stream comes to me, and you say to me, "Drink securely;" yea, whereas you alarm me as to the Fountain Himself, whereas you tell me there is falsehood in the Fountain, you say to me, "Drink securely".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:106
verses.text: What do I drink? What said John, that Christ spake falsely? Whence came John? From Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:107
verses.text: Is he who came from Him, to tell me truth, 			 when He from whom he came lied? I have read in the Gospel plainly, "John lay on the Lord's Breast;" but I conclude that he drank in truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:108
verses.text: What saw he as he lay on the Lord's Breast? What drank he in? what, but that which he poured forth? "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:109
verses.text: The Same was in the beginning with God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:110
verses.text: All things were made by Him, and without Him was nothing made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:111
verses.text: That which was made in Him was life, and the Life was the Light of men; And the Light shineth in darkness, and the darkness comprehended It not;" 			  nevertheless It shineth, and though I chance to have some obscurity, and cannot thoroughly comprehend It, still It shineth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:112
verses.text: "There was a man sent from God, whose name was John; he came to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:113
verses.text: He was not the Light:" who? John: who? John the Baptist.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:114
verses.text: For of him saith John the Evangelist, "He was not the Light;" of whom the Lord saith, "He was a burning, and a shining lamp".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:115
verses.text: But a lamp can be lighted, and extinguished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:116
verses.text: What then? whence drawest thou the distinction? of what place art thou enquiring? He to whom the lamp bare witness, "was the True Light".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:117
verses.text: Where John added, "the True," there art thou looking out for a lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:118
verses.text: But hear still the same Evangelist John pouring forth what he had drunk in; "And we beheld," saith he, "His glory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:119
verses.text: What did he behold? what glory beheld he? "The glory as of the Only-Begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:120
verses.text: See then, see, if we ought not haply to restrain weak or rash disputings, and to presume nothing false of the truth, to give to the Lord what is His due; let us give glory to the Fountain, that we may fill ourselves securely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:121
verses.text: "Now God is true, but every man a liar".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:122
verses.text: What is this? God is full; every man is empty; if he will be filled, let him come to Him That is full.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:123
verses.text: "Come unto Him, and be enlightened".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:124
verses.text: Moreover, if man is empty, in that he is a liar, and he seeks to be filled, and with haste and eagerness runs to the fountain, he wishes to be filled, he is empty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:125
verses.text: But thou sayest, "Beware of the fountain, there is falsehood there".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:126
verses.text: What else sayest thou, but "there is poison there"?  7.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:127
verses.text: "You have already," he says, "said all, already have you checked, already chastened me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:128
verses.text: But tell me how He did not speak falsely who said, 'I go not up,' and went up?" I will tell you, if I can; but think it no little matter, that if I have not established you in the truth, I have yet kept you back from rashness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:129
verses.text: I will nevertheless tell you, what I imagine you know even already, if you remember the words which I have set forth to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:130
verses.text: The words 			 themselves solve the difficulty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:131
verses.text: That feast was kept for many days.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:132
verses.text: On this, that is this present feast day, saith He, this day, that is when they hoped, He went not up; but when He Himself resolved to go.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:133
verses.text: Now mark what follows, "When He had said these words, He Himself stayed in Galilee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:134
verses.text: So then He did not go up on that feast day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:135
verses.text: For His brethren wished that He should go first; therefore had they said, "Pass from hence into Judaea".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:136
verses.text: They did not say, "Let us pass," as though they 			 would be His companions; or, "Follow us into Judaea," as though they would go first; but as though they would send Him before them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:137
verses.text: He wished that they should go before; He avoided this snare, impressing His infirmity as Man, hiding the Divinity; this He avoided, as when He fled into Egypt.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:138
verses.text: For this was no effect of want of power, but even of truth, that He might give an example of caution; that no servant of His might say, "I do not fly, because it is disgraceful;" when haply it might be expedient to fly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:139
verses.text: As He was going to say to His disciples, "When they have persecuted you in this city, flee ye into another;" He gave them Himself this example.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:140
verses.text: For He was apprehended, when He willed; He was born, when He willed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:141
verses.text: That they might not anticipate Him then, and announce that He was coming, and plots be prepared; He said, "I go not up to this feast day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:142
verses.text: He said, "I go not up," that He might be hid; He added "this," that He might not lie.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:143
verses.text: Something He expressed, something He suppressed, something He repressed; yet said He nothing false, for "nothing false proceedeth out of His Mouth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:144
verses.text: Finally, after He had said these words, "When His brethren were gone up;" the Gospel declares it, attend, read what you have objected to me; see if the passage itself do not solve the difficulty, see if I have taken from anywhere else what to say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:145
verses.text: This then the Lord was waiting for, that they should go up first, that they might not announce beforehand that He was coming, "When His brethren were gone up, then went He also up to the feast day, not openly, but as it were in secret".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:146
verses.text: What is, "as it were in secret"? He acts there as if in 			 secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:147
verses.text: What is, "as it were in secret"? Because neither was this really in secret.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:148
verses.text: For He did not really make an effort to be concealed, who had it in His Own power when He would be taken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:149
verses.text: But in that concealment, as I have said, He gave His weak disciples, who had not the power to prevent being taken when they would not, an example of being on their guard against the snares of enemies.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:150
verses.text: For He went up afterwards even openly, and taught them in the temple; and some said, "' Lo, this is 			 He; lo, He is teaching.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:151
verses.text: ' Certainly our rulers said that they wished to apprehend Him: 'Lo, He speaketh openly, and no one layeth hands on Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:152
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:153
verses.text: But now if we turn our attention to ourselves, if we think of His Body, how that we are even He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:154
verses.text: For if we were not He, "Forasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of Mine, ye have done it unto Me," would not be true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:155
verses.text: If we were not He, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me?" would not be true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:156
verses.text: So then we are He, in that we are His members, in that we are His Body, in that He is our Head, in that Whole Christ is both Head and Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:157
verses.text: Peradventure then He foresaw us that we were not to keep the feast days of the Jews, and this is, "I go not up to this feast day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:158
verses.text: See neither Christ nor the Evangelist lied; of the which two if one must needs choose one, the Evangelist would pardon me, I would by no means put him that is true before the Truth Himself; I would not prefer him that was sent to Him by whom he was sent.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:159
verses.text: But God be thanked, in my judgment what was obscure has been laid open.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:160
verses.text: Your piety will aid 			 me before God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:161
verses.text: Behold, I have, as I was best able, resolved the question, both concerning Christ and the Evangelist.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 82:162
verses.text: Hold fast the truth with me as men who love it, embrace charity without contention.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:2
verses.text: [CXXXV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John ix.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:5
verses.text: 4 and 31, "We must work the works of him that sent me," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:6
verses.text: Against the Arians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:7
verses.text: And of that which the man who was born blind and received his sight said, "We know that God heareth not sinners".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:8
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:9
verses.text: The Lord Jesus, as we heard when the Holy Gospel was being read, opened the eyes of a man who was born blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:10
verses.text: Brethren, if we consider our hereditary punishment, the whole world is blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:11
verses.text: And therefore came Christ the Enlightener, because the devil had been the Blinder.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:12
verses.text: He made all men to be born blind, who seduced the first man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:13
verses.text: Let them run to the Enlightener, let them run, believe, receive the clay made of the spittle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:14
verses.text: The Word is as 			 it were the spittle, the Flesh is the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:15
verses.text: Let them wash the face in the pool of Siloa.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:16
verses.text: Now it was the Evangelist's place to explain to us what Siloa means, and he said, "which is by interpretation, Sent".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:17
verses.text: Who is This That is Sent, but He who in this very Lesson said, "I am come to do the works of Him That sent Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:18
verses.text: Lo, Siloa, wash the face, be baptized, that ye may be enlightened, and that ye who before saw not, may see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:19
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:20
verses.text: Lo, first open your eyes to that which is said; "I am come," saith He, "to do the works of Him That sent Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:21
verses.text: Now here at once stands forth the Arian, and says, "Here you see that Christ did not His Own works, but the Father's who sent Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:22
verses.text: Would he say this, if he saw, that is, if he had washed his face in Him who was sent, as it were in Siloa? What then dost thou say? "Lo," says he, "Himself said it".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:23
verses.text: What said He? "I am come to do the 			 works of Him That sent Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:24
verses.text: Are they not then His Own? No.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:25
verses.text: What then is that which the Siloa Himself saith, the Sent Himself, the Son Himself, the Only Son Himself, whom thou complainest of as degenerate? What is that He saith, "All things that the Father hath are Mine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:26
verses.text: You say that He did the works of Another, in that He said, "I must do the works of Him That sent Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:27
verses.text: I say that the Father had the things of another: I am speaking according to your principles.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:28
verses.text: Why would you object to me that Christ said, "I am come to do His works" as if, "not Mine own but 'His That sent Me'"?  3.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:29
verses.text: I ask Thee, O Lord Christ, resolve the difficulty, put an end to the contention.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:30
verses.text: "All things," saith He, "that the Father hath are Mine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:31
verses.text: Are they then not the Father's, if they are Thine? For He doth not say, "All things that the Father hath He hath given unto Me;" although, if He had said even this, He would have shown His equality.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:32
verses.text: But the difficulty is that He said, "All things that the Father hath are Mine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:33
verses.text: If you understand it aright, All 			 things that the Father hath, are the Son's; all things that the Son hath, are the Father's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:34
verses.text: Hear Him in another place; "All Mine are Thine, and Thine are Mine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:35
verses.text: The question is finished, as to the things which the Father and the Son have: they have them with one consent, do not thou introduce dissension.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:36
verses.text: What He calleth the works of the Father, are His Own works; for, "Thine too are Mine," for He speaketh of the works of That Father, to whom He said, "All Mine are Thine, and Thine are Mine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:37
verses.text: So then, My works are Thine, and Thy works are Mine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:38
verses.text: "For what things soever the Father doeth;" Himself hath said, the Lord hath said, the Only-Begotten hath said, the Son hath said, the Truth hath said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:39
verses.text: What hath He said? "What things soever the Father doeth, these also doeth the Son in like manner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:40
verses.text: Signal expression! signal truth! signal equality.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:41
verses.text: "All things that the Father doeth, these doeth the Son also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:42
verses.text: Were it enough to say, "All things that the Father doeth, these doeth the Son also"? It is not enough; I add, "in like manner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:43
verses.text: Why do I add, 			 "in like manner"? Because they who do not understand, and who walk with eyes not yet open, are wont to say, "The Father doeth them by way of command, the Son of obedience, therefore not in like manner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:44
verses.text: But if in like manner, as the One, so the Other; so what things the One, the same the Other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:45
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:46
verses.text: "But," says he, "the Father commands, that the Son may execute".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:47
verses.text: Carnal indeed is thy conceit, but without prejudice to the truth, I grant it to you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:48
verses.text: Lo, the Father commands, the Son obeys; is the Son therefore not of the same Nature, because the One commands, and the Other obeys? Give me two men, father and son; they are two men: he that commands is a man; he that obeys is a man; he that commands and he that obeys have one and the same nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:49
verses.text: Does not he that 			 commands, beget a son of his own nature? Does he who obeys, by obeying lose his nature? Now take for the present, as you thus take two men, the Father commanding, the Son obeying, yet God and God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:50
verses.text: But the first two together are two men, the Latter together is but One God; this is a divine miracle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:51
verses.text: Meanwhile if you would that with you I acknowledge the obedience, do you first with me acknowledge the Nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:52
verses.text: The Father begat That which Himself is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:53
verses.text: If the Father begat ought else than what Himself 			 is, He did not beget a true Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:54
verses.text: The Father saith to the Son, "From the womb before the day-star, I begat Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:55
verses.text: What is, "before the day-star"? By the day-star times are signified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:56
verses.text: So then before times, before all that is called "before;" before all that is not, or before all that is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:57
verses.text: For the Gospel does not say, "In the beginning God made the Word;" as it is said, "In the beginning God made the Heaven and the earth;" or, "In the beginning was the Word born;" or, "In the beginning God begat the Word".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:58
verses.text: But what says it? "He was, He was, He was".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:59
verses.text: You hear, "He was;" believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:60
verses.text: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:61
verses.text: So often do ye hear, "Was:" seek not for time, for that He always "was".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:62
verses.text: He then who always was, and was always with the Son, for that God is able to beget without thee; He said to the Son, "From the womb before the day-star I begat Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:63
verses.text: What is from the womb? Had God a womb? Shall we imagine that God was fashioned with bodily members? God forbid! And why said He, "From the womb," but that it might be understood that He begat Him of His Own Substance? So then 			 from the womb came forth That which Himself was who begat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:64
verses.text: For if He who begat was one thing, and another came forth out of the womb; it were a monster, not a Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:66
verses.text: Therefore let the Son do the works of Him That sent Him, and the Father also do the works of the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:67
verses.text: "At all events," you say, "the Father wills, the Son executes".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:68
verses.text: Lo, I show, that the Son willeth, and the Father executeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:69
verses.text: Do you say, "where dost thou show this?" I show it at once.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:70
verses.text: "Father, I will".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:71
verses.text: Now here if I had a mind to cavil, lo, the Son commandeth, and the Father executeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:72
verses.text: What wilt Thou? "That where I am, they may be also with Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:73
verses.text: We have escaped, there shall we be, where He is; there shall we be, we have escaped.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:74
verses.text: Who can undo the "I Will" of the Almighty? You hear the will of His power, hear now the power of His will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:75
verses.text: "As the Father" saith He "raiseth up the dead and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom He will".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:76
verses.text: "Whom He will".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:77
verses.text: Say not, The Son quickeneth them, whom the Father commandeth Him to quicken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:78
verses.text: "He quickeneth whom He will".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:79
verses.text: So then whom the Father will, and whom Himself will: because where there is One Power, there is One Will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:80
verses.text: Let us then in a heart blind no more hold fast that the Nature of the Father and the Son is One and the Same; because the Father is very Father, the Son is very Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:81
verses.text: What He is, That did He beget: because the Begotten was not 			 degenerate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:82
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:83
verses.text: There is a something in the words of that man who was blind, which may cause perplexity, and peradventure make many who understand them not aright despair.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:84
