verses.text: For he said amongst the rest of his words, the same man whose eyes were opened, "We know that God heareth not sinners".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:85
verses.text: What shall we do, if God heareth not sinners? Dare we pray to God if He heareth not sinners? Give me one who may pray: lo, here is One to hear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:86
verses.text: Give me one who may pray, sift thoroughly the human race from the imperfect to the perfect.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:87
verses.text: Mount up from the spring to the summer; for this we have just chanted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:88
verses.text: "Thou hast made summer and spring;" that is, "Those who are already spiritual, and those who are still carnal hast Thou made;" for so the Son Himself saith, "Thine Eyes have seen My imperfect being".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:89
verses.text: That which is imperfect in My Body, Thine Eyes have seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:90
verses.text: And what then? Have they who are imperfect hope? Undoubtedly they have.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:91
verses.text: Hear what follows; "And in Thy Book shall all be written".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:92
verses.text: But perhaps, Brethren, the spiritual pray and are heard, because they are not sinners? What then must the carnal do? What must they do? Shall they perish? Shall they not pray to God? God forbid! Give me that publican in the Gospel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:93
verses.text: Come, thou publican, stand forth, show thy hope, that 			 the weak may not lose hope.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:94
verses.text: For behold the publican went up with the Pharisee to pray, and with face cast down upon the ground, standing afar off, beating his breast, he said, "Lord, be merciful to me a sinner.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:95
verses.text: And he went down justified rather than the Pharisee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:96
verses.text: Said he true or false, who said, "Be merciful to me a sinner"? If he said true, he was a sinner; yet was he heard and justified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:97
verses.text: What then is that, that thou whose eyes the Lord opened didst say, "We know that God heareth not sinners"? Lo, God doth hear sinners.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:98
verses.text: But wash thou thy inferior face, let that be done in thy heart, which hath been done in thy face; and thou wilt see that God doth hear sinners.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:99
verses.text: The imagination of thine heart hath deceived thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:100
verses.text: There is still something for Him to do to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:101
verses.text: We see that this man was cast out of the synagogue; Jesus heard of it, came to him, and said to him, "Dost thou believe on the Son of God?" And He said, "Who is He, Lord, that I should believe on Him?" 			  He saw, and did not see; he saw with the eyes, but as yet with the heart he saw not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:102
verses.text: The Lord said to him, "Thou both seest Him," that is, with the eyes; "and He that talketh with thee is He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:103
verses.text: He then fell down, and worshipped Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:104
verses.text: Then washed he the face of his heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:105
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:106
verses.text: Apply yourselves then earnestly to prayer, ye sinners: confess your sins, pray that they may be blotted out, pray that they may be diminished, pray that as ye increase, they may decrease: yet do not despair, and sinners though ye be, pray.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:107
verses.text: For who hath not sinned? Begin with the priests.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:108
verses.text: To the priests it is said, "First offer sacrifices for your own sins, and so for the people".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:109
verses.text: The sacrifices convicted the priests that if any one should call himself righteous and without sin, it might be answered him, "I look not at what thou sayest, but at what thou offerest; thine own victim convicteth thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:110
verses.text: Wherefore dost thou offer for thine own sins, if thou have no sins? Dost thou in thy sacrifice lie unto God?" But peradventure the priests of the ancient people were sinners; of the new people are not sinners.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:111
verses.text: Of a truth, Brethren, for that God hath so 			 willed, I am His priest; I am a sinner; with you do I beat the breast, with you I ask for pardon, with you I hope that God will be merciful.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:112
verses.text: But peradventure the Holy Apostles, those first and highest leaders of the flock, shepherds, members of The Shepherd, these peradventure had no sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:113
verses.text: Yes, indeed, even they had, they had indeed; they are not angry at this, for they confess it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:114
verses.text: I should not dare.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:115
verses.text: First hear the Lord Himself saying to the Apostles, "In this manner pray ye".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:116
verses.text: As those other priests were convicted by the sacrifices, so these by prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:117
verses.text: And amongst the other things which He commanded them to pray for, He appointed this also, "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:118
verses.text: What do the Apostles say? Every day they pray for their debts to be forgiven them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:119
verses.text: They come in debtors, they go out absolved, and return debtors to prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:120
verses.text: This life is not without sin, that as often as prayer is made, so often should sins be forgiven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:121
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:122
verses.text: But what shall I say? Peradventure when they learnt the prayer, they were still weak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:123
verses.text: Some one, perhaps, will say this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:124
verses.text: When the Lord Jesus taught them that prayer, they were yet babes, weak, carnal; they were not yet spiritual, who have no sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:125
verses.text: What then, Brethren? When they became spiritual, did they cease to pray? Then Christ ought to have said, "Pray in such wise now;" and to have given them, when spiritual, another prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:126
verses.text: It is one and the same.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:127
verses.text: He who 			 gave it is One and the Same; use it then in prayer in the Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:128
verses.text: But we will take away all controversy, when you say the Holy Apostles were spiritual, up to the time of the Lord's Passion they were carnal; this you must say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:129
verses.text: And indeed, the truth is, as He was hanging, they were in alarm, and the Apostles then despaired when the robber believed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:130
verses.text: Peter dared to follow, when the Lord was led to suffering, he dared to follow, who came to the house, and was wearied in the palace, and stood at 			 the fire, and was cold; he stood at the fire, he was frozen with a chilling fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:131
verses.text: Being questioned by the maid-servant, he denied Christ once; being questioned a second time, he denied Him; being questioned a third time, he denied Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:132
verses.text: God be thanked, that the questioning ceased; if the questioning had not ceased, long would the denial have been repeated.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:133
verses.text: So then after He rose again, then He confirmed them, then did they become spiritual.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:134
verses.text: Had they at that time then no sin? The Apostles spiritual, wrote spiritual epistles, they sent them to the Churches; "they had no sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:135
verses.text: This you say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:136
verses.text: I do not believe you, I ask themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:137
verses.text: Tell us, O holy Apostles, after the Lord rose again, and confirmed you with the 			 Holy Ghost sent from heaven; did ye cease to have sin? Tell us, I pray you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:138
verses.text: Let us hear, that sinners may not despair, that they may not leave off to pray to God, because they are not without sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:139
verses.text: Tell us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:140
verses.text: One of them saith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:141
verses.text: And who? He whom the Lord loved the most, and who lay on the Lord's Breast, and drank in the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven which he was to pour forth again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:142
verses.text: Him I ask; "Have ye sin or not?" He maketh answer and saith, "If we shall say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:143
verses.text: Now it is the same John who said, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:144
verses.text: See ye what heights he had passed, that he could reach to the Word! Such an one, and so great, who like an eagle soared above the clouds, who in the serene clearness of his mind saw, "In the beginning was the Word;" he hath said, "If we shall say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:145
verses.text: But if we shall confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 83:146
verses.text: Therefore pray ye.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:2
verses.text: [CXXXVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:4
verses.text: ]  On the same lesson of the Gospel, John ix.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:5
verses.text: , on the giving sight to the man that was born blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:7
verses.text: We have heard the lesson of the Holy Gospel which we are in the habit of hearing; but it is a good thing to be reminded: good to refresh the memory from the lethargy of forgetfulness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:8
verses.text: And in fact this very old lesson has given us as much pleasure as if it were new.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:9
verses.text: Christ gave sight to one blind from his birth; why do we marvel? Christ is the Saviour; by an act of mercy He made up that which He had not given in 			 the womb.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:10
verses.text: Now when He gave that man no eyes, it was no mistake of His surely; but a delay with a view to a miracle.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:11
verses.text: You are saying, it may be, "Whence knowest thou this?" From Himself I have heard it; He just now said it; we heard it all together.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:12
verses.text: For when His disciples asked Him, and said, "Lord, who did sin, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?" What answer He made, ye, as I did, heard.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:13
verses.text: "Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents, but that the works of God should be made manifest in him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:14
verses.text: Lo then wherefore it was that He delayed when He gave him no eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:15
verses.text: He did not give what He could give, He did not give what He knew He should give, when need was.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:16
verses.text: Yet do not suppose, Brethren, that this man's parents had no sin, or that he himself had not, when he was born, contracted original sin, for the remission of which sin infants are baptized unto remission of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:17
verses.text: But that blindness was not because of his parents' sin, nor because of his own sin; "but that the 			 works of God should be made manifest in him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:18
verses.text: For we all when we were born contracted original sin: and yet we were not born blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:19
verses.text: However enquire carefully, And we were born blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:20
verses.text: For who was not born blind? blind, that is, in heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:21
verses.text: But the Lord Jesus, for that He had created both, cured both.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:22
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:23
verses.text: With the eyes of faith ye have seen this man blind, ye have seen him too of blind seeing; but ye have heard him erring.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:24
verses.text: Wherein this blind man erred, I will tell you; first, in that he thought Christ a prophet, and knew not that He was the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:25
verses.text: And then we have heard an answer of his entirely false; for he said, "We know that God heareth not sinners".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:26
verses.text: If God heareth not sinners, what hope have we? If God heareth not sinners, why do we pray, and publish the record of our sin by the beating of the breast? Where again is that Publican, who went up with the Pharisee into the temple and while the Pharisee was boasting, parading his own merits, he standing afar off, and with his eyes fastened on the ground, and beating his breast, was confessing his sins? And this man, who confessed his sins, went down from the temple justified rather than the other Pharisee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:27
verses.text: Assuredly then God doth hear sinners.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:28
verses.text: But he who spake these words had not yet washed the face of the heart in Siloa.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:29
verses.text: The sacrament had gone before on his eyes; but in the heart had not been yet effected the blessing of the grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:30
verses.text: When did this 			 blind man wash the face of his heart? When the Lord admitted him into Himself after he had been cast out by the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:31
verses.text: For He found him, and said to him as we have heard; "Dost thou believe on the Son of God?" And he, "Who is He, Lord, that I may believe on Him?" With the eyes, it is true, he saw already; did he see already in the heart? No, not yet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:32
verses.text: Wait; he will see presently.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:33
verses.text: Jesus answered him, "I that speak with thee am He".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:34
verses.text: Did he doubt? No, forthwith he washed his face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:35
verses.text: For he was speaking with That Siloa, "which is by interpretation, Sent".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:36
verses.text: Who is the Sent, but Christ? Who often bare witness, saying, "I do the will of My Father That sent Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:37
verses.text: He then was Himself the Siloa.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:38
verses.text: The man approached blind in heart, he heard, believed, adored; washed the face, saw.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:39
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:40
verses.text: But they who cast him out continued blind, forasmuch as they cavilled at the Lord, that it was the sabbath when He made clay of the spittle, and anointed the eyes of the blind man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:41
verses.text: For when the Lord cured with a word, the Jews openly cavilled.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:42
verses.text: For He did no work on the sabbath day, when He spake, and it was done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:43
verses.text: It was a manifest cavil; they cavilled at Him merely commanding, they cavilled at Him speaking; as if they did not themselves speak all the sabbath day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:44
verses.text: I might say that they do not speak not only on the sabbath, but on no day, forasmuch as they have kept back from the praises of the True God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:45
verses.text: Nevertheless, as I have said, brethren, it was a manifest cavil.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:46
verses.text: The Lord said to a certain man, "Stretch forth thine hand;" he was made whole, and they cavilled for that He healed on the sabbath day.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:47
verses.text: What did He do? what work did He do? what burden did He bear? But in this instance, the spitting on the ground, the making clay, and anointing the man's eyes, is doing some work.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:48
verses.text: Let no one doubt it, it was doing a work.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:49
verses.text: The Lord did break the sabbath; but was not therefore guilty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:50
verses.text: What is that I have said, "He brake the sabbath"? He, the Light had come, He was removing the shadows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:51
verses.text: For the 			 sabbath was enjoined by the Lord God, enjoined by Christ Himself, who was with the Father, when that Law was given; it was enjoined by Him, but in shadow of what was to come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:52
verses.text: "Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:53
verses.text: He had now come whose coming these things announced.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:54
verses.text: Why do the shadows delight us? Open your eyes, ye Jews; the Sun is present.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:55
verses.text: "We know".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:56
verses.text: What do ye know, ye blind in heart? what know ye? "That this man is not of God, because he thus breaketh the sabbath day".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:57
verses.text: The sabbath, unhappy men, this very sabbath did Christ ordain, who ye say is not of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:58
verses.text: Ye observe the sabbath in a carnal manner, ye have not the spittle of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:59
verses.text: In this earth of the sabbath look also for the spittle of Christ, and ye will understand that by the sabbath Christ was prophesied.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:60
verses.text: But ye, because ye have not the spittle of Christ in the earth upon your eyes, ye have not come unto Siloa, and have not washed the face, and have continued blind, blind to the good of this blind man, yea now no longer blind either in body or 			 heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:61
verses.text: He received clay with the spittle, his eyes were anointed, he came to Siloa, he washed his face, he believed on Christ, he saw, he continued not in that exceedingly fearful judgment; "For judgment I came into this world, that they which see not may see, and that they which see may be made blind".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:62
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:63
verses.text: Exceeding alarm! "That they which see not may see:" Good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:64
verses.text: It is a Saviour's office, a profession of healing power, "That they which see not may see".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:65
verses.text: But what, Lord, is that Thou hast added, "That they which see may be made blind"? If we understand, it is most true, most righteous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:66
verses.text: Yet what is, "They which see"? They are the Jews.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:67
verses.text: Do they then see? According to their own words, they see; according to the truth, they do not see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:68
verses.text: What then is, 			 "they see"? They think they see, they believe they see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:69
verses.text: For they believed they did see, when they maintained the Law against Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:70
verses.text: "We know;" therefore they see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:71
verses.text: What is "We know," but we see? What is, "this Man is not of God, because He thus breaketh the sabbath day"? They see; they read what the Law said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:72
verses.text: For it was enjoined that whosoever should break the sabbath day, should be stoned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:73
verses.text: Therefore said they that He was not of God; but though seeing, they were blind to this, that for judgment He came into the world who is to be the Judge of quick and dead; why came He? "That they which see not may see:" that they who confess that they do not see, may be enlightened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:74
verses.text: "And that they which see may be made blind;" that is, that they who confess not their own blindness, may be the more hardened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:75
verses.text: And, in fact, "That they which see may be made blind," has 			 been fulfilled; the defenders of the Law, Doctors of the Law, the teachers of the Law, the understanders of the Law, crucified the Author of the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:76
verses.text: O blindness, this is that which "in part hath happened to Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:77
verses.text: That Christ might be crucified, and the fulness of the Gentiles might come in, "blindness in part hath happened to Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:78
verses.text: What is, "that they which see not may see"? That the fulness of the Gentiles might come in, "blindness in part hath happened to Israel".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:79
verses.text: The whole world lay in blindness; but He came, "that they which see not may see, and that they which see may be made blind".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:80
verses.text: He was disowned by the Jews, He was crucified by the Jews; of His Blood He made 			 an eye-salve for the blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:81
verses.text: They who boasted that they saw the light, being more hardened, being made blind, crucified the Light.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:82
verses.text: What great blindness? They killed the Light, but the Light Crucified enlightened the blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:83
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:84
verses.text: Hear one seeing, who once was blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:85
verses.text: Behold, against what a cross they have miserably stumbled, who would not confess their blindness to the Physician! The Law had continued with them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:86
verses.text: What serveth the Law without grace? Unhappy men, what can the Law do without grace? What doeth the earth without the spittle of Christ? What doeth the Law without grace, but make them more guilty? Why? Because hearers of the Law and not doers, and hereby sinners, transgressors.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:87
verses.text: The 			 son of the hostess of the man of God was dead, and his staff was sent by his servant, and laid upon his face, but he did not revive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:88
verses.text: What doeth the Law without grace? What saith the Apostle, now seeing, now of blind, enlightened? "For if there had been a Law given which could give life, verily righteousness should have been by the Law".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:89
verses.text: Take heed; let us answer and say; what is this that he hath said? "If there had been a Law given which could give life, verily righteousness should have been by the Law".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:90
verses.text: If it could not give life, why was it given? He went on and added, "But the Scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by the faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:91
verses.text: That the promise of illumination, the promise of love by the faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe, that Scripture, that is the Law, hath concluded all under sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:92
verses.text: What is, "hath concluded all under sin"? "I had not known concupiscence, except the Law had said, Thou shalt not lust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:93
verses.text: What is, "hath concluded all under sin"? Hath made the sinner a transgressor also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:94
verses.text: For it could not heal the sinner.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:95
verses.text: "It hath concluded all under sin;" but with what hope? The hope of grace, the hope of mercy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:96
verses.text: Thou hast received the Law: thou didst wish to keep it, thou wast not able; thou hast fallen from pride, hast seen thy weakness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:97
verses.text: Run to the Physician, wash the face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:98
verses.text: Long for Christ, confess Christ, believe on Christ; the Spirit is added to the letter, and thou 			 wilt be saved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:99
verses.text: For if thou take away the Spirit from the letter, "the letter killeth;" if it kill, where is hope? "But the Spirit giveth life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:100
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:101
verses.text: Let then Gehazi, Elisha's servant, receive the staff, as Moses the servant of God received the Law.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:102
verses.text: Let him receive the staff, receive it, run, go before, anticipate him, lay the staff upon the face of the dead child.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:103
verses.text: And so it was; he did receive it, he ran, he laid the staff upon the face of the dead child.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:104
verses.text: But to what purpose? what serveth the staff? "If there had been a Law given which could give life," the boy might have been raised to life by the 			 staff; but seeing that "the Scripture hath concluded all under sin," he still lies dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:105
verses.text: But why hath it concluded all under sin? "That the promise by the faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:106
verses.text: Let then Elisha come, who sent the staff by the servant to prove that he was dead; let him come himself, come in his own person, himself enter into the woman's house, go up to the child, find him dead, conform himself to the members of the dead child, himself not dead, but 			 living.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:107
verses.text: For this he did; he laid his face upon his face, his eyes upon his eyes, his hands upon his hands, his feet upon his feet, he straitened, he contracted himself, being great, he made himself little.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:108
verses.text: He contracted himself; so to say, he lessened himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:109
verses.text: "For being in the Form of God, He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:110
verses.text: What is He conformed Himself, alive to the dead? Do ye ask, what this is? Hear the Apostle; "God sent His Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:111
verses.text: What is, he conformed himself to the dead? Let him tell this, let him go on and declare it again; "In the likeness of flesh of sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:112
verses.text: This is to conform Himself Alive to the dead; to come to us in the likeness of flesh of sin, not in the flesh of sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:113
verses.text: Man lay dead in a flesh of sin, the likeness of flesh of sin conformed Himself to him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:114
verses.text: For He died who had not wherefore to die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:115
verses.text: He died, Alone "Free among the dead;" forasmuch as the whole flesh of men was indeed a flesh 			 of sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 84:116
verses.text: And how should it rise again, had not He who had no sin, conforming Himself to the dead, come in the likeness of flesh of sin? O Lord Jesus, who hast suffered for us, not for Thyself, who hadst no guilt, and didst endure its punishment, that thou mightest dissolve at once the guilt and punishment.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:2
verses.text: [CXXXVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:4
verses.text: ]  The tenth chapter of the Gospel of John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:5
verses.text: Of the shepherd, and the hireling, and the thief.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:7
verses.text: Your faith, dearly beloved, is not ignorant, and I know that ye have so learnt by the teaching of that Master from heaven, in whom ye have placed your hope, that our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath now suffered for us and risen again, is the Head of the Church, and the Church is His Body, and that in His Body the unity of the members and the bond of charity is, as it were, its sound health.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:8
verses.text: But whosoever groweth cold in charity, is become 			 enfeebled in the Body of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:9
verses.text: But He who hath already exalted our Head, is able also to make even the feeble members whole; provided, that is, that they be not cut off by excessive impiety, but adhere to the Body until they be made whole.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:10
verses.text: For whatsoever yet adhereth to the body, is not beyond hope of healing; whereas that which hath been cut off, can neither be in process of curing, nor be healed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:11
verses.text: Since then He is the Head of the Church, and the Church is His Body, Whole Christ is both the 			 Head and the Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:12
verses.text: He hath already risen again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:13
verses.text: We have therefore the Head in heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:14
verses.text: Our Head intercedeth for us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:15
verses.text: Our Head without sin and without death, now propitiateth God for our sins; that we too at the end rising again, and changed into heavenly glory, may follow our Head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:16
verses.text: For where the Head is, there are the rest of the members also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:17
verses.text: But whilst we are here, we are members; let us not despair, for we shall follow our Head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:18
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:19
verses.text: For consider, Brethren, the love of this our Head.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:20
verses.text: He is now in heaven, yet doth He suffer here, as long as His Church suffereth here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:21
verses.text: Here Christ is hungered, here He is athirst, is naked, is a stranger, is sick, is in prison.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:22
verses.text: For whatsoever His Body suffereth here, He hath said that Himself suffereth; and at the end, severing off this His Body to the right hand, and severing the rest by whom He is now trodden under foot to the left, He will say to those on the 			 right hand, "Come, ye blessed of My Father, receive the kingdom which hath been prepared for you from the beginning of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:23
verses.text: For what deservings? "For I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat;" and so He goes over the rest, as if He had Himself received; to such a degree that they, not understanding it, make answer and say, "Lord, when saw we Thee an hungred, a stranger, and in prison?" And He saith to them, "Forasmuch as ye have done it to one of the least of Mine, ye have 			 done it unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:24
verses.text: So also in our own body, the head is above, the feet are on the earth; yet in any crowding and throng of men, when any one treads on your foot, does not the head say, "You are treading upon me?" No one has trodden on your head, or on your tongue; it is above, in safety, no harm has happened unto it; and yet because by the bond of charity there is unity from the head even to the feet, the tongue does not separate itself therefrom, but says, "You are 			 treading upon me;" when no one has touched it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:25
verses.text: As then the tongue, which no one has touched, says, "You are treading upon me;" so Christ, the Head, which no one treadeth on, said, "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:26
verses.text: And to them who did not so, He said, "I was an hungred, and ye gave Me no meat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:27
verses.text: And how did He finish? Thus; "These shall go into everlasting burning, but the righteous into life eternal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:28
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:29
verses.text: When our Lord then was speaking on this occasion, He said, that He is "the Shepherd," He said also that He is "the Door".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:30
verses.text: You find them both in that place, both "I am the Door" and "I am the Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:31
verses.text: In the Head He is the Door, the Shepherd in the Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:32
verses.text: For He saith to Peter, in whom singly He formeth the Church; "Peter, lovest thou Me?" He answered, "Lord, I do love Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:33
verses.text: "Feed My sheep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:34
verses.text: And a third time, "Peter, lovest thou Me?" "Peter was grieved because He asked him the third time;" as though He who saw the conscience of the denier, saw not the confessor's faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:35
verses.text: He had known him always, had known him even when Peter had not known himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:36
verses.text: For he did not know himself at that time when he said, "I will be with Thee even unto death;" and how infirm he was he knew not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:37
verses.text: Just as it constantly happens in fact to invalids, that the sick man knows not what is going on within him, but the physician knows; when yet the former is suffering from the very sickness, and the physician is not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:38
verses.text: The physician can better tell what is going on in another, than he who is sick what is going on in himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:39
verses.text: Peter then was at that time the invalid, and the Lord the Physician.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:40
verses.text: The former declared that he had strength, when he had 			 not; but the Lord touching the pulse of his heart, declared that he should deny Him thrice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:41
verses.text: And so it came to pass, as the Physician foretold, not as the sick presumed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:42
verses.text: Therefore, after His resurrection the Lord questioned him, not as being ignorant with what a heart he would confess the love of Christ, but that he might by a threefold confession of love, efface the threefold denial of fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:43
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:44
verses.text: Therefore doth the Lord require this of Peter, "Peter, lovest thou Me?" As though, "What wilt thou give Me, what wilt thou do for Me, seeing that thou lovest Me?" What was Peter to do for his Lord risen again, and going into heaven, and sitting on the right hand of the Father? As if He had said, "This shalt thou give Me, this shalt thou do for Me, if thou lovest Me, feed My sheep; enter in by the Door, not go up by another way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:45
verses.text: Ye heard when the 			 Gospel was being read, "He that entereth in by Door, is the shepherd; but he that goeth up another way, is a thief and a robber; and he seeketh to disperse, and to scatter, and to spoil".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:46
verses.text: Who is he that entereth in by the Door? He that entereth in by Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:47
verses.text: Who is he? He who imitateth the Passion of Christ, who acknowledgeth the Humility of Christ; that whereas God was made Man for us, man may acknowledge himself to be, not God, but man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:48
verses.text: For whoso wisheth to appear God, when he is man, doth not imitate Him, who, being God, was made Man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:49
verses.text: But to thee it is not said, Be anything less than thou art; but acknowledge what thou art.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:50
verses.text: Acknowledge thyself feeble, 			 acknowledge thyself man, acknowledge thyself a sinner; acknowledge that it is He That justifieth, acknowledge that thou art full of stains.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:51
verses.text: Let the stain of thine heart appear in thy confession, and thou shalt belong to Christ's flock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:52
verses.text: For the confession of sins invites the physician's healing; as in sickness, he that says, "I am well," seeketh not the physician.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:53
verses.text: Did not the Pharisee and the Publican go up to the temple? The one boasted of his sound estate, the other showed his wounds to the Physician.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:54
verses.text: For the Pharisee said, "I thank Thee, O God, that I am not as this publican".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:55
verses.text: He gloried over the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:56
verses.text: So then if that publican had been whole, the Pharisee would have grudged it him; for that he would not have had any one over whom to extol himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:57
verses.text: In what state then had he come, who had this envious spirit? Surely he was not whole; and whereas he called himself whole, he went not down cured.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:58
verses.text: But the other casting his eyes down to the ground, and not daring to lift them up unto heaven, smote his breast, saying, "God be merciful to me a sinner".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:59
verses.text: And what saith the Lord? "Verily I say unto you, that the publican went down from the temple justified rather than the Pharisee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:60
verses.text: For every one that exalteth himself shall be abased, and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:61
verses.text: They then who exalt themselves, would go up into the sheepfold by another way; but they who humble themselves, enter in by the Door into the sheepfold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:62
verses.text: Therefore said He of the one, "he entereth in;" of the other, "he goeth up".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:63
verses.text: He that goeth up, you see, who seeks exaltation, does not enter in, but falls.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:64
verses.text: Whereas he that abases himself, that he may enter in by the Door, falls not, but is the shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:65
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:66
verses.text: But the Lord mentioned three characters, and our duty is to search them out in the Gospel, that of the shepherd, the hireling, and the thief.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:67
verses.text: I suppose you took notice when the lesson was being read, that He marked out the shepherd, the hireling, and the thief.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:68
verses.text: "The Shepherd," said He, "layeth down His life for the sheep," and entereth in by the door.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:69
verses.text: The thief and the robber, said He, go up by another way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:70
verses.text: "The hireling," He said, if he seeth a wolf or even a thief, "fleeth; because he careth not for the sheep;" for he is an hireling, not a shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:71
verses.text: The one entereth in by the door, because he is the shepherd; the second goeth up another way, because he is a thief; the third seeing them who wish to spoil the sheep feareth and fleeth, because he is an hireling, because he careth not for the sheep; for he is an hireling.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:72
verses.text: If we shall find these three characters, ye have found, holy brethren, both those whom ye should love, and those whom ye should tolerate, and those of whom ye must 			 beware.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:73
verses.text: The Shepherd is to be loved, the hireling is to be tolerated, of the robber must we beware.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:74
verses.text: There are men in the Church of whom the Apostle speaks, who preach the Gospel by occasion, seeking of men their own advantage, whether of money, or of honour, or human praise.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:75
verses.text: They preach the Gospel, wishing to receive rewards in whatsoever way they can, and seek not so much his salvation to whom they preach, as their own advantage.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:76
verses.text: But he who heareth the word of salvation from him who hath not salvation, if he believe Him whom he preacheth, and put not his hope in him, by whom salvation is preached to him; he that preacheth shall have loss; he to whom he preacheth shall have gain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:77
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:78
verses.text: You have the Lord saying of the Pharisees, "They sit in Moses' seat".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:79
verses.text: The Lord did not mean them only; as if He would send those who should believe on Christ to the school of the Jews, that they might learn there wherein is the way to the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:80
verses.text: Did not the Lord come for this end, that He might establish a Church, and separate those Jews who had a good faith, and a good hope, and a good love, as wheat from the chaff, and might make them one wall of the circumcision, to which should be joined another wall from the uncircumcision of 			 the Gentiles, of which two walls coming from different directions, Himself should be the Corner-Stone? Did not the same Lord therefore say of these two people who were to be one, "And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold"? Now He was speaking to the Jews; "Them also," said He, "must I bring, that there may be one fold, and One Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:81
verses.text: Therefore there were two ships out of which He had called His disciples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:82
verses.text: They figured these two people, when they let down their nets, and took up so great a draught and so large a number of fishes, that the nets were almost broken.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:83
verses.text: "And they laded," it is said, "both the ships".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:84
verses.text: The two ships figured the One Church, but made out of two peoples, joined together in Christ, though coming from different parts.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:85
verses.text: Of this too the two wives, who had one husband Jacob, Leah and Rachel, are a figure.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:86
verses.text: Of these two, the two blind men also are a figure, who sat by the way side, to whom the Lord gave sight.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:87
verses.text: And if ye pay attention to the Scriptures, ye will find the two Churches, which are not two but One, figured out in many places.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:88
verses.text: For to this end the Corner-Stone serveth, for to make of two One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:89
verses.text: To this end serveth That Shepherd, for to make of two flocks One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:90
verses.text: So then the Lord who was to teach the Church, and to have a school of His Own beyond the Jews, as we see at present, would He be likely to send those who believe on Him unto the Jews, to learn? But under the name of the 			 Scribes and Pharisees He intimated that there would be some in His Church who would say and not do; but, in the person of Moses He designated Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:91
verses.text: For Moses represented Him, and for this reason did he put a vail before him, when he was speaking to the people; because as long as they were in the law given up to carnal joys and pleasures, and looking for an earthly kingdom, a vail was put upon their face, that they should not see Christ in the Scriptures.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:92
verses.text: For when the vail was taken away, 			 after that the Lord had suffered, the secrets of the temple were discovered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:93
verses.text: Accordingly when He was hanging on the Cross, the vail of the temple was rent from the top even to the bottom; and the Apostle Paul says expressly, "But when thou shalt turn to Christ, the vail shall be taken away".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:94
verses.text: Whereas with him who turneth not to Christ, though he read the law of Moses, the vail is laid upon his heart, as the Apostle says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:95
verses.text: When the Lord then would signify beforehand that there would be some such in His Church, what did He say? "The Scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:96
verses.text: What they say, do; but do not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:97
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:98
verses.text: When wicked clerics hear this which is said against them, they would pervert it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:99
verses.text: For I have heard that some do wish to pervert this sentence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:100
verses.text: Would they not, if they might, efface it from the Gospel? But because they cannot efface it, they go about to pervert it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:101
verses.text: But the grace and mercy of the Lord is present, and allows them not to do so; for He hath hedged round all His declarations with His truth, and in such wise balanced them; that if any one would wish to cut off anything from them, or to introduce anything by a bad reading or interpretation, any right hearted man may join to the Scripture what has been cut off from the Scripture, and read what went above or below, and he will find the sense which the other wished to interpret wrongly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:102
verses.text: What then, think ye, do they say of whom it is said, "Do what they say"? That it is (and in 			 truth it is so) addressed to laymen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:103
verses.text: For what does the layman who wishes to live well say to himself, when he takes notice of a wicked cleric? "The Lord said, 'What they say, do; what they do, do not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:104
verses.text: ' Let me walk in the way of the Lord, not follow this man's conversation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:105
verses.text: Let me hear from him not his words, but God's.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:106
verses.text: I will follow God, let him follow his own lust.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:107
verses.text: For if I should wish to defend myself in such wise before God as to say, 'Lord, I saw that thy cleric living evilly, 			 and therefore I lived evilly;' would He not say to me, 'Thou wicked servant, hadst thou not heard from Me, "What they say, do, but what they do, do not"?' But a wicked layman, an unbeliever, who belongs not to Christ's flock, who belongs not to Christ's wheat, who as chaff is only borne with in the floor, what does he say to himself when the word of God begins to reprove him? "Away; why talkest thou to me? The very Bishops and Clergy do not do it, and dost thou force me to do 			 it?" Thus he seeks for himself not a patron for his bad cause, but a companion for punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:108
verses.text: For will that wicked one whosoever he be that he has chosen to imitate, will he ever defend him in the day of judgment? For as with all whom the devil seduces, he seduces them not to be partakers of a kingdom, but of his damnation; so all who follow the wicked, seek companions for themselves to hell, not protection unto the kingdom of heaven.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:109
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:110
verses.text: How then do they pervert this declaration when it is said to them in their wicked lives, "With good reason was it said by the Lord ,'What they say, do; what they do, do not'"? "It was well said," say they.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:111
verses.text: "For it was said to you, that ye should do what we say; but that ye should not do what we do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:112
verses.text: For we offer sacrifice, you may not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:113
verses.text: See the cunning craftiness of these men; what shall I call them? hirelings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:114
verses.text: For if they were shepherds, they 			 would not say such things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:115
verses.text: Therefore the Lord, that He might shut their mouths, went on, and said, "They sit in Moses' seat; what they say, do; but what they do, do not; for they say, and do not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:116
verses.text: What is it then, Brethren? If He had spoken of offering sacrifice; would He have said, "For they say, and do not"? For they do offer sacrifice, they do offer unto God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:117
verses.text: What is it that they say, and do not? Hear what follows; "For they bind heavy burdens, and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders, and they themselves will not touch them with one of their fingers".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:118
verses.text: So openly did He rebuke, describe, and point them out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:119
verses.text: But those men when they thus wish to pervert the passage, show plainly that they seek nothing in the Church but their own advantage; and that they have not read the Gospel; for had they known but this very page, and read the whole, they would never have dared to say this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:120
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:121
verses.text: But attend to a more clear proof that the Church hath such as these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:122
verses.text: Lest any one should say to us, "He spake entirely of the Pharisees, He spake of the Scribes, He spake of the Jews; for the Church hath none such".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:123
verses.text: Who then are they of whom the Lord saith, "Not every one that saith unto Me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven"? And He added, "Many shall say to Me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Thy Name, and in Thy Name done many mighty works, and in Thy Name have eaten and drunken?" What! do the Jews do these things in Christ's name? Assuredly it is manifest, that He speaks of them who have the Name of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:124
verses.text: But what follows? "Then will I say to them, I never knew you; depart from Me, all ye that work iniquity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:125
verses.text: Hear the Apostle sighing concerning such as these.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:126
verses.text: He says that some preach the Gospel "through charity," others "by occasion;" of whom he says, "They do not preach the Gospel rightly".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:127
verses.text: A right thing, but themselves not right.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:128
verses.text: What they preach is right; but they who preach it are not right.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:129
verses.text: Why is he not right? Because he seeketh something else in the Church, seeketh not God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:130
verses.text: If he sought God, he would be chaste; for the soul hath in God her lawful husband.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:131
verses.text: Whosoever seeketh from God ought besides God, doth not seek God chastely.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:132
verses.text: Consider, Brethren; if a wife love her husband because he is rich, she is not chaste.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:133
verses.text: For she loves not her husband, but her 			 husband's gold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:134
verses.text: Whereas if she love her husband, she loves him both in nakedness and poverty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:135
verses.text: For if she love him because he is rich; what if (as human chances are) he be outlawed and all on a sudden be reduced to need? She gives him up, mayhap; because what she loved was not her husband, but his property.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:136
verses.text: But if she love her husband indeed, she loves him even more when poor; for that she loves with pity too.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:137
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:138
verses.text: And yet, Brethren, our God never can be poor.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:139
verses.text: He is rich, He made all things, heaven and earth, the sea and Angels.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:140
verses.text: In the heaven, whatsoever we see, whatsoever we see not, He made it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:141
verses.text: But notwithstanding, we ought not to love these riches, but Him who made them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:142
verses.text: For He hath promised thee nothing but Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:143
verses.text: Find anything more precious, and He will give thee this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:144
verses.text: Beauteous is the earth, the heaven, and the Angels; but more beauteous is He who made them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:145
verses.text: They then 			 who preach God, as loving God; who preach God, for God's sake, feed the sheep, and are no hirelings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:146
verses.text: This chastity did our Lord Jesus Christ require of the soul, when He said to Peter, "Peter, lovest thou Me"? What is "Lovest thou Me"? Art thou chaste? Is not thine heart adulterous? Dost thou seek not thine own things in the Church, but Mine? If then thou be such an one, and lovest Me, "feed My sheep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:147
verses.text: For thou shalt be no hireling, but thou shalt be a shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:148
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:149
verses.text: But they did not preach chastely, concerning whom the Apostle sighs.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:150
verses.text: But what doth he say? "What then? Notwithstanding every way, whether by occasion or in truth, Christ is preached".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:151
verses.text: He suffers then that hirelings there should be.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:152
verses.text: The shepherd preacheth Christ in truth, the hireling by occasion preacheth Christ, seeking something else.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:153
verses.text: Notwithstanding, both the one and the other preacheth Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:154
verses.text: Hear the voice of the shepherd Paul; "Whether by occasion or in truth, Christ is preached".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:155
verses.text: Himself a shepherd, he was pleased to have the hireling.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:156
verses.text: For they act where they are able, they are useful as far as they are able.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:157
verses.text: But when the Apostle for other uses 			 sought for those whose ways the weak ones might imitate; he saith, "I have sent unto you Timotheus, who shall bring you into remembrance of my ways".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:158
verses.text: And what doth he say? "I have sent unto you a shepherd, to bring you into remembrance of my ways;" that is, who himself also walketh as I walk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:159
verses.text: And in sending this shepherd, what doth he say? "For I have no one so likeminded, who with sincere affection is anxious for you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:160
verses.text: Were there not many with him? But what follows? "For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's;" that is, "I have wished to send unto you a shepherd; for there are many hirelings; but it were not meet for an hireling to be sent".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:161
verses.text: An hireling is sent for the transaction of other affairs and business; but for those which Paul then desired, a shepherd was necessary.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:162
verses.text: And he scarcely found one shepherd among many hirelings; for the shepherds are few, the hirelings many.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:163
verses.text: But what is said of the hirelings? "Verily I say unto you, they have received their reward".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:164
verses.text: Of the shepherd, what saith the Apostle? "But whosoever shall cleanse himself from such as these shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and useful to the Lord, prepared always unto every good work".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:165
verses.text: Not unto certain things prepared, and unto certain not prepared, but "unto every good work prepared".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:166
verses.text: So much have I said, concerning the shepherds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:167
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:168
verses.text: But we will now speak of the hirelings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:169
verses.text: "The hireling when he seeth the wolf lying in wait for the sheep, fleeth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:170
verses.text: This the Lord said.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:171
verses.text: Why? "Because he careth not for the sheep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:172
verses.text: So long then is the hireling of use, as he seeth not the wolf coming, as he seeth not the thief and the robber; but when he seeth them, he fleeth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:173
verses.text: And who is there of the hirelings, who fleeth not from the Church, when he seeth the wolf and the robber? And wolves and robbers abound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:174
verses.text: They are they who go up by another way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:175
verses.text: Who are these who go up? They who of Donatus' way wish to make havoc of Christ's sheep, they go up by another way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:176
verses.text: They do not enter in by Christ, because they are not humble.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:177
verses.text: Because they are proud, they go up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:178
verses.text: What is, "they go up"? They are lifted up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:179
verses.text: Whereby do they go up? By another way: whence they wish to be named from their way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:180
verses.text: They who are not in unity are of another way, and by this way they go up, that is, are lifted up, and wish to spoil the sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:181
verses.text: Now mark how they go up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:182
verses.text: "It is we," they say, "who 			 sanctify, we justify, we make righteous".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:183
verses.text: See whither they have got up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:184
verses.text: "But he that exalteth himself, shall be abased".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:185
verses.text: Our Lord God is able to abase them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:186
verses.text: Now the wolf is the devil, he lieth in wait to deceive, and they that follow him; for it is said that "they are clothed indeed with the skins of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:187
verses.text: If the hireling observe anyone indulging in wicked talking, or in sentiments to the deadly hurt of his soul, or doing ought that is abominable and unclean, and notwithstanding that he seems to bear a character of some importance in the Church (from which if he hopes for advantage he is an hireling); says nothing, and when he sees the man perishing in his sin, sees the wolf following him, sees his throat dragged by his teeth to punishment; says not to him, "Thou sinnest;" 			 does not chide him, lest he lose his own advantage.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:188
verses.text: This I say is, "When he seeth the wolf, he fleeth;" he does not say to him, "Thou art doing wickedly".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:189
verses.text: This is no flight of the body, but of the soul.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:190
verses.text: He whom thou seest standing still in body flies in heart, when he sees a sinner, and does not say to him, "Thou sinnest;" yea when he even is in concert with him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:191
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:192
verses.text: My Brethren, does ever either Presbyter or Bishop come up here, and say anything from this higher place, but that the property of others must not be plundered, that there must be no fraud committed, no wickedness done? They cannot say ought else who sit in Moses' seat, and it is it that speaks by them, not they themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:193
verses.text: What then is, "Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?" and, "Every tree is known by his fruit"? Can a Pharisee speak good things? A Pharisee is a thorn; how from a thorn do I gather grapes? Because Thou, Lord, hast said, "What they say, do; but what they do, do not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:194
verses.text: Dost Thou bid me gather grapes of thorns when Thou sayest, "Do men gather grapes of thorns"? The Lord answereth thee, "I have not bidden thee gather grapes of thorns: but look, mark well, if haply, as is often the case, the vine when it trails all along upon the ground, be not entangled in thorns".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:195
verses.text: For we sometimes find this, my Brethren, a vine planted over sedge, how it has there a thorny hedge, and throws out its branches, and entangles them in the thorny hedge, and 			 the grape hangs among the thorns; and he that sees it plucks the grape, yet not from the thorns, but from the vine which is entangled in the thorns.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:196
verses.text: In like manner then the Pharisees are thorny; but by sitting in Moses' seat, the vine wraps them round, and grapes, that is, good words, good precepts, hang from them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:197
verses.text: Do thou pick the grape, the thorn will not prick thee, when thou readest, "What they say, do; but what they do, do not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:198
verses.text: But the thorn will prick thee, if thou do what they do.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:199
verses.text: So then that thou mayest gather the grape, and not be caught in the thorns, "What they say, do; but what they do, do not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:200
verses.text: Their deeds are the thorns, their words are the grapes, but from the vine, that is, from Moses' seat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:201
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:202
verses.text: These then flee, when they see the wolf, when they see the robber.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:203
verses.text: Now this it was that I had began to say, that from this higher place they can say nothing, but, "Do well," "do not forswear yourselves," "defraud not," "cheat not any".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:204
verses.text: But sometimes men's lives are so bad, that counsel is asked of a Bishop on the taking away of another man's estate, and from him is such counsel sought.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:205
verses.text: It has sometimes happened to ourselves, we speak from 			 experience: for we should not have believed it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:206
verses.text: Many men require from us evil counsels, counsels of lying, of fraud; thinking that they please us thereby.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:207
verses.text: But by the Name of Christ, if what we are saying is pleasing to the Lord, no such man has tempted us, and found what he wished in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:208
verses.text: For with the good pleasure of Him who hath called us, we are shepherds, not hirelings.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:209
verses.text: But as saith the Apostle, "But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man's day; yea, I 			 judge not even mine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:210
verses.text: For I am conscious of nothing by myself, but I am not hereby justified.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:211
verses.text: But He That judgeth me is the Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:212
verses.text: My conscience is not therefore good, because ye praise it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:213
verses.text: For how praise ye what ye do not see? Let Him praise, who seeth; yea let Him correct, if He seeth ought there which offendeth His Eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:214
verses.text: For I too do not say that I am perfectly whole; but I beat my breast, and say to God, "Be merciful, that I sin not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:215
verses.text: Yet I do think, for I speak in His Presence, that I seek nothing from you, but your salvation; and constantly do I groan over the sins of my brethren, and I suffer 			 distress, and am tormented in mind, and often do I reprove them; yea, I never cease reproving them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:216
verses.text: All who remember what I say are witnesses, how often my brethren who sin have been reproved, and earnestly reproved, by me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:217
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:218
verses.text: I am now treating of my counsel with you, holy Brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:219
verses.text: In Christ's Name ye are the people of God, ye are a Catholic people, ye are members of Christ; ye are not divided from unity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:220
verses.text: Ye are in communion with the members of the Apostles, ye are in communion with the memories of the Holy Martyrs, who are spread over the whole world, and ye belong to my cure, that I may render a good account of you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:221
verses.text: Now my whole account, what it is ye know.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:222
verses.text: "Lord, Thou knowest 			 that I have spoken, Thou knowest that I have not kept silence, Thou knowest in what spirit I have spoken, Thou knowest that I have wept before Thee, when I spake, and was not heard".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:223
verses.text: This I imagine is my whole account.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:224
verses.text: For the Holy Spirit by the prophet Ezekiel hath given me sure hope.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:225
verses.text: Ye know this passage concerning the watchman; "O son of man," saith He, "I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; if when I say unto the wicked, O wicked man, thou shalt die the death, thou 			 dost not speak;" that is (for I speak to thee that thou mayest speak), "if thou dost not announce it, and the sword," that is, what I have threatened on the sinner, "come, and take him away; that wicked man indeed shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at the watchman's hand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:226
verses.text: Why? Because he did not speak.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:227
verses.text: "But if the watchman see the sword coming, and blow the trumpet," that he may fly, and he took not to himself, that is, amend not himself, that it find him not in the punishment which God threateneth, and "the sword shall come and take any one away; that wicked man indeed shall die in his iniquity; but thou," saith He, "hast delivered thine own soul".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:228
verses.text: And in that place of the Gospel, what else saith He to the servant? when he said, 			 "Lord, I knew Thee to be a" difficult or "hard Man, in that Thou reapest where Thou hast not sowed, and gatherest where Thou hast not strawed; and I was afraid, and went and hid Thy talent in the earth, lo, Thou hast that is Thine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:229
verses.text: And He said, "'Thou wicked and slothful servant,' because thou knewest Me to be a difficult and hard Man, to reap where I have not sown, and to gather where I have not strawed, My very covetousness ought the more to teach thee, that I look for profit from My money.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:230
verses.text: 'Thou 			 oughtest therefore to have given My money to the exchangers, and at My coming I should have required Mine own with usury.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:231
verses.text: '" Did He say, "Thou oughtest to give, and require"? It is we then, Brethren, who give, He will come to require.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 85:232
verses.text: Pray ye, that He may find us prepared.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:2
verses.text: [CXXXVIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:5
verses.text: 14, "I am the good shepherd," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:6
verses.text: Against the Donatists.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:8
verses.text: We have heard the Lord Jesus setting forth to us the office of a good shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:9
verses.text: And herein He hath doubtless given us to know, as we may understand it, that there are good shepherds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:10
