verses.text: And yet that the multitude of shepherds might not be understood in a wrong sense; He saith, "I am the good Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:11
verses.text: And wherein He is the good Shepherd, He showeth in the words following; "The good Shepherd," saith He, "layeth down His life for the sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:12
verses.text: But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, seeth the wolf coming, and fleeth; because he careth not for the sheep, for he is an hireling".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:13
verses.text: Christ then is the good Shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:14
verses.text: What was Peter? was he not a good shepherd? Did not he too lay down his life for the sheep? What was Paul? what the rest of the Apostles? what the blessed Bishops, Martyrs, who followed close upon their times? What again our holy Cyprian? Were they not all good shepherds, not hirelings, of whom it is said, "Verily I say unto you, they have received their reward"? All these then were good shepherds, not simply for that they shed their blood, but that they shed it for the sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:15
verses.text: For not in pride, but in charity they shed it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:17
verses.text: For even among the heretics, they who for their iniquities and errors have suffered any trouble, vaunt themselves in the name of martyrdom, that with this fair covering disguised they may plunder the more easily, for wolves they are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:18
verses.text: Now if ye would know in what rank they are to be held, hear that good shepherd, the Apostle Paul, that not all who even give up their bodies in suffering to the flames, are to be accounted to have shed their blood for the sheep, but rather against the sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:19
verses.text: "If," saith he, "I speak with the tongues of men, and angels, but have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:20
verses.text: If I should know all 			 mysteries, and have all prophecy, and all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not charity, I am nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:21
verses.text: Now a great thing truly is this faith that removes mountains.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:22
verses.text: They are indeed all great things; but if I have them without charity, saith he, not they, but I am nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:23
verses.text: But up to this point he hath not touched them, who glory in sufferings under the false name of martyrdom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:24
verses.text: Hear how he toucheth, yea rather pierceth them through and through.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:25
verses.text: "If I should distribute," saith he, "all my goods to the poor, and deliver my body to be burned".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:26
verses.text: Now here they are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:27
verses.text: But mark 			 what follows; "but have not charity, it profiteth me nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:28
verses.text: Lo, they have come to suffering, come even to the shedding of blood, yea come to the burning of the body; and yet it profiteth them nothing, because charity is lacking.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:29
verses.text: Add charity, they all profit; take charity away, all the rest profit nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:31
verses.text: What a good is this charity, Brethren! What more precious? what yieldeth greater light? or strength? or profit? or security? Many are the gifts of God, which even the wicked have, who shall say, "Lord, we have prophesied in Thy Name, in Thy Name have cast out devils, in Thy Name done many mighty works".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:32
verses.text: And He will not answer, "Ye have not done them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:33
verses.text: For in the Presence of so great a Judge, they will not dare to lie or boast of things they have not done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:34
verses.text: But for that they had not charity, He answereth them all, "I know you not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:35
verses.text: Now how can he have so much as the smallest charity, who when even convicted, loves not unity? It was then as impressing on good shepherds this unity, that our Lord was unwilling to mention many shepherds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:36
verses.text: For it is not, as I have said already, that Peter was not a good shepherd, and Paul, the rest of the Apostles, and the holy Bishops who were after them, and blessed Cyprian.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:37
verses.text: All these were good shepherds; and notwithstanding to good shepherds, He commended not good shepherds, but a good Shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:38
verses.text: "I," saith He, "am the good 			 Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:39
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:40
verses.text: Let us question the Lord with such little understanding as we have, and in most humble discourse hold converse with so great a Master.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:41
verses.text: What sayest Thou, O Lord, Thou good Shepherd? For Thou art the good Shepherd, who art also the good Lamb; at once Pastor and Pasturage, at once Lamb and Lion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:42
verses.text: What sayest Thou? Let us give ear and aid us, that we may understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:43
verses.text: "I," saith He, "am the good Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:44
verses.text: What is Peter? is he either not a shepherd, or a bad 			 one? Let us see, if he be not a shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:45
verses.text: "Lovest thou Me?" Thou saidst to Him Lord, "Lovest thou Me?" And he answered, "I do love Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:46
verses.text: And Thou to him, "Feed My sheep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:47
verses.text: Thou, Thou, Lord, by Thine Own questioning, by the strong assurance of Thine Own words, madest of the lover a shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:48
verses.text: He is a shepherd then to whom Thou didst commit Thy sheep to be fed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:49
verses.text: Thou didst Thyself entrust them, he is a shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:50
verses.text: Let us now see whether he be not a good one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:51
verses.text: This we find by the very question, and his 			 answer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:52
verses.text: Thou didst ask, whether he loved Thee; he answered, "I do love Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:53
verses.text: Thou sawest his heart, that he answered truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:54
verses.text: Is he not then good, who loveth so great a Good? Whence that answer drawn from his inmost heart? Wherefore was this Peter, who had Thine eyes in his heart for witnesses, sad because Thou askedst him not once only, but a second and a third time, that by a threefold confession of love, he might efface the threefold sin of denial; wherefore, I say, being sad that he was 			 asked repeatedly by Him who knew what He was asking, and had given what He heard; wherefore being sad, did he return such an answer, "Lord, Thou knowest all things, Thyself knowest that I love Thee"? What! in making such a confession, such a profession rather, would he lie? In truth then, he made answer of his love to Thee, and from his inmost heart he gave utterance to a lover's words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:55
verses.text: Now Thou hast said, "A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:56
verses.text: So then he is both a shepherd, and a good shepherd; nothing it is true to the power and goodness of the Shepherd of shepherds; but nevertheless even he is both a shepherd, and a good one; and all other such are good shepherds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:57
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:58
verses.text: What means it then, that to good shepherds Thou dost set forth One Only Shepherd, but that in One Shepherd Thou teachest unity? and the Lord Himself explains this more clearly by my ministry, putting you, beloved, in remembrance by this Gospel, and saying, "Hear ye what I have set forth; I have said, 'I am the good Shepherd;' because all the rest, all the good shepherds, are My members".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:59
verses.text: One Head, One Body, One Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:60
verses.text: So then both the Shepherd of 			 shepherds, and the shepherds of the Shepherd, and the sheep with their shepherds under The Shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:61
verses.text: What is all this, but what the Apostle says? "For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:62
verses.text: Therefore if Christ be even so, with good reason doth Christ in Himself containing all good shepherds, set forth One, saying, "'I am the good Shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:63
verses.text: ' 'I am,' I Alone am, all the rest with Me are one in unity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:64
verses.text: Whoso feedeth without Me, feedeth against Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:65
verses.text: 'He that gathereth not with Me, scattereth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:66
verses.text: '" Hear then this unity more forcibly set forth; "Other sheep," saith He, "I have which are not of this fold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:67
verses.text: For He was speaking to the first fold of the stock of the fleshly Israel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:68
verses.text: But there were others of the stock of the faith of this Israel, and they were yet without, were among the Gentiles, predestinated, not yet gathered in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:69
verses.text: These He knew who had predestinated them; He knew, who had come to redeem them with the shedding of His Own Blood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:70
verses.text: He saw them who did not yet see Him; He knew them who yet believed not on Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:71
verses.text: "Other sheep," saith He, "I have which are not of this 			 fold;" because they are not of the stock of the flesh of Israel.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:72
verses.text: But nevertheless they shall not be outside of this fold, "for them also I must bring, that there may be One Fold, and One Shepherd".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:73
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:74
verses.text: With good reason then to This Shepherd of shepherds, doth His Beloved, His Spouse, His Fair One, but by Him made fair, before by sin deformed, beautiful afterward through pardon and grace, speak in her love and ardour after Him, and say to Him, "Where feedest Thou?" And observe how, by what transport this spiritual love is here animated.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:75
verses.text: And far better are they by this transport delighted, who have tasted ought of the sweetness of this love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:76
verses.text: They hear this properly, who love Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:77
verses.text: For in them, and of them, doth the Church sing this in the Song of Songs; who love Christ, as it seemed without beauty, yet the Only Beautiful One.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:78
verses.text: "For we saw Him," it is said, "and He had neither beauty nor comeliness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:79
verses.text: Such He appeared on the Cross, such when crowned with thorns did He exhibit Himself, disfigured, and without comeliness, as if He had lost His power, as if not the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:80
verses.text: Such seemed He to the blind.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:81
verses.text: For it is in the person of the Jews that Isaiah said this, "We saw Him, and He had no beauty nor comeliness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:82
verses.text: When it was said, "If He be the Son of God, let Him come down from the Cross.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:83
verses.text: He saved others, Himself He cannot save".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:84
verses.text: And smiting Him on the head with a reed, they said, "Prophesy unto us, thou Christ, who smote Thee?" Because "He had neither beauty nor comeliness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:85
verses.text: As such did ye Jews see Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:86
verses.text: For "blindness hath happened in part to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles enter in," until the other sheep come.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:87
verses.text: Because then blindness hath happened, therefore did ye see the Comely One without comeliness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:88
verses.text: "For had ye known Him, ye would never have crucified the Lord of Glory".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:89
verses.text: But ye did it, because ye knew Him not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:90
verses.text: And yet He who as though without beauty bare with you, all Beauteous as He was, prayed for you; "Father," saith He, "forgive them, for they know not what they do".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:91
verses.text: For if He were without comeliness, how is it that she loveth Him, who saith, "Tell me, O Thou whom my soul loveth"? How is it that she loveth Him? how is it that she burneth for Him? how is it that she feareth so much to stray from Him? How is it that she hath so great delight in Him, that her only punishment is to be without Him? What would there be for which He should be loved, if He were not beautiful? But how could she love Him so, if He appeared to her as He did to those blind men persecuting Him, and knowing not what they do? As what then did she love Him? As "comely in form above 			 the sons of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:92
verses.text: Comely in form above the sons of men, grace is poured abroad in Thy Lips".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:93
verses.text: So then from these Thy Lips, "Tell me, O Thou whom my soul loveth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:94
verses.text: Tell me," says she, "O Thou whom," not my flesh, but, "my soul loveth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:95
verses.text: Tell me where Thou feedest, where Thou liest down in the midday; lest haply I light, as one veiled, upon the flocks of Thy companions".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:96
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:97
verses.text: It seems obscure, obscure it is; for it is a mystery of the sacred marriage bed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:98
verses.text: For she says, "The King hath brought me into His chamber".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:99
verses.text: Of such a chamber is this a mystery.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:100
verses.text: But ye who are not as profane kept off from this chamber, hear ye what ye are, and say with her, if with her ye love (and ye do love with her, if ye are in her); say all, and yet let one say, for unity saith; "Tell me, O Thou whom my soul loveth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:101
verses.text: For they had one soul to Godward, and one heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:102
verses.text: Tell me where Thou feedest, where Thou liest down in the midday?" What does the midday signify? "Great heat, and great brightness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:103
verses.text: So then, "make known to me who are Thy wise ones," fervent in spirit, and brilliant in doctrine.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:104
verses.text: "Make known to me Thy Right Hand, and men learned in heart, in wisdom".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:105
verses.text: To them may I cleave in Thy Body, to them be united, with them enjoy Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:106
verses.text: Tell me then, "tell me, where Thou feedest, where Thou liest down in the midday;" lest I fall upon them who say other things of Thee, entertain other sentiments of Thee; believe other things of Thee, preach other things of Thee; and have their own flocks, and are Thy companions; for that they live of Thy table, and handle the sacraments of Thy table.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:107
verses.text: For companions are so called, because they eat 			 together, messmates as it were.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:108
verses.text: Such are reproved in the Psalm; "For if Mine enemy had spoken great things against Me, I would surely have hidden Myself from him; and if he that hated Me had spoken great things against Me, I would surely have hidden Myself from him; but thou a man of one mind with Me, My guide, and My familiar, who didst take sweet meats together with Me, in the house of God we walked with consent".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:109
verses.text: Why then now against the house of the Lord with dissent, but that "they have gone out from us, but they were not of us?" Therefore, "O Thou whom my soul loveth," that I may not fall upon such, Thy companions, but companions such as Samson's were, who kept not faith with their friend, but wished to corrupt his wife.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:110
verses.text: Therefore, that I may not fall upon such as these, "that I may not light upon them," that is, fall upon them, "as one that is veiled," as one that is concealed, that is, and obscure, not as established upon the mountain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:111
verses.text: "Tell me" then, "O thou whom my soul loveth, where Thou feedest, where Thou liest down in the midday;" who are the wise and faithful in whom Thou dost specially rest, lest by chance as in blindness I fall upon the flocks, not Thy flocks, but 			 the flocks of Thy companions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:112
verses.text: For thou didst not say to Peter, "Feed thy sheep," but, "Feed My sheep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:113
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:114
verses.text: Let then the "good Shepherd," and, "the Comely in form above the sons of men," make answer to this beloved one; make answer to her whom He hath made beautiful from among the children of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:115
verses.text: Hear ye what He answereth, and understand, beware of that wherewith He alarmeth, love that which He adviseth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:116
verses.text: What then doth He answer? How free from soft caresses, yea, to her caresses He returneth severity! He is sharp that He may bind her closely, that He may keep 			 her.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:117
verses.text: "If thou know not thyself," saith He, "O thou fair one among women:" for however fair others may be by the gifts of thy Spouse, they are heresies, fair in outward ornament, not within: fair are they without, and outwardly they shine, they disguise themselves by the name of righteousness; "but all the beauty of the King's daughter is within".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:118
verses.text: "If" then "thou know not thyself;" that thou art one, that thou art throughout all nations, that thou art chaste, that thou oughtest not to corrupt thyself with the disordered converse of evil companions.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:119
verses.text: "If thou know not thyself," that in uprightness, "he hath espoused thee to Me, to present you a chaste Virgin to Christ;" and that in uprightness thou shouldest present thine own self to Me, lest by evil converse, "as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds too should be corrupted from my purity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:120
verses.text: "If," I say, "thou know not thyself" to be such, "go thy way; go thy way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:121
verses.text: For to others I shall say, "Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:122
verses.text: To thee I shall not say, "Enter in;" but, "Go thy way;" that thou mayest be among those, who "went out from us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:123
verses.text: "Go thy way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:124
verses.text: That is, "if thou know not thyself," then, "go thy way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:125
verses.text: But if thou know thyself, enter in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:126
verses.text: But, "if thou know not thyself, go thy way by the footsteps of the flocks, and feed thy kids in the tents of the shepherds.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:127
verses.text: Go thy way by the footsteps," not "of the Flock," but, "of the flocks, and feed," not as Peter, "My 			 sheep," but, "thy kids; in the tents," not "of the Shepherd," but, "of the shepherds;" not of unity, but of dissension; not established there, where there is One flock and One Shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:128
verses.text: The beloved one was confirmed, edified, made stronger, prepared to die for her Spouse and to live with her Spouse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:129
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:130
verses.text: These words which I have quoted out of the Holy Song of Songs, of a kind of bridal song of the Bridegroom and the Bride (for it is a spiritual wedding, wherein we must live in great purity, for Christ hath granted to the Church in spirit that which His Mother had in body, to be at once a Mother and a Virgin); these words, I say, the Donatists accommodate to their own perverted sense in a very different meaning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:131
verses.text: And how I will not conceal from you, and what ye may 			 answer them, I will, by the Lord's help, as well as I shall be able, briefly recommend.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:132
verses.text: When then we begin to press them with the light of the Church's unity spread over the whole world, and demand of them to show us any testimony out of the Scriptures, where God hath foretold that the Church should be in Africa, as if all the rest of the nations were lost; they are in the habit of taking this testimony in their mouths, and saying; "Africa is under the midday sun; the Church then" they 			 say, "asking the Lord where He feedeth, where He lieth down; He answereth, 'Under the midday sun;'" as if the voice of her who put the question, were, "Tell me, O Thou whom my soul loveth, where Thou feedest, where Thou liest down;" and the Voice of Him who answereth, were, "Under the midday sun;" that is, in Africa.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:133
verses.text: If then it be the Church which asketh, and the Lord maketh answer where he feedeth, in Africa, because the Church was in Africa; then she who asketh was not in 			 Africa.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:134
verses.text: "Tell me," she saith, "O Thou whom my soul loveth, where Thou feedest, where Thou liest down;" and He maketh answer to some Church out of Africa, "Under the midday sun," in Africa I lie down, in Africa I feed, as if it were, "I do not feed in thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:135
verses.text: I repeat, if she who asketh is the Church, which no one disputes, which not even themselves gainsay; and they hear something about Africa; then she who asketh is out of Africa; and because it is the Church, the Church is out 			 of Africa.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:136
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:137
verses.text: But see, I admit that Africa is under the midday sun; although Egypt is rather under the meridian, under the midday sun than Africa.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:138
verses.text: Now after what fashion This Shepherd is there in Egypt, they who know, will acknowledge; and for them that know not, let them enquire how large a flock lie gathereth there, how great a multitude He hath of holy men and women who utterly despise the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:139
verses.text: That flock hath so increased, that it hath expelled superstitions even 			 thence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:140
verses.text: To pass over how it hath in its increase banished thence the whole superstition of idols, which had been firmly fixed there; I admit what you say, O evil companions; I admit it altogether, I agree that Africa is in the South, and that Africa is signified in that which is said, "Where feedest Thou, where dost Thou lie down under the midday sun?" But do ye too equally observe how that up to this point these are the words of the Bride, and not yet of the Bridegroom.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:141
verses.text: Hitherto it is the 			 Bride that saith, "Tell me, O Thou whom my soul loveth, where Thou feedest, where Thou dost lie down in the midday, lest by chance I light, as one veiled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:142
verses.text: O thou deaf, and blind one, if in the "midday" thou seest Africa, why in her that is "veiled" dost thou not see the Bride? "Tell me," she said, "O Thou whom my soul loveth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:143
verses.text: Without doubt she addresses her Spouse, when she says, "whom" [in the masculine] "my soul loveth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:144
verses.text: Just as if it were said, "Tell me, O thou whom [in the feminine] "my soul loveth;" we should understand that the Bridegroom spake these words to His Bride; so when you hear, "Tell me, O thou whom" (in the masculine) "my soul loveth, where Thou feedest, where Thou liest down;" add to this, to her words belongs also what follows, "In the midday".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:145
verses.text: I am asking, "where Thou feedest in the midday, lest by chance I light as one veiled upon the flocks of Thy companions".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:146
verses.text: I consent entirely, I admit what you understand of 			 Africa; it is signified by "the midday".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:147
verses.text: But then as you understand it, the Church of Christ beyond the sea is addressing her Spouse, in fear of falling into the African error, "O Thou whom my soul, loveth, tell me," teach me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:148
verses.text: For I hear that "in the midday," that is in Africa, there are two parties, yea rather many schisms.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:149
verses.text: "Tell me," then, "where Thou feedest," what sheep belong to Thee, what fold Thou biddest me love there, whereunto ought I to unite myself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:150
verses.text: "Lest by chance I light as one veiled".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:151
verses.text: For they mock me as if I were concealed, they mock me as destroyed, as though I existed nowhere else.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:152
verses.text: "Lest," then, "as one veiled," as if concealed, "I light upon the flocks," that is, upon the congregarious of the heretics, "thy companions; the 			 Donatists, the Maximinianists, the Rogatists and all the other pests who gather without, and who therefore scatter; "Tell me," I pray Thee, if I must seek my Shepherd there, that I fall not into the gulf of re-baptizing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:153
verses.text: I exhort you, I beseech you by the sanctity of such nuptials, love this Church, be ye in this holy Church, be ye this Church; love the good Shepherd, the Spouse so fair, who deceiveth no one, who desireth no one to perish.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:154
verses.text: Pray too for the scattered sheep; that they too may 			 come, that they too may acknowledge Him, that they too may love Him; that there may be One Flock and One Shepherd.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 86:155
verses.text: Let us turn to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:1
verses.text: Sermon LXXXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:2
verses.text: [CXXXIX.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:5
verses.text: 30, "I and the Father are one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:7
verses.text: Ye have heard what the Lord God, Jesus Christ, the Only Son of God, born of God the Father without any mother, and born of a Virgin mother without any human father, said, "I and My Father are One".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:8
verses.text: Receive ye this, believe it in such wise that ye may attain to understand it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:9
verses.text: For faith ought to go before understanding, that understanding may be the reward of faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:10
verses.text: For the Prophet hath said most expressly, "Unless ye believe, ye shall not understand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:11
verses.text: What then is simply preached is to be believed; what is with exactness discussed, is to be understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:12
verses.text: At first then to imbue your minds with faith we preach to you Christ, the Only Son of God the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:13
verses.text: Why is added, "The Only Son"? Because He whose Only Son He is, hath many sons by grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:14
verses.text: All the rest then, all saints are sons of God by grace, He Alone by Nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:15
verses.text: They who are sons of God by grace are not What the Father is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:16
verses.text: And no saint hath ever dared to say, what that Only Son saith, "I and My Father are One".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:17
verses.text: Is He not then our Father too? If He be not our Father, how say we 			 when we pray, "Our Father, which art in heaven"? But we are sons whom He hath made sons by His Own will, not begotten as sons of His Own Nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:18
verses.text: And in truth He hath begotten us too, but as it is said, as adopted ones, begotten by the favour of His adoption, not by Nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:19
verses.text: And this too are we called, for that "God hath called us into the adoption of sons;" we are though adopted, men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:20
verses.text: He is called the Only Son, the Only Begotten, in that, He is That which the Father is; but we are men, The Father is God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:21
verses.text: In then that He is That which the Father is; He said, and said truly, "I and My Father are One".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:22
verses.text: What is, "are One"? Are of one Nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:23
verses.text: What is, "are One"? Are of one Substance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:24
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:25
verses.text: Peradventure, ye but imperfectly understand what "of one Substance" is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:26
verses.text: Take we pains that ye may understand it; may God assist both me who speak, and you that hear; me, that I may speak such things as are true and fit for you; and you, that before and above all things ye may believe; and then that ye may understand as best ye can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:27
verses.text: What then is "of One Substance"? Let me make use of similitudes to you, that what is imperfectly understood may be made clear 			 by example.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:28
verses.text: As, suppose, God is gold.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:29
verses.text: His Son is gold also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:30
verses.text: If similitudes ought not to be given for heavenly things from things earthly, how is it written, "Now the Rock was Christ"? So then, Whatsoever the Father is, This is the Son also; as I have said, for example, "The Father is gold, the Son is gold".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:31
verses.text: For he who says, "The Son is not of the Very Substance which the Father is;" what else says he but, "The Father is gold, the Son is silver"? If the Father be gold, and the Son silver; the Only Son hath degenerated from the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:32
verses.text: A man begets a man; of what substance the father is who begets, of the same substance is the Son who is begotten.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:33
verses.text: What is, "of the same substance"? The one is a man, and the other is a man; the one hath a soul; so hath the other a soul; the one hath a body, so hath the other a body; what one is, that is the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:34
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:35
verses.text: But the Arian heresy makes answer, and says.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:36
verses.text: What says it to me? "Mark what thou hast said"? What have I said? "That the Son of a man may be compared to the Son of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:37
verses.text: Certainly he may be compared; but not as you suppose, in strictness of expression; but for a similitude.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:38
verses.text: But tell me now what you would make of this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:39
verses.text: "Do you not see," says he, "that the father who begets is greater in age, and the son who is begotten less? How then say ye? tell me; how then say ye, that the Father and the Son, God and Christ, are equal; when ye see that when a man begets a son, the son is less, and the father greater?" Thou wise one, in eternity thou art looking for times; where there are no times, thou art looking for differences of age! When the father is greater in age, and the son less, both are in time; the one groweth, for that the other groweth old.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:40
verses.text: For by 			 nature, the man, the father, did not beget one less, by nature, as I said, but by age.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:41
verses.text: Wouldest thou know, how that by nature he did not beget one less? Wait, let him grow, and he will be equal to his father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:42
verses.text: For a little boy even by growing attains to his father's full size.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:43
verses.text: Whereas you assert that the Son of God is in such wise born less, as never to grow, and by growing even to attain to His Father's size.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:44
verses.text: Now then a man's son born of a man, is born in a better 			 condition than the Son of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:45
verses.text: How? Because the former grows, and attains to his father's size.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:46
verses.text: But Christ, if it is as ye say, is in such wise born less, as that He must ever remain less, and no growth of years at least is to be looked for here.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:47
verses.text: Thus then you say that there is a diversity in nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:48
verses.text: But why say you so, but because you will not believe the Son to be of the Same Substance which the Father is? Finally, first acknowledge that He is of the Same Substance, and so call Him less.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:49
verses.text: Consider the case of a man, he is a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:50
verses.text: What is his substance? He is a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:51
verses.text: What is he whom he begets? He is less, but he is a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:52
verses.text: The age is unequal, the nature equal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:53
verses.text: Do you then say too, "What the Father is, That is the Son, but the Son is less"? Say so, make a step forward, say, "of the Same Substance, only less;" and you will get to His being equal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:54
verses.text: For it is not a little step you take, it is not a little approach you make to the truth, of acknowledging Him equal, if you shall 			 acknowledge Him to be of the Same Substance, though less.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:55
verses.text: "But He is not of the Same Substance," this you say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:56
verses.text: So then in that you say this, here is gold and silver; what you say is as if a man were to beget a horse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:57
verses.text: For a man is of one substance, a horse of another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:58
verses.text: If then the Son is of another substance than the Father, the Father hath begotten a monster.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:59
verses.text: For when a creature, that is a woman, gives birth to anything that is not a man, it is called a monster.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:60
verses.text: But that it be not a monster, 			 he that is born is that which he is that begat him, that is, a man and a man, a horse and a horse, a dove and a dove, a sparrow and a sparrow.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:61
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:62
verses.text: To His creatures hath He given to beget that which they are.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:63
verses.text: To His creatures, to mortal, earthly creatures, hath God given, hath granted to beget that which they are; and thinkest thou that He hath not been able to reserve this for Himself, He who is before all ages? Should He who hath no beginning of time, beget a son, different from That which Himself is, beget a degenerate son? Hear ye how great a blasphemy it is to say, that the Only Son of God is of another 			 substance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:64
verses.text: Most certainly if He is so, He is degenerate.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:65
verses.text: If you should say to any child of man, "Thou art degenerate," how great an offence is it! And yet in what sense is any child of man said to be degenerate? As, for example, his father is brave, he is a poltroon and a coward.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:66
verses.text: If any one sees him, and would rebuke him, as he thinks of his brave father, what does he say to him? "Get thee hence, thou degenerate one!" What is "degenerate one"? "Thy father was a brave man, and thou 			 tremblest through fear".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:67
verses.text: He to whom this is said, is degenerate by some fault, by nature he is equal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:68
verses.text: What is, "by nature he is equal"? He is a man, which his father also is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:69
verses.text: But the one brave, the other a coward; the one bold, the other timid; yet both men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:70
verses.text: By some fault then he is degenerate, not by nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:71
verses.text: But when you say, that the Only Son, the One Son of the Father, is degenerate, you say nought else, but that He is not What the Father is; and you do not say, that having been 			 already born, He has become degenerate; but He was begotten so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:72
verses.text: Who can endure this blasphemy? If they could in any sort whatever see this blasphemy, they would fly from it, and become catholics.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:73
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:74
verses.text: But what shall I say, Brethren? Let us not be angry with them; but pray we for them, that God would give them understanding; for peradventure they were born so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:75
verses.text: What is, were born so? They receive what they hold from their parents.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:76
verses.text: They prefer their birth to the truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:77
verses.text: Let them become what they are not, that they may be able to keep what they are; that is, let them become catholics, that they may keep their nature as men; that the creation of God in them perish not, let the grace of God be added to them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:78
verses.text: For they imagine that by their outrage of the Son they honour the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:79
verses.text: When you say to him, "Thou blasphemest;" he answers, 			 "Why do I blaspheme?" "In that thou sayest that the Son is not what the Father is".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:80
verses.text: And he answers me, "Yea, it is thou who blasphemest".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:81
verses.text: Why? "Because thou wouldest make the Son equal to the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:82
verses.text: "I do wish to make the Son equal with the Father, but is this to make a stranger equal? The Father rejoiceth when I equal with Him His Only Son; He rejoiceth because He is not envious.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:83
verses.text: And because God is not envious of His Only Son, therefore did He beget Him Such as He is 			 Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:84
verses.text: Thou doest wrong both to the Son, and to the Father Himself, for whose honour thou wouldest do outrage to the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:85
verses.text: For in truth for this reason dost thou say that the Son is not of the Same Substance, lest thou shouldest do wrong to His Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:86
verses.text: I will soon show thee, that thou doest wrong to both".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:87
verses.text: "How?" saith he.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:88
verses.text: "If I say to any man's son, Thou art degenerate, thou art not like thy father; degenerate, thou art not what thy father is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:89
verses.text: The son hears it, and is angry, and 			 says, 'Was I then born degenerate?' The father hears it, and is more angry still.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:90
verses.text: And in his anger what says he? 'Have I then begotten a degenerate son? If I then be one thing, and I have begotten another, I have begotten a monster.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:91
verses.text: ' What is it then, that whereas thou wishest to pay honour to the One by doing outrage to the Other, thou doest outrage to Both? Thou offendest the Son, but thou wilt not propitiate the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:92
verses.text: When thou honourest the Father by outraging 			 the Son, thou offendest both the Son and the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:93
verses.text: From whom wilt thou fly? to whom wilt thou fly? When the Father is angry with thee, dost thou fly to the Son? What doth He say to thee? 'To whom dost thou fly, to Me, whom thou hast made degenerate?' When the Son is offended, dost thou run to the Father? He too saith to thee; 'To whom dost thou fly, to Me who, thou hast said, have begotten a degenerate Son?'" Let this suffice for you; hold it fast, commit it to memory, inscribe it 			 in your faith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 87:94
verses.text: But that ye may understand it, pour out your prayers to God, the Father and the Son, who are One.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:1
verses.text: Sermon XC.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:2
verses.text: [CXL.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John xii.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:5
verses.text: 44, "He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:6
verses.text: Against a certain expression of Maximinus, a bishop of the Arians, who spread his blasphemy in Africa where he was with the Count Segisvult.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:8
verses.text: What is it, Brethren, which we have heard the Lord saying, "He that believeth on Me, believeth not on Me, but on Him that sent Me"? It is good for us to believe on Christ, especially seeing that He hath also Himself expressly said this which ye have now heard, that is, that "He had come a Light into the world, and whosoever believeth on Him shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:9
verses.text: Good then it is to believe on Christ; and a great evil it is not to believe on Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:10
verses.text: But because Christ the Son is, Whatsoever He is, of the Father, but the Father is not of the Son, but is the Father of the Son; He recommends to us indeed faith in Himself, but refers the honour to His Original.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:11
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:12
verses.text: For hold this fast as a firm and settled truth, if ye would continue Catholics, that God the Father begat God the Son without time, and made Him of a Virgin in time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:13
verses.text: The first nativity exceedeth times; the second nativity enlighteneth times.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:14
verses.text: Yet both nativities are marvellous; the one without a mother, the other without a father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:15
verses.text: When God begat the Son, He begat Him of Himself, not of a mother; when the Mother gave birth to her Son, she gave Him birth as a 			 Virgin, not by man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:16
verses.text: He was born of the Father without a beginning; He was born of a mother, as to-day at an appointed beginning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:17
verses.text: Born of the Father He made us; born of a mother He re-made us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:18
verses.text: He was born of the Father, that we might be; He was born of a mother, that we might not be lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:19
verses.text: But the Father begat Him equal to Himself, and All Whatsoever the Son is, He hath of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:20
verses.text: But What God the Father is, He hath not of the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:21
verses.text: Accordingly we say that the Father is God, of none; the Son, God of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:22
verses.text: Wherefore all that the Son doeth marvellously, all that He saith truly, 			 He attributeth to Him of whom He is; yet can He not be ought else than He of whom He is.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:23
verses.text: Adam was made a man; he had power to become something other than he was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:24
verses.text: For he was made righteous, and he had power to become unrighteous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:25
verses.text: But the Only-Begotten Son of God, What He is, This cannot be changed; He cannot be changed into anything else, cannot be diminished, What He was He cannot but be, He cannot but be equal to the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:26
verses.text: But undoubtedly He who gave all things to the Son by His Birth, 			 gave it to One not needing ought; without doubt this very equality too with the Father, the Father gave to the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:27
verses.text: How did the Father give It? did He beget Him less, and add to Him to complete His Form, that He might make Him equal? If he had done this, He would have given it to one in need.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:28
verses.text: But I have told you already what ye ought most firmly to hold fast, that is, that All That the Son is, the Father gave Him, gave Him, that is, by His Birth, not as in need of ought.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:29
verses.text: If He gave it to Him by 			 His Birth, and not as in need, then doubtless He both gave Him equality, and in giving Him equality, begat Him equal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:30
verses.text: And although the One be One Person, and the Other Another; yet is not the One one thing, and the Other another; but What the One is, That the Other also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:31
verses.text: He who is the One, is not the Other; but What the One, That too the Other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:32
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:33
verses.text: "He Who sent Me," saith He, ye have heard it; "He Who sent Me," saith He, "He gave Me a commandment what I should say, and what I should speak; and I know that His commandment is life everlasting".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:34
verses.text: It is John's Gospel, hold it fast.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:35
verses.text: "He Who sent Me, He gave Me a commandment what I should say, and what I should speak; and I know that His commandment is life everlasting".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:36
verses.text: O that He would grant me to say what I wish! For my poverty and His abundance straiteneth me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:37
verses.text: "He," saith He, "gave Me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak; and I know that His commandment is life everlasting".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:38
verses.text: Search in the Epistle of this John 			 the Evangelist for what he hath said of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:39
verses.text: "Let us believe," he says, "His True Son Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:40
verses.text: This is the True God and Everlasting Life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:41
verses.text: What is, "The True God, and Everlasting Life"? The True Son of God is the "the True God, and Everlasting Life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:42
verses.text: Why did He say, "On His True Son"? Because God hath many sons, therefore was He to be distinguished, by adding that He was the True Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:43
verses.text: Not by simply saying that He is the Son; but by adding, as I have said, that He is the True Son; therefore He was to be distinguished, because of the many sons which God hath.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:44
verses.text: For we are sons by grace, He by Nature.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:45
verses.text: We 			 made by the Father through Him; He Himself That Which the Father is; are we too That Which God is?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:46
verses.text: But some man coming across us, knowing not what he is saying, says, "For this reason was it said, "I and My Father are One; for that They have with One Another an agreement of will, not because the Nature of the Son is the Very Same as the Nature of the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:47
verses.text: For the Apostles too (now this is what he said, not I), for the Apostles too are one with the Father and the Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:48
verses.text: Horrible blasphemy! "And the Apostles," says he, "are one with the Father and the Son, in that they obey the will of the Father and the Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:49
verses.text: Has he dared to say this? Let Paul then say, "I and God are one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:50
verses.text: Let Peter say it, let every one of the Prophets say, "I and God are one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:51
verses.text: They do not say it; God forbid they should.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:52
verses.text: They know that they are a different nature, a nature that needeth to 			 be saved; they know that they are a different nature, a nature that needeth to be enlightened.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:53
verses.text: No one says, "I and God are one".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:54
verses.text: Whatsoever progress he may make, howsoever he may surpass others in holiness, with how great eminence soever of virtue he may excel, he never saith, "I and God are one;" for if he have excellence, and therefore saith it; by saying it, he loseth what he had.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:55
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:56
verses.text: Believe then that the Son is equal with the Father; but yet that the Son is of the Father; but the Father not of the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:57
verses.text: The Original is with the Father, equality with the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:58
verses.text: For if He be not equal, He is not a true Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:59
verses.text: For what are we saying, Brethren? If He is not equal, He is less; if He is less, I ask the nature that needeth to be saved, in its misbelief, "how is He born less?" Answer, Doth He as being less grow or not? If He groweth, then the Father 			 groweth old.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:60
verses.text: But if He will ever be what He was born; if He was born less, He will continue less; with this His loss He will be perfect; born perfect with this loss of the Father's Form, He is never to attain to the Father's Form.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:61
verses.text: Thus do ye ungodly assail the Son; thus do ye heretics blaspheme the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:62
verses.text: What then saith the Catholic faith? The Son is God, of God the Father; God the Father, not God of the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:63
verses.text: But God the Son equal with the Father, Born equal; not Born less, not made equal, but Born equal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:64
verses.text: What the Father is, That is He also who was born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:65
verses.text: Was the Father ever without the Son? God forbid! Take away your "ever," where there is no time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:66
verses.text: The Father always, the Son always.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:67
verses.text: The Father without beginning of time, the 			 Son without beginning of time; the Father never before the Son, the Father never without the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:68
verses.text: But yet because the Son is God of God the Father, and the Father God, but not of God the Son; let not the honouring of the Son in the Father displease us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:69
verses.text: For the honouring of the Son giveth honour to the Father, it diminisheth not His Own Divinity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:70
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:71
verses.text: Because then I was speaking of what I had brought forward, "And I knew," saith He, "that His commandment is everlasting life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:72
verses.text: Mark, Brethren, what I am saying; "I know that His commandment is everlasting life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:73
verses.text: And we read in the same John concerning Christ, "He is The True God and Everlasting Life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:74
verses.text: If the Father's commandment is "everlasting Life," and Christ the Son Himself is "everlasting Life;" the Son is Himself the Father's Commandment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:75
verses.text: For how is not That the Father's Commandment, which is the Father's Word? Or if you take the commandment given to the Son by the Father in a carnal sense, as if the Father said to the Son, "I command Thee this, I wish Thee to do that;" in what words spake He to the Only Word? When He gave commandment to the Word, 			 did He look for words? That the Father's Commandment then is "Life everlasting," and that the Son Himself is "Life everlasting," believe ye and receive, believe and understand, for the Prophet saith, "Unless ye believe ye shall not understand".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:76
verses.text: Do ye not comprehend? Be enlarged.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:77
verses.text: Hear the Apostle: "Be ye enlarged, bear not the yoke with unbelievers".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:78
verses.text: They who will not believe this before they comprehend, are unbelievers.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:79
verses.text: And because they have determined to be unbelievers, they will remain in their ignorance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:80
verses.text: Let them believe then that they may understand.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:81
verses.text: Most certainly the Father's Commandment is "everlasting Life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:82
verses.text: Therefore the Father's Commandment is the Very Son who was born this day; a Commandment not given in time but a Commandment Born.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:83
verses.text: The Gospel of John exercises our minds, refines 			  and uncarnalizes them, that of God we may think not after a carnal but a spiritual manner.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 88:84
verses.text: Let so much then, Brethren, suffice you; lest in length of disputation, the sleep of forgetfulness steal over you.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:1
verses.text: Sermon XCI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:2
verses.text: [CXLI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John xiv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:5
verses.text: 6, "I am the way, and the truth, and the life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:7
verses.text: Amongst other things, when the Holy Gospel was being read, ye heard what the Lord Jesus said, "I am the Way, and the Truth, and the Life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:8
verses.text: Truth and life doth every man desire; but not every man doth find the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:9
verses.text: That God is a certain Life Eternal, Unchangeable, Intelligible, Intelligent, Wise, Making wise, some philosophers even of this world have seen.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:10
verses.text: The fixed, settled, unwavering truth, wherein are all the principles of all things created, they saw indeed, but afar off; they saw, but amid the error in which they were placed; and therefore what way to attain to that so great, and ineffable, and beatific a possession they formed not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:11
verses.text: For that even they saw (as far as can be seen by man) the Creator by means of the creature, the Worker by His work, the Framer of the world by the world, the Apostle Paul is witness, whom Christians ought surely to believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:12
verses.text: For he said when he was speaking of 			 such; "The wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:13
verses.text: These are, as ye recognise, the words of the Apostle Paul; "The wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness, and unrighteousness of men; who detain the truth in unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:14
verses.text: Did he say that they do not detain truth? No: but, "They detained the truth in unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:15
verses.text: What they detain, is good; but wherein they detain it, is bad.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:16
verses.text: "They detain the truth in unrighteousness".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:17
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:18
verses.text: Now it occurred to him that it might be said to him, "Whence do these ungodly men detain the truth? Hath God spoken to any one of them? Have they received the Law as the people of the Israelites by Moses? Whence then do they detain the truth, though it be even in this unrighteousness?" Hear what follows, and he shows.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:19
verses.text: "Because that which can be known of God," he says, "is manifest in them; for God hath manifested it unto them".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:20
verses.text: Manifested it unto them to whom He hath not given the Law? Hear how He hath manifested it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:21
verses.text: "For the invisible things of Him are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:22
verses.text: Ask the world, the beauty of the heaven, the brilliancy and ordering of the stars, the sun, that sufficeth for the day, the moon, the solace of the night; ask the earth fruitful in herbs, and trees, full of animals, adorned with men; ask the sea, with how great and what kind of fishes filled; ask the air, with how great birds stocked; ask all things, and see if they do not as if it were by a language of their own make answer to thee, "God made us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:23
verses.text: These things have illustrious philosophers sought out, and by the art have come to know the Artificer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:24
verses.text: What then? Why is the wrath of God revealed against this ungodliness? "Because they detain the truth in unrighteousness?" Let him come, let him show how.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:25
verses.text: For how they came to know Him, he hath said already.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:26
verses.text: "The invisible things of Him," that is God, "are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made; 			 His eternal Power also and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:27
verses.text: Because that when they knew God, they glorified Him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:28
verses.text: They are the Apostle's words, not mine: "And their foolish heart was darkened; for professing themselves to be wise, they became fools".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:29
verses.text: What by curious search they found, by pride they lost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:30
verses.text: "Professing themselves to be wise," attributing, that is, the gift of God to themselves, "they became fools".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:31
verses.text: They are the Apostle's words, I say; "Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:32
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:33
verses.text: Show, prove their foolishness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:34
verses.text: Show, O Apostle, and as thou hast shown us whereby they were able to attain to the knowledge of God, for that "the invisible things of Him are clearly seen, being understood by those things that are made;" so now show how, "professing themselves to be wise, they became fools".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:35
verses.text: Hear; Because "they changed," he says, "the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the image of a corruptible man, and of birds, 			 and of four-footed beasts, and of creeping things".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:36
verses.text: For of figures of these animals, the Pagans made themselves gods.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:37
verses.text: Thou hast found out God, and thou worshippest an idol.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:38
verses.text: Thou hast found out the truth, and this very truth dost thou detain in unrighteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:39
verses.text: And what by the works of God thou hast come to know, by the works of man thou losest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:40
verses.text: Thou hast considered the universe, hast collected the order of the heaven, the earth, the sea, and all the elements; thou wilt not take heed to this, that the world is the work of God, an idol is the work of a carpenter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:41
verses.text: If the carpenter as he has given the figure, could also give a heart, the carpenter would be worshipped by his own idol.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:42
verses.text: For, O man, as God is thy Framer, so the idol's framer is a man.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:43
verses.text: Who is thy God? He That made thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:44
verses.text: Who is the carpenter's god? He That made him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:45
verses.text: Who 			 is the idol's god? He that made it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:46
verses.text: If then the idol had a heart, would he not worship the carpenter who made it? See in what unrighteousness they detained the truth, and found not the way that leadeth to that possession which they saw.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:47
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:48
verses.text: But Christ, for that He is with the Father, the Truth, and Life, the Word of God, of whom it is said, "The Life was the Light of men;" for that I say He is with the Father, the Truth, and Life, and we had no way whereby to go to the Truth, the Son of God, who is ever in the Father the Truth and Life, by assuming man's nature became the Way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:49
verses.text: Walk by Him as Man, and thou comest to God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:50
verses.text: By Him thou goest, to Him thou goest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:51
verses.text: Look not out for any way whereby to come to Him, besides Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:52
verses.text: For if He had not vouchsafed to be the Way, we should have always gone astray.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:53
verses.text: He then became the Way Whereby thou 			 shouldest come; I do not say to thee, seek the Way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:54
verses.text: The Way Itself hath come to thee, arise and walk.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:55
verses.text: Walk, with the life, not with the feet.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:56
verses.text: For many walk well with the feet, and with their lives walk ill.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:57
verses.text: For sometimes even those who walk well, run outside the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:58
verses.text: Thus you will find men living well, and not Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:59
verses.text: They run well; but they run not in the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:60
verses.text: The more they run, the more they go astray; because they are out of the Way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:61
verses.text: But if such men as these come to the Way, and hold on the Way, O how great is their security, because they both walk well, and do not go astray! But if they do 			 not hold on the Way, however well they walk, alas! how are they to be bewailed! For better is it to halt in the way, than to walk on stoutly outside the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:62
verses.text: Let this suffice for you, Beloved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 89:63
verses.text: Turn we to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:1
verses.text: Sermon XCII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:2
verses.text: [CXLII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:4
verses.text: ]  On the same words of the Gospel, John xiv.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:5
verses.text: 6, "I am the way," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:7
verses.text: The divine lessons raise us up, that we be not broken by despair; and terrify us again, that we be not tossed to and fro by pride.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:8
verses.text: But to hold the middle, the true, the strait way, as it were between the left hand of despair, and the right hand of presumption, would be most difficult for us, had not Christ said, "I am the Way, and the Truth, and the Life".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:9
verses.text: As if He had said, "By what way wouldest thou go? 'I am the Way'.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:10
verses.text: Whither wouldest thou go? 'I am the Truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:11
verses.text: ' Where wouldest thou abide? 'I am the Life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:12
verses.text: '" Let us then walk with all assurance in the Way; but let us fear snares by the way side.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:13
verses.text: The enemy does not dare to lay his snares in the way; because Christ is the Way; but most certainly by the way side he ceases not to do so.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:14
verses.text: Whence too it is said in the Psalm, "They have laid stumblingblocks for me by 			 the way side".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:15
verses.text: And another Scripture saith, "Remember that thou walkest in the midst of snares".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:16
verses.text: These snares among which we walk are not in the way; but yet they are "by the way side".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:17
verses.text: What fearest thou, what art thou alarmed at, so thou walk in the Way? Fear then, if thou forsake the Way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:18
verses.text: For for this reason is the enemy even permitted to lay snares by the way side, lest through the security of exultation the Way be forsaken, and ye fall into the snares.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:19
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:20
verses.text: Christ Humbled is the Way; Christ the Truth and the Life, Christ Highly Exalted and God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:21
verses.text: If thou walk in the Humbled, thou shalt attain to the Exalted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:22
verses.text: If infirm as thou art, thou despise not the Humbled, thou shalt abide exceeding strong in the Exalted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:23
verses.text: For what cause was there of Christ's Humiliation, save thine infirmity? For solely and irremediably did thine infirmity press thee in, and this circumstance it was that made so great a Physician come to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:24
verses.text: For if 			 thy sickness had been even such, that thou couldest have gone to the Physician, this infirmity might have seemed endurable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:25
verses.text: But because thou couldest not go to Him, He came to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:26
verses.text: He came teaching humility, whereby we might return; for that pride allowed us not to return to life; yea had even made us depart from life.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:27
verses.text: For the heart of man being lifted up against God, and neglecting in its sound state His saving precepts, the soul fell away into infirmity; let her in her infirmity learn to 			 hear Him whom in her strength she despised.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:28
verses.text: Let her hear Him that she may rise, whom she despised, that she might fall.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:29
verses.text: Let her at length, taught by experience, give ear to what she had no mind, when taught by precept, to obtain.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:30
verses.text: For her misery hath taught her, how evil a thing it is to go a whoring from the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:31
verses.text: For to fall away from that Simple and Singular Good, into this multitude of pleasures, into the love of the world, and earthly corruption, is to go a whoring from the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:32
verses.text: And He 			 hath addressed her as in a sense a harlot, to warn her to return: very often by the Prophets doth He reproach her as a harlot, but yet not despaired of, for that He who reproacheth the harlot hath in His Hands the cleansing of the harlot too.
