verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:33
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:34
verses.text: For He doth not so reproach as to insult her; but He would bring her to confusion of face to heal her.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:35
verses.text: Vehement are the exclamations of Scripture, nor doth it deal softly by flattery with those whom it would by healing recover.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:36
verses.text: "Ye adulterers, know ye not that the friend of this world is constituted the enemy of God?" The love of the world maketh the soul adulterous, the love of the Framer of the world maketh the soul chaste; but unless she blush for her corruption, she hath no desire to return to that chaste embrace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:37
verses.text: Be she confounded that she may return, who was vaunting herself that she should not return.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:38
verses.text: It was pride then that hindered the soul's return.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:39
verses.text: But whoso reproacheth doth not cause the sin, but showeth the sin.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:40
verses.text: What the soul was loth to see, is placed before her eyes; and 			 what she desired to have behind her back, is brought before her face.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:41
verses.text: See thyself in thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:42
verses.text: "Why seest thou the mote in thy brother's eye, but perceivest not the beam in thine own eye?" The soul which went away from herself, is recalled to herself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:43
verses.text: As she had gone away from herself, so went she away from her Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:44
verses.text: For she had respect to herself, and pleased herself, and became enamoured of her own power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:45
verses.text: She withdrew from him, and abode not in herself; and from her own self she is repelled, and from herself shut out, and she falleth away unto things without her.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:46
verses.text: She loves the world, loves the things of time, loves earthly things; who if she but loved herself 			 to the neglect of Him by whom she was made, would at once be less, at once fail by loving that which is less.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:47
verses.text: For she is less than God; yea less by far, and by so much less as the thing made is less than the Maker.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:48
verses.text: It was God then That ought to have been loved, yea in such wise ought God to be loved, that if it might be so, we should forget ourselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:49
verses.text: What then is this change? The soul hath forgotten herself, but by loving the world; let her now forget herself, but by loving the world's 			 Maker.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:50
verses.text: Driven away even from herself, I say, she hath in a manner lost herself, and hath not skilled to see her own actions, she justifies her iniquities; she is puffed up, and prides herself in insolence, in voluptuousness, in honours, in posts of authority, in riches, in the power of vanity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:51
verses.text: She is reproved, rebuked, is shown to herself, mislikes herself, confesses her deformity, longs for her first beauty, and she who went away in profusion returns in confusion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:52
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:53
verses.text: Seemeth he to pray against her, or for her, who says, "Fill their faces with shame"? It seems to be an adversary, it seems an enemy.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:54
verses.text: Hear what follows, and see whether a friend can offer this prayer.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:55
verses.text: "Fill," says he, "their faces with shame, and they shall seek Thy Name, O Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:56
verses.text: Did he hate them whose faces he desired to be filled with shame? See how he loves them whom he would have seek the Name of the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:57
verses.text: Does he love only, or hate only? or does he both hate, and love? Yea, he both hates, and loves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:58
verses.text: He hates what is thine, he loves thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:59
verses.text: What is, "He hates what is thine, he loves thee"? He hates what thou hast made, he loves what God hath made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:60
verses.text: For what are thine own things but sins? And what art thou but what God made thee, a man after His 			 Own image and likeness? Thou dost neglect what thou wast made, love what thou hast made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:61
verses.text: Thou dost love thine own works without thee, dost neglect the work of God within thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:62
verses.text: Deservedly dost thou go away, deservedly fall off, yea, deservedly even from thine own self depart; deservedly hear the words, "A spirit that goeth and returneth not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:63
verses.text: Hear rather Him That calleth and saith, "Turn ye unto Me, and I will turn unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:64
verses.text: For God doth not really turn away, and turn again; Abiding the Same He rebuketh, Unchangeable He rebuketh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:65
verses.text: He hath turned away, in that thou hast turned thyself away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:66
verses.text: Thou hast fallen from Him, He hath not fallen away from thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:67
verses.text: Hear Him then saying to thee, "Turn ye unto Me, and I will turn unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:68
verses.text: For this is, "I turn unto you, in that ye turn unto Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:69
verses.text: He followeth on the back of him that flieth, He enlighteneth the face of him that returneth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:70
verses.text: For whither wilt thou fly in flying from God? Whither wilt thou fly in flying from Him who is contained in no place, and is nowhere absent? He That delivereth him that turneth to him, punisheth him that turneth away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:71
verses.text: Thou hast a Judge by flying; 			 have a Father by returning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:72
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:73
verses.text: But he had been swollen up by pride, and by this swelling could not return by the strait way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:74
verses.text: He who became the Way, crieth out, "Enter ye in by the strait gate".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:75
verses.text: He tries to enter in, the swelling impedes him; and his trying is so much the more hurtful, in proportion as the swelling is a greater impediment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:76
verses.text: For the straitness irritates his swelling; and being irritated he will swell the more; and swelling more, when will he enter in? So then let him bring down the swelling.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:77
verses.text: And how? Let him take the medicine of humility; let him against the swelling drink the bitter but wholesome cup; drink the cup of humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:78
verses.text: Why doth he squeeze himself? The bulk, not for its size, but for its swelling, doth not allow him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:79
verses.text: For size hath solidity, swelling inflation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:80
verses.text: Let not him that is swollen fancy himself of great size; 			 that he may be great, and substantial, and solid, let him bring down his swelling.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:81
verses.text: Let him not long after these present things, let him not glory in this pomp of things failing and corruptible; let him hearken to Him who said, "Enter in by the strait gate," saying also, "I am the Way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:82
verses.text: For as if some swollen one had asked, "How shall I enter in?" He saith, "'I am the Way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:83
verses.text: ' Enter in by Me; Thou walkest only by Me, to enter in by the door".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:84
verses.text: For as He said, "I am the Way;" so also, "I am the Door".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:85
verses.text: Why seekest thou whereby to return, whither to return, whereby to enter in? Lest thou shouldest in any respect go astray, He became all for thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:86
verses.text: Therefore in brief He saith, "Be humble, be meek".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:87
verses.text: Let us hear Him saying this most plainly, that thou mayest see whereby is the way, what is the way, whither is the way.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:88
verses.text: Whither wouldest thou come? But peradventure in covetousness thou wouldest possess all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:89
verses.text: "All things are delivered unto Me of My Father," 			  saith He.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:90
verses.text: It may be thou wilt say, "They were delivered to Christ: but are they to me?" Hear the Apostle speak; hear, as I said some time ago, lest thou be broken by despair; hear how thou wert loved when thou hadst nothing to be loved for, hear how thou wert loved when unsightly, deformed, before there was ought in thee which was meet to be loved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:91
verses.text: Thou wast first loved, that thou mightest be made meet to be loved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:92
verses.text: For Christ, as the Apostle says, "died for the 			 ungodly".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:93
verses.text: What! will you say that the ungodly deserved to be loved? I ask, what did the ungodly deserve? To be damned.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:94
verses.text: Here you will answer, Yet, "Christ died for the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:95
verses.text: Lo, what was done for thee when ungodly; what is reserved for thee now godly? "Christ died for the ungodly".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:96
verses.text: Thou didst desire to possess all things; desire it not through covetousness, seek it through piety, seek it through humility.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:97
verses.text: For if thou seek thus, thou shalt possess.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:98
verses.text: For thou shalt have Him by 			 whom all things were made, and with Him shalt possess all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:99
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:100
verses.text: I do not say this as though the result of reasoning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:101
verses.text: Hear the Apostle himself saying, "He that spared not His Own Son, but delivered Him up for us all; how hath He also not with Him given us all things?" Lo, covetous one, thou hast all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:102
verses.text: All things that thou lovest, despise, that thou be not kept back from Christ, and hold to Him in whom thou mayest possess all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:103
verses.text: The Physician Himself then needing no such medicine, yet that He might encourage the sick, drank what He had no need of; addressing him as it were refusing it, and raising him up in his fear, He drank first.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:104
verses.text: "The Cup," saith He, "which I shall drink of;" "I who have nothing in Me to be cured by that Cup, am yet to drink it, that thou who needest to drink it, may not disdain to drink".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:105
verses.text: Now consider, Brethren, ought the human race to be any longer sick after having received such a medicine? God hath been now Humbled, and is man still proud? Let him hear, let him learn.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:106
verses.text: "All things," saith He, have been delivered unto Me of My Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:107
verses.text: If thou desirest all things, thou shalt have them with Me; if thou desirest the Father, by Me and in Me thou shalt have Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:108
verses.text: "No man knoweth the Father but the Son".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:109
verses.text: Do not despair; come to the Son.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:110
verses.text: Hear what follows, "And he to whom the Son will reveal Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:111
verses.text: Thou saidst, "I am not able.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:112
verses.text: Thou callest me through a strait way; I am not able to enter in by a strait way".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:113
verses.text: "Come," saith He, "unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:114
verses.text: Your burden is your 			 swelling.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:115
verses.text: "Come unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:116
verses.text: Take My yoke upon you, and learn of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:117
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:118
verses.text: The Master of the Angels crieth out, the Word of God, by whom all reasonable souls are without failing fed, the Food That refresheth, and abideth Entire, crieth out and saith, "Learn of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:119
verses.text: Let the people hear Him, saying, "Learn of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:120
verses.text: Let them make answer, "What do we learn of Thee?" For we must be going to hear I know not what from the Great Artificer, when He saith, "Learn of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:121
verses.text: Who is it that saith, "Learn of Me"? He who formed the 			 earth, who divided the sea and the dry land, who created the fowls, who created the animals of the earth, who created all things that swim, who set the stars in the heaven, who distinguished the day and the night, who established the firmament, who separated the light from the darkness, He it is who saith, "Learn of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:122
verses.text: Is He haply about to tell us this, that we should do these things with Him? Who can do this? God Only doeth them.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:123
verses.text: "Fear not," He saith, "I am not laying any burden on 			 thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:124
verses.text: 'Learn of Me,' this which for thy sake I was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:125
verses.text: 'Learn of Me,'" saith He, "not to form the creature which by Me was made.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:126
verses.text: Neither do I tell you indeed, to learn those things which I have granted to some, to whom I would, not to all, to raise the dead, to give sight to the blind, to open the ears of the deaf; nor to wish as for some great thing to learn these things of Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:127
verses.text: The disciples returned with joy and exultation, saying, "Lo, even the devils are subject unto us 			 through Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:128
verses.text: And the Lord said to them, "In this rejoice not, that the devils are subject unto you; rejoice rather, because your names are written in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:129
verses.text: To whom He would, He gave the power to cast out devils, to whom He would, He gave the power to raise the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:130
verses.text: Such miracles were done even before the Incarnation of the Lord; the dead were raised, lepers were cleansed; we read of these things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:131
verses.text: And who did them then, but He who in after time was the Man-Christ after David, but God-Christ before Abraham? He gave the power for all these things, He did them Himself by men; yet gave He not that power to all.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:132
verses.text: Ought they to whom He gave it not to despair, and say that they have no part in Him because they have not been thought worthy to receive these gifts? In the body are divers members: this member can do one thing, that another.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:133
verses.text: God hath compacted the body together, He hath not given to the ear to see, nor to the eye to hear, nor to the forehead to smell, nor to the hand to taste; He hath not given them these functions; but to all the members hath He given soundness, hath given union, hath given unity, hath by His Spirit quickened and united all alike.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:134
verses.text: And so here He hath not given to some to 			 raise the dead, to others He hath not given the power of disputation; yet to all what hath He given? "Learn of Me, that I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:135
verses.text: Forasmuch as we have heard Him say, "I am meek and lowly in heart;" here, my Brethren, is our whole remedy, "Learn of Me, that I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:136
verses.text: What doth it profit a man if he do miracles, and is proud, is not meek and lowly in heart? Will he not be reckoned in the number of those who shall come at the last day, and say, 			 "Have we not prophesied in Thy Name, and in Thy Name have done many mighty works?" But what shall they hear? "I know you not, Depart from Me, all ye that work iniquity".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:137
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:138
verses.text: What then doth it profit us to learn? "That I am meek," saith He, "and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:139
verses.text: He engrafteth charity, and that most genuine charity, without confusion, without inflation, without elation, without deceit; this doth He engraft, who saith, "Learn of Me, that I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:140
verses.text: How can one proud and puffed up have any genuine charity? He must needs be envious.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:141
verses.text: And mayhap one who is envious, loves, and we are mistaken? God forbid that any one should be so mistaken, as to say that an envious man hath charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:142
verses.text: And so what saith the Apostle? "Charity envieth not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:143
verses.text: Why doth it not envy? "It is not puffed up;" he immediately annexed the cause for which he took away envying from charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:144
verses.text: Because it is not puffed up, it envieth not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:145
verses.text: It is true, he said first, "Charity envieth not;" but as though thou didst ask, "Why doth it not envy?" he added, "It is not puffed up.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:146
verses.text: If then it envieth because it is puffed up; if it be not puffed up, it envieth not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:147
verses.text: If charity is not puffed up, and therefore envieth not; then doth He engraft charity who saith, "Learn of Me, that I am meek 			 and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:148
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:149
verses.text: Let any man have then what he will, let him boast himself of what he will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:150
verses.text: "If I speak with the tongues of men and of Angels, but, have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:151
verses.text: What is more sublime than the gift of divers tongues? It is "brass," it is "a tinkling cymbal," if thou take charity away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:152
verses.text: Hear other gifts; "If I should know all mysteries".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:153
verses.text: What more excellent? what more magnificent? Hear yet another; "if I should have all prophecy, and all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not charity, I am nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:154
verses.text: He comes to still greater things, Brethren.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:155
verses.text: What else has he said? "If I should distribute all my goods to the poor".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:156
verses.text: What more perfect thing can be done? When indeed the Lord commanded the rich man this for perfection's sake, saying, "If thou wilt be perfect, go, sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:157
verses.text: Was he then at once perfect, because he sold all his goods and gave them to the poor? No; and therefore He added, "And come, follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:158
verses.text: "Sell all," saith He, "give to the poor, and come, follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:159
verses.text: "Why should I follow Thee? Now that I have sold all, and distributed to the poor, am I not perfect? What need is there that I should follow Thee?" "Follow Me," that thou mayest learn that "I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:160
verses.text: For what? can any man sell all he 			 hath, and give to the poor, who is not yet meek, not yet lowly in heart? Assuredly he can.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:161
verses.text: "For if I should distribute all my goods to the poor".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:162
verses.text: And hear still further.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:163
verses.text: For some, who had left all they had and had already followed the Lord, but not yet followed Him perfectly (for to follow Him perfectly is to imitate Him), could not bear the trial of suffering.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:164
verses.text: Peter, Brethren, was already one of those who had left all and followed the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:165
verses.text: For as that rich man went away in sadness, when 			 the disciples bring troubled, asked how then any one could be perfect, and the Lord consoled them, they said to the Lord, "Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed Thee; what shall we have therefore?" And the Lord told them what He would give them here, what He would reserve for them hereafter.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:166
verses.text: Now Peter was already of the number of those who had so done.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:167
verses.text: But when it came to the crisis of suffering, at the voice of a maid-servant he denied Him thrice with whom he had promised that he was ready to die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:168
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:169
verses.text: Take good heed then, Beloved: "Go," saith He, "sell all that thou hast, give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven, and come, follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:170
verses.text: Peter is perfect, now that the Lord sitteth in heaven at the right Hand of the Father, then did he attain perfection and maturity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:171
verses.text: For when he followed the Lord to His Passion, he was not perfect; but when there began to be no one on earth for him to follow, then was he perfected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:172
verses.text: But thou 			 truly hast always One before thee to follow; the Lord hath set up an example on earth, when He left the Gospel with thee, in the Gospel He is with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:173
verses.text: For He did not speak falsely when He said, "Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:174
verses.text: Therefore follow the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:175
verses.text: What is, "Follow the Lord"? Imitate the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:176
verses.text: What is, "Imitate the Lord"? "Learn of Me, that I am meek and lowly in heart".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:177
verses.text: Because if I should distribute all my goods to the poor, and give up my body to be burned, but not have charity, it profiteth me nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:178
verses.text: To this charity then I exhort your Charity; now I should not exhort to charity, but with some charity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:179
verses.text: I exhort then that what is commenced may be filled up; and pray that what is 			 begun may be perfected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:180
verses.text: And I beg that ye would offer this prayer for me, that what I advise may be perfected in me also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:181
verses.text: For we are all now imperfect, and there shall we be perfected, where all things are perfect.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:182
verses.text: The Apostle Paul says, "Brethren, I do not reckon myself to have apprehended".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:183
verses.text: He says, "Not that I have already attained, either am already perfect".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 90:184
verses.text: And shall any man dare to vaunt himself on perfection? Yea rather let us acknowledge our imperfection, that we may attain perfection.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:1
verses.text: Sermon XCIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:2
verses.text: [CXLIII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John xvi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:5
verses.text: 7, "I tell you the truth; it is expedient for you that I go away," etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:7
verses.text: The medicine for all the wounds of the soul, and the one propitiation for the offences of men, is to believe on Christ; nor can any one be cleansed at all, whether from original sin which he derived from Adam, in whom all men have sinned, and become by nature children of wrath; or from the sins which they have themselves added, by not resisting the concupiscence of the flesh, but by following and serving it in unclean and injurious deeds: unless by faith they are united and compacted into His Body, who was conceived without any enticement of the flesh and deadly pleasure, and whom His Mother nourished in her womb without sin, and "Who did no sin, neither was deceit found in His 			 Mouth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:8
verses.text: They verily who believe on Him, become the children of God; because they are born of God by the grace of adoption, which is by the faith of Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:9
verses.text: Wherefore, dearly Beloved, it is with good reason that the same Lord and our Saviour mentions this one sin only, of which the Holy Ghost convinces the world, that it believeth not on Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:10
verses.text: "I tell you the truth," He saith, "It is expedient for you that I go away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:11
verses.text: For if I go not away, the Comforter will not come 			 unto you; but if I depart, I will send Him unto you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:12
verses.text: And when He shall come, He will convince the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:13
verses.text: Of sin, because they believe not on Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:14
verses.text: Of righteousness, because I go to the Father, and ye shall see Me no more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:15
verses.text: Of judgment, because the prince of this world is already judged".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:17
verses.text: Of this one only sin then He would have the world to be convinced, that they believe not on Him; to wit, because by believing on Him all sins are loosed, He would have this one imputed by which the rest are bound.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:18
verses.text: And because by believing they are born of God, and become children of God; "For," saith he, "to them gave He power to become the sons of God, to them that believe on Him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:19
verses.text: Whoso then believeth on the Son of God, in so far as he adhereth to Him, and becometh himself also by adoption a son and heir of God, and a joint-heir with Christ, in so far he sinneth not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:20
verses.text: Whence John saith, "Whosoever is born of God sinneth not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:21
verses.text: And therefore the sin of which the world is convinced is this, that they believe not on Him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:22
verses.text: This is the sin of which He also saith, "If I had not come, they had not had sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:23
verses.text: For what! had they not innumerable other sins? But by His coming this one sin was added to them that believed not, by which the rest should be retained.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:24
verses.text: Whereas in them that believe, because this one was wanting, it was brought to pass that all should be remitted to them that believe.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:25
verses.text: Nor is it with any other view that the Apostle Paul saith, "All have sinned, and have need of the glory of God; that "whosoever believeth on Him, should not be confounded;" as the Psalm also saith "Come ye unto Him, and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be confounded".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:26
verses.text: Whoso then glorieth in himself shall be confounded; for he shall not be found without sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:27
verses.text: Accordingly he only shall not be confounded who glorieth in the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:28
verses.text: "For all have sinned, and have need of the glory of God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:29
verses.text: And so when he was speaking of the infidelity of the Jews, he did not say, "For if some of them have sinned, shall their sin make the faith of God of none effect?" For how should he say, "If some of them have sinned;" when he said himself, "For 			 all have sinned"? But he said, "If some of them believed not, shall their unbelief make the faith of God of none effect?" That he might point out more expressly this sin, by which alone the door is closed against the rest that they by the grace of God should not be remitted.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:30
verses.text: Of which one sin by the coming of the Holy Ghost, that is by the gift of His grace, which is granted to the faithful, the world is convinced, in the Lord's words, "Of sin, because they believed not on Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:31
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:32
verses.text: Now there would be no great merit and glorious blessedness in believing, if the Lord had always appeared in His Risen Body to the eyes of men.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:33
verses.text: The Holy Ghost then hath brought this great gift to them that should believe, that Him whom they should not see with the eyes of flesh, they might with a mind sobered from carnal desires, and inebriated with spiritual longings, sigh after.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:34
verses.text: Whence it was that when that disciple who had said that he would not believe, unless 			 he touched with the hands His Scars, after he had handled the Lord's Body, cried out as though awaking from sleep, "My Lord and my God;" the Lord said to him, "Because thou hast seen Me, thou hast believed; blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:35
verses.text: This blessedness hath the Holy Ghost, the Comforter, brought to us, that the form of a servant which He took from the Virgin's womb, being removed from the eyes of flesh, the purified eye of the mind might be directed to This Form of God, in which He continued equal with the Father, even when He vouchsafed to appear in the Flesh; so as that with the Same Spirit filled the Apostle might say, "Though we have known Christ after the flesh; yet now we know Him so no longer".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:36
verses.text: Because even the Flesh of Christ he knew not after the flesh, but after the Spirit, who, not by touching in curiosity, but in believing assured, acknowledgeth the power of His Resurrection; not saying in his heart, "Who hath ascended into heaven? that is, to bring Christ down; or, Who hath descended into the deep? that is, to bring back Christ from the dead".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:37
verses.text: "But," saith he, "the word is nigh thee, in thy mouth, that Jesus is the Lord; and if thou shalt believe in 			 thine heart that God hath raised Him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:38
verses.text: For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:39
verses.text: These, Brethren, are the words of the Apostle, pouring them forth with the holy inebriation of the Holy Ghost Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:40
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:41
verses.text: Forasmuch then as we could in no way have had this blessedness by which we see not and yet believe, unless we received it of the Holy Ghost; it is with good reason said, "It is expedient for you that I go away.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:42
verses.text: For if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send Him unto you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:43
verses.text: By His Divinity indeed He is with us always; but unless He had in Body gone away from us, we had always seen His Body after the flesh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:44
verses.text: and never believed after a spiritual sort; by the which belief justified and blessed we might attain with cleansed hearts to contemplate the Very Word, God with God, "by whom all things were made," and "who was made Flesh, that He might dwell among us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:45
verses.text: And if not with the contact of the hand, but "with the heart man believeth unto righteousness;" with good reason is the world, which will not believe save what it sees, convinced of our righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:46
verses.text: Now that we might have that righteousness of faith of which the unbelieving world should be convinced, therefore 			 said the Lord, "Of righteousness, because I go to the Father, and ye shall see Me no more".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:47
verses.text: As if He had said, "This shall be your righteousness, that ye believe on Me, the Mediator, of whom ye shall be most fully assured that He is risen again and gone to the Father, though ye see Him not after the Flesh; that by Him reconciled, ye may be able to see God after the Spirit".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:48
verses.text: Whence He saith to the woman who represents the Church, when she fell at His Feet after His Resurrection, "Touch 			 Me not, for I am not yet ascended to the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:49
verses.text: Which expression is understood mystically, thus.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:50
verses.text: "Believe not in Me after a carnal manner by means of bodily contact; but thou shalt believe after a spiritual manner; that is, with a spiritual faith shalt touch Me, when I shall have ascended to the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:51
verses.text: For, "blessed are they who do not see, and believe".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:52
verses.text: And this is the righteousness of faith, of which the world, which hath it not, is convinced of us who are not without it; for "the just liveth by faith".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:53
verses.text: Whether it be then that as rising again in Him, and in Him coming to the Father, we are invisibly and in justification perfected; or that as not seeing and yet believing we live by faith, for that "the just liveth by faith;" with these meanings said He, "Of righteousness, because I go to the Father, and ye shall see Me no more".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:54
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:55
verses.text: Nor let the world excuse itself by this, that it is hindered by the devil from believing on Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:56
verses.text: For to believers the prince of the world is cast out, that he work no more in the hearts of men whom Christ hath begun to possess by faith; as he worketh in the children of unbelief; whom he is constantly stirring up to tempt and disturb the righteous.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:57
verses.text: For because he is cast out, who once had dominion interiorly he wageth war exteriorly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:58
verses.text: Although then by means of his persecutions, "the Lord doth direct the meek in judgment;" nevertheless in this very fact of his being cast out, is he "judged already".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:59
verses.text: And of this, "judgment" is the world convinced; for in vain doth he who will not believe on Christ complain of the devil whom, judged, that is, cast out, and for the exercising of us allowed to attack us from without, not only men, but even women, and boys, and girls, Martyrs have overcome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:60
verses.text: Now in whom have they overcome, but in Him on whom they have believed, and 			 whom seeing not, they loved, and by whose dominion in their hearts they have got rid of a most oppressive lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:61
verses.text: And all this by grace, by the gift, that is, of the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 91:62
verses.text: Rightly then doth the Same Spirit convince the world, both of "sin," because it believeth not on Christ; "and of righteousness," because they who have had the will have believed, though Him on whom they believed they saw not; and by His Resurrection have hoped that themselves also should be in the resurrection perfected; "and of judgment," because if they had had the will to believe, they could 			 be hindered by none, "for that the prince of this world hath been judged already".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:1
verses.text: Sermon XCIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:2
verses.text: [CXLIV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:4
verses.text: ]  On the same words of the Gospel, John xvi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:5
verses.text: 8, "He will convict the world in respect of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgement".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:6
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:7
verses.text: When our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ was speaking at length of the coming of the Holy Ghost, He said among the rest, "He shall convince the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:8
verses.text: Nor when He had said this, did He pass on to another subject; but vouchsafed to convey a somewhat more explicit notice of this same truth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:9
verses.text: "Of sin," said He, "because they believed not on Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:10
verses.text: Of righteousness, because I go to the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:11
verses.text: Of judgment, because the prince of this world hath been judged already".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:12
verses.text: There arises therefore within us a desire of understanding, why as if it were men's only sin, not to believe on Christ, He said it of this alone, that the Holy Ghost should convince the world; but if it is plain that besides this unbelief there are manifold other sins of men, why of this alone should the Holy Ghost convince the world? Is it because all sins are by unbelief retained, by faith remitted; that therefore God imputeth this one above all the rest, by which it comes 			 to pass that the rest are not loosed, so long as proud man believes not in an Humbled God? For so it is written; "God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:13
verses.text: Now this grace of God is a gift of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:14
verses.text: But the greatest gift is the Holy Ghost Himself; and therefore is it called grace.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:15
verses.text: For forasmuch "as all had sinned, and needed the glory of God; because by one man sin entered into the world, and death by his sin in whom all have sinned;" therefore is it grace because given gratuitously.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:16
verses.text: And therefore is it given gratuitously, because it is not rendered as a reward after a strict scrutiny of deserts, but given as a gift after the pardon of sins.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:17
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:18
verses.text: Therefore of sin are unbelievers, that is, the lovers of the world, convinced; for they are signified by the name of the world.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:19
verses.text: For when it is said, "He will convince the world of sin;" it is of none other sin than that they have not believed on Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:20
verses.text: For if this sin exist not, no sins will remain, because when the just man lives by faith, all are loosed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:21
verses.text: Now the difference is great as to whether one believe that Jesus is Christ, or whether he believe on Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:22
verses.text: For that Jesus is Christ even the devils believed, and yet the devils believed not on Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:23
verses.text: For he believeth on Christ, who both hopeth in Christ and loveth Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:24
verses.text: For if he have faith without hope and love, he believeth that Christ is, but he doth not believe on Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:25
verses.text: Whoso then believeth on Christ, by believing on Christ, Christ cometh unto him, and in a manner uniteth Himself to him, and he is made a member in His Body.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:26
verses.text: Which cannot be, but by the accession of hope and love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:27
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:28
verses.text: What mean again His words, "Of righteousness, because I go to the Father"? And first must we enquire, if the world is convinced of sin, why it is also of righteousness? For who can rightly be convinced of righteousness? Is it indeed that the world is convinced of its own sin, but of Christ's righteousness? I do not see what else can be understood; since He saith, "Of sin, because they believed not on Me.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:29
verses.text: Of righteousness, because I go to the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:30
verses.text: They 			 believed not, He goeth to the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:31
verses.text: Their sin therefore, and His righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:32
verses.text: But why would He name righteousness in this only, that He goeth to the Father? Is it not righteousness also that He came hither from the Father? Or is that rather mercy, that He came from the Father to us, and righteousness, that He goeth to the Father?  4.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:33
verses.text: So, Brethren, I think it expedient, that in so profound a depth of Scripture, in words, wherein peradventure there lies some hidden truth which may in due season be laid open, we should as it were together enquire faithfully, that we may attain to find healthfully.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:34
verses.text: Why then doth He call this righteousness, in that He goeth to the Father, and not also in that He came from the Father? Is it that in that it is mercy that He came, therefore it is righteousness that He goeth? that so in our own case too we may learn that righteousness cannot be fulfilled in us, if we are slow to give a place first to mercy, "not seeking our own things, but the things of others also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:35
verses.text: Which advice when the Apostle had given, he immediately joined to it the example of our Lord Himself; "Doing nothing," saith he, "through strife or vain glory; but in lowliness of mind, each esteeming the other better than themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:36
verses.text: Not looking every man on his own things, but also on the things of others".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:37
verses.text: Then he added immediately, "Let this mind be in each of you which was also in Christ 			 Jesus, who, being in the Form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God; but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men, and found in fashion as a man; He humbled Himself, having become obedient even unto death, yea the death of the cross".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:38
verses.text: This is the mercy whereby He came from the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:39
verses.text: What then is the righteousness whereby He goeth to the Father? He goes on and says; "Wherefore God also hath exalted Him, and given Him a Name which is above every name; that at the Name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth, and that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the Glory of God the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:40
verses.text: This is the righteousness whereby He 			 goeth to the Father.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:41
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:42
verses.text: But if He Alone goeth to the Father, what doth it profit us? Why is the world convinced by the Holy Ghost of this righteousness? And yet if He did not Alone go to the Father, He would not say in another place, "No man hath ascended up to heaven, but He That descended from heaven, the Son of man who is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:43
verses.text: But the Apostle Paul also says, "For our conversation is in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:44
verses.text: And why is this? Because he also says, "If ye be risen with Christ, seek the things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:45
verses.text: Mind the things which are above, not those which are upon the earth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:46
verses.text: For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:47
verses.text: How then is He Alone? Is He therefore Alone because Christ with all His members is One, as the Head with His Body? Now what is His Body, but the Church? As the same teacher says, "Now ye are the Body of Christ, and members in particular".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:48
verses.text: Forasmuch then as we have fallen, and He descended for our sakes, what is, "No man hath ascended, but He That descended;" but that no man hath ascended, except as made one with Him, and as a member fastened into His Body who descended? And thus He saith to His disciples, "Without Me ye can do nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:49
verses.text: For in one way is He One with the Father, and in another one with us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:50
verses.text: He is One with the Father, in that the Substance of the Father and the Son is One; He is One with the Father, in that, "Being in the Form of God, He thought it not robbery to be equal with God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:51
verses.text: But He was made One with us, in that "He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant;" He was made one with us, according to the seed of Abraham, "in whom all nations shall be blessed".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:52
verses.text: Which place when 			 the Apostle had brought forward, he said, "He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy Seed, which is Christ".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:53
verses.text: And for that we too belong to that which is Christ, by our incorporation together, and coherence to That Head, It is One Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:54
verses.text: And also for that he says to us too, "Therefore are ye Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:55
verses.text: For if the seed of Abraham be One, and That One Seed of Abraham can only be understood of Christ; but this seed of Abraham we also are; therefore This Whole, that is, the Head and the Body, is One Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:56
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:57
verses.text: And therefore we ought not to deem ourselves separated from that righteousness, which the Lord Himself makes mention of, saying, "Of righteousness, because I go to the Father".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:58
verses.text: For we too have risen with Christ, and we are with Christ our Head, now for a while by faith and hope; but our hope will be completed in the last resurrection of the dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:59
verses.text: But when our hope shall be completed, then shall our justification be completed also.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:60
verses.text: And the Lord who was to complete it showed us in His Own Flesh (that is, in our Head), Wherein He rose again and ascended to the Father, what we ought to hope for.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:61
verses.text: For that thus it is written, "He was delivered for our sins, and rose again for our justification".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:62
verses.text: The world then is convinced "of sin" in those who believe not on Christ; "and of righteousness," in those who rise again in the members of Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:63
verses.text: Whence it is said, "That we may be the righteousness of God in him".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:64
verses.text: For if not in Him, in no way righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:65
verses.text: But if in Him, He goeth with us Whole to the Father, and this perfect righteousness will be fulfilled in us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:66
verses.text: And therefore "of judgment" too is the world convinced, "because the prince of this world hath been judged already;" that is, the devil, the prince of the unrighteous, who in heart inhabit only in this world which they love, and therefore are called "the world;" as our conversation is in heaven, if we have risen 			 again with Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:67
verses.text: Therefore as Christ together with us, that is His Body, is One; so the devil with all the ungodly whose head he is, with as it were his own body, is one.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 92:68
verses.text: Wherefore as we are not separated from the righteousness, of which the Lord said, "Because I go to the Father;" so the ungodly are not separated from that judgment, of which He said, "Because the prince of this world hath been judged already".

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:1
verses.text: Sermon XCV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:2
verses.text: [CXLV.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John xvi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:5
verses.text: 24 , "Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name;" and on the words of Luke x.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:6
verses.text: 17 , "Lord, even the demons are subject unto us in thy name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:8
verses.text: When the Holy Gospel was being read, we heard what in truth ought at once to put every earnest soul in motion to seek, not to faint.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:9
verses.text: For whoso is not moved, is not changed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:10
verses.text: But there is a dangerous movement, of which it is written, "Suffer not my feet to be moved".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:11
verses.text: But there is another movement of him who seeketh, knocketh, asketh.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:12
verses.text: What then has been read we have all heard; but I suppose we have not all understood.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:13
verses.text: It makes mention of that which together with me ye should seek, with me ask, for the receiving of which ye should with me knock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:14
verses.text: For as I hope the grace of the Lord will be with us, that whereas I wish to minister to you, I too may be thought worthy to receive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:15
verses.text: What is it, I pray you, that we have just heard that the Lord said to His disciples? "Hitherto have ye asked nothing in My Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:16
verses.text: Is He not speaking to those disciples, who, after He had sent them, having given them power to preach the Gospel, and to do mighty works, returned with joy, and said to Him, "Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through Thy Name"? Ye recognise, ye recollect this which I have quoted from the Gospel, which in every passage and every sentence speaketh truth, nowhere false, nowhere deceiveth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:17
verses.text: How then is it true, "Hitherto have ye asked nothing in My Name"? and, "Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through Thy name"? Of a surety this puts the mind in motion to ascertain the secret of this difficulty.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:18
verses.text: Therefore ask we, seek, knock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:19
verses.text: Be there in us faithful godliness, not a restlessness of the 			 flesh, but a submission of the mind, that He who seeth us knocking may open unto us.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:21
verses.text: What the Lord then may give to be ministered unto you, do ye with earnest attention, that is, with hunger, receive; and when I shall have spoken it, ye will doubtless with sound taste approve what is placed before you out of the Lord's store.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:22
verses.text: The Lord Jesus knew whereby the soul of man, that is, the rational mind, made after the image of God, could be satisfied: only, that is, by Himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:23
verses.text: This He knew, and knew that it was as yet without that fulness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:24
verses.text: He knew that He was manifest, and He knew that He was hidden.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:25
verses.text: He knew what in Him was exhibited, what concealed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:26
verses.text: He knew all this.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:27
verses.text: "How great," says the Psalm, "is the multitude of Thy sweetness, O 			 Lord, which Thou hast hidden to them that fear Thee; which Thou hast wrought for them that hope in Thee!" "Thy sweetness" both great and manifold "hast Thou hidden to them that fear Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:28
verses.text: If thou hidest it to them that fear Thee, to whom dost Thou open it? "Thou hast wrought it for them that hope in Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:29
verses.text: A twofold question has arisen, but either is solved by the other.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:30
verses.text: If any one inquires after the other, what is this, "Thou hast hidden it to them that fear Thee; wrought it for them that hope in Thee"? Are they that fear, and they that hope, different? Do not 			 the very same who fear God, hope in God? Who hopeth on Him who doth not fear Him? Who in a godly sort feareth Him, and hath not hope in Him? Let this then first be solved.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:31
verses.text: Somewhat would I say concerning those who hope and those who fear.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:32
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:33
verses.text: The Law hath fear, Grace hope.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:34
verses.text: But what difference is there between the Law and Grace, since the Giver both of the Law and Grace is One? The Law alarmeth him who relieth on himself, Grace assisteth him who trusteth in God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:35
verses.text: The Law, I say, alarmeth; do not make light of this because it is brief; weigh it well, and it is considerable.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:36
verses.text: Look well at what I have said, take what we minister, prove wherefrom we take it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:37
verses.text: The Law alarmeth him who relieth on himself, Grace 			 assisteth him who trusteth in God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:38
verses.text: What saith the Law? Many things: and who can enumerate them? I bring forward one small and short precept from it which the Apostle hath brought forward, a very small one; let us see who is sufficient for it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:39
verses.text: "Thou shalt not lust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:40
verses.text: What is this, Brethren? We have heard the Law; if there be no grace, thou hast heard thy punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:41
verses.text: Why dost thou boast to me whosoever thou art that hearing this dost rely upon thyself, why dost thou boast to me of innocence? Why dost thou flatter thyself thereupon? Thou canst say, "I have not plundered the goods of others;" I hear, I believe, perhaps I even see it, thou dost not plunder the goods of others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:42
verses.text: Thou hast heard, "Thou shalt not lust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:43
verses.text: "I do not go in 			 to another man's wife;" this again I hear, believe, see.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:44
verses.text: Thou hast heard, "Thou shalt not lust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:45
verses.text: Why dost thou inspect thyself all round without, and dost not inspect within? Look in, and thou wilt see another law in thy members.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:46
verses.text: Look in, why dost thou pass over thyself? Descend into thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:47
verses.text: Thou wilt "see another law in thy members resisting the law of thy mind, and bringing thee into captivity in the law of sin which is in thy members".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:48
verses.text: With good reason then is the sweetness of God hidden to thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:49
verses.text: The law placed in thy members, resisting the law of thy mind, bringeth thee into captivity.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:50
verses.text: Of that sweetness which to thee is hidden, the holy Angels drink; thou canst not drink and taste that sweetness, captive as thou art.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:51
verses.text: "Thou hadst not known concupiscence, unless the Law had said, Thou shalt not lust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:52
verses.text: Thou heardest, fearedst, didst try to fight, couldest not overcome.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:53
verses.text: For "sin taking occasion by the 			 commandment wrought death".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:54
verses.text: Surely ye recognise them, they are the Apostle's words.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:55
verses.text: "Sin taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:56
verses.text: Why didst thou vaunt thyself in thy pride? Lo, with thine own arms hath the enemy conquered thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:57
verses.text: Thou verily, didst look for a commandment as a defence: and, lo, by the commandment the enemy hath found an occasion of entering in.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:58
verses.text: "For sin taking occasion by the commandment," he saith, "deceived me, and by it slew me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:59
verses.text: What means what I said, "With thine own arms hath the enemy conquered thee"? Hear the same Apostle going on, and saying; "Wherefore the Law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:60
verses.text: Make answer now to the revilers of the Law: make answer on the Apostle's authority, "The commandment is holy, the Law holy, the commandment just and good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:61
verses.text: Was then that which is good, made death unto me? God forbid! But sin that it might appear sin, by that which is good wrought death in me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:62
verses.text: Why is this but because on receiving the commandment thou didst fear, not love? Thou fearedst punishment, thou didst not love righteousness.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:63
verses.text: Whoso feareth punishment, wisheth, if it were possible, to do what pleaseth him, and not to have what he feareth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:64
verses.text: God forbiddeth adultery, thou hast coveted another's wife, thou dost not go in unto her, thou dost not do so, opportunity is given thee, thou hast time, a favourable place is open, witnesses are absent, yet thou dost not do 			 it, wherefore? Because thou fearest the punishment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:65
verses.text: But no one will know it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:66
verses.text: Will not God know it? So it is clear, because God knoweth what thou art about to do, thou doest it not; but here thou fearest the threatenings of God, not lovest His commandments.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:67
verses.text: Why dost thou not do it? Because if thou do, thou wilt be cast into hell fire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:68
verses.text: It is the fire thou fearest.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:69
verses.text: O if thou didst love chastity, thou wouldest not do it, even though thou mightest be altogether unpunished.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:70
verses.text: If God were to say to 			 thee, "Lo, do it, I will not condemn thee, I will not condemn thee to hell fire, but I will withhold My Face from thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:71
verses.text: If thou did it not because of this threat, it would be from the love of God that thou didst not do it, not from the fear of judgment.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:72
verses.text: But thou wouldest do it, perhaps I mean thou wouldest do so; for it is not my place to judge.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:73
verses.text: If thou do it not on this principle because thou abhorrest the contamination of adultery, because thou lovest His precepts, that thou mayest 			 obtain  His promises, and not because thou fearest His condemnation, it is the grace which maketh saints that aideth thee; it is all of grace, ascribe it not to thine own self, attribute it not to thine own strength.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:74
verses.text: Thou actest from delight in it, well; thou actest in charity, well; I assent, I agree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:75
verses.text: Charity worketh by thee, when thou actest with thy will.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:76
verses.text: At once dost thou taste sweetness, if thou hope on the Lord.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:77
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:78
verses.text: But whence hast thou this charity, if yet thou hast it? for I am afraid lest even yet it is through fear thou doest it not, and lest thou seem great in thine own eyes.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:79
verses.text: Now if it is through charity that thou doest it not, thou art truly great.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:80
verses.text: Hast thou charity? "I have," you say.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:81
verses.text: Whence? "From myself".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:82
verses.text: Far art thou from sweetness, if thou hast it from thine own self.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:83
verses.text: Thou wilt love thine own self, because thou wilt love that from which thou hast it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:84
verses.text: But I 			 will convict thee that thou hast it not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:85
verses.text: For in that thou dost think that thou hast so great a thing from thine own self, by that very fact I do not believe thou hast it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:86
verses.text: For if thou hadst, thou wouldest know from whence thou hadst it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:87
verses.text: Hast thou charity from thyself, as if it were some light, some little thing? "If thou shouldest speak with the tongues of men and Angels, but have not charity, thou wouldest be a sounding brass and a tinkling cymbal.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:88
verses.text: If thou shouldest know all mysteries, and 			 have all knowledge, and all prophecy, and all faith so that thou couldest remove mountains, but not have charity," these things could not profit thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:89
verses.text: "If thou shouldest distribute all thy goods to the poor, and deliver up thy body to be burned, but not have charity, thou wouldest be nothing".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:90
verses.text: How great is this charity, which if it be wanting, all things profit nothing! Compare it not to thy faith, not to thy knowledge, not to thy gift of tongues, to lesser things, to the eye of thy body, the hand, the foot, the belly, to any one lowest member compare charity, are these least things to be in any way compared to charity? So then the eye and nose thou hast from God, and hast thou charity from thine own self? If thou hast given thyself charity which surpasseth all things, thou hast made God of light account with thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:91
verses.text: What more can God give thee? Whatever He may have given, is less.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:92
verses.text: Charity which 			 thou hast given thyself, surpasseth all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:93
verses.text: But if thou hast it, thou hast not given it to thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:94
verses.text: "For what hast thou which thou hast not received?" Who gave to me, who gave to thee? God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:95
verses.text: Acknowledge Him in His gifts, that thou feel not His condemnation.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:96
verses.text: By believing the Scriptures, God hath given thee charity, a great boon, charity, which surpasseth all things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:97
verses.text: God gave it thee, "because the charity of God hath been shed abroad in our hearts;" by thine own self, perhaps? God forbid; "by the Holy Ghost, who hath been given us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:98
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:99
verses.text: Return with me to that captive, return with me to my proposition.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:100
verses.text: "The Law alarmeth him that relieth on himself, grace assisteth him who trusteth in God".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:101
verses.text: For look at that captive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:102
verses.text: "He seeth another law in his members resisting the law of his mind, and leading him captive in the law of sin, which is in his members".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:103
verses.text: Lo, he is bound, lo, he is dragged along, lo, he is led captive, lo, he is subjected.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:104
verses.text: What hath that profited him, "Thou shalt not lust"? He hath heard, "Thou shalt not lust;" that he might know his enemy, not that he might overcome him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:105
verses.text: "For he had not known concupiscence," that is, his enemy, "unless the Law had said, Thou shalt not lust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:106
verses.text: Now thou hast seen the enemy, fight, deliver thyself, make good thy liberty, let the suggestions of pleasure be kept down, unlawful delight be utterly destroyed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:107
verses.text: Arm thyself, thou hast the Law, march on, conquer if thou canst.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:108
verses.text: For what good is it that through the little portion of God's grace thou hast already, thou "delightest in the Law of God after the inward man? But thou seest another law in thy members resisting the law of thy mind;" not "resisting" yet 			 powerless for aught, but "leading thee captive in the law of sin".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:109
verses.text: Behold, whence to thee who fearest that "plentifulness of sweetness is hidden!" to him that feareth it "is hidden," how is it" wrought" out for him that "trusteth"? Cry out under thine enemy, for that thou hast an assailant, thou hast an Helper too, who looketh upon thee as thou fightest, who helpeth thee in difficulty; but only if He find thee "trusting;" for the proud He hateth.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:110
verses.text: What then wilt thou cry under this enemy? "Wretched man that I am!" Ye see it already, for ye have cried out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:111
verses.text: Be this your cry, when haply thou art distressed under the enemy, say ye, in your inmost heart say, in sound faith say, "Wretched man that I am!" Wretched that I am! "Therefore wretched," because "I".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:112
verses.text: "Wretched man that I am," both because "I," and because "man".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:113
verses.text: For "he is disquieted in vain".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:114
verses.text: For though "man walketh in the Image;" yet, "wretched man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" Wilt thou thyself? where is thy strength, where is thy confidence? Of a surety thou both criest out, and art silent; silent, that is, from extolling thyself, not from calling upon God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:115
verses.text: Be silent, and cry out.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:116
verses.text: For God Himself too is both silent, and crieth aloud; He is silent from judgment, He is not silent from precept; so be thou too silent from elation, not from invocation; lest God say to 			 thee, "I have been silent, shall I be silent always?" Cry out therefore, "O wretched man that I am!" Acknowledge thyself conquered, put thine own strength to shame, and say, "Wretched man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" What did I say above? The Law alarmeth him that relieth upon himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:117
verses.text: Behold, man relied upon himself, he attempted to fight, he could not get the better, he was conquered, prostrated, subjugated, led captive.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:118
verses.text: He learnt to rely upon God, and it remaineth that him whom the Law 			 alarmed while he relied upon himself, grace should assist now that he trusteth in God.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:119
verses.text: In this confidence he saith, "Who shall deliver me from the body of this death? The grace of God by Jesus Christ our Lord".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:120
verses.text: Now see the sweetness, taste it, relish it; hear the Psalm, "Taste and see that the Lord is sweet".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:121
verses.text: He hath become sweet to thee, for that He hath delivered thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:122
