verses.text: Thou wast bitter to thine own self, when thou didst rely upon thyself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:123
verses.text: Drink sweetness, receive the earnest of so great abundance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:124
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:125
verses.text: The disciples then of the Lord Jesus Christ while yet under the Law had to be cleansed still, to be nourished still, to be corrected still, to be directed still.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:126
verses.text: For they still had concupiscence; whereas the Law saith, "Thou shalt not lust".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:127
verses.text: Without offence to those holy rams, the leaders of the flock, without offence to them I would say it, for I say the truth: the Gospel relates, that they contended which of them should be the greatest, and whilst the Lord was yet on earth, they were agitated by a dissension about pre-eminence.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:128
verses.text: Whence was this, but from the old leaven? whence, but from the law in the members, resisting the law of the mind? They sought for eminence; yea, they desired it; they thought which should be the greatest; therefore is their pride put to shame by a little child.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:129
verses.text: Jesus calleth unto him the age of humility to tame the swelling desire.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:130
verses.text: With good reason then when they returned too, and said, "Lord, behold even the devils are subject unto us through Thy Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:131
verses.text: (It was for a nothing that they rejoiced; of what importance was it compared to that which God promised?) The Lord, the Good Master, quieting fear, and building up a firm support, said to them, "In this rejoice not that the devils are subject unto 			 you".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:132
verses.text: Why so? Because "many will come in My Name, saying, Behold, in Thy Name we have cast out devils; and I will say to them, I know you not.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:133
verses.text: In this rejoice not, but rejoice because your names are written in heaven".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:134
verses.text: Ye cannot yet be there, yet notwithstanding ye are already written there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:135
verses.text: Therefore "rejoice".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:136
verses.text: So that place again, "Hitherto have ye asked nothing in My Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:137
verses.text: For what ye have asked, in comparison with that which I am willing to give, is nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:138
verses.text: For what have ye asked in My Name? That the devils should be subject unto you? "In this rejoice not," that is, what ye have asked is nothing; for if it were anything, He would bid them rejoice.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:139
verses.text: So then it was not absolutely nothing, but that it was little in comparison of that greatness of God's rewards.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:140
verses.text: For the Apostle Paul was not really not anything; and yet in comparison of God, 			 "Neither is he that planteth anything, neither he that watereth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:141
verses.text: And so I say to you, and I say to myself, both to myself and you I say, when we ask in Christ's Name for these temporal things.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:142
verses.text: For ye have asked undoubtedly.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:143
verses.text: For who doth not ask? One asketh for health, if he is sick; another asketh for deliverance, if he is in prison; another asketh for the port, if he is tossed about at sea; another asketh for victory, if he is in conflict with an enemy; and in the Name of Christ he asketh all, and what he asketh is nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:144
verses.text: What then 			 must be asked for? "Ask in My Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:145
verses.text: And He said not what, but by the very words we understand what we ought to ask.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:146
verses.text: "Ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be full.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:147
verses.text: Ask, and ye shall receive, in My Name".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:148
verses.text: But what? Not nothing; but what? "That your joy may be full;" that is, ask what may suffice you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:149
verses.text: For when thou askest for temporal things, thou askest for nothing.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:150
verses.text: "Whoso shall drink of this water, shall thirst again".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:151
verses.text: He letteth down the watering pot of desire into the well, he taketh up whereof to drink, only that he may thirst again.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:152
verses.text: "Ask, that your joy may be full;" that is, that ye may be satisfied, not feel delight only for a time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:153
verses.text: Ask what may suffice you; speak Philip's language, "Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:154
verses.text: The Lord saith to you, "Have I been so long time with you, and have ye not known Me? Philip, he that seeth Me, seeth the Father also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:155
verses.text: Render then thanks to Christ, made weak for you that are weak, and make ready your desires for Christ's Divinity, to be satisfied therewith.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 93:156
verses.text: Turn we to the Lord, etc.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:1
verses.text: Sermon XCVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:2
verses.text: [CXLVI.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:4
verses.text: ]  On the words of the Gospel, John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:5
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:6
verses.text: 16, "Simon, son of John, lovest thou me?" etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:8
verses.text: Ye have observed, beloved, that in to-day's lesson it was said by the Lord to Peter in a question, "Lovest thou Me?" To whom he answered, "Thou knowest, Lord, that I love thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:9
verses.text: This was done a second, and a third time; and at each several reply, the Lord said, "Feed My lambs".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:10
verses.text: To Peter did Christ commend His lambs to be fed, who fed even Peter himself.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:11
verses.text: For what could Peter do for the Lord, especially now that He had an Immortal Body, and was about to ascend into heaven? As though He had said to him, "'Lovest thou Me?' Herein show that thou lovest Me, 'Feed my sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:12
verses.text: '" So then, Brethren, do ye with obedience hear that ye are Christ's sheep; seeing that we on our part with fear hear, Feed My sheep"? If we feed with fear, and fear for 			 the sheep; these sheep how ought they to fear for themselves? Let then carefulness be our portion, obedience yours; pastoral watchfulness our portion, the humility of the flock yours.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:13
verses.text: Although we too who seem to speak to you from a higher place, are with fear beneath your feet; forasmuch as we know how perilous an account must be rendered of this as it were exalted seat.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:14
verses.text: Wherefore, dearly beloved, Catholic plants, Members of Christ, think What a Head ye have! Children of God, think What a 			 Father ye have found.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:15
verses.text: Christians, think What an Inheritance is promised you.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:16
verses.text: Not such as on earth cannot be possessed by children, save when their parents are dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:17
verses.text: For no one on earth possesses a father's inheritance, save when he is dead.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:18
verses.text: But we whilst our Father liveth shall possess what He shall give; for that our Father cannot die.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:19
verses.text: I add more, I say more, and say the truth; our Father will Himself be our Inheritance.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:20
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:21
verses.text: Live consistently, especially ye candidates of Christ, recently baptized, just regenerated, as I have admonished you before, so say I now, and give expression to my solicitude; for the present lesson of the Gospel hath forced upon me a greater fear: take heed to yourselves, do not imitate evil Christians.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:22
verses.text: Say not I will do this, for many of the faithful do it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:23
verses.text: This is not to procure a defence for the soul; but to look out for companions unto hell.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:24
verses.text: Grow ye in this floor 			 of the Lord; herein ye will find good men to please you, if ye yourselves are good.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:25
verses.text: For are ye our private property? Heretics and schismatics have made their own private property out of what they have stolen from the Lord, and would feed, not Christ's flocks, but their own against Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:26
verses.text: It is true indeed, they place His title on these their spoils, that their robberies may be as it were maintained by the title of His Power.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:27
verses.text: What doeth Christ when such as these are 			 converted, who have received the title of His Baptism out of the Church? He casteth out the spoiler, He doth not efface the title, and taketh possession of the house; because He hath found His title there.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:28
verses.text: What need is there that He should change His Own Name? Do they take heed to what the Lord said to Peter, "Feed My lambs, feed My sheep"? Did He say to him, "Feed thy lambs;" or, "Feed thy sheep"? But for them who are shut out, what said He in the Song of Songs, unto the Church? 			 The Spouse speaking to the Bride, saith, "If thou know not thyself, O thou fair one among women, go forth".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:29
verses.text: As though He said, "I do not cast thee out, 'go forth, if thou know not thyself, O thou fair one among women,' if thou know not thyself in the mirror of divine Scripture, if thou give not heed, O thou fair woman, to the mirror which with no false lustre deceiveth thee; if thou know not that of thee it is said, 'Thy glory shall be above all earth;' that of thee it is said, 'I will give thee nations for thine inheritance, and the limits of the earth for thy possession;' and other innumerable testimonies which set forth the Catholic Church.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:30
verses.text: If then thou know not these, thou hast no part in Me, thou canst not make thyself My heir.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:31
verses.text: 'Go forth then in the footsteps of the flocks' not in the fellowship of the flock; and feed thy goats, not as it was said to Peter, 'My sheep.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:32
verses.text: '" To Peter it was said, "My sheep;" to schismatics it is said," thy goats".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:33
verses.text: In the one place "sheep," in the other "goats;" in the one place 			 "Mine," in the other "thine".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 94:34
verses.text: Recollect the right Hand and the left of our Judge; recollect where the goats shall stand, and where the sheep; and it will be plain to you where is the right hand, where the left, the white and the black, the lightsome, and the darksome, the fair and the deformed, that which is about to receive the kingdom, and that which is to find everlasting punishment.

chapters.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:1
verses.text: Sermon XCVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:2
verses.text: [CXLVII.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:3
verses.text: Ben.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:4
verses.text: ]  On the same words of the Gospel of John.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:5
verses.text: xxi.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:6
verses.text: 15, "Simon, son of John, lovest thou me more than these?" etc.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:7
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:8
verses.text: Ye remember that the Apostle Peter, the first of all the Apostles, was disturbed at the Lord's Passion.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:9
verses.text: Of his own self disturbed, but by Christ renewed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:10
verses.text: For he was first a bold presumer, and became afterwards a timid denier.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:11
verses.text: He had promised that he would die for the Lord, when the Lord was first to die for him.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:12
verses.text: When he said then, "I will be with Thee even unto death," and "I will lay down my life for Thee;" the Lord answered 			 him, "Wilt thou lay down thy life for Me? Verily I say unto thee, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny Me thrice".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:13
verses.text: They came to the hour; and because that Christ was God, and Peter a man, the Scripture was fulfilled, "I said in my panic, Every man is a liar".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:14
verses.text: And the Apostle says, "For God is true, and every man a liar".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:15
verses.text: Christ true, Peter a liar.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:16
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:17
verses.text: But what now? The Lord asketh him as ye heard when the Gospel was being read, and saith to him, "Simon, son of John, lovest thou Me more than these?" He answered and said, "Yea Lord Thou knowest that I love Thee".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:18
verses.text: And again the Lord asked this question, and a third time He asked it.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:19
verses.text: And when he asserted in reply his love, He commended to him the flock.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:20
verses.text: For each several time the Lord Jesus said to Peter, as he said, "I love thee;" "Feed My lambs," feed My "little sheep".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:21
verses.text: In this one Peter was figured the unity of all pastors, of good pastors, that is, who know that they feed Christ's sheep for Christ, not for themselves.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:22
verses.text: Was Peter at this time a liar, or did he answer 			 untruly that he loved the Lord? He made this answer truly; for he made answer of that which he saw in his own heart.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:23
verses.text: Whereas when he said, "I will lay down my life for Thee," he would presume on future strength.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:24
verses.text: Now every man knows it may be what sort of man he is at the time when he is speaking; what he shall be on the morrow, who knows? So then Peter turned back his eyes to his own heart, when he was asked by the Lord, and in confidence made answer of what he saw there: "'Yea, Lord, 			 Thou knowest that I love Thee.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:25
verses.text: ' What I tell Thee, Thou knowest; what I see here in my heart, Thou seest also".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:26
verses.text: Nevertheless, he did not venture to say what the Lord had asked.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:27
verses.text: For the Lord had not simply said, "Lovest Thou me?" but had added, "Lovest thou Me more than these?" that is, "Lovest thou Me more than these here do?" He was speaking of the other disciples; Peter could not say ought but, "I love Thee;" he did not venture to say, "more than these".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:28
verses.text: He would not be 			 a liar a second time.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:29
verses.text: It were enough for him to bear testimony to his own heart; it was no duty of his to be judge of the heart of others.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:30
Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:31
verses.text: Peter then was true; or rather was Christ true in Peter? Now when the Lord Jesus Christ would, He abandoned Peter, and Peter was found a man; but when it so pleased the Lord Jesus Christ, He filled Peter, and Peter was found true.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:32
verses.text: The Rock (Petra) made Peter true, for the Rock was Christ.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:33
verses.text: And what did He announce to him, when he answered a third time that he loved Christ, and a third time the Lord commended His little sheep to Peter? He announced to him 			 beforehand his suffering.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:34
verses.text: "When thou wast young," saith He, "thou girdedst thyself, and wentest whither thou wouldest; but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thine hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:35
verses.text: The Evangelist hath explained to us Christ's meaning.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:36
verses.text: "This spake He," saith he, "signifying by what death he should glorify God;" that is that he was crucified for Christ; for this is, "Thou shalt stretch forth thine hands".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:37
verses.text: Where now is that denier? Then after this the Lord Christ said, "Follow Me".

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:38
verses.text: Not in the same sense as before, when he called the disciples.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:39
verses.text: For then too He said, "Follow Me;" but then to instruction, now to a crown.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:40
verses.text: Was he not afraid to be put to death when he denied Christ? He was afraid to suffer that which Christ suffered.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:41
verses.text: But now he must be afraid no more.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:42
verses.text: For he saw 			 Him now Alive in the Flesh, whom he had seen hanging on the Tree.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:43
verses.text: By His Resurrection Christ took away the fear of death; and forasmuch as He had taken away the fear of death, with good reason did He enquire of Peter's love.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:44
verses.text: Fear had thrice denied, love thrice confessed.

verses.name: Augustine: Sermons of the New Testament 95:45
verses.text: The threefoldness of denial, the forsaking of the Truth; the threefoldness of confession, the testimony of love.
